title: THE POLITICS OF INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: In Politics of Indigenous Australia we will explore a wide range of topics related to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander politics. This subject enables you to understand what Indigenous politics include, from Dreaming Lore to the introduction of British colonial law. You will learn about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander heroes of the resistance to Frontier violence, and civil rights activism against racial discrimination. The history of the fight for First Nation rights in Australia will be compared to other countries colonised by the British, and the subject teaches students to critically analyse the effectiveness of government policies such as the White Australia policy, Aboriginal Protection Acts, the Racial Discrimination Act, Native Title Amendments Act, and Closing the Gap. The final topic is reconciliation and allyship – to teach students how to go forward with their knowledge of Indigenous politics and be part of a decolonised future where truth telling, healing, and treaty can see Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians work together respectfully.
learning_outcomes: Apply research methods to demonstrate a written understanding of the subject matter.
Reflect on your own identity and how this affects your positionality in debates related to Indigenous politics.
Produce a developed written argument that reflects Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives of the subject matter.
Develop your knowledge to understand the key topics of the politics of Indigenous Australia.
Analyse a range of materials in the field of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies.

title: DECOLONISING ABORIGINAL STUDIES
syllabus_overview: This subject explores colonisation through a critical lens to encourage innovative social change. Topics include accounts of colonialism, Indigeneity, and survival. You will critically examine how past and current Indigenous knowledges are represented in the Western academy, and ongoing contestation of Indigenous perspectives within research governance, pedagogy and curriculum design. You will be inspired to think beyond Western boundaries as places of containment and sites of struggle for Indigenous peoples within a global, national and local context. This subject collectively and individually fosters new ways to be innovative whilst respectful, through critically examining colonial structures and relationships rather than subjectively problematizing Indigenous peoples and cultures.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of aspects of Aboriginal history, research practices, politics and community.
Analyse the impact of historical changes to Aboriginal society and contrast with contemporary Aboriginal Australia.
Analyse key ethical and cultural issues relating to Aboriginal society and Australian relations.
Evaluate key Aboriginal Studies topics and theories of Aboriginal Studies.

title: ANTHROPOLOGY OF ABORIGINAL AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: In this subject we take an anthropological view of contemporary Aboriginal life in all its variety, but we also look at the relationship between the pre-colonial past and the post-colonial present in the forging of Aboriginal identities. You will gain an anthropological understanding of features of Aboriginal life which to an extent predate the European settlement of Australia, such as foraging economies, systems of kinship and marriage, and the culture of 'the Dreaming'. We also take an anthropological view of the impact of colonisation and how Aboriginal economy, society and culture have been transformed through relationships with non-Indigenous Australians. In particular, we consider how Aboriginal people have become increasingly conscious of themselves as a single people defined as an Indigenous minority in a settler nation.
learning_outcomes: Present a sustained written argument in Aboriginal Anthropology.
Evaluate diverse positions/arguments regarding a relevant topic in Aboriginal Anthropology.
Apply ethical and cultural awareness to issues in Aboriginal Anthropology.
Summarise research and arguments on a relevant topic in Aboriginal Anthropology.
Produce a well researched response to a relevant topic in Aboriginal Anthropology.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ABORIGINAL AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to various elements of Indigenous Australia. You will study a broad range of issues of relevance to contemporary Aborigines and Torres Strait Islander people. There will be a particular emphasis on the Indigenous topics of Australia, in addition, students will gain an understanding of regional variation throughout Australia. Issues discussed include cultural continuity and differences, identity, self-representation, spirituality, family, gender, land, politics, law, economics, education, health, history, art and music. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a range of texts in the field of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander studies
Produce a sustained, complex written argument about social research methods relating to a topic on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
Apply knowledge to understanding concepts and issues, and interpreting data about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia and the world today
Apply suitable research methods to addressing social issues involving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people

title: WOMINJEKA LA TROBE: INDIGENOUS CULTURAL LITERACY FOR HIGHER EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: Wominjeka La Trobe is a short one-hour compulsory online subject that introduces all La Trobe students to Indigenous Australian history, culture and customs. A rich and relevant cultural heritage education is important for everyone. This topic highlights the link between Indigenous knowledge and values and broader cultural literacy. It asks you to think critically about your own attitudes, values and beliefs.
learning_outcomes: Reflect critically on your own cultural attitudes, values and beliefs
Demonstrate knowledge of and respect for Indigenous Australian perspectives and experiences, history, culture and customs, including an appreciation of the local people and country
Recall important details regarding the history, culture, customs and people of Indigenous Australia
Understand the need for and value of appropriate and effective intercultural communication

title: GOVERNANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In today's fast-paced corporate world, aligning company operations with stakeholder interests is crucial for maximizing firm value. The collapse of high-profile companies at the dawn of the 21st century has highlighted the critical importance of robust corporate governance and risk management. In Australia, it is argued that the downfall of firms are due to inadequate governance serves as a stark reminder of this need. This subject empowers students with a deep understanding of corporate governance and risk management, promoting transparency, accountability, ethical practices, and effective risk mitigation within organisations. In this subject, students will gain knowledge of both theoretical and practical aspects of these critical fields, equipping them to navigate and thrive in the modern business landscape.
learning_outcomes: Communicate both individually and as part of a team in a group assignment
Analyse and evaluate approaches to risk management in organisations
Critically analyse practical and theoretical foundations of corporate governance
Critically evaluate the major influences and mechanisms of corporate governance

title: ACCOUNTING INFORMATIONAL SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: The digital transformation of business operations has led to an increasing demand for accounting and business professionals to develop information and communications technology (ICT) skills. This subject is designed to develop your ICT skills in the context of accounting practice. You will apply the key concepts and principles underlying the recognition, measurement, recording and provision of accounting information using accounting information systems that are powered by information technologies, business intelligence, and accounting software. You will also learn to employ these tools to develop, manage and control accounting information systems, as well as to critically evaluate the relevance and sufficiency of such systems and communicate the findings to relevant stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate current ICT processes and controls within an organisation and develop solutions to make them more effective
Engages pro-actively with team members in team decision making, and facilitates the achievement of project outcomes
Communicate findings related to AIS and their implications to relevant stakeholders in a clear and appropriate manner
Employ accounting software, information technologies and business intelligence tools to develop, manage and control accounting information systems within organisations

title: AUDITING AND ASSURANCE
syllabus_overview: Auditing is a fundamental component of professional services. Auditing provides confidence in the quality of financial reports. This subject examines the nature and purpose of audit and assurance services, and the legal, regulatory and professional environment in which it operates. You will learn to apply relevant auditing standards to plan, execute and report findings to internal and external users. Modern auditing and data analytics tools will also be explored in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate audit and assurance findings to relevant stakeholders in a clear and appropriate manner
Identify and assess the risks of material misstatement in the financial statements and consider the impact on the audit strategy
Discuss the nature and purpose of audit and assurance and its operating environment
Apply relevant auditing standards, laws, regulations and tools to an audit of general-purpose financial statements

title: ACCOUNTING INFORMATION SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: The digital transformation of business operations has led to an increasing demand for accounting and business professionals to develop information and communications technology (ICT) skills. This subject is designed to develop your ICT skills in the context of accounting practice. You will apply the key concepts and principles underlying the recognition, measurement, recording and provision of accounting information using accounting information systems that are powered by information technologies, business intelligence, and accounting software. You will also learn to employ these tools to develop, manage and control accounting information systems, as well as to critically evaluate the relevance and sufficiency of such systems and communicate the findings to relevant stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively in a team to produce high quality work
Effectively and appropriately communicate findings about and from AIS and their implications to relevant stakeholders.
Employ accounting software, information technologies and business intelligence tools to develop, manage and control accounting information systems within organisations.
Critically evaluate current ICT processes and controls within an organisation and develop solutions to make them more effective.

title: FORENSIC ACCOUNTING
syllabus_overview: Forensic accounting involves the application of specialist accounting knowledge and investigative skills in the areas of litigation support and fraud examination. This subject focuses on the fraud examination aspects of forensic accounting. You will develop your understanding of key theoretical and conceptual aspects of fraud examination. You will explore the nature and types of fraud, approaches to fraud prevention, methods of fraud detection, and the key elements involved in conducting a fraud investigation.
learning_outcomes: Explain key concepts, functions, (and practices) of forensic accounting and fraud examination.
Analyse the characteristics, methods, and implications of financial statement fraud.
Evaluate approaches to preventing and detecting fraud and fraud schemes
Evaluate different types of fraud, including organisational, consumer, and e-commerce-related fraud.

title: FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING AND REPORTING
syllabus_overview: Currently over 100 countries have adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), or their equivalent, to prepare financial statements by listed companies. A sound knowledge about IFRS is essential for accounting professionals to prepare comparable and understandable financial information to users. This subject focuses on applying IFRS and Australian accounting standards to account for complex practical issues. This includes applying accounting standards involving measurement and professional judgement to recognise common revenue transactions, analyse business acquisition, and preparing consolidated financial statements.
learning_outcomes: Explain the national and international environment of financial reporting including the current conceptual framework, regulatory and legal frameworks
Present complex business concepts and strategies demonstrating clarity, coherence, and engagement with the audience

Apply International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and the equivalent Australian Accounting Standards Board (AASB) standards to account for business transactions and prepare consolidated financial statements
Interpret financial and non-financial information, including corporate sustainability reporting, and communicate the findings professionally to various stakeholders

title: FORENSIC ACCOUNTING
syllabus_overview: Forensic accounting involves applying specialist accounting knowledge and investigative skills in the areas of litigation support and fraud examination. This subject focuses on the fraud examination aspects of forensic accounting. It aims to develop your knowledge of key theoretical and conceptual aspects of fraud examination. In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the nature of fraud, different types of fraud, approaches to fraud prevention, methods of fraud detection, and key elements of fraud investigations.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate approaches to preventing and detecting fraud and fraud schemes
Evaluate fraud against organisations, consumer fraud and fraud in the e-commerce environment
Explain the underlying concepts and functions of forensic accounting and fraud examination
Critically assess financial statement fraud

title: COST INFORMATION FOR DECISION MAKING
syllabus_overview: The Cost Information for Decision Making subject provides organisational decision-makers relevant accounting information to assist with their planning, controlling and performance management. You will develop knowledge and skills relating to various management accounting principles and techniques used in contemporary organisations. You will learn and apply budgeting, product and service costing, pricing, control and performance evaluation, and undertake evidence-based inquiry to critically analyse and solve real-world business problems.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate costing techniques to determine product and service cost and price
Apply relevant management accounting methods and information to support organisational planning, control, and performance management
Prepare detailed budgets and forecasts to support effective organisational planning and control
Prepare professional reports to inform management’s decision-making

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF ACCOUNTING
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with an understanding of accounting process and application in the business environment. The subject covers the conceptual framework underlying accounting practices and the application of accounting information systems in the process of recording and reporting business transactions. After studying this subject, you will be enabled to use accounting information to make business decisions and judgments incorporating both technical knowledge and ethical principles.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of accounting in the business environment
Use information communications technology (ICT) in the process of reporting, recording and analysing accounting information
Apply fundamental accounting concepts and ethical principles in recording and reporting business transactions
Prepare basic financial statements and analyse financial reports for decision making purposes

title: ACCOUNTING FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the nature of accounting and its role in business. Accounting for Business develops students’ understanding of the language of business through the analysis of financial transactions and statements to assess a business’s financial health and performance, and apply this understanding to decision making in a variety of roles. You will also learn the ethical requirements underpinning financial statements and how to interpret financial statements. Additionally, you will understand a budget and its importance to the business as well as the information required to make strategic and tactical decisions from a non-accountant user’s perspective.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret financial statements and discuss implications for business decision-making
Explain the importance of accounting reporting and ethical and corporate governance issues as they apply to managerial decisions
Develop teamwork skills to prepare and apply Budgets, Variances, and Cost-Volume-Profit analysis in business decision-making
Understand the interaction of decision-making across various organisational functions on financial performance

title: ADVANCED ACCOUNTING
syllabus_overview: Advanced accounting is an integral part of an organisation’s financial reporting function. Financial reporting furnishes investors with valuable information to aid in decision-making regarding resource allocation to the entity. This subject focuses on applying accounting theories to more advanced practical issues involving measurement and judgement. This involves examining motivators behind firms’ disclosure of both financial and non-financial information, analysing accounting policy choices and firms’ responses to varying accounting standards, and addressing complex industry-specific issues. Additionally, this subject introduces the impacts of emerging digital technologies in financial reporting.
learning_outcomes: Critically review and apply relevant accounting theories to accounting practices and regulations
Evaluate current developments in financial reporting and information, including the impact of emerging digital technologies on accounting practice
Exercise ethical professional judgement in the measurement and assessment of accounting issues
Apply international and Australian accounting standards to account for complex issues in financial reporting

title: INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides opportunities to explore and discuss challenges and successes relating to Indigenous communities developing and managing their own business. There will be a focus on the history and continuity of Aboriginal community self determination and sovereignties. Students will critically assess case studies relevant to Indigenous community development principles and practices and the role of government legislation and intervention frameworks. Indigenous voices will be privileged across all topics relating to this subject.
learning_outcomes: Reflect and critique on the academic literature relating to social policy and practice and the intersection with legislative and community frameworks.
Analyse, discuss and critique a range of texts in the field of Indigenous development, Australian or international government policies and academic literature.
Compare and analyse contemporary perspectives of Indigenous peoples and their cultures' community development aspirations and how these are impacted by colonialism.
Apply learnt concepts from lectures, tutorials and readings through assessment tasks.

title: INTEGRATED ACCOUNTING PROJECT
syllabus_overview: Business problems in practice are often complex and require accountants to have integrated knowledge from different fields in order to analyse the root cause of problem and develop a solution that benefits different stakeholders. This capstone subject is designed to give you an opportunity to integrate your knowledge from different subjects and skills into action, and apply what you have learnt in the classroom to solve real-world business problems. For example, you will apply strategic management accounting principles to evaluate the performance of organisations, including its products or services, and people. You will use data analytics tools to assist data-driven decision making. You will exercise professional judgements in the context of financial and non-financial information disclosure. You will undertake practical accounting projects that simulate the management of an organisation to prepare you for your transition to the workplace.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the performance of an organisation, including its processes, products, and people, and develop strategies for continual improvement
Integrate accounting knowledge and skills to solve practical accounting problems in diverse contexts
Communicate accounting information clearly and effectively, both individually and as part of a team, to various stakeholders from diverse backgrounds
Apply appropriate technologies and data analytics tools to strengthen internal control, planning, performance, and evidence-based decision-making processes

title: TAXATION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an understanding of Commonwealth income tax legislation and the implications of income tax on individuals and businesses. A problem solving, application-based approach is taken to the subject matter. You will study the general concepts of assessable income and allowable deductions (including substantiation provisions) and be introduced to capital gains and fringe benefits tax. The taxation of entities will also be covered, including the taxation of partnerships, companies and trusts. The subject will also cover the basic aspects of tax administration and assessments, objections and appeals.
learning_outcomes: Explain various types of taxation including income tax, taxes on capital, goods and services tax and fringe benefits tax.
Identify the sources of Australian taxation law and the framework in which taxation is administered.
Critically analyse the taxation issues associated with international transactions.
Critically apply fundamental tax concepts, legislative provisions as well as judicial principles to analyse personal, property and business taxable income and tax payable scenarios.

title: ACCOUNTING PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES
syllabus_overview: Accounting principles are critical for ensuring consistent and reliable accounting practices. This unit develops students’ understanding of fundamental accounting principles and their application to various accounting processes and systems. Students will learn how to systematically identify and analyse business transactions, prepare financial statements, and evaluate businesses financial performance using relevant accounting tools. Students will also enhance their professional judgment and data analytics skills by exposure to real-world business scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and record business transactions, and prepare financial statements using double-entry accounting principles.
Evaluate the accounting purpose, processes and systems within the Australian or an international regulatory environment
Critically evaluate financial performance of firms to inform decision making using relevant information.
Exercise professional judgement to solve accounting problems from ethical, social, and regulatory perspectives, and effectively communicate relevant information to a range of stakeholders

title: ACCOUNTING INFORMATION SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: The proliferation of digital technologies in business is resulting in a growing need for accounting and business professionals to cultivate their proficiency in information and communications technology (ICT) and business intelligence systems. This subject develops students’ knowledge of accounting information systems and business intelligence tools to measure, record and generate accounting information for analysis and decision-making within the framework of accounting principles and procedures. Students will learn how to critically evaluate and use these tools to record, manage, report, and communicate business processes and accounting information to various stakeholders, and determine how these tools can help organisations to effectively manage internal control risks.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively in a team to produce high quality work
Develop and employ accounting software application and/or an enterprise business intelligence tool to record, manage and communicate business processes to various stakeholders.
Critically evaluate the role, use and impact of accounting information systems and technologies on organisation’s business operations, processes, data analysis and decision making.

Critically evaluate the role and adequacy of ICT processes and controls in identifying, managing and reporting risks in organisations and improving organisational systems, processes and communications.

title: STRATEGIC BUSINESS LEADER
syllabus_overview: Strategic business leadership is integral to organizations survival, performance, and competitiveness in a highly competitive business world. This subject develops students' knowledge of organisational leadership and senior consultancy or advisory capabilities and relevant professional skills. Students will learn the main aspects of leadership including qualities of leadership, professionalism, ethics and governance, strategy, risk, technology and data analytics, organizational control and audit, financial decision-making, change management, and professional skills.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the effectiveness of the governance and agency system in a complex organisational environment.
Apply leadership and professional skills in the organisational context and in preparation for career success
Enable organizational success and change management through practical thinking, disruptive technology, talent management, performance management, strategic change, and effective project management.
Apply appropriate tools to evaluate organization’s strategic position, risks, internal controls, audit systems, and ethical and social responsibility, and develop relative strategic actions.

title: ADVANCED PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Performance management is integral to organisations' strategic planning, continuous improvement to processes, people and outcomes and goal congruence. This subject develops students’ knowledge of advanced management accounting and performance management practices. Students will learn how to exercise professional judgement to contribute to the strategic planning, control, and evaluation and management of the performance of an organisation and its strategic and operational development.
learning_outcomes: Apply strategic planning and control models to plan, monitor and evaluate organisational performance.
Assess the impact of risk and uncertainty on organisational performance.
Evaluate the strategic performance of organisations and communicate findings of corporate success and failure to various stakeholders.
Evaluate the impact of developments in information systems and technology on organisations performance measurement and management systems.

title: FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING AND REPORTING
syllabus_overview: Financial accounting and reporting is integral to organization's preparation of financial and non-financial information to various stakeholders. This subject will develop students’ knowledge and skills of financial accounting and reporting by appropriately applying the relevant accounting standards involving measurement and professional judgement to a variety of practical scenarios in the current business environment. This subject will also focus on developing students’ knowledge in group accounts and sustainability reporting.
learning_outcomes: Apply International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and the equivalent Australian Accounting Standards Board (AASB) standards to account for business transactions appropriately.
Apply the relevant IFRS and AASB accounting standards to prepare consolidated financial statements
Communicate financial and non-financial data to various stakeholders from global, social, economic, and regulatory perspectives.
Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies, estimates, and judgments used in preparing financial statements

title: ADVANCED AUDIT AND ASSURANCE
syllabus_overview: Audit is a systematic and independent examination of an organisation’s financial records, transactions, and operational procedures. This subject advances students’ auditing knowledge and skills to analyse, evaluate and conclude on the assurance engagement and other audit and assurance issues in the context of best practice and current development. Students will delve into various topics, including the regulatory landscape encompassing international frameworks for audit and assurance services, anti-money laundering regulations, legal and regulatory requirements, professional ethics, quality control, and practice management. Additionally, they will learn about planning and executing audits of historical financial data, finalising, reviewing, and reporting findings, as well as auditing social, environmental, and integrated reports.
learning_outcomes: Apply the International Standards on Auditing to audit assignments, and formulate the work required to meet the objectives of audit and non-audit assignments.
Evaluate the current issues and developments relating to the provision of audit and assurance services.
Evaluate the international legal and regulatory environment and its impact on audit and assurance practices of auditors.
Critically assess appropriate quality control policies and procedures in practice management and make recommendations for improvement.

title: STRATEGIC BUSINESS REPORTING
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to advance your financial accounting and reporting knowledge and skills. You will discuss, apply and evaluate the concepts, principles and practices that underpin the preparation and interpretation of corporate reports in various contexts. You will examine corporate reporting not only from the preparer’s perspective, but also from a variety of stakeholders’ perspective. You will evaluate management’s corporate reporting decisions and their implications for a range of stakeholders and entities. Accounting professional and ethical responsibilities are also explored in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the financial statements and performance of groups of entities, and effectively present them to diverse stakeholders using appropriate tools.
Apply professional judgement in accordance with ethical and professional principles in the context of financial reporting in real-world business scenarios
Evaluate the appropriateness of the financial reporting framework, and critically discuss changes in accounting regulation and the impact on financial reporting

title: SUSTAINABILITY AND ESG REPORTING
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a comprehensive introduction to sustainability reporting within the context of contemporary business practices. You will explore the principles of 'Triple Bottom Line Accounting' and develop expertise in both external and internal reporting aspects of corporate social and environmental sustainability. The subject examines how sustainability information can be integrated into organisational decision-making processes and explores the implications for assurance functions in modern accounting practice. Sustainability Reporting addresses the growing demand for accounting professionals with expertise in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks, climate-related financial disclosures, and sustainability metrics. Through a combination of theoretical foundations and practical applications, you will develop the skills needed to navigate the rapidly evolving landscape of sustainability reporting.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively in teams to analyse organisational sustainability reporting practices
Communicate sustainability reporting findings clearly and persuasively to professional and academic audiences using appropriate formats and conventions
Critically evaluate the value of sustainability reporting, accountability, and reporting in contemporary business contexts
Apply relevant theoretical concepts to analyse complex sustainability reporting issues with consideration of ethical, social, and environmental consequences

title: ADVANCED ACCOUNTING ISSUES
syllabus_overview: Professional judgement is essential for the application of principle-based international financial and sustainability reporting standards to accounting practice. This subject develops students' systematic understanding of contemporary accounting issues, including theories underpinning firms' accounting policy choices, global harmonisation of financial reporting standards, and advanced industry-specific measurement challenges. Students will also explore emerging global issues including climate-related financial disclosures and the digital transformation of accounting practices.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of technology innovation on accounting practices.
Design a research-based accounting project proposal and execute the project both independently and as part of a team.
Critically apply accounting theories and international financial reporting standards to address contemporary issues in national and international accounting practices.
Examine factors that influence the quality of financial reporting to determine the faithful representation and relevance of accounting information.

title: AUDITING AND ASSURANCE
syllabus_overview: Financial report audit is an independent examination of a company's financial statements and related disclosures by an auditor. This subject develops students’ knowledge of the core principles and objectives of financial report auditing, as well as the responsibilities of auditors in delivering high-quality reports to stakeholders. Students will acquire the skills to apply relevant auditing standards to effectively plan, execute, and communicate audit findings to both internal and external stakeholders. Additionally, the subject will expose students to various audit techniques used by auditors to conduct audit procedures and assess evidence. By engaging with real-world auditing case studies, students will enhance their analytical skills and problem-solving abilities while employing technical audit principles and standards.
learning_outcomes: Apply quantitative methods and relevant technologies in audit and assurance engagement.
Evaluate the nature, purpose and stages of auditing, and the professional, legal and regulatory requirements for auditors.
Evaluate the audit evidence and communicate audit opinion to relevant stakeholders.

Critically apply relevant auditing standards, regulations and laws to audit general-purpose financial statements, and assess the risks of material misstatement in the financial statements and develop strategies for audit.

title: MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING
syllabus_overview: Management accounting is integral to businesses strategic planning, resource allocation, operations, and performance management. This subject develops students’ knowledge of management accounting. Students will learn how to cost and price products and services, prepare budgets, and evaluate variances, manage customer and supplier costs and design performance management systems. The subject will also focus on developing students’ ability to solve business problems in complex contexts using social and environmental, ethical, economic, behavioural, regulatory, and global perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the performance of organisations, and their products, people and business segments.
Critically research and apply management accounting techniques and information for decision making and control in businesses.
Evaluate the budgeting processes and prepare budgets to support organisational planning, control and management.
Use various software to generate management accounting data and professional reports to support managements decision-making, performance management and control.

title: TAXATION
syllabus_overview: Australian taxation laws and regulations are vital to the Australian way of life given its significant impact on individuals and businesses taxable income and tax responsibilities. This subject develops students’ knowledge and application of relevant tax legislation and case law principles to determine the taxable income and tax liability of individuals and companies in Australia, and taxation implications to other taxable structures including trusts, partnerships, and their associated entities. Students will also learn about different Fringe Benefits Tax and the Goods and Services Tax. The unit will also focus on tax administration and technologies and anti-avoidance provisions for tax minimisation, avoidance, or evasion.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the sources of Australian taxation law and the framework in which taxation is administered.
Critically analyse the general, social and ethical issues associated with international transactions.
Investigate various types of taxation including income tax, taxes on capital, goods and services tax and fringe benefits tax.

Critically apply fundamental tax concepts, legislative provisions and judicial principles to calculate taxable income and tax payable of individuals, entities and businesses, and provide relative tax advice to concerned stakeholders

title: ADVOCACY IN CONTEMPORARY DISABILITY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Choice and control by people with a disability over their own lives, is central to the new model of funding for disability support services introduced by the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS). In parallel, political participation and the inclusion of people with disability in shaping social systems is central to the United National Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD). In this subject, students will explore the complexities that exercising choice and control poses for people with cognitive disability, and develop knowledge and skills in new approaches such as supported decision making. It will also explore the challenges and strategies for ensuring the collective voices of people with cognitive disabilities are heard about systemic issues. Finally this subject will support professionals to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to support people with disabilities and their families to navigate the NDIS and the uncertain interfaces between mainstream support and specialist disability support.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disability (UNCRPD and the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS and their impact on the lived experience of people with disabilities and their support network.
Interpret and transmit information about support for decision making frameworks for people with cognitive disabilities.
Demonstrate the ability to advocate for people with a disability and their families.
Critically analyse the different levels at which people with disabilities, with and without cognitive impairment, might exercise choice and control over their life.
Critically evaluate specialist disability and mainstream service systems available to people with a disability.

title: SCOPING REVIEWS IN DISABILITY RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop a detailed protocol for a scoping review of research literature to identify core issues and gaps in the literature that is related to a field of disability practice. Students will undertake background work to justify their scoping review, construct and refine a review question, design a comprehensive search for relevant research literature, design unbiased methods to select and evaluate the research literature, and select appropriate methods for the extraction and synthesis of data from the included studies. Students will work closely with their thesis supervisor while developing independent research skills, including the ability to access and critically evaluate relevant literature.
learning_outcomes: Design unbiased methods to select and evaluate the research literature.
Formulate a research question in a disability-related field of practice.
Critically evaluate the data obtained so as to address the research question.
Synthesise information and transmit knowledge in the form of a scoping review suitable for publication.
Select and apply appropriate methods for the extraction and synthesis of data.
Use appropriate databases to search for evidence.

title: AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY
syllabus_overview: This subject will investigate the past, present and future of agriculture, and its impact on Australia and the world. At the end of this subject, you will have a deeper understanding of the importance and context of agriculture from a range of different perspectives. You will examine the pre-and post-colonial agriculture in Australia and around the world. In understanding the past, you will cover the influence of agriculture on Australian history, landscapes and regional and rural development. What were the historical constraints, what are the current constraints, and what will they be in the future? To address the present, you will investigate the role of agriculture in addressing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, the role of agriculture in global food production and trade, and in the modern Australian economy. The future of agriculture will involve the increased use of precision – in data collection and analysis, forecasting, sensors and robotics. The increase in protected cropping will mean more diseases, but more control over inputs – how will this be achieved in a sustainable way to feed the world? What will the impact of this be on future workforce and society?
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of how global trade and regulatory issues influence farming practices
Describe the importance of the interplay between natural capital and farming systems
Work collaboratively with peers to present a solution to an agricultural problem
Demonstrate critical thinking in an understanding of agriculture
Define the constraints that limit food production locally, nationally and globally
Describe the drivers regulating the diversity of current and future agricultural systems
Describe the place of agriculture in Australia's past, present and future

title: SUPPORT PLANNING WITH PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES
syllabus_overview: Person Centred planning and practice has become a catch all phase referring to the development and implementation of effective individualised support plans for people with disability. This subject explores the different contexts and types of individualised plans that professionals may be required to utilise and the key skills and elements of the planning process. These will include effective communication, including verbal and non-verbal techniques, strategies for identifying needs and resources, and using multiple theoretical stances to provide insights into different perspectives on needs.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on how to work with a person with cognitive disability to develop a person centred support plan.
Differentiate the elements of an effective individualised support plan.
Communicate effectively and sensitively a support plan to a person with cognitive disability, their family and carers.
Work autonomously and as part of a team to develop an individualised support plan for a person with cognitive disability.
Critically evaluate various individualised support plans for people with cognitive disabilities.

title: RESEARCH THESIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will independently conduct a project which addresses a research question relevant to the field of disability practice. You will design, investigate, critically analyse and report your research findings by producing a thesis which outlines the contribution of the work to the field. This subject will prepare you for designing and conducting independent research, either in the workplace, or as part of a research degree.
learning_outcomes: Work autonomously to plan and deliver a substantial research-based project which makes a contribution to disability practice.
Propose a research design which is justified in relation to the research question posed.
Collect, analyse, synthesise and present data in a way that aligns with and responds to the research question.
Communicate research findings effectively and sensitively in both written and oral forms with colleagues, clients and the public.
Implement an appropriate method that addresses a research question relevant to the field of disability practice.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ANIMAL AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES
syllabus_overview: In the first part of this subject you will be introduced to key concepts in animal science, including animal breeding, biotechnology, nutrition, growth, reproduction, lactation and animal welfare, and major global issues such as food security and environmental impacts of animal agriculture through flip teaching (weeks 1 - 7). You will then follow a more applied module (weeks 8-12) in which you will analyse agricultural issues like sustainability, climate and environment, and sustainable cropping and grazing systems.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain basic concepts in animal and agricultural sciences and apply this knowledge to real-world problems in Australian or global agricultural/animal industries.
Effectively communicate scientific information in a written format to a variety of audiences.
Appraise issues associated with animal and/or agricultural production systems, including welfare issues, environmental issues, and food security.

title: BIOCHEMISTRY FOR AGRICULTURE AND ANIMAL SCIENCES
syllabus_overview: What do herbicides, tequila, biofuel, cow stomachs and hibernating bears have in common? Biochemistry! The rapidly changing climate, population growth and the increase in microbial diseases have led to a technological revolution focused at dealing with these food security and environmental challenges. This subject will explore the biochemical underpinnings of animal and plant production and health and will cover selected topics from the broad field of agriculture and animal science. This includes the photobiological basis for photosynthesis, plant nitrogen fixation, bioactive molecules acting as competitive inhibitors of metabolism, animal energy metabolism and regulation, and metabolic adaptations in animals and plants. This subject will be delivered via a combination of on-line modules and face-to-face workshop sessions. The weekly 3-hour workshops are compulsory and involve in-class assessment
learning_outcomes: Research, analyse and evaluate scientific information and communicate this in a clear and professional way in written form.

Explain how solar energy is converted to chemical energy which if then used for carbohydrate production in plants and research and explain how the process of photosynthesis is affected by environmental conditions.

Explain how nitrogen fixation and amino acid biosynthesis in plants function and research and discuss how carbon and nitrogen metabolism are affected by environmental condition and agricultural practice.
Investigate and explain how biochemical knowledge of animal and plant metabolism and recent biotechnological advances can help us face food security and environmental challenges.
Explain the metabolic pathways involved in energy production in animals as well as their regulation in order to achieve homeostasis.

title: ANIMAL NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: The essential dietary nutrients are chemically and functionally very diverse and in this subject we will provide an introduction and overview of the fundamental scientific principles through which animal nutrition is studied. We will demonstrate these principles through examples using production animals, companion animals and captive wild animals. The links between nutrition and biochemical and physiological functions will also be drawn in order to illustrate the interrelating aspects of nutrition with other life sciences.
learning_outcomes: Formulate diets for a range of animals in captivity including animals of agricultural importance, pets and captive wild animals.
Analyse experimental data and communicate the results to a variety of audience including professional bodies and the public.
Access and evaluate evidence from a range of sources including original research articles to support nutritional recommendations.

Evaluate the diets of these animals and prepare advice to farmers and other clients on how to correct for any deficiencies or excess of nutrients supplied from the diets; explain the scientific basis of such advice.

title: INTRODUCTION TO LAND AND SOIL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject, is designed an introduction to land and soil management, particularly in agriculture and the environment. Topics covered include, soil formation, soil classification, soil structure and soil nutrients are covered. The physical, chemical and biological processes in soils and landscapes are investigated. Important issues such as salinity, sodicity will also be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Understand the significance and relevance of soil properties for agriculture and the environment.
Understand a range of soil properties and their relationship to plant growth and performance.
Explain the development and variation of soil properties across the landscape, and their relevance to plant growth and land use.
Be capable of synthesising soil data to construct a land capability assessment.

title: WINE EVALUATION 1
syllabus_overview: The objective of this subject is to introduce you to the principles and practices of the sensory evaluation of wine. You do not need prior wine evaluation skills. During extensive practical wine tasting sessions, skills in wine assessment will be developed via palate training exercises that explore sight, smell, taste, flavour and mouth feel of the samples. A unique and comprehensive set of wines will be tasted across various quality categories. You will also develop an understanding of environmental conditions related to wine quality. Storage and serving conditions within a tasting context will be explored along with protocols for wine show stewarding and scoring.
learning_outcomes: Assess aspects of wine quality and make conclusions on wine longevity by sensory methods
Use appropriate methods and language to describe analytical sensory evaluation of wine varieties
Identify, describe and apply the principles of analytical sensory evaluation

title: ADVANCED ANIMAL NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on applying animal nutrition principles to optimise the productivity, health, performance, and welfare of domestic animals, with dairy nutrition as a major component. It also covers the nutritional needs of livestock, companion animals, equine and captive wild species. Topics include the relationship between diet and disease, explored through relevant case examples. The subject incorporates the use of diet formulation software and AI tools to analyse and design balanced rations. Engagement with industry professionals and development of skills in scientific writing are integral, with a focus on presenting nutrition information clearly and accurately to both technical and general audiences.
learning_outcomes: Research the role of nutrition in animal health and develop preventative strategies for diet related issues.
Use sources, including original research articles and feed formulation software, to develop accurate suggestions regarding animal nutrition.
Examine animal nutrition data and communicate effectively with diverse audiences to educate about animals' nutritional needs.

Understand the nutritional needs of livestock (dairy), companion, and captive wild animals, to formulate precise rations and implement feeding strategies to enhance animal welfare and performance while minimising environmental impact.

title: WORK INTEGRATED LEARNING PROGRAM
syllabus_overview: This placement program has been developed to allow students from Agriculture and Animal and Veterinary Biosciences to extend their formal academic learning beyond the classroom. It aims to provide students with an opportunity to link theory with practice in a second year vocational subject. The subject allows students to bring their learning from the university into a work environment and test out their knowledge in a real-world job. It brings together the expertise of industry partners and La Trobe University staff for the benefit of the student's professional development.
learning_outcomes: Apply problem solving skills when issues affecting organization are identified
Communicate effectively using innovative resources.
Speak and write effectively to a wide variety of stakeholders.
Identify roles within work teams and comprehend group dynamics in decision making, leadership and problem solving.
Identify innovative and sustainable best practice in the workplace.
Interact effectively in professional contexts with people from different backgrounds to show understanding of cultural and social diversity.

title: AGRONOMY 2
syllabus_overview: This subject will extend your knowledge of agronomy and apply understanding of plant structures and functions to the management of agricultural systems. Exercises will be the basis for exploring crop and pasture establishment and management options in both dry land and irrigated environments, through measurement of plant performance at the appropriate growth stages. You will also examine the interrelationships between technology, crop performance, production efficiency and sustainability, including genetic modification and precision agriculture. You will use crop simulation software to determine the impact-of and interactions-between climate, components of crop and pasture production and plant nutrition to crop yields. Conventional and alternative weed and pest management options, along with pesticide resistance, will be explored, with a focus on ecology and ethics.
learning_outcomes: Integrate aspects of crop/pasture production into sustainable management plans to improve yields and quality
Analyse crop models, growth data and apply results of experimental trials to develop a crop or pasture management plan and present in a format suitable for a professional audience
Discuss the ecological basis for weed, insect and disease impacts and their management including environmental and ethical issues
Evaluate and utilise different technologies including precision agriculture that are specific to Agronomic enterprises
Describe agronomic practices of crops and pastures in both dryland and irrigated environments

title: CASE STUDIES IN ANIMAL SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will participate in a series of animal science case studies where they will work in teams and act as advisers to clients/industry/research representatives on how best to manage their animal or agricultural business. You will access and evaluate relevant information from local and global case studies and research, and develop their recommendations for the client in the case study, for a series of problems areas.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse complex animal production issues affecting sustainability and profitability.
Synthesise information from multiple sources to address animal and plant problems in managed production systems
Write a consultant report, complete a quiz and prepare a self-recorded video presentation that recommends appropriate management strategies based on analysis of animal production problems and risks.
Work in teams to propose solutions drawing on relevant local and global case studies and research.

title: INTERNATIONAL WINE STYLES
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on the knowledge of wine tasting developed in Wine Evaluation I and the knowledge of Australian grape varieties and styles developed during the course. You will gain theoretical and technical knowledge of different wine styles. The practical aim of the subject is to provide you with hands-on experience in tasting international wine styles so that they can identify, by taste, several major regional wine styles and identify major wine- making practices. To this end the subject will include an overview of Old and New World wine-making regions, an analysis of production practices and an examination of major international wine styles. In addition, the subject will include some discussion of the relationship between culture and wine preferences.
learning_outcomes: Identify the major international wine regions and styles.
Compare production techniques, with respect to Appellation rules and wine style
Apply the process of qualitative wine evaluation in assessing wine quality within the context of the various international Appellation systems
Identify, compare and describe the sensory characteristics of a range of international wine styles

title: PLANT PESTS AND PATHOGENS
syllabus_overview: This is a 3rd year undergraduate subject that focuses primarily on agricultural plant health. Historical and ecological aspects of the increasing global problems with plant pests and diseases will be presented. The diversity, broad classification into taxa, life-history and ecology of the main organisms adversely affecting crop production (including: insects, mites, and nematodes, fungi, fungi-like organisms, bacteria, viruses) will be examined. The principles and practice of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in agriculture, based on deployment of resistant cultivars, cultural and biological control measures and judicious use of pesticides, will be demonstrated in online interviews and face-to-face interactions and recordings with IPM experts and hands on practical experiments and demonstrations in the lab. In the practical classes students will study arrange of insect pests and plant pathogens to understand the biology of different pests and diseases, how to look for signs of infection/infestation and how to control pests and pathogens.
learning_outcomes: Locate and synthesise information from appropriate online resources about plants, pests and disease.
Analyse pest and disease situations that are faced by commercial crop producers and recommend innovative and integrated approaches to their control
Explain and apply the theories of Integrated Pest Management.
Describe, explain and synthesise various aspects of the diversity and biology of the full range of pest and pathogen organisms that adversely affect crop plants.

title: LAND AND SOIL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject covers chemical, physical and biological aspects of soil and uses a field study of lime plots at the university farm to illustrate concepts. The importance of nutrient recycling and carbon dynamics in sustainable land use, and their impacts on the environment are studied. Management of land degradation including soil acidification, subsoil constraints and soil contamination is also an important component.
learning_outcomes: Generate and critically evaluate datasets and effectively communicate scientific results using tables and graphs.
Explain the development and variation of soil properties and processes and critically review their management in farming systems/sustainable land use.
Analyse soil properties as affected by long-term lime application and relate to strategies for management of soil acidity to improve plant growth and nodulation of legume plants.
Work effectively as a team member to communicate scientific results in oral and written formats.

title: APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECT 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete the second part of an applied research project initiated in the subject Applied Research Project 1. You will apply knowledge and skills to undertake a small research project including: the collection, analysis and interpretation of data, adherence to ethics considerations, and the development of recommendations and/or materials for industry. You will develop time management skills, ability to organize, liaise and work closely with external collaborators and will be . required to demonstrate the processes you used to manage the project. Projects are in either the “Experimental Stream” for laboratory or field research projects or in the “Industry Stream” which completes research to address an industry problem to develop recommendations and/or materials for the industry. You are provided with research supervision by teaching staff and/or appropriate industry professionals. This subject addresses La Trobe's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Essential. which entails developing the ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas, taking calculated risks and creating change to achieve ambitions - now and in the future.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate research collaboration to enhance project outcomes
Critically evaluate data from a research project to make evidence-based recommendations based on the results.
Manage an applied research project to produce research data.
Assemble and critique research results to present to experts in the field

title: WATER MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Water Management explores the role of water in the context of agribusiness decision-making. It draws on environmental and agribusiness industry expertise to explore key concepts underpinning water management in Australia, including fundamental hydrological, environmental and economic factors impacting sustainable management of water resources; the historic alignment of the development water resources and regional prosperity; and the current institutional and operational frameworks that influence water management decisions.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the issues arising for agribusiness managers in a resource constrained future.
Explain and apply legal, cultural, biological and ethical considerations that constrain water use and protect water resources.
Effectively communicate scientific information in written and verbal formats to a variety of audiences, individually or as part of a team.

Demonstrate knowledge of water resource management in Australia including an understanding of the basic principles of hydrology, environmental water requirements and competing consumptive use of water resources.

title: FIELD CROP AGRONOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will participate in a series of case studies focusing on key issues facing cropping regions in rural Victoria. You will act as advisers to grower clients on how best to manage their crop production business. You will develop skills in accessing relevant information and in a range of teamwork and communication activities, as you develop your recommendations for a series of problems areas, for the client in the case study. In the workshops you will learn practical agronomy and research skills.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse complex crop production problems/scenarios through consideration of the interacting biological, economic, and social factors that affect sustainable production and profitability in agricultural production systems.
Write consultant reports for clients which synthesise the analysis of the real life agricultural production problems or risks and recommend the most appropriate management strategies.
Access and synthesise information from multiple sources to address and understand real life problems in managed crop production systems.
Develop basic agronomic field assessment skills
Identify key crop, weed, disease, pest and beneficial invertebrate species.

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT A
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and have fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree with a major in a relevant discipline. The Bachelor of Science (Honours) program provides undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and/or theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program imparts undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Under supervision of a La Trobe University academic, you will formulate a research question, conduct a research study, and write a research thesis of 12,000 to 15,000 words in which you demonstrate the capacity to make an original contribution to your discipline. AGR401A is the first subject of a sequence of four subjects in which students undertake a research project in an agriculture and environment discipline and write a thesis. You must obtain approval from an academic supervisor prior to enrolment and must complete AGR401A first.
learning_outcomes: Design ethical approaches to investigate problems and test possible solutions relevant to an agriculture and environment discipline, with guidance.
Interpret and compare scientific information from multiple sources in an agriculture and environment discipline to support research and analysis.
Communicate scientific ideas orally and in writing using basic disciplinary conventions, with guidance.
Analyse discipline-specific literature to propose informed approaches to research questions, with guidance.
Demonstrate intellectual curiosity and apply guided judgement in scholarly activities under supervision.

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE B
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Honours in Agriculture consists of a one year (full-time) or two years (part-time) individual research project, supervised by a SABE scientist whose research is in the disciplines of crop science and/or plant science. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. AGR401B is the second or third subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take AGR401A first.
learning_outcomes: Develop knowledge in crop science and/or plant science when devising experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Analyse published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Develop practical experience and advanced knowledge in the fields of crop science and/or plant science.
Build oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Develop intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT C
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and have fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree with a major in a relevant discipline. The Bachelor of Science (Honours) program provides undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and/or theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program imparts undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Under supervision of a La Trobe University academic, you will formulate a research question, conduct a research study, and write a research thesis of 12,000 to 15,000 words in which you demonstrate the capacity to make an original contribution to your discipline. AGR401C is the third subject in a four-part sequence where students conduct a research project in an agriculture and environment discipline and write a thesis. While EEE401B and AGR401C may be completed in either order, AGR401A must be completed first, and EEE401D must be completed last.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and integrate scientific information from diverse sources to support reasoned arguments in an agriculture and environment discipline.
Apply advanced knowledge and technical skills in an agriculture and environment discipline to address research questions, with minimal guidance.
Demonstrate intellectual initiative and sound judgement in independently planning and executing scholarly activities with ethical and academic integrity.
Communicate scientific ideas clearly and effectively to scientific audiences, demonstrating sound use of disciplinary conventions.

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE D
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Honours in Agriculture consists of a one year (full-time) or two years (part-time) individual research project, supervised by a SABE scientist whose research is in the disciplines of crop science and/or plant science. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. AGR401D is the final subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take AGR401D last.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Apply knowledge in crop science and/or plant science research when devising experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Apply practical experience and advanced knowledge in the fields of crop science and/or plant science.
Utilise intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice.
Formulate an original research question based on the comprehensive review of published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.

title: APPLIED EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE IN ALLIED HEALTH
syllabus_overview: Evidence-based practice (EBP) is the use of best available evidence combined with patient preferences, available resources and therapist expertise in making decisions about the care of patients. Evidence-based health care requires the allied health professional to be able to perform the five steps of evidence-based practice. In this subject, you will produce a written Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) for publication in a web-based clinical resource. This resource will be peer reviewed, with you further applying your EBP skills in order to critically appraise the work of other students. In this manner you will further develop the necessary skills to perform EBP, while gaining a greater understanding of the peer review process and contributing to a valuable evidence-based resource. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Integrate findings from research to formulate answers to clinically focused research questions.
Critically appraise the methodology of study designs to determine the relative weight of evidence of effectiveness.
Critically reflect on and apply professional behaviours to productively participate in group situations.
Evaluate clinical knowledge and identify gaps to adapt for best available evidence.
Critically review the strengths and weaknesses in evidence-based practice steps to develop more efficient processes.

title: WORKING WITH DIVERSE CLIENT POPULATIONS
syllabus_overview: Allied health professionals work with diverse client populations. In this subject you will develop your knowledge and skills to undertake client assessment and provide client-centered health care that is safe and culturally appropriate for people from different cultures, age groups and abilities. You will explore diverse understandings of health and wellbeing including First Nations perspectives to provide a model of practice based on cultural safety. You will reflect on your own cultural identity and ways of communicating in order to reduce cultural and other bias, support power sharing, cultural safety and humility. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical principles in working with diverse client populations, including issues related to confidentiality, autonomy, and informed consent.
Describe the legal and regulatory frameworks that apply to the provision of health care services to diverse client populations.
Apply knowledge of diversity in client populations to evaluate inclusive and accessible practices to ensure health care services are equitable and responsive to the diverse needs of clients.

Apply skills in cultural responsiveness and cultural safety around issues of diversity, equity and justice to conceptualise, plan and act within culturally diverse contexts and with First Nations People.

title: ANATOMY 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, we will take you on a fascinating journey to discover how you were made. You will learn about the developmental processes that occurred to result in being human, which all started when a sperm fertilised an egg. We will learn how these processes influence your adult anatomy and how this anatomy is changed when development does not go exactly to plan.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to critically evaluate information and develop well-reasoned explanations of real world case studies.
Apply relevant anatomical principles to describe the structure and function of selected body systems.
Apply relevant anatomical principles to integrate structure and function of body systems within an anatomical region.

title: PARTICIPATE IN WORK HEALTH AND SAFETY PROCESSES
syllabus_overview: Students will learn the skills and knowledge required to recognise and report hazards in cultural heritage workplaces and to follow workplace safety procedures and directions.
learning_outcomes: Participate in arrangements for maintaining the health and safety of all people in the workplace.
Follow safe practices during work operations.
Follow workplace procedures for hazard identification and risk control.

title: ALLIED HEALTH MANAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop your capacity to make an effective contribution in an evolving health care environment. You will be introduced to the foundations of leadership and management theory and will gain an understanding of the political, economic, professional, ethical, social and cultural influences on clinical decision-making. You will explore your own professional career objectives and consider the varied organisational contexts within which you may work, including government, non-government organisations, and the private sector. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Justify the contribution of economic evaluation to informed decision making.
Communicate technical knowledge clearly and coherently to peers and specialist audiences.
Adapt principles of business leadership and management within allied health contexts.
Critically analyse the institutions, structures and processes that constitute the Australian health system
Articulate business and practice management principles in the context of allied health practice.

title: INTRODUCTION TO HUMAN ANATOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the fundamentals of human anatomy. You will develop a strong foundation in anatomical terminology, including concepts such as anatomical position, planes, directional terms, and movements. Through focused study of the major body systems—particularly the musculoskeletal and nervous systems—you will learn to apply anatomical knowledge to real-world scenarios and communicate effectively using precise anatomical language.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate how the nervous system integrates sensory and motor control, and the effects of its dysfunction/impairment.
Describe the anatomical structure and function of major body systems using the appropriate anatomical terminology.
Analyse the role of the musculoskeletal system in facilitating movement and assess the impacts following injury.

title: ANATOMY FOR PHYSIOTHERAPY A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to foundational concepts and terminology for the study of human anatomy and biomechanics. These concepts will then be applied in detail to the study of the lower limb, as relevant to physiotherapy. Teaching will include both online learning and face-to-face teaching sessions including practical classes involving cadaver materials and clinical anatomy. You will be required to work together in small groups, to take responsibility for your own learning and understanding of anatomy so that you are able to identify anatomical structure and function on a living body as you would in a clinical physiotherapy context.
learning_outcomes: Identify musculoskeletal structures within the lower limb through surface anatomy.
Apply relevant anatomical principles to describe normal structure and function of body systems within the lower limb, including its role in support, locomotion and posture.

Apply observational and communication skills, individually or as part of a team, using appropriate anatomical and lay terminology for use with clients or other health care professionals, to make accurate observations of anatomical structures or events and infer their relationship to function using cadaveric material, anatomical models, the living body or medical imaging.
Apply foundational biomechanical principles, including the concepts of force, motion and leverage, to analyse human movement within the lower limb.

title: APPLIED HUMAN ANATOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will build on previously learned anatomical principles and terminology, to cover the applied regional anatomy of the upper limb, lower limb and the trunk (including the vertebral column, as well as the thorax and its role in breathing), and neuroanatomy in relation to sensation and motor control.
