learning_outcomes: Synthesise and condense complex information into an accurate but visually appealing and easily understandable format to communicate scientific concepts and findings effectively.
Apply advanced oral communication skills to present scientific knowledge including experimental data to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.

Formulate an original research question based on a critical and comprehensive review of published scientific information and acquired research data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Apply advanced knowledge in specialist areas within the broad field of biotechnology.
Apply practical research skills, including independent and responsible planning, conduct, recording and reporting of laboratory-based experiments, to contribute to an overarching research project.

title: SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus on a variety of modes of scientific communication and research skills including data presentation, aspects of copyright and plagiarism, the use of scientific journals, scientific databases, abstracting journals and online resources. You will be expected to engage with and interpret recent scientific literature, write literature reviews, use online software for referencing support and deliver an oral presentation.
learning_outcomes: Design, present and evaluate a scientific poster.
Write a critical literature review using appropriate scientific language and academic referencing techniques in a format suitable for publication as a thesis or journal article.
Use databases to acquire and organise relevant scientific literature.
Interpret and present data from a scientific paper at a level appropriate to the audience.
Collaborate to retrieve, analyse and present scientific information.

title: TECHNIQUES IN BIOTECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will learn about a wide range of currently used techniques in biotechnology. They will be exposed to research scientists who are specialists in cutting-edge techniques relevant to current applications in the biotechnology industry and the research laboratory. The subject has a strong focus on providing students with the opportunity to understand, design, apply and analyse experiments based on state-of-the-art technology. BIO5TEC delivers theoretical concepts in concert with experimental design, application and analyses of a range of techniques used in modern biotechnology. The breadth of such techniques is vast and growing, so students will be exposed to techniques at the current forefront of experimental applications in a molecular biology setting. The subject is highly integrated, and the techniques are presented in a logical progression, from the identification of a gene of interest, the cellular location, functions, biophysical characteristics, structure of the protein it encodes and biotechnological engineering approaches.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and critically evaluate the validity of data from experiments applying of current techniques in biotechnology.
Explain advanced biotechnology techniques, which integrate fundamental biochemical concepts from a diverse range of fields.
Recognise and apply established knowledge and concepts relating to a range of current techniques in the fields of biotechnology.
Apply specialist knowledge of techniques to independently design experiments aimed at answering defined scientific questions.
Report data and its analysis in a meaningful and clear context using appropriate technical language.
Convey an expert understanding of scientific methods and their application through verbal communication.

title: BIOTECHNOLOGY ADVANCES IN PHARMACOLOGY AND MEDICINE
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to the major biotechnologies impacting pharmacology, biomedical science and medicine today. You will learn how the information in your genome can determine an individual and population response to important drugs for common diseases; how genomic information can be harnessed and edited to improve disease outcomes using a precision medicine approach; and how to interrogate the genome (bioinformatics). Advances in high throughput sequencing, drug screens, nanotechnology, synthetic biology, vaccines and regenerative medicine and their applications/limitations will be explored. The ethics of biotechnology use in humans will be discussed as well as the governance overlying genetically modified organisms.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the key methodologies underlying research platforms/techniques currently used in biomedical research and their applications, strengths and limitations (including genetic engineering, next generation sequencing/bioinformatics and immunotherapies).
Critically evaluate, select and apply appropriate contemporary biomedical technologies to address case studies.
Analyse the implications of ethical, social and cultural issues and evaluate their importance in the exercise of professional skills and responsibilities in biotechnologies.
Communicate scientific and technological knowledge across a wide range of cultural contexts, and effectively communicate within working groups.
Analyse how the variability in pharmacogenetics between populations can impact drug efficacy in a range of diseases.

title: INFECTIOUS DISEASE EPIDEMIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: Infectious disease epidemiology is a comprehensive and advanced subject that delves into the principles, methods and applications of epidemiology specifically focused on infectious diseases. Students will develop a deep understanding of the dynamics, transmission patterns, and control strategies related to infectious diseases. Via a combination of interactive lecture content and scenario-based workshop classes, students will undertake activities to explore the epidemiological principles and methods used in infectious disease transmission, surveillance and outbreak investigations of existing, emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in outbreak investigation including case identification, contact tracing, and source identification.
Interpret and evaluate infectious disease epidemiological digital surveillance data to identify outbreak sources and public health risks.
Analyse infectious diseases from a global health perspective addressing issues related to international travel, emerging infections and the impact of globalization on disease spread.
Explain the key concepts and definitions used to describe the frequency, distribution and transmissibility of infectious diseases.

Evaluate the effectiveness of various public health interventions such as vaccination programs, vector control, and quarantine measures and examine the ethical considerations associated with implementing these interventions.

title: INNER LIFE OF PLANTS
syllabus_overview: Inner Life of Plants explores the use of physiological and modern molecular techniques to study plant biology, with an emphasis on the analysis and explanation of the cellular processes that control the development, growth and productivity of plants. The ability of plants to acquire nutrients is investigated through hands-on practical experiments. The physiology component builds on concepts introduced in first year biology subjects, and is further developed in a series of hands-on practicals. The application of new molecular techniques is explored using real-life examples in the lectures, and a number of closely aligned practicals.
learning_outcomes: Explain mechanisms in plant nutrition, physiology and development.
Communicate scientific information in written and verbal formats to different audiences.
Apply the scientific method to conduct laboratory experiments that address specific questions in plant biology.

title: PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY THEORY
syllabus_overview: This subject covers the latest developments in biotechnology and molecular biology with a strong focus on plants, including specific applications, issues and limitations. Topics include the general principles and techniques commonly used to study and genetically modify plants including gene editing, approaches to investigate gene function by technologies such as RNA seq, single cell transcriptomics or large-scale genome-wide mutation experiments, and molecular breeding. Practicals and workshops give students experience with the techniques required for CRISPR gene editing in plants. Specific case-studies are used to illustrate how these technologies are being applied to current problems, including pest and pathogen resistance, and increasing pressure on food production.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and discuss the key technologies used to identify and understand gene function in plants (and animals and apply this knowledge to current real-world problems
Analyse and discuss general principles in biotechnology and molecular biology
Synthesise information from research publications and prepare a clearly written essay on a current relevant topic in (plant biotechnology for an expert audience.

title: MANAGE MEETINGS
syllabus_overview: Students will learn the skills and knowledge required to manage a range of meetings including overseeing meeting preparation processes, chairing meetings, organising minutes, and reporting meeting outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Prepare for meetings.
Follow up meetings.
Conduct meetings.

title: PLANT DIVERSITY AND ECOLOGY
syllabus_overview: Important aspects of biodiversity and its conservation in Australia are covered in this subject and represent an introduction to plant ecology and plant diversity. In the component on plant diversity, the origin and evolution of the Australian flora is discussed. Recognition and biology of major Australian plant families are covered in detail. In the component on plant ecology, the broad topic of the effects of environmental and biotic factors on the distribution of plant species is covered. Topics discussed include community assembly, patterns of diversity in space and time, and plant population processes. Skills are developed in plant collecting and the use of keys for identification of Australian flowering plants. A 4.5 day field trip to far western Victoria is an essential part of the subject.
learning_outcomes: Utilise scientific data to solve real-world plant ecological problems.
Describe and compare the characteristics, floral morphology and biology of major Australian plant families.
Critically evaluate and synthesise scientific information to explain research findings and discuss plant diversity and ecological issues.
Demonstrate understanding of botanical specimen collections through use and interpretation of online collections-based resources OR preparation of specimens to professional standards.
Apply standard plant ecology sampling methods to survey vegetation and effectively communicate patterns of vegetation in a written assignment.

title: SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING
syllabus_overview: You will be introduced to key dimensions of management and marketing in diverse organisational contexts. Informed by the need for sustainable value creation in contemporary organisations, you will be able to explore how external and internal environments influence management, sustainability and marketing behaviour and practice. You will engage with these issues by considering and analysing real world examples, informed by theoretical and analytical frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to assess marketing problems and solutions from a value exchange perspective to promote sustainable value creation in real-life business situations.
Conduct a business environmental analysis and communicate findings effectively in writing for a variety of stakeholders.
Integrate sustainable management and marketing ideas and apply the conventions of attribution and citation accurately.
Critically analyse key management concepts and trends for use in contemporary business decision making.

title: ACCOUNTING AND FINANCE FOR MANAGERS
syllabus_overview: Accounting and finance are critical skills for all professionals in the modern global environment. In this subject, you will be provided with an introduction to key concepts, theories and practical applications associated with accounting and finance in diverse organisational contexts. You will be exposed to content which will cover the nature of the accounting and financial environment and the types of accounting and financial practice and decision-making required from a business perspective.
learning_outcomes: Construct, interpret, analyse and communicate information contained in a firms financial statements using appropriate digital and information tools.
Examine and apply financial mathematics tools and techniques to determine cash flows, cost of capital, capital investments.
Prepare budgets, manage working capital, and make appropriate pricing and production decisions.
Examine the importance of basic accounting and finance principles, and differentiate the appropriate sources of finance for a firm.

title: NAVIGATING THE AI ECONOMY
syllabus_overview: Navigating the AI Economy develops advanced economic and analytical capability for organisational decision making in an AI-driven global economy. The subject applies key economic concepts and frameworks to business, organisational, and societal challenges shaped by artificial intelligence, data, and automation. You will use digital and AI-enabled tools to interpret economic data, analyse market behaviour, and evaluate financial and organisational performance. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking, problem solving, and the construction of sound economic arguments to support evidence-based strategic decisions in complex and uncertain environments.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and interpret economic data, market behaviour, and organisational decision making using appropriate economic and financial frameworks to support evidence-based inquiry and decision making.
Develop and communicate coherent economic arguments that apply AI-enabled analysis to contemporary business and policy challenges, drawing on relevant economic concepts, models, and evidence.

Evaluate the economic, social, and ethical implications of AI-driven decision making for organisations, markets, and society, applying economic reasoning to assess responsible and sustainable practices and outcomes.

title: ECONOMICS FOR GLOBAL LEADERS
syllabus_overview: Economics impacts on all aspects of business and society. Key individual, organisational and government decisions around the allocation of scarce resources are at the core of economics, and an understanding of economic concepts, frameworks and language can greatly enhance a leader’s capacity to make sound decisions and influence the decisions of those around them. This subject develops students’ knowledge of economic concepts and provides the opportunity to apply this knowledge to real world situations. Students will apply economic concepts and frameworks to current issues of concern for organisations and society. Students will learn how to evaluate and apply critical aspects of economics such as the main market forces of supply and demand; the choices producers make in relation to their costs; revenues and profit; competitive and monopoly market structures and how these affect market prices; the use of game theory to make more strategic economic decisions; measuring a nation's income and the cost of living; the drivers of economic growth and the causes of unemployment.
learning_outcomes: Apply economic frameworks to business and social problems for policy and decision-making.
Construct and present logical and persuasive economic arguments and communicate concepts professionally.
Research and apply economic concepts to predict how changes in economic conditions may impact individuals, businesses and industries within market structures.
Critically analyse economic data to explain relationships between economic variables and their impacts on policy, business and individuals.

title: PRINCIPLES OF FINANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the concepts, theories, and applications of finance. You will examine the role of the financial sector within the economy at large and the role of finance in the management of organisations. A particular focus will be on how investment and funding decisions are made within organisations, including an introduction to capital budgeting and project evaluation. This will lead to an introduction to a wide range of financial markets, including equity and debt markets. The mechanics of each market are examined, and the characteristics of the instruments traded in each market are explored. Consideration is then given to the concepts of risk and return and their application to portfolio theory and asset pricing models.
learning_outcomes: Formulate the risk and return of individual financial assets and portfolios and describe the Capital Asset Pricing Model and its implications when evaluating financial assets' expected return and risk.
Identify and review the fundamental concepts of capital structure theories and explain the critical factors which impact managerial decisions in developing capital structure and dividend policy
Identify the financial manager's critical financial decisions, discuss the financial system's primary role, and explain how interest rates are determined.
Compute bonds and share prices using the time value of money. Evaluate and explain the capital budget decision rules and apply these rules to a firm's investment decisions.

title: STATISTICS FOR BUSINESS AND FINANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop basic data-analysis skills to investigate real-life problems in business and finance. You will focus on basic concepts in statistics and probability theory, methods of statistical inference, measures of linear relationship between variables including linear regression analysis. There is a strong emphasis on the application of these techniques to practical problems in business and finance using Microsoft Excel. The contents of the subject are in line with the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) quantitative analysis curriculum. Successful completion of this subject will lay a solid foundation for the further study of data analysis in business and finance.
learning_outcomes: Ability to present work in a professional manner and to communicate effectively to a professional audience
Use statistical principles and research skills in a collaborative team environment to solve practical problems and communicate the findings to people with various viewpoints
Apply probability theory in business and financial decision making
Apply and interpret concepts of descriptive statistics to real life data and interpretation of results
Conduct estimating linear regression models and testing hypothesis to aid decision-making

title: APPLIED ECONOMICS
syllabus_overview: Organisations must navigate the economic landscape both domestically and internationally. Key organisational decisions around the allocation of scarce resources are at the core of economics, and an understanding of economic concepts, frameworks and language can greatly enhance a leader’s capacity to make sound decisions and to influence the decisions of those around them. In this subject you will draw on key economic concepts and apply them to business, organisational and societal challenges. You will use digital technology and hone your critical thinking and problem-solving skills to examine the links between theory and practice, and the principles that underpin markets, economic policy and business decision making. You will gain the skills to interpret economic data, to apply economic frameworks to contemporary challenges and to construct sound economic arguments.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse economic challenges and opportunities facing organisations and generate and communicate recommendations to improve organisational outcomes.
Using independent research predict and evaluate how changes in economic conditions and government policies may affect businesses and industries.
Construct and present logical and persuasive economic arguments and communicate concepts professionally using digital technologies.
Critique government policy options and evaluate the potential impact of alternative proposed solutions.

title: MASTERS BUSINESS RESEARCH THESIS 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students conduct independent applied research projects under faculty supervision. Emphasis is placed on applying theoretical frameworks and decision-making tools to real-world business issues. Students design research questions, collect, analyse, and interpret data ethically. They learn to communicate findings effectively through written reports and oral presentations, highlighting practical implications for businesses. The subject fosters critical reflection on research experiences, encouraging students to consider challenges, lessons learned, and future directions. Through this integrated approach, students develop advanced research skills, preparing them for roles requiring analytical rigor and innovative problem-solving in logistics and supply chain management.
learning_outcomes: Design research questions and collect, analyse and interpret data, and report your research findings in an ethical manner
Conduct an independent applied research project under supervision, based on the effective application of theoretical frameworks and decision making tools to solve real-world business problems.
Reflect on your research experience and possible practical implications of your findings in business domain

title: STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: Strategy develops your ability to design, assess, and implement value‑creating strategies for organisations operating in complex, technology‑infused and generative AI‑driven business environments. The subject integrates contemporary strategic management principles with insights from responsible AI leadership, preparing you to lead ethically and strategically as AI reshapes competitive landscapes. You will examine strategic tools and frameworks used by organisations ranging from startups to multinational enterprises and evaluate how strategic choices are influenced by global markets, technological disruption, and evolving regulatory expectations. The subject builds your capability to assess competitive position, evaluate strategic options, and support strategic decision making as AI and digital technologies transform industries. Emphasis is placed on aligning strategy with organisational goals, risk, and long‑term performance in dynamic and uncertain environments.
learning_outcomes: Design and justify value-creating strategies that align organisational goals, risk, and long-term performance, demonstrating ethical and socially responsible judgement.
Apply leadership and teamwork skills to develop, communicate, and support the implementation of strategy in diverse organisational contexts.
Critically analyse strategic positions and options in technology and AI-driven business environments to support informed and evidence-based decision making.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be provided with an overview of the new and emerging field of global corporate governance. Numerous corporate failures and environmental disasters in recent times have provided a surge of interest in ensuring companies reflect not only regulatory standards but also conduct their operations to reflect community and society norms. By the conclusion of this subject you should be able to add value to your organisations through your understanding of corporate governance in a global context and of the role of the board of directors and management. Working independently, and working together with others, you will learn about corporate governance through solving business problems and develop ethical, critical thinking and problem solving skills required to add value to organisations.
learning_outcomes: Examine the significance of corporate governance principles and practices including legal and professional regulation
Explain the importance of good corporate governance and its role in corporate success within the broader context of the world, society and community
Analyse organisational governance practices and recommend improvements
Critically review organisations' institutional environments and their impact on organisational practices
Apply ethical, critical thinking and problem solving skills in analysing corporate governance issues at the organisational level.

title: ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION
syllabus_overview: Entrepreneurial thinking and innovation develops an entrepreneurial mindset and advanced capability to identify, evaluate, and lead innovation initiatives in both business start‑ups and established organisations. The subject integrates creative problem‑solving with Artificial Intelligence (AI) initiatives to support new venture creation, business growth, digital transformation, and organisational change. You will explore how entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs recognise opportunities, develop and test business concepts, and apply innovation frameworks to the design of new products, services, processes, and ventures. Through practical analysis and applied activities, you will assess feasibility, risk, and scalability across start‑up and enterprise contexts.
learning_outcomes: Design viable business concepts and innovation initiatives by integrating creative problem solving with strategic, financial, and risk analysis to justify recommendations for implementation.

Justify strategic alignment decisions for innovation ventures by critically evaluating market opportunities and organisational context to support evidence-based entrepreneurial leadership and contemporary entrepreneurship issues.

Critically evaluate entrepreneurial opportunities in start-up and organisational contexts using contemporary entrepreneurship, innovation, and AI frameworks to produce evidence-based assessment of viability and strategic fit.

title: ACCOUNTING FOR MANAGERS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain a critical understanding of the role and functions of accounting information in business decision making. These include the use of information in external financial reports as a basis for evidence-based financial judgements and how managers use a range of internal financial and non-financial information to make strategic decisions. Independently and with others, you will work on various activities including case studies to become a judicious user of accounting information. You will also explore the role of accounting and associated reporting of broader ethical and social issues.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the basis and structure of conventional accounting reports, their constituent elements and the related user information needs.
Examine how managers use a range of financial and non-financial information to make evidence-based strategic decisions.
Analyse, interpret and critically evaluate the information in external financial reports to make financial judgements.
Consider the role of accounting and associated reporting of broader ethical, social and environmental issues and related accountability expectations.

title: PEOPLE AND CULTURE STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: In a highly competitive and rapidly changing business environment, effectively managing human capital is essential for an organisation's success, and is increasingly part of an organisation's strategy development and implementation. People and Culture (P&C) and Human Resource Management (HRM) is often a distinct unit within an organisation, but it is also increasingly integrated within the general management role. Thus, effective general managers must be able to retain talent, manage staff wellbeing and enhance employees' productivity. In this subject, you will explore contemporary HRM concepts for leading and implementing people and culture strategies that contribute to organisational sustainability, productive employment and decent work for all (UN SDG 8). You will be encouraged to critically examine how current people and culture practices can be applied in the general management context.
learning_outcomes: Formulate contemporary people and culture strategies to promote sustainable organisations, productive employment and decent work for all
Evaluate the strategic contribution that human resource management can make to organisational performance and sustainability
Critically analyse how local, national, and global trends affect HR management
Investigate and contextualise current trends impacting people and culture strategies, employee wellbeing and human resource management

title: FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop knowledge and skills in financial management. The subject will facilitate advanced understanding of financial management policy and application, and how financial management decision-making affects the risk, growth and profitability of firms and, combining these elements, firm valuation outcomes. You will consider financial management outcomes, and particularly the underlying goal of the maximisation of the valuation of the firm, through the key decision-making areas investment, financing and distribution decisions. In turn, this will incorporate the consideration of the requisite usage of debt and equity financing and the need for efficient management of working capital to ensure adequate liquidity and short-term resource and cash flow availability.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of financial management theory, concepts and models and associated application by analysing issues involved in valuation, financing and dividend policy decisions.
Demonstrate the ability to interpret and communicate financial information effectively.
Apply financial management concepts and principles to company risk assessment, cost of capital estimation, corporate valuation and corporate strategic planning and analysis
Apply quantitative and spreadsheeting models and techniques in completing investment decision-making tasks associated with assessing project risk, valuation and feasibility.

title: INTERNATIONAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: As the fourth industrial revolution connects people and industries throughout the world, managers and organisations must increasingly navigate issues related to globalisation, regionalisation and environmental analysis as well as assess political risk, culture and diversity, and global corporate responsibility. In this subject you will analyse and critique the interconnected issues of strategy, structure, culture, and people management in international business operations.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the role of ethics and corporate governance in international management.
Critically analyse how local, national and global trends affect management and strategy in multinational and transnational enterprises.
Apply relevant theories and research to align talent management with the strategic objectives and practical challenges of international management.
Apply relevant international management theories and research to practical management problems and challenges in multinational and transnational enterprises

title: RESPONSIBLE LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the evolving role of business in society through the lens of responsible leadership. Taking a multi-level perspective, you will critically analyse the intersection of social responsibility with a range of approaches to leadership, including stakeholder theory and shared leadership. Working individually and with other students you will evaluate contemporary organisational leaders and yourself against leadership frameworks; and you will critically reflect on how organisations, leaders, and managers can more effectively 'avoid harm' and 'do good'.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your own and other leaders' strengths, constrains on behaviour, and areas for improvement with respect to responsible leadership.
Research and apply leadership frameworks to increase responsible leadership at multiple levels of the organisation.
Critically analyse a range of perspectives on responsible leadership and evaluate their relevance in contemporary organisation settings.

title: DESIGN THINKING FOR MANAGERS
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a contemporary approach to strategy formulation and implementation. The emphasis is on design-thinking and creative ideation for solving problems and strategy execution in a rapidly changing global environment. Independently and with others, you will explore and apply concepts that offer a basis for solving complex strategic issues facing organisations. You will conceptualise and validate solutions to a problem using an evidence -based analysis.
learning_outcomes: Conceptualise and demonstrate a practical and actionable investment pitch and articulate a compelling rationale to proceed with the solutions.
Critically reflect and using teamwork skills apply creative thinking to solve complex problems facing organisations.
Use an evidence-based methodology to analyse, implement and validate solutions to a complex problem.

title: CRITICAL SKILLS FOR SUCCESS
syllabus_overview: With the new world of work comes new challenges for business leaders. This subject reflects on the evolving workplace landscape and examines the knowledge and skills you need to promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, productive employment and decent work for all (UN SDG 8). You investigate the impact of the changing world of work on your personal leadership style and how you lead others. You will also review contemporary approaches to strategy, strategic thinking and planning processes. Through industry guest presenters and workshop activities you interpret and analyse capabilities to meet organisations workplace challenges.
learning_outcomes: Examine changes in the industry environment and devise leadership skills to progress the UN SDG 8 target to promote sustainable economic growth, inclusive and productive employment and decent work for all.
Research and produce academic and business writing that demonstrates critical analysis and is presented in an appropriate style.
Examine and assess personal and professional knowledge, skills and capabilities required to lead contemporary organisations.

title: MARKETING FOR MANAGERS
syllabus_overview: You will be provided with a solid foundation of contemporary marketing concepts designed to assist you in making critical marketing decisions. Particular emphasis is placed on assessing marketing trends and the associated strategic and tactical frameworks that give rise to the formulation and implementation of marketing plans. You will draw on your experience as a manger to undertake a review of a marketing case study and deploy marketing tools to solve a real-world marketing problem.
learning_outcomes: Investigate and undertake a review of marketing problems and devise solutions from insights gained through data collection.
Critically analyse the role of marketing, assess marketing performance and apply contemporary concepts to different industry and organisational contexts.
Conduct evidence based research to inform the integration and application of marketing tactics to a practical situation.

title: MANAGING PEOPLE AND ORGANISATIONS
syllabus_overview: Examine the theory and practice of modern management in contemporary organisations. and critically evaluate current thinking on organisational design, strategy, and managing employees and operations to adapt to the current world of work. Through application of different philosophical perspectives to practical case studies, you will explore the opportunities and constraints in designing innovative, flexible, and adaptive organisations that promote sustainable economic growth and productive employment. You will assess and apply management theories and practices to optimise changes in organisational design and culture that fosters equality (UN SDG 5) and employee well-being (UN SDG 3).
learning_outcomes: Instigate and apply management theories and practices that foster flexible and adaptive organisations and operational systems.
Evaluate organisational change frameworks to address business sustainability, productive employment, inclusive practices and employee well-being.
Apply management theories to analyse specific organisational problems and develop practical and evidence-based approaches for resolving those problems.
Assess people and operational management theories, concepts, and practices to optimise sustainable organisations and productive employment.

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to develop your ability to critically assess the role of the UN Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary organisations. It also provides you with an opportunity to reflect on your role as a leader in terms of diversity and inclusion in the workplace. Through the use of frameworks, concepts and real-world scenarios you will aim to build your capacity to develop sustainable practices for organisations and to include global ethical concepts in organisational decision-making. Workplace inclusion is examined with particular regard to the most pressing challenges in the Australian and global contexts, and informed by theories of human rights, just distribution, respect and equity. A selection of other relevant topics (e.g., conflict within teams, the future of work) will be introduced, shaped by current research, current events, and your interest.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and apply to real-world business contexts through examination of practices.
Critically apply workplace inclusion frameworks through case analysis of organisational practices.
Explain and evaluate frameworks and techniques for managing businesses' role in economic, social and environmental sustainability.

title: DATA ANALYTICS CONCEPTS
syllabus_overview: Modern organisations depend on data‑driven insights to inform strategic decisions. In this subject, you’ll learn how to prepare, analyse and model data using two complementary toolsets. First, you’ll build competence in Excel: cleaning and shaping datasets, creating dashboards with PivotTables and charts, applying probability distributions and regression techniques, and developing simple forecasts. You’ll also explore emerging AI‑assisted features that automate data cleaning and trend detection. Second, you’ll develop proficiency with Structured Query Language (SQL), progressing from basic retrieval commands through joins, subqueries, common table expressions and window functions to extract and transform data from relational databases. By the end of the subject, you’ll be able to combine Excel and SQL to build data‑driven solutions, communicate findings effectively and approach business problems with a structured, analytical mindset.
learning_outcomes: Apply probability distributions and regression analysis to business data.
Import, clean and model data in Excel using automation tools.
Use Structured Query Language (SQL) proficiently to retrieve and manipulate data.
Create insightful data visualisations and dashboards using Excel ensuring ethical principles in the collection, analysis, and reporting of data.

title: BUSINESS ANALYSIS AND MODELLING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to basic statistics and quantitative techniques and their application to decision making and problem solving in business and commerce disciplines such as Accounting, Economics, Finance, Data Analytics, Management and Marketing. You will be exposed to working with business data and employing spreadsheet and modelling tools for analysis, visualisation, interpretation and decision-making purposes. The topics covered in this subject include numerical descriptive measures and graphical descriptive techniques; types of data and sampling techniques; probability and uncertainty measurement, variable and sample distribution identification and visualisation; hypothesis testing and linear regression analysis. You will be introduced to this content with a focus on the understanding and interpretation of statistical information and application to business, market and industry scenarios and problem solving.
learning_outcomes: Present business information using appropriate digital tools and platforms that facilitate informed decision-making
Engage professionally and effectively to contribute to the success of a diverse team, including use of a variety of modes of communication and appropriate digital tools
Quantify business risk / uncertainty using probability theory and statistical measurement and relate this to business, consumer or investment outcomes
Apply appropriate descriptive measures and visualisation techniques to summarise and interpret different types of business information

title: DISRUPTION IN BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: Traditional business models are being disrupted by numerous factors. Chief among them are new technologies that change how businesses operate. One commonality observed among these disruptive trends is the role of data. Data has become a highly valued business asset, forming a strong foundation to high quality decision processes. This subject will introduce you to the role of data in disrupting traditional business operations and formulating business strategy. You will gain an appreciation of how data can be turned into business insights through a process called analytics, using examples across a range of business problems. On completion of this subject, you will appreciate the pivotal role that data and analytics play in various strategic initiatives within organisations, and the strategies that link analytics to business performance while balancing issues such as ethical and data governance.
learning_outcomes: Discuss how business performance management can be linked to any data strategy and data analytics initiatives.
Understand the value of analytics from various case examples across key business functions and industries.
Recognise the importance of data ethics and governance to business success and longevity.
Explain the role of data and analytics in disrupting traditional business models.

title: MARKETS, POLICY AND THE ECONOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will undertake research into current economic issues and apply economic concepts and frameworks to critically analyse problems and suggest appropriate public policy responses to them. You will learn how the forces of demand and supply coordinate the behaviour of individuals and businesses in the market and how government policy settings affect those market outcomes. You will study the decisions that businesses make in determining how much to produce and at what cost, and analyse how the market structure and public policy settings affects firms’ choices. From an economy-wide perspective, you will investigate how to measure economic activity, inflation and unemployment, and you will examine the factors that influence these variables and the impacts on individuals, businesses and governments.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the relationships between macroeconomic variables and their impacts on businesses, individuals, and society.
Use models to predict and analyse the impacts of changing market conditions and/or public policy responses and their impacts on society
Research and analyse current issues and/or events in the economy by integrating data and other information sources
Explain fundamental economic concepts with written communication incorporating diagrams, equations, and other media

title: DATA FUNDAMENTALS FOR BUSINESS DECISIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject equips you with the skills to transform raw data into actionable insights that drive informed business decisions. You will learn key Excel functionalities crucial for data manipulation, analysis, and visualisation. The statistical component covers key concepts such as descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation), probability distributions, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis. Emphasis is placed on interpreting statistical outputs and applying findings to real-world business scenarios. You will gain skills in designing dashboards that summarise complex data sets for managerial review and strategic planning. Overall, you will be equipped with the foundational knowledge and skills to harness data as a strategic asset in driving business success.
learning_outcomes: Apply Excel proficiency using fundamental statistical methods to evaluate business problems
Use appropriate software and statistical techniques to present business data to inform decision-marking
Apply statistical analysis and hypothesis testing techniques to economic, financial and business data to draw conclusions

title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping the foundations of business and commerce. In this subject, you will explore the technical capabilities and practical applications of Generative AI and other forms of AI within business and industry contexts. You will develop a critical understanding of the ethical, regulatory, and societal implications of AI, including the risks associated with its use. Through workshops, case studies, and hands-on activities, you will build and evaluate Generative AI solutions to address business challenges, with a strong focus on ethical, responsible, and informed practice.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and discuss key risks, ethical considerations, regulatory issues, and principles of responsible AI use in business.
Identify and explain the technical capabilities of Generative AI in business and industry applications.
Describe the role and contribution of Generative AI in contemporary business contexts.
Use basic Generative AI tools to develop and assess solutions to common business problems.

title: ANALYSE AND IDEATE
syllabus_overview: Innovative thinking is one of the key attributes global businesses look for in employees. In this subject you will be challenged to identify and analyse problems from multiple disciplinary perspectives and synthesise these findings in ways that suggest new ideas. You will develop a set of creative thinking skills to employ in the process of idea generation and refinement. You will learn how to conduct research to explore a challenge and the potential of ideas to address it. In the process, you will develop communication and interpersonal skills through working in multidisciplinary, multicultural teams. This is the first of a three-subject entrepreneurial core of the Bachelor of Commerce, along with Evaluate and Negotiate and Execute and Manage Change. On completion of these subjects, as a Bachelor of Commerce graduate you will be able to analyse a problem, creatively think outside the box to define a solution, negotiate the terms of that solution with a diverse range of stakeholders, and manage the implementation of that solution in an existing business or one you will create for yourself.
learning_outcomes: Apply structured processes and techniques to formulate innovative solutions.
Develop ability to communicate effectively within a multidisciplinary context.
dentify real-world challenges confronting business and society and/or opportunities for value creation.
Analyse real-world challenges and/or opportunities using relevant approaches and tools.

title: SUSTAINABILITY
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the concept of sustainability, and a systems approach to understanding the complex interactions between the environmental, economic and social dimensions of sustainability. The subject attracts students from a range of fields, bringing a multidisciplinary team perspective to the researching, analysis and problem-solving aspects of creating positive change for sustainability. In teams, you are required to critically evaluate the stakeholder management and sustainability efforts of large business corporations across the world. This subject provides you with the opportunity to enhance, demonstrate and document work-ready skills appropriate to your chosen career path.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate innovative, systems-based solutions through the application of disciplinary knowledge and skills to researching, analysing and resolving sustainability challenges.
Apply the theory and frameworks developed in the subject to analyse and appraise a range of stakeholder and sustainability-related issues.
Identify the interplay between the social, environmental and economic pillars of sustainability, and the implications for ethically complex decision-making.
Demonstrate an ability to engage effectively in diverse teams to complete complex team tasks or structured projects in culturally diverse educational settings.

title: DATA ENGINEERING & PYTHON
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces the essential principles and practical techniques of modern data engineering. You will learn to design and construct reliable data pipelines by navigating the full data engineering lifecycle, from generation to serving. With a hands-on approach using Python and SQL, the subject covers data sourcing, cleaning, transformation, and storage. A significant focus is dedicated to the ethical and security responsibilities of a data professional. Finally, the subject explores the downstream applications of data engineering through the lens of exploratory data analysis and data visualisation, enabling you to derive and communicate insights for various business problems responsibly.
learning_outcomes: Apply core principles of data security, privacy, and ethics in a data pipeline context.
Design and build reliable data pipelines using Python and SQL to source, transform, and store data.
Analyse and visualise the engineered data to derive initial insights, uncover patterns, and communicate findings effectively.

title: CUSTOMER ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In today’s data-driven business environment, customer analytics plays a vital role in shaping effective marketing strategies and improving organisational decision-making. This subject will introduce you to the principles and practices of customer analytics, focusing on how data can be used to understand customer behaviour, segment markets, and inform targeting strategies. You will engage with key marketing metrics and models to analyse real-world problems such as market share, customer churn, and retention. Case studies and applied activities provide opportunities to develop practical skills in using customer analytics tools, while also emphasising ethical and secure approaches to handling customer data. By the end of the subject, you will be able to apply customer analytics techniques to support strategic business decisions and customer-centric innovation.
learning_outcomes: Identify business objectives and design appropriate analytical approaches that address customer challenges, demonstrating awareness of data ethics and cybersecurity considerations.
Interpret and visualise customer data and model outcomes to generate evidence-based managerial strategies and recommendations.
Evaluate and apply marketing metrics and models to analyse customer-related business problems, including market share, and customer churn and targeting.

title: ECONOMICS FOR A CHANGING WORLD
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will take an inquiry based approach to motivate a rich and deep appreciation of how economic principles and frameworks can be used to analyse our world and to inform policymakers. You will cover a range of trends that are shaping modern society such as: scarcity and choices; the capitalist revolution; technological change; population growth and economic growth; economics and the environment; the firm and its customers; and a study of markets and their complexities. You will gain an understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of various approaches to economic problems, and an appreciation of the relationship of economics to other disciplines.
learning_outcomes: Utilise and critique a range of economic tools and approaches to draw conclusions and make recommendations.
Apply economic concepts and principles to analyse economic problems in the real world.
Reflect on the differences between institutions across economies and analyse the impact of economic policy.
Analyse the impact of economic growth and innovation over time on the welfare of contemporary society.
Interpret evidence as part of an exploratory process and critically reflect on its application.

title: PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: Predictive Analytics is the use of statistical algorithms and machine learning techniques to analyse historical data for future event prediction, providing organisations with data-driven decision-making. This subject equips you with the skills to design and implement predictive models using well-known algorithms to solve regression and classification problems. You will also learn to interpret results, understand variable significance, and communicate findings effectively. When emphasising evaluation metrics and overfitting prevention, you will develop the skills needed to ensure the robustness and reliability of your models. In addition to technical proficiency, you will explore ethical and security considerations in the development and deployment of predictive models, including responsible data use, fairness, transparency, and safeguarding sensitive information.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical, secure, and responsible practices in the use of predictive analytics to address real-world business challenges.
Interpret model outputs to understand variable significance and communicate predictive insights clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Design and implement reliable predictive models using a range of machine learning algorithms to solve regression and classification problems.
Apply appropriate evaluation metrics and experimental design to assess the performance and robustness of predictive models.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND BUSINESS AUTOMATION
syllabus_overview: The rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the last decade has changed the way businesses operate. Innovative AI solutions are increasingly adopted to help businesses understand customer behaviours from massive data, accurately predict future demands, and improve operation efficiency via automation. AI is also the enabler of game-changing products and business models such as self-driving cars, chat-bots, AI-driven healthcare, FinTech, smart energy, and intelligence supply chains. In this subject you will learn about the competitive opportunities from emerging AI technologies and automated decision-making. You will be given the opportunity to gain hands-on experience during workshops on widely used AI platforms and learn how to build AI solutions for real-world problems, such as building energy forecasting, customer complaint analyses, dynamic pickup and delivery optimisation, and automated product recommendation. A number of related AI and modern optimisation techniques such as statistical learning, deep learning, and swarm intelligence will be introduced. Challenges of executing AI projects and criteria to evaluate AI solutions will also be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Explain the importance of AI and automation to rapidly changing business environments and evaluate key components of AI and automation solutions under different criteria
Design and critique the challenges of AI projects and evaluate using AI ethics.
Develop and analyse AI solutions in a number of business problems using suitable AI platforms

title: SUSTAINABILITY
syllabus_overview: This subject develops your understanding of sustainability through a systems-thinking approach, enabling you to explore and critically analyse the dynamic and interdependent relationships between environmental, economic, and social dimensions. You will engage with sustainability from a global, multidisciplinary perspective, collaborating in diverse teams to investigate and address real-world sustainability challenges faced by organisations. The subject fosters critical reflection and problem-solving, requiring you to evaluate stakeholder engagement strategies and sustainability practices using relevant theories, frameworks, and evidence. Through applied learning and teamwork, you will further develop and demonstrate work-ready skills essential for ethical and sustainable professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate stakeholder roles, interests, and engagement strategies in organisational sustainability governance and performance.
Collaborate effectively in diverse teams, showing leadership, initiative, and intercultural skills in sustainability projects.
Reflect on how the social, environmental, and economic dimensions of sustainability intersect and influence ethical and responsible decision-making in diverse global business contexts.
Apply systems-thinking to analyse sustainability problems, revealing interconnections and informing evidence-based responses.

title: AGRIBUSINESS AND ITS PLACE IN THE ECONOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the how agriculture and, in recent history, agribusiness have played a critical role in human development. This subject will deepen your understanding of agribusiness in the broader economy and it is aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal number 12 Responsible Consumption and Production. In particular, you will investigate the place of agriculture in the Australian context, and how the establishment of agribusinesses has played a role in the post-colonial Australian economy. Through guided case studies you will consider how the development of agricultural trade has influenced global economic development and explore the key international agreements and partnerships that sustain and contain global agribusiness.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the evolution of agribusiness in the Australian context.
Critically reflect on the future challenges and opportunities for agribusiness in the economy.
Critically reflect on the evolution of agribusiness in Australia and the role of globalisation.

title: ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about entrepreneurship and innovation typology in terms of their relevance in the business environment. You will apply an entrepreneurial mindset to understand current business problems in order to coordinate the activities of different stakeholders and ecosystems. You will study the role of innovation in society and how it affects start-ups and business competitiveness. This will include thinking about innovation and technology processes and how this affects growth and value creation. You will also explore contemporary issues in entrepreneurship and innovation.
learning_outcomes: Apply entrepreneurial approaches and validation tools to create value in achieving economic and social outcomes
Analyse the role and importance of entrepreneurship and innovation in dynamic entrepreneurial ecosystems and global competitiveness
Analyse the characteristics and mindset of entrepreneurs and/or new venture development processes
Evaluate contemporary issues in entrepreneurship

title: SOCIAL MEDIA AND VISUALISATION
syllabus_overview: Unlike many traditional business models which are product-centric or focused, the modern businesses of today are very much customer-oriented. A consequence of being customer-oriented is the need for businesses to engage positively, proactively and effectively on social media and be good at creating a strong narrative for the products or services that the business offers. In this subject, you will learn about the role that social media plays, taking a data analytics view of social media and its role to building brand equity. You will also investigate various storytelling techniques and tools, including effective creation of slide decks, and use of infographics and dashboards to engage consumers. Lastly, you will be introduced to the new developments poised to disrupt businesses, gaining an appreciation and understanding of how to manage these disruptors within the organisational structure as well as in the customer-facing aspects of the business.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of social media in a customer-focused environment of modern businesses.
Analyse and communicate the implication of new technological developments that can become agents of disruption to businesses.
Demonstrate how social media, using visualisation and data story telling, can be used to engage the customer effectively.
Design effective social media campaigns and apply appropriate data story telling through visualisation for a given business problem.

title: CONTEMPORARY APPROACHES TO MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In today’s complex, digital-first world, future business leaders must go beyond traditional operational management. They are expected to navigate constant change, embrace ambiguity, and lead under pressure and with purpose. This subject provides a foundational introduction to the mindsets, skills, and tools required to manage and lead responsibly in dynamic, diverse, and fast-evolving organisational environments. You will explore contemporary approaches to management by engaging with real-world scenarios in innovation, behavioural science and negotiation. Through hands-on experiences, simulations, and collaborative projects, you will develop practical capabilities in decision-making, ethical leadership, team dynamics, and strategic influence. Emphasis is placed on experiential learning, self-reflection, and problem-solving to equip students with transferable skills relevant across industries. This subject lays the groundwork for you to become adaptive, ethical, and forward-thinking.
learning_outcomes: Apply foundational management concepts to contemporary organisational challenges
Demonstrate negotiation and influence skills in practical simulations
Design and collaborate in agile teams to generate innovative ideas
Identify and mitigate decision-making biases using behavioural insights while reflecting on personal development as an emerging manager

title: EVALUATE AND NEGOTIATE
syllabus_overview: Professionals need strong analytic skills to evaluate a range of potential solutions to problems. They also need the ability to negotiate support, resources and the terms on which the solution will be acceptable to a range of diverse stakeholders. This requires understanding the causes of behaviour as a result of individual differences. You will explore the values, beliefs and personal attributes which define you as an individual, as well as those that define others in your team, and the stakeholders with whom you must negotiate solutions to the problems you are seeking to solve. In this subject you will gain valuable insights into how to be a more effective communicator and negotiator, within a diverse multidisciplinary, multicultural context. Evaluate and Negotiate is the second of a three-subject entrepreneurial core in the Bachelor of Commerce. On completion of Analyse and Ideate, you will have learnt how to analyse a problem, creatively think outside the box to define a solution. On completion of Evaluate and Negotiate you will have learnt how to negotiate the terms of that solution with a diverse range of stakeholders. Subsequently, on completion of Execute and Management Change you will have learnt how to manage the implementation of that solution in an existing business or one that you will create for yourself.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a negotiation situation and develop a strategic negotiation plan.
Evaluate competing solutions to real-world business and social challenges.
Identify the stakeholders in a real-world context and what they attempt to achieve.
Effectively negotiate solutions to real-world challenges with the stakeholders and reflect on the negotiation process.

title: ANALYTICS PROJECT
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject will allow you to apply your acquired analytics knowledge and skills in a real-world industry problem through the development of an analytics project in a team-setting. You will be involved in professional skills development to prepare you for work-readiness by working in a team-oriented project-based learning environment. You will learn important skills, including a demonstrated understanding of ethics in AI and analytics, data and ICT governance, security and privacy considerations, etc., to prepare you for working in the analytics and analytics-related industries.
learning_outcomes: Develop and apply appropriate analytics techniques, considering data ethics and cybersecurity measures using contemporary technology platforms to solve real-world problems
Demonstrate ethical and professional behaviour in teamwork, stakeholder engagement, and the use of data, algorithms, and insights.
Create, interpret and communicate analytics proposals, findings, and recommendations clearly and professionally to diverse stakeholders

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: The rapid advancement of digital technologies is reshaping international business strategy, decision-making, and operations. This subject examines how technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and predictive analytics drive automation and insight generation, while blockchain, smart contracts, and fintech solutions enhance efficiency and trust in international transactions. You will also explore how cloud computing supports business scalability and global collaboration, and how big data analytics supports market entry, competitive positioning, and consumer engagement. The subject further investigates the role of extended reality (XR) technologies, including augmented and virtual reality, in transforming marketing, remote teamwork, and cross-cultural communication. Emphasis is also placed on the critical importance of cybersecurity in protecting digital infrastructure across borders. Through real-world case studies and practical applications, you will critically evaluate the risks and opportunities presented by emerging technologies in the context of global business.
learning_outcomes: Propose innovative and competitive strategies for international business based on an assessment of the impact of digital technologies on decision-making.
Critically evaluate the role of digital technologies in international business to develop strategic responses to global market opportunities and challenges.
Apply theoretical and conceptual frameworks to analyse how digital technologies are adopted in international business contexts.
Work collaboratively in a team to investigate and present insights on how digital technologies are reshaping contemporary issues in international business.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND BUSINESS AUTOMATION
syllabus_overview: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the way organisations operate, compete, and innovate. This subject explores how AI technologies and automation are reshaping modern business practices, driving operational efficiency, and enabling data-driven decision-making. You will learn how AI empowers businesses to analyse data, understand customer behaviour, forecast future trends, and automate processes across diverse functions such as marketing, finance, and customer service. The subject introduces key AI concepts and practical tools through a blend of theoretical learning and hands-on activities. You will gain experience using AI and automation platforms to address real-world business problems, including demand forecasting, customer sentiment analysis, and chatbot development for business automation purposes. Core AI and optimisation techniques such as Machine Learning(ML), Deep Learning, Swarm Intelligence, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) will be explored alongside emerging technologies like Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI. Ethical and responsible AI practices form a critical component of the subject, encouraging students to critically assess issues of fairness, transparency, and accountability in AI-driven decision-making. By the end of the subject, you will be equipped with both the technical and critical thinking skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate AI solutions for business innovation and automation.
learning_outcomes: Design AI projects, identify and critique the challenges they present, and evaluate these projects using principles of AI ethics.
Develop and analyse AI solutions in a number of business problems using suitable AI platforms
Explain the role of AI and automation in dynamic business environments and evaluate their core components against organisational and technical criteria.

title: BUSINESS WORK PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides practical experience to prepare you for a successful business career. The work placement offers a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between theory and practice by immersing yourself in a business environment. You will have the chance to apply your knowledge to real-world scenarios and contribute to organisational projects. Working alongside experienced professionals and undertaking specific business tasks you will gain valuable insights into local, national or multinational workplaces. A work placement develops your analytical and problem-solving skills, enhances your communication and teamwork abilities, and cultivates the confidence necessary to thrive in a competitive business landscape. Dedicated academic staff provide supervision to ensure you continue to develop your employability skills and enrich your work placement experience. By participating in our work placement subject, you not only gain a competitive edge in the job market but also build a strong foundation for your future career.
learning_outcomes: Apply relevant theoretical perspectives to practical work tasks.
Reflect on personal experience, acknowledge strengths as a responsible employee, and develop strategies to improve your career prospects.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge about your host organisation and articulate how you will apply your degree knowledge to tasks and projects
Use critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and technology to address business issues.

title: RESPONSIBLE AI FOR SUSTAINABILITY
syllabus_overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming businesses and industries, often with a focus on performance outcomes such as increased revenue, cost reduction, and competitive advantage. This subject critically examines the risks, biases, and harms associated with one-sided, performance-driven AI strategies. You will explore approaches that promote the responsible, ethical, and sustainable use of AI in organisational contexts. The subject draws on the EU AI Act and related regulatory frameworks as foundations for understanding responsible AI governance. These concepts are applied and tested through classroom-based experimentation and evaluation of AI applications. In alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME), the subject further examines how AI can support sustainability and equity in business and society.
learning_outcomes: Design and develop simulations of responsible AI systems for business applications
Analyse key regulatory frameworks, ethics and security for the responsible and ethical adoption of AI
Interpret and explain the risks, biases, and potential harms associated with AI in organisational and societal contexts
Critically evaluate the role of AI in advancing sustainability and equity, with reference to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

title: GLOBAL BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
syllabus_overview: The Global Business Experience subject offers a unique opportunity for students to gain an international work integrated learning experience. You will collaborate in small teams to tackle real-world business challenges in a foreign country gaining first-hand experience of the complexities operating in a foreign institutional and cultural environment. The learning experience will also include visits to foreign-host businesses and cultural sites relevant to the business context of the specific study abroad tour, engaging with local authorities, businesspeople as well as staff and peers from La Trobe’s partner institutions in the host country. Students will apply their theoretical knowledge and business tool skills gained thus far in their studies. The subject aims to help students develop a global mindset and gain transferable employability skills.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess and apply the theoretical frameworks and business tools necessary to tackle real-world business problems in a foreign country
Critically evaluate one’s own global business experiential learning
Enhance cultural (self)awareness, assess foreign institutional and industry settings, and work effectively within a team

title: DIGITAL BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: In this online subject you will develop and enhance your online research and communication skills. In so doing you will explore the business models of digital disruptors such as eBay, Apple, Google, Facebook and Amazon, who are using digital business models to disrupt established businesses in telecommunications, transportation, advertising, e-commerce, automotive, insurance, education and many other industries. You will also explore how established businesses are responding with new business models of their own to meet challenges posed by the expanding digital economy. Through this subject you will develop the skills required to design innovative solutions using digital technologies, to enhance the ability of businesses and community organisations to achieve strategic goals.
learning_outcomes: Assess and design your personal online brand
Identify and analyse emerging digital business trends and strategies
Evaluate different types of business problems given the impact of digital change.

title: ENTREPRENEURSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject offers you the opportunity to use disciplinary knowledge and skills to start a business or resolve a business challenge. The subject attracts students from a range of fields, bringing a multidisciplinary perspective to the researching, analysis and problem-solving aspects of the challenge. You will be required to design entrepreneurship validation tools aimed at creating sustainable value through the provision of a particular product or service to meet an identified market opportunity. The projects aim to enhance the well-being of your community or aim to solve a social, health, economic or environmental problem. The subject is designed to provide you with the opportunity to enhance, demonstrate and document work-ready skills appropriate to your chosen career path.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate an entrepreneurial idea or solution in a professional manner to diverse audiences.
Critically analyse a business venture or opportunity by examining the offerings, processes and practices to achieve social and financial outcomes.
Analyse the start-up formation process, examine the entrepreneurial qualities, and impact of the context and emerging trends.
Develop and apply entrepreneurship validation tools to justify the merit and values of an entrepreneurial idea or innovative solution to customer or business problems.

title: DIRECTED READINGS
syllabus_overview: An individual reading project. This subject will be available as necessary and at the discretion of the Head of Department and/or School.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically analyse relevant academic literature in business as it applies to a specific business problem.
Describe, apply and critically evaluate relevant business theory and principles as they apply to specific business problems.
Recognise and articulate business issues

title: LEADING DISRUPTION
syllabus_overview: Disruption is now a defining feature of modern business environments, requiring leaders who can drive change with agility, foresight, and responsibility. In this subject, you will apply your technical and business knowledge to design and lead effective change initiatives. You will learn how to create a persuasive business case for change, supported by data and analytics, and develop the leadership, negotiation, and influencing skills needed to guide people through disruption. Emphasis is placed on managing technological change through data-driven approaches, including how to stage, implement, and sustain initiatives to deliver long-term organisational value. You will also critically examine how responsible and secure data practices, including fairness, transparency, and the protection of sensitive information, shape the ethical execution of change. By the end of this subject, you will be equipped to evaluate complex disruption scenarios and lead innovative, ethical, and sustainable organisational transformations.
learning_outcomes: Apply leadership, teamwork, and influencing skills to manage change initiatives in disrupted business contexts.
Design data-driven change management plans that ensure successful transition, adoption, and long-term impact.
Critically evaluate and justify change strategies, effectively communicating recommendations and addressing stakeholder concerns.
Develop a business case for change that considers ethical and secure use of data, and technology.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN ANALYTICS AND DIGITALISATION
syllabus_overview: Technology-enabled supply chains are becoming increasingly effective, efficient, and transparent. In the future scenario of smart supply chains, a supply chain in the real world will be simulated by its digital twin deployed in a cloud computing platform. Real-time data in factories, warehouses, and transport vehicles will be collected and processed by Internet of Things (IOT) devices, and then sent to the supply chain’s digital twin. The data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) models behind the digital twin will analyse the data, simulate the supply chain processes in the real word, and help us to make informed decisions for supply chain management, such as inventory control and redeployment for supply chain disruptions, dynamic management of suppliers, and fast responses to customers’ complaints. In this subject you will learn how to model and design smart supply chains to enable data driven decision making, optimisation of operations, and adaptation to changing market conditions. Using authentic case studies and practical digital tools, you will develop the critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to identify problems in the smart supply chains and develop practical solutions to address these problems.
learning_outcomes: Assess the potential effectiveness, efficiency, and transparency of a smart supply chain design.
Model and explain a data driven smart supply chain based on best practice technology and data integration.
Critique an existing supply chain design with the intention of improving technology contributions.

title: ACCOUNTING AND FINANCE FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the fundamental components of accounting and finance and their role in business. You will learn to record and report business transactions, assess financial health, and manage business assets.
