You will also learn the ethical requirements underpinning financial statements, how to compile and interpret financial statements and critically assess different sources of financing. You will develop your critical thinking and ability to make strategic planning and pricing decisions.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret financial statements and prepare a budget for managing business finances
Critically assess the relationship between risk and return and how these impact on using different sources of capital to fund business operations
Communicate to stakeholders the business investment options and rules as they relate to the funding and investment decisions of the business.
Explain the importance of accounting and financial reporting and ethical and corporate governance issues as they apply to managerial decisions .

title: BUSINESS ESSENTIALS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to contemporary business operations in local, regional and global environments where you will consider both current and future operational needs. You will engage actively with current business issues, focusing particularly on the impact of external and internal environments on businesses and individuals. In addition, this subject is designed to develop your critical thinking and creative problem-solving with a particular focus on management, marketing and human resource practices. You will also examine and address contemporary business social issues drawn from various organisational and cultural contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse an existing local, regional, or global businesses environment and make informed strategic decisions.
Communicate effectively to culturally-diverse audiences through structured written arguments.
Demonstrate and justify the use of management skills to solve a contemporary social problem in a dynamic business environment

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the nature and function of business. However, business leaders are challenged by the effective and competitive adoption of AI. This subject provides you with an industry-ready skillset to empower productivity, innovation and decision-making across the business ecosystem. You will learn to apply prompting techniques, build and evaluate AI chatbots, construct and articulate AI strategies. Alongside AI capabilities, you will recognise and address the risks of AI, ethics and cybersecurity through a deep understanding of local and international guidelines, regulations and governance. You will foster an AI-first mindset for the effective and responsible practice of AI in any business or industry environment.
learning_outcomes: Apply and critically evaluate prompting techniques and AI tools in diverse business contexts
Analyse and critically evaluate AI strategies and policies to support responsible adoption in varied business environments
Design and develop in teams, AI chatbot solutions that address complex business challenges, demonstrating alignment with ethical principles, governance frameworks, and cybersecurity standards.

title: PRINCIPLES OF BUSINESS ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to business and data analytics with a strong focus on practical outcomes that are directly applicable to business contexts. It provides a comprehensive understanding of current theories, frameworks, applications, and technologies that support data-driven decision-making in organisations. You will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard analytics platforms to conduct descriptive analytics and build interactive dashboards aligned with business needs. The subject explores the strategic role of analytics in digital transformation, performance management, and continuous improvement. Key topics include descriptive analytics, visualisation tools, data ethics, and cybersecurity. Industry-based guest lectures provide insights into how organisations are applying analytics to enhance business performance and address emerging challenges. Upon completion, you will be able to explain the role of analytics in business environments, apply analytical tools, evaluate ethical considerations, and align analytics strategies with organisational objectives.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced analytics techniques and tools aligned with industry best practice to generate data-driven insights, design effective dashboards, and support evidence-based decision-making.
Evaluate cybersecurity, data protection, and ethical challenges in organisational analytics and AI, and apply frameworks to ensure responsible and compliant data practices.
Critically examine the purpose and strategic value of analytics and AI in organisations to enhance decision-making, operational efficiency, and innovation.

title: VIBE CODING FOR STARTUPS
syllabus_overview: Vibe coding and AI-assisted coding are recent AI capabilities that significantly reduce the cost, time and expertise required for technology adoption and development. These unlock innovation opportunities for SMEs and startups operating with limited budgets. This subject will provide you with technical, creative and problem-solving skills for the design, development and evaluation of prototypes for startups and related business environments. The risks and limitations of vibe coding will be learned alongside conventional coding methods, ethics and cybersecurity guidelines. The ecosystem, opportunities and challenges of AI startups will be a further topic of this subject.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate technology prototypes for diverse business and industry settings using vibe coding and AI-assisted coding.

Develop and evaluate AI startup strategies to address complex industrial challenges and advance the UN Sustainable Development Goals, demonstrating effective collaboration and teamwork in professional settings.
Analyse risks and limitations of vibe coding and apply conventional coding methods, ethical principles, and cybersecurity guidelines to address these challenges.

title: CYBERSECURITY FOR BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: Cybersecurity for Business provides a comprehensive overview of cybersecurity principles, practices, and frameworks for managing cybersecurity risks in organisations. Cybersecurity plays a critical role in an organisation's operations by safeguarding its assets, ensuring regulatory compliance, and enhancing overall business resilience. The subject covers key topics, including cybersecurity threats, attacks, governance frameworks, cybersecurity risk management, cybersecurity policies and procedures, and compliance. You will explore cybersecurity for businesses through a combination of tailor-made case studies and hands-on workshops, offering a comprehensive understanding of theoretical principles alongside practical application in real-world scenarios. It develops the skills necessary to craft effective cybersecurity strategies that align with organisational goals and regulatory requirements. The course will also examine the ethical, legal, and regulatory dimensions of cybersecurity.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse different types of cyber threats, attack methods, and AI-driven threats, to assess their potential impact on business operations, risk management, and compliance obligations.

Design and justify ethical and governance-aligned cybersecurity strategies using appropriate frameworks, AI-enabled tools, and security models to strengthen threat detection, incident response, resilience, and regulatory compliance.
Identify and apply fundamental cybersecurity principles to recognise and evaluate common organisational security challenges, including those arising from emerging technologies and AI.
Communicate cybersecurity governance strategies and AI-informed risk mitigation plans clearly and appropriately to diverse technical and non-technical stakeholders in professional business contexts.

title: CLOUD PLATFORMS AND ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: Organisations are rapidly migrating technology infrastructure and applications into cloud platforms, due to increased availability, security, reliability and cost-effectiveness. Moreover, cloud platforms are crucial in enabling artificial intelligence, big data analytics and data engineering of Internet of Things, social media data streams and multimedia data. In response, these platforms are gradually becoming user-centric and customisable to suit the technology requirements of small to large scale organisations. Technical knowledge, practical skills, and IT security implements in cloud platforms are a strategic advantage in the modern workplace. You will develop a range of technical knowledge and practical skills required to instantiate, configure, secure and manage a cloud platform for organisational needs. You will learn how to leverage a cloud platform and its components for business automation, security risk management, robotic process automation, data integration and data analytics and artificial intelligence applications.
learning_outcomes: Assess and apply cloud adoption frameworks to justify, plan, implement, and govern cloud platforms, in alignment with organisational culture, business objectives, sustainability, and ethical practice.
Critically evaluate and apply cloud-based products and services to meet organisational needs for data, networking, and computing, while ensuring cybersecurity, privacy, and ethical compliance.
Design and synthesise end-to-end cloud-based platforms that deliver secure and ethical data, analytics, and AI capabilities aligned with organisational objectives and industry standards.
Configure and critically explain the components, capabilities, deployment, and cybersecurity features of modern cloud computing platforms.

title: QUANTITATIVE DATA ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the quantitative analysis techniques that are commonly used by business researchers, analysts and managers to analyse data to provide answers to business problems and research questions. You will develop the ability to analyse, interpret and report quantitative data, using justifiable univariate and multivariate methods.
learning_outcomes: Generate quantitative insights utilising a prescribed statistical package.
Define and justify the use of univariate and/or multivariate data analysis techniques to address a research problem
Communicate the methods and/or results of the quantitative approaches utilised in a professional and scholarly way to an academic and practitioner audience

title: DESIGNING BUSINESS ANALYTICS SOLUTIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject is Part 1 of the Capstone. It consolidates the knowledge and skills acquired in BUS5PR1 on the design, development and evaluation of analytics, artificial intelligence and automation solutions. You will work in groups to critically review state-of-the-art theoretical and technical developments and IT security management functions to address the diverse challenges of an industry, business or research context. They will formulate a conceptual model and/or technical design that advance the professional practice and scholarship of the domain. Communications and documentation reflecting this professional practice and scholarship will be demonstrated.
learning_outcomes: Create, evaluate and explicate the ethics, IT security and governance considerations of this design
Work in groups to abstract and synthesise the review outcomes for the diverse challenges of an industry or research context
Critically review state-of-the-art theoretical and technical developments of analytics, artificial intelligence and automation applications
Propose and prescribe a conceptual modelling, technical design and IT security management that advance the professional practice and scholarship of analytics, artificial intelligence and automation

title: OPERATIONALISING BUSINESS ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates students' knowledge and skills in business analytics, focusing on the design, development, and evaluation of analytics, artificial intelligence, and automation solutions. Working in collaborative groups on real-life projects, students will critically engage with cutting-edge theoretical and technical developments to address complex challenges in industry, business, or research contexts. They will propose and implement business analytics solutions, assess technical feasibility, and evaluate key considerations such as IT security, ethical implications, and real-world applicability. Students will also explore technology pathways, develop and test prototypical solutions, and assess their performance within an agile project environment. The subject strengthens students’ technical competencies while enhancing their communication, problem-solving, critical thinking, and project management skills.
learning_outcomes: Propose and justify conceptual models, technical designs, and IT and cybersecurity strategies that advance professional practice in analytics, AI, and automation, considering platform constraints, user requirements, and governance.

Collaboratively develop and test prototypical solutions, critically assessing functionality, implications including ethics, privacy, and cybersecurity, and communicating findings effectively through rigorous, professional technical documentation.

Analyse and evaluate feasible implementation pathways by assessing business context, analytics capabilities, tool suitability, integration constraints, and agile methods for iterative solution development.
Critically evaluate and synthesise advanced developments in analytics, AI, and automation to address real-world challenges, with attention to stakeholder needs, ethical concerns, and governance.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF BUSINESS RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the epistemology of research and explore the critical role that independent research, when conducted to the highest standards, contributes to our society. You will hone your ability to undertake sophisticated literature searches and manage this body of knowledge using reference management systems in accordance with academic conventions. You will enhance your ability to analyse relevant literature to identify a research gap and develop logical and detailed justifications for your arguments.
learning_outcomes: Effectively manage your literature library using a reference management system
Evaluate the ideas and debates of the philosophy of science in the context of business research
Communicate arguments and syntheses of research in a professional and scholarly manner
Generate appropriate research questions from a rigorous literature review of a relevant body of knowledge

title: RESEARCH DESIGN
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about research design as the foundation for conducting high quality research. You will learn the hallmarks of social research methods, including observational, survey, and experimental designs. You will develop skills to evaluate the strengths, limitations, and ethical considerations of these designs for answering specific research questions.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate various research design and methodologies
Identify ethical issues within a research setting and develop an appropriate response to these issues
Develop and justify a written research proposal designed to address research questions within your discipline

title: ECONOMETRICS AND DATA ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will enhance your proficiency in quantitative data analysis while acquiring quantitative techniques commonly used in business. These skills will enable you to effectively address critical research inquiries and make informed strategic choices. The curriculum encompasses various topics like time-series modelling and panel data analysis. Moreover, you will delve into the realm of data mining and machine learning, acquiring hands-on experience with software tools. This subject will provide you with the expertise and competence to apply econometrics and data analytics techniques in academic research and business scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Appraise different quantitative data analysis techniques and justify the selection of techniques for addressing research questions in business
Communicate the methods and results of the utilised quantitative approaches in a professional manner
Apply appropriate and various quantitative data analysis techniques using software tools

title: BUSINESS WORK PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides practical experience to prepare you for a successful business career. The work placement offers a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between theory and practice by immersing yourself in a business environment. You will have the chance to apply your knowledge to real-world scenarios and contribute to organisational projects. Working alongside experienced professionals and undertaking specific business tasks you will gain valuable insights into local, national or multinational workplaces. A work placement develops your analytical and problem-solving skills, enhances your communication and teamwork abilities, and cultivates the confidence necessary to thrive in a competitive business landscape. Dedicated academic staff provide supervision to ensure you continue to develop your employability skills and enrich your work placement experience. By participating in our work placement subject, you not only gain a competitive edge in the job market but also build a strong foundation for your future career.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse relevant theoretical perspectives and apply them to practical work.
Use critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and technology to address business issues.
Synthesise information about your host organisation and articulate how you will apply your degree knowledge to tasks and projects
Reflect on personal experience, acknowledge strengths as a responsible leader/manager, and develop strategies for improvement.

title: QUALITATIVE DATA ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the opportunity to develop skills in qualitative research practice in the field of business. This involves developing an appreciation of the skills needed to collect qualitative data using appropriate methods, including interviews, focus groups, document analysis and observation. You will also learn how to analyse, interpret, and report qualitative data to a variety of audiences.
learning_outcomes: Communicate the methods and results from the qualitative approaches and analysis in a professional and scholarly way
Critique the five main qualitative approaches relevant to business research
Generate qualitative insights from data collected through interviews, documents, observation, focus groups and case studies

title: RESPONSIBLE AI FOR SUSTAINABILITY
syllabus_overview: Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the design, development, deployment, and adoption of AI systems that minimise risks to people, society, and the environment while ensuring alignment with human values and societal norms. This subject begins by studying the harms, risks and challenges of AI, followed by frameworks and approaches that address these issues through the responsible, ethical and sustainable practice of AI in organisations. Students will experiment with these methods in building AI systems that align with the principles and practice of responsible AI, including ethics and cybersecurity guidelines. Drawing on United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and PRME, the subject further develops knowledge and critical thinking of how AI contributes towards sustainability and equity in business and society.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and evaluate the risks, harms, and challenges posed by AI to individuals, organisations, societies, and the environment.
Formulate, compare, and evaluate responsible AI adoption frameworks and strategies aligned with local and international guidelines and regulations.
Design, build, and critically assess AI systems that align with the principles and practices of responsible AI, including ethical and cybersecurity guidelines.

title: DIGITAL STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: Digital Strategy explores the strategic role of digital technologies in transforming organisations and driving competitive advantage in today’s digital economy. The subject covers key concepts such as digital disruption, digital business models, digital capabilities, and digital strategy frameworks. You will learn how to develop, implement, and evaluate digital strategies that leverage emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things to foster competitive advantages in organisations.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate organisational digital capabilities and their alignment with business objectives, considering the strategic implications of emerging technologies and industry trends.
Design and justify digital strategies and implementation roadmaps using theory-based approaches and industry-relevant frameworks.
Critically analyse concepts of digital strategy development, implementation, and value to inform organisational digital transformation.
Implement and (critically) evaluate digital strategies to ensure alignment with organisational goals, ethical practice and innovation while demonstrating effective communication and leadership.

title: GLOBAL BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
syllabus_overview: The Global Business Experience subject offers a unique opportunity for students to gain an international work integrated learning experience. You will collaborate in small teams to tackle real-world business challenges in a foreign country gaining first-hand experience of the complexities operating in a foreign institutional and cultural environment. The learning experience will also include visits to foreign-host businesses and cultural sites relevant to the business context of the specific study abroad tour, engaging with local authorities, businesspeople as well as staff and peers from La Trobe’s partner institutions in the host country. Students will apply their theoretical knowledge and business tool skills gained thus far in their studies. The subject aims to help students develop a global mindset and gain transferable employability skills.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess and apply the theoretical frameworks and business tools necessary to tackle real-world business problems in a foreign country
Enhance cultural (self)awareness, assess foreign institutional and industry settings, and work effectively within a team
Critically evaluate one’s own global business experiential learning

title: BUSINESS SYSTEMS DESIGN AND ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: Business Systems Design and Analysis is a dynamic and practical course that focuses on the requirement analysis, design, and development of business systems to enhance organizational performance. The course covers key stages in the requirement gathering, business system design lifecycle and change management methodologies using an agile approach. In this subject, you will learn the fundamentals of system analysis and design, business process modelling, user-centric design thinking, and agile methodologies. You will learn to identify business requirements, and critically analyse the capabilities and limitations of business systems thereby designing effective system solutions to meet organizational objectives.
learning_outcomes: Design and critically evaluate change management and system redesign strategies that enhance user experience, strengthen data security, and uphold ethical data practices aligned with organisational goals.
Critically evaluate the stages of the business systems lifecycle to identify opportunities for digital transformation and design for innovation in complex organisational contexts.
Design, model, and justify advanced business process flows using user-centred design thinking and agile methodologies to address complex, real-world business challenges.

title: BUSINESS INFORMATION SYSTEMS INDUSTRY PROJECT
syllabus_overview: Information Systems in business play a crucial role in transforming data into useful information that supports management in making informed decisions. Business Information Systems assists businesses operate more efficiently by streamlining processes, automating tasks, and ensuring smooth daily operations. It enables decision-makers to analyse trends, identify opportunities, address challenges, and have effective IS in enhancing competitive edge. In this subject you will be actively engaged with real industry professionals in project planning, analysis, and designing solutions to various business problems associated with information systems. You will work in groups and be part of a simulated Business Intelligence consulting enterprise and work in partnership with a real consulting firm to tackle business problems and challenges faced by a real industry client. You will prepare a design for solutions, implement it, and deploy it in the client's business environment.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement advanced business information systems project methodologies to develop effective solutions in complex organisational contexts
Critically evaluate and manage client relationships and expectations to deliver successful project outcomes
Analyse and interpret complex datasets to support strategic decision-making, ensuring integrity, security, and adherence to ethical and legal standards.
Collaborate to deliver professional-standard presentations, demonstrations, and project reports to industry stakeholders.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF BUSINESS INFORMATION SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: Fundamentals of Information Systems provides a comprehensive understanding of the foundation concepts, principles, and technologies that underpin modern business information systems. The subject covers key topics such as the role of information systems in organisations, the strategic importance of information systems, the components and architecture of information systems, and the management of information systems, the ethics, privacy and security of information systems. The real-world case studies and tailored hands-on workshops offered in the subject enable you to develop practical skills to manage and leverage information systems effectively to address business needs. This subject builds a foundation for you with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the complexities of business information systems and make informed decisions in dynamic organisational environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and critically evaluate how information systems, leveraging advanced software, hardware, and analytical tools, drive innovation, competitiveness, and strategic business outcomes in complex organisational contexts
Apply concepts, principles, and technologies of information systems to support the design and implementation of solutions for complex business environments

Critically evaluate ethical, cultural, security, and cybersecurity issues associated with information systems in diverse business environments, and design informed strategies to address these challenges effectively

title: BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION
syllabus_overview: Conducting a Business Intelligence (BI) project is part of the day-to-day operation of the business analysts which involves project planning, client's requirements analysis, solution design, implementation, and deployment. An effective BI project produces a solution for corporate leaders to make more informed, strategic decisions, improve operational efficiency, gain a competitive edge, and drive sustainable, data-driven growth for their organisations. In this unit, students will have the opportunity to apply many of the aspects covered in this program through undertaking project preparation, construction, testing, and deployment of a real-world BI system. Working in small groups/project teams for a simulated consulting firm, students will implement a project solution design in the form of a BI dashboard for a real client. Students will fully develop the design, and then present it in a demo to the client. Students will also document a blueprint of the final product for the client and plan for the deployment, client training, post-implementation review, and maintenance.
learning_outcomes: Assess the suitability of business intelligence frameworks and apply them effectively to generate data-driven insights in varying business environments.
Demonstrate professional competence in managing client relationships and stakeholder expectations within diverse, real-world business contexts
Lead and collaborate in multidisciplinary teams to research, produce, and deliver professional-standard reports and presentations for industry stakeholders.
Critically evaluate, design, and apply advanced business intelligence project methodologies to address complex industry problems.

title: CUSTOMER ANALYTICS AND SOCIAL MEDIA
syllabus_overview: Humans have become information triggering and transmitting 'devices' due to the use of ATMs, credit cards, telephones, loyalty cards, call centres, digital television, internet etc. Using customer analytics, such information can be used by organizations to understand their customer lifestyles, life stages, personal values and financial status, which helps to gain new customers, keep existing customers longer and increase the frequency and value of customers thus becoming more competitive and profitable. Social media now plays a significant role in the customer relationship both as a way of marketing products and services and also a medium through which customer segments and sentiments could be captured. Ability to efficiently make use of social media information is now becoming an essential part of customer analytics. This unit provides the necessary knowledge and skills to use data analytics technologies to better understand customers resulting in happier, content and loyal customers leading to a better customer relationship. Case studies will be throughout to concepts, techniques and tools.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate various customer analytics techniques for a variety of business problems.
Design social media analytics solutions to enhance customer intelligence through customer sentiment analysis.
Apply the appropriate analytics tools for customer analytics tasks including customer segmentation and profiling, churn analysis and prediction, target-marketing analysis.

title: ANALYTICS AND AI IN INDUSTRY
syllabus_overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and analytics are central to how businesses innovate and make decisions. Whether as business professional or an analytics specialist, this subject prepares you to collaborate across disciplines to create value and innovate through data-driven AI and analytics solutions. You will build practical skills in issue identification, problem structuring, method selection, data gathering, analysis, project governance, benefits realisation and developing evidence based proposals. You will also learn communication competencies, including data visualisation, reporting, and communicating insights to diverse stakeholders. Your learning will be grounded in authentic business problems drawn from industry perspectives, giving you an immersive experience in applying the practice of AI and analytics in a meaningful context.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply business analysis techniques and stakeholder engagement strategies to address organisational challenges and recommend AI and analytics driven solutions across diverse contexts.
Create and deliver professional artefacts and stakeholder presentations that communicate insights and project outcomes using appropriate communication strategies and evidence based reasoning.
Plan and evaluate end-to-end project management strategies that incorporate ethical, regulatory, and cyber security considerations for the sustainable delivery of AI and data analytics projects.
Design and justify data driven business proposals using advanced AI and analytical techniques, creative thinking, and problem solving methods tailored to diverse stakeholder needs.

title: DIRECTED READINGS
syllabus_overview: An individual reading project which allows you to follow a course of directed study at masters level under the supervision on an academic staff member. Only available for students who are recommended by the relevant Program Director to apply and approved by the Head of Department.
learning_outcomes: Describe, apply and critically evaluate relevant business theory and principles as they apply to specific business problems.
Identify and critically analyse relevant academic literature in business as it applies to a specific business problem.
Recognise and articulate business issues

title: DATA WRANGLING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the various techniques of data wrangling with a strong focus on hands-on experience in programming using Structured Query Language (SQL) and the Python programming language. It will cover the basic concepts in relational database design including Entity Relationship (ER) modelling and SQL as a tool for basic data wrangling. You will also learn various types of data sources and common data formats. The subject equips you with skills in data wrangling, including data import and export, basic data integration, assessment and transformation. Upon completion, you will be able to perform a variety of data wrangling tasks using SQL and a programming language for different kinds of data types.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement database models that meet business requirements using advanced data modelling and querying techniques to enable analytics initiatives.

Analyse data by developing SQL queries and data wrangling scripts using programming tools with responsible use of generative AI to support data transformation and insight generation for data-driven business decisions.
Evaluate and compare data sources, formats, and structures to prepare and transform data for analysis, considering ethical, legal, and cybersecurity risks in business analytics.
Formulate data and data-wrangling requirements that address the technical challenges of analytics tasks, incorporating data governance, ethical principles, and cybersecurity constraints.

title: ENTERPRISE INFORMATION SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: Organisations today are employing many enterprise information systems such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) for developing customer-centric business strategies and integration of business processes in accounting, finance, human resources, sales and marketing. In this subject, you will be provided with an overview of enterprise-wide computing and integrated enterprise systems concepts. You will be introduced to the skills needed to become an ERP consultant and have the opportunity to develop your capacity to analyse and reengineer business processes based on ERP life cycle using well known ERP tools like SAP S/4 HANA. You will critique business process re-engineering strategies of organisations in the context of ERP systems. Case studies and software packages such as SAP S/4 HANA will be used to provide you with hands-on experience.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and evaluate business process reengineering strategies and their alignment with enterprise resource planning(ERP) systems to support organisational transformation
Collaboratively assess organisational size, complexity, and context to inform the strategic selection, design, and implementation of ERP systems
Manage business data and information in ERP systems by applying advanced ERP knowledge and technical skills using the latest technology, such as SAP S/4HANA.
Analyse the role of AI and intelligent enterprise technologies in enhancing ERP capabilities, including data-mining, CRM, and data-driven decision-making

title: MANAGING IT PROJECTS
syllabus_overview: IT projects involve multiple stakeholders with competing interests, operate in dynamic business environments and must deliver projects in increasingly short time-frames. In this subject you will examine the foundations of project management involving scope, cost, time, human resources, procurement, risk, quality, communication and integration in the context of information systems projects and methodologies. Management techniques to effectively respond to the organisational, political and cultural barriers IT projects typically face will be discussed. Risk and stakeholder analysis, and critical chain scheduling will be taught. You will also consider advanced topics like management of cross-organisational projects, societal issues, teamwork issues, project office functions and project management toolsets. The agile project management concepts and development are also discussed.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the methodologies for managing IT project requirements across the full project lifecycle
Assess the processes required for IT project initiation to incorporate scope, time, cost, and quality management
Demonstrate leadership, collaboration, and accountability in managing project teams and producing professional-standard project documentation and reports
Apply advanced techniques in executing, monitoring, and controlling IT projects, with consideration for risk, communication, and stakeholder engagement

title: PRINCIPLES OF BUSINESS ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to business and data analytics with a strong focus on practical outcomes that are directly applicable to business contexts. It delivers a comprehensive understanding of current theories, frameworks, applications and technologies that support modern data-driven decision-making process. You will gain hands-on experience state-of-the-art analytics platforms to design and develop analytics solutions. The subject focuses on introducing key descriptive analytics topics, data wrangling, text processing and data ethics. Industry-based guest lectures will present fresh perspectives on the managerial role in planning and implementing business analytics initiatives and the emerging role of analytics in business performance management. Upon completion, you will be able to transform business problems into analytics solutions, understand key issues, analytics frameworks, techniques, determine business value of analytics outcomes and appreciate its role in BPM.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate requirements, methodologies and technologies for analytics-based business performance management.

Analyse and evaluate the function of key elements of a typical analytics solution; technology infrastructure, data architecture, data management, analytics methodologies, analytics techniques, reports, dashboards, responsibilities of groups and individuals within the business environment.
Examine the purpose and importance of analytics within a business environment, alongside implications for technologies, workflows, participation and management.

title: PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: The information age has combined with the widespread adoption of digital technology to turn information into a key business asset. Organisations have access to volumes of data and require skills and expertise in using this information for strategic decision making. Predictive analytics refers to the statistical and analytical techniques used to develop models that predict future events from data. You will learn the skills to build and use predictive models in real business scenarios. Case studies such as target marketing and customer churn analysis will be used to demonstrate the business value of predictive analytics. A number of related data mining and machine learning techniques such as neural networks, decision trees, customer segmentation and profiling will also be taught.
learning_outcomes: Build and evaluate predictive analytics models for solving complex business problems, considering ethical, fairness, privacy, and data security implications.
Appraise and justify the selection of predictive analytics models and techniques for business case studies, highlighting their value and application.
Critically analyse the predictive analytics lifecycle, explaining the role and importance of each stage in building effective predictive models.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND HYPERAUTOMATION
syllabus_overview: This subject expatiates knowledge and skills acquired in the course hitherto, by focusing on a real-world, hands-on, industry-focused project that requires students to apply, experiment, create and evaluate an end-to-end analytics solution that addresses complex end-user requirements for data-driven decision-making. Students will learn an agile scrum-based approach that use Jupyter Notebooks, Google Collaboratory, and Python libraries for developing analytics techniques based on machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing algorithms. Professional and interpersonal communication skills required to present an analytics start-up pitch, data-driven insights, analytics teamwork practice and project management updates to an industry-based audience will be discussed, demonstrated and assessed. Ethics of artificial intelligence and analytics data and ICT governance, security management, and related human factors which are equally important to a successful analytics project with positive social impact will be formulated and evaluated in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively and ethically with diverse stakeholders, demonstrating professional communication, adaptability, and teamwork capabilities in industry-focused problem solving.
Critically evaluate guidelines and regulation for ethics, cybersecurity, governance, and human factors to ensure the safe and responsible use of AI and Analytics technologies
Design and evaluate advanced analytics and AI systems to address complex business problems and enable data-driven decision-making

Analyse and apply analytics and AI techniques, including machine learning, natural language processing, prompt engineering, and generative AI using state-of-the-art platforms for agile solution development and comparison.

title: DATA WAREHOUSING AND BIG DATA ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the knowledge and skills necessary to conceptualise, design, develop, implement, and use such technology platforms. You will learn to design and develop an actual data warehouse on cloud computing infrastructure. You will use this warehouse to build cubes for OLAP, write SQL and MDX queries, apply machine learning algorithms, generate reports, and dashboards to communicate actionable insights. You will learn how to configure and use a cloud computing environment (based on Microsoft Azure) to develop a technology platform that encompasses computing, networking, security, and data management components. You will execute analytics techniques and machine learning algorithms on a live Hadoop instance to derive insights from unstructured data. Upon completion of the subject, you will demonstrate practical knowledge and skills necessary to construct and evaluate a modern technology platform that addresses Big Data complexities
learning_outcomes: Apply analytical and reporting technologies to design queries, build data models, and create dashboards that generate and communicate actionable insights from a data warehouse.
Design and implement data warehouse solutions that support data-driven decision making and enable scalable, secure business intelligence in organisational contexts.
Analyse infrastructure requirements for computing, networking, cybersecurity, and data processing, and configure cloud based platforms to support secure, scalable big data analytics solutions.

Critically evaluate contemporary big data technologies and architectures for performance, scalability, and suitability to address organisational analytics challenges, considering data privacy, security, and ethical implications.

title: VISUAL ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: As data becomes ever more complex to analyse, the need for tools to help integrate the user's knowledge and inference capability into the analytical process becomes important. In analytics, this is generally referred to as visualisation, which this subject will cover in detail from various perspectives, for example, temporal, spatial, spatial-temporal, multi-variate, text/documents, graphs and networks, and more. These perspectives will be covered with various business applications in mind including, statistical and summary reporting, trends spotting and projections, process capture, and real-time reporting. These applications will be discussed with reference to various visual analytics frameworks and theories as well as case examples.
learning_outcomes: Select and critically evaluate appropriate visualisation techniques for diverse business problems throughout the solution process, considering ethical implications and cybersecurity requirements.
Analyse and explain visualisation frameworks for solving a variety of business problems.
Use data visualisation techniques to present analytics clearly and effectively for managers and other stakeholders.
Apply advanced tools to visualise data and analytical findings that meet specific user requirements.

title: MEDUSA TO THE MCG: ANCIENT GREEK AND ROMAN CULTURE IN THE MODERN WORLD
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an informative and fun introduction to the cultures of Ancient Greece and Rome and where they turn up in the modern world, from Medusa in the Percy Jackson franchise, through to Melbourne’s own version of the Colosseum, the MCG. You will explore the fascinating worlds of Greece and Rome, including the places where their histories, societies and languages have influenced our own culture. You will learn about the worlds of Circe and Socrates, Caesar and Cicero; and discover what we have taken from ancient political structures ('democracy', 'senate', 'fascism'), sport (the Olympics; gladiators), language, philosophy, law, science, medicine, mythology and more. This is a level 1 subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge about two ancient cultures and their historical context
Explain their acquired knowledge and review their classmates' analyses of ancient and modern cultures
Identify and evaluate connections between two ancient cultures and their own (modern) culture.
Construct a persuasive, evidence-based argument in an essay relating aspects of ancient Greek and Roman culture to modernity
Find, analyse and properly reference primary source material and scholarship relating to ancient Greek and Roman culture and language.

title: ANCIENT GREECE: MYTH, ART, WAR
syllabus_overview: In this subject students are introduced to the diversity of the ancient Greek achievement, which has exercised a fundamental and continuing influence upon later European literature and culture. The subject commences with a detailed treatment of Homer's Iliad and the myth of the Trojan war. This is one of the dominant myths in the Greek tradition and is narrated in some detail in epic poetry, in drama, and in art and architecture. We explore how myths are 'read' in their historical context, especially in the contexts of the Persian and Peloponnesian wars of the 5th Century BC. A variety of sources are treated to enable students to build up a picture of Greek society as a whole. Texts are read in translation and students are encouraged to consider certain questions of method, (for example, historical versus literary evidence) in dealing with the study of a culture removed in time and nature from our own. This is a level 1subject. The Blended instance includes face to face sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation. The Online instance is taught asynchronously
learning_outcomes: Research, identify, and critique primary sources (both textual and material and secondary sources (modern lines of interpretation and argument), employing appropriate methodologies.
Research and produce written work deploying both primary and secondary sources, including an appropriate specialised bibliography.
Develop skills in academic writing and visual analysis of material culture.
Analyse key texts and artefacts within the context of the wider culture of a different society (Ancient Greece).

title: ANCIENT ROME: SLAVES, EMPIRE AND FILM
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the society, literature and art of ancient Rome through major historical figures such as Julius Caesar, Cleopatra, Augustus and Nero. You will also learn more about the legacy of Roman culture in the modern world. You will read ancient Roman literature and examine material culture to better understand Roman hierarchies of power, based around class, slavery, gender roles and entertainment, such as arena spectacles. While we focus on the city of Rome, you will also study Pompeii, and consider Rome's history of military conquest in building a vast empire. Central to this subject is looking forward to the way in which Rome is now depicted in art and on screen in television and movies, including HBO's series Rome , Russell Crowe in Gladiator , and Doctor Who: Fires of Pompeii . Through studying these modern texts alongside ancient sources you will be introduced to the discipline of Classical Reception Studies. This is a level 2 subject. Please consider the subject pre-requisites before enrolling. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and articulate a persuasive, evidence-based argument in an essay relating to ancient Roman society and its connections to modern culture.
Synthesise, critique and apply disciplinary scholarship in the context of interpreting ancient Roman society and its connections to the modern world.
Comprehend , analyse and evaluate primary and secondary sources, using both in historical enquiry
Identify the context of ancient literary and historical sources, and articulate the relevance of this context in analyses of ancient texts and material artefacts.

title: CLASSICAL MYTHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will read and interpret ancient Greek and Roman mythology, and be introduced to theoretical approaches to interpreting these myths. You will learn about Greek and Roman creation myths, and tales involving the Olympian gods, heroes and heroines, including Heracles, Jason, Perseus, Odysseus, Medea, Ariadne, Romulus and Lucretia. As you work your way through these myths, you will encounter thematic elements of classical mythology such as the figure of the monster, the sexual conduct of gods and mortals, conception and birth, ethnic identities, gender roles, the foundation of cities, death, and images of the underworld, and life after death. This is a level 2 subject. Please consider the subject pre-requisites before enrolling.
learning_outcomes: Contextualise and analyse literary and material primary source evidence relating to ancient Greek and Roman mythology
Formulate and articulate a persuasive, evidence-based argument in an essay relating to ancient Greek and Roman mythology
Critique disciplinary scholarship and apply appropriate theoretical approaches in the context of interpreting ancient Greek and Roman mythology
Synthesise and interpret primary source evidence using disciplinary scholarship from Classics and Ancient History

title: MEDICINE AND SOCIETY IN ANCIENT GREECE AND ROME
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to ancient Greek and Roman medicine and its role in society. Through the writings of Hippocratic doctors, Galen and other doctors we will learn about the theories and practices of ancient scholarly medicine. We will also examine temple medicine, magical healing and folk remedies to consider how all forms of medicine contributed to wider ancient debates concerning how the body works, what causes disease, what distinguishes rationality from superstition, why humans experience emotions, how gender and ethnicity are constructed, and how doctors should behave. We will read extracts from ancient playwrights, philosophers, speech-writers and historians to consider the experience of patients, the role of women in medicine, and conceptions of mental health and disability in antiquity. We will place ancient Graeco-Roman medicine in the wider history of medicine and debate the continuing relevance of ancient medical ideas today, from the Hippocratic Oath to the precept to 'first, do no harm'.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast social and cultural attitudes to medical understandings of the body, disease and treatment in order to explore themes of continuity and change over time and place.
Critically analyse a source in depth in order to understand its context and implications.
Synthesise, critique and apply ancient medical literature and modern disciplinary scholarship to draw relevant ethnographic parallels
Demonstrate effective communication of concepts through written work and debate activities

title: DEATH, BURIAL AND AFTERLIFE
syllabus_overview: This subject investigates cultural approaches to the single event which occurs to all humankind: death. While concentrating on the archaeology, art and textual evidence of Greco-Roman antiquity, the subject also draws upon case studies from later periods and other societies to illustrate the richness, variety and complexity of cultural responses to death, employing modern ethnographic parallels to aid the interpretation of past practices. Topics covered include the role of burial practices in defining living societies through declarations of social status, age, gender and ethnicity in funerary procedures and monuments constructed to commemorate the dead. You will learn about the ideas, literature and art surrounding the afterlife, ghosts and underworld; the role of religion in the formulation of burial rites; and social approaches to ways of death such as war, disease and crime.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate increased and sophisticated knowledge of the material culture and literature of Greco-Roman societies and relevant ethnographic parallels
Analyse a source in depth in order to understand its context, implications and associated debates
Deploy advanced writing skills for the effective communication of complex concepts and debates
Compare and contrast social and cultural attitudes to human mortality in order to explore themes of cultural continuity and change over time and place.

title: ADVANCED CONSTRUCTION SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide a solid understanding of contemporary construction practices, materials development and application of applicable techniques for medium to high rise residential buildings, commercial buildings that includes industrial, educational, medical and other related classes of buildings. You will be engaged with the technological processes involved from design to construction and develop an understanding in assembling the inherent structural systems and built form of these buildings. You will develop essential skills for the executing piling and basements construction; retention systems; industrial buildings, portal frames and ground slabs; precast construction systems for walls and floors; prestressing applications and construction systems for buildings and infrastructure elements; hybrid and composite construction systems.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse innovative construction methods adopted for constructing medium to high rise buildings.
Evaluate and propose alternative construction systems to suit specific requirements by applying advanced technical knowledge.
Interpret advanced construction drawings and communicate construction solutions by using sketches, drawings, models and technical reports consistent with project design criteria.
Distinguish between various structural systems and materials and select the appropriate ones for various building typologies.
Critically evaluate factors influencing construction processes and construction requirements in medium to high rise buildings.

title: GODS, LOVE AND WAR IN ROMAN EPIC
syllabus_overview: This subject explores Ancient Roman epic poetry, the literary genre which deals with grand mythical narratives involving heroes, gods, war, and love affairs. Epic was the most prestigious literary form in the ancient world. Roman poets adapted and developed Greek epics, particularly influenced by the Homeric Iliad and Odyssey . Roman epics similarly deal with divine and heroic material, but Roman poets also weave contemporary and topical themes into the mythical subject matter. The primary text for this subject is Ovid's Metamorphoses , which tells many tales of the gods, nymphs, heroes, and monsters through a series of transformations. This poem is both comic and disturbing; its critique of power imbalances, gender politics and sexual exploitation remains relevant in the twenty-first century. Epics that influenced Ovid will also be studied, particularly Virgil's Aeneid . And we shall consider Ovid as a major influence upon artists and writers, from Shakespeare to David Malouf.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast societies
Demonstrate improved writing skills
Analyse a source in depth and detail
Show increased knowledge of foundation texts of the Western literary tradition

title: BUILDING INFORMATION MODELLING
syllabus_overview: You will gain understanding as to how Building Information Modelling (BIM) technologies are utilised for developing and delivering simple to complex projects in the Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) industries, and explore how BIM is practically used to design, undertake procurement, develop costing and manage buildings and infrastructure projects. Learning from this subject will also equip you with the necessary knowledge required to demonstrate how BIM is used to support effective decision making, assess alternative solutions and manage site safety and quality for building and infrastructure works. You will develop skills to integrate and facilitate construction work using intelligent design, 3D and other technologies and their application to architecture, engineering, costing, construction, and project management and the future of BIM technology.
learning_outcomes: Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to evaluate and appraise the potential of BIM to develop cost and program schedules.
Apply principles of Building Information Modelling (BIM and related application to construction processes.
Critically analyse complex environment requirements and simulate processes for the design and construction using BIM
Apply digital principles of 3D integrated modelling technology for various construction processes

title: CONSTRUCTION AND ENGINEERING PROJECT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to the nature of the construction industry and enable you to develop an understanding of the roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders involved in building and infrastructure projects. You will further review construction project management principles and the application of established management frameworks to the life cycle of building and infrastructure projects. You will also develop an understanding of how various building and infrastructure organisations function in construction and engineering project delivery, and develop an understanding of how planning for buildings and infrastructure projects is undertaken; the requirements for allocation of resources (Materials, Plants and Labour) and processes including construction scheduling principles; and the management of industrial relations issues, project operations mechanisms and management at various phases.
learning_outcomes: Apply project management principles for construction projects and team work in construction projects.
Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to analyse site management procedures to specific sites for efficient use of labour, plant and material.
Analyse site management procedures to maximise efficiency and productivity on construction sites including managing industrial relations.
Evaluate professional skills and specialist knowledge of project management to effectively manage project teams and stakeholders to achieve successive project delivery.
Analyse the role of the design and delivery team, their responsibilities for project delivery and communicate project scope and delivery strategy to achieve the best project outcome.

title: PROJECT PROCUREMENT METHODS
syllabus_overview: This subject will give you in-depth understanding of supply chain management related to construction project procurement from project planning, conducting, controlling and close out. You will dissect construction procurement processes and assess the linkage between contractual parties including international procurement strategies related to project alliancing and public-private partnerships. Your evaluation of project procurement options, decision support tools will build on and extend your understanding of strategic decisions that influence project and organisational success while delivering value. You will further apply procurement principles and theories and develop a framework for managing associated risks, and examine procurement themes related to ethics in procurement and public procurement concerns.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the structure, processes and attributes of various procurement models in construction projects.
Analyse construction procurement principles and project procurement options.
Individually and in groups identify and critically examine ethical implications associated with selecting a procurement model and overall impact on a construction projects.
Evaluate and manage project risks for various procurement methods by applying relevant principles/strategies in construction projects.
Analyse the relationship between project success and procurement processes and evaluate the impacts on project value.

title: CHEMISTRY 1B
syllabus_overview: This subject prepares you for your advanced studies in your chosen field of interest by building understanding of the chemical principles that underpin a broad range of disciplines, including biological, health, pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences. This subject incorporates topics in the principles of molecular attractive and repulsive forces, carbon chemistry, the chemistry of living organisms and electrochemistry fundamentals, reinforced by some practical activities.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret chemical behaviour in chemical complexation, solubility equilibria, and electrochemistry using thermodynamic and kinetic principles.

Demonstrate proficiency in practical laboratory techniques relevant to organic and biological chemistry, including safe handling of chemicals, synthesis, analysis, and interpretation of experimental data.
Identify and explain the structure, properties, speciation and reactivity of key biological molecules.
Describe and apply fundamental concepts of organic chemistry, including bonding, molecular geometry, isomerism, and reactivity, to predict the behaviour of organic molecules.

title: CHEMISTRY 1A
syllabus_overview: This subject presents key chemical concepts needed by students throughout their degree and career in science, including chemical hazards and the safe handling of chemicals (through practical activities), stoichiometric relationships and concentrations, introduction to atomic and molecular structure, introduction to organic and functional group chemistry, chemical equilibrium for gas and solution phase reactions, acid and base reactions, chemical thermodynamics and chemical Kinetics.
learning_outcomes: Identify, name, and relate the structure and reactivity of organic molecules to their physical and chemical properties.
Analyse and predict the behaviour of chemical systems using concepts of equilibrium, thermodynamics, and acid-base chemistry.

Demonstrate proficiency in practical laboratory techniques relevant to organic and biological chemistry, including safe handling of chemicals, synthesis, analysis, and interpretation of experimental data.
Apply fundamental chemical principles to solve problems involving atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, and chemical reactions.

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: Various management systems are employed in construction projects. This subject will introduce you to the primary management systems used in the construction industry. These include quality, environmental and safety management systems. You will learn to develop and integrate management plans required for the effective and efficient management of construction and engineering projects. Through application you will further your knowledge of the various systems and compliance requirements, with consideration of local and international quality standards, regulation and environmental and safety codes of practice. You will further develop and apply your learning to material and plant management, essential in building and infrastructure projects.
learning_outcomes: Analyse key processes and framework for QMS, EMS and SMS and assess implications for implementation.
Apply advanced process management strategies to effectively manage environmental performance issues associated with specific projects.
Develop an effective QMS plan to enhance project quality at corporate and project level.
Develop an effective SMS plan compliant with the relevant legislation by conducting hazard identification and risk assessment.
Analyse relevant legislation and associated standards with various management systems such as QMS; EMS; and SMS.

title: APPLICATIONS OF CHEMISTRY
syllabus_overview: In Applications of Chemistry you will learn how foundation concepts and knowledge of the first semester chemistry subject CHE1CHF are applied in a broad range of fields, including the chemistry of living organisms, the manufacture of synthetic materials, and identifying and alleviating chemical pollution. This subject will prepare you to advance to second year studies in chemistry and related disciplines, enable you to develop laboratory skills, and apply chemistry knowledge and skills within your chosen discipline.
learning_outcomes: Safely employ the scientific method to observe and measure chemical phenomena in the laboratory, and communicate findings by written report.

Recognise chemical and physical properties of chemical reactions, including equilibrium, thermodynamics, kinetics and their relationship to industrial, biological and environmental chemical processes.
Use practical techniques and tools to observe and measure the outcomes of laboratory procedures to recognise connections between theoretical and practical phenomena.
Examine the properties of water in an environmental and chemical context.
Choose appropriate methods of analysis for the detection and quantification of elements and compounds.
Employ mathematical tools to solve chemical problems.

title: CHEMISTRY FOUNDATIONS
syllabus_overview: Chemistry Foundations is an introductory subject designed for students who have no or little previous experience or study in chemistry. Students will be introduced to foundation concepts, knowledge and skills that will enable these students to apply chemical principles during their university degree and future employment. This one-semester subject covers topics common to senior high-school chemistry and introductory university chemistry, that prepares students to advance to second semester chemistry. Students will encounter atomic and molecular structure, bonding, chemical reactions, organic chemistry, and physical chemistry.
learning_outcomes: Communicate in written form using the language of chemistry; interpreting and using chemical symbols, conventions and nomenclature.
Classify types of chemical reactions and predict the chemical products.
Safely employ the scientific method to observe and measure chemical phenomena in the laboratory and communicate findings by written report.
Manipulate quantitative mathematical relationships to solve chemistry problems such as the stoichiometric relationships that determine the quantitative behaviour of chemical systems
Interpret thermochemistry data to determine whether reactions will occur and if they do, to what extent.
Explain the properties of matter using concepts of chemical structure.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF CHEMISTRY A
syllabus_overview: Fundamentals of Chemistry A is a core second year chemistry subject. Students are introduced to the principles and applications associated with the instrumental techniques of mass spectrometry, NMR spectroscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and ultraviolet / visible spectroscopy. These techniques are routinely used by chemists to identify and characterise chemical species. Students will also be introduced to inorganic and coordination chemistry, and study important trends in the reactivity of the elements. Learning activities include lectures, tutorials, online learning activities, workshops and laboratory classes.
learning_outcomes: Interpret Infrared and Ultraviolet-Visible spectra in terms of the spectroscopic transitions that occur within vibrational and electronic energy levels.
Analyse key properties of coordination and organometallic compounds such as structure, nomenclature and bonding.
Apply Mass Spectrometry and NMR Spectroscopy for the identification and characterisation of chemical species.
Use the periodic table to predict trends in the chemical properties and reactivity of the elements.

Demonstrate practical skills needed to conduct chemical synthesis and chemical analysis, and be able to interpret and report results from observations and measurements to characterise compounds and materials.

title: MEDICINAL AND ORGANIC CHEMISTRY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the principles required for understanding how drugs interact with proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates or lipids to impart a biological effect. You will also explore the scientific endeavour required to take a lead compound through to a commercially available drug, gaining knowledge and experience in the strategies of drug discovery, design, synthesis and development.
learning_outcomes: Identify chemical features of drugs and devise strategies for the optimisation of their pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic properties.
Employ aromatic and heteroaromatic reactions for drug design and synthesis.
Use the major concepts and language of pharmaceutical, medicinal and organic chemistry correctly.
Interpret and report experimental results.
Illustrate the ways that drugs can interact with their biomolecular targets in order to understand structure-activity relationships.

title: GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF CHEMISTRY
syllabus_overview: General Principles of Chemistry is a cornerstone subject for students who have some previous knowledge or study in chemistry. The subject introduces and reinforces fundamental chemistry concepts, knowledge and skills that will enable you to apply chemical principles during their university study and future employment. You will encounter atomic and molecular structure, bonding, chemical reactions, organic chemistry, and physical chemistry including thermochemistry and equilibrium. .
learning_outcomes: Predict the outcome of types of chemical reactions and describe the influence of factors affecting the progress of chemical changes.
Employ mathematical tools to solve chemical problems.

Recognise chemical and physical properties of chemical elements, organic and inorganic compounds in order that substances can be categorised and their behaviour predicted in specified chemical environments.

Describe the individual properties of the three states of matter as well as how the different states interact with each other and explain how these properties are dependent on environmental conditions.
Use practical techniques and tools to observe and measure the outcomes of laboratory procedures to recognise connections between theoretical and practical phenomena.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF CHEMISTRY B
syllabus_overview: This subject will develop and expand your knowledge of key concepts and skills in organic and physical chemistry. The organic chemistry component has a strong focus on stereochemistry and reaction mechanisms. The physical chemistry component covers chemical kinetics, catalysis and their relationship with reaction mechanism, with a focus on applications in organic chemistry. Learning activities include lectures, tutorials, online learning activities, workshops and laboratory classes.
learning_outcomes: Determine experimental rate laws, infer reaction mechanisms, and assess how chemical reaction rates may be controlled.
Identify and describe key stereochemistry elements in organic compounds, and the changes to stereochemistry that occur during chemical reactions.
Demonstrate practical skills needed to conduct chemical synthesis, chemical analysis and be able to interpret and report the results of spectroscopic measurements.
Use reaction mechanisms to describe the important reactions of organic compounds.

title: ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY
syllabus_overview: Chemical analysis is widely used in forensic, pharmaceutical, and environmental science. In this subject you will learn about modern analytical chemistry skills, including the preparation and analysis of different types of real-world samples using a variety of instrumental techniques. In workshops and practical classes you will develop the ability to critically assess experimental results and judge their validity. The analytical techniques you will explore include electrochemistry, spectroscopy, chromatography, and atomic absorption and emission spectrometry.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and report results from observations and measurements accurately.
Assess the requirements for the collection, storage, and preparation of samples.
Interpret data from chemical analysis to account for major strengths and weaknesses of different analytical techniques.
Perform basic numerical calculations and apply statistical methods, including error analysis, to experimental results.
Explain appropriate application of chemical techniques and instrumental methods for chemical analysis

title: BIOPHARMACEUTICS
syllabus_overview: Drugs are used in a wide range of dosage forms and pharmacists need to understand the design and rationale behind available dosage forms. Also, in order to properly advise patients on the use of drugs it is necessary to understand the mechanisms by which the drugs are absorbed and interact in the body. Fundamental principles of biopharmaceutics are discussed with emphasis on the qualitative and quantitative description of factors which influence drug disposition. Drugs are used in a wide range of dosage forms and pharmacists need to understand the design and rationale behind these available dosage forms. We will investigate different types of formulation and how the ingredients in a formulation together with method of manufacture, can influence the bioavailability of a drug within the body.
learning_outcomes: Explain the function and properties of excipients and actives in common pharmaceutical formulations.
Evaluate the current advances in the biopharmaceutical industry.
Analyse how the use of pharmacokinetics can be used to predict drug disposition and assist in effective drug therapy.
Assess the effects of excipients and the type dosage form used on the bioavailability of a drug.

title: CHEMISTRY AND THE ENVIRONMENT
syllabus_overview: Understanding the sources, stores and activity of natural and anthropogenic chemicals is central to understanding our environment, including long term sustainability. Taking a molecular perspective, you will study concepts associated with energy and climate, chemicals in waters and sediments, and important analytical techniques such as separation science and atomic spectroscopy. In this subject you will gain experience conducting and interpreting laboratory experiments related to environmental chemistry.
learning_outcomes: Analyse laboratory findings with well supported interpretations using correctly referenced professional prose for experiments related to chemical analysis and analytical measurements of chemical species of environmental concern.

Demonstrate knowledge of scientific principles and chemical techniques related to the concepts of energy and fuels, chemicals in the environment, separation science and instrumental analysis for chemical species of environmental concern.

Integrate knowledge of the key concepts of stoichiometry, chemical reactions, structure and properties of chemicals, instrumental and analytical methods for chemical species of environmental concern..
Utilise professional laboratory skills associated with the use of chemicals and instrument methods for the measurement for chemical species of environmental concern.

title: ADVANCED CHEMISTRY LABORATORY
syllabus_overview: In this practical-based subject, you will build on your previous laboratory experience and develop enhanced experimental skills through the synthesis and characterisation of complex molecules, the acquisition and interpretation of advanced spectroscopic and physical data, and the investigation of chemical systems through computational techniques. You will have the opportunity to undertake an integrated and industry-focused laboratory program with the opportunity for industry visits to places such as the Victoria Police Forensics facility or a pharmaceutical manufacturing plant. You will also be introduced to research-based chemistry through integrated experiments. Throughout the subject there is a focus on skill development in a range of techniques utilised in a modern chemistry laboratory that are relevant to both industry and chemistry research, and has a global context.
learning_outcomes: Apply globally accepted professional integrity and safe laboratory practices when designing and performing experiments, collecting data and reporting results.
Demonstrate knowledge of principles and concepts of theoretical and computational chemistry.
Write coherent descriptions of chemical principles and report experimental and computational findings with well supported interpretations using correctly referenced professional prose.
Solve abstract, routine and real-world problems of chemical relevance by sourcing, collating and summarising trusted scientific information.

Apply appropriate mathematical, graphical and computational methods to acquire, manipulate, interpret and evaluate chemical data and summarise results using appropriate significant figures and internationally accepted units.
Research, design, and implement laboratory-based strategies to tackle complex scenarios as part of a team.

title: ADVANCED TOPICS IN CHEMISTRY
syllabus_overview: A deep understanding of the fundamental principles of chemistry across the breadth of the discipline is essential for anyone seeking an advanced position in industry or commencing a career in research. In Advanced Topics in Chemistry, you will study advanced aspects of chemistry from the core areas of inorganic, organic, physical, and analytical chemistry. You will learn how fundamental aspects of chemistry underpin the cutting edge of knowledge and research in a wide range of scientific disciplines and applications. Successful completion of the subject will equip you with the theoretical knowledge and understanding to progress into a higher degree by research or into a rewarding career in industry.
