Write concurrent programs using threads that are deadlock free.
Apply lambda functions in a program

title: NETWORK ENGINEERING FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students are introduced to the foundational concepts of computer networking. The subject covers the OSI reference model and its associated protocols to provide a layered understanding of network communication. Students will explore the lifecycle of a data packet across a network and learn the principles of IP addressing. The subject also includes hands-on experience with basic network device configuration and an introduction to static routing, enabling students to build and manage simple network topologies.
learning_outcomes: Describe the overall OSI model and how layers interact with adjacent layers in the model.
Apply appropriate network physical standards for different network scenarios.
Identify functions of each OSI layer and apply this knowledge to build a Network.
Describe TCP/IP based network protocol suite and compare with OSI model.
Describe the evolution of Local Area Network (LAN technology) with focus on Ethernet.

title: WIRELESS NETWORK AND SECURITY
syllabus_overview: Due to the ubiquitous nature of mobile and wireless technology in our daily lives and business operations, ensuring wireless security is becoming a top priority. This subject explores the security vulnerabilities in wireless networks and covers the fundamental concerns of confidentiality, integrity and availability. The following key areas will be covered: Wireless LAN Security - Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP), Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA), Authentication Servers (RADIUS), 802.11i security standard; Securing Ad-Hoc Networks - MAC layer misbehaviour, secure routing protocols, types of attacks and solutions, key management, broadcast authentication.
learning_outcomes: Apply suitable wireless network security architectures and settings for homes, enterprises and public environments
Create security risk assessment reports based on the identification and appraisal of various threats and attacks on wireless systems
Assess and evaluate potential and existing security risk levels and vulnerabilities in wireless systems
Apply techniques for addressing the impairments in wireless communication

title: USER INTERFACE DESIGN
syllabus_overview: User Interface (UI) Design focuses on creating interactive interfaces which are intuitive and easy to access and understand. This subject will introduce you to the main theories, methods and techniques that are applied to UI design and evaluation. Main topics include design thinking, user research analysis, iteration and prototyping, and user testing. Based on these UI theories and techniques, you will create mobile prototypes with wireframe tools and evaluate them with UI testing methods in practice classes and assignments.
learning_outcomes: Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to analyse and identify UI design issues based on UI design principles.
Apply wireframe tools to both low-fidelity and high-fidelity UI prototype design.
Conduct UI evaluations with cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation.
Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to use statistical methods to interpret and evaluate usability testing results.

title: SYSTEM ANALYSIS AND DESIGN
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to system analysis and design with Object-oriented (OO) modelling techniques for software system engineering. Major topics include introduction to software development process, requirements modelling, domain modelling, behavioural modelling, structural modelling and dynamic modelling. You will learn the use of Unified Modelling Language (UML) for the analysis and design phases of systems. You will gain the ability to apply knowledge of basic science and software engineering fundamentals to software systems analysis and design.
learning_outcomes: Document system analysis and designs using Unified Modelling Language (UML).
Analyse system requirements and model the system behaviour.
Apply standard techniques to gather system requirements effectively
Create conceptual and concrete models of systems with Object-oriented (OO) techniques.

title: DEEP LEARNING
syllabus_overview: Deep learning is currently the central machine learning method fueling the artificial intelligence revolution. In this subject you will learn how to apply deep learning algorithms to solve real-world computer vision and natural language processing problems. This subject does not assume you have previous machine learning experience, therefore it starts teaching deep learning at a very introductory level. You will learn how deep learning techniques can be applied to tasks such as image recognition, sentiment classification, machine translation, question and answering, speech synthesis, etc. The practical skills taught in this subject will allow you to build production level deep learning software that can scale out to millions of users. You will be introduced to the popular deep learning programming framework of Pytorch and popular model architectures such as convolutional, recurrent and transformer neural networks.
learning_outcomes: Given a real-world problem where labels are scarce, investigate different deep-learning approaches to tackle this problem. Approaches include transfer learning, semi-supervised learning, unsupervised pre-training, etc.
Analyse the machine learning requirements of a business and then propose deployment and maintenance strategies for deep learning production systems in the cloud.
Analyse a given industry problem and then investigate which deep learning algorithm best solves the problem.
Analyse the advantages and disadvantages of using traditional machine learning algorithms versus deep learning algorithms for solving industry problems.
Write PyTorch code to implement deep learning algorithms to solve computer vision and natural language processing problems.

title: DATA SECURITY AND INFORMATION ASSURANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject will cover basic aspects of information and data security including integrity models, message authentication, authentication tools, access controls and cryptography. Topics will focus on data assurance and prevention methods including data integrity methods. This subject also covers basic cyber-attack defences such as firewalls.
learning_outcomes: Analyse security risks and apply appropriate technical and security controls to protect organisational information systems
Evaluate security policies, ethical practices, and data maintenance methods to ensure compliance, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational information.
Describe key concepts of data security and information assurance, including the CIA triad, information assets, and common organisational security challenges.
Identify and analyse threats, vulnerabilities, and risks affecting organisational information systems.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PENETRATION TESTING
syllabus_overview: Penetration testing encompasses the evaluation of organizational vulnerabilities by conducting thorough security testing. This subject provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles and procedures involved in system penetration testing and the ethical and legal obligations. It explores the utilization of popular software tools employed during penetration testing exercises. Through this course, students will acquire knowledge about different types of penetration testing and their respective phases, as well as gain expertise in interpreting results obtained from commonly utilized penetration testing tools. Additionally, students will recognize the significant value of penetration testing for businesses and organizations and will develop the skills to effectively report on and enhance an organization's security resilience using testing outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Apply penetration testing methodologies and techniques.
Identify and exploit common security vulnerabilities and recommend security controls.
Review and compare different concepts of penetration testing
Develop and produce client reports, explaining key findings to diverse audiences.

title: ADVANCED NETWORK ENGINEERING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn advanced topics in local and wide area networks. The topics include the design and implementation of Virtual LAN (VLAN) using Virtual Trunk Protocols (VTP), inter-VLAN routing using routing protocols learned in CSE3INE and wide-area networking protocols. Advanced networking topics such as Etherchannel, IP flow, SNMP and RMON will be introduced in a top-down fashion.
learning_outcomes: Analyse LAN operation protocols and LAN management protocols with understanding of LAN optimization
Analyse configurations of Ethernet ports in switching operations
Design and implement VLANs using Virtual Trunking Protocols (VTP)
Design and implement VLANs using Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)
Construct 3-layer hierarchical network design models

title: BLOCKCHAIN AND CRYPTOCURRENCIES
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the principles and processes involved in blockchain technologies. The blockchain offers a way to secure transactions online between two parties, when there is no trusted intermediary available. A common use is in financial transactions without a bank as an intermediary, such as bitcoins and other cryptocurrencies. This subject covers the fundamentals of blockchain technology, including how the blockchain works, and how it is applied to modern digital transactions, including cryptocurrencies and smart contracts.
learning_outcomes: Explain different types of security measures in distributed ledgers to minimise risk.
Analyse different usecases and building blocks of blockchain and cryptocurrencies.
Demonstrate the use of blockchains and different cryptocurrencies to create a set of recommendations for appropriate usage by business and industry.
Assess the commercial and legal environments needed for cryptocurrency start-ups to ensure business success.

title: BIG DATA MANAGEMENT ON THE CLOUD
syllabus_overview: Companies are acquiring massive amounts of data and providing Internet-based service to millions of people. This is extremely challenging due to the large scale of data involved and the huge number of concurrent requests by users. This subject will cover the current state-of-the-art technologies for analysing huge amounts of data and responding to millions of user requests within one second. Currently the most cost-efficient way of achieving the above aim is to use large-scale cloud-based services offered by vendors such as Amazon, Google, IBM, Microsoft, etc. You will have the opportunity to learn how to use the cloud services provided by Amazon Web Services to meet the big data needs of businesses. The subject will also cover how to program the world’s most popular Big Data analytics framework called Hadoop with a focus on Map Reduce, Hive and Apache Spark. This subject will also cover the following topics: cloud architectures, parallel database systems, key value stores, transaction support in the cloud, virtualization, and multi-tenant database systems.
learning_outcomes: Apply your knowledge of Amazon Web Services to design a cloud-based solution for a given application scenario.
Analyse the performance benefits of contrasting No SQL stores.
Implement fundamental cloud-based services using Amazon Web Service interfaces.
Solve big data analytics problems by implementing solutions using the Hadoop ecosystem.
Analyse the internals of the Map Reduce Framework.

title: CAPSTONE PROJECT
syllabus_overview: This subject enables you to develop your skills to implement a small or medium-sized project in a team. You will address a real-life problem in software engineering or cybersecurity. The subject covers the skills to manage, implement and report on the delivery of a substantive project to appropriate stakeholders. You will make milestone presentations with your team. You MUST complete both CSE3PM and CSE3CAP in two consecutive semesters.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced project management skills to the implementation phases of a substantive development project
Report project development outcomes to technical and non-technical audiences and reflect on feedback
Construct professional system documentation and advanced technical reports to meet the requirements of software or cybersecurity industry standards
Devise and implement industry standard technical solutions in software or cybersecurity practices

title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER FORENSICS
syllabus_overview: This subject considers the procedures related to digital forensic investigation in computing and networking scenarios. Students critically appraise the key concepts associated with data hiding, evidence collection and validation and traffic analysis required to perform forensic analysis in a digital environment. Students learn the importance of legal considerations in the documentation of forensic evidence. Case studies are incorporated for students to apply practical forensic tools.
learning_outcomes: Apply investigative procedures to perform forensic Investigations of different types of digital systems
Investigate and explain different phases of digital forensic process
Analyse digital evidence with physical forensic evidence tools and techniques
Summarise ethical and legal considerations in the documentation of forensic evidence

title: DATABASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: This subject covers important concepts of database management systems and recent developments in the area. How various database technologies are utilised to support the need of modern database systems. Several well known RDBMS and non-RDBMS platforms will be observed. Advanced application and implementation of database management systems, such as data analytic queries, non-relational databases and complex data types will be covered as well. Case studies using real industry-based sample dataset and problems will enrich students' experiences. Future trends of database management systems will also be studied and discussed to broaden students' horizon to deal with future advancement in the area.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement a NoSQL database for non-relational data management
Utilise advanced data types to create a database and perform data retrieval queries
Create and evaluate complex SQL queries for efficient data retrieval and optimization
Explain the key concepts of database management system architecture

title: COMPUTATIONAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DATA ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: Quantitative analysis plays an important role in business analytics and knowledge engineering, thus it is very useful to develop computing skills for data regression and classification. This subject covers some fundamentals of computational intelligence techniques, including classical learning and inference systems, neural networks, and reinforcement learning systems. The subject is designed with a focus on solving forecasting problems using learning and inference systems, where learning mechanisms and learning rule extraction from numerical data are addressed. Some advanced learning techniques for training neural networks will also be highlighted. In labs and assignments, students will work with real-world datasets for prediction using a learning system, which helps to consolidate the knowledge taught in the lectures and gain a hands-on experience on computational intelligence applications in practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the learning technology, i.e., intelligent systems and the links between CIS and knowledge engineering.
Implement a neural network system for data forecasting.
Explain the major components and issues in developing computational intelligence systems, such as regression and classification systems using machine learning and neural networks.
Identify the technologies and applications of computational intelligence systems (CIS).

title: EMERGING TOPICS IN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: The subject focuses on one or more topics which are not covered in depth elsewhere in the curriculum and which are becoming important in the IT discipline. Recent examples of such topics include: data mining, human-computer interaction, internet information systems and mobile computing platforms. Students will explore the topics, surveying the literature, practice and application in the area. Each student will typically also research one aspect in depth, presenting that to others in the subject.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse a new Information technology area or issue.
Prepare and deliver a presentation to a professional standard, the results of an assigned research topic.
Conduct a literature survey of an emerging Information Technology.
Present a written report or paper detailing the results of assigned work or conducted research.
Identify appropriate methodology for investigation of emerging Information Technology.

title: CLOUD-BASED WEB APPLICATION
syllabus_overview: Creating websites that scale to serve hundreds of millions of users with acceptable response times is challenging. The main focus of this subject is on cloud computing concepts and tools needed to make websites scalable. This subject builds on students' prior experience with programming and information technology systems. The subject will cover topics in the cloud computing concept and technologies, such as cloud repository, virtualisation, the framework for frontend and backend development, API, web server storage, and the management of application development (CI/CD)
learning_outcomes: Evaluate JavaScript web front end designs for given web application specifications.
Build and deploy web applications using cloud infrastructure and web services
Compare and critique appropriate storage technologies for website designs
Design and build backend web servers to meet web application requirements
Use modern software engineering tools to build and deploy robust code for scalable websites

title: FRONTIERS IN NETWORK TECHNOLOGIES
syllabus_overview: This subject will strengthen and reinforce your knowledge of the design, development and deployment of network infrastructure, including OSI and TCP/IP layering architecture, routing protocols, LANs, WLANs and VLANS; network management; network security through ACLs, firewalls; and network virtualization and automation. Labs are designed carefully to broaden your understanding of how to apply theoretical concepts in designing a large-scale network. The content of this subject prepares you for Cisco Academy certification. This subject assesses competency and only pass or fail grades are awarded.
learning_outcomes: Describe the fundamental design of Network visualization by using Network automation
Design, develop and deploy networks using IPv4 and IPv6 addressing schemes.
Implement secure routing protocols to integrate a designed campus network with Internet.
Design Local Area Network (LAN) and Wide Area Network (WAN) to user specifications including VLAN when appropriate.

title: INDUSTRY BASED LEARNING A
syllabus_overview: Students undertake a 20-week full-time or equivalent industry based learning program. A member of the academic staff acting in the capacity of industry based learning coordinator liaises with the placement provider to formulate and structure a program of learning for each student. This program is normally project based, with day-to-day supervision by the placement provider. Progress is monitored at regular intervals.
learning_outcomes: Identify, select and utilise the appropriate tools, techniques, and skills acquired throughout the course in a professional work environment.
Gain practical experience and learn new IT skills through on the job training.
Demonstrate high level of professionalism and leadership skills.
Communicate effectively and professionally through documentation and presentations.

title: INDUSTRY EXPERIENCE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject students are provided with the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge learnt in other subjects of the course and to gain practical knowledge in the Information Technology professions. The student will undertake a 13 week full-time work program with an external organisation, which has been approved as an industry employer by the Subject and Course co-ordinators. The work to be undertaken by the student must be in a recognised Information Technology area and provide an appropriate learning environment. The employer will nominate a workplace supervisor who will oversee the student's work program and liaise with the Subject co-ordinator.
learning_outcomes: Gain practical experience and learn new IT skills through on the job training.
Communicate effectively and professionally through documentation and presentations.
Identify, select and utilise the appropriate tools, techniques, and skills acquired throughout the course in a professional work environment.
Demonstrate professional conduct, appropriate workplace behaviour, of a work ready IT professional.

title: INDUSTRY BASED LEARNING B
syllabus_overview: Students undertake a 20-week full-time or equivalent industry based learning program. A member of the academic staff acting in the capacity of industry based learning coordinator liaises with the placement provider to formulate and structure a program of learning for each student. This program is normally project based, with day-to-day supervision by the placement provider. Progress is monitored at regular intervals.
learning_outcomes: Gain practical experience and learn new IT skills through on the job training.
Demonstrate high level of professionalism and leadership skills.
Identify, select and utilise the appropriate tools, techniques, and skills acquired throughout the course in a professional work environment.
Communicate effectively and professionally through documentation and presentations.

title: INDUSTRY BASED LEARNING A
syllabus_overview: You are to undertake a 12 x 20hr per week or equivalent industry based learning program. A member of the academic staff acting in the capacity of industry based learning coordinator liaises with the placement provider to formulate and structure a program of learning for each student. This program is normally project based, with day-to-day supervision by the placement provider. Progress is monitored at regular intervals.
learning_outcomes: Describe, compare, comment, and justify learned skills alignment with industry requirement.
Applying learned skills to industry, and describe, analyse and evaluate application of such skills to industry.
Apply, describe and justify subject and course knowledge in relation to industry skills requirement.

title: INDUSTRY BASED LEARNING B
syllabus_overview: Students undertake a 12-week x 20hr per week or equivalent industry based learning program. A member of the academic staff acting in the capacity of industry based learning coordinator liaises with the placement provider to formulate and structure a program of learning for each student. This program is normally project based, with day-to-day supervision by the placement provider. Progress is monitored at regular intervals.
learning_outcomes: Apply, describe and justify subject and course knowledge in relation to industry skills requirement.
Applying learned skills to industry, and describe, analyse and evaluate application of such skills to industry.
Describe, compare, comment, and justify learned skills alignment with industry requirement.

title: INTERMEDIATE NETWORK ENGINEERING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will explore the structure and function of routers and examine key network routing concepts. The subject covers both static and dynamic routing, focusing on core protocols such as distance vector ,link state and, path vector ). Students will gain hands-on experience in configuring routers, building and interpreting routing tables, and evaluating the performance of these protocols across diverse network environments.
learning_outcomes: Broadly explain the scope of the TCP and UDP protocols.
Recognize the strengths and weaknesses of routing protocols.
Describe and evaluate IPng addressing scheme and subnetting and their issues
Implement multiprotocol network.
Implement distance vector and link state routing protocols.

title: NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
syllabus_overview: Natural language processing (NLP) is broadly concerned with the interactions between computer and natural (i.e. human) languages; more particularly, it is concerned with the question of how to program computers to process and analyse large amounts of natural language data. This subject covers NLP fundamentals and computerized models for real-world applications such as text categorisation, language modelling and recognition, speech recognition and synthesis, etc. You will develop and apply practical skills learned on NLP projects.
learning_outcomes: Critique NLP methods for speech recognition and synthesis
Apply NLP methods for text sentiment analysis and topic modelling
Apply NLP methods for language modelling and entity recognition
Clearly articulate NLP techniques and their applicability in feature extraction and text data understanding
Implement an NLP project and evaluate the results

title: MOBILE APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject is an introduction to mobile application development, including programming paradigms, models, technologies and platforms. The unique considerations for programming with mobile devices will be studied, including application architectures, mobile user interface issues, context-aware computing, the use of mobile sensing, middleware, mobile data management, and programming with wireless connections. You will develop a range of mobile applications compatible with smartphones tablets of varying sizes. You will learn about wearables and develop cross-platform applications in your major programming assignment.
learning_outcomes: Utilize and implement software development methodologies to build and enhance modern mobile applications in teams
Analyse the principles underlying mobile applications and mobile computing by comparing them to applications on different platforms
Design and construct applications based on the notion of context-aware computing, including using sensors and location services.
Investigate mobile user interface abstractions and mobile usability issues, design and program mobile applications for mobile devices on at least one platform

title: NETWORK SYSTEMS AND WEB SECURITY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore current and emerging topics in Network Systems and Web Security. Beginning with an analysis of security attacks on system services and a discussion of both traditional and modern security mechanisms, the subject expands to cover security paradigms across various domains. The subject topics include system security, network security, web security, cloud security, and innovative approaches in cybersecurity.
learning_outcomes: Apply cryptographic algorithms, including encryption methods, hash functions, digital signatures, and key exchange protocols, to secure systems, networks and clouds.
Analyse systems and networks for vulnerabilities and security flaws, incorporating modern tools and techniques for comprehensive analysis.
Identify and investigate ethical and legal considerations relevant to information privacy and security issues.
Examine and apply key security tools and protocols, such as Kerberos, PGP, IPSec, SSL/TLS, and emerging frameworks.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: Entrepreneurship is an essential element of today’s society. This subject will outline the basic principles of Entrepreneurship. It will examine the steps required in developing an idea into a business and will explore the tools and necessary insights to make a successful venture. You will interpret and apply theory to case studies. Guest speakers will present and discuss start-up issues, pitfalls, and the ingredients for success. You will also develop professional skills related to ethical and moral decision making, and evaluate the social implications of entrepreneurship in the broader global context.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate diverse funding options for supporting entrepreneurial endeavors while considering the essential development steps
Critically analyse IT business ventures based on social, legal and ethical issues and examine the responsibilities of IT professionals to employers, clients, and society as part of a team
Apply ethical theory to analyse ethical dilemmas in IT and business through debate.

Reflect on personal viewpoints related to managing relationships and individual entrepreneurial capacity, effectively developing and presenting personal and professional reflections to become career-ready

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Project management is the process of leading the work of a team to achieve specified goals and outcomes in a specified time. This subject provides necessary skills and techniques to manage small or medium-sized information technology projects, with strong focus on the analytical side of project management, referring to scheduling, cost, and resource management, as well as the 'people' and client management issues that must be dealt with in order to ensure successful projects. In the subject you will work in a team to cover the skills required to assess, identify and manage risks to projects, to prepare realistic plans and appropriate documentation, track activities across project schedules and report appropriately to stakeholders. Your team's project will be assessed at different stages. You MUST complete both CSE3PM and CSE3CAP in two consecutive semesters.
learning_outcomes: Develop professional project design documentation to meet the requirements of software or cybersecurity industry standards.
Critically appraise, analyse, refine and document system requirements to solve real-time problems in software or cybersecurity systems.
Develop an IT project management framework that integrates security analysis and risk mitigation throughout the project's lifecycle.
Prepare effective and collaborative project team meetings through application of team dynamics knowledge.

title: SOFTWARE MEASUREMENT AND TESTING
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a modern view on how to assess, evaluate and measure software and systems quality. In this subject, you will gain hands-on, practical experience with planning, strategising, designing, measuring and assessing software and systems quality. Topics include manual and automated testing using industry-recognised techniques and frameworks, performance testing, metrics for measuring test progress and software quality and complexity, and guidance on how international standards can be utilised to enhance software quality. The industry-based roles, processes and practices associated with software testing and measurement are taken as models to describe and demonstrate the types of tasks and practices undertaken by professionals within this sector of the IT industry.
learning_outcomes: Analyse, interpret and apply quality metrics to investigate program quality and complexity and test status
Design and execute manual and automated test cases, with the support of structured test design techniques and tools
Analyse software and systems requirements to identify requirement issues, quality risks, test cases, and inputs to test plans and strategies
Relate the multiple industry-based roles and processes involved in modern software testing across the fundamental software testing process, and within the software development life cycle

title: PROFESSIONAL SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: Throughout your studies to date, you’ve learned how to program a computer. You should already be very familiar with the basic building blocks of computer programs: variables, loops, branching structures, functions, and the like. This subject will focus on tools and techniques for software development , the process of designing, delivering, and maintaining high-quality software. You will develop substantially complex software using design patterns in the C++ programming language, and you will learn about the realities of software development from industry experts.
learning_outcomes: Engineer object-oriented software using design patterns.
Analyse emerging trends in software development and forecast how they will evolve.
Critique design patterns and their uses in object-oriented software design.
Implement software using design patterns in the C++ programming language.

title: IMAGE PROCESSING
syllabus_overview: This subject covers both fundamentals of image processing as well as computing techniques with applications in many cutting-edge domains such as image recognition, object detection and segmentation, image registration and retrieval. Design issues on image recognition will be addressed, which contain eigenface technology, image feature extraction, similarity measurement, and performance evaluation. Practice on image recognition will be offered in Labs.
learning_outcomes: Implement object detection models for real-time image recogination
Write python code to implement an image classification task and address design issues
Evaluate the performance and robustness of image processing techniques for real world applications
Analyze a real-world problem, and investigate different image processing techniques for classification, object detection, segmentation, and retrieval.

title: NETWORK ENGINEERING FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: This subject offers an in-depth study of modern computer networking, emphasising analytical understanding and application in complex environments. It extends foundational knowledge by critically examining the OSI reference model and major protocol families, highlighting their role in enabling scalable and interoperable communication. Students will examine how data moves across different network environments, exploring core IPv4 (Internet Protocol) addressing, basic subnetting, and routing concepts. Hands -on activities include configuring, testing, and troubleshooting network devices, as well as applying static routing to support simple network layouts.
learning_outcomes: Employ professional skills to debug and troubleshoot errors in different LAN sizes using different methodologies.
Generate a documentation for different computer networks by the application of well-developed knowledge and skill
Analyse and compare the operation and performance of various network protocols
Design appropriate addressing schemes to solve problems across different network sizes using different approaches
Construct, design and implement different Local Area Networks (LAN) sizes
Configure and test state-of-the-art industry networking devices that meet network requirements and achieve optimal performance

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: Semester 1/Term 2: subject description: The field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) engages computers for reasoning and decision-making. In this subject, you will be introduced to the fundamental concepts and different applications of AI. The main topics include searching, knowledge representation and reasoning, expert system design and development, and responsible AI principles and applications. Practice in the design and development of AI models for real world problems will be offered in laboratory classes. (Includes subject intended learning outcomes 1-4) Semester 2/Term 4: subject description: This subject gives you an introduction to AI and how AI transforms business and society. You will learn principal AI concepts, explore a variety of AI techniques for solving different types of problems, and examine ethical issues and concerns associated with AI. Upon completion of the subject, you will be equipped to recognise, select, and apply existing AI methods in both computer science and non-computer science fields that engage with AI technologies. (Includes subject intended learning outcomes 5-8)
learning_outcomes: Semester 2/Term 4 - Assess ethical, social, and technical implications of AI systems to inform responsible decision-making.
Semester 1/Term 2 - Analyse and design basic machine learning algorithms to model a practical case.
Semester 2/Term 4 - Evaluate the suitability of different AI approaches for real-world problems and justify their selection in practical scenarios.
Semester 2/Term 4 - Apply AI approaches to solve business or technology challenges, considering constraints and objectives.
Semester 1/Term 2 - Represent knowledge using semantic networks, scripts, frames and logic-based mechanisms and write simple Prolog programs to enable automated reasoning.
Semester 1/Term 2 - Construct simple expert systems to solve a real-world problem.
Semester 1/Term 2 - Devise appropriate representations for state space search and game playing to solve practical problems.
Semester 2/Term 4 - Critically interpret and explain the core concepts of artificial intelligence and evaluate how common AI models are designed to operate and generate outputs in varied contexts.

title: HUMAN COMPUTER INTERACTION
syllabus_overview: Human-computer Interaction (HCI) refers to the design and use of computer technology, focusing on the interfaces between users and computer systems. The goal of HCI is to create user-friendly computer systems that are also functional. In this subject, students will be introduced to principles, techniques, and open areas of development in HCI. Main topics include ergonomic aspects, human perception, interface style, interface design guidelines, usability testing, current commercial offerings, existing and evolving standards.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and compare interfaces with respect to their usability and other desirable properties.
Design quantitative and qualitative tests to evaluate a given interface.
Justify the principles of HCI and their importance
Apply the user-centered design framework to HCI design.

title: CYBER SECURITY PRINCIPLES
syllabus_overview: In the Internet era, industries and organisations need to be aware of, and be prepared to defend against threats and attacks. Stakeholders should be familiar with the basic principles and best practices of cyber security to better protect their businesses. In this subject, the principles, the state of the art, and strategies for the future of cyber security is explored thoroughly. The topics will focus on information security, ethical and legal practices, mitigating cyber vulnerabilities, and the process of incident response and analysis. The outline of the subject is targeted at ensuring the privacy, reliability, confidentiality and integrity of information systems. Cyber security is a very broad discipline, and therefore, this subject is only intended to cover the basics of the recent state of the art and leading cyber security topics.
learning_outcomes: Analyse approaches to security networks, firewalls, intrusion detection systems and intrusion prevention systems
Appraise key terms and concepts in cyber security, cyber law, intellectual property and cyber crime
Formulate approaches for incident analysis, risk management in cyber space and incident response
Analyse various software design practices and principles of web security

title: DATABASE FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: This subject starts with an overview of the architecture and management of database systems, and a discussion of different existing database models. The main focus includes relational database analysis, design, and implementation. The students learn: relational algebra as the formal foundation of relational databases; relational conceptual design using an entity-relationship diagram; relational logical database design; security and integrity; and SQL implementation of relational database queries. Students will also learn advanced normalization theory and the techniques to remove data anomalies and redundancies. In this subject, students are required to design a database application that meets the needs of a system requirement specification, and to implement the system using a commercial standard database system such as ORACLE.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate database design in terms of data anomalies and redundancies by applying the appropriate normalization techniques.
Design a relational database using an ER or EER diagram, and use a transformation process to change the ER or EER diagram to a relational database design
Evaluate the possible risks and ethical and social considerations relevant to designed systems.
Explain the underlying model of relational database operations using relational algebra.
Implement database systems using SQL and advanced PL/SQL including stored procedures and triggers.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the fundamentals of software design and development using the Python programming language. It focuses on solving practical problems through algorithm design, program structure, and core programming concepts such as conditionals, loops, functions, and data structures. Students will learn to analyse problems, design solutions, and implement code, while also exploring debugging, error handling, and modular programming. The subject introduces basic secure coding practices and highlights Python’s strengths in rapid prototyping and software development. Learning is supported through workbook exercises, lab-based tasks, and assessments that apply concepts to real-world scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Utilise basic data structures such as lists and dictionaries to handle batch data processing, ensuring efficiency and maintainability in problem-solving
Develop and implement Python programs using fundamental programming techniques, including expressions, control structures, functions, and objects, to solve computational problems effectively
Analyse and design algorithmic solutions for data processing problems by identifying relevant data and selecting appropriate programming constructs such as sequence, selection, and iteration
Apply secure and maintainable coding practices by writing well-structured Python programs that incorporate modular design, error handling, and secure programming principles.

title: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn computer system organization and its associated topics. It covers the hardware components of the computer, data storage and retrieval, and introduces system software, computer networks, data communications, the Internet, operating systems, file management systems and security. You will also be introduced to information systems and application software packages.
learning_outcomes: Design and construct basic web pages using HTML and style sheets based on specific requirements.
Critically examine simple problems and develop spreadsheets to model these problems.
Differentiate between main types of computer networks and explain the purpose of major network components including any advantages and disadvantages of different data communication media.
Identify and critically evaluate functions of the main hardware components of computers.
Analyse and evaluate the requirements and functionality of different types of software.
Develop and interpret simple database tables, queries and reports based on specific requirements.

title: THESIS A
syllabus_overview: Students undertake research, across both CSE5001 and CSE5TSB, that takes the equivalent of eight or nine months of continuous work under the supervision of a member of staff. In the first semester, a literature review is written up and submitted as a hurdle requirement for the subject. A list of prospective thesis topics is available from the Department of Computer Science and Information Technology.
learning_outcomes: Appraise problems relevant to the field of CS/IT
Develop a research plan to solve a complex CS/IT problem through literature analysis.
Critically review the relevant literature and assess its quality and relevance to the field of CS/IT
Effectively communicate your research proposal to the relevant stakeholders
Develop a literature review and research proposal using a suitable academic style

title: WIRELESS NETWORK ENGINEERING
syllabus_overview: Due to the ubiquitous nature of mobile and wireless technology in our daily lives and business operations, ensuring wireless security is becoming a top priority. This subject explores the security vulnerabilities in wireless networks and covers the fundamental concerns of confidentiality, integrity and availability. The following key areas will be covered: Wireless LAN Security - Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP), Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA), Authentication Servers (RADIUS), 802.11i security standard; Securing Ad-Hoc Networks - MAC layer misbehaviour, secure routing protocols, types of attacks and solutions, key management, broadcast authentication.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate the techniques for addressing the impairments in wireless communication.
Produce security risk assessment reports based on the identification and appraisal of various threats and attacks on wireless systems.
Critically analyse different wireless network security architectures and apply suitable settings for home, enterprises and public environments.
Assess and evaluate potential and existing security risk levels and vulnerabilities in wireless systems

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this subject is to outline the basic principles of Entrepreneurship. It will examine the steps required in developing an idea into a business and will explore the tools and necessary insights to make a successful venture. The subject will involve theory, case studies and guest speakers on start-up issues, pitfalls, and ingredients for success. Students will also develop professional skills related to ethical and moral decision making and evaluate the social implications of their work and the broader global context. The subject requires active participation in group discussions and activities.
learning_outcomes: Write, express and present a business plan that will be ready for venture capitalist review by collaborating in a team
Examine various types of resources to develop and finance an entrepreneurial venture.

Create a personal ethical framework for IT practice that incorporates awareness of cultural and global issues and apply ethical theory to analyze ethical dilemmas in IT and business using a comprehensive approach.

Reflect on personal viewpoints related to managing relationships and individual entrepreneurial capacity, effectively developing and presenting personal and professional reflections to become career-ready.

title: CLOUD-BASE WEB APPLICATION
syllabus_overview: Creating websites that scale to serve hundreds of millions of users with acceptable response times is challenging. The main focus of this subject is on cloud computing concepts and tools needed to make websites scalable. This subject builds on students' prior experience with programming and information technology systems. The subject will cover topics in cloud computing and technologies, such as cloud repositories, virtualisation, the framework for frontend and backend development, API, web server storage, and the management of application development (CI/CD). This subject will also cover the fundamentals of cloud computing platforms and their features.
learning_outcomes: Design and build a stateless web server based on cloud technologies
Investigate storage technologies to determine optimal choice for a web site.
Design and Develop web applications using JavaScript
Use modern software engineering tools to build and deploy robust code for scalable web sites.
Design and customize backend Web applications based on user requirements

title: MOBILE APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject is an introduction to mobile application development, including programming paradigms, models, technologies and platforms. The unique considerations for programming with mobile devices will be studied, including application architectures, mobile user interface issues, context-aware computing, the use of mobile sensing, middleware, mobile data management, and programming with wireless connections. You will develop a range of mobile applications compatiable with smartphones and tablets of varying sizes. You will learn about wearables and develop cross-platform applications in your major programming assignment.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate, design and program mobile applications for mobile devices, including interface abstractions and usability issues
Apply suitable software development methodologies to collaboratively design, build, and enhance modern mobile applications, demonstrating effective teamwork and project management skills.
Design and implement applications based on context-aware computing and artificial intelligence.
Compare applications on different platforms

title: PROFESSIONAL SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: Throughout your studies to date, you’ve learned how to program a computer. You should already be very familiar with the basic building blocks of computer programs: variables, loops, branching structures, functions, and the like. This subject will focus on tools and techniques for software development , the process of designing, delivering, and maintaining high-quality software. You will develop substantially complex software using design patterns in the C++ programming language, and you will learn about the realities of software development from industry experts.
learning_outcomes: Analyse emerging trends in software development and forecast how they will evolve.
Implement software using design patterns in the C++ programming language.
Critique design patterns and their uses in object-oriented software design
Implement object-oriented software using design patterns

title: SOFTWARE MEASUREMENT AND TESTING
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a modern view on how to assess, evaluate and measure software and systems quality. In this subject, you will gain hands-on, practical experience with planning, strategising, designing, measuring and assessing software and systems quality. Topics include manual and automated testing using industry-recognised techniques and frameworks, performance testing, metrics for measuring test progress and software quality and complexity, and guidance on how international standards can be utilised to enhance software quality. The industry-based roles, processes and practices associated with software testing and measurement are taken as models to describe and demonstrate the types of tasks and practices undertaken by professionals within this sector of the IT industry.
learning_outcomes: Analyse software and systems requirements to identify, compare and contrast requirement issues, quality risks, test cases, and inputs to test plans and strategies
Analyse, apply and evaluate the benefits of quality metrics, to drive investigation and evaluation of program quality and complexity and test status
Design, execute and evaluate the outcomes of manual and automated testing, evaluating the benefits and shortcomings of test design techniques and tools

Compare and contrast the multiple industry-based roles and processes involved in modern software testing across the fundamental software testing process, and within the software development life cycle

title: INSIDE THE MIND OF A HACKER
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the motivations, mindset and techniques used by hackers. Although their activities are illicit and illegal, hackers have a finely attuned understanding of computer networks and systems and how users/customers behave in online environments. If nothing else, they have developed new - albeit illegal and unethical business models that exploit vulnerabilities in computer networks and systems. By looking at systems and practices through the eyes of a hacker, you can better identify weaknesses, emerging threats and develop more effective defences.
learning_outcomes: Recommend processes and practices to reduce the likelihood of data breaches
Deconstruct and critically analyze the profit models, value chain, and standard business security practices from the viewpoint of a hacker.
Critically analyse the various tactics that hackers use in breaching communication networks.
Critically analyse typologies of hackers, their mindsets and the motivations behind hacking.

title: SECURE PROGRAMMING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the ideals and practices of secure programming. Students begin by learning secure software concepts and requirements. Students will then learn a procedural language (Python - Anaconda Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab), including the Python compiler and interpreter, functions, control structures (branching and looping), references and arrays, structures, and file I/O. Students then learn to identify and analyse common coding practices that lead to security vulnerabilities, such as buffer overflows, SQL injection and Cross Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Students will return to coding, learning to use secure coding techniques and strategies to avoid security vulnerabilities. Finally, students will be introduced with secure software testing and some recent topics in secure software development.
learning_outcomes: Create source codes to avoid security vulnerabilities

Construct fit for purpose solutions to programming problems using functions and control structures, and accurately transform functions and control structures into Python code to produce a working program securely
Critically review the basic concepts of secure software testing and be able to formulate a test plan
Evaluate security vulnerabilities in Python and other languages, including web applications
Critically review the basic concepts and requirements of secure software development

title: RESEARCH METHODS AND INNOVATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about essential research methods that are used in computer science and information technology domains. You will learn about information collection and analysis techniques suitable for research and industry settings, quantitative and qualitative evaluation metrics and ethics, and academic written and oral scientific presentation skills. Upon completion, you will be able to plan, develop, and effectively communicate research proposals and ideas of innovation to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
learning_outcomes: Appropriately apply ethical issues and design principles to conduct research.
Plan a research project and evaluate complex ideas and concepts
Communicate research ideas and proposals to specialist and non-specialist audiences effectively in both oral and written form.
Apply knowledge and skills to new situations with creativity and initiative
Retrieve, critique and analyse existing literature on research and practical projects

title: SERVICENOW APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: As one of the world’s largest and most popular digital workflow management platforms, there is high demand for people with ServiceNow expertise. Designed and offered in partnership with ServiceNow, this subject will prepare you to sit for two valuable industry certifications, the ServiceNow Certified System Administrator and Certified Application Developer. You will learn the fundamentals of creating applications within the ServiceNow platform, including user-access rights, process automation, data integration and pre-deployment application validation. You will also be introduced to advanced scripting concepts to be implemented in the development of a ServiceNow application. On successful completion of this course, you will receive vouchers which allow you to take the ServiceNow Certified System Administrator and Certified Application Developer exams.
learning_outcomes: Explain the design decisions and usage of the developed application to a Certified ServiceNow Application Developer.
Evaluate the database structure of ServiceNow and hence design compatible tables and forms with suitable access controls.
Develop and employ strategies by collaborating in a team to design and create a ServiceNow application.
Effectively assess and evaluate the ServiceNow platform and identify the process of automation, data integration and validation.
Design and automate advanced tasks using scripting and Flow Designer.

title: ALGORITHMS AND DATA STRUCTURES (PG)
syllabus_overview: This subject covers a range of important algorithms and data structures. Data structures for implementing containers are covered and include linear structures, tree structures and hash tables. Algorithms for insertion and deletion of elements, and algorithms for searching and sorting on these structures are covered where appropriate. Graphs and graph algorithms are also covered. You will learn the construction and workings of the data structures and algorithms covered. They will learn to analyse the effectiveness of each data structure and algorithm for specific problems and categories of problems. You will also implement in programs a wide range of the structures and algorithms covered.
learning_outcomes: Explain the overall objectives of the field of Algorithms and Data Structures, and the theoretical and experimental techniques for evaluating algorithms and data structures.
Analyse a range of data structures and searching and sorting algorithms in terms of time or space complexity.
Analyse a problem, design a solution, implement it in Java, and evaluate its performance using multiple measures.
Implement a range of data structures and searching and sorting algorithms in Java, whose programs are of high quality in terms of coding style and comments.
Distinguish a range of data structures and searching and sorting algorithms in terms of their mechanism, strengths, weaknesses, and conditions appropriate for the related applications.

title: AI AND TECH INNOVATION FRONTIER
syllabus_overview: This subject equips students with the mindset, skills, and practical tools needed to identify opportunities, validate ideas, and develop entrepreneurial responses to complex real-world challenges. Positioned at the intersection of innovation, entrepreneurship, and emerging technology, the subject introduces students to the role of AI-enabled tools in accelerating the innovation process, including opportunity discovery, customer insight generation, ideation, prototyping, market validation, and venture communication. While the subject does not teach AI techniques or technical AI development, it enables students to critically and responsibly use contemporary AI tools as part of a broader innovation toolkit. The subject addresses a critical gap in entrepreneurship education by combining the psychological foundations of entrepreneurial thinking with a rigorous, evidence-based approach to market validation, aligning with La Trobe University’s strategic focus on innovation, employability, and industry engagement. Throughout this subject, students will actively ideate and tackle complex challenges, develop robust innovation frameworks and prototypes, and rigorously validate product-market fit. They will use AI-supported tools to accelerate research, explore customer needs and behaviours, generate and refine concepts, test assumptions, and produce actionable evidence to inform product development, marketing strategies, and venture decisions. Students will strategically identify and leverage resources to reduce the risks associated with new ventures, while critically evaluating the quality, limitations, ethical implications, and societal impact of AI-assisted innovation practices. These outcomes empower students to make evidence-based decisions, maximise the likelihood that their product or service will resonate with target audiences, and develop a sustainable pathway to value creation and profitability. Students will also cultivate advanced professional competencies in ethical and moral decision-making and consider their innovations within a broader global context. The subject demands proactive engagement in collaborative group discussions and practical activities, and integrates entrepreneurial theory, applied case studies, AI-enabled innovation workflows, and insights from industry guest speakers addressing start-up challenges, pitfalls, and key success factors. Entry into this subject involves an Expression of Interest (EoI) process, followed by a short interview. Please contact the subject coordinator for further details of this process.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate complex entrepreneurial problems to generate innovative, evidence‑based solutions, integrating advanced analytical frameworks and emerging technologies across varied industry contexts.
Formulate strategic venture decisions using market‑validation evidence, lean innovation methodologies, and resource optimisation principles to guide product, pricing, and growth strategy development.
Work collaboratively to generate and justify entrepreneurial decisions, and communicate resulting solutions clearly to professional and non specialist audiences.
Synthesize qualitative and quantitative market research data to generate advanced customer insights, identify emerging market opportunities, and substantiate venture hypotheses.

Demonstrate expert-level creativity and initiative in conceiving, developing, and systematically refining prototypes or Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) through iterative design processes, critically integrating and adapting design thinking principles in response to stakeholder feedback and emerging challenges.

title: ADVANCED NETWORK ENGINEERING
syllabus_overview: In this subject students cover advanced topics in local and wide area networks. The topics include the design and implementation of Virtual LAN (VLAN) using Virtual Trunk Protocols (VTP), inter-VLAN routing using routing protocols learned in CSE3INE, wide-area networking protocols like Frame Relay, PPP, teleworker services using DSL, cable-modem and broadband wireless, redundant LAN switching through the use of Spanning Tree protocols. The unit will also introduce basic network security at layer-2 using Port blocking, Access control lists, and network troubleshooting using top-down approach.
learning_outcomes: Describe and define various WLAN concepts
Display understanding of basic switch concepts by analysing various configurations of Ethernet ports in switching operations.
Demonstrate understanding of the functions of each of the three layers of the hierarchical network design model by constructing a 3 layer hierarchical model.
Demonstrate understanding of Virtual Trunking Protocol (VTP and Spanning Tree Protocol (STP by analysing and designing and implementing VLANs

title: APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: The project focuses on developing students' skills in system design, implementation, testing and documentation for solving Research problems in Information Technology. Students learn to understand the underlying research question specific to the chosen project; design, develop, test and document a software(or simulation) system for the analysis of the research problem.
learning_outcomes: Conduct effective research using methodology appropriate to the discipline of the project.
Produce comprehensive written reports to effectively communicate research outcomes
Compare and critically evaluate research conducted in the relevant discipline to identify innovative contributions.
Conduct professional oral presentations of research work to expert and non-expert audiences.
Develop prototype implementations of research relevant systems to professional standards accepted by the discipline research community.

title: THE BLOCKCHAIN AND CRYPTOCURRENCIES
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the principles and processes involved in blockchain technologies. The blockchain offers a way to secure transactions online between two parties, when there is no trusted intermediary available. A common use is in financial transactions without a bank as an intermediary, such as bitcoins and other cryptocurrencies. This subject covers the fundamentals of blockchain technology, including how the blockchain works, and how it is applied to modern digital transactions, including cryptocurrencies and smart contracts.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the use of innovative use of blockchains and different cryptocurrencies to create a set of recommendations for appropriate usage by business and industry.
Critically compare and orally present the use of blockchains and distributed ledgers as alternatives to traditional approaches to financial transactions in trust-free transactions.
Assess the contemporary commercial and legal environments needed for cryptocurrency start-ups to ensure business success.
Evaluate security measures in distributed ledgers to minimise risk.

title: BIG DATA MANAGEMENT ON THE CLOUD
syllabus_overview: Companies are acquiring massive amounts of data and also providing internet based service to millions of people. This is extremely challenging due to the large scale of data involved and the huge number of concurrent requests by users. In this subject we will study the current state-of-the-art technologies for analysing huge amounts of data and responding to millions of user requests within one second. Currently the most cost efficient way of achieving the above aim is to use large-scale cloud-based services offered by vendors such as Amazon, Google, IBM, Microsoft, etc. We will study how to use the cloud services provided by Amazon Web Services to meet the big data needs of businesses. We will also teach how to program the world’s most popular Big Data analytics framework called Hadoop. In particular the Hadoop software systems that we will learn in detail include Map Reduce, Hive and Apache Spark. This subject will also teach the following topics: cloud architectures, parallel database systems, key value stores, transaction support in the cloud, virtualization, and multi-tenant database systems.
learning_outcomes: Implement fundamental cloud-based services using Amazon Web Service interfaces.
Analyse the internals of the Map Reduce Framework.
Analyse complex cloud computing architectures and propose remedies to any identified flaws.
Apply your knowledge of Amazon Web Services to design a cloud-based solution for a given application scenario.
Analyse the performance benefits of contrasting No SQL stores.
Solve big data analytics problems by implementing solutions using the Hadoop ecosystem.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BIOINFORMATICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces artificial intelligence (AI) in bioinformatics and biomedicine. It covers complex biological analysis, the application of AI principles, and the integration of diverse biological content through different AI technologies. On completing this subject you will be able to understand and apply AI techniques such as data modelling, machine learning, deep learning, statistical methods and data mining in Bioinformatics and Biomedicines problems. They will also understand how AI in bioinformatics technologies can be applied to DNA,RNA and protein structure and folding problems, molecular interactions, drug discovery, digital health, genetics and metabolic pathways.
learning_outcomes: Select and effectively use existing AI tools to solve bioinformatics tasks such as pattern recognition and gene identification.
Clearly present data analysis results of molecular interactions and biological knowledge discovery.
Evaluate and interpret the results generated by bioinformatics tools to a high standard.
Analyse the characteristics of biological and biomedical data using AI approaches.

title: PROGRAMMING FOR ENGINEERS AND SCIENTISTS (PG)
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the steps involved in designing and creating software solutions for a range of practical problems. To enable you to design and implement solutions, you will be introduced to methods for analysis of task definitions, algorithm design, and the writing of program source code. To develop your problem-solving skills, a variety of problems, with increasing complexity, will be presented for your practice. The Python programming programming language will be used as the program language for implementing software solutions. The strengths of Python, in particular its support of rapid prototyping of ideas, will be exploited to facilitate the development of your problem-solving skill and effective software development practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply the three basic programming constructs of sequence, selection, and iteration to design computational solutions, and reason about which construct is most suitable when multiple approaches are possible.
Implement understandable and maintainable code in Python programming language to solve computational problems, making effective use of functions, objects, and comments.
Use basic data structures such as lists and dictionaries to solve batch data processing problems, and correct identify which problems need to be solved in this way.
Analyse a data processing problem to correctly identify both the data and high-level processing involved.
Analyse a complex domain-specific task definition in order to design and communicate an effective algorithmic solution.

title: COMPUTER FORENSICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the procedures related to computer forensics and digital investigations including formal case management and evidential best practices. The subject will start with an overview of operating system architectures, data structures and file systems. Students will explore the key principles associated with digital forensic processes, data hiding, evidence collection and validation required to perform forensic analysis. The subject will also cover how to conduct technical forensic processes that comply with legal requirements and documentation for forensic evidence, and the use of practical forensic tools.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the different forensics tools and techniques used on varying types of hardware, when gathering and analysing digital evidence
Describe and orally present computer architectures and key concepts associated with data structures, evidence collection and validation.
Create investigative procedures to perform forensic Investigations of different types of digital systems
Apply legally-compliant processes and procedures for forensically gathering and analysing digital evidence, and presentation of findings.

title: CYBERSECURITY PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will explore the alignment between business and cyber strategy, and how vertical functions in organisations can support effective responses. Students will review common cyber technologies and emerging trends in responses, including awareness, training and education. Students will become familiar with security metrics and frameworks that can be used to assess the effectiveness of security controls.
learning_outcomes: Formulate requirements for a cyber security management program
Evaluate contracts and service agreements to support the security function
Determine appropriate mechanisms to build a security culture
Create and communicate appropriate policies, procedures and guidelines to manage risk

title: CYBER RISK MANAGEMENT AND COMPLIANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to a range of cybersecurity incidents and data/privacy breaches and examines how organisations manage them in relation to the risks they pose. It invites students to investigate real-world incidents and apply various techniques for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks. The subject develops practical skills by following ISO and NIST frameworks in creating incident response plans and playbooks, business continuity and crisis communication plans, and conducting post-incident reviews.
learning_outcomes: Apply cost-effective methods and other controls for managing cyber risks.
Design and develop playbooks tailored to specific types of cyber incidents.
Construct a business continuity plan to enhance organisational resilience during and after cyber incidents.
Analyse different risk management strategies and incident response approaches across various cybersecurity incidents and breaches, with consideration of teamwork and collaborative problem-solving.

title: COMPUTER VISION
syllabus_overview: Computer vision is an interdisciplinary scientific field that deals with how computers can be made to gain high-level understanding from digital images or videos. From the perspective of engineering, it seeks to automate tasks that the human visual system can do. In this subject, you will be introduced to topics in computer vision, covering areas from early vision to mid and high-level vision such as camera imaging geometry, feature detection and matching, stereo, motion estimation and tracking, scene understanding and image captioning. You will use statistical models and machine learning models for various computer vision tasks. You will have the opportunity to implement algorithms for real-world computer vision applications in labs.
learning_outcomes: Implement and analyse statistical and machine learning models for advanced computer vision tasks and address design issues.
Critique image processing techniques for basic computer vision tasks and address design issues.
Analyze a given real-world problem and investigate different computer vision approaches to provide optimal solution
Design, implement and evaluate a machine vision model to recognise visual concepts from images.

title: DATA EXPLORATION AND ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with specialist knowledge and tools required to formulate solutions to complex data problems encountered by data scientists. You will learn various data exploration techniques and analysis tools. Selected topics include data cleaning, data normalisation, data visualisation and data exploration. One or more applications associated with each problem will also be discussed. You will learn the fundamentals of exploratory data analysis techniques, statistical learning, and correlation analysis to solve these problems. You will also learn to implement data exploration methods and analysis tools using the R programming language.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the performance of data exploration and data analysis techniques.
Develop comprehensive data reduction and data cleaning techniques for application to dimensionality problems.
Formulate comprehensive solutions to data science problems
Effectively construct data analytics tools for application to complex data sets.
Investigate and critically analyse common problems encountered by data scientists in practice.

title: CYBERSECURITY GOVERNANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to common cyber technologies, methods for assessing cybersecurity maturity, and organisational technical and legal requirements. It guides students in developing cybersecurity policies aligned with international standards and frameworks (e.g., COBIT, NIST- CSF, ISO/IEC) to manage and govern cybersecurity programs, along with implementing organisation-specific compliance strategies. The subject builds practical skills in designing and evaluating cybersecurity programs and governance frameworks aligned with business objectives, using metrics and assessment tools.
learning_outcomes: Design organisation-specific governance and management frameworks to enhance cybersecurity maturity and posture.
Evaluate the effectiveness of cybersecurity controls, governance, and management frameworks using metrics and KPIs.
Apply governance and management frameworks to develop and communicate cybersecurity policies aligned with organisational objectives.
Analyse technical, legal, and business requirements for organisations to inform the development of a cybersecurity programs and governance frameworks for organisation.

title: DEEP LEARNING
syllabus_overview: Deep learning is currently the central machine learning method fuelling the artificial intelligence revolution. In this subject you learn how to apply deep learning algorithms to solve real-world problems. This subject does not assume you have previous machine learning experience, therefore it starts teaching deep learning at a very introductory level. You learn how deep learning techniques can be applied to such tasks as image recognition, sentiment classification, machine translation, question and answering, speech synthesis, etc. The practical skills taught in this subject will allow you to build production level deep learning software that can scale out to millions of users. You will be introduced to the popular deep learning programming frameworks of Pytorch and Tensorflow and advanced deep learning techniques such as reinforcement learning, generative adversarial networks and few shot learning.
learning_outcomes: Design the architecture of a generative adversarial network that can generate realistic data.
Propose deployment and maintenance strategies for deep learning production systems in the cloud based on the analysis from the machine learning requirements of a business.
Given a real-world problem where labels are scarce, investigate different deep learning approaches to tackle this problem.
Write/produce Pytorch code to implement deep learning algorithms to solve computer vision and natural language processing problems.

Analyse a given industry problem and then recommend which deep learning algorithm best solves the problem. This requires the student to know which best learning algorithm is most suitable to solve each type of problem.
Analyse the advantages and disadvantages of using traditional machine learning algorithms versus deep learning algorithms for solving industry problems.

title: DATA MINING
syllabus_overview: Data Mining refers to various techniques which can be used to uncover hidden information from a database. The data to be mined may be complex data including big data, multimedia, spatial and temporal data, biological and health data. Data Mining has evolved from several areas including: databases, artificial intelligence, algorithms, information retrieval and statistics. This subject is designed to provide you with a solid understanding of data mining concepts and tools. You will learn various data exploration techniques and analysis tools. The subject also covers algorithms and techniques for data pre-processing, data classification, association rule mining, and data clustering. The subject also discusses domain applications where data mining techniques are used.
learning_outcomes: Implement classification, clustering, and association rule mining techniques for pattern discovery from selected datasets.
Analyse a given data science problem and recommend data mining strategies suitable to solve the problem.
Evaluate the performance of data mining models using appropriate metrics.
Present data-driven insights by written reports and visualizations and make data-informed recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Assess the quality and suitability of data for mining tasks and develop effective data cleaning, reduction and transformation solutions.

title: FRONTIERS IN NETWORK TECHNOLOGIES
