syllabus_overview: This subject will strengthen and reinforce your knowledge of the design, development and deployment of network infrastructure, including OSI and TCP/IP layering architecture, routing protocols, LANs, WLANs and VLANS; network management; network security through ACLs, firewalls; network virtualization and automation. Labs are designed carefully to broaden students understanding of how to apply theoretical concepts in designing a large-scale network. The content of this subject prepares students for Cisco Academy certification. No grades are awarded for the completion of this subject. The knowledge gained in this subject will be used in the Industry Capstone-Project to offer solutions to Industry-based problems.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge to design, develop and deploy networks using IPv4 and IPv6 addressing schemes.
Implement secure routing protocols to integrate a designed campus network with Internet.
Accurately and effectively design Local Area Network (LAN to user specifications including VLAN when appropriate.)

title: INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT PROJECT
syllabus_overview: The project focuses on developing students' skills in teamwork, system design, implementation, testing and documentation. Students learn to design Information Technology projects covering network management or software development or data science for efficiency, portability and re-use, as well as to take advantage of different standards and system utilities, data and information management techniques. The projects require students to work in small development teams and result in the development of a small-scale industry-based system. The laboratory work is designed to bring students up to speed on relevant development skills and to provide them with a working knowledge sufficient for industrial-type network, data science and software development projects. The subject also integrates previously learned project management skills and knowledge relating to social and ethical issues.
learning_outcomes: Produce professional quality documentation to clearly articulate industry relevant outcomes.
Constructively consider specifications and the use of relevant standards to the design of software or network systems
Apply advanced skills and knowledge to effectively manage industry-based project meetings and progress
Use professional oral communication skills to effectively convey industry applicable outcomes to expert and non-expert audiences.
Develop and implement product prototypes following industry standard AGILE project methodologies

title: INDUSTRY BASED LEARNING
syllabus_overview: Students undertake a 12 x 20hr per week or equivalent industry based learning program. A member of the academic staff acting in the capacity of industry based learning coordinator liaises with the placement provider to formulate and structure a program of learning for each student. This program is normally project based, with day-to-day supervision by the placement provider. Progress is monitored at regular intervals.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical information technology skills to industry skills requirement
Communicate and justify the alignment of one's personal and technical skills with the industry environment
Analyse and evaluate the application of information technology skills to industry

title: INTERMEDIATE NETWORK ENGINEERING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will examine the role of routers while exploring key concepts in network routing. The subject addresses both static and dynamic routing, with emphasis on core protocol types including distance vector, link state, and path vector. Students will also study how routing metrics and attributes influence route selection and routing decisions. Students will develop practical skills in configuring routers, constructing and interpreting routing tables, and assessing protocol performance across a variety of network environments. The applied activities will build a strong foundation for selecting and implementing appropriate routing strategies in organisational contexts.
learning_outcomes: Implement multiprotocol networks for large scale networks.
Design and implement topologies using emerging technologies.
Design and evaluate IPng (Internet Protocol)addressing scheme and sub-netting, including VLSM (Variable Length Subnet Mask).
Evaluate the performance distance vector and link state routing protocols.
Differentiate the scope of the TCP (Transmission Control Protocol and UDP Protocols (User Datagram Protocols).
Implement distance vector and link state routing protocols.

title: IOT TECHNOLOGY AND APPLICATIONS
syllabus_overview: The explosive growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) is changing our world. The term itself, IoT, is used to mean a variety of ideas, depending on the motivation and background of the speaker. The goal of this subject is to provide you with a solid understanding of the latest IoT technology and its applications. This subject will cover the topics: 1) IoT and relevant concepts; 2) IoT devices, including popular IoT hardware and operating systems; 3) IoT architecture, including IoT networks structures and protocols; 4) IoT cloud platforms; 5) IoT security and privacy issues; 6) IoT applications, including Industry 4.0, smart cities, smart agriculture, smart vehicles, IoT healthcare, etc. 7) Research methodology in the area of IoT.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and reflect upon the ethical issues and ethical challenges of the Internet of Things synthesising arguments for and against these issues and challenges.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of key terms and concepts in Internet of Things (IoT by the critical analysis of the current state-of-the-art IoT technologies.

Critically evaluate current Internet of Things technologies or solutions to propose the most suitable for use in a particular given application scenarios, such as smart factories, smart cities, smart homes, smart agriculture, smart vehicles and smart health-care.
Analyse the current state of the art of the Internet of Things with the understanding of the current technologies and application areas, as well as the research methodology
Critically reflect upon the benefits, practical requirements, risks and future trends of Internet of Things

Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to communicate and interpret technical information, theories and well-informed critical analyses in the field of Internet of Things to expert and lay audiences

title: IOT PROGRAMMING
syllabus_overview: Deploying an end-to-end Internet of Things (IoT) solution requires the development of IoT devices and a responsive backend server, as well as a reliable communication channel. In this subject, you will learn about the development of IoT solutions from the beginning with Python / Micro Python as the programming language. The subject will cover: 1) working with different control boards and board components; 2) interaction with sensors and actuators; 3) IoT operating systems; 4) working with real-time IoT and cloud services; 5) understanding IoT data through the application of basic analysis and visualisation methods.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse Internet of Things (IoT data obtained from Internet of Things (IoT devices and evaluate Internet of Things (IoT data via virtualisation in the cloud.
Design and build a complete Internet of Things (IoT network including sensors, actuators and gateways based on a deep knowledge of Internet of Things (IoT architecture.
Initiate and carry out an end-to-end Internet of Things (IoT solution for a particular application collaboratively.
Analyse, assess and develop Internet of Things (IoT applications based on current advanced Internet of Things (IoT application protocols and cloud services.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the latest Internet of Things (IoT technology architectures through the implementation of Internet of Things (IoT solutions.

title: NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
syllabus_overview: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is broadly concerned with the interactions between computers and natural (i.e., human) languages; more particularly, it is concerned with the question of how to program computers to process and analyse large amounts of natural language data. Following a review of the essential mathematical and linguistic concepts underlying natural language processing, you will develop skills in important natural language processing sub-tasks including accessing corpora, tokenisation, morphological analysis, word sense disambiguation, part-of speech tagging, and analysing sentence structure. You will then apply these skills in the context of applications such as text categorisation, text clustering, text recommendation, and information retrieval. Where appropriate, both lexical (i.e. dictionary-based) and machine learning approaches will be used.
learning_outcomes: Devise natural language processing(NLP)processing pipelines using existing NLP code libraries, textcorpora, and lexical resources such as WordNet.

Apply natural language processing sub tasks, including tokenisation, morphological analysis, word sense disambiguation, part-of-speech tagging, and analysing sentence structure, to natural languages texts.
Describe and evaluate the methods and algorithms used to process different types of textual data.
Critically evaluate results of applying natural language processing methods to real-world tasks such as text categorisation, text clustering, text recommendation and information retrieval.

title: MACHINE LEARNING
syllabus_overview: Quantitative analysis plays an important role in industrial data analytics and knowledge engineering, which makes it very useful to develop computing skills for data regression and classification. This subject covers fundamentals of machine learning techniques in theory and practice. The subject is designed to focus on solving industrial data modelling problems using neural networks. You will learn how to test various learning algorithms and compare performance evaluations. Some advanced machine learning techniques for data classification will also be addressed. You will work with industrial data modelling in labs and assignments to consolidate your knowledge and gain hands-on experience with machine learning applications
learning_outcomes: Implement a neural network with different learning algorithms for time- series forecasting with real world data from industry.
Analyse data to design, implement and evaluate machine learning techniques for real world problem solving.
Explain associated concepts and applications of machine learning techniques for data analytics.
Critically identify the major components and system design in developing neural networks data regression and classification.

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY IN IOT
syllabus_overview: The Internet of Things (IoT) is driving the digitalization of all industries; however, it also brings new security and privacy threats due to new technology applications. This subject thoroughly explores the state of the art IoT security and privacy strategies and future trends. You will study topics including: 1) security and vulnerabilities in IoT architecture; 2) threats to access control, privacy, and availability; 3) authentication/authorization for smart devices; 4) security protocols and privacy issues in IoT; 5) security in IoT cloud platforms; 6) confidentiality and security concerns in IoT applications; and 7) ethics of developing end-to-end IoT solutions.
learning_outcomes: Implement best practice techniques for Internet of Things (IoT) authentication, authorization and encryption in IoT hardware and software.
Critically review and analyse security features in Internet of Things (IoT) protocols.
Evaluate emerging Internet of Things (IoT) security, privacy and ethical issues and propose appropriate solutions.
Critically evaluate the challenges involved in securing current Internet of Things (IoT) networks, architectures and devices.

title: CYBERSECURITY INCIDENT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will explore the art and science of incident response, delving into strategies and methodologies for effectively managing cybersecurity incidents. They will develop incident response plans, business continuity plans, and crisis communication plans and evaluate their role in sustaining business operations during incidents. Students will learn key tools and approaches for attacker identification and attribution, understanding the involvement of law enforcement, vendors, and governments in critical infrastructure protection.
learning_outcomes: Analyse incident response approaches against various cyber threats and attacks
Evaluate and propose a business continuity plan
Develop legal and regulatory compliance strategies to support incident management
Identify business and technical measures to respond to cybersecurity incidents

title: NETWORK SYSTEMS AND WEB SECURITY
syllabus_overview: This subject explores current and emerging topics in Network Systems and Web Security, reflecting the latest advancements and challenges in the field of cybersecurity. It covers advanced security paradigms across various domains. The subject topics include advanced network and Internet security, system security, web security, cloud security, and innovative approaches in IoT, Edge, ZTNA, as well as SD-WAN security.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate key security tools and frameworks, such as Kerberos, IPSec, SSL/TLS, and emerging technologies, such as Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) and Secure Access Service Edge (SASE).
Evaluate systems, networks, and the Internet to identify vulnerabilities and security flaws, leveraging contemporary tools and methodologies.
Critically evaluate and synthesise ethical and legal considerations related to information privacy, cybersecurity practices, and the adoption of cutting-edge security technologies.
Apply cryptographic algorithms, including encryption methods, hash functions, digital signatures, and key exchange protocols, to secure systems, networks and clouds.

title: PENETRATION TESTING PRINCIPLES
syllabus_overview: Penetration testing involves assessment of organisational vulnerabilities through the design and execution of technical system tests. This subject introduces students to the principles and processes involved in system penetration testing. It examines common software tools used in a penetration testing exercise. Students will learn various types of penetration testing and their phases, and the interpretation of results from commonly used penetration testing tools. Students will learn of the value of penetration testing for businesses and organisations, and how to use testing results to report on, and to improve, an organisation's security resilience.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise a range of penetration testing methodologies to identify vulnerabilities and reduce risk.
Apply simple penetration test methods and produce client reports, explaining key findings to diverse audiences.
Evaluate the results of penetration testing in phases in a range of contexts and systems to make recommendations
Analyse appropriate tools, techniques, and legal and ethical obligations used in penetration testing

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides necessary skills and techniques to manage large-scale information technology projects, with strong focus on the analytical side of project management, referring to scheduling, cost, and resource management, as well as the 'people' and client management issues that must be dealt with in order to ensure successful projects. Students learn to design Information Technology projects covering network management or software development or data science for efficiency, portability and re-use, as well as to take advantage of different standards and system utilities, data and information management techniques.
learning_outcomes: Critique and apply principles of project management from various stakeholder viewpoints
Formulate comprehensive strategies based on best practice, for modelling, capturing and storing design information in technology projects.
Conduct effective and collaborative project team meetings through application of team dynamics knowledge.
Develop an IT project management framework that integrates security analysis and risk mitigation throughout the project's lifecycle.

title: IOT PROTOCOLS AND PLATFORMS
syllabus_overview: Standards, technologies and platforms targeting Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem are being developed at a very fast pace for many different types of applications including healthcare, home and industry automation. This subject provides students with a solid understanding of the latest IoT protocols, including communication protocols, infrastructure protocols and data protocols. Moreover, this subject will also cover state of the art IoT platforms, including both commercial and open source IoT platforms. You will obtain detailed knowledge for analysing and evaluating the right protocol/platform/architecture for various IoT applications.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate security aspects and characteristics of IoT protocols and platforms.
Critically review the current commercial and open source IoT platforms/ecosystems through the synthesis of IoT systems.
Critically evaluate IoT protocols and platforms for IoT applications in smart cities, smart homes, smart agriculture, smart vehicles and smart health-care.
Analyse, communicate, and interpret IoT related technical information for lay audiences.
Critically evaluate the state-of-the-art Internet of Things (IoT) protocols and standards to propose the most suitable combinations to implement IoT applications.

title: INTRODUCTION TO ROBOTICS
syllabus_overview: While the field of Robotics is concerned broadly with the design, construction, operation, and use of robots, this subject provides an artificial intelligence approach where you will learn to program an intelligent robot for applications involving sensing, navigation, planning, and learning. Topics include: robotics paradigms, system architecture, control system principles, robot kinematics and motion control, simultaneous localisation and mapping, path-planning, decision-making, and machine-learning. Practical exercises will provide you with the opportunity to apply this knowledge to a practical robotics task.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and provide solutions to problems involving robotic localization, kinematics, and path-planning.
Implement and evaluate the performance of various path-finding algorithms on practical robot navigation tasks.
Critique the hierarchical, reactive, and hybrid deliberative/reactive robotics paradigms.
Apply advanced robotics knowledge and skills to practical robotics tasks.

title: THESIS B
syllabus_overview: Students undertake a research, across both CSE5001 and CSE5TSB that takes the equivalent of eight or nine months of continuous work under the supervision of a member of staff. In the second semester, a minor thesis is written up and submitted as a hurdle requirement for the subject. The student also required to deliver a presentation based on the research at the end of the semester.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse the requirements and constraints of a proposed research model in order to design solution methodology
Design and develop a solution based on the proposed methodology
Adhere to strict ethical and privacy standards in developing software or and frameworks in the fields of CS&IT.
Devise a suitable mechanism to validate your proposed methodology
Effectively communicate your research findings to a variety of stakeholders

title: MOVE AND STORE COLLECTION MATERIAL
syllabus_overview: Students will gain the skills and knowledge required to handle, pack and unpack collection material when moving or storing it in accordance with established guidelines.
learning_outcomes: Determine movement and storage requirements.
Complete collection material packing procedures.
Move collection material.
Arrange collection material and update records.

title: IMPLEMENT PREVENTIVE CONSERVATION ACTIVITIES
syllabus_overview: Students will gain the skills and knowledge required to contribute to the preventive conservation of objects or collections in a museum or keeping place context.
learning_outcomes: Undertake preventive conservation.
Assess condition of collection material.
Monitor environmental conditions.
Finalise basic preservation activities.

title: ORAL HEALTH PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you'll delve into the essential skills and knowledge required for dental and oral health practitioners. You'll engage in hands-on learning in the pre-clinical laboratory to enhance your understanding of preventive, periodontal, and restorative procedures. Additionally, you'll gain insight into the scope of practice, safe working practices, and minimally invasive dentistry.
learning_outcomes: Perform basic dental procedures in the management of periodontal and restorative cases in a simulated setting.
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviour in a pre-clinical setting.
Apply diagnostic investigation to the practice of minimal intervention dentistry.
Apply the principles and practices of infection control in the preclinical environment with respect to the provision of clinical care.

title: DENTAL SCIENCE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the anatomical organisation of the body and the basics of cell structure, function, nutrition and metabolism. The fundamentals of the nervous and endocrine systems will be explored in the context of mechanisms of physiological control and homeostasis. This information will provide the foundation for the study of the major organ systems of the body, and an understanding of the oral systemic connections. Communication is important in engaging patients and communities in relation to oral health, so you will also learn to communicate in groups with peers about the body systems.
learning_outcomes: Explain how a given body system contributes to homeostasis under normal conditions.
Explain how cellular activity contributes to the function of organs and the body as a whole.
Relate the anatomical organisation of the human body to whole body function.
Work effectively individually and with peers to apply professional and medical terminology into communicating oral-systemic connections.

title: DENTAL SCIENCE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the gross anatomy of structures predominantly in the region of the head and neck. The subject will include a histology component where you will learn details of normal histology of structures within the oral cavity The subject will also include embryology where you will learn about the development of teeth. Principles of anatomy will be introduced and applied to the anatomy of the head and neck relevant for Dentistry and Oral Health. The subject will also introduce you into other visceral cavities of the head and neck which will then provide you with relevant background for future clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe the histological features of different tooth components and discuss the processes involved in the formation and differentiation of dental tissues during embryogenesis

Explain the structure and function of the head and neck including its role in housing visceral structures, special sense organs and the central nervous system using appropriate medical terminology, surface anatomy and observational skills
Be able to identify anatomical structures and infer their relationship to function and communicate anatomical concepts using correct medical terminology in writing.
Describe the anatomical basis of some common abnormalities of, or injuries to structures in the head and neck.

title: PRECLINICAL ORAL HEALTH SIMULATED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you'll advance your fundamental skills and knowledge. Through hands-on practice in the pre-clinical laboratory and simulated patient settings, you'll develop expertise in examining periodontal health. Additionally, you'll learn about the scope of practice, safe working practices, and minimally invasive dentistry. By the end of the subject, you will be expected to have achieved competency in foundational pre-clinical skills.
learning_outcomes: Apply different diagnostic techniques and procedures and when they would be incorporated into a clinical setting.
Demonstrate restorative skills for restoration in the dentition.
Demonstrate subgingival periodontal instrumentation.
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviour in a pre-clinical setting.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will study the anatomy of the head and face with a focus on anatomy of the teeth. You will study human tooth morphology, where morphology is the study of the form and structure, in this instance of teeth and their specific structural features. This subject will also introduce you to the core values of a health practitioner and awareness of the First Nations culture which set a foundation to the development of your professional identity.
learning_outcomes: Articulate core concepts related to the foundational cultural awareness and cultural responsiveness for improving the health outcomes in the First Nations peoples
Identify and discuss the anatomy of each tooth in the human dentitions and determine their functions
Contextualise the characteristics of a professional oral health practitioner with reference to professional behaviour, ethical principles and communication
Apply discipline-specific terminology and nomenclature to describe the functional anatomy of the orofacial region

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore microbiology (bacteriology, mycology and virology) and immunology, gaining foundational knowledge for future study in both general and oral health. You will examine dental caries and periodontal disease in terms of their aetiology and pathogenesis, classification and prevention.
learning_outcomes: Describe the classification, aetiology and pathogenesis of periodontal disease.
Analyse the aetiology, pathogenesis and modifying factors of dental caries.
Apply concepts of inflammation and microbiology to general health and oral disease.
Communicate concepts of immunology, microbiology, periodontal disease and dental caries using multimedia presentations.

title: ORAL HEALTH PROMOTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn the determinants of health and oral health that operate at individual and community levels. You will explore how to analyse the risk factors and behaviours that influence an individual or group and how this can affect their oral health and access to care. You will develop skills in preventing oral diseases at individual and community levels. You will be challenged to explore evidence-based oral health promotion approaches suitable to improve the oral health and well-being of priority groups and communities. You will work individually and with peers to prepare recommendations for better oral health of communities.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of prevention and early intervention in the management of oral diseases
Describe the determinants of health, risk factors and behaviours that influence individual and community oral health.

Apply the principles of population health and health promotion and explain the role of health policy for collaboratively developing, implementing and evaluating evidence-based health promotion strategies.

Demonstrate familiarity with Australian standards on safety and quality in health care and appraise the concept of person-centred care, including the identification of high-risk populations, and the provision of trauma-informed care.
Discuss the access and provision of oral health care services in Australia and the environmental impact of providing health care.

title: PRECLINICAL SKILLS 2B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will further develop your restorative skills by preparing multi-surface restorations. You will be introduced to paediatric restorative and extraction techniques, learn to obtain clinical records as part of patient orthodontic assessments, and practice your communication skills in an authentic dental clinic environment in preparation for application on clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competence in management of medical emergencies in a simulated patient clinical environment
Demonstrate competence in the administration of patient intra-oral local anaesthesia
Demonstrate competence in the provision of direct tooth restorations for multi-surface permanent and deciduous dentition
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours in a pre-clinical and simulated patients’ settings.
Demonstrate a level of competence in obtaining and recording clinical information in a well-organised simulated patient record.

title: PRECLINICAL SKILLS 2A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build upon foundational practical skills acquired in year one. In a simulated environment, you will learn how to obtain relevant intra-oral radiographs, administer intra-oral local anaesthesia on a patient, undertake restorations on permanent teeth, and perform non-surgical periodontal instrumentation. You will use the skills and expertise developed in this subject to inform future clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours in a pre-clinical environment while managing simulated patients.
Demonstrate competence in obtaining and recording patient clinical information in a well-organised simulated patient record
Demonstrate within a simulated environment competence in non-surgical periodontal instrumentation
Demonstrate competence in the provision of posterior approximal direct tooth restorations
Demonstrate within a simulated environment competence in intra-oral radiographic techniques

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 2A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will build upon theoretical foundations, translating principles guiding periodontal condition management into clinical contexts for diagnosis, care planning, and preventive strategies. Additionally, they will relate the theoretical concepts underpinning radiographic techniques and the administration of local anaesthesia, to ensure safe and effective clinical practice. Furthermore, they will extend their insight into the theoretical principles of operative dentistry, in general, and minimal intervention dentistry specifically, as applied to both the paediatric and adult dentitions. This holistic approach will equip students with the knowledge needed to navigate diverse clinical presentations and deliver optimal person-centred care.
learning_outcomes: Applying the theoretical principles of Minimal Intervention Dentistry to the provision of person-centred care.
Critique the theoretical principles underpinning intra-oral radiographic techniques, panoramic imaging principles, and radiographic image interpretation for clinical application.
Compare and contrast the management of periodontal conditions, encompassing diagnosis, treatment planning, and preventive interventions to uphold periodontal health.
Relate concepts and principles of local anaesthetics intra and extra oral administration to patient safety and potential complications.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 2B
syllabus_overview: This subject covers key theoretical and practical aspects of dentistry, encompassing various specialised areas, including paediatric dentistry, where students engage with restorative techniques, pulp therapy, behavior management, and preventive care for children. Additionally, they will explore childhood development assessment, orthodontic principles, craniofacial growth theories, and occlusion concepts. This subject will emphasise personal, professional and ethical practice, enhancing students' ability to deliver compassionate person-centred care. Furthermore, students will learn about culturally safe and responsive practices, acknowledging and respecting the unique cultural needs of First Nations peoples in healthcare provision.
learning_outcomes: Explain culturally safe and responsive practices, acknowledging and respecting the unique cultural needs and perspectives of First Nations peoples in the provision of health care.

Compare and contrast the theoretical principles and concepts applicable to minimal intervention dentistry in a paediatric patient, incorporating behaviour management, restorative interventions, pulp therapy, and preventive measures.
Demonstrate an understanding of orthodontic concepts, including growth and development in relation to the identification and management of malocclusion.
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours to inform the delivery of compassionate and ethical person-centred care.

title: GENERAL MEDICINE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you study the relevance of systemic disease and potential impacts on oral health. The subject encompasses the principles and fundamentals of altered homeostasis and demonstrates the pathological processes at both cellular and gross level, essential for patient care.
learning_outcomes: Describe the mechanisms of cellular injury, adaptation, and repair, including inflammation, haemodynamic disorders, and the basis of neoplasia.
Explain how health disorders impact oral health
Professionally engage with team members to prepare a media presentation.
Explain the pathophysiological processes of major organ systems, including the cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, renal, nervous, and endocrine.

title: FOUNDATION SKILLS IN REMOVABLE PROSTHODONTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, foundation skills in Removable Prosthodontics – the replacement of teeth and soft tissues with a non-permanent prosthesis that can be removed – will be introduced and developed. Technical and clinical concepts and principles will guide the construction of complete dentures which replace a full arch of teeth. A similar approach will be undertaken to replace a number of teeth of individual or grouped tooth spaces by fabricating a partial denture.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate preclinical competence in the technical and clinical skills of impression recording and facebow bite registration.
Appropriately handle and manipulate a range of dental materials used in denture construction both in the dental laboratory and chairside.
Apply knowledge of oral anatomy to the different stages involved in denture design and construction to produce a registration rim that is retentive, comfortable, and replicates natural oral tissues.
Demonstrate behaviours and standards which are consistent with the Dental Board of Australia’s Professional Code of Conduct, legislation and La Trobe University policies.

title: MEDICINE FOR DENTISTRY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to pharmacology and therapeutics, with a focus on medications used in dentistry and oral health, and the impact of selected medications used to treat systemic diseases on oral health. This knowledge will then be applied to ascertaining and analysing a complex medical patient history, focusing on the pharmacological, therapeutics and pathophysiological impact on oral health and the risks associated with dental treatment.
learning_outcomes: Identify conditions and manifestations of systemic diseases and therapeutics that may put patients at risk in a dental environment
Interpret a medical history in the context of oral health
Analyse risks for dental treatment and oral health care arising from the effects of pharmacology and systemic disease and the implications for patient management
Describe the pharmacology and therapeutics used in dentistry and oral health

title: INTRODUCTION TO CLINICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will be introduced to the clinical setting where they will adapt themselves to the professional standards required of them as student clinicians. This will be reflected in compliance with a high standard of infection control in the clinical environment, advanced self-preparation in readiness to undertake clinical work and the ability to integrate within a broader clinical and administrative team. Students will have the opportunity to engage in discussions with experienced educators, exploring the concepts and principles presented in the first two years of study. These opportunities will build on their theoretical basis, to establish a clinical foundation. As part of required clinical skill development, students will focus on history taking as part of a comprehensive oral examination to develop individualised care plans for the patients they are assigned to manage.
learning_outcomes: Review personal and clinical practice through applying self-reflection in all activities.
Recognise and relate different patient medical history presentations to their oral manifestation and impact on different structures.
Prepare oral care plans for non-complex cases in the clinical setting.
Deliver culturally appropriate, empathetic and respectful professional practice in the provision of person-centred care.

title: PRECLINICAL SKILLS 3
syllabus_overview: In this subject, skill development in Removable Prosthodontics will be progressed in the simulation environment building on the concepts and principles introduced in Semester 1. New skills in minor oral surgery (adult exodontia) and advanced direct restorative techniques will be applied to more complex simulated situations. Acquiring the necessary technical skills is in preparation for their transferal into the provision of direct patient care in the senior years on clinical placement. Ongoing demonstration of professional behaviour and conduct remains an expectation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the principles of adult tooth removal on a manikin in a simulated environment.
Apply the principles of denture design and tooth arrangement - arch form, balanced occlusion, compensating curves, denture stability and aesthetics - to recreate a patient’s natural dentition.
Demonstrate behaviours and standards which are consistent with the Dental Board of Australia’s Professional Code of Conduct, legislation and La Trobe University Policies.
Apply advanced direct restorative techniques in the management of complex presentations on a manikin in a simulated setting.

title: CLINICAL DENTISTRY 1
syllabus_overview: Students will continue to build their clinical skills, by broadening their scope of practice, through demonstrating their ability to apply the affective, cognitive and psychomotor skills they have previously learnt. Time management will be emphasised as too the completion of year level specific clinical competencies. In achieving competencies, students will demonstrate a level of clinical competence that requires minimal intervention from their clinical educators. Students will advance skill progression in the areas of patient history taking, intra/extra oral patient examination, occlusal, hard tissue assessment, prescribing and exposing of diagnostically and clinically relevant intra-oral radiographs, and completion of individualised patient care plans. There should be minimal breaches related to infection control and professionalism to inform student progression to different external agencies for ongoing clinical placement experience.
learning_outcomes: Develop and justify oral care plans for non-complex cases in the clinical setting for both the adult and child patient.
Appraise and critically analyse personal and clinical practice through self-reflection.
Evaluate patients’ systemic and medical histories and manage within scope of practice their presentation which impacts oral structures, in conjunction with other healthcare professionals if required.
Deliver patient treatments adhering to management principles relevant to different dental disciplines.
Demonstrate provision of clinical skills under certain time management parameters informed by patient presentation complexity.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 3A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the principles of Care Planning and their application to person centred care. You will also gain the theoretical knowledge needed to support development of your clinical skills in the dental disciplines of Removable Prosthodontics and Orthodontics. This knowledge is required for your introduction into clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Formulate comprehensive individual care plans, informed by the collation, analysis and interpretation of relevant clinical data, to provide patient management relative to treatment need.
Compare and contrast the fundamental principles applicable to denture construction in relation to the provision of a removable prosthesis required to restore and rehabilitate the oral environment.
Acquire and demonstrate the professional behaviours and attitudes essential for managing complex patients in a dental setting
Explain the mechanical principles involved in controlling orthodontic force application to achieve optimal tooth movement and treatment outcomes.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 3B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will continue to construct the theoretical knowledge required to support the progressive development of your clinical skills. The dental disciplines of endodontics and minor oral surgery will be introduced. Advanced concepts and principles relevant to periodontics and restorative practice will be presented to inform ongoing clinical practice of more complex patient presentations.
learning_outcomes: Develop an advanced theoretical knowledge of complex direct coronal restorations, incorporating the principles and techniques applicable to their design and construction for anterior and posterior permanent teeth.
Gain a comprehensive theoretical understanding of minor oral surgery, encompassing patient assessment, surgical techniques, post-operative care, and complication management.
Apply the principles of denture construction to the management of a an edentulous and or partially dentate patient to re-establish oral health and patient quality of life.
Analyse and critique the theoretical and clinical principles and concepts which underpin an evidence-based approach to the management of an endodontic patient.

title: ORAL PATHOLOGY AND ORAL MEDICINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore orofacial diseases appropriate for a general dentist. You will learn the epidemiology, aetiology, pathogenesis, prognosis of pathological oral tissues. You will also learn recognising various clinical appearances, radiology and histology investigations used in diagnosing and managing orofacial lesions.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the epidemiology, aetiology and pathogenesis of orofacial diseases and apply this knowledge in the context of patient care.
Differentiate between normal and pathologic oral tissues as identified during a routine dental check up to a level appropriate for a general dentist.
Interpret common investigations used in diagnosing orofacial lesions at radiological and histological levels.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 4A
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable students the opportunity to extend their engagement with, and insight of, various dental speciality disciplines, including but not limited to orthodontics, endodontics, special needs dentistry and paediatric dentistry. Students will be equipped with the knowledge, skills and ethical considerations necessary for competent and compassionate dental care across diverse patient populations and communities. An inter-disciplinary approach to care planning will be progressed through exposure to more complex cases and participation in authentic case base studies.
learning_outcomes: Develop preventive and restorative care plans tailored to the specific needs of paediatric patients.

Formulate comprehensive orthodontic care plans incorporating different treatment modalities as informed by patient assessment and analysis of relevant clinical data as part of the clinical decision-making process.
Apply advanced communication and behavioural management strategies to enhance patient compliance during different dental procedures.
Investigate key endodontic topics related to the management of trauma in the permanent dentition, analgesia and pain management, and complex care planning.
Design individualised care plans that incorporate patient-specific medical, psychological, and behavioural considerations and challenges.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 4B
syllabus_overview: This advanced-level subject is an exploration into the nuanced and intricate domains of advanced periodontics, oral surgery, endodontics, and fixed and removable prosthodontics. Students will be required to create care plans for complex patients integrating multidisciplinary approaches that incorporate an evidence-based approach to the management of the most challenging of presentations encountered in clinical dental practice.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the surgical management options for periodontal conditions through developing an appreciation for periodontics – restorative clinical interface.
Design fixed and removable prosthodontic care plans informed by patient assessment and individual risk status.
Formulate complex endodontic care plans for the medically compromised patient, instances of trauma to the permanent dentition and or those requiring pharmacological pain management
Develop diagnostic processes which inform the different stages in the management of minor oral surgery cases specifically related to third molar surgery, odontogenic infections and orofacial trauma.

title: CLINICAL DENTISTRY 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will attend clinical placement in regional – rural Victoria to progress clinical experience in dental procedures including but not limited to the provision of direct restorations, periodontal instrumentation, simple extractions, radiography, endodontics and removable prosthodontics. Students will provide direct patient care to a broad and varied demographic, a component of which will be to develop a clinical e-portfolio. This document will showcase their clinical skills and professional competence not only in specific dental disciplines but also in communication and health promotion. Upon completion, students will be prepared for ongoing clinical placements where more complex patients and procedures will be undertaken.
learning_outcomes: Construct a clinical e-portfolio that showcases acquired technical and non-technical skills applicable to a range of clinical procedures.
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours in all interactions with patients, staff, students and fellow healthcare professionals internal and external to the clinical environment.

Progress clinical skill development in a range of treatment modalities across diverse dental disciplines, encompassing periodontics, endodontics, exodontia, removable prosthodontics and general direct restorative procedures under the guidance and direction of clinical educators.
Formulate comprehensive and individualised care plans working collaboratively with interprofessional teams through referral pathways to enhance the oral health and well-being of diverse communities.

Engage in dialogic self-reflection to critically evaluate personal, ethical and clinical practices, fostering continuous improvement and self-awareness through active participation in clinical discussions.

title: CLINICAL DENTISTRY 3
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will continue to extend their clinical skill development through the provision of direct patient care whilst on regional-rural clinical placement. This will be demonstrated through the provision of multi-surface direct restorations, advanced periodontal care, extractions including surgical procedures and diagnostic intra-oral radiography. Students will develop and administer care plans related to endodontics and removable prostheses as part of the provision of holistic patient care. Techniques related to the complex management of indirect tooth restoration will be progressively introduced informed by patient treatment need and risk assessment. Students will continue to develop their clinical e-portfolio to demonstrate the progression of clinical and professional skills advancement within their scope of practice.
learning_outcomes: Implement clinical skills in a range of treatment modalities across diverse dental disciplines under the guidance and direction of clinical educators
Model dialogic self-reflection and awareness to critically evaluate personal and professional practice, through demonstration of continuous improvement.

Extend clinical e-portfolio development to effectively showcase acquired non-technical and technical skills, through providing a comprehensive demonstration of ongoing of personal and professional growth in the clinical domain.

Provide individual comprehensive patient care plans by working collaboratively and inclusively with interprofessional teams through referral pathways to enhance the oral health and well-being of diverse communities
Apply personal and professional behaviours to all interactions with external and internal stakeholders involved with clinical placement

title: DENTISTRY INDUSTRY PROJECT A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will apply their knowledge of project planning and management to commence an industry-relevant project in collaboration with a small group of their peers. In doing so, students will develop experience with project management, stakeholder engagement, and collection of data. Students will work closely with an academic and/or industry supervisor who'll supervise their progress and provide advice as they work through the project. Students will complete their project inDEN5IRB (Dentistry Industry Project B) in Semester 1 of the final year of the course.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on and apply professional behaviours to successfully lead and influence project management processes.
Apply principles of team project management to communicate project processes and outcomes to a range of stakeholders.
Apply advanced knowledge and skills, plan and execute a substantial team project to solve an industry problem.
Initiate an industry-relevant team project that integrates the principles of academic integrity and ethical conduct.
Clearly and coherently communicate individual professional capabilities in team project management.

title: PRECLINICAL SKILLS D
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply the principles of endodontics and indirect restoration of teeth in pre-clinical simulation. You will be asked to demonstrate competence in endodontic access, canal instrumentation and obturation, and demonstrate competence in advanced tooth preparation.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning and judgement in a reflective practice approach to support the development of new skills in a simulated pre-clinical setting
Apply the principles of advanced tooth preparation for indirect restorations in a simulated setting.
Demonstrate competence in endodontic procedures in a simulated setting.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 5A
syllabus_overview: This subject integrates capstone knowledge from the dental disciplines of Periodontics, Oral Medicine, Oral Surgery, Fixed and Removable Prosthodontics and Endodontics to enable comprehensive interdisciplinary care planning for complex treatment requirements. This subject confirms the principles of management for acute and chronic pain of orofacial origin and provides the foundation learning in the use of dental implants for the replacement of missing teeth.
learning_outcomes: Appraise the multifactorial origin of orofacial pain and demonstrate awareness through competency in the diagnosis and management of patient described pain experience.
Develop comprehensive treatment plans for restoring extensively damaged teeth, prioritising evidence-based and patient-centered tooth replacement for full dental rehabilitation.
Critique personal and professional limitations relevant to identifying appropriate timing and methods for patient referral to multidisciplinary care.
Integrate relevant elements from various specialist disciplines to determine management interventions appropriate to acute and chronic medical conditions and patient circumstances.

title: SCIENTIFIC AND CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE 5B
syllabus_overview: This subject complements the knowledge obtained in the specialist disciplines of dentistry with further learning in orthodontics, paediatric dentistry and special needs dentistry to facilitate care planning and treatment provision. The subject incorporates content pertaining to the fundamentals of administration and teamwork in dental practice in conjunction with capstone learning in professionalism, ethics, and jurisprudence as preparation for entry to independent practice on course completion as a graduate dentist.
learning_outcomes: Relate relevant personnel supervision and regulatory requirements to the concepts and principles required of dental practice administration.
Apply initiative and judgement to determine the management of paediatric patients or those patients having special individual treatment needs.
Identify anomalies in tooth position to inform patients of their Orthodontic treatment needs, options and implications of available treatment alternatives.
Apply leadership skills to work collaboratively and effectively in dental and healthcare teams in the provision of effective and holistic person-centred care.
Acquire and practice awareness of professional and legal responsibilities in the provision of person-centred care and delivered within an ethical framework to individuals and communities.

title: DENTISTRY RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will commence your research project developed in HLT4RPP (Research Project Planning) and in doing so, develop experience with project planning, human ethics approval, participant recruitment, obtaining informed consent, and the collection and preliminary analysis of data. You will work closely with an experienced researcher who'll supervise your progress and provide advice as you work through your project. You will complete your project in your final year in DEN5RPB (Dentistry Research Project B).
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge and skills to plan substantial research-based projects under supervision.
Apply initiative and judgement to adapt advanced discipline knowledge to diverse settings.
Conduct research that integrates principles of academic integrity, ethical conduct and peer review.
Synthesise and communicate draft theoretical propositions and methodologies to professional audiences in both written and oral formats.

title: CLINICAL DENTISTRY 4
syllabus_overview: In this clinical subject you will undertake clinical placements in public dental clinics across regional-rural Victoria where you will provide a full range of treatments to patients. Building upon your previous clinical experience, you will continue to practice critical self-reflection as you monitor personal and professional outcomes. You will be expected to demonstrate a level of professional competence appropriate for a final-year student in terms of communication, leadership, health promotion, infection control, clinical information gathering, diagnosis, care planning, clinical treatment and evaluation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in diverse areas of dentistry, including infection prevention, periodontal, orthodontic, endodontic, restorative, and prosthetic aspects, while recognising personal scope of professional practice and referral pathways.
Show professionalism in patient interactions, integrating critical thinking and reflective practice to optimise treatment outcomes and promote oral health within the community.
Incorporate culturally safe and sensitive practices with empathy, adhering to ethical principles and legal obligations in all aspects of dental care provision.

Attain proficiency in gathering essential patient information through comprehensive patient histories and oral examinations, utilising specialised investigations to inform specific diagnostic decision and clinical need determinations.

Demonstrate mastery commensurate with being a safe practitioner in formulating evidence-based care plans, adeptly communicating them to patients through facilitating informed consent by conducting personalised evaluations and comprehensive discussions of treatment options and requirements.

title: CLINICAL DENTISTRY 5
syllabus_overview: In this clinical subject, you will complete a placement in public dental clinics across regional Victoria, delivering a comprehensive range of treatments to patients. Building on your prior clinical experience, you'll engage in ongoing critical reflection to assess outcomes. Expected to demonstrate advanced professional competence aligned with final-year standards, encompassing effective communication, leadership, health promotion, clinical data gathering, diagnosis, management planning, treatment execution, and evaluation. By the conclusion of the year, you should present evidence of competency and safety across diverse practice areas, qualifying you for registration as a dental practitioner.
learning_outcomes: Practice culturally safe and sensitive practices with empathy, adhering to ethical and moral principles and legal obligations in all aspects of the provision of dental care.
Demonstrate proficiency in formulating and implementing inclusive evidence-based treatment plans that address patient needs.

Appraise performance as a clinician in the collation, analysis, interpretation and evaluation of relevant patient data and diagnostic information applicable to clinical decision-making in the delivery of person-centred care.

Evaluate personal and professional standards and values expected of a dental practitioner as demonstrated through interactions with patients and other healthcare professionals in order to optimise treatment outcomes and promote oral health of individuals and communities.
Demonstrate proficiency in different dental disciplines applicable to scope of practice, incorporating recognised referral pathways where relevant.

title: DENTISTRY INDUSTRY PROJECT B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will complete their industry-relevant project commenced in DEN4IPA(Industry Project A) in collaboration with a small group of their peers. In this subject, students will develop experience with project management, stakeholder engagement, the collection and analysis of data, and interpretation of results. Dissemination of findings will occur through the preparation of a project report and oral seminar presentation. Students will work closely with an academic and/or industry supervisor who'll supervise their progress and provide advice. Upon successful completion of the subject, students will have demonstrated ability to work relatively independently and collaboratively to undertake a complex industry-relevant project.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on and apply advanced professional behaviours to successfully lead and influence project management processes.
Apply advanced knowledge and skills to execute a substantial team project to solve an industry problem.
Apply principles of team project management to communicate project processes and outcomes to a range of stakeholders.
Reflect on issues arising in team project management and clearly communicate these to peers.
Clearly and coherently communicate your professional capabilities in team project management.

title: DENTISTRY RESEARCH PROJECT B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete the research project commenced in DEN4RPA (Dentistry Research Project A). In doing so, you will develop experience with data analysis and interpretation. Students will prepare a journal-ready manuscript and oral presentation, working closely with an experienced researcher who'll supervise progress and provide advice. Upon successful completion of this subject, you will have demonstrated an ability to undertake a research project suitable for publication and presentation relatively independently.
learning_outcomes: Conduct research that integrates the principles of academic integrity, ethical conduct and peer review.
Synthesise research findings and communicate outcomes and conclusions to professional audiences in both written and oral formats.
Apply advanced knowledge and skills to execute substantial research-based projects, with some independence.
Using judgment, analyse and interpret research data, with some independence.

title: AUSTRALIAN SIGN LANGUAGE 1A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop practical abilities in both receptive and production skills in Auslan to a level of basic communicative competence. You will be introduced to key grammatical structures of Auslan and the use of the language in its appropriate cultural, social context and begin to understand the history of Auslan and the deaf community. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. This is a level 1 subject. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate language awareness through describing similarities and differences between Auslan and English.
Recognise and respond to basic vocabulary and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A1 level in the CEFR framework.
Identify and describe the broad challengers and issues experienced by the deaf community nationwide and worldwide.
Produce a range of basic vocabulary items and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A1 level in the CEFR framework.

title: AUSTRALIAN SIGN LANGUAGE 1B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will continue to develop practical abilities in both receptive and production skills in Auslan to a level of basic communicative competence. You will be introduced to key grammatical structures of Auslan and the use of the language in its appropriate cultural, social context and begin to understand the history of Auslan and the deaf community. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. This is a level 1 subject. Please note the prerequisite requirement for enrolling in this subject. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Produce a range of more basic vocabulary and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A1 level in the CEFR framework.
Demonstrate language awareness through describing similarities and differences between Auslan and English.
Identify and describe the historical challenges and issues experienced by the deaf community.
Recognise and respond to more basic vocabulary and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A1 level in the CEFR framework.

title: AUSTRALIAN SIGN LANGUAGE 2A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop intermediate levels of communicative competence in Auslan in the areas of both receptive and production skills. You will look at differences and similarities in both Auslan and English, and will also discuss current and past medical approaches and challenges had by the deaf community. This is a level 2 subject. Please consider the subject pre-requisites before enrolling. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe the medical approaches/interventions and issues experienced by the deaf community.
Demonstrate language awareness through describing similarities and differences between Auslan and English.
Produce a range of intermediate vocabulary items and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A2 level in the CEFR framework.
Recognise and respond to intermediate vocabulary and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A2 level in the CEFR framework.

title: AUSTRALIAN SIGN LANGUAGE 2B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop your intermediate level of Auslan communicative competence through both receptive and production skills. You will look at differences and similarities in both Auslan and English as well as how sociolinguistics has an influence on language use. You will also explore how Deaf Gain has had its impact on society nationwide and worldwide. This is a level 2 subject. Please consider the subject pre-requisites before enrolling. This subject includes live sessions with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and respond to more intermediate vocabulary and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A2 level in the CEFR framework.
Identify and describe the benefits of Deaf Gain within our society.
Demonstrate language awareness through describing similarities and differences between Auslan and English.
Produce and appraise a range of more intermediate vocabulary items and grammatical constructions in Auslan consistent with the A2 level in the CEFR framework.

title: VIRTUAL AND INTELLIGENT HEALTHCARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of how technology can be combined with healthcare delivery to provide remote medical services, diagnosis, monitoring, and consultation. With a focus on telemedicine, remote monitoring, the Internet of Medical Things, digital health records, chatbots, and emerging technologies, you will gain insight into the rapidly evolving landscape of virtual and intelligent healthcare. Emphasising the significant growth and adoption of these technologies, you will analyse the role of advancements in technology and the rising demand for accessible and convenient healthcare solutions. The subject highlights the transformative impact of virtual and intelligent healthcare on improving access, efficiency, and quality of healthcare delivery, empowering patients to actively manage their health. However, it also addresses critical challenges such as data privacy concerns, regulatory complexities, and disparities in technology access, emphasising the need for solutions to ensure widespread adoption and success. Through interdisciplinary study and critical analysis, you will develop a nuanced understanding of the opportunities and challenges inherent in this dynamic field.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of how technology intersects with healthcare delivery, including the mechanisms enabling remote medical services, diagnostics, monitoring, and consultations

Assess key technologies such as telemedicine, remote monitoring, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), digital health records, chatbots, and emerging technologies within the context of virtual and intelligent healthcare.

Critically assess the challenges facing virtual and intelligent healthcare, including data privacy concerns, regulatory complexities, and disparities in technology access, and propose strategies to address these challenges

Evaluate key technologies such as telemedicine, remote monitoring, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), digital health records, chatbots, and emerging technologies within the context of virtual and intelligent healthcare.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DIGITAL HEALTH SOLUTIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will acquire a thorough understanding of design thinking methodology aimed at analysing health problems and crafting digital solutions with a human-centred approach. The emphasis lies on the practical application of digital health solutions through activities such as role-play, case discussions, and observation in relevant work settings. Moreover, the subject explores the change management strategy essential for facilitating the adoption of digital changes. Additionally, it focuses on project management frameworks and skills specific to the digital health landscape, guiding you through the development of project concepts, implementation planning, and evaluation. This will equip you with the foundational knowledge necessary to create a roadmap for transforming solution prototypes into reality.
learning_outcomes: Design innovative digital health solutions to tackle recognised ethical, social, cultural and environmental challenges in efficiency and effectiveness
Critically evaluate healthcare-related issues with a design thinking lens to grasp user needs for digital solutions.
Critically evaluate the application of change management philosophy in facilitating the adoption of digital health solutions, assessing its effectiveness and implications within healthcare settings.

Compare and contrast digital transformation strategies utilising project management theory and principles, demonstrating leadership and teamwork skills in navigating adaptability and self-management throughout the process.

title: STRATEGIC DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain digital health strategic planning knowledge and see how this can be applied to relevant work contexts through the use of role-play, case discussion and observation. You will explore topics related to digital transformation in the context of healthcare sector. You will examine frameworks to assess organisational readiness and how to develop a systematic digital transformation roadmap. You will learn more about project and change management processes that can help foster and embrace digital change.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the digital transformation needs of an organisation.
Propose a roadmap to implement the strategy fostering and embracing digital change.
Develop a digital transformation strategy through clear articulation of benefits, projects and partnerships.
Assess organisational readiness to identify capabilities, gaps, and opportunities within the health system.

title: DIGITAL HEALTH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will further develop your digital health knowledge and skills through engagement in supervised professional practice placements in healthcare and related agencies across the whole-of-health. The purpose of the subject is to enable you to apply theoretical knowledge to practice. You will undertake 100 hours of placement and complete a range of academic assessments. Regular contact with University supervisors is maintained during placements via telephone, email and on-site visits. As this is a course capstone placement subject, it must be completed by all students. No advanced standing is available. To meet professional competency requirements students must pass both the professional placement and academic components of the subject.
learning_outcomes: Create a professional portfolio based on a critical reflection of current digital health theory and practice. Compare and contrast digital health processes and technology across healthcare agencies, aiming to translate newfound insights into innovative solutions or practices.
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of Digital Health solutions, critically evaluate their application in the health system and suggest solutions not yet developed.

Demonstrate application of digital health skills through supervised engagement in activities that build upon academic studies, including the ability to work independently, collaboratively, professionally, and ethically.

Design and use effective project and time management planning to demonstrate an ability to develop and achieve objectives, effectively participate in multidisciplinary environments and high-level communication across various mediums.

title: DIGITAL HEALTH DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will consolidate digital health solution design & implementation knowledge and develop skills to apply your knowledge to relevant work contexts through the use of role-playing, case discussion, and observation. You will gain knowledge about problem analysis and solution design using co-design, human-centered and experience-based approaches. The subject will also provide foundational knowledge of solutions interoperability and change management. You will learn about implementation science in regard to behaviour change design and aspects of converting prototypes into reality.
learning_outcomes: Assess digital health opportunities to address identified problems of efficiency and effectiveness.
Evaluate digital health solution adoption using implementation science for continuous improvement.
Apply co-design framework in building digital health solutions.
Critically analyse the healthcare-related problems to understand user needs around digital technologies.

title: BIG DATA AND HEALTH ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain an understanding of what "big data" is, why it is important to the health and healthcare sectors, and how it can be used in real-world applications. You will investigate how data analytics can benefit healthcare delivery, and improve system efficiency and patient outcomes data collection. You will develop a working knowledge of the analytical techniques used to mine big data and visualise it. You will explore the requirements for data research infrastructure, review the current big data landscape (including assets, facilities, and services), and investigate the requirements around information privacy and security in relation to big data in digital health. Data linkage techniques and various strategies to tackle problems relating to data linkage quality will also be explored.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively assess Big Data analytics to understand how they can extract insights and foster teamwork, through effective communication, problem-solving, and collective interpretation.
Identify, synthesise and evaluate opportunities for data sharing to provide solutions for real-world problems.
Appraise the role of Big Data in health and the impacts on healthcare provision.
Assess and predict data integrity issues, technical and legislative challenges of data integration for the application of Big Data & analytics in health systems.
Evaluate the requirements for research platforms that house and use Big Data for health data analytics.

title: TRENDS IN DIGITAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain an understanding of the growing technological trends, its related issues/problems, and strategies to tackle healthcare problems. It will help you compare and contrast technologies using standard frameworks. You will explore the role of digital health technologies and how they are applied in healthcare, public health and health promotion. You will also learn ethics and law in relation to digital health innovations, and research updates in digital health.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the role of digital health innovations relevant to healthcare practices (e.g. improving clinical/health outcomes, patient care and safety, health and well-being, public health and health promotion).
Critically review and interpret current research findings in digital health.
Evaluate digital health innovations in relation to contemporary issues and problems faced in healthcare practices and propose appropriate solutions.
Compare and contrast digital health innovations with regards to their advantages and disadvantages.

title: COMMUNICATING DIGITAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the fundamental skills to communicate effectively in the digital age with internal and external stakeholders, such as healthcare professionals, administrative staff, government bodies, IT vendors, and patients, among others. You will explore different types of digital communication platforms including websites & social media to communicate with different healthcare audiences. You will also gain a deeper understanding of strategic digital communication planning for different types of digital health case studies and identified audiences.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate communication strategies and techniques to communicate professionally in a digital world
Critique how communication can be used as an effective tool to connect various healthcare audiences in the digital age
Justify the types of digital media tools needed to communicate to different healthcare audiences
Develop strategic communication plans on digital health issues for an identified audience

title: VIRTUAL CARE AND THE INTERNET OF MEDICAL THINGS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the evolution of virtual care models by learning the "art and science" behind virtual care applications and keeping abreast with the latest developments in technologies (including devices from the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)) used for health delivery. You will learn about the ethical challenges that are faced in this space. You will also evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of these technologies and understand the need to provide evidence-based virtual care.
learning_outcomes: Identify and synthesise ethical challenges in implementing virtual care models and IoMT devices.
Critically evaluate the quality of evidence for virtual care technologies and applications (including IoMT).
Identify and synthesise evidence to inform and implement virtual care solutions.
Critique the types of technologies and applications used for virtual care solutions (including IoMT).

title: GLOBALISATION AND DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: Globalisation is a process by which distant regions are increasingly linked, shaping our lives, and impacting on the fate of nations. We often think of globalisation primarily in terms of industry, trade and technology, but in this introductory level subject you will use the UN Sustainable Development Goals to take a broader view. We will explore some of the world's most pressing current problems, including but not limited to poverty and conflict, environmental degradation, gender equity, racism and access to health and well being. Case studies from a range of contexts, including Latin America, Africa, Asia, and Indigenous communities in Australia and the Pacific, will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the intersections, strengths, and limitations of key practice areas and sustainable development goals
Synthesise research and arguments related to approaches and objectives of sustainable development.
Research and summarize key perspectives and debates on globalisation and sustainable development
Demonstrate understanding of key trends, perspectives, approaches, and practices related to sustainable development.

title: DEVELOPMENT IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus on the practical skills used in development work. Guest speakers from various agencies share their experiences of the development field, providing you with an opportunity to draw on professional expertise. The subject is organised around the idea of the 'development project'. You are introduced to key development tools, processes and debates surrounding the implementation of development projects. On completion you will be familiar with grant proposal writing, practical tools used in development, and with debates about the best forms of development intervention.
