In this subject, you will develop and deploy a tool kit of practical techniques and strategies to address sustainability and development challenges that transcend borders, in culturally aware ways that promote community agency and social cohesion. You are encouraged to explore a particular region of interest, for example, Latin America, Africa, Asia or the Pacific. This is a level 3 subject. Please consider the subject pre-requisites before enrolling.
learning_outcomes: Write in a professional mode relevant to development aimed at contributing to a sustainable future.
Communicate knowledge and facilitate learning about a specific development tool in a group and reflect upon how methodological choices impact the public good and obligations to future generations.
Critically reflect on one's position in relation to "development practice" using texts and self-reflection.
Develop specific solutions to defined problems based on research and critical thinking.
Apply the principles of good development practice keeping in mind interactions between natural, socio-political, economic and cultural systems in a simulated project.

title: HOW SOCIAL CHANGE HAPPENS
syllabus_overview: This subject scrutinizes phenomena of social, political and economic change. It does so by combining the practical perspectives offered by Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), and other change agents, with the latest academic research from a wide range of disciplines. Students will learn the ways in which entities such as the government, the media and the business community may influence change, and are themselves targets for change. Students will also learn about how change agents define, negotiate, and pursue notions of social improvement, paying particular attention to the importance of coalition building, leadership, and activism. Over the semester, practitioners--coming from NGOs, Multilateral Organizations, Transnational Corporations, social enterprises, political and community organizations--will introduce students to relevant case studies, and share insights from their field experience. The subject is designed for students doing the Master of International Development, but it is relevant to students from the across the social sciences and health sciences.
learning_outcomes: Analyse strengths and weaknesses of relevant interventions
Demonstrate the application of concepts and theories of social change
Demonstrate an understanding of how different actors (such as NGOs, Governments, Media, Business influence social change and are themselves targets for social change.
Apply and critically evaluate contending theoretical perspectives on how social change occurs

title: MAKING DEVELOPMENT MATTER
syllabus_overview: This subject provides foundational knowledge and skills concerning the history and various perspectives on sustainable international and community development. Weekly topics will provide an opportunity for you to critically debate contemporary development perspectives on global issues such as poverty, sustainability, justice, social change and community, as well as question the relevance of concepts such as 'overseas' development assistance, capacity-building, and participatory development. The subject enables you to understand and critically evaluate the dynamics of change in the development sector, and generate new ideas about how development matters to people around the world.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge and research skills to evaluate contemporary development practice.
Critically evaluate contemporary perspectives on sustainable international development.
Understand key development concepts, practices, and organisations.

title: MAKING DEVELOPMENT MATTER
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to historical and contemporary approaches to and perspectives on sustainable international and community development. Weekly topics will provide an opportunity for you to critically debate evolving contemporary development perspectives on global issues such as poverty, sustainability, justice, social change and community, as well as question the relevance of concepts such as 'overseas' development assistance, capacity-building, and participatory development . The subject enables you to understand and question the dynamics of change in the development sector and the generation and effective management of new ideas about "making development matter". Through collaboration and effective communication you will further development their creativity in resolving complex development challenges and their capacity to apply theory, locate and synthesise knowledge resources, prioritise meaningful action, and manage associated risks.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate contemporary approaches, perspectives or debates in the theory and practice of sustainable international development.
Demonstrate an understanding of an important development concept, practice, debate or organisation.
Synthesise research and arguments on contemporary development practice.
Research and summarise knowledge on sustainable development-related topics.

title: DEVELOPMENT IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides foundational knowledge and skills about development practice for postgraduate coursework students. Guest speakers from various agencies share their experiences in the development field, providing you with an opportunity to draw on professional expertise. You are introduced to key development tools, processes and debates surrounding the implementation of development projects. On completion you will be familiar with grant proposal writing, practical tools used in development intervention, and with debates about the best forms of development intervention. In this subject, you will develop and deploy a tool kit of practical techniques and strategies to address sustainability and development challenges that transcend borders, in culturally aware ways that promote community agency and social cohesion.
learning_outcomes: Design specific solutions to defined problems based on advanced research and critical thinking.
Apply advanced knowledge of good development practice keeping in mind interactions between natural, socio-political, economic and cultural systems
Critically analyse "development practice" using texts and self-reflection.
Write professionally on development issues in order to contribute to a sustainable future.

title: HUMAN SECURITY AND DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject looks at human security from a humanitarian perspective. This subject challenges assumptions about aid and intervention, discussing the current trends that impact on humanitarian work In addition to examining the Human Security framework, students explore the international humanitarian system, developments in protecting civilians in armed conflict, civil-military interaction in complex emergencies and the Women, Peace and Security Agenda. Current developments such as the World Humanitarian Summit, the push towards innovation in humanitarian responses, and the focus on inclusive programming in disasters will also be explored. . This subject will be delivered in collaboration with a number of guest speakers.
learning_outcomes: Understand the way the concept of human security relates to humanitarian contexts.
Demonstrate advanced and integrated knowledge of the relevant humanitarian and legal frameworks for human security.
Understand some of the specific challenges to human security in humanitarian contexts.
Reflect on the appropriate responses to human security issues in humanitarian contexts.

title: CONTEMPORARY APPROACHES TO DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject we analyse the evolution of development theory. Central themes include growth-centred development, human development, post-development, gender and development, indigenous development, participatory development and alternative development. The development of each theory is placed in a historical perspective with the focus then moving to evaluating its contemporary influence on development theory and development practice. The subject has been designed for students doing the Master of International Development but it is relevant to other students in the social sciences, health sciences and business.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on approaches to development, based on texts.
Apply critical insight into development theories and approaches to selected development issues and themes.
Critically evaluate the central transitions and tensions in the practice of international development.
Communicate knowledge about development theories and approaches

title: INTRODUCTION TO NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will study the major food sources, functions and metabolism of macro-nutrients (protein, fat and carbohydrate), alcohol, and micro-nutrients (vitamins and minerals) and be aware of the consequences of over and under-nutrition. Principles of energy balance (energy intake and energy expenditure), basic techniques for assessment of nutrient adequacy of individual diets and simple techniques for assessing body composition in adults will be explored. You will also be introduced to the Australian Dietary Guidelines and Nutrient Reference Values, and the use of food guides in assessing the diets of populations. You will also be introduced to the Nutrition Society of Australia Competencies. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe the main food sources, structure, functions, digestion and absorption of macronutrients (protein, fat, carbohydrate), water and alcohol and discuss the consequences of macronutrient imbalances.
Describe the role of the Australian Dietary Guidelines in health, and the application of food guides in assessing diets of populations.
Apply simple techniques to measure body composition of individuals.
Apply simple dietary analysis techniques to assess diets.
Identify and describe common food sources, functions and absorption of micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) and discuss the causes and consequences of micronutrient deficiencies and toxicities.
Describe methods for collecting dietary intake and estimating energy expenditure, and use principles of energy balance to determine an individual's energy balance status.

title: CHEMISTRY OF FOOD AND COOKING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the fundamentals of food chemistry relevant for the study of human nutrition science including composition, structure and function of food, chemistry of key food molecules such as macro and micro nutrients. Also the physical, chemical, nutritional and sensory changes in preparation, cooking and storage of food.
learning_outcomes: Describe the link between food groups/commodities and the chemistry of key macro and micronutrients.
Understand and demonstrate how to prepare and cook food in a manner that meets Australian food safety standards and apply principles of food chemistry.
Identify the chemical reactions of key macro and micronutrients in the deterioration of food.
Demonstrate an understanding of the roles and composition of key macro and micronutrients, water, and alcohol in foods and drinks
Describe the chemical reactions and interactions that occur between nutrients in foods during cooking, as well as physical changes.

title: FOOD SECURITY AND SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the Australian and global food systems and will explore key stakeholders that influence our food supply such as government, food industry, consumers, the healthcare industry, and other NGOs. Through a series of activities, the students will begin to unpack the complex relationships between sustainability and food and nutrition security and how they relate to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Students will identify the bi-directional interplay between key food commodities, human health and environmental sustainability and their impact on vulnerable communities. In this subject, students will also learn about traditional food ways, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait islander food ways, and other dietary patterns and their contribution to a sustainable food system.
learning_outcomes: Outline the principles of sustainable diets based on the diet for planetary health and traditional food ways/dietary patterns.

Summarise the bi-directional relationship between key food commodities, food choices, human health and environmental sustainability with a focus on food and nutrition security in Australia and globally.
Identify the components of and stakeholders influencing the food system in Australia and globally.
Describe the impact of the environment, climate change and global events on the food supply and how it relates to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: INTRODUCTION TO NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will study the major food sources and the functions of macronutrients (energy, protein, fat and carbohydrate) and micro- nutrients (vitamins and minerals). Principles of energy balance (energy intake and energy expenditure), basic techniques for assessment of nutrient adequacy of individual diets and simple techniques for assessing body composition will be explored. You will also be introduced to the Australian Dietary Guidelines and the use of food guides in assessing the diets of populations.
learning_outcomes: Apply simple dietary analysis techniques to assess diets.
Identify and describe the main food sources of macronutrients ( protein, fat, carbohydrate and alcohol)
Use the basic principles of energy balance to determine an individual's energy balance status.
Apply simple techniques to measure body composition of individuals.
Identify and describe common food sources of selected micronutrients (vitamins and minerals).
Describe the role of the Australian Dietary Guidelines in health, and the application of food guides in assessing diets of populations.

title: SPORT AND EXERCISE NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn the essentials of sport and exercise nutrition that improve and sustain optimal performance of athletes and active individuals. This subject will cover topics including nutrition for training and competition, sports foods and supplements; nutrition for specific sports and life stages and current issues in sports nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the nutritional demands of athletic performance across a variety of sports
Analyse the nutritional demands of athletic performance across a variety of life stages
Assess and apply evidence-based literature regarding current issues in sports nutrition.
Demonstrate an understanding of professional scope of practice in relation to nutrition and where referral to other health professionals is warranted.
Apply literacy and communication skills to translate scientific information effectively to a wide variety of audiences

title: PRINCIPLES OF HUMAN NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the major food sources, metabolism and storage of the major food molecules carbohydrate, protein and fat (the macronutrients), alcohol, vitamins and minerals (the micronutrients), and water, and be aware of the consequences of over and under-nutrition. You will also develop an understanding of the principles of energy balance. Students will be introduced to techniques for measuring and evaluating nutrient adequacy of diets of individuals and populations, including the use of nutrient databases, nutrient reference standards and food guides. You will also be introduced to simple techniques for measuring body composition of adults.
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe sources, functions and absorption of micronutrients and discuss the causes and consequences of micronutrient deficiencies and toxicities.
Demonstrate comprehension of national nutrient and food based dietary recommendations and apply these recommendations to assess dietary adequacy.
Apply lab techniques to analyse food and biological samples, including resolving unexpected outcomes and interpreting results with referral to nutritional status implications.
Analyse dietary intake of individuals using food composition databases and dietary analysis software.
Explain, evaluate, and apply techniques to measure the body composition of individuals.
Explain and critique methods for collecting dietary intake and estimating energy expenditure and apply these methods to determine an individual's energy balance status.
Identify and describe the structure, metabolism and digestion, sources, and functions of macronutrients, alcohol and water, and discuss the consequences of macronutrient imbalances.

title: NUTRITION FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the major food sources, metabolism and storage of the major food molecules carbohydrate, protein and fat (the macronutrients), alcohol, vitamins and minerals (the micronutrients), and water, and be aware of the consequences of over and under-nutrition. You will also develop an understanding of the principles of energy balance. You will be introduced to techniques for measuring and evaluating nutrient adequacy of diets of individuals and populations, including the use of nutrient databases, nutrient reference standards and food guides. You will also be introduced to simple techniques for measuring body composition of adults.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate comprehension of national nutrient and food based dietary recommendations and apply these recommendations to assess dietary adequacy.
Analyse dietary intake of individuals using food composition databases and dietary analysis software.
Explain and evaluate techniques for the measurement of body composition of individuals.
Identify and describe the structure, metabolism and digestion, sources, and functions of macronutrients, water and alcohol and discuss the consequences of macronutrient imbalances.
Identify and describe the sources, functions and absorption of micronutrients and discuss the causes and consequences of micronutrient deficiencies and toxicities.
Explain and critique methods for collecting dietary intake and estimating energy expenditure and apply these methods to determine an individual's energy balance status.

title: NUTRITION EDUCATION FOR ADULTS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on how to interpret the nutrition priorities of target audiences, understanding their educational needs and use learning and education principles and science translation approaches to translate nutrition science for everyday audiences. Using the Program Management Cycle, you will systematically approach nutrition education and develop a suite of nutrition education resources for specific community groups. This is a practical skills subject that supports your development and delivery of nutrition information for the benefit of community members.
learning_outcomes: Apply learning and educational principles and nutrition science translation and communication approaches to design and deliver group nutrition education sessions
Analyse and interpret the health, food, nutrition and socio-cultural factors affecting nutrition outcomes for priority groups to determine nutrition needs in Australian contexts.
Develop a nutrition education intervention to influence the food and nutrition for a target audience through application of a systematic program planning approach.
Participate in reflective practice as part of developing personal practice, recognising limitations of practice, providing and responding to feedback.
Apply learning and educational principles and nutrition science translation and communication approaches to design and use nutrition education resources and materials.

title: NUTRITION ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you’ll develop essential knowledge and practical skills in nutrition assessment, equipping you to evaluate the dietary adequacy and nutritional status of individuals and populations. Through a deeper understanding of Nutrition Asessment as the first step in the Nutrition Care Process, you will explore a range of assessment techniques, including dietary intake analysis using nutrient databases, reference standards, and food guides, as well as methods for assessing body composition and understanding energy balance. In addition to these technical skills, you’ll strengthen your ability to communicate nutrition assessment data effectively, while developing a clear understanding of professional identity and the scope of practice for nutrition health professionals. The subject highlights the importance of interprofessional collaboration and appropriate referral pathways in practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Explain and evaluate methods used to measure and estimate energy balance, energy expenditure, physical activity and fitness, body mass, and body composition.

Apply principles of nutrition and dietary assessment, including quantitative and qualitative dietary analysis methods to population groups and individuals, and analyse the suitability of methodologies across a range of scenarios.
Recognise and assess own limitations and demonstrate the ability to refer to other professionals in accordance with nutrition professionals scope of practice and values.
Communicate physical and dietary assessment outcomes in a culturally sensitive, ethical, and honest manner to maintain the integrity and dignity of nutrition professionals and the individual.

title: DIET DISEASE RELATIONSHIPS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the relationships between nutrition and disease. You will explore key diseases in which nutritional factors have a role in the aetiology (as a platform for future studies in the prevention and management of nutrition-related diseases). You will consolidate skills in critical appraisal of the scientific literature in relation to the pathophysiology of nutrition-related disease. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award
learning_outcomes: Critically review the role of nutrition in the aetiology of given diseases to identify population groups at increased or reduced risk and explain the associated epidemiological evidence and pathophysiology.
Apply critical thinking to identify foods/nutrients that may be protective in preventing disease and explain the proposed mechanisms and evidence
Critically appraise a scientific paper examining the role of nutritional factors in the aetiology of a disease.

title: NUTRITION PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject allows students to extend their formal academic learning beyond the classroom. Students complete a minimum of 80 hours of placement or experiential learning combined with academic activities that require reflection on self-efficacy, skill application and skill development. This subject provides students with opportunities to apply and adapt their skills to a real-world environment, whether in the workplace, or in an international setting or via online practice-based projects with industry to develop employability skills and build networks. This subject brings together the expertise of industry partners and La Trobe University staff to benefit of students' professional development. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Develop graduate capabilities of autonomy, inquiry and analytical skills in preparation for and within a professional environment.
Apply complex theoretical and practical nutrition and food or broader health knowledge and skills in a real-world setting.
Appraise learning through a critical reflection relevant to a professional in a fieldwork setting.
Apply effective communication skills, professional attitudes and ethical behaviour in new professional or cultural environments.

title: SOCIETY, FOOD HABITS AND CONSUMPTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an informed understanding of the many factors influencing food, food use and food habits for individuals, communities and populations. These will include personal, social, cultural, environmental, economic and political factors. Through readings and media, discussion and assignments, you will review cuisines from a variety of cultures. An understanding of how the role of food has changed from ancient times to present day will be developed, and you will be introduced to factors influencing patterns and trends in food consumption worldwide.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the socio-cultural influences on food habits, food behaviour, and consumption trends.
Critically evaluate the history and future of food, both from a worldwide and Australian perspective.
Analyse and communicate the impact of sociological factors on the food choices of individuals, groups, communities, populations, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Assess the influences of food policy, food technology, ecology and agriculture on Australian and worldwide food systems.

title: NUTRITION RESEARCH MINOR PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will undertake a small nutrition-related research project. The project will provide you with experience and skills in project management, data collection, data analysis and interpretation, critical analysis, and preparation of a scientific report. You are expected to attend workshops, work independently in self- directed learning, and meet regularly with your project supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise the literature related to project area
Apply the principles of ethical conduct of research
Clearly communicate research findings through written and oral formats to a variety of audiences
Design and implement a data collection tool, and gain practical skills in data collection
Analyse and interpret data using simple statistical techniques

title: NUTRITIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY AND RESEARCH SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of the fundamentals of epidemiology and epidemiological study designs and research concepts. These will be of direct relevance to the role of food and nutrition in the prevention, causation and management of disease. Nutrition measurement techniques for the assessment of diet and body composition of individuals and populations will be covered in depth. You will cover sources of data on mortality and morbidity, measures of disease prevalence, incidence and risk, chance, bias and confounding variables of relevance to nutritional epidemiology. Standard parametric and non-parametric statistical techniques will be reviewed, and you will have the opportunity to use statistical software programs to analyse a population dataset.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate skills and techniques to manage data related to dietary intake, anthropometry and body composition.
Analyse small population datasets using biostatistics and interpret results in accordance with the NHMRC ethical code of conduct.
Appraise different study designs used in nutritional epidemiology.
Apply understanding of terms and definitions used in epidemiology, and concepts of measurements of disease.

title: APPLIED FOOD SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with detailed knowledge of how food processing impacts individual food components and offers the opportunity to apply nutrition and food science knowledge in the development of a food product. Through a series of activities, students will critically examine the processes involved in producing foods for human consumption with a focus on food safety, sustainability, and various changes (biological, chemical, physical, and/or nutritional) that occur at key points of the food supply chain. Students will work in groups using user-centred design approaches to design or reformulate a market-ready food product that meets market trends, incorporates sustainable practices, and complies with the Food Standards Code. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Utilise an approach to food product development which integrates the key components of the food system notably consumer demand, food regulations and labelling laws, environmental sustainability, food processing, nutrition science, and innovations in food science.
Discuss the complexities of sustainability in food production, processing, manufacturing, and distribution for key food commodities.

Work collaboratively to develop or re-formulate, package, label and market 'suitable for sale' food product that meet market and consumer trends, specific nutritional criteria and comply with the Food Standards Code.
Analyse the chemical, physical, sensory, and nutritional changes to food along the food supply chain including food production, preservation, packaging, and transport.
Analyse food safety and food preservation practices that are commonly used in food production for the control of key pathogens and spoilage microorganisms.

title: NUTRITION THROUGHOUT LIFE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of nutrition requirements and physiological changes across the lifespan: pre-conception, pregnancy and foetal development, lactation, infancy, toddlerhood, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and ageing. You will also learn about food and nutrition dietary patterns across the different life stages. You will be able to combine prior nutritional and biosciences knowledge and skills to gain a more in depth understanding of human nutritional needs, and habits/practices/behaviours.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and critically review the physiological differences / changes occurring during different stages of the life span.
Evaluate and critically review the dietary/nutritional issues and habits and behaviours of particular relevance to each life stage group.
Analyse and critically review the nutritional requirements for preconception, pregnancy, lactation, infants, children, adolescents, adults & older persons.

title: NUTRITION FOR SPORTS PERFORMANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn the essentials of human nutrition that improve and sustain optimal performance for sport and exercise for athletes and active individuals. This subject will cover topics including assessment of energy needs, dietary intake and body composition in athletes; training and competition nutrition, sports foods and supplements; nutrition for specific sports and life stages and current issues in sports nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Assess and apply evidence-based literature regarding current issues and practices in sports nutrition.
Appraise and critique the evidence and application of food, supplements and sports foods to athletes in a variety of sports and life stages.
Evaluate and assess the nutritional demands of athletic performance in a variety of sports and life stages.
Demonstrate an understanding of professional scope of practice in relation to nutrition and where referral to other health professionals is warranted
Demonstrate well developed literacy and communication skills suitable for a variety of key stakeholders and audiences.

title: ADVANCES IN NUTRITIONAL SCIENCE AND NUTRIGENOMICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will build on knowledge gained in first and second year nutrition subjects. It discusses advanced topics in nutritional sciences focussing on the most recent nutrition research and current topics in the media, as well as emerging nutrition related issues. The subject also addresses nutrition's impact on health, chronic disease prevention and management.
learning_outcomes: Investigate contemporary and emerging topics in nutritional science, and critically reflect upon their role in health management.
Evaluate and critique nutritional messages in various forms of media communication to identify communication bias and develop skills in objective health communications.
Demonstrate critical understanding of key concepts and potential applications in the field of nutrigenomics and personalised nutrition.

title: ADVANCED FOOD SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be able to advance your food skills by translating your skills and complex knowledge of nutrition science, public health principles and food systems into recipes and dishes for diverse populations using a variety of food and cooking techniques. You will also reflect on your food knowledges and food skills and how they impact on your current and future practice. This subject is delivered in a blended mode including online learning and practical classes in a teaching kitchen in Melbourne. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Use food and cooking to deliver simple, safe and evidence-based nutrition messages, in line with the Australian Dietary guidelines, to a specific population.

Translate knowledge of nutrition science, Australian dietary guidelines and food laws, sustainability, food science, socio-ecological model of health, and latest evidence into recipes, dishes and special foods to address the National Health Priority Areas,
Reflect on own food knowledges and skills in relation to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander food and food practices and formulate relevant learning goals to inform future practice.
Co-design recipes and dishes with culturally and linguistically diverse people and discuss the significance of food and eating across a range of cultures in Australia.

title: HONOURS IN NUTRITION B
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will develop research skills to independently conduct a research project in their chosen area of nutrition and report the findings of their work in a scientific format. The skills and capabilities gained in this year-long subject include independent thinking, critical evaluation of literature, selection of appropriate experimental designs, practical application of nutrition research tools, data analysis and interpretation, and oral and written communication of findings. The full program lasts approximately 9 months and starts early February.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate research findings in written and oral format.
Critically appraise the literature related to a given project area to formulate project aims and methods.
Apply principles of ethical research conduct to project implementation.
Develop skills in the design and conduct of nutrition research
Analyse and interpret data using appropriate statistical techniques.

title: EPIDEMIOLOGY AND RESEARCH SKILLS FOR NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of the fundamentals of epidemiology and epidemiological study designs and research concepts. These will be of direct relevance to the role of food and nutrition in the prevention, causation and management of disease. Nutrition measurement techniques for the assessment of diet and body composition of individuals and populations will be covered in depth. You will cover sources of data on mortality and morbidity, measures of disease prevalence, incidence and risk, chance, bias and confounding variables of relevance to nutritional epidemiology. Standard parametric and non-parametric statistical techniques will be reviewed, and you will have the opportunity to use statistical software programs to analyse a population dataset.
learning_outcomes: Apply understanding of terms and definitions used in epidemiology, and concepts of measurements of disease.
Analyse small population datasets using biostatistics and interpret results in accordance with the NHMRC ethical code of conduct.
Appraise different study designs used in nutritional epidemiology.
Apply appropriate skills and techniques to manage data related to dietary intake, anthropometry and body composition.

title: SPORTS NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn the essentials of human nutrition that improve and sustain optimal performance for sport and exercise for athletes and active individuals. This subject will cover topics including assessment of energy needs, dietary intake and body composition in athletes; training and competition nutrition, sports foods and supplements; nutrition for specific sports and life stages and current issues in sports nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and critique the evidence and application of food supplements and sports foods to athletes in a variety of sports foods and life stages.
Apply literacy and communication skills to translate scientific information effectively to a wide variety of audiences
Assess and apply evidence-based literature regarding current issues in sports nutrition.
Evaluate and assess the nutritional demands of athletic performance across a variety of sports and life stages.
Demonstrate an understanding of professional scope of practice in relation to nutrition and where referral to other health professionals is warranted

title: APPLIED RESEARCH IN NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply your research skills to real-life or industry projects. Working in a group you will plan and conduct the project and analyse and interpret the data collected. Individually and as a group, you will be expected to apply critical thinking skills and creativity when communicating the project outcomes and recommendations to relevant stakeholders or industry.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and justify outcomes and/or recommendations which are supported by relevant scientific nutrition evidence and acknowledge the strengths and limitations of nutrition-related research methodology.
Apply the principles of ethical conduct of research and standards of ethics for nutrition professionals.
Communicate scientifically, truthfully and professionally to disseminate the project outcomes and/or recommendations to a range of stakeholders.

Design and conduct a feasible and small-scale nutrition project that is informed on contemporary nutrition evidence, uses relevant nutrition assessment skills, and uses appropriate data analysis methods to solve a real-world scenario.

title: ADVANCED MEDICAL NUTRITION THERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject extends your learning from DTN5002 to consolidate and progress knowledge of medical nutrition therapy and the nutrition care process. You will learn about the management of a range of diseases and conditions and be introduced to advanced practice skills related to collaborative decision making, shared responsibility and shared vision within and across teams. Further, you will explore the incorporation of technologies, such as telehealth, into the nutrition care process. You will advance skills related to the nutrition care process by simulating nutrition monitoring and evaluation. This subject is taught at the city campus as a number of lectures will be delivered by clinical dietetics experts who work in large tertiary hospitals across metropolitan Melbourne. You will undertake two full day observational placements at a metropolitan Melbourne Hospital. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise information to develop advanced care plans, discharge plans and referrals to other services where appropriate, in accordance with jurisdictional legislation, policy or standards
Critically evaluate and explore a variety of tools and technologies to support the nutrition care process.
Critically reflect on complex diet – disease relationships and demonstrate an understanding of this in professional practice.
Perform nutrition assessments, demonstrating problem-solving, clinical reasoning and tailored approaches for individuals.
Systematically implement, evaluate and adapt nutrition care plans, programs and services in accordance with legislation, policy or standards.

Critically evaluate the roles, responsibilities, and priorities of interprofessional team members and employ collaborative practice to create nutrition plans that meet the shared vision of healthcare teams

title: DIETETIC PRACTICE AND COUNSELLING SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the foundations of dietetic practice, including scope of practice, diversity of dietetic roles, professional behaviours, the national competency standards for dietitians and the importance of reflective practice and lifelong learning. You will develop communication and counselling skills for effective dietetic practice to engage and empower people as equal partners in their healthcare. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and apply counselling behaviour change theory in food and nutrition contexts.

Evaluate the foundations of dietetic practice, including scope of practice, professional behaviours, the national competency standards for dietitians and perform critical reflective practice to construct an emerging professional Dietitian Identity.

Develop and implement evidence-based communication strategies tailored to individuals' diverse health literacy levels and preferences, fostering active engagement and empowerment in healthcare decision-making processes.
Critically reflect on the impact of emotions on practice and devise strategies to take responsibility for managing personal health and wellbeing.
Critically evaluate processes for the collection, assessment and interpretation of athropometric, clinic and dietary data of individuals.
Recognise strength-based approaches for culturally safe communication to foster trust and building of respectful relationship with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

title: MEDICAL NUTRITION THERAPY
syllabus_overview: The focus of this subject is on teaching you the key medical nutrition therapy and practice skills required to practice as a dietitian, including collecting data from clients and building clinical knowledge to formulate and modify intervention plans. In this subject, you will be introduced to the concept of medical nutrition therapy. You will learn about diet-disease relationships and how to locate, evaluate and apply evidence-based guidelines for the dietary management of a range of conditions. You will be introduced to the nutrition care process (nutrition assessment, nutrition diagnoses, nutrition intervention, nutrition monitoring and evaluation). This subject is taught at the city campus as a number of lectures will be delivered by clinical dietetics experts who work in large tertiary hospitals across metropolitan Melbourne.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on diet-disease relationships and medical nutrition therapy guidelines and demonstrate understanding in professional practice
Collect and interpret medical, cultural, social, psychological, economic, personal, environmental, and dietary information using established nutrition assessment methods.
Synthesize relevant nutrition assessment data to determine the nutrition status of individuals and make appropriate nutrition diagnoses.
Develop and effectively communicate nutrition care plans to accepted standards for relevant audiences.
Integrate nutrition assessment data and use clinical reasoning to prioritise key issues, formulate goals and objectives, and prepare individualised, realistic nutrition intervention plans.
Implement appropriate nutrition education and counselling intervention strategies based on outcomes of nutrition assessment.

title: EMPLOYABILITY IN NUTRITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore various nutrition-related career pathways and you will learn workplace specific problem-solving skills and professional communication to enhance your employability.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate the rationale for decisions made in workplace environments.
Apply initiative and judgement to problem-solving in workplace environments
Analyse various discipline-specific career pathways in the field of nutrition science.
Appraise personal practice to identify areas for improvement in professional communication and workplace problem solving skills.

title: DIETETICS FOR A DIVERSE SOCIETY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the diversity of the society we live in and how diversity impacts on health and dietetic practice. You will learn about principles of public health nutrition including the socio-ecological approach to health prevention. This subject will equip you to advocate for ethical and evidence-based solutions to address the nutrition-related health of individuals, groups and communities. You will critically analyse and apply the nutrition care process in public health settings. You will learn about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander history and colonisation. In addition, you will engage with individuals with lived experiences of marginalisation to learn about systems of power, privilege, and oppression and undertake self-reflection to understand your place in these systems. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Develop teamwork strategies to effectively perform duties related to curriculum groupwork as part of developing professional practice
Critically analyse and reflect upon social, historical and political significance of a range of cultural food practices and foodways exploring implications for communities and dietitians.

Critically reflect on colonisation, systemic racism, and the social, cultural, behavioural, and economic factors which impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples’ health outcomes and demonstrate an understanding of how this might influence dietetic practice and outcomes.
Evaluate the factors that influence public health nutrition priorities and critically appraise current public health nutrition priorities and programs in Australia.
Critically appraise socio-ecological approaches in health promotion and public health nutrition that aim to influence population nutritional status.

Acknowledge and critically reflect on the ways in which your own culture, values, beliefs, attitudes, biases, assumptions, privilege and power may influence your dietetic practice and critically appraise social structures which perpetuate systems of power and oppression, and the impacts of these systems on diverse peoples and communities.

title: DIETETICS FOR MENTAL HEALTH, DISABILITY AND AGED CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will use three emerging areas of dietetic practice – Mental Health, Disability and Aged Care – as a conceptual framework to explore advanced practice dietetic skills, including those related to: working within interdisciplinary teams; person-centred care, working with carers and translators; prioritisation and advocacy; the impact of medications on nutrition care planning. You will explore the bidirectional relationship between clinical, social, economic, psychological and personal factors in ageing populations and individuals with a disability or experiencing mental health concerns. You will also explore the bidirectional relationship between nutrition and mental health. Using relevant examples, you will develop an understanding of modifiable and non-modifiable factors that influence the human gut microbiome, and the role of the gut microbiome in mediating the efficacy of dietary interventions. You will practice modifying foods for vulnerable populations in kitchen practicals.
learning_outcomes: Critically review and reflect upon opportunities, roles and skills required for dietitians to improve health outcomes in emerging dietetic workforce sectors such as aged care, mental health and disability

Create nutrition plans and/or programs that demonstrate an understanding of the practical, cognitive, pharmacological and dietary issues impacting older people and people with mental health concerns and disabilities
Critically evaluate and apply collaborative practice and advanced communication and counselling skills for priority populations, and their health care teams, families, carers and interpreters.
Develop strategies to effectively and safely respond to disclosure of mental health concerns.
Develop and apply key dietetic practice skills, including interprofessional practice, advocacy and prioritisation, to improve the food and nutrition of priority populations

title: FOOD SERVICE MANAGEMENT THEORY AND PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to food service management theory and practice. You will apply the nutrition care process in the food system setting. You will learn about systems thinking in food supply and food service management and food regulation. You will develop an understanding of the processes and resources required to feed populations in a range of institutionalized settings through 15 days of intensive placement activity. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Use a systems thinking approach to critically appraise environmental sustainability issues, food legislation, regulations, and standards to promote and advocate for safe and nutritious food systems.
Critically evaluate and demonstrate an understanding of foodservice systems and processes.
Apply organisational, business and management skills in food service management, and describe the roles and responsibilities of individuals working in food service.

Apply the principles of food chemistry and nutrition science to critically analyse and modify foods, recipes and menus in accordance with nutrition standards and the medical, personal, economic and cultural needs of individuals and groups.
Conduct critical self-reflection, demonstrating insight and self-awareness and ability to adapt practice in response to feedback from supervisors, peers, and mentors.
Assess and mitigate risks, incidents, and errors for food service, including managing HACCP plans, food safety programs, and allergen management, in accordance with codes of practice.

Collaborate with food service stakeholders to systematically implement the Nutrition Care Process in food service management through the design, delivery and dissemination of an ethical food service systems project using a systematic program approach.

title: PUBLIC HEALTH NUTRITION PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will complete 25 days of placement in a professional practice setting focused on a public health nutrition project underpinned by the socio-ecological approach to health. Successful completion of this subject requires assessment of performance commensurate with relevant National Competency Standards for Dietitians. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply a systematic program management approach to conduct, appraise and disseminate an ethical public health nutrition project that is grounded in socio-ecological theory.
Employ a variety of workplace communication strategies to effectively convey public health approaches to lay and professional audiences.
Develop interpersonal skills to build the capacity of and collaborate with peers, colleagues, and stakeholders, to improve nutrition and health outcomes
Perform critical self-reflection, demonstrating insight and self-awareness and ability to adapt practice in response to feedback from supervisors, peers, and mentors.

title: PROFESSIONAL DIETETIC PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will complete 50 days of placement focused on the application of medical nutrition therapy and communications skills in individual case management. Placement will take place across a range of settings where individual case management occurs including hospital and community settings. You will apply your clinical knowledge, counselling skills and the nutrition care process to support the nutrition-related health of individuals. Successful completion of this subject requires assessment of performance commensurate with relevant National Competency Standards for Dietitians. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Perform individual case management in a consistently safe, ethical, and legal manner.
Exhibit high-level interpersonal and written and oral communication skills in interactions with people from various cultural, socioeconomic, organisational, and professional backgrounds.
Critically reflect on and demonstrate leadership and organisational skills, cultural safety, and responsiveness in individual case management settings
Collaborate within and across teams to influence food systems and improve the nutrition and health outcomes of individual clients.
Perform critical self-reflection, demonstrating insight and self-awareness and ability to adapt practice in response to feedback from supervisors, peers, and mentors.

Critically evaluate and consistently demonstrate an understanding of diet-disease relationships and medical nutrition therapy guidelines to develop individual nutrition care plans that consider client’s priorities, dietary preferences and diverse personal needs.

title: APPLIED RESEARCH SKILLS IN DIVERSE PRACTICE SETTINGS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will participate in an inquiry-based project in a professional practice setting. Research may occur in a range of settings where dietitians may be employed such as: hospitals, community health, private practice, aged care, higher education providers, Non-government organisations and professional sport settings. The subject allows you to undertake an applied research project that aligns with an area of interest. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the impact of research findings and advocate for the role that research in nutrition and dietetics plays in improving health.
Collect, analyse and interpret qualitative and quantitative research, evaluation, and quality-management data.
Develop effective written and oral communication strategies to disseminate research findings to key stakeholders such as health professional peers, industry partners and clients
Perform critical self-reflection, demonstrating insight and self-awareness and ability to adapt practice in response to feedback from supervisors, peers, and mentors.
Develop effective teamwork strategies to effectively perform duties in a research team
Critically evaluate and apply ethical processes and established research methods to the conduct of research, evaluation, and quality management processes in professional practice settings.

title: ECONOMIC DATA ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: Economic analysis involves understanding and interpreting a vast amount of information. As an economist, you need to be able to source and interpret the data relevant for advising government or firms. You will need to be able to describe and present this information so that policy makers, managers and other stakeholders can understand it. In this subject you will develop hands on experience with real-world data to assist in developing solutions to contemporary issues in society You will learn to connect the theoretical aspects of economics to the empirical techniques for analysing and interpreting data.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the role of data analysis in effective economic decision-making and its relationship to economic theory.
Research and interpret real-world data as part of a team to critically analyse economic statistics.
Use data analysis tools to calculate descriptive statistics and inferential statistics for economic policy analysis.
Effectively communicate potential solutions to an economic problem with statistical techniques and data analysis.

title: EMPLOYABILITY BUSINESS AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP SKILLS FOR DIETITIANS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on work done at the start of your degree and consolidate your understanding of dietetics as a profession and what it means to practice professionally as a dietitian. Specific topics covered will include professional practice, ethics, entrepreneurship, leadership, management, working in teams, navigating processes for setting up your own business in dietetics, applying for and performing in work roles, and advanced emotional regulation, self-care and burnout prevention, identification and management. You will finalise your competency portfolio to demonstrate how you have achieved each of the National Competency Standards for Dietitians in Australia, prepare a job application for a new graduate role, and develop a group business plan. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Create strategies for dietitian self-care and emotional regulation to ensure client safety and prevent dietitian burnout.

Appraise business and entrepreneurial opportunities for dietitians and evaluate and apply specialist organisational, business, leadership, marketing and management skills required in the broad landscape of dietetic practice.
Create applications for entry-level nutrition and dietetic jobs and create a personal development plan in preparation for future, aspirational roles
Critically reflect and provide evidence for attainment of Dietitians Australia National Competency Standards

title: SPECIALISED AND FUTURE READY DIETETICS
syllabus_overview: This subject will focus on specialist areas of dietetic practice and the importance of lifelong learning, so you are prepared to tackle future-focused challenges and work in new ways, incorporating novel technologies and emerging science and evidence into your practice. This subject focuses especially on two future-ready issues for our profession: environmental sustainability and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health. It will encourage you to consider the future of dietetic practice and identify opportunities and advocate for change to the wider social, cultural, political, and environmental issues to improve nutrition and the food system. This subject will also consolidate your understanding of the ways in which education and health systems can impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People’s health with a view to bridging the gaps that currently exist in health outcomes. This subject will enable you to explore a future-focussed area of personal interest in dietetics by engaging with literature and experts in your area of interest. You will further practice skills related to leadership, advocacy, conflict resolution and teamwork
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate independence, leadership, negotiation, conflict resolution, problem solving, professional conduct and responsibility for own actions in familiar and unfamiliar settings in professional practice/contexts.
Apply advanced client-centred counselling skills to negotiate and facilitate nutrition, behaviour and lifestyle change and empower clients with self-management skills.
Develop effective teamwork strategies AND demonstrate effective professionalism, collaboration, proactivity, responsibility, and accountability to achieve a shared goal.

Critically review and reflect on the impact of whole systems including health and education as responsible for improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health and collaborate with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander individuals and/or communities to advocate for social justice and health equity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Critically evaluate and construct a systems-thinking approach to environmental sustainability issues with a key focus on food, nutrition and health.
Reflect on future dietetic practice and identify opportunities and advocate for change to the wider social, cultural, political, and environmental issues to improve nutrition, and the food system

title: FUTURE READY AND SPECIALISED DIETETIC PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject will focus on specialist areas of dietetic practice and the importance of lifelong learning so you are prepared to tackle future-focused challenges and work in new ways, incorporating novel technologies and emerging science and evidence into your practice. In this subject, you will further develop practice skills related to leadership, advocacy, conflict resolution and teamwork. This subject includes core content that focuses on two future-ready issues for the Dietetics profession: environmental sustainability and Aboriginal and Torres Strait-Islander health. This core content will encourage you to consider the future of dietetic practice and identify opportunities and advocate for change to the wider social, cultural, political, and environmental issues to improve nutrition and the food system. Further, this content will also consolidate your understanding of the ways in which education and health systems can impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People’s health with a view to bridging the gaps that currently exist in health outcomes. In addition to undertaking core content, in this subject you will undertake additional, in depth study in a specialised area of dietetic practice, which may include areas such as: Sports Nutrition, Eating Disorders or Paediatric Dietetics. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced client-centred counselling skills to negotiate and facilitate nutrition, behaviour and lifestyle change and empower clients with self-management skills.

Demonstrate independence, leadership, negotiation, conflict resolution, problem solving, professional conduct and responsibility for own actions in familiar and unfamiliar settings in professional practice/contexts.

Critically review and reflect on the impact of whole systems including health and education as responsible for improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health and collaborate with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander individuals and/or communities to advocate for social justice and health equity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Develop effective teamwork strategies AND demonstrate effective professionalism, collaboration, proactivity, responsibility, and accountability to achieve a shared goal.
Reflect on future dietetic practice and identify opportunities and advocate for change to the wider social, cultural, political, and environmental issues to improve nutrition, and the food system
Critically evaluate and construct a systems-thinking approach to environmental sustainability issues with a key focus on food, nutrition and health.
Apply advanced knowledge in a specialised dietetic practice area to demonstrate high quality client nutrition care planning

title: ECONOMETRICS
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the necessary skills in statistical and econometric techniques to carry out independent empirical research. This subject presents the theory of multiple regression used to estimate and test the validity of economic and financial relationships. You will study OLS estimation, the Gauss-Markov Theorem, diagnostic tests and GLS estimation. You will also study the applications of these techniques to various empirical examples using Econometrics software.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of statistical formulas and apply them to specific example.
Use a statistical software package to estimate a model using economic and financial data and carry out and hypothesis tests.
Demonstrate an understanding of the properties of good estimators, the Gauss-Markov Theorem and the assumptions required.
Effectively communicate the results of the model estimation.
Critically analyse a statistically estimated model of economic or financial relationship.

title: ECONOMIC DATA ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: Economic analysis involves understanding and interpreting a vast amount of information. As an economist, you will need to be able to source and interpret relevant data for advising governments or firms. You will also be expected to describe and present this information so that policy makers, managers and other stakeholders can understand it. In this subject you will develop hands on experience with real-world data to assist in developing solutions to contemporary issues in society. You will learn to connect the theoretical aspects of economics to the empirical techniques for analysing and interpreting data, allowing you to develop and critically evaluate economic policies.
learning_outcomes: Use data analysis tools and empirical techniques to summarise important information and provide inferential statistics for economic policy analysis.
Research and interpret real-world data and use this information to critically analyse economic issues.
Effectively communicate policy solutions to problems using statistical techniques and data analysis.
Analyse the role of data analysis in effective economic decision-making and its relationship to economic theory.

title: RECESSIONS, INFLATION AND ECONOMIC GROWTH
syllabus_overview: In Recessions, Inflation and Economic Growth, you will get to know the economy as a whole. You will apply simple models to better understand the driving forces of phenomena such as inflation, unemployment, economic growth, foreign debt, and the current account deficit; and discover about their effects on our prosperity and wellbeing. Importantly, you will explore the effectiveness and desirability of policymakers' responses to various economic situations via monetary and fiscal policy. For example, you will discuss whether and when should the central bank change the interest rate, whether the government should run surpluses or deficits, and many other real world relevant questions.
learning_outcomes: Present arguments about macroeconomics concepts and propose possible policy solutions.
Describe the aggregate-demand-and-supply model, and utilize it for analysis of developments in the macroeconomy and policy solutions
Interpret changes in national income, cost of living, exchange rates, the financial system and labour markets over time, and discuss their impact on people’s wellbeing.
Identify and distinguish the key characteristic of monetary and fiscal policies, and assess their implications for inflation, unemployment and economic growth.

title: CONSUMERS, FIRMS AND COMPETITION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on the knowledge developed in your first year economics subjects, developing skills that are essential for undertaking applied microeconomic policy analysis in both private and public sectors. You will focus on consumer and producer decisions using a range of approaches, considering market equilibrium under different degrees of competitiveness, including perfect competition, monopoly and the impact of market power.
learning_outcomes: Use models of consumer and producer decision-making to critically evaluate the welfare implications of different equilibria and critically evaluate the case for policy interventions by government.
Apply analytical reasoning to demonstrate and explain the incentives faced by individuals, firms, other non-government groups and the state.
Analyse consumer, household and producer decisions demonstrating and explaining relevant economic trade-offs.

title: PRINCIPLES OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND RESOURCE ECONOMICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the field of environmental and resource economics. You will explore the basic relationships between the economy and the environment and learn how to tackle environmental and resource degradation issues using economic principles and methods. In particular, you will examine (i) the theoretical framework for the optimal management of natural resources and environmental quality, (ii) various analytical tools to assess environment policies, including benefit-cost analysis, and (iii) different policy approaches to address environmental externalities, such as command-and-control and incentive based strategies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the concepts of sustainable development and policy appraisal using the principles of the optimal allocation of resources over time
Evaluate various policy instruments in the management of environmental and natural resources
Analyze and evaluate the linkages between the economy and the environment to demonstrate how a lack of well-defined property rights and market failure contribute to environmental problems
Apply cost-benefit analysis and use appropriate environmental valuation techniques in economic decision making

title: INTERNATIONAL TRADE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore key economic theories of international trade and their application to contemporary global economic issues. You will examine why countries engage in trade, the gains from trade, patterns of trade and specialisation, and the distributional effects of free trade on industries, workers, and consumers. You will analyse how international trade outcomes relate to economic growth and inequality, with reference to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDGs), particularly UNSDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and UNSDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities). You will also explore selected issues in international trade policy, including tariffs, export subsidies, and other trade distortions. You will evaluate how global disruptions and government policies affect international trade flows, supply chains, and Australia's position in the global economy.
learning_outcomes: Apply economic theories to explain why countries engage in international trade.
Implement cost-benefit analysis to evaluate the effects of protectionist and industry incentive policies on economic welfare.
Use economic reasoning to assess the consequences of international trade to the economy, including national welfare, production specialisation, and the distribution of income.
Work effectively in group to critically analyse the position and role of Australia in the global economy.

title: BUSINESS IN THE WORLD ECONOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will draw on a range of disciplines and skills to examine the factors that influence countries' and firms' participation in the international environment. You will directly interact with the specialised industry, both in the classroom and in the field, to explore firms' current issues and challenges, as well as their best practices and strategies to succeed in the global marketplace. You will identify trends towards global and regional integration and predict the benefits and pitfalls of entering foreign markets.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the salient features of the global business environment and the strategic measures and policies that firms need to implement to succeed in the global market.
Synthesise and examine research data and complex information to be presented to a diverse audience in a variety of engaging formats.

Research, construct and effectively utilise key indicators in international business and economics to critically evaluate the main characteristics, evolution and prospects of the global marketplace and its main participants.
Work effectively with a team to engage with the industry and elicit, research and analyse current issues faced by organisations in international business.

title: MACROECONOMIC POLICY AND APPLICATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore key macroeconomic issues and apply economic theories and frameworks to critically analyse real-world policy challenges. You will examine how governments, central banks, and international institutions respond to short-term economic fluctuations and promote long-term economic growth. You will learn how macroeconomic variables and policies interact and affect individuals, businesses, and governments. You will also learn about the role of financial markets in economic stability, as well as the challenges posed by income inequality, globalisation, and climate change. Through case studies, data analysis, and policy debates, you will develop the skills to interpret macroeconomic indicators, critically assess government and central bank decisions, and formulate evidence-based policy recommendations. By the end of this subject, you will be equipped to analyse macroeconomic trends, develop effective policy responses, and evaluate their implications for society.
learning_outcomes: Apply macroeconomic models to examine how fiscal and monetary policies can deal with national and international economic challenges.
Communicate macroeconomic insights effectively through written reports and policy briefs, incorporating theoretical frameworks and empirical evidence.
Analyse macroeconomic variables and policies to assess their impact on business, government, individuals, and broad economic outcomes in society.
Critically evaluate and interpret macroeconomic data from sources such as the ABS, World Bank, and central banks to assess economic trends and policy implications.

title: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: The aim of this subject is to introduce students to the socio-cultural, political, historical as well as economic values, the metrics and other factors that affect the process of economic growth and development. The objective is for students to be able to explain and analyse the complexities of economic development in a global environment, with a particular focus on developing countries. Why have some countries experienced rapid economic growth while others a lack of growth? Why do some people benefit from economic growth and others do not? Is growth sustainable, or is it the result of depleting natural resources and destroying the natural environment? In completing this subject it is expected students will build on their analytical and problem solving abilities in applying economic principles in a global context, to understand the difficulties facing developing economies. Students will also recognise the diversity of perspectives and values in a world of complex interdependence.
learning_outcomes: Use economic principles and research skills in a collaborative team environment to solve complex problems and communicate the findings to people with various viewpoints
Plan and produce an economic research report that examines the economic development of a low income country
Critically evaluate theories of economic growth and development and their applications to the analysis of developing countries in a global context
Analyse and evaluate the linkages between determinants and outcomes of economic growth and development, such as education, inequality, poverty and environmental sustainability

title: CLIMATE CHANGE ECONOMICS AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the concept of climate change and its predicted impacts on natural and built environments. Using climate change economics, you will evaluate various national and international policy frameworks including carbon markets to mitigate human-induced climate change. You will also explore a range of business implications arising from climate change mitigation and adaption policy responses.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate core strategic issues relating to international policy coordination of countries' climate policies
Analyse the empirical evidence relating to climate change and its adverse impacts on natural and built environments
Apply economic principles relating to climate change and evaluate key mitigation and adaptation policies
Compare and assess appropriate adaptation and business strategies in response to climate change

title: COMPETITION, MARKET FAILURE AND GOVERNMENT
syllabus_overview: In Competition, Market Failure and Government you will study advanced models of markets, individual behaviour and government responses to a range of market failures. We will extend your understanding of markets and efficiency by studying general equilibrium. We will then build on this benchmark by considering a range of extensions that are broadly defined as market failures. Examples include information asymmetry and public goods and externalities. You will build your technical expertise and understanding of important economic concepts, providing you with experience in solving models and problems that explain equilibrium in a diverse range of settings, accounting for individual behaviour and social welfare. This will provide you with a framework and skills to analyse policy problems facing individuals, firms and governments and provide economic policy recommendations.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the concepts of competitive equilibrium, Pareto efficiency and welfare theorems of economics in a manner that informs policy formation and analysis.
Explain the nature, consequences and policy responses to various forms of market failure using written, mathematical and graphical approaches.
Use a variety of economic models and a range of techniques to critically evaluate a range of economic problems.

title: PUBLIC POLICY AND ITS IMPACTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will consolidate your knowledge of economics and of the skills required to practice economics in a professional capacity. On completion of the subject you will be equipped to analyse the impacts of public policy on individuals, businesses and the wider impacts on society. The subject involves analysing real world cases and data to explain the impact of policy and economic events. This subject will be taught in three Modules, delivered by academic or industry experts on a range of topics. The subject provides an opportunity to consider cases drawn from current issues and topics using contemporary techniques and analysis.
learning_outcomes: Apply analytical reasoning to write explanations of the incentives and behaviour of individuals, firms and policymakers.
Use models and data to analyse economic events and propose and influence optimal policy responses
Provide written analysis of government policy interventions intended to address market failures using evidence taken from real world examples
Demonstrate a thorough understanding of the knowledge and skills required to practice their chosen discipline

title: INTRODUCTION TO LANGUAGE AND LITERACY
syllabus_overview: This subject engages students with skills required for academic language and literacy purposes at an introductory level for tertiary students. The subject explores the components and conventions of spoken and written English, as well as the developmental stages of language and literacy learning. An introduction to the English writing system provides a framework for students to gain preliminary knowledge about literacy instruction in the classroom.
