Students will be taught to apply skills in the (i) use of professional oral communication, (ii) critical appraisal of academic sources and (iii) academic writing skills. The subject is scaffolded through a hurdle diagnostic test where students will establish areas of strength and areas that require development.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in speaking and writing in English for formal academic purposes at tertiary level.
Critically appraise academic texts at an introductory level.
Define the components and conventions of spoken language and literacy at an introductory level.
Explain the processes of language development and proficiency in literacy and identify key differences between them.

title: ECONOMICS OF INNOVATION
syllabus_overview: Innovation is one of the fundamental sources of economic growth and development. It offers new opportunities, but its central role in a rapidly changing socio-economic environment also presents challenges to government agencies, organisations, firms and individuals alike. Digital technologies, organisational and social innovations continuously transform the modes of production, consumption and social interactions, defying our understanding of how economic systems work. In this subject you will examine the determinants and effects of innovation using various analytical and empirical economic frameworks. You will explore key elements in innovation such as research and development, property rights, market competition, technological and organisational change, innovative systems, as well as the impact of automation and digitalisation on the economy with special emphasis on the labour market. The main objective is to prepare you to be an active participant in the economic process of digital transformation, be aware of its challenges and make the most of the opportunities it presents. This subject addresses the Sustainable Development Goal 9 “Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure".
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the roles of stakeholders of innovation and their interactions
Analyse market and institutional incentives to innovate, and their shortcomings
Synthesise the different dimensions of innovation and its measurement to explain its economic impact
Analyse and evaluate the economic imperative of innovation especially in the context of digital transformation.

title: HOW HUMANS DEVELOP
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces preservice teachers to major theories and features of human development from infancy to late adolescence, from biopsychosocial perspectives. They will learn how the human brain typically develops from infancy to late adolescence, how neurological differences contribute to neurodiversity, and ways in which neurological changes (over time) and differences (between learners) impact on cognitive and socio-emotional development. This subject also examines how socio-ecological influences, including family structure, First Nations cultures, cultural capital, and trauma, impact on learner development. A focus throughout the subject is on the implications for teacher practice. Finally, this subject introduces basic cognitive science concepts that are important for teachers and educators to understand, to optimise student learning.
learning_outcomes: Describe how the human brain typically develops from infancy to late adolescence and identify neurological differences associated with neurodiversity, and the implications for educational practice.
Describe the influence of socio-ecological factors on infant, child, and adolescent development, and the implications for educational practice.
Describe physical, cognitive, and socio-emotional developmental milestones that often occur in infancy, early and middle childhood, and adolescence, and their implications for educational practice.
Demonstrate an emerging understanding of the brain’s information processing and memory systems and their role in learning.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND PLANNING FOR LEARNING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to foundational understandings of curriculum, pedagogy and evaluating learning. Students engage with key concepts in curriculum and the influence of knowledge, ideology, and stakeholders in curriculum frameworks. Building on this knowledge, students develop an understanding of teaching and learning through analysis and deconstruction of the lesson plan to gain a sense of defining and sequencing learning. Using the framework of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) students understand how to sequence learning experiences that include all learners across a range of contexts, including digital learning environments. Students engage with a variety of worked examples to understand best practice for planning tasks and lessons, with a focus on explicit modelling. Finally, students begin to evaluate student learning and consider the role of feedback and coaching conversations and justifying their pedagogical approaches in teaching in impactful learning environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate the elements of a lesson plan.
Demonstrate integration of digital tools to enhance learning experiences.
Evaluate student data for the purpose of providing feedback and setting learning goals that provide achievable challenges for students of varying abilities and characteristics.
Design learning sequences that align with universal design for learning principles.
Demonstrate an understanding of the curriculum, pedagogy and assessment cycle.

title: DIGITAL LITERACIES
syllabus_overview: Through this subject, students will develop core knowledge and skills to learn through, with and about digital platforms, especially as they apply to their future teaching careers. They will learn to become critical and literate users of digital technologies in education, and to better understand the impact of digital technologies on the lives of their future students, both within and beyond the classroom. The implications of emerging technologies including AI will be explored, including ethical, legal and cognitive aspects. Students will undertake hands-on exploration of a range of educational technologies and begin to establish an evidence-based repertoire of practices for digitally-informed learning.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively illustrate ethical concerns in digital spaces using multimodal and visual literacies.
Demonstrate knowledge of a range of digital skills and tools and how these can be used in accessing, processing and communicating information.
Appraise contemporary research and demonstrate a foundational understanding of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning.
Build a professional digital presence applicable to providing evidence of learning.

title: FRAMING CULTURAL IDENTITIES
syllabus_overview: This is a cornerstone subject in which first year education students develop core knowledge, skills and dispositions required to be equity-oriented teachers. The subject embeds intercultural understanding and the development and deepening of students’ understanding of the diversity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages, societies, cultures, world views, histories and contemporary experiences. Students examine their own cultural identities, representations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and become critically reflective of the historical circumstances that have impacted on people in Australia. Students will investigate policies, programs and practices of direct concern to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate how media representations and personal histories and experiences shape and influence perceptions of and assumptions about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and their community life, and how this impacts on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students' attitudes towards school and education.

By exploring theories of cultural identity, learn how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders' cultural identity and linguistic background play a role in shaping their understanding of education and how to productively engage in challenging conversations around equity and diversity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education.

Critically reflect on ethics, beliefs, and emerging teaching philosophies relating to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students' culture and education to understand how to address the impact of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture on students.

Demonstrate knowledge of and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and histories, along with understanding of the impact of culture, cultural identity and linguistic background on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
Examine significant events impacting on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, as well as current rights-based approaches, educational policy and practices related to Indigenous education.

title: NUMERACY IN EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the opportunity to identify and practise the numeracy knowledge and skills needed to understand how mathematical information is used in meaningful real-world contexts to make decisions. Emphasis is put on supporting learners’ development of mathematical critical thinking, reasoning, questioning, and problem-solving. Strategies are developed for teaching the key aspects of numeracy applicable to the various learning areas of the Australian Curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Explain how answers to context-based mathematical problems are determined.
Illustrate mathematical skills through modelling, problem solving, and argumentation.
Design numeracy teaching strategies and identify their application in various teaching areas.
Apply critical numeracy skills to identify the way in which mathematics is conveyed in media reports and other texts.

title: UNDERSTANDING SELF, RELATIONSHIPS AND LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: This subject will support pre-service teachers to develop as critically reflective practitioners with the capacity to develop productive relationships and establish positive learning environments. Pre-service teachers develop a strength-based approach to developing productive relationships with members of their classroom and school community, and to understanding and valuing the perspectives of diverse groups including EAL/D, neurodivergent, gender-fluid, and First Nations students. They will develop an understanding of how positive relationships impact student behaviour and learning. Pre-service teachers learn about and plan to implement proactive practices that support productive classroom relationships, including creating safe and predictable learning environments, setting high expectations for learning and behaviour, and using specific positive feedback. Pre-service teachers also learn about and rehearse classroom management strategies for maintaining positive relationships, including modelling desired behaviour, use of pre-corrections, and verbal and non-verbal responses. Finally, this subject examines the role of teacher relationships with family, community, and other professions in maintaining positive learning environments, learning effective ways to engage with family, and the positive impact of engaging with community.
learning_outcomes: Describe effective practices for engaging with colleagues, families, community, and other professionals, and explain how these can contribute to maintaining positive learning environments.
Describe self-concept, classroom and community diversity, and how biases, assumptions and worldviews can impact both learner and teacher behaviours and attitudes in the classroom.

Explain and plan classroom management strategies for maintaining positive relationships, including modelling desired behaviour, setting and reinforcing expectations, use of pre-corrections, verbal and non-verbal responses, and use of calm, expected and escalating responses.

Describe the evidence showing the impact of relationships on behaviour and learning, and identify and plan proactive practices to cultivate positive relationships and positive, culturally safe, learning environments.

title: BECOMING AN ETHICAL EDUCATION PROFESSIONAL
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will gain an introduction to what it means to become an ethical education professional. In doing so, PSTs will learn about formal codes and ethics that regulate the profession, as well as informal ethics and education ethical theories. PSTs will learn how to recognise different values and beliefs, including their own, and how these can affect professional practice. They will learn how they can use this information to bring about ethically informed outcomes in their future educational decision-making processes. PSTs will develop skills to critically reflect on their own values and beliefs and how these could impact their future students, parents/carers and members of the community. PSTs undertake service-learning in their local communities to engage with diverse groups to learn more about their own values and beliefs, and those held by other people.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of education ethics theories and approaches.
Articulate a professional ethical position in relation to education.
Demonstrate critical awareness of own values and beliefs, and how this can affect professional practice as an educator.
Demonstrate knowledge of codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.
Demonstrate understanding of diverse values and beliefs in the community.

title: ROUTINES AND BEHAVIOURS FOR IMPACTFUL PEDAGOGIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will become proficient at understanding the routines and behaviours of teachers who have a positive impact on student learning and the complex contexts in which learning can occur. You will develop an understanding of the routines and behaviours of teachers that support the learning of students across different situations, including setting clear expectations, preparing students for collaborative learning and how teachers can establish coaching conversations and goal setting with students. Through engaging with a range of the practices of teaching, pre-service teachers will prepare for professional experience. This subject involves a 10-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of a broad range of impactful teaching strategies.
Analyse evidence of student learning and identify learning goals based on evidence.
Apply understanding of teaching practices to professional experience.
Prepare and communicate content into effective learning and teaching experiences.
Critically reflect on teaching practice and feedback and set goals for future improvement.
Apply strategies for differentiating teaching to meet the specific learning needs of students across the full range of abilities

title: HOW HUMANS LEARN
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on the foundational knowledge of EDU1002 How Humans Develop. Preservice teachers will learn to apply evidence-based cognitive, social, and behavioural learning science principles to maximise the effectiveness of their teaching of knowledge and skills across all areas of the curriculum. Particular attention will be given to the importance of considering students’ level of mastery (novice versus expert). This subject will also ensure preservice teachers can identify, appraise, and apply research evidence that is both relevant and rigorous, to support the design and delivery of impactful pedagogies as appropriate to their students’ level of mastery.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding and application of the science of learning as it relates to knowledge acquisition, including information processing theory, schema theory, and memory consolidation methods.
Identify and appraise relevant peer-reviewed research evidence to inform and justify pedagogical planning and practices.

Demonstrate understanding and application of the science of learning as it relates to skill development, including principles of effective modelling, scaffolded practice, and behavioural reinforcement.

Demonstrate awareness of different types of educational research and evidence, including pedagogical evaluation strategies and the evidence disproving neuromyths, and Indigenous perspectives on research.

title: DESIGNING, EVALUATING AND VALUING LEARNING
syllabus_overview: This subject will overview the development and enactment of a broad range of teaching practices, including Indigenous pedagogies. The influences and research supporting these practices will be investigated. With a mind towards student achievement, PSTs will engage in student learning data and evidence that can be recorded from student learning. From data evidence, learning strategies for positive impact will provide the direction for teaching. Strategies will include instructional teaching and identifying and analysing the use of digital tools to support the student learning. PSTs will also learn about the nature and efficacy of both proactive and responsive positive behaviour management practices, and plan and rehearse effective techniques for use in the classroom. This subject involves a 10-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge in creating learning opportunities that show the relationship between curriculum, pedagogy, assessment and classroom management.
Collect, analyse and respond to student data utilising this in planning for future learning experiences
Critically analyse pedagogical choices made by teachers in response to student learning
Demonstrate understanding of a broad range of evidence that can be used to inform teaching and learning
Demonstrate understanding of feedback approaches in response to evidence of student learning

title: ETHICAL PROFESSIONAL RELATIONSHIPS IN EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will further their understanding of what it means to be an ethical education professional. In this subject, PSTs will learn more about the formal laws, codes and ethics that regulate the profession in terms of professional relationships, as well as relevant informal ethics and their own developing education ethical positions. PSTs will learn how to recognise different values and beliefs, including their own, and how these can affect professional relationships with colleagues, students, parents/carers and members of the community. They will learn how they can use this information to bring about ethically informed relations in their future professional practice. PSTs will further develop skills and dispositions of critical reflection on their own values and beliefs and how these impact other people. PSTs undertake professional placement with an emphasis on professional relationships. This placement experience forms the basis of their final assessment task for the subject. This subject involves a 15-day placement for PSTs in the Secondary stream. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.
Demonstrate understanding of relationships with parents/carers and community.
Demonstrate understanding of legislative, administrative and organisational requirements, policies and processes.
Apply ethical theoretical position to case studies regarding professional relationships, including placement experiences.
Demonstrate understanding of social and cultural norms and their operation in education contexts.

title: UNDERSTANDING ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: Pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of theories, strategies and pedagogical approaches that align with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges and perspectives. Pre-service teachers will learn about the impact of culture, cultural identity and linguistic backgrounds on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
learning_outcomes: Prepare and deliver a presentation to peers that uses culturally inclusive practices in relation to curriculum, teaching strategies and pedagogical approaches that align with local Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives and knowledges.

Critically reflect on what it means to be culturally competent, demonstrating your understanding of implementing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, knowledges and identity for all students, including students with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
Demonstrate understanding of culturally safe and inclusive resources from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspective.
Design a lesson demonstrating ability to provide learning opportunities that are culturally appropriate, culturally safe and responsive to all students’ needs.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION IN SCHOOL CONTEXTS
syllabus_overview: Pre-service teachers explore the notion that every child, regardless of their challenges, has the ability to learn and that every learner has the opportunity to be successful in learning. PSTs develop an understanding of educational institutions' responsibilities for inclusive approaches to the diversity of learners. PSTs become familiar with the varied resources that students bring with them and the specific challenges that different individuals and groups confront in educational settings. Differentiated teaching and learning strategies are explored to maximize the educational experience and achievements of a range of diverse learners including: students with learning difficulties and disabilities; high performing students and students with rich multilingual, limited literacy, diverse cultural and socio-economic backgrounds. PSTs learn how to engage with the school community, including parents, to identify and respond to the needs of all students. PSTs undertake 20 days of practicum in an educational setting as part of this subject, this is a hurdle requirement. This subject involves a 20-day placement. Integral to this placement is the use of a reflective teaching practice cycle (Plan-Teach-Assess-Reflect-Evaluate) that supports preservice teachers to employ a range of strategies to evaluate the impact of their teaching programs in order to improve student learning. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of differentiated teaching practices that cater for students across a range of abilities.
Employ reflective teaching practices to evaluate the impact of teaching programs in order to improve student learning.
Identify and apply the legislative requirements and teaching approaches that support the inclusion of a broad range of diverse learners.
Design individual learning plans for students with specific learning needs.
Engage with external professionals, community members, families and carers to inform individual learning programs.
Identify the complex dimensions of the social, cultural and physical differences that impact on learners and their learning.

title: EVIDENCE OF LEARNING AND USING LEARNER DATA
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will use a construct-based approach to create developmental rubrics and use data and evidence to assess and identify where a learner is in their learning. You will use a set of student assessment data as a basis for determining students’ level of mastery and design a sequence of lessons that build upon each other based on an identified learning progression (construct map). Your sequence will reflect the individual learning needs of your data set and illustrate how you use differentiated practices to support all learners. Assessment data, formative and summative, is a key source of evidence for student learning and achievement and this subject will develop your professional capacity to design effective and impactful teaching and assessment strategies. This subject will encompass data literacy, digital data, analysing and interpreting student learning data, justifying your practice to colleagues, parents, and students, and evaluating your own teaching and learning needs.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse emerging developments and resources that support data-driven teaching to maintain professional skills and knowledge.

Work collaboratively in a professional team to moderate and make judgements about student assessment data, to generate feedback for students about their learning and for parents/carers about student achievement.
Assemble, appraise and interpret a range of student assessment data to plan, review, and modify teaching practice for both individual and whole class scenarios.
Analyse and synthesise student data to design a justified learning sequence of three lessons.

title: RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHERS
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop teachers who can participate in and contribute to embedding a culture of respect and equality across a school community. The focus will be on relationship-based approaches to building resilient and connected learning communities through an exploration of inclusive approaches and practices. The subject aims to apply theoretical understandings of social cultural theories in the broader school community context through community network participation and critical reflection.
learning_outcomes: Draw on theoretical knowledge to reflect critically on their professional relationships and inform/develop their professional identity as teachers.
Develop the skills to create classroom environments that ensure the social, emotional, and cultural safety of all learners.
Develop the skills to participate in professional and community networks and forums to broaden knowledge and improve practice.
Identify and adopt inclusive and respectful attitudes and interactions to engage and support all members of the learning community.
Develop the skills to establish and maintain respectful, collaborative relationships with students, parents/carers and colleagues regarding their children's learning and wellbeing.

title: CHANGE AND CONTINUITY: PREPARING FOR EDUCATIONAL FUTURES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will think critically and creatively about Educational futures as part of their transition into the education professions. In doing so, PSTs will learn about how Education and care are not static and unchanging spaces, but ones in which continual change and adaptation is needed. PSTs will learn about policy and curriculum review and reform; constantly evolving education research and evidence bases, shifts in pedagogy and technological advances, and the changing ethics, morals and laws impacting education and care and how these can affect professional practice. They will learn how they can think critically and creatively to bring about ethical and impactful outcomes in their future educational decision-making processes. PSTs will develop skills to critically and creatively reflect on education and care futures and how these could impact the eventual students, parents/carers and members of the community. PSTs will learn how to plan for their future professional learning and development towards sustaining ethical impactful pedagogy throughout their future careers in education.
learning_outcomes: Articulate an ethical professional pedagogical position.
Demonstrate understanding of need for professional learning and development.
Demonstrate critical and creative thinking about education futures.
Demonstrate understanding of why education pedagogy and practice needs to be critically examined on an ongoing basis.
Demonstrate understanding of the changing nature of education over time.

title: ARTS SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a secondary Arts (Drama and/or Media and/or Visual Arts) educator at levels 7-10. In this subject, PSTs will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing and evaluating appropriate to Arts education as well as preparation for the senior secondary Arts subjects. PSTs will be introduced to relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards Arts education. They will engage in critique of a selected secondary Arts curriculum document and employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare secondary learners for the task.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of various pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching secondary Arts curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ an appropriate learning and teaching sequence using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies.

title: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, pre-service teachers apply the principles and practices of teaching and learning in the context of their final professional experience. The subject integrates theory of practice through collaboration, critical reflection, analysis, observation, inquiry, and adaptation in connection to the placement experience. The subject includes the pre-service teacher’s final placement (25 days or equivalent). Completing this placement successfully is a requirement to pass the subject. To meet the expectations of the final placement, preservice teachers apply proactive practices in establishing rules and routines, managing behaviour, planning for diverse learning needs, teaching and assessing learning to illustrate graduate readiness. Alongside the placement experience, the pre-service teacher develops and collects evidence for the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA). The GTPA submission enables graduate teachers to demonstrate their experience of planning, teaching, and assessing student learning. The GTPA illustrates one learning sequence within the final placement. This learning sequence is focused on one curriculum area and the relevant cross curricula connections. The GTPA details how the preservice teacher planned for, sequenced learning, and assessed growth for the whole class and three focus students. The GTPA submission will showcase graduate teacher readiness through the development of a portfolio of evidence that justifies the decisions made throughout the learning sequence. The GTPA addresses five practices, planning using data and evidence, teaching and learning, assessing, reflecting and appraising impact of teaching. A minimum of four practices must meet expectations to demonstrate Graduate teacher readiness. In each practice the preservice teacher will justify the decisions made in connection with research, data (evidence), curriculum guidance, pedagogy, and assessment, informed by the context and learner diversity.
learning_outcomes: Establish students’ current level of performance, desired level of performance, and readiness for learning.
Teach general capabilities, including literacy and numeracy, required for student success in learning.
Employ a range of suitably challenging and engaging teaching and learning strategies that connect to and build on students’ prior learning.
Discuss how collected data of learning was used to monitor student progress and to modify teaching and assessment strategies.
Examine and discuss teaching decisions, including in-the-moment decisions taken in the classroom, addressing how they were effective or not effective in progressing student learning and why.
Use the official curriculum and other relevant materials to plan connected teaching and learning sequences.
Make suitable adjustments to teaching based on ongoing student data gathering and analysis.
Select and use a variety of assessment tools and practices, addressing fitness for purpose and principles of inclusion.
Collect, interpret and use a variety of student data for diagnostic, formative and summative purposes.
Engage in moderation of student work.
Identify and justify future teaching and assessment practices in relation to relevant theory.
Identify opportunities for explicit teaching of general capabilities including literacy and numeracy in the curriculum.
Provide feedback to learners to inform student self-assessment, goal setting, and to progress learning.
Describe and analyse the scope and sufficiency of initial and ongoing data choices for identifying students’ learning needs and informing next-step teaching.
Identify and describe differences between planned and enacted teaching, and related pedagogical reasoning.
Provide differentiated teaching and learning opportunities.
Make judgements of the quality of student work with reference to curriculum and achievement standards.
Connect theory, enacted practice, and the curated body of evidence to evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and demonstrate its impact on student learning.

title: ARTS SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a senior secondary Arts educator (Drama or Media or Visual Arts). In this subject, PSTs will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing and evaluating appropriate to Arts education as well as the high stakes examinations contexts of senior secondary education. PSTs will be introduced to relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards Arts education. They will engage in critique of a selected senior secondary Arts curriculum document within the context of high stakes examinations and employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate senior secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare senior secondary learners for the task
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of various pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching senior secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ an appropriate learning and teaching sequence using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies (including literacy and numeracy teaching strategies appropriate to Arts).

title: ENGLISH SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a secondary English educator at levels 7-10. They will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing, and evaluating appropriate to English and English as an Additional Language education as well as preparation for the senior secondary English subjects. PSTs will engage with a variety of worked examples to understand best practice for planning tasks and lessons and explicit modelling of key English skills that is curriculum-aligned. The Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model will be used to design an appropriate English secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare secondary learners for the task, with particular focus on appropriate sequencing and scaffolding of materials.

title: HEALTH AND PHYSICAL EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will undertake both a theoretical and practical study of the Health and Physical Education/PDHPE curriculum/syllabus. title: CROSS CURRICULUM PRIORITIES
syllabus_overview: This subject is for pre-service teachers with a double curriculum specialisation (e.g. Humanities: History & Legal Studies; Science: Biology & Chemistry; HPE: Health Education & Physical Education; etc.). In this subject, pre-service teachers will learn how to integrate the Cross-Curriculum Priority areas of Sustainability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures, and Asia and Australia’s engagement with Asia into their teaching and curriculum. The focus is on developing knowledge and understanding of specific content and pedagogical approaches to competently integrate the Cross Curriculum Priorities with their method area.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply place-based learning in the curriculum.
Apply sustainability, cultural and global perspectives in teaching and learning design.
Demonstrate understanding of curriculum integration and pedagogical approaches to the Cross Curriculum Priorities.

title: THE PERMEABLE CLASSROOM
syllabus_overview: This subject is for pre-service teachers with a double curriculum specialisation (e.g. Humanities: History & Legal Studies; Science: Biology & Chemistry; HPE: Health Education & Physical Education etc) In this subject, pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of the ‘permeable classroom’ (Taylor, Fahey, Kriewaldt & Boon, 2019). The Permeable Classroom invites learning that ignores the confines of classroom walls by bringing together the classroom and ‘real’ world by taking learning out into it, or by bringing ‘real world’ learning in. Pre-service teachers will examine the evidence base for experiential and authentic learning and affective, embodied pedagogies (including during remote learning) and consider practical considerations (e.g. duty of care, risk assessment, consent). Pre-service teachers will research, design and justify a permeable classroom learning experience for their second curriculum specialisation, building on what they have already studied in their curriculum specialisation subjects.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of affective pedagogies.
Demonstrate understanding of approaches that can be used in a permeable classroom.
Demonstrate understanding of duty of care and other professional teacher responsibilities.
Demonstrate understanding of effective pedagogies.
Demonstrate ability to design an affective and effective learning sequence for a permeable classroom.

title: OUTDOOR EDUCATION SECONDARY CURRICULUM 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers develop knowledge and skills for teaching senior secondary outdoor education, particularly in relation to the Victorian Certificate of Education (VCE) Framework. Pre-service teachers learn to develop sequences of work and assessment tasks appropriate for the VCE Outdoor Environmental Studies subject to aid in the progression of skills to attain mastery, with a focus on the critical curriculum knowledge required for students to progress in the subject. Alternative pathways such as the VET Outdoor Recreation framework may be addressed. Strategic advice relating to teaching this discipline is based on learning theories, safety and legal responsibilities, application of learning technologies, audio-visual materials, and resources. Pre-service teachers learn to critically analyse teaching and learning processes in relation to their own experiences on professional placement.
learning_outcomes: Develop and analyse tools and practices for assessing, recording and reporting student learning progress in VCE OES to parents and other stakeholders.
Develop an understanding of senior secondary curriculum study and assessment structures commonly used in outdoor education in Australian schools.
Use a critical incident analysis framework and relevant literature to investigate a critical incident in outdoor education teaching and make recommendations for future professional practice.
Plan a learning sequence to prepare pre-service teachers for assessment tasks consistent with the VCE Outdoor Environmental Studies (VCE OES) study design content and assessment processes.

title: OUTDOOR EDUCATION SECONDARY CURRICULUM 1
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to establish a knowledge and skill base for pre-service teachers in the areas of critical curriculum knowledge, pedagogy, planning, sequencing, assessment and reporting in Outdoor Education for secondary students in the junior and middle years of secondary schooling (Years 7-10). The subject is designed to develop pre-service teachers' understanding of their own positionality in relation to contemporary theory, concepts and skills in Outdoor Education teaching as applied in classroom and outdoor contexts. Theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles and state and national curriculum structures within Outdoor Education are examined and applied in the evaluation, design and implementation of learning resources that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners whilst being considerate of biases and assumptions in worldviews. Strategic advice relating to teaching this discipline includes safety management and legal responsibilities, application of learning technologies and resources.
learning_outcomes: Describe, design and evaluate a sequence of work involving a variety of teaching strategies that cater for individual differences in student learning across the full range of abilities and integrate general capabilities, cross curriculum priorities, literacy and numeracy in Outdoor Education.

Examine the relationships between formative and summative assessment, feedback and reporting, learning task design, student engagement and understanding in Outdoor Education. Apply these relationships to the development and evaluation of sequence plans.

Critically analyse outdoor education theory to develop knowledge of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies to enhance student learning. Articulate a professional position on pedagogy in this field with reference to your own positionality.

Plan and synthesise a range of Outdoor Education learning and teaching activities and sequences for junior secondary students (7-10). These include a variety of pedagogical approaches and resources (including safe and ethical pedagogy and use of resources including ICT appropriate to state and national curricula).

title: EAL/D SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to establish a knowledge and skill base for Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) in the areas of curriculum, pedagogy, planning, assessment and reporting for English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) in years 7-10 or for beginning learners in adult education contexts. The subject develops PSTs’ understanding and application of contemporary theories and concepts (e.g., plurilingualism), pedagogies, and skills related to lower secondary student learning or the early stages of the formal learning of English. PSTs will learn how to support student learning through examining institutional transitions (e.g. primary to secondary school; language centre to mainstream school) and making explicit links across learning areas (e.g., numeracy). PSTs will learn how to effectively plan and sequence learning and assessment tasks and explicitly teach, model and demonstrate key concepts and skills in ways that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners, including students with refugee and disrupted educational experiences.
learning_outcomes: Locate, evaluate and design effective, engaging and inclusive teaching, learning and assessment resources for English as an additional language learning and the development of plurilingualism for diverse students and appropriate to state and national curricula. Justify ideas and approaches against curriculum, pedagogy and theoretically- and research-based knowledge.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies related to English as an additional language, linked to an in-depth understanding of the nature of additional language learning and the diversity of English as an additional language learning experiences.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for diagnostic, formative and summative assessment using knowledge of relevant English as an additional language curricula.
Formulate a professional and pedagogical position in relation to secondary English as an additional language curriculum and research-based knowledge of second language acquisition.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant EAL curriculum, second language acquisition principles, the SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy

title: EAL/D SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to develop a knowledge and skill base for Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) in the areas of curriculum, pedagogy, planning, assessment and reporting in English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) for students in the later years of formal learning (Years 11-12) and adult education contexts. The subject is designed to develop PSTs’ understanding and application of contemporary theories and concepts (e.g., plurilingualism), pedagogies, and skills related to students in more advanced levels of formal school learning of EAL/D or in the later stages of adult education programs. Explicit links will be made to teaching EAL/D across learning areas (including cross-curriculum priorities). PSTs will learn how to effectively plan and sequence EAL/D learning and assessment tasks and explicitly teach, model and demonstrate key concepts and skills in relation to state and national curriculum structures and Year 11 & 12 assessment requirements. PSTs will apply their insights into evaluating, designing and implementing high-quality learning and assessment experiences that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners in school and adult education settings.
learning_outcomes: Locate, evaluate and design effective, engaging and inclusive teaching, learning and assessment resources for English as an additional language learning and the development of plurilingualism for diverse students at the senior secondary and adult levels and appropriate to state and national curricula. Justify ideas and approaches against curriculum, pedagogy and theoretically- and research-based knowledge.
Identify, compare and evaluate learning options for English as an additional language learners at senior secondary and adult levels in the school, vocational and community sectors.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies related to senior secondary and adult learning and teaching, as well as an understanding of key characteristics of additional language learning by people in these settings.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant EAL curriculum, additional language acquisition principles, the SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy in ways that explicitly address learner diversity of prior experiences and that integrate cross curriculum priorities.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for diagnostic, formative and summative assessment using knowledge of relevant English as an additional language curricula and research based principles of additional language acquisition.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers will deepen their understanding of; state and national curriculum structures related to the Program for Students with a Disability; theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles, evidence-based approaches to cater for specific needs and disabilities and requirements for diagnostic, formal and informal assessment and reporting (learning analytics). Content will include the legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to inclusion and support including international agreements. Pre-service teachers will apply this knowledge in the design and implementation of learning resources that are responsive to the needs of individual students with disability and impairment within a MTSS framework.
learning_outcomes: Apply curriculum, assessment and reporting knowledge to inform individualised learning programs for students with special needs in mainstream or special education settings.
Evaluate a range of assessment tools designed to optimise the strengths of students with diverse learning needs.
Integrate and apply a range of strategies for reporting to students and parents/carers and the purpose of keeping accurate and reliable records of student achievement.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to extend knowledge and skill in working collaboratively with families, health services and other agencies in the development and implementation of programs for students with additional needs. In this subject pre-service teachers will deepen insights into theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles and processes in relation to state and national curriculum structures. Requirements for supporting students with additional needs and the development of consulting, negotiating and facilitating skills will be addressed.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge and understanding to the methodologies that support student with disabilities and impairments through collaborative partnerships involving schools, families and learning communities.
Examine personal and professional communication skills required for engaging with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
Examine the role of external professionals and community representatives in broadening teacher's professional knowledge and practice.
Review and analyse a broad range of strategies for involving parents/carers and professionals in the educative process.

title: UNDERSTANDING LEARNING AND DIFFERENTIATION
syllabus_overview: This subject is concerned with how humans learn new information, from infancy to early adulthood, in circumstances of both typical and atypical development. You will learn about development of the human brain and the physical, cognitive, linguistic, and social processes supported by this; you will examine the role of cultural and linguistic diversity in learning and achievement at school and will learn to apply Response to Intervention principles across all tiers of instruction and support. You will differentiate evidence-informed practices from those that are pseudoscientific and fail to deliver on robust outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of typical and atypical neurodevelopment to the instructional context to respond to the needs of diverse learners in the classroom in a Response to Intervention (RTI) framework.
Demonstrate the ability to design whole class instructional and progress monitoring activities that align with the principles of contemporary learning science frameworks.
Demonstrate the ability to identify students requiring intervention and the role of family-school connections, community agencies, representatives and external professionals in meeting such needs
Differentiate between teaching and intervention approaches that are well-supported by rigorous research evidence and those that are of low efficacy and impact.

title: FRAMING IDENTITIES AND CULTURES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop core knowledge, skills and dispositions required to be equity-oriented teachers. The subject foregrounds intercultural understanding and the development and deepening of students’ understanding of the diversity among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages, societies, cultures, world views, histories and contemporary experiences. You will examine your own cultural identities, representations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and become critically reflective of the historical circumstances that have impacted people in Australia. You will develop an understanding of theories, strategies, and pedagogical approaches that align with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledge and perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate and evaluate how media representations and personal histories and experiences shape and influence perceptions of and assumptions about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and community life.
Explore and analyse theories of cultural identity, and productively engage in challenging conversations around equity, diversity and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education.
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and histories.
Demonstrate understanding of culturally safe and inclusive resources and pedagogies from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspective.
Critically reflect on ethics, beliefs and emerging teaching philosophies.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND ASSESSING INTEGRATED CURRICULUM
syllabus_overview: This subject provides Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) with a deep understanding of how to design and assess integrated curriculum that acknowledges that meaningful and transferable learning occurs across discipline areas and stages of schooling (F-12). PSTs will identify and synthesise unifying concepts across learning areas (including cross-curriculum priority areas) and general capabilities (e.g., competencies). Primary-focused PSTs will learn disciplinary and pedagogical knowledges across Health and Physical Education (e.g., PDHPE), Humanities, English, and Mathematics, and secondary-focused PSTs will explore opportunities to apply an integrated curriculum approach to their discipline/learning area. PSTs will learn how to make meaningful connections between these learning areas as well as cross-curricular priorities and general capabilities. Furthermore, PSTs will learn how to explicitly teach reading, writing and numeracy within discipline-specific content, justifying their approach with research relating to how this improves student engagement and academic achievement. In addition to learning how to design an integrated lesson and/or unit, PSTs will also develop their understanding of evidence-based assessment practices relating to diagnostic, formative and summative assessment. Drawing upon a developmental assessment approach, PSTs will learn how to select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning. Through developing familiarity with curriculum documents and key resources, students will understand the strength and potential of integrated learning for their ongoing teaching practice. This subject includes evidence-informed instructional and assessment practices in reading, writing, numeracy and multimodal learning.
learning_outcomes: Select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning.
Demonstrate understanding of integrated curriculum and how it contributes to learning and disciplinary knowledge in Humanities, Health and Physical Education/PDHPE, English and Mathematics.
Demonstrate core disciplinary knowledge in Humanities, Health and Physical Education/PDHPE, English and Mathematics.
Design learning and assessment sequences that incorporate integration across curriculum areas.

title: LEARNING DESIGN AND CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) to knowledge and skills that educators need for impactful pedagogies in their teaching. PSTs will examine and engage with national and state-based curricula and learn evidence-based instructional and assessment strategies. Guided by the framework of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), PSTs will learn how to sequence learning experiences for learners across a range of ability levels and contexts, including digital learning environments. PSTs will also learn about the nature and efficacy of both proactive and responsive positive behaviour management practices, and plan and rehearse effective techniques for use in the classroom. Digital literacy is embedded throughout, with PSTs developing understanding of teaching and learning using digital tools, alongside ethical and legal concerns. This subject involves 15 or 20 days of placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Plan learning sequences that include classroom rules and routines and other proactive practices for establishing a structured, safe, and positive learning environment to enhance student engagement.
Demonstrate understanding of a broad range of evidence that can be used to inform teaching and learning, including for managing students with challenging behaviours.
Design learning sequences that align with universal design for learning principles.

Demonstrate integration of digital skills and tools to enhance learning experiences, demonstrating understanding of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning.
Demonstrate understanding of the relationship between curriculum, pedagogy, assessment and classroom management.
Evaluate student data for the purpose of providing feedback and setting learning goals.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF LANGUAGE AND EARLY READING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the process of children’s oral language acquisition and how literacy is mastered. You will critically appraise a range of theoretical models describing the process of reading and consider the implications for classroom instruction. You will also explore the structure of oral language and how this pertains to early reading instruction and progress across the school years. In particular, you will be taught about linguistic concepts that are pertinent to the teaching of reading, spelling, and writing.
learning_outcomes: Describe and contrast the processes of oral language acquisition with the mastery of literacy.
List and define the components of oral language and explain how oral language skills form the foundation for learning literacy.
Examine various theoretical models of reading and identify those that have empirical support for translation into classroom practice.
Describe the linguistic structure of the English writing system and explain how this informs instruction in the core elements of literacy: reading spelling and writing.

title: PROFESSIONAL IDENTITY AND ETHICS FOR EDUCATORS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop their understanding of what it means to be an ethical education professional. Students will learn about the laws, formal professional codes and informal ethical frameworks that regulate and guide professional relationships in education settings. They will explore how these formal ethical practices and regulations shape decisions regarding inclusive pedagogical practices and proactive classroom management and apply these understandings during their placement. They will engage in critical reflection to consider their own values and beliefs and how these affect their professional relationships with other people in educational contexts, including with students, staff, parents/carers and communities. This subject involves a 15 or 20 day placement based on your course commencement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Apply formal and informal ethical frameworks to guide and justify professional practice.
Demonstrate knowledge of education ethics theories and approaches.
Demonstrate knowledge of formal codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.
Demonstrate knowledge of legal obligations, requirements and responsibilities for education professionals.

title: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (STEAM)
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop the knowledge, skills and competencies needed to teach science and technology (ST) in primary schools. In addition to pedagogies that deepen student learning in ST, PSTs will explore teaching ST. PSTs will identify high quality curriculum resources for teaching ST topics, which will then be used to develop an interdisciplinary unit plan. Contemporary issues and historical and cultural contributions to ST, and implications for ST teaching, will be examined. PSTs will demonstrate developing knowledge of the general capabilities and cross curricular priorities and how these intersect with the ST Curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Critically select and reflect on age-appropriate knowledge of historical and cultural contributions to science and technology as well as related contemporary issues, including the concepts, substance and structure of the content and assessment.
Apply understanding of science and technology curriculum, the general capabilities and cross-curriculum priorities to learning and assessment sequences.
Research and justify the science and technology knowledge, methods, skills and resources required to communicate science and technology understandings and findings.
Demonstrate understanding of assessment strategies, including informal and formal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches to assess student learning.
Apply digital literacy knowledge to select and design inclusive science resources.
Identify and apply contemporary pedagogical and multidisciplinary approaches, such as the 5E instructional model or a design cycle, for planning and teaching science and technology.

title: TEACHING MATHEMATICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers will explore pedagogies appropriate for the learning and teaching of mathematics in the primary years of schooling. The subject will emphasise tailoring instruction to match learner expertise and diverse ability levels, including the importance of explicit instruction (avoiding self-directed approaches) for novice learners and independent problem-solving once a student approaches proficiency in underpinning mathematical concepts. The subject will model the implementation of rich tasks that promote mathematical proficiencies and working mathematically (communication, problem solving, reasoning, understanding and fluency), mathematical inquiry, and mathematics skill development for school students across the strands, scope and sequence documents of the Australian, Victorian and NSW Curricula. An emphasis will be placed on the relationships among teacher mathematics content knowledge, pedagogy, models of learning, resource selection, differentiation and inclusive teaching and student achievement in mathematics. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and cultural understanding of Primary Mathematics will be embedded. Engagement in the subject will include pre-service teachers participating in a community of learners to design and deliver teaching episodes using digital technologies to their peers for evaluation and constructive feedback.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate mathematics learning and teaching resources accounting for learner characteristics such as novice/expert status, development of executive functioning skills, and working memory limitations.

Justify the selection, application, and adaptation of learning resources to address all students’ learning needs, including the progressive removal of scaffolding as learners become more proficient in mathematical concepts and skills and general thinking skills.

Identify and apply appropriate, inclusive pedagogies for developing and assessing mathematical concepts and skills (numerical, spatial, graphical, statistical, and algebraic) and proficiencies (understanding, fluency, problem solving and reasoning).

Demonstrate an understanding of mathematical knowledge and skills appropriate for primary teaching and explain the importance of this understanding for instructing novice learners (teacher-led schema development).

title: TEACHING ENGLISH AND EAL
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will draw on their previously learned knowledge about the foundations of literacy and curriculum development to further build reflexive understandings, skills and competencies needed to teach the English and English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EAL/D) Curricula in primary schools. Students will explore pedagogical applications of core conceptual understandings about culturally responsive teaching of English and EAL/D. They will engage in critical self-inquiry to understand how their own and existing possible biases and assumptions about diverse groups and worldviews can have implications on the teaching of literacy, literature and the English language. They will plan for and assess EAL/D student learning by implementing culturally responsive practices including Indigenous knowledges and perspectives. Students will demonstrate their ongoing intercultural development and knowledge of the English and EAL/D Curricula and how these guide content selection and pedagogical approaches for teaching and assessment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse student work samples to demonstrate understanding of how assessment of student learning informs teaching.
Examine the major issues involved in the teaching of English language, literature and literacy in the culturally and linguistically diverse primary school setting.
Design learning sequences that reflect understanding of English and EAL/D curriculum content and pedagogy.

Demonstrate understanding and critical analysis of current research and methodologies for teaching English literature, language and literacy in a digital multiliterate world to all students including those from EAL/D backgrounds.
Examine pedagogies, assessment strategies, and learning sequences relevant for teaching English to learners for whom English is not their first language.

title: INTEGRATED CURRICULUM: ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER HISTORIES AND CULTURE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with a deep and experiential understanding of pedagogical and disciplinary approaches to Indigenous cultures, perspectives and knowledges, across the Arts, Humanities, English, and Mathematics. Practical examples of what cultural safety can look like in practice will be explored. Through developing a familiarity with curriculum documents, you will understand the strength and potential of integrated learning for your ongoing teaching practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify, understand and apply different models and approaches to enhance student learning in the primary school Humanities and Arts setting.

Integrate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories, perspectives and culture with Humanities, the Arts, English and Mathematics into effective teaching and learning in the primary school setting.
Apply a sense of place and the connection to land and community into pedagogical and curriculum design.
Apply knowledge and understanding of Indigenous cultures and perspectives into pedagogical and disciplinary content of Humanities and the Arts and design

title: RESEARCHING TEACHER IMPACT
syllabus_overview: This subject equips students to engage with and be discerning consumers and producers of research. Students will develop their skills and understanding of the purpose, structure and processes of research and evaluate how research informs teacher professional inquiry. Students will generate a strong understanding of quality, credibility and reliability when evaluating research on evidence-based teacher practice. They will apply this understanding to engage in collaborative inquiry with their peers and supervising teacher to develop an area of technical knowledge. Throughout the subject, students will develop critical reflection and analysis capacities in evaluating how research can inform and improve their teaching practice and influence student learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Develop skills to conduct and report on ethical and professional teacher inquiry.
Systematically engage with literature to inform evidence-based teacher practice.
Develop an area of technical knowledge through collaborative teacher professional inquiry.
Critically review and reflect on evidence collected through systematic inquiry.

title: TEACHING FOR IMPACT AND INCLUSION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers critically analyse the breadth of educational settings and student learning needs in the context of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) and the Practice Principles. Pre-service teachers investigate the notion that every child, regardless of their challenges, has the ability to learn and that every learner has the opportunity to be successful. Pre- service teachers learn ways in which differences between learners (including their developmental characteristics, prior learning, literacy and numeracy levels, wellbeing, and mental health) impact on their specific needs for engagement and learning. This will provide a context for better understanding of some challenging behaviours such as disengagement, withdrawal, confrontation, and bullying. This will be evidenced by using evidence-informed judgements to apply various teaching strategies including the Victorian Teaching and Learning Model (VTLM) to improve students’ academic (literacy and numeracy) as well as social-behavioural outcomes. Through the materials encountered in the subject, preservice teachers generate their future classroom design of a positive, inclusive, differentiated and effective learning environment.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement a micro-teaching moment that embeds effective pedagogical practices addressing the social-emotional and academic needs (including for literacy and numeracy) of students.
Describe ways in which research-informed relational teaching strategies can help to support healthy classroom relationships, inclusion, and wellbeing.

Identify evidence-based, age-appropriate approaches that consider student academic (including literacy and numeracy), wellbeing, and mental health when addressing challenging student behaviours such as disengagement, withdrawal, bullying and confrontation.
Illustrate positive, safe learning environments that embed professional and community requirements.
Develop Individual Education Plans (IEPs) for students for students with diverse socio-emotional and academic (including literacy and numeracy) needs.
Develop and annotate inclusive and differentiated lesson plans utilising teaching strategies that maximise learning outcomes (including in literacy and numeracy) for all students.

title: INTEGRATED CURRICULUM: GENERAL CAPABILITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) develop knowledge and skills related to teaching and assessing general capabilities/competencies (including literacy and numeracy) in primary or secondary settings. Pre-service teachers learn how to support and scaffold students’ development of general capabilities/competencies in both personal and educational contexts and across discipline areas over time through evidence-based learning and assessment design. General capabilities/competencies are examined, specifically, within the Arts, PDHPE, English, and Mathematics, and PSTs learn to plan, teach and assess learners within an integrated curriculum that incorporates general capabilities/competencies. Overall, the aim of this subject is to enable pre-service teachers to identify the relevance and importance of general capabilities/competencies and learn to apply this knowledge across the curriculum, including when designing integrated curricula.
learning_outcomes: Locate and analyse general capabilities/competencies in curriculum and communicate how they contribute to learning and disciplinary knowledge in Arts, Health and Physical Education, English, and Mathematics.
Demonstrate understanding of general capabilities/competencies in personal and educational contexts.
Evidence and apply knowledge of general capabilities/competencies to create inclusive integrated teaching and learning experiences.
Design assessment strategies, including informal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches, to assess students’ development of general capabilities/competencies.

title: LITERACY AND NUMERACY ACROSS THE CURRICULUM
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will demonstrate understanding of how a focus on literacy and numeracy can evidence outcomes for learning areas other than English and mathematics. Preservice teachers will design teaching and learning experiences across the discipline areas of the Australian Curriculum. For literacy, preservice teachers will focus on various genres of writing for discipline-specific purposes and how to integrate their application across the primary curriculum. In relation to numeracy, preservice teachers will identify the way in which numerical information and mathematical representations are embedded in meaningful contexts and how the mathematics can be used to make evidence-based informed decisions. A critical literacy and numeracy framework will be used to explore the utility of various resources for learning and teaching purposes.
learning_outcomes: Utilise ICT/digital technology to support and extend literacy and numeracy in a learning activity.
Identify reasons for and describe methods of explicitly teaching literacy and numeracy across the curriculum.
Apply understanding of how literacy and numeracy can enhance learning in areas other than English and Mathematics.
Identify the purpose and audience for different written and communication genres and identify associated literacy teaching opportunities and strategies.

title: SUSTAINING EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject pre-service teachers apply the principles and practices of teaching and learning to independently plan and execute units of learning. The subject applies evidence-based practices to a range of school contexts. The subject includes the pre-service teacher’s final professional experience placement (25 days or equivalent) during which the pre-service teacher develops and collects evidence required to complete the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA). The GTPA enables graduate teachers to demonstrate how they align curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment, taking account of school contexts and learner diversity. The GTPA addresses five practices, of which a minimum of four must be demonstrated at a satisfactory standard. This subject provides confirmation of graduate teachers’ readiness for classroom teaching. This subject involves a 25-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Identify and justify future teaching and assessment practices in relation to relevant theory.
Identify opportunities for explicit teaching of general capabilities including literacy and numeracy in the curriculum.
Provide differentiated teaching and learning opportunities.
Use the official curriculum and other relevant materials to plan connected teaching and learning sequences.
Select and use a variety of assessment tools and practices, addressing fitness for purpose and principles of inclusion.
Design summative assessments and make judgements of the quality of student work with reference to curriculum and achievement standards.
Identify and describe differences between planned and enacted teaching, and related pedagogical reasoning.

Provide feedback to learners to inform student self-assessment, goal setting, and to progress learning. Including feedback as learning that is specific, honest, construe. The uses explicit teaching strategies to re-teach concepts, scaffold, or correct misconceptions as necessary.
Employ a range of suitably challenging and engaging teaching and learning strategies that connect to and build on students’ prior learning.
Establish students’ current level of performance, desired level of performance, and readiness for learning and plan introductory lessons based on this knowledge.
Teach general capabilities, including literacy and numeracy, required for student success in learning.
Make suitable adjustments to teaching based on ongoing student data gathering and analysis.
Engage in moderation of student work using developmental rubrics with criteria tailored to a specific tasks and/or work samples.
Connect theory, enacted practice, and the curated body of evidence to evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and demonstrate its impact on student learning.
Discuss how collected data of learning was used to monitor student progress and to modify teaching and assessment strategies.
Collect, interpret and use a variety of student data for diagnostic, formative and summative purposes.
Describe and analyse the scope and sufficiency of initial and ongoing data choices for identifying students’ learning needs and informing next-step teaching.
Examine and discuss teaching decisions, including in-the-moment decisions taken in the classroom, addressing how they were effective or not effective in progressing student learning and why.

title: DIGITAL LITERACIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) will develop skills and knowledge related to digital literacies in the curriculum and society at large, with a focus on preparing them to effectively teach and model digital literacy in the classroom. PSTs will analyse personal digital literacies and technical skills within the expertise of their discipline, understanding that good teaching starts with demonstrating and showing students what they need to do. Knowing that the characteristics of digital literacies are ever evolving, PSTs will research digital literacy education policies and the impact of digital literacy on teaching and learning. Developing the capacity to interact and collaborate with an online community of peers, PSTs will exchange ideas and work together to develop valuable constructs and co-create professional learning resources that embed the cross-curricula priorities and capabilities.
