By the end of this subject, PSTs will be able to confidently model and demonstrate digital literacy skills to their students in the classroom.
learning_outcomes: Research and critically select effective and engaging teaching strategies to create, manage, communicate and investigate digital literacies across disciplines.

Demonstrate and apply practical skills in designing digital technology tools and innovations for effective engagement in the classroom, including teaching resources that develop students' sense of digital citizenship and digital literacies in effective and ethical ways, while confidently modelling digital literacy skills to guide students.

Synthesise and develop teacher professional development resources on how to teach digital literacies in the classroom that encompass the complex issues impacting on effective and ethical digital literacies.
Examine trends in digital literacies and their deployment in education and society at large, embedding considerations of the capabilities and cross-curricula priorities.
Analyse educational theories, frameworks and policies, specifically those that relate to the application of digital literacies in secondary school environments.

Appraise digital devices or systems, learning to make the most of the available technologies, adapting to new ways of doing things as technologies evolve and protecting the safety of self and others in digital environments.

title: DIVERSE LEARNERS AND PEDAGOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) develop an understanding of teachers' and educational institutions' responsibilities for proactively catering for students with disability and working collaboratively with families, carers and other agencies to achieve optimal learning conditions for students with disability. The specific challenges that different individuals and groups confront in educational settings are explored, as are the legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to student inclusion and support, which require that students with disability should have the same opportunities and choices in their education as students without disability. Pre-service teachers will consider evidence-based strategies to maximise the educational experience and achievements of students with diverse needs, including through Tier 1 teaching practices. High prevalence examples of diversity in the classroom, such as Autism Spectrum Disorder, learning disabilities and learning difficulties, are introduced in this subject. Using Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles, students will apply theoretical understandings to real world issues of learner difference to identify barriers to learning and participation and to maximise learning for all students. Pre-service teachers will analyse school and teacher approaches to responding to student diversity including adaptive pedagogies, individualised learning plans, approaches to curriculum design, and multi-tiered systems of support.
learning_outcomes: Understand the need to cater for diversity and the major issues involved in teaching in diverse classrooms.
Demonstrate knowledge of responsive teaching strategies which optimise the strengths and needs of all students.
Plan for and design individualised learning programs to support students with additional needs for maximum participation in learning.
Explore evidence-based strategies for supporting diverse learners through collaborative partnerships involving schools, families and allied health professionals.
Utilise instructional approaches that maximise learning outcomes for students with additional needs, including Tier 1 instruction.

title: ACADEMIC CULTURE
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to academic culture and different forms of academic communication. Students examine the conventions of academic culture and identify strategies to support learning success. They compare the purposes of different genres of academic communication in the context of discipline differences and are introduced to the concept of academic integrity. Students develop transferable skills in time-management, note-taking, academic writing, critical reading, case study analysis and online learning. Assessments are low stakes and include text summary and written comprehension as well as text analysis.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply study and learning strategies in an online academic environment
Recognise and apply the specific characteristics of academic communication and culture
Compare different academic genres and styles and identify their requirements required for specific purposes
Identify principles of academic integrity and relate them to the attribution of work

title: TRANSITIONS AND PEDAGOGIES: MIDDLE AND SENIOR SCHOOL
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this subject is to develop pre-service teachers' in-depth understanding of how young people transition through secondary schooling contexts as whole beings. It explores how educators can effectively support these transitions by drawing on key concepts in human learning and adolescent development. Topics include brain development, socio-emotional and moral growth, memory function, cognitive overload, and the debunking of common neuromyths. These are examined through the lens of the personal, social, ethical, critical, and creative dimensions of the curriculum. There is a focus on the decisions and choices that secondary school students are making about their learning and career pathways. The subject also emphasizes the creation of positive classroom environments to support transitions, highlighting the importance of rules and routines, and strategies that foster lifelong learning habits, resilience, responsibility, and independence. Effective approaches for engaging with families to promote learning in secondary contexts are also explored.
learning_outcomes: Develop strategies and approaches, including rules and routines, that promote positive behaviour and support young people in secondary schooling contexts to develop lifelong learning habits.

Demonstrate an understanding and ability to navigate curriculum and syllabi to support student learning through secondary schooling, including personal and social, ethical, critical and creative dimensions of curriculum and understanding the role of language and culture.

Research and develop an understanding of transitions and changes that affect young people in secondary schooling contexts, including effective approaches for engaging with families to promote learning and career pathways.

Critically engage with learning and development theories with specific focus on how the brain develops from childhood to young adulthood, in order to support the knowledge acquisition of young people transitioning through secondary schooling contexts.
Research and demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of engaging with and motivating young peoples’ interests through student voice and agency.

title: ACADEMIC WRITING
syllabus_overview: This subject enables students to develop skills in researching, planning, drafting and editing an essay for academic purposes. Students identify the conventions and purpose of academic essay writing and the development and anchoring of an academic argument. All stages of the essay writing process are supported by peer review and lecturer feedback. Assessments include an annotated bibliography, an essay plan and a final essay draft.
learning_outcomes: Identify, source, critically analyse, organise and reference research materials to support an opinion
Analyse an essay question, form an opinion and develop an academic argument in response
Recognise and apply the principles of essay writing for academic purposes
Identify principles of academic integrity and relate them to the attribution of work

title: ACADEMIC PRESENTATIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject enables students to develop skills in researching, planning, drafting and submitting individual digital and oral presentations for academic purposes. Students identify the conventions and purpose of presentations in different discipline contexts and the development and anchoring of an academic argument on a subject of their choice All stages of the development process are supported by reflection and constructive lecturer feedback. Assessments include an annotated bibliography, an abstract and a digital presentation in an approved mode.
learning_outcomes: Use appropriate strategies (including identifying relevant support services to manage concerns related to giving presentations
Appropriately use selected technology to develop and deliver a presentation for academic purposes.
Source, organise and correctly attribute research materials to support an opinion
Demonstrate skills in choosing, analysing and refining a research topic for presentation in an academic context.

title: THINKING CRITICALLY
syllabus_overview: Students are introduced to critical thinking as concept and as practice. Students are encouraged to engage with differing viewpoints, question received knowledge and to recognise the difference between lower and higher order thinking. Opportunities are provided for the development, transference and application of metacognitive thinking, critical analysis and creative problem solving. Using the concept of World View, students interrogate their own identity positions and analyse how these social, environmental and biological factors impact their perspectives. Through a range of learning tasks, students develop capacity for reasoning, analysis and reflection. Assessments include a peer reviewed reflective journal and a short research essay.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in reflective and critical writing for academic purposes.
Explain and apply critical thinking concepts, relating them to metacognition and to lower and higher order thinking skills.
Identify that World View is individually mediated by a composite of biological, social and environmental factors.
Give and receive constructive peer feedback in the context of developing a reflective journal

title: CRITICAL INQUIRY
syllabus_overview: Students develop and enhance their critical thinking skills and critical literacy through the analysis of a diverse range of media and popular cultural texts. In the context of contemporary issues and arguments, students learn to identify a range of persuasive techniques and representational strategies and to recognise that all media is socially constructed. Students are encouraged to engage with differing view points, challenge received knowledge and to question issues of voice, identity, access and power. Through a range of learning tasks, students develop capacity for textual analysis, collaborative group work, reasoning and reflection.
learning_outcomes: Explain why popular culture media representations should be subject to critical analysis
Analyse the way that media representation directly and indirectly impacts structures of power and received knowledge
Identify and give examples of specific representational strategies and persuasive techniques
Create a persuasive text using digital media

title: CRITICAL REASONING
syllabus_overview: In the context of a range of contemporary issues, students are encouraged to engage with differing viewpoints, question received knowledge and to recognise unsound or fallacious arguments. Students develop and extend critical thinking skills by identifying, constructing and evaluating academic arguments. Opportunities are provided for the development, transference and application of the principles of reasoning and logic. Assessments include a peer reviewed digital journal and a short argumentative essay.
learning_outcomes: Develop and present a sound academic argument related to a contemporary issue
Explain the structural principles of logical argument and differentiate between a sound and unsound academic argument
Analyse and evaluate different texts, concepts and sources for legitimacy, credibility, reliability and appropriateness.
Demonstrate skills in reflective and argumentative writing for academic purposes.

title: THINKING MATHEMATICALLY
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to a spectrum of mathematical thinking and mathematics skills required for future learning in general university programs. Students will develop conceptual knowledge and procedural skills in a range of topics including arithmetical rules and operations, percentages and decimals, rates and ratios and measurement and data. Students will be enabled to solve a variety of mathematical problems using appropriate strategies, methods and techniques and to apply mathematical concepts and knowledge to different real world situations. Assessments tasks are based on cumulative development of skills and include online quizzes and two project tasks.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and apply appropriate concepts and methods to solve mathematical problems
Explain the reasoning, arguments and strategies involved in solving problems and recognise incorrect reasoning
Identify and mathematically solve a problem or situation
Use whole numbers, fractions, percentages, decimals and ratios to calculate and interpret answers across a range of situations and contexts

title: FOUNDATION ALGEBRA
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to a spectrum of algebraic thinking and skills required for future learning in general university programs. Students will be enabled to solve a variety of mathematical and algebraic problems using appropriate strategies, methods and techniques and to apply algebraic concepts and knowledge to different real world situations. Assessments tasks are based on cumulative development of skills and include online quizzes and one project task.
learning_outcomes: Use simple indices, square roots, brackets, alternative conventions for division and signed numbers to express, interpret and solve formula, rules and equations
Recognise and represent expressions using algebraic language and apply the rule of algebra in substitution and simplification of expressions
Identify that a problem or situation may be represented and solved with algebraic concepts and rules
Explain the reasoning, arguments and strategies involved in solving algebraic problems and recognise incorrect reasoning

title: FOUNDATION STATISTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to a spectrum of statistical thinking and skills required for future learning in general university programs. Students will develop conceptual knowledge and procedural skills in statistical analysis. Students will develop skills in Excel use sufficient to manage and analyse simple data sets. Assessments tasks are based on cumulative development of skills and include online quizzes and a project task.
learning_outcomes: Identify the ways that statistical analysis and skills are employed to describe data and use the data to make observations and predictions about the population from which the data was drawn.
Conduct basic statistical analysis of data using spreadsheet programs (such as Excel)
Develop Excel graphs, transfer these graphs to other applications (such as Word and generate reports on these findings
Demonstrate understanding of statistics as a mathematical framework to research, understand, and make predictions about the real world, and develop basic skills in data collection

title: THINKING SCIENTIFICALLY
syllabus_overview: This subject enables students to develop knowledge and skills which support future study in general university programs including Nursing, Allied Health, Education and Science degrees. It introduces students to a comprehension of the different disciplines which have traditionally been categorised as science. Students learn to think of science as a process rather than an outcome and to understand the elements and steps which constitute the scientific method. Students develop a hypothesis and undertake experimental design. Assessment is comprised of a digital journal which records the experiment from initial observations through to reporting on findings.
learning_outcomes: Develop a simple hypothesis and undertake experimental design.
Explain science as process rather than an outcome and identify an everyday situation that can be represented scientifically
Demonstrate familiarity with language and concepts in the discipline of science including scientific method and the creation and validation of an hypothesis

title: WORLD CHANGING SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: Students are introduced to a range of world changing ideas in science, from initial concept to gradual adoption to mainstream understanding. Key scientific advances in agriculture, medicine, technology, energy and conservation are overviewed in the context of their global impact. The ethical considerations of scientific advancement are analysed and applied to real world situations as is the reporting and communicating of scientific information. Students will undertake an inquiry investigation and write a report on a selected field of scientific research and development. Students will also maintain a digital journal detailing the development of their scientific thinking.
learning_outcomes: Apply a scientific approach to inquiry and investigation
Identify world changing ideas in science and the transferability of knowledge about small ideas to larger applications and understanding
Demonstrate familiarity with ethical considerations and applications in science
Explain the relationships between science, technology, human society and the environment

title: MATHEMATICAL COMMUNICATION
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to concepts and conventions relating to mathematical expression and communication. Students will develop conceptual knowledge and procedural skills in a range of topics, including the application and interpretation of significant figures and scientific notation. Students will be enabled to solve and express a variety of mathematical problems using appropriate language, strategies, methods and techniques and to apply mathematical concepts and knowledge to different real world situations. Assessment tasks include online quizzes and a project task.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and use scientific notation to express and solve problems at a foundational level
Articulate the language of mathematics when applied through measurement
Recognise and apply index and logarithmic laws at an introductory level.
Apply significant figures to data and measurement

title: INTRODUCTION TO LANGUAGE AND LITERACY
syllabus_overview: This subject engages students with skills required for academic language and literacy purposes at an introductory level for tertiary students. The subject explores the components and conventions of spoken and written English, as well as the developmental stages of language and literacy learning. An introduction to the English writing system provides a framework for students to gain preliminary knowledge about literacy instruction in the classroom. Students will be taught to apply skills in the (i) use of professional oral communication, (ii) critical appraisal of academic sources and (iii) academic writing skills. The subject is scaffolded through a hurdle diagnostic test where students will establish areas of strength and areas that require development.
learning_outcomes: Define the components and conventions of spoken language and literacy at an introductory level.
Demonstrate proficiency in speaking and writing in English for formal academic purposes at tertiary level.
Critically appraise academic texts at an introductory level.
Explain the processes of language development and proficiency in literacy and identify key differences between them.

title: HOW HUMANS DEVELOP
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces preservice teachers to major theories and features of human development from infancy to late adolescence, from biopsychosocial perspectives. They will learn how the human brain typically develops from infancy to late adolescence, how neurological differences contribute to neurodiversity, and ways in which neurological changes (over time) and differences (between learners) impact on cognitive and socio-emotional development. This subject also examines how socio-ecological influences, including family structure, First Nations cultures, cultural capital, and trauma, impact on learner development. A focus throughout the subject is on the implications for teacher practice. Finally, this subject introduces basic cognitive science concepts that are important for teachers and educators to understand, to optimise student learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an emerging understanding of the brain’s information processing and memory systems and their role in learning.
Describe the influence of socio-ecological factors on infant, child, and adolescent development, and the implications for educational practice.
Describe how the human brain typically develops from infancy to late adolescence and identify neurological differences associated with neurodiversity, and the implications for educational practice.
Describe physical, cognitive, and socio-emotional developmental milestones that often occur in infancy, early and middle childhood, and adolescence, and their implications for educational practice.

title: DIGITAL LITERACIES
syllabus_overview: Through this subject, students will develop core knowledge and skills to learn through, with and about digital platforms, especially as they apply to their future teaching careers. They will learn to become critical and literate users of digital technologies in education, and to better understand the impact of digital technologies on the lives of their future students, both within and beyond the classroom. The implications of emerging technologies including AI will be explored, including ethical, legal and cognitive aspects. Students will undertake hands-on exploration of a range of educational technologies and begin to establish an evidence-based repertoire of practices for digitally-informed learning.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively illustrate ethical concerns in digital spaces using multimodal and visual literacies.
Appraise contemporary research and demonstrate a foundational understanding of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning.
Demonstrate knowledge of a range of digital skills and tools and how these can be used in accessing, processing and communicating information.
Build a professional digital presence applicable to providing evidence of learning.

title: FRAMING CULTURAL IDENTITIES
syllabus_overview: This is a cornerstone subject in which first year education students develop core knowledge, skills and dispositions required to be equity-oriented teachers. The subject embeds intercultural understanding and the development and deepening of students’ understanding of the diversity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages, societies, cultures, world views, histories and contemporary experiences. Students examine their own cultural identities, representations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and become critically reflective of the historical circumstances that have impacted on people in Australia. Students will investigate policies, programs and practices of direct concern to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate how media representations and personal histories and experiences shape and influence perceptions of and assumptions about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and their community life, and how this impacts on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students' attitudes towards school and education.

Critically reflect on ethics, beliefs, and emerging teaching philosophies relating to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students' culture and education to understand how to address the impact of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture on students.
Examine significant events impacting on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, as well as current rights-based approaches, educational policy and practices related to Indigenous education.

Demonstrate knowledge of and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and histories, along with understanding of the impact of culture, cultural identity and linguistic background on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.

By exploring theories of cultural identity, learn how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders' cultural identity and linguistic background play a role in shaping their understanding of education and how to productively engage in challenging conversations around equity and diversity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND PLANNING FOR LEARNING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to foundational understandings of curriculum, pedagogy and evaluating learning. Students engage with key concepts in curriculum and the influence of knowledge, ideology, and stakeholders in curriculum frameworks. Building on this knowledge, students develop an understanding of teaching and learning through analysis and deconstruction of the lesson plan to gain a sense of defining and sequencing learning. Using the framework of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) students understand how to sequence learning experiences that include all learners across a range of contexts, including digital learning environments. Students engage with a variety of worked examples to understand best practice for planning tasks and lessons, with a focus on explicit modelling. Finally, students begin to evaluate student learning and consider the role of feedback and coaching conversations and justifying their pedagogical approaches in teaching in impactful learning environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate the elements of a lesson plan.
Design learning sequences that align with universal design for learning principles.
Demonstrate an understanding of the curriculum, pedagogy and assessment cycle.
Evaluate student data for the purpose of providing feedback and setting learning goals that provide achievable challenges for students of varying abilities and characteristics.
Demonstrate integration of digital tools to enhance learning experiences.

title: UNDERSTANDING SELF, RELATIONSHIPS AND LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: This subject will support pre-service teachers to develop as critically reflective practitioners with the capacity to develop productive relationships and establish positive learning environments. Pre-service teachers develop a strength-based approach to developing productive relationships with members of their classroom and school community, and to understanding and valuing the perspectives of diverse groups including EAL/D, neurodivergent, gender-fluid, and First Nations students. They will develop an understanding of how positive relationships impact student behaviour and learning. Pre-service teachers learn about and plan to implement proactive practices that support productive classroom relationships, including creating safe and predictable learning environments, setting high expectations for learning and behaviour, and using specific positive feedback. Pre-service teachers also learn about and rehearse classroom management strategies for maintaining positive relationships, including modelling desired behaviour, use of pre-corrections, and verbal and non-verbal responses. Finally, this subject examines the role of teacher relationships with family, community, and other professions in maintaining positive learning environments, learning effective ways to engage with family, and the positive impact of engaging with community.
learning_outcomes: Describe the evidence showing the impact of relationships on behaviour and learning, and identify and plan proactive practices to cultivate positive relationships and positive, culturally safe, learning environments.
Describe self-concept, classroom and community diversity, and how biases, assumptions and worldviews can impact both learner and teacher behaviours and attitudes in the classroom.

Explain and plan classroom management strategies for maintaining positive relationships, including modelling desired behaviour, setting and reinforcing expectations, use of pre-corrections, verbal and non-verbal responses, and use of calm, expected and escalating responses.
Describe effective practices for engaging with colleagues, families, community, and other professionals, and explain how these can contribute to maintaining positive learning environments.

title: NUMERACY IN EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the opportunity to identify and practise the numeracy knowledge and skills needed to understand how mathematical information is used in meaningful real-world contexts to make decisions. Emphasis is put on supporting learners’ development of mathematical critical thinking, reasoning, questioning, and problem-solving. Strategies are developed for teaching the key aspects of numeracy applicable to the various learning areas of the Australian Curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical numeracy skills to identify the way in which mathematics is conveyed in media reports and other texts.
Explain how answers to context-based mathematical problems are determined.
Design numeracy teaching strategies and identify their application in various teaching areas.
Illustrate mathematical skills through modelling, problem solving, and argumentation.

title: HISTORY AND PHILOSOPHIES OF EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers will examine childhood in the contexts of a contemporary and changing world. Pre-service teachers engage with historical and contemporary philosophies of early childhood education and care. They will examine the impact of past and current policies and practices and will critically engage with current research and theoretical perspectives informing multiple understandings of children and childhoods. Through engagement with broad range of perspectives, pre-service teachers will be provided with the opportunity to challenge universal representations of child and childhood, to engage with concepts of the multiplicity of childhood and diversity of children's lived experiences, child agency and children as competent and capable learners and members of a community. A range of contemporary issues and social contexts impacting on children's learning are examined in relation to diversity and inclusivity, including social, cultural, and religious background, gender, indigeneity, ethnicity, rurality, learning styles and needs.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically reflect on the impact of a range of contemporary issues and social contexts on the lives of young children and the impact these have on their learning.

Critique universal representations of child and childhood, and articulate understandings of concepts of the multiplicity of childhood and diversity of children's lived experiences, child agency and children as competent and capable learners and community members.

Demonstrate understanding of history and philosophies which have influenced past and current early childhood education and care practices, and critically engage with current research and theoretical perspectives to demonstrate awareness of multiple understandings of children and childhoods.
Demonstrate critical thinking, teamwork, speaking skills and the use of appropriate writing conventions.

title: BECOMING AN ETHICAL EDUCATION PROFESSIONAL
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will gain an introduction to what it means to become an ethical education professional. In doing so, PSTs will learn about formal codes and ethics that regulate the profession, as well as informal ethics and education ethical theories. PSTs will learn how to recognise different values and beliefs, including their own, and how these can affect professional practice. They will learn how they can use this information to bring about ethically informed outcomes in their future educational decision-making processes. PSTs will develop skills to critically reflect on their own values and beliefs and how these could impact their future students, parents/carers and members of the community. PSTs undertake service-learning in their local communities to engage with diverse groups to learn more about their own values and beliefs, and those held by other people.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a professional ethical position in relation to education.
Demonstrate knowledge of education ethics theories and approaches.
Demonstrate critical awareness of own values and beliefs, and how this can affect professional practice as an educator.
Demonstrate understanding of diverse values and beliefs in the community.
Demonstrate knowledge of codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.

title: 21ST CENTURY DIGITAL LEARNERS
syllabus_overview: This is a cornerstone subject in which all first-year education students will develop core knowledge and skills required to learn through digital platforms. In the formation of knowledge, the theories that underpin learning in the digital world will be explored. Foundational understandings of digital competencies, literacy, creativity and collaboration skills will be addressed through a variety of applications. Students will learn how to work in the digital space in a safe, ethical and responsive manner as a community of learners in the global space. Multimodal and visual literacies will be introduced as digital platforms which support the acquisition of new knowledge. Students will establish a Digital Portfolio that will be a portal to document learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of a range of digital skills and ICT and how these can be used in accessing, processing and communicating.
Examine a range of contexts that utilise digital tools and develop appropriate applications to engage within these contexts.
In a team, research and demonstrate an understanding of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning.
Plan and develop a professional digital presence applicable to providing evidence of learning.

title: INTRODUCTION TO INCLUSIVE PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject is an introduction to the philosophy, concepts and contentions impacting on school age students with disabilities and impairments. Pre-service teachers will be introduced to the legislative and ethical requirements as well as major issues informing the provision of education for students with disability and impairment.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the legislative and ethical requirements that support participation and learning for students with disability and impairment
Identify the major issues and contentions involved in catering for students with disability and impairment (1.3, 1.5, 1.6 )
Analyse the historical context and contemporary issues in inclusive education for students with disability and impairment

title: MODELS OF APPLIED LEARNING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore and develop critical understanding of the emergence and diversity of learning theories associated with applied learning including claims made for programs framed by these theories and their significance. You will apply theoretical knowledge and consider your own understandings of learning and teaching; analyse learning scenarios; and design an applied program suitable for use with a diverse range of students.
learning_outcomes: Understand social and cultural dimensions of applied learning.
Evaluate and appraise an applied learning experience illustrating the connections between theory and practice.
Develop knowledge and understanding of the theories that underpin applied learning programmes and enable student learning.
Demonstrate understanding of curriculum considerations and educational philosophies underpinning models of applied learning, including the ability to critically examine aims and purposes.

title: HOW HUMANS LEARN
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on the foundational knowledge of EDU1002 How Humans Develop. Preservice teachers will learn to apply evidence-based cognitive, social, and behavioural learning science principles to maximise the effectiveness of their teaching of knowledge and skills across all areas of the curriculum. Particular attention will be given to the importance of considering students’ level of mastery (novice versus expert). This subject will also ensure preservice teachers can identify, appraise, and apply research evidence that is both relevant and rigorous, to support the design and delivery of impactful pedagogies as appropriate to their students’ level of mastery.
learning_outcomes: Identify and appraise relevant peer-reviewed research evidence to inform and justify pedagogical planning and practices.
Demonstrate understanding and application of the science of learning as it relates to knowledge acquisition, including information processing theory, schema theory, and memory consolidation methods.

Demonstrate awareness of different types of educational research and evidence, including pedagogical evaluation strategies and the evidence disproving neuromyths, and Indigenous perspectives on research.

Demonstrate understanding and application of the science of learning as it relates to skill development, including principles of effective modelling, scaffolded practice, and behavioural reinforcement.

title: DESIGNING, EVALUATING AND VALUING LEARNING
syllabus_overview: This subject will overview the development and enactment of a broad range of teaching practices, including Indigenous pedagogies. The influences and research supporting these practices will be investigated. With a mind towards student achievement, PSTs will engage in student learning data and evidence that can be recorded from student learning. From data evidence, learning strategies for positive impact will provide the direction for teaching. Strategies will include instructional teaching and identifying and analysing the use of digital tools to support the student learning. PSTs will also learn about the nature and efficacy of both proactive and responsive positive behaviour management practices, and plan and rehearse effective techniques for use in the classroom. This subject involves a 10-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge in creating learning opportunities that show the relationship between curriculum, pedagogy, assessment and classroom management.
Demonstrate understanding of a broad range of evidence that can be used to inform teaching and learning
Critically analyse pedagogical choices made by teachers in response to student learning
Demonstrate understanding of feedback approaches in response to evidence of student learning
Collect, analyse and respond to student data utilising this in planning for future learning experiences

title: ROUTINES AND BEHAVIOURS FOR IMPACTFUL PEDAGOGIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will become proficient at understanding the routines and behaviours of teachers who have a positive impact on student learning and the complex contexts in which learning can occur. You will develop an understanding of the routines and behaviours of teachers that support the learning of students across different situations, including setting clear expectations, preparing students for collaborative learning and how teachers can establish coaching conversations and goal setting with students. Through engaging with a range of the practices of teaching, pre-service teachers will prepare for professional experience. This subject involves a 10-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Analyse evidence of student learning and identify learning goals based on evidence.
Prepare and communicate content into effective learning and teaching experiences.
Critically reflect on teaching practice and feedback and set goals for future improvement.
Apply understanding of teaching practices to professional experience.
Demonstrate knowledge of a broad range of impactful teaching strategies.
Apply strategies for differentiating teaching to meet the specific learning needs of students across the full range of abilities

title: UNDERSTANDING ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: Pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of theories, strategies and pedagogical approaches that align with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges and perspectives. Pre-service teachers will learn about the impact of culture, cultural identity and linguistic backgrounds on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
learning_outcomes: Prepare and deliver a presentation to peers that uses culturally inclusive practices in relation to curriculum, teaching strategies and pedagogical approaches that align with local Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives and knowledges.
Demonstrate understanding of culturally safe and inclusive resources from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspective.

Critically reflect on what it means to be culturally competent, demonstrating your understanding of implementing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, knowledges and identity for all students, including students with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
Design a lesson demonstrating ability to provide learning opportunities that are culturally appropriate, culturally safe and responsive to all students’ needs.

title: TEACHING READING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students build on knowledge gained from Introduction to Language and Literacy (EDU1001) and apply this to evidence-informed reading instructional practices for the classroom across all levels of primary school. Students focus in on the theoretical and practical methods for teaching decoding in a systematic and explicit way. Links to spelling will be considered simultaneously. Students also consider the multiple contributors to reading comprehension and how to incorporate these into classroom practice. Contents also cover how to assess, score and interpret the different components of reading to inform teaching practices. Students are also taught how and when to identify students who are struggling with reading and how to intervene.
learning_outcomes: To explain the importance of early identification of struggling readers along with how and when to apply Tier-2 instruction (according to a Response-to-Intervention model).
To list and describe the contributors to students’ reading comprehension and implement teaching practices to support all students.
To define phonics instruction and explain the benefits of a systematic and explicit approach to teaching.
To identify a suite of evidence-informed assessment tools (for reading and spelling) and explain how and why they provide progress monitoring for students.
To compare and contrast various approaches to a comprehensive reading instruction program and explore the theoretical bases of these.

title: TEACHING SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop competence and skills to teach science in Australian early childhood settings and primary schools. We will explore science, with a particular focus on the concepts based on an inquiry approach within physical, biological, earth and space, and chemical sciences. Students will explore best-practice pedagogies for teaching and learning in science and investigate the curriculum resources available to enhance scientific literacy. We will also examine science inquiry skills, safety, science as a human endeavour and contemporary issues that intersect with science education and are suitable for classroom exploration. ICT skills associated with accessing, processing, and communicating in a blended learning environment are embedded within the course and utilised in activities and assessment tasks.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on science learning in order to improve professional knowledge and professional skills for responsible futures.
Design science learning environments that are meaningful, engaging and safe for learners, and meet their learning needs.
Develop science-specific assessment tasks of teaching and learning for a variety of diagnostic, formative, and summative purposes.

Demonstrate an ability to find and incorporate appropriate curriculum knowledge and scientific literacy associated with teaching science in schools through effective planning for teaching including the ability to access relevant science curriculum documents and apply them in planning for learning, and to select appropriate resources.
Access relevant science curriculum documents and apply them in planning for interdisciplinary learning.

title: CREATING COMMUNITIES OF LEARNERS
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers will investigate the educational, social and emotional needs of young people who display significant challenging behaviours. The neuroscience associated with developmental trauma and the impact on learning will be examined. A holistic perspective informed by sound theoretical and applied models will form the foundation of the investigation and choice of appropriate strategies. Proactive and reactive strategies will be examined within an inclusive education framework. Teacher resilience and relational skills required to work with students with challenging behaviours will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the purpose and structure of an Individualised Behaviour Management Plan
Demonstrate an understanding of a range of motivations and neurological differences that drive challenging behaviours.

Analyse a range of pedagogical principles and practices, including communication strategies, that build relational agency and promote student well being, positive student behaviours and learning participation.
Develop the foundations of a personalised pedagogical philosophy and practice that promotes resilience and positive student behaviours.

title: ETHICAL PROFESSIONAL RELATIONSHIPS IN EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will further their understanding of what it means to be an ethical education professional. In this subject, PSTs will learn more about the formal laws, codes and ethics that regulate the profession in terms of professional relationships, as well as relevant informal ethics and their own developing education ethical positions. PSTs will learn how to recognise different values and beliefs, including their own, and how these can affect professional relationships with colleagues, students, parents/carers and members of the community. They will learn how they can use this information to bring about ethically informed relations in their future professional practice. PSTs will further develop skills and dispositions of critical reflection on their own values and beliefs and how these impact other people. PSTs undertake professional placement with an emphasis on professional relationships. This placement experience forms the basis of their final assessment task for the subject. This subject involves a 15-day placement for PSTs in the Primary and Secondary stream or a 20-day placement for PSTs in the EC/Primary stream. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of social and cultural norms and their operation in education contexts.
Apply ethical theoretical position to case studies regarding professional relationships, including placement experiences.
Demonstrate understanding of relationships with parents/carers and community.
Demonstrate understanding of legislative, administrative and organisational requirements, policies and processes.
Demonstrate understanding of codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.

title: UNDERSTANDING CULTURALLY DIVERSE LEARNING AND DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject encourages preservice teachers to view learning and development from a range of perspectives, including the perspectives of socially, culturally and linguistically diverse children and families. Preservice teachers will learn to use theory to analyse learning and development in contemporary early childhood education, and to think critically about child development. This subject includes a 10-day professional experience placement in a birth-to-two years early education and care setting.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of a range of contemporary theories to analyse children's learning and development in socially, culturally and linguistically diverse communities.

Demonstrate research informed practices of critiquing contemporary theories of child development to understand children's learning and development in socially, culturally and linguistically diverse communities.
Understand the need for different theoretical perspectives for different contexts of children's development.

title: LANGUAGE, LITERACIES AND COMMUNICATION
syllabus_overview: Students will explore language and multiple literacies in Early Education; strategies for teaching and learning of reading, writing, speaking, listening and viewing in the early years and for supporting culturally and linguistically diverse families and ESL children; inclusive practices and diverse abilities in language and multiple literacies; documenting children's learning of language and investigating how children communicate their ideas.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the backgrounds of children from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds for the development of spoken English and written literacies.
Employ teaching and appropriate scaffolding skills that assist the development of children's oral language, thinking and emergent literacy.
Develop an applied understanding of children's language acquisition, communication and expression leading to the development of literacy.
Plan, document and assess language and literacy promoting experiences based on children's interests.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION IN SCHOOL CONTEXTS
syllabus_overview: Pre-service teachers explore the notion that every child, regardless of their challenges, has the ability to learn and that every learner has the opportunity to be successful in learning. PSTs develop an understanding of educational institutions' responsibilities for inclusive approaches to the diversity of learners. PSTs become familiar with the varied resources that students bring with them and the specific challenges that different individuals and groups confront in educational settings. Differentiated teaching and learning strategies are explored to maximize the educational experience and achievements of a range of diverse learners including: students with learning difficulties and disabilities; high performing students and students with rich multilingual, limited literacy, diverse cultural and socio-economic backgrounds. PSTs learn how to engage with the school community, including parents, to identify and respond to the needs of all students. PSTs undertake 20 days of practicum in an educational setting as part of this subject, this is a hurdle requirement. This subject involves a 20-day placement. Integral to this placement is the use of a reflective teaching practice cycle (Plan-Teach-Assess-Reflect-Evaluate) that supports preservice teachers to employ a range of strategies to evaluate the impact of their teaching programs in order to improve student learning. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Identify the complex dimensions of the social, cultural and physical differences that impact on learners and their learning.
Engage with external professionals, community members, families and carers to inform individual learning programs.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of differentiated teaching practices that cater for students across a range of abilities.
Design individual learning plans for students with specific learning needs.
Identify and apply the legislative requirements and teaching approaches that support the inclusion of a broad range of diverse learners.
Employ reflective teaching practices to evaluate the impact of teaching programs in order to improve student learning.

title: TEACHING ARTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject students learn about teaching and learning in the Arts in early childhood settings and Primary school F– 6 settings. Students develop practical skills and theoretical knowledge appropriate to the Arts and apply these in the planning of meaningful and inclusive Arts learning. Students examine the relationship between the Arts, cultures and societies.
learning_outcomes: Examine and develop a strong working knowledge of the F – 6 Arts curriculum and apply this knowledge in the development of achievable and inclusive Arts teaching and learning for children.
Investigate, describe, practise and apply Arts skills, techniques and language appropriate in F – 6 settings.
Plan and practise evidence-based teaching and assessment of meaningful, inclusive, and strengths-based Arts learning activities in F- 6 Arts settings, including teaching and learning strategies.
Participate in, present, and reflect upon individual and collaborative creative practices in the Arts as evidence of their professional learning and teacher-as-artist identity.
Investigate the ways students learn in and through the Arts to form knowledge and understanding about traditions, cultures and societies.

title: TEACHING HUMANITIES
syllabus_overview: The subject will give third year students core knowledge, skills, and dispositions required for understanding the landscape of curriculum theory, and the contested ideological approaches. Throughout the subject, students will engage with different pedagogical approaches that are relevant to the Australian context with a focus on primary Humanities and Social Sciences curriculum additionally developing skills and knowledge of integration within and between disciplines that provide opportunities for exploring cross-curriculum priorities and general capabilities in the Australian curriculum. This subject will enable students to explore key themes in the Humanities and Social Sciences, including global citizenship, social justice, critical diversity, and the evolving role of the professional, equipping them with the knowledge and critical thinking skills needed to engage ethically and effectively in diverse social and cultural contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop knowledge and skills for planning integrated lesson sequences and justify knowledge of and approaches to teaching integrated Primary Humanities.
Demonstrate understanding of Curriculum and key humanities elements that include content ideologies, and concepts in Australian/Victorian curriculum.
Appraise the importance of assessment strategies for HASS in inquiry learning and curriculum integration.
Develop resources and implement strategies suitable for primary level to engage students in learning in HASS.
Examine relationships and justify inclusion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives in primary Humanities and Social Sciences.

title: TEACHING ENGLISH AND LITERACY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will examine and understand the scope of the F-6 English curriculum, including English as an Additional Language, and will gain expertise in the effective teaching of English and literacy. Students will build on knowledge gained from Introduction to Language and Literacy (EDU1001) and Teaching Reading (EDU2010) to develop an understanding of what is required to teach all aspects of the Early Years Learning Framework and Australian English Curriculum F-6. Particular attention will be paid to how pre-service teachers (PSTs) explicitly teach reading and writing in order to equip their students with the understanding and engagement needed to attain academic mastery in English. Students will explore pedagogies and core conceptual understandings related to teaching and learning in English and Literacy, with an emphasis on making English and literacy education accessible for culturally and linguistically diverse learners. PSTs will demonstrate their developing knowledge of content and pedagogical approaches for teaching and assessment, including those for young children, and develop their capacity to engage in critical self-inquiry as part of their professional teaching practice.
learning_outcomes: Design coherent planning and sequencing of tasks and lessons that reflect understanding of curricular content and research-backed pedagogy including for students with English as an Additional Language.
Examine the major issues involved in the teaching and assessing of English and literacy in a primary school setting.
Demonstrate understanding of how assessment of student learning informs effective reading and writing instruction.
Demonstrate understanding of current research and critical curriculum knowledge and how to deliver effective teaching of literacy and English in a digital multi-literate world.

title: TEACHING MATHEMATICS AND NUMERACY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers will explore pedagogies appropriate for the learning and teaching of mathematics in the early childhood and primary years of schooling. The subject will model the implementation of rich tasks that promote play-based, hands-on numeracy encounters in early childhood, as well as classroom dialogue, problem-solving, and mathematics skill development for school students across the strands of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics. An emphasis will be placed on the relationships among teacher mathematics content knowledge; emergent numeracy and development; pedagogical approaches; models of learning; resource selection, differentiation, and implementation; and student achievement. Engagement in the subject will include pre-service teachers participating in a community of learners to design and deliver teaching episodes using digital technologies to their peers for evaluation and constructive feedback.
learning_outcomes: Justify the selection and adaptation of learning resources that address student learning needs and promote student achievement.
Evaluate mathematics learning and teaching resources.
Articulate understanding of mathematical knowledge and skills appropriate for primary teaching and communicate these in a scholarly and appropriate manner.
Identify appropriate pedagogies for delivery of mathematical understanding and problem-solving skills.

title: CREATING INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: This subject will draw from the ecological model and disabilities studies to explore learning environments that respond to learner diversity. Applying the principles of universal design for learning, students will apply theoretical understandings to real world issues of learner difference to identify barriers and design learning environments that maximise learning for all students. Students will explore unique differences including complex trauma, Autism, ADHD and learning difficulty to design learning experiences that cater for the cognitive, social and sensory needs of these students.
learning_outcomes: Identify the education and social implications for students with diverse learning needs
Design practices that apply access and equity approaches to the learning environment
Identify the physical, pedagogical and social barriers within a learning environment

title: ASSESSMENT AND REPORTING IN EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the theories and strategies for developing authentic assessment and reporting in early childhood education. Students examine assessment and evaluation as an integral part of the teaching and learning process. They also explore the use of assessment for diagnostic and curriculum development purposes.
learning_outcomes: Explore the various tools of assessment throughout Early Childhood Services.

Demonstrate quality observations and documentation to monitor, interpret, plan for, and reflect upon a child's interests, emerging development, thinking styles, social interactions, emotional status, physical abilities and capabilities.
Identify the authentic assessment and diagnostic tools utilised locally for assessing and reporting in Early Childhood Education.

title: CHILDREN AND THE ARTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will explore how young children learn in and through the arts. They will become familiar with pedagogies and practices across the visual arts, 3-dimensional arts, music, creative movement/dance, and drama. Preservice teachers will engage in and reflect upon their own creative processes, with reference to arts-based theories, practices, and research. They will create a teaching resource that connects their learning in this subject with their work-based experience.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement quality arts experiences for young children.
Demonstrate a familiarity with arts education pedagogies and practices.
Understand the role of the teacher in supporting young children’s learning in the arts.

title: CONNECTIONS AND TRANSITIONS: 3-5 YEAR OLD PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject will present pre-service teachers with understandings and knowledge of the importance of continuity in the learning experience. Pre-service teachers will engage with particular transition practices which form a component of the year prior to formal school and which support young children's entry to the school system. Attention will be given to key issues impacting on effective and supportive transition for students between early learning settings and school contexts. Pre-service teachers will develop skills and strategies that are responsive to sector based policies and practices to support children's wellbeing and safety and their engagement in learning, and which reflect knowledge and understanding of relevant legislation and curriculum requirements. Particular consideration will be given to the correlation between the Australian Curriculum and the Early Years Learning Framework. A range of strategies to effectively engage families and professional colleagues in these aspects of the learning process will be examined. Professional Experience of 20 days in a 3-5 year old early learning setting is included in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a range of strategies used to effectively and sensitively promote partnerships between teachers, children, families and other professionals to support transitions and the continuity of the learning process.

Demonstrate understanding of skills and strategies that are responsive to sector based policies and practices to support children's wellbeing and safety and their engagement in learning, and which reflect knowledge and understanding of relevant legislation and curriculum requirements.

Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of the importance of continuity in the learning experience and the key issues which impact on an effective transition between early learning settings and school contexts, with particular consideration given to the correlation between the Australian Curriculum and Early Years Learning Framework.

title: EARLY CHILDHOOD CURRICULUM
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a global view of early childhood curriculum theories and pedagogical practices. You will learn to create and critically analyse curriculum using theoretical perspectives to further understand ways in which curriculum is connected to pedagogy, play, learning and assessment.
learning_outcomes: Design curriculum for an early childhood setting which reflects current perspectives on curriculum design, incorporating the EYLF.
Demonstrate research informed understandings of global perspectives of early childhood curriculum which contribute to children's learning and development.
Demonstrate an understanding of reflective planning cycles and the role of critical reflection in program evaluation to inform curriculum and pedagogy.

title: EARLY YEARS LITERACY AND NUMERACY
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers explore the fundamentals of literacy development and mathematical thinking for teaching and learning for children from birth to 5 years. Pre-service teachers are presented with the theories of early learning alongside the practicalities of shaping appropriate learning experiences for early learners. The notion of curriculum for young children is addressed using the Early Years Learning Framework and the Victorian Early Years Learning & Development Framework. Pre-service teachers will examine early mathematical concepts and processes; such as one to one correspondence, matching and sorting, memory, spatial reasoning and problem solving; and early literacy concepts and processes, including repetition, imitation, text exploration, reading and a range of texts. Representational processes such as drawing, painting and writing, including left/right orientation will be considered. Music, rhythm, beat and movement will be incorporated as tools of creativity which enhance the development of language, literacy and mathematics.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of relevant theoretical perspectives and concepts in literacy and mathematics teaching for children from birth to 5 years of age.

Research and develop appropriate and effective learning experiences, teaching strategies, including play based and intentional teaching, to shape literacy and mathematics curriculum for children from birth to 5 years of age, in response to relevant curriculum documents.
Describe a range of research informed literacy and mathematics learning processes for young children from birth to 5 years.
Develop and collate a range of appropriate ideas and resources to support young children’s learning in areas of literacy and mathematics, including relevant ICT resources.

title: TEACHING EARLY YEARS SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers examine how young children in early childhood education settings can develop their understandings and skills in science and technology. Pre-service teachers will learn to develop curriculum to facilitate problem-solving and inquiry learning as teaching methodologies using social constructivist theory. The content of this subject will be informed by the research and practice of the schools of Reggio Emilia, in conjunction with the requirements of the relevant state and national curriculum documents. Pre-service teachers will enhance their knowledge and understanding of relevant curriculum documents and core concepts in science and technology and they will develop their teaching strategies to ensure these can be introduced to children in meaningful and engaging ways. The Victorian Early Years Learning and Development Framework and the Early Years Learning Framework are included in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Design and evaluate effective teaching and learning experiences and assessment tools in the curriculum areas of science and technology in early childhood education settings, with appropriate reference to relevant state and national curriculum documents.
Demonstrate effective knowledge and understanding of research which indicates that creative problem-solving and inquiry-based projects are effective learning and teaching processes.
Demonstrate effective knowledge and understanding of relevant science and technology curriculum requirements and appropriate teaching strategies in these teaching areas.

title: OUTDOOR AND NATURE PLAY
syllabus_overview: Students in this subject investigate the notion that unstructured play outdoors (nature play) is fundamental to a healthy childhood in that it provides benefits for health, cognitive, social and emotional development and helps to build resilience and creativity. Students also address the proposition that experience in nature as a child may lead to environmental sensitivity and responsibility later in life. Students design effective outdoor settings for children's nature play and manage aspects of safety while maximising exploration and free play. Students identify and document the learning that emerges from outdoor and nature play.
learning_outcomes: Manage aspects of safety while maximising exploration and free play.
Identify and document learning emerging from outdoor and nature play.
Design an effective outdoor setting for children's nature play.

title: TEACHING INDIGENOUS LEARNERS
syllabus_overview: In this subject students develop an understanding of Indigenous education in Australian schools. Pre-service teachers explore educational strategies and pedagogy to support Indigenous children and maximise learning outcomes. Preservice teachers seek to identify the challenges in indigenous teaching and learning and utilize research and resources to inform best practice. The subject will promote positive attitudes within the broader community towards Indigenous students and their cultural protocols.
learning_outcomes: Design indigenous curriculum demonstrating knowledge of a range of resources, including ICT that engage students in their learning.

Demonstrate broad knowledge of understanding and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories, cultures and languages and explore the impact of culture identity and linguistic background on the education of students.
Demonstrate broad knowledge and understanding of the impact of cultural identity and linguistic background on the education of students from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.
Critically examine personal assumptions, preconceptions and values when relating to teaching Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander learners.

title: SPORT AND SKILL ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will analyse both theoretical and practical aspects of a variety of sporting skills, on and off-campus. The off-campus sessions are a series of practical tutorials. In these tutorials, you are introduced to the fundamentals of skill acquisition from a theoretical and practical perspective before learning about the scientific principles of sport skill analysis using a range of analytical systems and tools. You will learn how to analyse, teach, instruct and correct different sporting skills in a progressive learning sequence. You will be introduced to the theory behind sports performance analysis and sport-specific pedagogical frameworks that can be used in a physical education setting. You will then apply different pedagogical frameworks to teach and analyse sporting skills, using different forms of technology to capture and analyse data. You will then produce a Matrix of Analysis for Sports Tasks and provide feedback and strategies on how to improve future performance in a selected sport.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise information to provide feedback to teach and evaluate sporting skills.
Differentiate the different methods used to obtain and analyse sporting skills
Identify the common skill errors and how to rectify them when teaching a variety of sporting skills.
Demonstrate the key teaching points and drills to teach a variety of sporting skills.

title: HOW HUMANS LEARN
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the educational psychology underpinning human learning, including topics such as information processing theory, schema theory, memory consolidation, and executive control. You will take a neurodevelopmental perspective, focusing on the school years. There will be a particular focus on Sweller’s Cognitive Load Theory and Dehaene’s Four Pillars of Learning. You will learn how to use established principles of cognitive science and contemporary behavioural psychology to design learning experiences for maximum impact and to discern pseudoscientific educational approaches from those that align with empirically supported theories. You will also build your confidence to share what you learn in this subject with your teaching colleagues and/or parents to maximise your professional impact.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of current evidence-based approaches to analysing and designing learning experiences.
Differentiate scientifically-aligned educational theories and practices from those for which the evidence-base is weak or non-existent.

Demonstrate strong knowledge of the development of executive functioning in children and adolescents, and information processing models of learning, including selective attention, working memory, and Cognitive Load Theory.

title: RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHERS
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop teachers who can participate in and contribute to embedding a culture of respect and equality across a school community. The focus will be on relationship-based approaches to building resilient and connected learning communities through an exploration of inclusive approaches and practices. The subject aims to apply theoretical understandings of social cultural theories in the broader school community context through community network participation and critical reflection.
learning_outcomes: Develop the skills to establish and maintain respectful, collaborative relationships with students, parents/carers and colleagues regarding their children's learning and wellbeing.
Identify and adopt inclusive and respectful attitudes and interactions to engage and support all members of the learning community.
Draw on theoretical knowledge to reflect critically on their professional relationships and inform/develop their professional identity as teachers.
Develop the skills to participate in professional and community networks and forums to broaden knowledge and improve practice.
Develop the skills to create classroom environments that ensure the social, emotional, and cultural safety of all learners.

title: EVIDENCE OF LEARNING AND USING LEARNER DATA
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will use a construct-based approach to create developmental rubrics and use data and evidence to assess and identify where a learner is in their learning. You will use a set of student assessment data as a basis for determining students’ level of mastery and design a sequence of lessons that build upon each other based on an identified learning progression (construct map). Your sequence will reflect the individual learning needs of your data set and illustrate how you use differentiated practices to support all learners. Assessment data, formative and summative, is a key source of evidence for student learning and achievement and this subject will develop your professional capacity to design effective and impactful teaching and assessment strategies. This subject will encompass data literacy, digital data, analysing and interpreting student learning data, justifying your practice to colleagues, parents, and students, and evaluating your own teaching and learning needs.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse emerging developments and resources that support data-driven teaching to maintain professional skills and knowledge.
Assemble, appraise and interpret a range of student assessment data to plan, review, and modify teaching practice for both individual and whole class scenarios.

Work collaboratively in a professional team to moderate and make judgements about student assessment data, to generate feedback for students about their learning and for parents/carers about student achievement.
Analyse and synthesise student data to design a justified learning sequence of three lessons.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND BUILDING LEADERSHIP CAPABILITIES
syllabus_overview: The content is tailored to both current school-based leaders and principals, as well as aspiring leaders looking to attain leadership roles in education. Demonstrate expert, specialised and technical knowledge in broad educational areas of implementation to address the needs of diverse stakeholders across a range of educational contexts. Analyse the relationship between leadership practices and capacity building, workplace culture, strategy, people and structure as a means of reaching organisational goals and learning outcomes. Critically evaluate sources of leadership issues and identify strategies to effectively address, manage and develop both personnel and stakeholder productivity in educational organisations.
learning_outcomes: Analyse situations thoroughly before making decisions and act decisively in choices including taking responsibility for outcomes.

Analyse and evaluate current research and contemporary literature in leadership and implementation science, including the roles of communication skills; self-leadership; gender issues; ethical issues; and change and innovation.
Reflect critically about their own leadership approaches and capabilities.
Identify, discuss and suggest viable approaches to leadership strategies for future action that demonstrate appropriate behaviours and attitudes.

title: CHANGE AND CONTINUITY: PREPARING FOR EDUCATIONAL FUTURES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will think critically and creatively about Educational futures as part of their transition into the education professions. In doing so, PSTs will learn about how Education and care are not static and unchanging spaces, but ones in which continual change and adaptation is needed. PSTs will learn about policy and curriculum review and reform; constantly evolving education research and evidence bases, shifts in pedagogy and technological advances, and the changing ethics, morals and laws impacting education and care and how these can affect professional practice. They will learn how they can think critically and creatively to bring about ethical and impactful outcomes in their future educational decision-making processes. PSTs will develop skills to critically and creatively reflect on education and care futures and how these could impact the eventual students, parents/carers and members of the community. PSTs will learn how to plan for their future professional learning and development towards sustaining ethical impactful pedagogy throughout their future careers in education.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of need for professional learning and development.
Demonstrate understanding of why education pedagogy and practice needs to be critically examined on an ongoing basis.
Articulate an ethical professional pedagogical position.
Demonstrate critical and creative thinking about education futures.
Demonstrate understanding of the changing nature of education over time.

title: UTILISING EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES
syllabus_overview: Future-focused educators and leaders will be equipped to critically examine and practically engage with the emerging technologies shaping contemporary education, with a particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI). Students will explore the ethical, pedagogical, and systemic implications of these technologies across diverse educational contexts. In addition to interrogating the challenges—such as bias, surveillance, and automation—students will engage with real-world use cases to understand how AI and related tools can be responsibly and effectively used to improve teaching, communication, leadership, and organisational efficiency. The subject supports educators and leaders to become informed, reflective, and strategic in their use of technology, ensuring its alignment with inclusive and ethical educational practices.
