The subject supports students to become informed decision-makers who can harness technology with integrity, creativity, and purpose in diverse educational contexts.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast AI use cases across different educational contexts, analysing their implications for teaching, equity, and school operations.
Describe the potential benefits and challenges of utilising AI into learning and teaching environments.
Assess the effectiveness, efficiency, and ethical soundness of a selected AI or digital tool used in education.
Analyse the impact of emerging technologies on different student populations and/or educational contexts.

title: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, pre-service teachers apply the principles and practices of teaching and learning in the context of their final professional experience. The subject integrates theory of practice through collaboration, critical reflection, analysis, observation, inquiry, and adaptation in connection to the placement experience. The subject includes the pre-service teacher’s final placement (25 days or equivalent). Completing this placement successfully is a requirement to pass the subject. To meet the expectations of the final placement, preservice teachers apply proactive practices in establishing rules and routines, managing behaviour, planning for diverse learning needs, teaching and assessing learning to illustrate graduate readiness. Alongside the placement experience, the pre-service teacher develops and collects evidence for the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA). The GTPA submission enables graduate teachers to demonstrate their experience of planning, teaching, and assessing student learning. The GTPA illustrates one learning sequence within the final placement. This learning sequence is focused on one curriculum area and the relevant cross curricula connections. The GTPA details how the preservice teacher planned for, sequenced learning, and assessed growth for the whole class and three focus students. The GTPA submission will showcase graduate teacher readiness through the development of a portfolio of evidence that justifies the decisions made throughout the learning sequence. The GTPA addresses five practices, planning using data and evidence, teaching and learning, assessing, reflecting and appraising impact of teaching. A minimum of four practices must meet expectations to demonstrate Graduate teacher readiness. In each practice the preservice teacher will justify the decisions made in connection with research, data (evidence), curriculum guidance, pedagogy, and assessment, informed by the context and learner diversity.
learning_outcomes: Provide feedback to learners to inform student self-assessment, goal setting, and to progress learning.
Select and use a variety of assessment tools and practices, addressing fitness for purpose and principles of inclusion.
Identify and justify future teaching and assessment practices in relation to relevant theory.
Make judgements of the quality of student work with reference to curriculum and achievement standards.
Employ a range of suitably challenging and engaging teaching and learning strategies that connect to and build on students’ prior learning.
Make suitable adjustments to teaching based on ongoing student data gathering and analysis.
Discuss how collected data of learning was used to monitor student progress and to modify teaching and assessment strategies.
Collect, interpret and use a variety of student data for diagnostic, formative and summative purposes.
Provide differentiated teaching and learning opportunities.
Engage in moderation of student work.
Connect theory, enacted practice, and the curated body of evidence to evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and demonstrate its impact on student learning.
Describe and analyse the scope and sufficiency of initial and ongoing data choices for identifying students’ learning needs and informing next-step teaching.
Identify and describe differences between planned and enacted teaching, and related pedagogical reasoning.
Examine and discuss teaching decisions, including in-the-moment decisions taken in the classroom, addressing how they were effective or not effective in progressing student learning and why.
Teach general capabilities, including literacy and numeracy, required for student success in learning.
Establish students’ current level of performance, desired level of performance, and readiness for learning.
Use the official curriculum and other relevant materials to plan connected teaching and learning sequences.
Identify opportunities for explicit teaching of general capabilities including literacy and numeracy in the curriculum.

title: STRATEGIC COMMUNICATION FOR EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: Effective communication is at the core of successful educational leadership, shaping the dynamics between school leaders, teachers, students, parents, the wider community and stakeholders. Explore how strategic communication enhances decision-making to foster creative inclusive environments that support shared goals and vision. Utilise diverse communication channels, such as digital platforms and face-to-face interactions, to actively engage stakeholders, address concerns, and celebrate achievements. Develop effective communication techniques to manage change, resolve conflicts, and align organizational priorities to meet stakeholder expectations. Analyse the political, cultural and economic contexts within which contemporary communication and reputation management occur.
learning_outcomes: Contextualise the evolution of contemporary communication to enhance decision-making, foster collaboration, and build trust among stakeholders.
Examine the role of strategic communication in different professional education sectors and contexts
Apply communication theories to independent and collaborative projects across a range of media.
Identify challenges and opportunities for strategic communication practice in different educational contexts
Critically examine internal and external communication engagement

title: TEACHING TECHNOLOGIES AND STEM
syllabus_overview: In this subject, Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) will examine the diversity of curriculum design, considering key priorities of the teaching profession as children age and progress in education settings. They will develop innovative and sustainable design solutions to promote safe, ethical and practical applications to theory by engaging in activities and research across disciplines. This subject will contribute to PSTs’ knowledge and skills to effectively integrate curriculum in early childhood and primary classrooms, whilst developing valuable learning resources that embed cross curricula priorities and capabilities. PSTs will evaluate models of integrated curriculum, culminating in a researched response to effective and innovative integrated curriculum design.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate graduate level knowledge of curriculum and assessment, including embedding the capabilities and cross-curricula priorities, in the innovative design of integrated learning experiences.
Illustrate knowledge of a range of technology tools, resources and innovations that effectively and ethically engage students in their learning.
Critically reflect on content specific knowledge and legislative requirements for maintaining safe learning environments for all students.
Analyse integrated curriculum research and models of curriculum design for effective teaching and learning in primary schools.

title: TEACHING ENGLISH LITERATURE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will draw on knowledge gained from previous subjects in Literacy and Teaching English to build their knowledge of children’s and young adult literature and how to teach the literature strand of the English curriculum in the primary years. The subject focuses on current research in the field of literary theory with an emphasis on the multimodal nature of children’s and young adult literature. The breadth and scope of Australian Children’s literature will be explored including classic and contemporary literature, the narrative traditions and contemporary literature of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and how Australian literature is situated within the international context.
learning_outcomes: Make informed choices about age appropriate literature.
Demonstrate understanding of current research and approaches for teaching literature in a digital multi-literate world.
Examine the major issues involved in the teaching and assessing of Literature in a primary school setting.
Demonstrate understanding of current research and approaches for assessing student learning about literature in a digital multi-literate world.

title: TEACHING PHYSICAL EDUCATION AND HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will explore contemporary approaches to Health and Physical Education curriculum development and teaching through theoretical and practical learning experiences. Preservice teachers will design and apply Health and Physical Education resources and learning experiences. Health and physical literacies will be investigated via a strengths-based approach to learning. Preservice teachers will analyse the key principles of the Health and Physical Education curriculum, explicitly addressing cross-curriculum priorities and capabilities relevant to the discipline, to develop knowledge and skills for application in the primary school classroom.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on planning, resource use including physical spaces, safety and supportive and challenging environments for learning in physical education.
Evaluate a teaching resource embedding digital literacies to expand health learning opportunities for students.
Plan and implement a physical education learning experience, illustrating effective teaching strategies aligned to curriculum and relevant policies.

Examine relevant curriculum, including the capabilities and cross curriculum priorities, contemporary literature and resources, and the implications for student wellbeing and safety in Health and Physical Education.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of research into how students learn and the implications for teaching resources.

title: ARTS SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a secondary Arts (Drama and/or Media and/or Visual Arts) educator at levels 7-10. In this subject, PSTs will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing and evaluating appropriate to Arts education as well as preparation for the senior secondary Arts subjects. PSTs will be introduced to relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards Arts education. They will engage in critique of a selected secondary Arts curriculum document and employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare secondary learners for the task.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant secondary Arts curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ an appropriate learning and teaching sequence using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of various pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant secondary Arts curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.

title: MATHEMATICS FOR UNDERSTANDING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers explore the nature of mathematical learning and the curriculum documents that guide the delivery of the mathematical strands, proficiencies, and mathematical processes. Explicit and responsive teaching approaches embedded with quality contemporary teaching strategies, mathematical teaching resources and technology applications worthy of exploration in the primary years of schooling will be investigated. Pre-service teachers will design sequential learning experiences for students to observe phenomena, ask questions, conduct investigations, look for patterns and relationships, and make conjectures and generalisations to produce, interpret, and evaluate problem solutions. Differentiation and assessment in the mathematics classroom will be explored within the context of regular mathematics learning opportunities. The subject culminates in the pre-service teachers expressing their emerging mathematics teacher identity that is supported by research literature, personal experience, and observed classroom practice, with connection to authentic cross-curriculum contexts and the use of digital technologies.
learning_outcomes: Appraise curriculum resources that build mathematical understandings incorporating relevant theory and practices that reflect differentiation.
Evaluate teaching strategies and planning appropriate for effective learning of the mathematics curriculum for the primary years of schooling.
Demonstrate competence in mathematical understanding, pedagogical content knowledge, and assessment practices for the learning and teaching of mathematics.
Design and evaluate learning and teaching resources related to sequential learning experiences in mathematics.

title: ARTS SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a senior secondary Arts educator (Drama or Media or Visual Arts). In this subject, PSTs will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing and evaluating appropriate to Arts education as well as the high stakes examinations contexts of senior secondary education. PSTs will be introduced to relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards Arts education. They will engage in critique of a selected senior secondary Arts curriculum document within the context of high stakes examinations and employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate senior secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare senior secondary learners for the task
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ an appropriate learning and teaching sequence using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies (including literacy and numeracy teaching strategies appropriate to Arts).
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of various pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching senior secondary Arts curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Arts curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.

title: ENGLISH SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a secondary English educator at levels 7-10. PSTs will learn how to effectively deliver reading and writing instruction that will lead students to understand what mastery in English skills, including text analysis and creative writing, can look like. They will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing, and evaluating appropriate to English and English as an Additional Language education as well as preparation for the senior secondary English subjects. PSTs will engage with a variety of worked examples to understand best practice for planning tasks and lessons and explicit modelling of key English skills that is curriculum-aligned. PSTs will be introduced to relevant theories about curriculum and pedagogy. They will engage in critique of a selected junior secondary English and English as an Additional Language curriculum document. The Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model will be used to design an appropriate English secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare secondary learners for the task, with particular focus on appropriate sequencing and scaffolding of materials.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching junior secondary English and English as an Additional Language, delivering explicit reading and writing instruction to improve student learning.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ coherent and deliberate planning and sequencing of tasks and lessons using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of how to meet students where they are in their learning, using knowledge of curriculum-aligned secondary English content and effective teaching strategies to progress skills needed to attain mastery.

Demonstrate ability to plan for diagnostic, formative, and summative assessment for the purposes of evaluating students against a standard or benchmark to gauge an understanding of the level of mastery attained, using knowledge of relevant secondary English curriculum knowledge and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.
Demonstrate critical curriculum knowledge and understanding of the concepts and structure of the content of junior secondary English and English as an Additional Language.

title: HEALTH AND PHYSICAL EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will undertake both a theoretical and practical study of the Health and Physical Education/PDHPE curriculum/syllabus. PSTS will establish a knowledge and skill base in the areas of curriculum, pedagogy, planning, assessment and reporting in Health and Physical Education/PDHPE education for students in secondary schooling (Years 7-10.) Theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles and state and national curriculum structures within Health and Physical Education/PDHPE are examined and applied in the design, implementation and evaluation of learning resources that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners. Learning experiences will focus on the application of contemporary models and approaches to teaching Health and Physical Education/PDHPE that align with relevant curriculum frameworks in the construction of student-centred activities that enhance student learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of contemporary models and approaches to teaching HPE/PDHPE, and can apply these approaches in the middle years of secondary schooling.

Rationalise, describe, design and evaluate a unit of work involving a variety of teaching strategies that cater for individual differences in student learning across the full range of abilities and integrate general capabilities, including integrate literacy and numeracy capabilities and cross curriculum priorities in HPE/PDHPE.

Apply contemporary models and approaches to teaching HPE/PDHPE that align with relevant curriculum frameworks that will enhance student learning in the middle years of secondary schooling. These include a variety of pedagogical approaches and resources (including safe and ethical pedagogy and use of resources including ICT) appropriate to state and national curricula
Demonstrate knowledge of the concepts, skills, structure of the content and teaching strategies of HPE/PDHPE, and an in depth understanding of how students learn in health or physical education

Examine the relationships between assessment, feedback and reporting, learning task design, student engagement and understanding in HPE/PDHPE. Apply these relationships to the development and modification of curriculum documents.

title: ENGLISH SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be a senior secondary English educator. PSTs learn how to effectively deliver reading and writing instruction that will lead students to understand what mastery in senior English skills, including analysis of various English textual objects, can look like. They will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing, and evaluating appropriate to English and English as an Additional Language education as well as preparation for the senior secondary English subjects. PSTs will engage with a variety of worked examples to understand best practice for planning tasks and lessons and explicit modelling of key English skills that is curriculum-aligned for the high stakes examinations contexts of senior secondary education. PSTs will be introduced to relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards English education. They will engage in critique of a selected senior secondary English curriculum document within the context of high stakes examinations. They will then employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate senior secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare senior secondary learners for the task, with particular focus on appropriate sequencing and scaffolding of materials.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments to gather and interpret information about student learning as learning is taking place, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary English curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise and sequence content into effective lessons underpinned by long-term memory and retrieval practices for high-stakes examinations purposes, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary English curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.
Demonstrate critical curriculum knowledge and understanding of the concepts and structure of the content of senior secondary English subjects.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching the various senior secondary Englishes, delivering explicit reading and writing instruction to improve student learning.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment against senior standards or benchmarks to gauge an understanding of the level of mastery attained, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary English curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ coherent and deliberate planning and sequencing of tasks and lessons using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, demonstrate knowledge of how to meet students where they are in their learning, using knowledge of curriculum-aligned senior secondary English content and effective teaching strategies to progress skills needed to attain mastery knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies (including literacy and numeracy teaching strategies appropriate to English).

title: LANGUAGES SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, as a pre-service teacher (PST) you will develop your understanding of what it means to be a secondary Languages educator at Level 7-10. In this subject, you will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing and evaluating appropriate to Languages education in the first years of secondary education with a view of what language learning may have preceded these years as well as what options may follow for language learning in the senior years of school. You will be introduced to relevant curricula/syllabuses and pedagogical theories, developing, and justifying a pedagogical approach towards languages education. You will engage in critique of selected Languages curricula/syllabuses. You will design an appropriate assessment task and rubric that addresses an area within a relevant language curriculum/syllabus. You will then ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence that prepares secondary learners for successfully completing the assessment task with particular focus on appropriate sequencing and scaffolding of materials.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant Languages curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant Languages curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant Languages curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant Languages curriculum.

title: MATHEMATICS SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of what it means to be an effective Year 7-10 secondary Mathematics educator. PSTs will engage with contemporary approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, assessing, and evaluating appropriate to Mathematics education. PSTs will be introduced to current relevant curriculum and pedagogical theories to develop and justify their pedagogical approach towards Mathematics education. They will engage with Year 7-10 secondary Mathematics curriculum documents and will develop appropriate learning and teaching within lesson design and lesson sequences for students to build mastery.
learning_outcomes: Integrate assessment practices that provide ongoing evidence of student learning and level of mastery attained.
Design effective teaching strategies that address student learning in Year 7-10 mathematics, including discipline specific literacy and numeracy teaching strategies.
Construct learning sequences using Year 7-10 mathematics curriculum and a range of resources (including ICT).
Select resources appropriate for various student learning needs.

Design effective teaching strategies that address student learning in senior secondary mathematics.

title: JUNIOR SCIENCES SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of teaching Junior Science at levels 7-10. PSTs will engage critically with approaches to curriculum, pedagogy, planning, designing, and assessing, appropriate to science education. PSTs will also learn how to plan integrated units in STEM/STEAM, with appropriate content sequencing and well-justified inclusion of high quality explicit teaching.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for summative assessment using knowledge of relevant secondary Science curriculum and UbD planning model, including design and justification of an assessment task and rubric.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant secondary Science curriculum.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant secondary Science curriculum.

title: SCIENCE SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop their understanding of senior secondary science curriculum and pedagogy. PSTs will learn evidence-informed approaches to planning, designing, assessing and evaluating senior secondary science learning, including how to prepare learners for high stakes examinations in one of the disciplines of Biology/Chemistry/Physics/Psychology. PSTs will engage in critique of a selected senior secondary Science curriculum/syllabus (Biology / Chemistry / Physics / Psychology) document and employ the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model to design an appropriate senior secondary assessment task and rubric and to ‘backwards design’ a learning and teaching sequence appropriate to prepare senior secondary learners for the task. .
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of various pedagogical approaches relevant to teaching senior secondary Science curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant senior secondary Science curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Science curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy.

Demonstrate ability to ‘backwards design’ an appropriate learning and teaching sequence using the Understanding by Design (UbD) planning model, knowledge of student learning, content and effective teaching strategies (including literacy and numeracy teaching strategies appropriate to Science).

Demonstrate ability to organise content into a sequence enabling various forms of diagnostic and formative assessments for the purposes of evaluation, reflection and goal setting, using knowledge of relevant senior secondary Science curriculum.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant secondary Humanities curriculum.
Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant secondary Humanities curriculum, SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy

title: CROSS CURRICULUM PRIORITIES
syllabus_overview: This subject is for pre-service teachers with a double curriculum specialisation (e.g. Humanities: History & Legal Studies; Science: Biology & Chemistry; HPE: Health Education & Physical Education; etc.). In this subject, pre-service teachers will learn how to integrate the Cross-Curriculum Priority areas of Sustainability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures, and Asia and Australia’s engagement with Asia into their teaching and curriculum. The focus is on developing knowledge and understanding of specific content and pedagogical approaches to competently integrate the Cross Curriculum Priorities with their method area.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of curriculum integration and pedagogical approaches to the Cross Curriculum Priorities
Demonstrate and apply place-based learning in the curriculum
Apply sustainability, cultural and global perspectives in teaching and learning design

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content of relevant senior secondary Humanities curriculum.

title: SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND PLAY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers examine how learning environments are designed to support young children to develop their understandings and skills in science and technology through play. Preservice teachers learn to develop curriculum to facilitate problem solving and inquiry learning using social constructivist, cognitive science, educational psychology, neuroscience and place-based theories. The content will be informed by core concepts in science, technology, play and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges in conjunction with requirements of relevant state and national curriculum documents. Preservice teachers will engage with real world examples to explore evidence-based pedagogies and develop teaching strategies to convey science concepts to children in culturally responsive, meaningful, and engaging ways. This subject contains 15 days of placement.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise research-informed theories to design learning environments, engagement and feedback strategies that support inquiry-based science and technology learning.
Critically evaluate inquiry-based planning, pedagogy, and assessment practices that support inclusive and high-quality science and technology learning.

Design and evaluate learning and teaching experiences in connection with authentic assessment tools with informed understanding of the concepts, skills, and capabilities important to science and technology curriculum streams.
Evaluate curriculum and pedagogical decisions in relation to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges, including Country, community, and history.
Outline and apply knowledge of key science and technology concepts, and evidence-based pedagogical approaches to play-based learning in early childhood contexts.

title: THE PERMEABLE CLASSROOM
syllabus_overview: This subject is for pre-service teachers with a double curriculum specialisation (e.g. Humanities: History & Legal Studies; Science: Biology & Chemistry; HPE: Health Education & Physical Education etc) In this subject, pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of the ‘permeable classroom’ (Taylor, Fahey, Kriewaldt & Boon, 2019). The Permeable Classroom invites learning that ignores the confines of classroom walls by bringing together the classroom and ‘real’ world by taking learning out into it, or by bringing ‘real world’ learning in. Pre-service teachers will examine the evidence base for experiential and authentic learning and affective, embodied pedagogies (including during remote learning) and consider practical considerations (e.g. duty of care, risk assessment, consent). Pre-service teachers will research, design and justify a permeable classroom learning experience for their second curriculum specialisation, building on what they have already studied in their curriculum specialisation subjects.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of affective pedagogies.
Demonstrate understanding of effective pedagogies.
Demonstrate understanding of approaches that can be used in a permeable classroom.
Demonstrate ability to design an affective and effective learning sequence for a permeable classroom.
Demonstrate understanding of duty of care and other professional teacher responsibilities.

title: SAFE AND ETHICAL EARLY CHILDHOOD SETTINGS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will establish core understandings about how to provide children with safe and ethical early childhood settings. This includes learning about child safety, child development, and how to use established principles of cognitive science and contemporary behavioural psychology to design learning experiences for children across age ranges. Pre-service teachers will consider the importance of family, culture and context to ensure that early childhood settings are culturally safe and inclusive. Pre-service teachers will begin to investigate early childhood curriculum, including the interconnections between learning, development and play, and how these provide a context for designing learning experiences. The implications of policy, curriculum and quality are considered in connection with curriculum approaches. An emphasis on translating these principles into practice will enable students to make connections between ideas and early childhood teaching.
learning_outcomes: Analyse how early childhood curriculum promotes cultural safety, children’s learning and agency in accordance with National Quality Standards and Early Years Learning Framework.
Document and analyse learning information to inform inclusive teaching practices and build meaningful, safe relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
Evaluate and apply relevant theories from the learning sciences and child development to analyse early learning and development in diverse contexts .
Critically examine growth, safety, development, learning, and play in children from birth to five, and apply this to ethical early childhood teaching practice.

title: LANGUAGE, LITERACIES AND PLAY
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers explore opportunities for engaging with children’s literacies in early childhood. The fundamentals of language development and literacy learning are explored from various perspectives including cognitive, developmental and cultural lenses. Pre-service teachers will reflect on the way that theory, development, and pedagogy translate into the intentional way that they work with children. Literacy curriculum for young children is explored, including the Early Years Learning Framework V2.0, the Victorian Early Years Learning & Development Framework, State/Territory interpretations and the Victorian/Australian Curriculum documents. Students will learn to identify early literacy concepts, skills, and resources, and will engage with the notions of multimodal and multiliteracies, and cross curriculum connections. Students will consider the crucial role of culture and families in emergent language and literacy and begin to explore their own developing pedagogy.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and apply research-informed language and literacy learning processes for children from birth to 5 years.

Select, adapt and evaluate a range of culturally responsive, multimodal, and play-based strategies to support young children’s language and literacy development, including children with English as an Additional Language
Critically evaluate theoretical perspectives and concepts relevant to language and literacy teaching for children from birth to 5 years

Demonstrate respectful and informed engagement with First Nations language diversity, including the selection and integration of appropriate local Indigenous language and knowledge into early years practice.

Research and develop appropriate and effective learning experiences and pedagogy, including play based and intentional teaching, to shape literacy and language curriculum for children from birth to 5 years of age, in line with relevant curriculum documents.

title: CURRICULUM, TEACHING AND LEARNING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces participants to foundational ideas, current trends, debates and discussions in higher education curriculum, teaching and learning. Normally, this subject is taken first in the Graduate Certificate of Higher Education. Participants will investigate how teaching can promote active learning through increased opportunities for a variety of forms of learner interactions. They will explore how current trends in higher education affect an institution's teaching and learning strategic plans. Participants will have opportunities to consider their own teaching.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on how current trends in learning and teaching in higher education impact your practice.
Critically analyse the higher education literature in relation to your practice in curriculum, teaching and learning.
Apply the principles of learner interactions and active learning in the design of a teaching and learning activity.
Integrate a scholarly approach to your professional practice.

title: DESIGN AND DELIVERY ONLINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, participants will have an opportunity to develop a deep knowledge and understanding of the key theories and principles in online teaching and curriculum design and apply this knowledge to their practice. They will design learner-centred activities, assessment tasks and feedback processes for online delivery that makes use of inclusive design principles and accommodates diverse learner needs. Furthermore, the subject will enable participants to explore a range of digital tools that encourage engagement and effective learning .
learning_outcomes: Design and evaluate online assessments to achieve learning objectives, including formal and informal feedback processes for diverse learners.
Integrate a scholarly approach to your professional practice.
Apply learning theories and principles to the development and evaluation of meaningful online learning interactions to promote higher-order learning.
Critically analyse and appraise learner-centred approaches to the design and delivery of online learning.

title: EARLY INCLUSIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will investigate the social, emotional and educational needs of children. The neuroscience associated with developmental trauma and impact on learning will be examined. Social justice-based principles of inclusion will be promoted to allow educators to actively include children according to diverse backgrounds, genders and abilities. A holistic perspective informed by sound theoretical and applied models will form the foundation of the investigation and choice of appropriate strategies. Proactive and reactive strategies will be examined within an inclusive education framework. Educator resilience and relational skills required to enable successful inclusion will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Validate curriculum decisions, partnership with families and other professionals to ensure all children participate in and learn from the everyday routines, interactions and play and learning experiences that occur in early learning settings.

Analyse a range of pedagogical principles and practices, including communication strategies, that build relational agency and promote student wellbeing, positive behaviours and learning participation.
Identify and understand the significance of inclusion and strategies for intervention and opportunities for all children.

Identify and understand a range of motivations and neurological differences that influence physical, sensory, intellectual or autism spectrum disorder, behavioural or psychological disorder, communication, learning or developmental delay. Describe and identify a variety of ways to accommodate children with diverse and special needs when planning learning activities.

title: GLOBAL EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS
syllabus_overview: This subject enhances educator perspectives of working equitably and ethically with an understanding of global influences on Early Childhood Education and Care. You will investigate different contexts and policies with the aim of improving learning through professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Critical analysis of documents and contexts by reflecting on and synthesising complex information, concepts, and theories informed by equitable and ethical practices.
Apply education theory, concepts and models to workplace learning and practice that reflect changing global and local circumstances.
Design creative approaches to address events/issues in workplace settings taking local and international perspectives into account.

title: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND WELLBEING
syllabus_overview: In this subject a lifespan approach to human development is undertaken including a focus on theories of physical, social, emotional and moral development as well as the needs and importance of effectively engaging with parents/carers are considered. The socio-ecological context of human development including a capacity to engage effectively with social, environmental and challenges in the contemporary world are explored to examine impacts on human development, well-being and sustainable living. School-based strategies to promote development, and health and well-being are also considered. Contemporary socio-cultural factors that influence child and adolescent development are explored.
learning_outcomes: Explain the socio-ecological context of and possible impacts on, development, wellbeing and sustainable living.
Develop communication skills to identify and cater for the strengths and needs of children, differing family structures and to engage with engage parents/carers.
Describe patterns of development from the pre-natal stage to young adulthood and their implications for wellbeing.
Use a case study to analyse possible impacts on development and wellbeing and to research and describe appropriate school based interventions to support development, learning and wellbeing.

title: HIGHER EDUCATION CURRICULUM DESIGN
syllabus_overview: Good curriculum design in higher education is a critical factor in student satisfaction, success and retention. In this subject, participants explore the practical applications of contemporary higher education curriculum design, models and theories, and reflect on their own educational beliefs and values. Participants take a scholarly approach to curriculum design and gain practical expertise in critically reviewing curricula in higher education.
learning_outcomes: Integrate a scholarly approach to your professional practice.
Critically review and evaluate curriculum design in accordance with contemporary leading practice in higher education.
Analyse and reflect on curriculum theory and how this relates to your professional practice.
Critically evaluate constructive alignment of curriculum in your context.

title: INDEPENDENT READING PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject students examine an area of theoretical and/or professional interest. Students negotiate with the Course Coordinator the specific problem to be investigated; the means by which the problem can be investigated; and the manner in which the findings are to be presented for assessment.
learning_outcomes: Present the findings and or implementation of the research.
Develop and contextualise an area of theoretical or professional interest to be investigated.
Develop the means by which the problem will be investigated and the findings presented.

title: TEACHING IN HIGHER EDUCATION: EFFECTIVE, REFLECTIVE PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Recent trends in the purpose and function of higher education have resulted in a changed understanding of the importance of teaching and learning support. This subject focuses on developing a reflective approach that seeks improvement using feedback that is viewed through a range of lenses. You will engage in critical reflection of your own practice that makes use of personal experience but also the perspectives of students, colleagues, and the literature to improve your teaching and the learning experience of your students. You will also examine the role and function of feedback in student learning and develop evidence-based strategies to improve the quality of feedback that you provide.
learning_outcomes: Generate a cycle of continuous teaching improvement using self, peer and student feedback lenses to reflect on changes to your practice.
Develop quality feedback strategies that are informed by relevant literature in assessment and feedback in higher education.
Integrate a scholarly approach to your professional practice.
Evaluate your teaching practice using reflective practice principles from the higher education literature.

title: LEARNING DIFFICULTIES AND ABILITIES
syllabus_overview: Children may experience a range of learning difficulties that will interfere with learning. In this subject students explore strategies to identify and reduce the impact of learning challenges in education contexts.
learning_outcomes: Describe and identify a variety of ways to accommodate children with diverse learning needs when planning learning activities.

Implement and plan individual learning programs that utilise best practice teaching strategies and interventions and maximise learning outcomes for children with diverse learning needs, while reflecting non-discriminatory practice.
Identify educational and social implications for children with diverse learning needs.

title: LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT IN EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers will examine a broad range of leadership styles and management roles in an early childhood context and recognise their own goals for leadership and management, identifying what success will mean in their future professional and personal lives. They will also investigate the issues that shape early childhood leadership such as: policy, legal requirements, political influences, professional ethics and operational management. Additionally, Pre-service teachers will examine advocacy through leadership research and practice and consider ways to advocate for professional and community awareness of the importance of early childhood education.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and identify personal goals and demonstrate an ability to reflect on own professional abilities and continuous improvement.
Explore aspects of leadership and management and evaluate the attributes of an effective and motivational leader in an Early Childhood context.
Articulate and demonstrate the meaning and purpose of advocacy and activism through leadership.

title: MOVEMENT ANALYSIS IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an alternative to traditional Physical Education (PE) programmes. Since games and sports represents a large proportion of PE programmes within Australia, an appropriate understanding of current trends surrounding the teaching of games that are suitable for children of varying ages is important for pre-service teachers in order to enhance student learning. Subsequently, this subject is designed to introduce pre-service teachers to the educational benefits of student-designed games by integrating different models of PE through creative and innovative projects.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and reflect on the advantages and disadvantages of different pedagogical approaches to the teaching of games and sports in physical education.
Apply and integrate different pedagogical models and approaches to teaching PE and sport through student-designed games that are creative and innovative, and will enhance movement competency.
Analyse contemporary trends surrounding the teaching major and minor of games that are suitable for children of varying ages that enhance student learning in Physical Education (PE) and Sport.

title: MULTIMODAL LITERACIES AND MATHEMATICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will investigate and analyse current research and policy in digital learning, literacy and mathematics including multi-literacies and multimodal resources, with the aim of engaging children and enhancing literacy, mathematical and digital learning in the early years. Relevant research and curriculum documents are used to examine mathematics, literacy and digital curriculum content and identify pedagogical practices which engage children in learning. You will research, plan and analyse inquiry based methodologies as a tool for differentiating the learning activities and assessment opportunities for children with individual learning styles.
learning_outcomes: Examine and analyse policies that legislate and guide safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT for learning and how these policies better position effective engagement with digital literacies in educational contexts .
Design and evaluate integrated early childhood curriculum that incorporates an inquiry approach, with special emphasis on the use of multi-literacies, including an emphasis on multi-modal elements.
Design and evaluate curriculum that build mathematical understandings incorporating relevant theory and practice which reflect differentiation.

title: OUTDOOR EDUCATION SECONDARY CURRICULUM 1
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to establish a knowledge and skill base for pre-service teachers in the areas of critical curriculum knowledge, pedagogy, planning, sequencing, assessment and reporting in Outdoor Education for secondary students in the junior and middle years of secondary schooling (Years 7-10). The subject is designed to develop pre-service teachers' understanding of their own positionality in relation to contemporary theory, concepts and skills in Outdoor Education teaching as applied in classroom and outdoor contexts. Theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles and state and national curriculum structures within Outdoor Education are examined and applied in the evaluation, design and implementation of learning resources that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners whilst being considerate of biases and assumptions in worldviews. Strategic advice relating to teaching this discipline includes safety management and legal responsibilities, application of learning technologies and resources.
learning_outcomes: Describe, design and evaluate a sequence of work involving a variety of teaching strategies that cater for individual differences in student learning across the full range of abilities and integrate general capabilities, cross curriculum priorities, literacy and numeracy in Outdoor Education.

Examine the relationships between formative and summative assessment, feedback and reporting, learning task design, student engagement and understanding in Outdoor Education. Apply these relationships to the development and evaluation of sequence plans.

Plan and synthesise a range of Outdoor Education learning and teaching activities and sequences for junior secondary students (7-10). These include a variety of pedagogical approaches and resources (including safe and ethical pedagogy and use of resources including ICT appropriate to state and national curricula).

Critically analyse outdoor education theory to develop knowledge of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies to enhance student learning. Articulate a professional position on pedagogy in this field with reference to your own positionality.

title: OUTDOOR EDUCATION SECONDARY CURRICULUM 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers develop knowledge and skills for teaching senior secondary outdoor education, particularly in relation to the Victorian Certificate of Education (VCE) Framework. Pre-service teachers learn to develop sequences of work and assessment tasks appropriate for the VCE Outdoor Environmental Studies subject to aid in the progression of skills to attain mastery, with a focus on the critical curriculum knowledge required for students to progress in the subject. Alternative pathways such as the VET Outdoor Recreation framework may be addressed. Strategic advice relating to teaching this discipline is based on learning theories, safety and legal responsibilities, application of learning technologies, audio-visual materials, and resources. Pre-service teachers learn to critically analyse teaching and learning processes in relation to their own experiences on professional placement.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of senior secondary curriculum study and assessment structures commonly used in outdoor education in Australian schools.
Use a critical incident analysis framework and relevant literature to investigate a critical incident in outdoor education teaching and make recommendations for future professional practice.
Develop and analyse tools and practices for assessing, recording and reporting student learning progress in VCE OES to parents and other stakeholders.
Plan a learning sequence to prepare pre-service teachers for assessment tasks consistent with the VCE Outdoor Environmental Studies (VCE OES) study design content and assessment processes.

title: EAL/D SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to develop a knowledge and skill base for Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) in the areas of curriculum, pedagogy, planning, assessment and reporting in English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) for students in the later years of formal learning (Years 11-12) and adult education contexts. The subject is designed to develop PSTs’ understanding and application of contemporary theories and concepts (e.g., plurilingualism), pedagogies, and skills related to students in more advanced levels of formal school learning of EAL/D or in the later stages of adult education programs. Explicit links will be made to teaching EAL/D across learning areas (including cross-curriculum priorities). PSTs will learn how to effectively plan and sequence EAL/D learning and assessment tasks and explicitly teach, model and demonstrate key concepts and skills in relation to state and national curriculum structures and Year 11 & 12 assessment requirements. PSTs will apply their insights into evaluating, designing and implementing high-quality learning and assessment experiences that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners in school and adult education settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant EAL curriculum, additional language acquisition principles, the SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy in ways that explicitly address learner diversity of prior experiences and that integrate cross curriculum priorities.

Locate, evaluate and design effective, engaging and inclusive teaching, learning and assessment resources for English as an additional language learning and the development of plurilingualism for diverse students at the senior secondary and adult levels and appropriate to state and national curricula. Justify ideas and approaches against curriculum, pedagogy and theoretically- and research-based knowledge.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies related to senior secondary and adult learning and teaching, as well as an understanding of key characteristics of additional language learning by people in these settings.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for diagnostic, formative and summative assessment using knowledge of relevant English as an additional language curricula and research based principles of additional language acquisition.
Identify, compare and evaluate learning options for English as an additional language learners at senior secondary and adult levels in the school, vocational and community sectors.

title: EAL/D SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to establish a knowledge and skill base for Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) in the areas of curriculum, pedagogy, planning, assessment and reporting for English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) in years 7-10 or for beginning learners in adult education contexts. The subject develops PSTs’ understanding and application of contemporary theories and concepts (e.g., plurilingualism), pedagogies, and skills related to lower secondary student learning or the early stages of the formal learning of English. PSTs will learn how to support student learning through examining institutional transitions (e.g. primary to secondary school; language centre to mainstream school) and making explicit links across learning areas (e.g., numeracy). PSTs will learn how to effectively plan and sequence learning and assessment tasks and explicitly teach, model and demonstrate key concepts and skills in ways that are responsive to the needs of diverse learners, including students with refugee and disrupted educational experiences.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence for diagnostic, formative and summative assessment using knowledge of relevant English as an additional language curricula.
Formulate a professional and pedagogical position in relation to secondary English as an additional language curriculum and research-based knowledge of second language acquisition.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance and structure of the content and teaching strategies related to English as an additional language, linked to an in-depth understanding of the nature of additional language learning and the diversity of English as an additional language learning experiences.

Demonstrate ability to organise content into an effective learning and teaching sequence using knowledge of relevant EAL curriculum, second language acquisition principles, the SOLO taxonomy and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy

Locate, evaluate and design effective, engaging and inclusive teaching, learning and assessment resources for English as an additional language learning and the development of plurilingualism for diverse students and appropriate to state and national curricula. Justify ideas and approaches against curriculum, pedagogy and theoretically- and research-based knowledge.

title: RELATIONSHIPS AND SEXUALITY EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore a number of key topics specific to Relationships and Sexuality Education, including gender and sexual identity, diversity and inclusion in relation to sexuality, the sexual health of individuals, sexual ethics, respectful relationships and consent. Major approaches to teaching Relationships and Sexuality Education in primary and secondary schools are examined and critiqued. You will develop your own evidence-based pedagogical positions in relation to Relationships and Sexuality Education, using their positions to inform and design teaching and learning experiences against relevant elements of Health and Physical Education curricula.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a professional and pedagogical position in relation to the Relationships and Sexuality components of the Health and Physical Education curriculum.
Critically reflect on concepts and issues raised in the subject and their implications for students and young people in educational contexts.
Use evidence to justify and plan learning experiences for Relationships and Sexuality Education relevant to the Australian and Victorian Curricula.
Use research evidence to critically examine various approaches to Relationship and Sexuality education.
Identify, describe and explain a range of issues and perspectives related to the development of gender, sexual identity, relationships and positive sexual health.
Utilise and review professional, community and industry supports to broaden teaching knowledge and practice and to improve student learning in Relationships and Sexuality education.

title: UNSETTLING SUSTAINABILITY EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will critically reflect on their role & responsibilities as citizens and educators in an Australian and global context. Students will explore underlying social, cultural, historical and institutional factors driving unsustainable ecological, economic and sociopolitical trajectories. In this context, students examine connections between colonialism, globalisation, social and environmental sustainability, and their own approach to teaching and learning. Students will critically reflect on default narratives & initiatives in ‘sustainability education’ (research, curriculum and pedagogy) in global, Australian and local contexts. This work culminates in students exploring how pedagogies informed by relationality, reciprocity, respect, responsibility & circularity can underpin the design of an educational programme that enhances student learning about, and capacity to address, the root causes of global issues as they manifest in local environmental, social and educational settings.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of key axiological beliefs (values) underpinning sustainable and unsustainable systems.
Understand social, cultural, historical and institutional factors driving unsustainable ecological, economic and sociopolitical trajectories issues on a local, national and global scale.
Critically analyse the framing of environmental and sustainability education curriculum and pedagogies.
Incorporate key pedagogical frameworks for sustainability education in the design of a sustainability learning experience about a global issue as experienced in the local context.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject pre-service teachers will deepen their understanding of state and national curriculum structures related to the Program for Students with a Disability, theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles, evidence-based approaches to cater for specific needs and disabilities and requirements for diagnostic, formal and informal assessment and reporting (learning analytics). Content will include the legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to inclusion and support including international agreements. Pre-service teachers will apply this knowledge in the design and implementation of learning resources that are responsive to the needs of individual students with disability and impairment within a MTSS framework.
learning_outcomes: Integrate and apply a range of strategies for reporting to students and parents/carers and the purpose of keeping accurate and reliable records of student achievement.
Evaluate a range of assessment tools designed to optimise the strengths of students with diverse learning needs.
Apply curriculum, assessment and reporting knowledge to inform individualised learning programs for students with special needs in mainstream or special education settings.

title: INCLUSIVE EDUCATION SECONDARY PEDAGOGIES 2
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to extend knowledge and skill in working collaboratively with families, health services and other agencies in the development and implementation of programs for students with additional needs. In this subject pre-service teachers will deepen insights into theoretical concepts, pedagogical principles and processes in relation to state and national curriculum structures. Requirements for supporting students with additional needs and the development of consulting, negotiating and facilitating skills will be addressed.
learning_outcomes: Examine personal and professional communication skills required for engaging with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
Examine the role of external professionals and community representatives in broadening teacher's professional knowledge and practice.
Review and analyse a broad range of strategies for involving parents/carers and professionals in the educative process.
Apply knowledge and understanding to the methodologies that support student with disabilities and impairments through collaborative partnerships involving schools, families and learning communities.

title: SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY LEARNING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will write a proposal to study in a school, community or industry based setting. You will negotiate placement with the Subject Coordinator, conduct the study and evaluate the work placement experience. All placements must be negotiated with the Subject Coordinator prior to writing up the proposal
learning_outcomes: Identify best practice in a learning area of your choice.
Reflect on your own professional experience and your capacity to implement best practice to improve learning outcomes for students with diverse abilities.

title: TEACHER AS A RESEARCHER 1 - RESEARCH METHOD
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore and assess approaches to educational research including teacher inquiry to assist in identifying a research topic and undertaking a literature review. You will analyse aspects of and issues connected to educational research in preparation for a research project to be undertaken in EDU4TR2 Teachers as Researchers 2.
learning_outcomes: Utilise critical approaches to understand and analyse educational research to account for research results.
Analyse and explain the value of teacher inquiry for enhancing professional practice about teaching and learning.
Evaluate the rationale, principles and design of educational research.

title: WORK-BASED LEARNING
syllabus_overview: In this subject students complete a culminating placement in their focus area. The practicum associated with this subject is a work-based experience in a supervised capacity. This subject enables you to participate in an authentic program with an emphasis on applied learning. You are required to undertake Professional experience of 20 days.
learning_outcomes: Construct, apply and maintain a safe and challenging learning environment.
Demonstrate the ability to consistently plan and assess whole programs for effective learning.
Undertake full planning and administrative responsibility for a consecutive two-week block, inclusive of parent liaison and supervision of support workers.
Employ a range of teaching practices and resources to engage children in effective learning.

title: TEACHER AS RESEARCHER 2: RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will design, implement and report on a small scale teacher research project that is aimed at enhancing practice. You will engage in critical reflection and analysis of how educational research can enhance professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Design and present an overview of a small scale teacher research proposal focused on enhancing practice.
Ethical generation of data and systematic analysis of its importance.
Critical reflection and analysis of how educational research supports professional learning.
Design, implement and report on a small scale teacher research project focused on enhancing practice.

title: INCLUSION EQUITY AND ACCESS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are provided with an overview of inclusive education including a critical analysis of issues related to equity, access, participation and life transitions. Relevant policy and legislation that inform the participation and rights of students with a diverse range of abilities will be explored.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain the international and Australian legislative context for considering disability within a rights framework.
Research and examine the ethical considerations that underpin Inclusive Education.
Compare and critically evaluate the differences between medical and socio-cultural models of disability.

title: LANGUAGE AND LINGUISTICS FOR READING INSTRUCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will learn about the structure and development of oral language and how this pertains to early reading instruction and progress across the school years. In particular, students will master the linguistic concepts that define the English writing system as a basis for teaching reading and spelling as reversible processes.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of structural and figurative aspects of oral language to the promotion of spoken language development across the primary and secondary years
Apply knowledge of the linguistic structure of the English writing system to the design and delivery of explicit classroom instruction and support in reading, writing, and spelling.
Demonstrate an understanding of the distinction between oral language and written language, from both developmental and educational perspectives

title: INSTRUCTIONAL DESIGN FOR LANGUAGE AND LITERACY TEACHING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore and critique contemporary models for language and literacy instruction through the cognitive science lens. You will apply this to a whole-of-school approach that incorporates a low-variance curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Describe the theoretical foundations and empirical support for contemporary instructional design models and pedagogical practices.
Employ cognitive psychology frameworks to make informed pedagogical decisions regarding language and literacy (reading, writing and spelling) instruction for all learners.
Examine the role of the low-variance curriculum as a whole-of-school approach to instructional design and implementation

title: MULTI-TIERED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT ACROSS YEAR LEVELS
syllabus_overview: This subject is concerned with effective instructional design using the principles of Multi-Tiered Systems of Support, including Response to Intervention. You will learn about standardised and non-standardised screening and diagnostic monitoring tools and how to effectively use assessment data to design, deliver and evaluate classroom instruction. The importance of whole-school policy and practice will be emphasised.
learning_outcomes: Implement and evaluate pedagogical practices across instructional tiers of intervention informed by reliable and valid diagnostic assessment data.
Apply effective and evidence-based principles of progress monitoring within a Multi-Tiered Systems of support model.
Select and apply standardised and non-standardised assessment tools including administration, scoring and interpretation.

title: COGNITIVE SCIENCE MODELS OF READING AND WRITING
syllabus_overview: This subject is concerned with a range of theoretical models describing the components and the processes essential for reading and writing proficiency. Drawing on linguistic models and cognitive models of information processing, you will critique the empirical support for these models and make research-informed decisions about classroom practice at primary and secondary levels.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply evidence-based models of reading and writing instruction for novice and established learners across year levels.
Apply knowledge of information processing to the teaching of reading and writing.
Critique selected theoretical models of reading and writing and examine multi-tiered levels of instruction.

title: UNDERSTANDING LEARNING AND DIFFERENTIATION
syllabus_overview: This subject is concerned with how humans learn new information, from infancy to early adulthood, in circumstances of both typical and atypical development. You will learn about development of the human brain and the physical, cognitive, linguistic, and social processes supported by this; you will examine the role of cultural and linguistic diversity in learning and achievement at school and will learn to apply Response to Intervention principles across all tiers of instruction and support. You will differentiate evidence-informed practices from those that are pseudoscientific and fail to deliver on robust outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to design whole class instructional and progress monitoring activities that align with the principles of contemporary learning science frameworks.
Apply knowledge of typical and atypical neurodevelopment to the instructional context to respond to the needs of diverse learners in the classroom in a Response to Intervention (RTI) framework.
Differentiate between teaching and intervention approaches that are well-supported by rigorous research evidence and those that are of low efficacy and impact.
Demonstrate the ability to identify students requiring intervention and the role of family-school connections, community agencies, representatives and external professionals in meeting such needs.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND ASSESSING INTEGRATED CURRICULUM
syllabus_overview: This subject provides Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) with a deep understanding of how to design and assess integrated curriculum that acknowledges that meaningful and transferable learning occurs across discipline areas and stages of schooling (F-12). PSTs will identify and synthesise unifying concepts across learning areas (including cross-curriculum priority areas) and general capabilities (e.g., competencies). Primary-focused PSTs will learn disciplinary and pedagogical knowledges across Health and Physical Education (e.g., PDHPE), Humanities, English, and Mathematics, and secondary-focused PSTs will explore opportunities to apply an integrated curriculum approach to their discipline/learning area. PSTs will learn how to make meaningful connections between these learning areas as well as cross-curricular priorities and general capabilities. Furthermore, PSTs will learn how to explicitly teach reading, writing and numeracy within discipline-specific content, justifying their approach with research relating to how this improves student engagement and academic achievement. In addition to learning how to design an integrated lesson and/or unit, PSTs will also develop their understanding of evidence-based assessment practices relating to diagnostic, formative and summative assessment. Drawing upon a developmental assessment approach, PSTs will learn how to select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning. Through developing familiarity with curriculum documents and key resources, students will understand the strength and potential of integrated learning for their ongoing teaching practice. This subject includes evidence-informed instructional and assessment practices in reading, writing, numeracy and multimodal learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate core disciplinary knowledge in Humanities, Health and Physical Education/PDHPE, English and Mathematics
Design learning and assessment sequences that incorporate integration across curriculum areas
Select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning.
Demonstrate understanding of integrated curriculum and how it contributes to learning and disciplinary knowledge in Humanities, Health and Physical Education/PDHPE, English and Mathematics

title: FRAMING IDENTITIES AND CULTURES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop core knowledge, skills and dispositions required to be equity-oriented teachers. The subject foregrounds intercultural understanding and the development and deepening of students’ understanding of the diversity among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages, societies, cultures, world views, histories and contemporary experiences. You will examine your own cultural identities, representations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and become critically reflective of the historical circumstances that have impacted people in Australia. You will develop an understanding of theories, strategies, and pedagogical approaches that align with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledge and perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of culturally safe and inclusive resources and pedagogies from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspective.
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of and respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and histories

Illustrate and evaluate how media representations and personal histories and experiences shape and influence perceptions of and assumptions about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and community life.
