Critically reflect on ethics, beliefs and emerging teaching philosophies.
Explore and analyse theories of cultural identity, and productively engage in challenging conversations around equity, diversity and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education.

title: PROFESSIONAL IDENTITY AND ETHICS FOR EDUCATORS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop their understanding of what it means to be an ethical education professional. Students will learn about the laws, formal professional codes and informal ethical frameworks that regulate and guide professional relationships in education settings. They will explore how these formal ethical practices and regulations shape decisions regarding inclusive pedagogical practices and proactive classroom management and apply these understandings during their placement. They will engage in critical reflection to consider their own values and beliefs and how these affect their professional relationships with other people in educational contexts, including with students, staff, parents/carers and communities. This subject involves a 15 or 20 day placement based on your course commencement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of legal obligations, requirements and responsibilities for education professionals.
Demonstrate knowledge of formal codes of conduct and ethics for education professionals.
Apply formal and informal ethical frameworks to guide and justify professional practice
Demonstrate knowledge of education ethics theories and approaches.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF LANGUAGE AND EARLY READING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the process of children’s oral language acquisition and how literacy is mastered. You will critically appraise a range of theoretical models describing the process of reading and consider the implications for classroom instruction. You will also explore the structure of oral language and how this pertains to early reading instruction and progress across the school years. In particular, you will be taught about linguistic concepts that are pertinent to the teaching of reading, spelling, and writing.
learning_outcomes: Describe the linguistic structure of the English writing system and explain how this informs instruction in the core elements of literacy: reading spelling and writing.
List and define the components of oral language and explain how oral language skills form the foundation for learning literacy.
Describe and contrast the processes of oral language acquisition with the mastery of literacy.
Examine various theoretical models of reading and identify those that have empirical support for translation into classroom practice.

title: TEACHING MATHEMATICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers will explore pedagogies appropriate for the learning and teaching of mathematics in the primary years of schooling. The subject will emphasise tailoring instruction to match learner expertise and diverse ability levels, including the importance of explicit instruction (avoiding self-directed approaches) for novice learners and independent problem-solving once a student approaches proficiency in underpinning mathematical concepts. The subject will model the implementation of rich tasks that promote mathematical proficiencies and working mathematically (communication, problem solving, reasoning, understanding and fluency), mathematical inquiry, and mathematics skill development for school students across the strands, scope and sequence documents of the Australian, Victorian and NSW Curricula. An emphasis will be placed on the relationships among teacher mathematics content knowledge, pedagogy, models of learning, resource selection, differentiation and inclusive teaching and student achievement in mathematics. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and cultural understanding of Primary Mathematics will be embedded. Engagement in the subject will include pre-service teachers participating in a community of learners to design and deliver teaching episodes using digital technologies to their peers for evaluation and constructive feedback.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of mathematical knowledge and skills appropriate for primary teaching and explain the importance of this understanding for instructing novice learners (teacher-led schema development).

Identify and apply appropriate, inclusive pedagogies for developing and assessing mathematical concepts and skills (numerical, spatial, graphical, statistical, and algebraic) and proficiencies (understanding, fluency, problem solving and reasoning).

Justify the selection, application, and adaptation of learning resources to address all students’ learning needs, including the progressive removal of scaffolding as learners become more proficient in mathematical concepts and skills and general thinking skills.
Evaluate mathematics learning and teaching resources accounting for learner characteristics such as novice/expert status, development of executive functioning skills, and working memory limitations.

title: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (STEAM)
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) will develop the knowledge, skills and competencies needed to teach science and technology (ST) in primary schools. In addition to pedagogies that deepen student learning in ST, PSTs will explore teaching ST. PSTs will identify high quality curriculum resources for teaching ST topics, which will then be used to develop an interdisciplinary unit plan. Contemporary issues and historical and cultural contributions to ST, and implications for ST teaching, will be examined. PSTs will demonstrate developing knowledge of the general capabilities and cross curricular priorities and how these intersect with the ST Curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Apply digital literacy knowledge to select and design inclusive science resources.
Apply understanding of science and technology curriculum, the general capabilities and cross-curriculum priorities to learning and assessment sequences.

Critically select and reflect on age-appropriate knowledge of historical and cultural contributions to science and technology as well as related contemporary issues, including the concepts, substance and structure of the content and assessment.
Identify and apply contemporary pedagogical and multidisciplinary approaches, such as the 5E instructional model or a design cycle, for planning and teaching science and technology.
Research and justify the science and technology knowledge, methods, skills and resources required to communicate science and technology understandings and findings.
Demonstrate understanding of assessment strategies, including informal and formal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches to assess student learning.

title: LEARNING DESIGN AND CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) to knowledge and skills that educators need for impactful pedagogies in their teaching. PSTs will examine and engage with national and state-based curricula and learn evidence-based instructional and assessment strategies. Guided by the framework of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), PSTs will learn how to sequence learning experiences for learners across a range of ability levels and contexts, including digital learning environments. PSTs will also learn about the nature and efficacy of both proactive and responsive positive behaviour management practices, and plan and rehearse effective techniques for use in the classroom. Digital literacy is embedded throughout, with PSTs developing understanding of teaching and learning using digital tools, alongside ethical and legal concerns. This subject involves 15 or 20 days of placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of a broad range of evidence that can be used to inform teaching and learning, including for managing students with challenging behaviours.
Design learning sequences that align with universal design for learning principles.
Plan learning sequences that include classroom rules and routines and other proactive practices for establishing a structured, safe, and positive learning environment to enhance student engagement.

Demonstrate integration of digital skills and tools to enhance learning experiences, demonstrating understanding of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning.
Evaluate student data for the purpose of providing feedback and setting learning goals.
Demonstrate understanding of the relationship between curriculum, pedagogy, assessment and classroom management.

title: UNDERSTANDING RESEARCH FOR PROFESSIONAL ENQUIRY
syllabus_overview: This subject equips you to engage with and be discerning consumers of research. You will develop their skills and understanding of the purpose, structure, and processes of research and evaluate how research informs teacher professional inquiry. Students will generate a strong understanding of quality, credibility, and reliability when evaluating research on evidence-based teacher practice. Throughout the subject, you will develop critical reflection and analysis capacities in evaluating how research can inform and improve your teaching practice and influence student learning outcomes. Master of Teaching (Primary) students must conduct their research within their undergraduate discipline area in order to develop specialist content and pedagogical knowledge. Specialist classroom practice is undertaken in ‘Teaching for Inclusion and Impact’.
learning_outcomes: Critically review educational research literature and evaluate its relevance to professional teaching practice.
Identify the nature, scope, contributions to, and limitations of research on professional, practical and critically reflective teacher knowledge.
Conceptualise and design a teacher research project for professional inquiry.
Critically reflect on a range of theoretical and practical perspectives in the research literature and evaluate how this can inform teaching practice.

title: TEACHING ENGLISH AND EAL/D
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will draw on their previously learned knowledge about the foundations of literacy and curriculum development to further build reflexive understandings, skills and competencies needed to teach the English and English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EAL/D) Curricula in primary schools. Students will explore pedagogical applications of core conceptual understandings about culturally responsive teaching of English and EAL/D. They will engage in critical self-inquiry to understand how their own and existing possible biases and assumptions about diverse groups and worldviews can have implications on the teaching of literacy, literature and the English language. They will plan for and assess EAL/D student learning by implementing culturally responsive practices including Indigenous knowledges and perspectives. Students will demonstrate their ongoing intercultural development and knowledge of the English and EAL/D Curricula and how these guide content selection and pedagogical approaches for teaching and assessment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse student work samples to demonstrate understanding of how assessment of student learning informs teaching.
Examine the major issues involved in the teaching of English language, literature and literacy in the culturally and linguistically diverse primary school setting.

Demonstrate understanding and critical analysis of current research and methodologies for teaching English literature, language and literacy in a digital multiliterate world to all students including those from EAL/D backgrounds.
Examine pedagogies, assessment strategies, and learning sequences relevant for teaching English to learners for whom English is not their first language.
Design learning sequences that reflect understanding of English and EAL/D curriculum content and pedagogy.

title: INTEGRATED CURRICULUM: ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER HISTORIES AND CULTURE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with a deep and experiential understanding of pedagogical and disciplinary approaches to Indigenous cultures, perspectives and knowledges, across the Arts, Humanities, English, and Mathematics. Practical examples of what cultural safety can look like in practice will be explored. Through developing a familiarity with curriculum documents, you will understand the strength and potential of integrated learning for your ongoing teaching practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify, understand and apply different models and approaches to enhance student learning in the primary school Humanities and Arts setting.
Apply knowledge and understanding of Indigenous cultures and perspectives into pedagogical and disciplinary content of Humanities and the Arts and design
Apply a sense of place and the connection to land and community into pedagogical and curriculum design

Integrate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories, perspectives and culture with Humanities, the Arts, English and Mathematics into effective teaching and learning in the primary school setting.

title: TEACHING FOR IMPACT AND INCLUSION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers critically analyse the breadth of educational settings and student learning needs in the context of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) and the Practice Principles. Pre-service teachers investigate the notion that every child, regardless of their challenges, has the ability to learn and that every learner has the opportunity to be successful. Pre- service teachers learn ways in which differences between learners (including their developmental characteristics, prior learning, literacy and numeracy levels, wellbeing, and mental health) impact on their specific needs for engagement and learning. This will provide a context for better understanding of some challenging behaviours such as disengagement, withdrawal, confrontation, and bullying. This will be evidenced by using evidence-informed judgements to apply various teaching strategies including the Victorian Teaching and Learning Model (VTLM) to improve students’ academic (literacy and numeracy) as well as social-behavioural outcomes. Through the materials encountered in the subject, preservice teachers generate their future classroom design of a positive, inclusive, differentiated and effective learning environment.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate positive, safe learning environments that embed professional and community requirements.

Identify evidence-based, age-appropriate approaches that consider student academic (including literacy and numeracy), wellbeing, and mental health when addressing challenging student behaviours such as disengagement, withdrawal, bullying and confrontation.
Describe ways in which research-informed relational teaching strategies can help to support healthy classroom relationships, inclusion, and wellbeing.
Develop Individual Education Plans (IEPs) for students for students with diverse socio-emotional and academic (including literacy and numeracy) needs.
Design and implement a micro-teaching moment that embeds effective pedagogical practices addressing the social-emotional and academic needs (including for literacy and numeracy) of students
Develop and annotate inclusive and differentiated lesson plans utilising teaching strategies that maximise learning outcomes (including in literacy and numeracy) for all students.

title: RESEARCHING TEACHER IMPACT
syllabus_overview: This subject equips students to engage with and be discerning consumers and producers of research. Students will develop their skills and understanding of the purpose, structure and processes of research and evaluate how research informs teacher professional inquiry. Students will generate a strong understanding of quality, credibility and reliability when evaluating research on evidence-based teacher practice. They will apply this understanding to engage in collaborative inquiry with their peers and supervising teacher to develop an area of technical knowledge. Throughout the subject, students will develop critical reflection and analysis capacities in evaluating how research can inform and improve their teaching practice and influence student learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Critically review and reflect on evidence collected through systematic inquiry.
Systematically engage with literature to inform evidence-based teacher practice.
Develop skills to conduct and report on ethical and professional teacher inquiry.
Develop an area of technical knowledge through collaborative teacher professional inquiry.

title: LITERACY AND NUMERACY ACROSS THE CURRICULUM
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will demonstrate understanding of how a focus on literacy and numeracy can evidence outcomes for learning areas other than English and mathematics. Preservice teachers will design teaching and learning experiences across the discipline areas of the Australian Curriculum. For literacy, preservice teachers will focus on various genres of writing for discipline-specific purposes and how to integrate their application across the primary curriculum. In relation to numeracy, preservice teachers will identify the way in which numerical information and mathematical representations are embedded in meaningful contexts and how the mathematics can be used to make evidence-based informed decisions. A critical literacy and numeracy framework will be used to explore the utility of various resources for learning and teaching purposes.
learning_outcomes: Apply understanding of how literacy and numeracy can enhance learning in areas other than English and Mathematics.
Identify reasons for and describe methods of explicitly teaching literacy and numeracy across the curriculum.
Identify the purpose and audience for different written and communication genres and identify associated literacy teaching opportunities and strategies.
Utilise ICT/digital technology to support and extend literacy and numeracy in a learning activity.

title: INTEGRATED CURRICULUM: GENERAL CAPABILITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) develop knowledge and skills related to teaching and assessing general capabilities/competencies (including literacy and numeracy) in primary or secondary settings. Pre-service teachers learn how to support and scaffold students’ development of general capabilities/competencies in both personal and educational contexts and across discipline areas over time through evidence-based learning and assessment design. General capabilities/competencies are examined, specifically, within the Arts, PDHPE, English, and Mathematics, and PSTs learn to plan, teach and assess learners within an integrated curriculum that incorporates general capabilities/competencies. Overall, the aim of this subject is to enable pre-service teachers to identify the relevance and importance of general capabilities/competencies and learn to apply this knowledge across the curriculum, including when designing integrated curricula.
learning_outcomes: Design assessment strategies, including informal, diagnostic, formative and summative approaches, to assess students’ development of general capabilities/competencies.

Locate and analyse general capabilities/competencies in curriculum and communicate how they contribute to learning and disciplinary knowledge in Arts, Health and Physical Education, English, and Mathematics.
Demonstrate understanding of general capabilities/competencies in personal and educational contexts
Evidence and apply knowledge of general capabilities/competencies to create inclusive integrated teaching and learning experiences.

title: TRANSITIONS AND PEDAGOGIES: MIDDLE AND SENIOR SCHOOL
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this subject is to develop pre-service teachers' in-depth understanding of how young people transition through secondary schooling contexts as whole beings. It explores how educators can effectively support these transitions by drawing on key concepts in human learning and adolescent development. Topics include brain development, socio-emotional and moral growth, memory function, cognitive overload, and the debunking of common neuromyths. These are examined through the lens of the personal, social, ethical, critical, and creative dimensions of the curriculum. There is a focus on the decisions and choices that secondary school students are making about their learning and career pathways. The subject also emphasizes the creation of positive classroom environments to support transitions, highlighting the importance of rules and routines, and strategies that foster lifelong learning habits, resilience, responsibility, and independence. Effective approaches for engaging with families to promote learning in secondary contexts are also explored.
learning_outcomes: Research and develop an understanding of transitions and changes that affect young people in secondary schooling contexts, including effective approaches for engaging with families to promote learning and career pathways.

Demonstrate an understanding and ability to navigate curriculum and syllabi to support student learning through secondary schooling, including personal and social, ethical, critical and creative dimensions of curriculum and understanding the role of language and culture.
Develop strategies and approaches, including rules and routines, that promote positive behaviour and support young people in secondary schooling contexts to develop lifelong learning habits.

Critically engage with learning and development theories with specific focus on how the brain develops from childhood to young adulthood, in order to support the knowledge acquisition of young people transitioning through secondary schooling contexts.
Research and demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of engaging with and motivating young peoples’ interests through student voice and agency.

title: DIGITAL LITERACIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) will develop skills and knowledge related to digital literacies in the curriculum and society at large, with a focus on preparing them to effectively teach and model digital literacy in the classroom. PSTs will analyse personal digital literacies and technical skills within the expertise of their discipline, understanding that good teaching starts with demonstrating and showing students what they need to do. Knowing that the characteristics of digital literacies are ever evolving, PSTs will research digital literacy education policies and the impact of digital literacy on teaching and learning. Developing the capacity to interact and collaborate with an online community of peers, PSTs will exchange ideas and work together to develop valuable constructs and co-create professional learning resources that embed the cross-curricula priorities and capabilities. By the end of this subject, PSTs will be able to confidently model and demonstrate digital literacy skills to their students in the classroom.
learning_outcomes: Examine trends in digital literacies and their deployment in education and society at large, embedding considerations of the capabilities and cross-curricula priorities.
Analyse educational theories, frameworks and policies, specifically those that relate to the application of digital literacies in secondary school environments.

Synthesise and develop teacher professional development resources on how to teach digital literacies in the classroom that encompass the complex issues impacting on effective and ethical digital literacies.

Appraise digital devices or systems, learning to make the most of the available technologies, adapting to new ways of doing things as technologies evolve and protecting the safety of self and others in digital environments.
Research and critically select effective and engaging teaching strategies to create, manage, communicate and investigate digital literacies across disciplines.

Demonstrate and apply practical skills in designing digital technology tools and innovations for effective engagement in the classroom, including teaching resources that develop students' sense of digital citizenship and digital literacies in effective and ethical ways, while confidently modelling digital literacy skills to guide students.

title: DIVERSE LEARNERS AND PEDAGOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers (PSTs) develop an understanding of teachers' and educational institutions' responsibilities for proactively catering for students with disability and working collaboratively with families, carers and other agencies to achieve optimal learning conditions for students with disability. The specific challenges that different individuals and groups confront in educational settings are explored, as are the legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to student inclusion and support, which require that students with disability should have the same opportunities and choices in their education as students without disability. Pre-service teachers will consider evidence-based strategies to maximise the educational experience and achievements of students with diverse needs, including through Tier 1 teaching practices. High prevalence examples of diversity in the classroom, such as Autism Spectrum Disorder, learning disabilities and learning difficulties, are introduced in this subject. Using Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles, students will apply theoretical understandings to real world issues of learner difference to identify barriers to learning and participation and to maximise learning for all students. Pre-service teachers will analyse school and teacher approaches to responding to student diversity including adaptive pedagogies, individualised learning plans, approaches to curriculum design, and multi-tiered systems of support.
learning_outcomes: Explore evidence-based strategies for supporting diverse learners through collaborative partnerships involving schools, families and allied health professionals.
Demonstrate knowledge of responsive teaching strategies which optimise the strengths and needs of all students.
Plan for and design individualised learning programs to support students with additional needs for maximum participation in learning.
Utilise instructional approaches that maximise learning outcomes for students with additional needs, including Tier 1 instruction.
Understand the need to cater for diversity and the major issues involved in teaching in diverse classrooms.

title: SUSTAINING EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject pre-service teachers apply the principles and practices of teaching and learning to independently plan and execute units of learning. The subject applies evidence-based practices to a range of school contexts. The subject includes the pre-service teacher’s final professional experience placement (25 days or equivalent) during which the pre-service teacher develops and collects evidence required to complete the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA). The GTPA enables graduate teachers to demonstrate how they align curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment, taking account of school contexts and learner diversity. The GTPA addresses five practices, of which a minimum of four must be demonstrated at a satisfactory standard. This subject provides confirmation of graduate teachers’ readiness for classroom teaching. This subject involves a 25-day placement. Successfully completing this placement is a requirement to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Discuss how collected data of learning was used to monitor student progress and to modify teaching and assessment strategies.
Design summative assessments and make judgements of the quality of student work with reference to curriculum and achievement standards.
Identify and describe differences between planned and enacted teaching, and related pedagogical reasoning.
Describe and analyse the scope and sufficiency of initial and ongoing data choices for identifying students’ learning needs and informing next-step teaching.
Employ a range of suitably challenging and engaging teaching and learning strategies that connect to and build on students’ prior learning.
Establish students’ current level of performance, desired level of performance, and readiness for learning and plan introductory lessons based on this knowledge.
Examine and discuss teaching decisions, including in-the-moment decisions taken in the classroom, addressing how they were effective or not effective in progressing student learning and why.
Identify opportunities for explicit teaching of general capabilities including literacy and numeracy in the curriculum.
Use the official curriculum and other relevant materials to plan connected teaching and learning sequences.
Engage in moderation of student work using developmental rubrics with criteria tailored to a specific tasks and/or work samples.

Provide feedback to learners to inform student self-assessment, goal setting, and to progress learning. Including feedback as learning that is specific, honest, construe. The uses explicit teaching strategies to re-teach concepts, scaffold, or correct misconceptions as necessary.
Identify and justify future teaching and assessment practices in relation to relevant theory.
Make suitable adjustments to teaching based on ongoing student data gathering and analysis.
Teach general capabilities, including literacy and numeracy, required for student success in learning.
Select and use a variety of assessment tools and practices, addressing fitness for purpose and principles of inclusion.
Provide differentiated teaching and learning opportunities.
Collect, interpret and use a variety of student data for diagnostic, formative and summative purposes.
Connect theory, enacted practice, and the curated body of evidence to evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and demonstrate its impact on student learning.

title: REVIEWING EDUCATIONAL LITERATURE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with the necessary knowledge and skills to conduct traditional narrative literature reviews. Students will learn about the purposes and features of different types of literature reviews, including how traditional narrative literature reviews compare with systematic literature reviews. They will learn how to identify, analyse, and synthesise high quality, relevant literature (including peer-reviewed and grey literature) and how to locate proposed research questions and projects within this broader literature. Literature search strategies and the use of reference management systems will also be addressed.
learning_outcomes: Justify the significance, originality, and coherence of a set of proposed research aims and associated questions.
Distinguish between different kinds of literature reviews in terms of their defining features and purposes.
Locate, critically analyse, and synthesise existing theories, knowledge, ideas, and research methods relevant to an identified research problem.
Identify knowledge gaps and weaknesses within the existing research literature on a topic.

title: EDUCATION RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject supports students to develop an understanding of a range of methodologies used in educational research. It explores both general methodological questions and concerns in the field of educational research as well as the use of specific research methodologies and methods, spanning qualitative and quantitative approaches. Students will consider the general affordances and limitations of different methods and methodologies, before exploring a methodological approach relevant to their own research question(s) in more depth.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of specific research methods suited to their research aims and questions.
Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to research ethics and integrity.
Analyse the strengths and limitations of a range of methodologies used in the field of educational research.
Identify specific statistical analyses and the types of research question they can address.

title: EDUCATION RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject requires students to develop and execute a small (one semester) research project, in the form of secondary research, for example a desktop study or document analysis. Students will begin by developing a research proposal outlining (1) a rationale for the project, including the purpose of the research, its significance, and the research question(s) to be investigated; (2) a brief review of pertinent literature; (3) an overview of the proposed methodology and its appropriateness for answering the research question(s) within the given time constraints; and (4) an outline of the project timeline. The subject will culminate in the submission of a report on the research undertaken and the associated findings and implications.
learning_outcomes: Conduct a small research project, analyse the findings, and identify key conclusions and implications.
Critically evaluate and synthesise relevant research literature to demonstrate the originality and significance of the proposed study.
Clearly define and justify a coherent and feasible research design for a small (one semester) research project.
Identify and justify a coherent and significant research topic, problem and question(s) for a small-scale research project.

title: EDUCATIONAL SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: Develop your understanding of education systems in Australia and internationally, including how they have developed over time, are organised and the social, political and economic contexts that influence them. Explore the complex Australian education system, including early childhood, primary, secondary, tertiary, Vocational and developmental education, and the services that support and regulate them. Consider theories of globalization, the changing role of the state, the restructuring of education, and current development models, in order compare approaches to educational systems and policymaking locally and internationally.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate international awareness and openness to the world, based on understanding and appreciation of social and cultural diversity and respect for individual human rights and dignity
Critique education systems, policy and management in contemporary society
Critically analyse education systems in Australia, and the social, political and economic contexts that influence them.

title: LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS: APPLICATIONS OF THE LEARNING SCIENCES
syllabus_overview: The Learning Sciences is an interdisciplinary field, which investigates how people learn (EDU4001) and how learning environments are designed to support effective, inclusive, and enduring learning. In this subject, you will engage with foundational theories and emerging research drawn from cognitive science, educational psychology, sociology and neuroscience to better understand how educators create environments for learning. Through critical engagement with research and real-world examples, students will explore principles that underpin evidence-based teaching and learning in contemporary educational settings. By the end of the subject, students will be equipped to critically evaluate educational practices through a learning sciences lens.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the role of classroom routines, engagement strategies, and feedback mechanisms in designing learning environments.
Identify one’s own assumptions about teaching and learning in light of current research in the Learning Sciences.
Interpret and apply cognitive theories to real-world teaching scenarios.
Apply interdisciplinary insights from the Learning Sciences to design a professional learning session.

title: EVALUATING EVIDENCE IN EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: Learn about the nature of evidence as a contextual, politicised concept that can take many forms, and the ways that it is utilised in education. Explore key debates about evidence in education curriculum, policy-making and reform both locally and internationally. Engage with evidence-based teaching, and the numerous forms of evidence and critically evaluate their usefulness in varied education scenario, and to varied stakeholders. Critically reflect on your own positioning and engage with different research-informed perspectives around evidence, what it constitutes, and to whom.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse current applications of evidence in education policies and reforms, including those related to curriculum, drawing on relevant research literature.
Reflect critically on how evidence in education reflects diversity and your own perspectives and positioning in relation to education debates about evidence.
Critically analyse evidence-based teaching, and apply the knowledge and skills to varied education scenarios

title: DRIVING EDUCATIONAL CHANGE AND IMPROVEMENT
syllabus_overview: Explore core principles and concepts related to educational change and improvement and strategic partnerships across various organisations, including NGOs, public and private enterprises, community corporations, government departments, and inter-agency alliances. The focus is on using a cross-disciplinary approach to understand the impact of both educational reforms and strategic partnerships on organisational effectiveness, creativity, cost efficiency, and synergy. Key theories such as systems theory, complexity theory, network theory, and change theory, as well as the applied sciences, will be reviewed to analyse and critique aspects like negotiations, shared vision, network building, organisational change, strategic management, participative leadership, and problem-solving. The goal is to develop critical reflective and cross-organisational skills to advance strategic goals. Additionally, the subject addresses the need for flexibility, teamwork, customisation, and problem-solving in response to social, economic, and political changes, particularly in educational organisations. It emphasises understanding change management theories and the applied sciences in order to apply them to real-world experiences and practices. Case studies and practical strategies will be used to develop management skills and enable stakeholders to effectively handle organisational changes.
learning_outcomes: Apply management theories and the applied sciences to analyse specific organisational problems in education and develop practical and evidence-based approaches for problem resolution.
Critically evaluate organisational stakeholders to support and manage change and strategic alliances.
Critically analyse the process of organisational change and educational partnerships from broad social and economic perspectives.
Critically analyse strategic effective education partnerships that include setting goals, communication, mutual benefits.
Initiate and apply management theories, the applied sciences and practices that foster flexible and adaptive education organisations and operational systems.

title: EARLY CHILDHOOD ASSESSMENT AND REPORTING
syllabus_overview: This subject investigates the authentic use of assessment in early childhood education. Preservice teachers examine the way that assessment is used to inform their understanding of the child, to identify intent behind supports needed, pedagogy, curriculum and making children’s learning and development visible. The purpose of assessment is critiqued and considered in connection to culture, the view of the child, curriculum practices and inclusion. Collaboration with families and colleagues are positioned as integral in developing rich authentic assessment practices and in showcasing assessment leadership. This subject contains 20 days of placement.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate leadership in assessment practice by aligning assessment philosophy, curriculum, and pedagogy in professional contexts.
Document, interpret, plan, and reflect on children’s learning by observing and analysing their emergent interests, development, and capabilities across relevant domains.
Apply assessment-aligned curriculum decisions to support children’s learning, and demonstrate leadership in equitable and aspirational teaching.
Select and justify the use of authentic, everyday assessment practices and tools aligned with early childhood curriculum frameworks.
Outline and justify a relevant, reliable, and research-informed pedagogical philosophy for understanding children’s learning and development that includes varied tools and strategies.

Critically evaluate and apply the purposes and implications of assessment in early childhood education focussed on collaboration with First Nations peoples, families, colleagues, and inclusion professionals.

title: THE ARTS AND PLAY
syllabus_overview: Preservice teachers (PSTs) will explore how young children learn in and through the arts. They will become familiar with pedagogies and practices across the visual arts, 3-dimensional arts, music, creative movement/dance, and drama. PSTs will engage in and critically reflect upon their own creative processes, with reference to arts-based theories, practices, and research. They will create an informed teaching resource that connects their learning in this subject with their work-based experience.
learning_outcomes: Describe and justify impactful arts-based pedagogies with reference to relevant literature
Design, implement and critically reflect on teaching support for engaging and educational arts experiences for young children.
Critically analyse and apply arts education pedagogies and practices to support Early Childhood Education.
Design, implement, and critically reflect on arts-based learning experiences that align with early childhood curriculum and children’s developmental needs.

title: EARLY CHILDHOOD LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: In this subject, pre-service teachers will examine the significance and complexities of early childhood leadership. Connections will be made with professional practice, ethical practice and leadership aspirations. Issues that shape early childhood leadership, such as policy, legal requirements, political influences, professional ethics, and operational management, are explored and implications for leadership practice are addressed. Additionally, pre-service teachers will engage in leadership research, developing a small-scale research project focused on transforming practice through leadership. The insights from the research project will be used to inform future leadership growth and development.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and communicate research findings to diverse audiences to support leadership development and professional discourse
Design and conduct teacher research in connection with an aspect of early childhood leadership.
Critically evaluate the significance and complexities of leadership in early childhood contexts.
Apply and justify leadership decisions in early childhood practice using relevant policy, legislation, ethical frameworks, operational principles, and research.
Develop future leadership aspirations based on the research process including implications for future practice.

title: MATHEMATICS, NUMERACY AND PLAY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, preservice teachers will explore pedagogies important to facilitating numeracy understandings in early childhood education. As part of this exploration the interconnection of mathematics and numeracy will be deconstructed, particularly the way that numbers, patterns, measurement, time, spatial awareness, chance, data, and mathematical thinking can be supported within play-based learning. Preservice teachers will think critically about the intentionality in observing, facilitating, planning for and assessing mathematics and numeracy learning and development. Drawing from contemporary approaches to supporting numeracy and mathematical development and in consultation with Australian curriculum frameworks preservice teachers will develop trialed resources to support practice. This subject includes 25 days of placement.
learning_outcomes: Design and evaluate intentional provocations that respond to children’s interests and support mathematical learning through interdisciplinary approaches, including ICT, the arts, nature play, and literacy.
Analyse and explain numeracy and mathematics learning processes in young children, drawing on relevant research and theoretical perspectives.
Critically analyse pedagogical and assessment strategies that support numeracy and mathematical learning in early childhood.
Research and design innovative numeracy and mathematics learning experiences and intentional teaching strategies aligned with relevant curriculum documents and play-based pedagogies.
Evaluate mathematics learning and teaching resources that support play-based learning in early childhood contexts.

title: AUTISM SPECTRUM AND ENGAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the complex and unique cluster of attributes that a student with an Autism Spectrum Disorder may have and analyse how that may impinge on learning. You will explore relevant and inclusive teaching strategies as you relate to communication, social skills, behaviour and sensory integration for students with autism. You will focus on the implications that learning differences will have for the student and how teachers and schools can be more responsive to the student's educational needs.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise the knowledge, skills and attitudes in a professional portfolio of research, resources and teaching strategies appropriate for students with autism.
Demonstrate how the complex nature of the attributes of a student with autism spectrum disorder may influence the way a student learns.
Identify and analyse learning difficulties and teaching strategies associated with communication, social skills, behaviour and sensory integration for students with autism
Evaluate research and resources in the field of autism and apply these to learning contexts
Critically analyse the contentions involved in Inclusive education for students with autism and their parents/carers/teachers

title: GENDER AND EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an advanced theoretical understanding of gender, sexuality, society and education through engagement with current academic research and scholarship. You will critically analyse the relationships between gender, sexuality and society, and how these relate to various educational contexts through examination of contemporary case studies. You will research evidence-based ethical and inclusive approaches to gender and sexuality and develop strategies for use in education practice and educational contexts. As such, this subject will be of particular interest to educators and those in positions of education leadership, or students with a background in humanities and/or social sciences.
learning_outcomes: Develop evidence-based ethical and inclusive approaches to gender and sexuality for use in teaching practice and educational contexts
Critically analyse the relationships between gender, sexuality, society and education and how these are formed
Demonstrate advanced theoretical understanding of gender, sexuality, society and education

title: LEADERSHIP, DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to some of the major issues that dominate today's thinking about organisational leadership. It provides you an opportunity to explore and critique the need for leaders in education and other organisations to implement suitable leadership strategies and approaches that will effectively respond to the diverse management and leadership needs of today's complex and culturally diverse organisations. Participants examine the context of the changing demographics of today's organisation and the eminence of globalisation, along with the need for paradigmatic-shift in conventional leadership mindsets and practices towards diversity and inclusion. Relevant theories of diversity and inclusion are investigated including: theory of equity and attribution, as they relate to ethnicity, race, religion, gender, sexuality and age. You will demonstrate a fact-based understanding of existing case studies and models of best leadership practices, and a critical awareness of relevant factors influencing leadership effectiveness.
learning_outcomes: Identify key issues affecting diversity and inclusion in contemporary workforce with particular reference to education.

Identify contemporary leadership capabilities that contribute to effective diversity and inclusive practices in education and develop a personal critical perspective on models of best leadership practices.
Critically examine how prevailing leadership practices respond to local contexts of diversity and inclusion in Australia and in various international contexts.
Critically examine the terms diversity and inclusion, equity and attribution and related theories.

title: INDUSTRY BASED PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject you are expected to plan and conduct a research-based project to investigate a specific issue in a professional education context. The project should demonstrate the your ability to conduct a systematic investigation which draws on relevant literature and an appropriate educational research methodology.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and transmit knowledge and ideas to practitioners in education contexts
Critically analyse educational practices by reflecting on and synthesising complex information, problems, concepts and theories
Research and apply education theory, concepts and models in order to investigate practice-based issues in professional educational contexts

title: SCHOOLS AND WELL-BEING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore issues related to well-being and school responsiveness. You will examine the topics of trauma, anxiety, depression and bullying to understand how complex personal and socio-cultural issues can impinge on wellness and learning. You will apply principles from various health promotion frameworks to whole school approaches and classroom strategies to promote learning. You will examine how schools and individual teachers can take a proactive stance to improve well-being.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the causes and prevalence of wellness issues for students in schools and assess how they may influence learning
Evaluate school policies, resources and processes to address the well-being needs of the students and to inform and propose future actions to improve school responsiveness
Explain and justify whole school approaches to mental health and well-being and model the role that critical reflection may have in classroom management

Examine the principles that underpin relational agency in schools and classrooms and determine how those principles may inform pedagogy and learning for student who have experienced well-being issues.
Analyse the influences that various challenges such as trauma, anxiety, depression and bullying may have on learning

title: TRAUMA THEORY AND PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the impact of early childhood trauma on learning. The transdisciplinary approach draws from multiple perspectives and includes current research, pedagogies and practices informing the provision of trauma informed education.
learning_outcomes: Draw on current theoretical knowledge of early traumatic experience to reflect critically on the implications for student learning and professional practice
Apply indigenous perspectives and understandings of the impact of generational trauma, to the education of students from traumatic backgrounds
Develop research skills to justify and interpret theoretical perspectives and current research in trauma informed education.
Examine the principles that underpin trauma informed education and determine how those principles may inform pedagogy and learning for students who have experienced trauma.

title: ANIMAL REPRODUCTION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a comprehensive program on basic and applied aspects of animal reproduction, with particular emphasis on livestock, domestic animals and wildlife. Fundamental topics include: the structure and function of male and female reproductive systems, endocrine, neuroendocrine and environmental control of reproduction, development of gametes, embryos, pregnancy and parturition. An understanding of assisted reproductive technologies, impact of environmental endocrine disruptors and fertility control of wildlife and pest species will be developed through lectures, workshops, online modules and assignments. In addition, practical training in skills associated with reproductive assessment and management is provided (i.e. artificial insemination, pregnancy detection, sperm analysis).
learning_outcomes: Relate the structure of the different parts of the reproductive system to their role in reproduction, gestation, parturition and lactation.
Develop a better understanding of career options and trajectories in the reproductive field by working in teams to collaborate on interviewing experts in the field.
Explain concepts of animal reproduction using key terms correctly.

Apply knowledge of the role of hormones in the control of reproduction and lactation to explain assisted reproductive technologies and/or fertility control in production animals, wildlife conservation and fertility control in pest species.
Critically review scientific literature to present written and oral overviews of reproductive topics.

title: ANIMAL BEHAVIOUR
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject in animal behaviour brings together foundational knowledge from earlier years to solve real-world challenges through applied behavioural biology. In this subject you will examine the diversity that we see in animal behaviour within a framework that incorporates animal ecology and evolution. You will focus on functional explanations of behaviour, namely how behaviour contributes to survival and/or reproductive success, and address some of the underlying mechanisms that contribute to this diversity. Topics include social behaviour, finding prey and avoiding predators, and animal communication strategies. You will learn about common methods and techniques used to study behaviour, and design and conduct your own investigation.
learning_outcomes: Communicate scientific ideas and research outcomes effectively to diverse audiences using appropriate formats.
Critically evaluate and apply behavioural research methods to investigate ecological and evolutionary questions.
Integrate knowledge of animal ecology, evolution, and behavioural biology to explain the diversity and function of animal behaviours.
Design and conduct an independent investigation into animal behaviour, interpreting findings in the context of survival and reproductive success.

title: HONOURS IN ENVIRONMENT AND GENETICS A
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Honours in Environment and Genetics consists of a one year (full-time) or two years (part-time) individual research project, supervised by a SABE scientist whose research is in the disciplines of ecology, environment and/or genetics. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. EEE401A is the first subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take EEE401A first.
learning_outcomes: Understand published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Show intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice
Recall knowledge in ecology, environment and/or genetics when conducting experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Obtain practical experience and advanced knowledge in the fields of ecology, environment and/or genetics.
Extend oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT B
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and have fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree with a major in a relevant discipline. The Bachelor of Science (Honours) program provides undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and/or theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program imparts undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Under supervision of a La Trobe University academic, you will formulate a research question, conduct a research study, and write a research thesis of 12,000 to 15,000 words in which you demonstrate the capacity to make an original contribution to your discipline. EEE401B is the second subject in a four-part sequence where students conduct a research project in an agriculture and environment discipline and write a thesis. While EEE401B and AGR401C may be completed in either order, AGR401A must be completed first, and EEE401D must be completed last.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate developing intellectual initiative and apply informed judgement in conducting scholarly tasks with ethical and academic integrity, with moderate guidance.
Interpret and compare scientific information from multiple sources in an agriculture and environment discipline to support research and analysis.
Analyse discipline-specific literature to refine approaches to research questions, with guidance.
Communicate scientific ideas orally and in writing using appropriate disciplinary conventions, with some independence.
Design ethical approaches to investigate problems and test possible solutions relevant to an agriculture and environment discipline, with guidance.

title: HONOURS IN ENVIRONMENT AND GENETICS C
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Honours in Environment and Genetics consists of a one year (full-time) or two years (part-time) individual research project, supervised by a SABE scientist whose research is in the disciplines of ecology, environment and/or genetics. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. EEE401C is the second or third subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take EEE401A first.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Develop advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Demonstrate knowledge in ecology, environment and/or genetics research when devising experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Develop intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice
Refine practical experience and advanced knowledge in the fields of ecology, environment and/or genetics.

title: HONOURS IN AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT D
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and have fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree with a major in a relevant discipline. The Bachelor of Science (Honours) program provides undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and/or theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program imparts undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Under supervision of a La Trobe University academic, you will formulate a research question, conduct a research study, and write a research thesis of 12,000 to 15,000 words in which you demonstrate the capacity to make an original contribution to your discipline. EEE401D is the final subject of a sequence of four subjects in which students undertake a research project in an agriculture and environment discipline and write a thesis. You must complete EEE401D last.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate, interpret and synthesise scientific information in an agriculture and environment discipline to support reasoned arguments.
Demonstrate independent and reflective learning and scholarly practice with ethical and academic integrity.
Apply advanced knowledge and technical skills in an agriculture and environment discipline to address research questions.
Justify approaches used to investigate problems by drawing on advanced knowledge and evidence in an agriculture and environment discipline.
Communicate complex scientific ideas orally and in writing to scientific audiences, demonstrating knowledge of scholarly conventions in an agriculture and environment discipline.

title: HONOURS IN ECOLOGY, ENVIRONMENT AND EVOLUTION X
syllabus_overview: This subject code caters to Honours students who wish to complete their 4th year honours program part-time, over 18 months. In all other respects this subject is equivalent to EEE4HNA and EEE4HNB and you may commence in either February or July. This fourth year course is available to students who have fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelor degree with a major in a relevant discipline, provided their previous academic record is of a sufficient standard. The course consists of a supervised research project, together with other prescribed work including essays, workshops and seminars. You should consult with potential supervisors during your final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice.
Analyse using a systematic approach to reasoning and conceptualising scientific ideas to solve real work scientific and technical problems consistent with faculty standards.

Develop rational and rigorous arguments to interrogate assumptions, synthesise scientific information, formulate hypotheses, draw unbiased conclusions and defend scientific ideas consistent with faculty standards.
Employ academic integrity and scientific rigour in conducting and evaluating scientific research, and managing self in professional practice consistent with faculty standards.

Demonstrate writing ability at a level that is consistent for the task and faculty standards, and that uses correct grammar and terminology to summarise and communicate coherent exposition of knowledge and ideas to a variety of audiences, such as peers and scientific community.

Perform statistical analysis, consolidation and synthesis of data collected from scientific experiments, as well as interpretation of scientific data, scientific reports and journal to make evidence based conclusions consistent with faculty/discipline standards
Develop coherent and advanced knowledge of the underlying principles and concepts consistent with faculty/discipline standards.

Conduct clearly spoken presentations that are consistent with faculty/discipline standards and use correct terminology to summarise and communicate coherent exposition of knowledge and ideas to a variety of audiences, such as peers and scientific community.
