Building upon the foundations learnt in STM1001 Making Sense of Data, or BIO2POS Practice of Science the subject covers the principles of statistical design for surveys, experiments, and observational studies; some new methods for analysing data, including analysis of variance (ANOVA), multiple regression, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and some nonparametric methods that are particularly suited to analysing multispecies ecological data; and how to critically evaluate the statistical arguments made in scientific reports and journal articles. Laboratory sessions and assignments will give students the opportunity to apply what they learn using statistics packages.
learning_outcomes: Perform data analyses and generate figures using contemporary statistical software.
Evaluate statistics reported in the media and scientific journal articles.
Communicate statistical analyses in report form.
Design sample surveys, experiments and observational studies in life sciences.
Choose appropriate analyses for given research questions and data sets.

title: WOMEN THROUGH HISTORY IN EUROPE AND LATIN AMERICA
syllabus_overview: Long before the Feminist movement took shape, there existed women who fought for women's rights and advocated for women's participation in public life. This subject explores case studies centred on the analysis of works (literary, philosophical, and filmic texts, as well as artworks) by key women from Europe and Latin America. You will learn about and discuss female icons, women writers, scholars, and artists from ancient to contemporary times , who contributed to reshape the socio-cultural norms of their societies by breaking out of the roles traditionally ascribed to their gender. Through this subject, you will gain a deeper understanding of the history of European and Latin American societies thereby developing the instruments to analyse and critique topical movements and social issues of our contemporary global societies. You will be made aware that single and apparently dispersed instances of resistance to a social status quo, when read as part of a larger context, can become the key in identifying and understanding an enduring call to build momentum towards social and cultural change. All classes are conducted in English.
learning_outcomes: Demostrate knowledge of a variety of historical contexts examined through European and Latin American written and visual texts, including creative literary works and scholarly material.
Understand, analyse, and interpret the different forms that socio-cultural change has taken in different historical periods, countries, and across various disciplinary fields.
Communicate effectively in written and oral formats, demonstrating understanding of differences across cultures, and collaboratively engage in group activities to enhance teamwork skills.
Critically analyse historical and literary texts clearly and effectively in academic English; reporting and summarizing debates, and making cogent and considered arguments.

title: MEMORY AND IDENTITY IN WORLD CINEMA
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will critically examine the interrelated themes of memory and identity through the lens of world cinema, with films in Spanish, Italian, Greek, French, and English. Through the subject’s emphasis on multilingual and transcultural narratives, you will engage with cinematic representations of individuals and communities navigating cultural dislocation, linguistic plurality, and the complexities of belonging. Rather than approaching each linguistic tradition in isolation, the selected films foreground intersections between languages and cultures, enabling a sustained inquiry into the legacies of colonisation, the dynamics of mobility, and the negotiation of identity across borders. Through close analysis of filmic form and content, you will develop an understanding of cinema as a site where memory and identity are constructed, contested, and reimagined.
learning_outcomes: Analyse cinematic texts from diverse linguistic and cultural contexts to identify and interpret how memory and identity are represented and negotiated through film

Construct evidence-based arguments that demonstrate an understanding of cinema as a medium through which memory and identity are constructed, contested, and reimagined across geopolitical and linguistic boundaries
Reflect on how languages, cultures, and histories shape individual and collective identities on screen
Critically evaluate the ways in which multilingual and transcultural cinematic narratives engage with themes of cultural dislocation, identity, colonisation, and mobility

title: GEOPOLITICS OF LANGUAGES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the common origin and the shared history of European languages with a focus on French, Greek, Italian, and Spanish. You will reflect on how linguistic evolution intersects with political, social, cultural, and economic forces, and investigate the role of colonisation, migration, and globalisation in shaping linguistic landscapes, and the impact of language policy and power dynamics on identity and communication. In our digital age and with the rise of artificial intelligence, you will question how technologies like machine translation, large language models, and automated communication tools are reshaping linguistic hierarchies, language documentation, and global power dynamics. Case studies from different regions will be used to highlight the complex interplay between language, technology, and geopolitics across time.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the historical development and shared origins of major European languages—particularly French, Greek, Italian, and Spanish—and understand the socio-political, cultural, and economic forces that have shaped their evolution
Critique the implications of digital technologies—such as machine translation, large language models, and AI communication tools—on linguistic hierarchies and global language politics

Apply interdisciplinary approaches to analyse case studies that demonstrate the dynamic interplay between language, technology, and geopolitics, and construct evidence-based arguments on current and emerging language-related issues

Critically assess the role of colonisation, migration, and globalisation in shaping linguistic landscapes, with attention to the intersections of language, identity, and power in diverse geopolitical contexts and across time

title: TRANS EUROPEAN TRANSLATION
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to promote linguistic, cultural and translation skills, as well as skills of textual analysis and the capacity for self-reflection. You will have the opportunity to translate literary texts, informative texts, advertising, audiovisual materials and public health texts, among others. The subject is offered in bilingual mode with key topics in translation theory provided in English, accompanied by face-to-face workshops conducted in the target language (French, Greek, Italian and Spanish streams are typically offered). The subject is aimed at students with strong language skills, who have completed five semesters of language study at university and who desire an in-depth knowledge of the language and culture of the focus country or countries. While it is not a professional qualification, it offers a pathway towards professional translation and/or interpreter training.
learning_outcomes: Write fluently and correctly, with appropriate stylistic nuances, including when translating a range of source text types
Identify and articulate linguistic and cultural differences between the two languages under examination, and demonstrate well-developed research, negotiation, decision-making and translation skills
Articulate and justify an interpretation of a text and the translation strategies selected
Identify, analyse and appraise audiences, text types, cultural differences, and stylistic effects

title: ADVANCED EXERCISE BIOMECHANICS
syllabus_overview: This subject will advance your theoretical and practical understanding of exercise and sports biomechanics. In this subject you will explore the relationship between biomechanical principles of human movement that underpin common activities of daily living to observe, describe, measure and analyse gross body movements relevant to performance in sport and exercise. This subject will examine the biomechanics of human walking and running gait and the changes which occur with development and ageing. This subject will introduce you to principles of tissue mechanics and will explore the contribution of biomechanics to the field of sports injury prevention.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the biomechanical properties of human tissue and analyse adaptations to loading, over and under use, aging and pathological function.
Evaluate injury occurrence and predisposing factors across sport and exercise performance including assessment of injury mechanisms.
Analyse and evaluate (individually and in groups) biomechanical data in order to solve quantitative problems involving linear and angular kinematic and kinetic quantities.
Critically assess appropriate measurement methods and perform and report biomechanical measurements involving temporal- spatial, kinematic and kinetic quantities.

Evaluate the stages of development and patterns of muscular activity for normal gait, and identify biomechanical parameters that are commonly assessed in clinical gait analysis, including aging and pathological function.

title: APPLIED EXERCISE PROGRAMMING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop knowledge and skills in exercise assessment, prescription and delivery to apparently healthy individuals. You will evaluate the implementation of various exercise modalities and will apply skills in pre-exercise assessments, health and exercise testing and exercise program design and delivery.
learning_outcomes: Apply strategies to teach and correct exercise technique.
Evaluate evidence to inform exercise programming and adapt client-centred exercise programs in consideration of the evidence-base.
Apply exercise testing, prescription and delivery skills within the individual's scope of practice and code of conduct.
Interpret pre-exercise health screening and exercise assessments to inform exercise prescription.

title: ADVANCED EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will investigate the influence of individual variation, environmental stress, nutritional supplementation and ergogenic aids on exercise training, performance and recovery. You will evaluate normal and abnormal, acute and chronic responses to exercise, with reference to individual determinants of the participant and environmental stress. In addition, you will evaluate nutritional interventions and ergogenic aids to enhance physiological adaptation, exercise capacity and performance.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the emerging influence of gene expression on exercise science.
Evaluate the physiological principles and biochemical pathways related to energy metabolism, muscle fatigue and soreness.
Critically evaluate the use of nutritional interventions and ergogenic aids with reference to safety, physiological adaptations to training and exercise performance.
Analyse the specific physiological adaptations to a variety of exercise training modalities.
Assess acute and chronic physiological responses to exercise to determine normal and abnormal patterns of responses.
Evaluate the effects of environmental stress on exercise performance and adaptations to exercise training.
Apply appropriate measurement techniques in exercise physiology to evaluate a research question.

title: EXERCISE PROGRAMMING AND PRESCRIPTION FOR PEOPLE WITH SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply skills in exercise testing prescription and delivery to client-centred exercise interventions; as well as, enhance skills in exercise service delivery to apparently healthy populations with special considerations including pregnancy, children and adolescents, older adults, lower back pain, overweight and mental illness.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse participants technique during exercise to interpret dysfunctional movement patterns and apply corrective strategies.
Adapt the delivery of exercise programs after individual evaluation of needs, capacity and stage of the lifespan.
Apply and evaluate knowledge and skills in accordance with the professional scope of practice and in line with the charter and spirit of the code of professional conduct in a work context.
Analyse the physiological changes across the lifespan and the effects of exercise, including contraindications, during particular stages of growth and development.
Analyse the purpose, limitations, contraindications or considerations that may require the modification to exercise assessments and exercise programming.

title: EXERCISE SCIENCE PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will undertake projects in exercise science. You will develop fundamental research skills and apply discipline knowledge and techniques to address questions in exercise science. Individually, or as part of a small group, you will work on projects that will include planning, project management, data collection, data analysis, critical interpretation and dissemination; whilst also considering cultural, linguistic and disability issues in relation to exercise prescription. You will also apply and evaluate knowledge and skills in accordance with the professional scope of practice and in line with the charter and spirit of the code of professional conduct in a work context.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate methods to adapt exercise prescription and delivery to clients from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, and clients with disability.
Collate, analyse and synthesise data using appropriate methods and report findings to different audiences.
Conduct independent scholarly work within the discipline of exercise science.
Critically assess literature to address an exercise science question that informs exercise assessment, prescription and delivery to clients.

title: PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND HEALTH ACROSS THE LIFESPAN
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will evaluate the influence of sedentary behaviour and physical activity behaviours on chronic diseases. You will use key determinants of health to identify people at risk of insufficient physical activity and sedentary behaviour. With reference to current research, you will appraise a range of physical activity guidelines as they relate to people across the lifespan. You will develop an understanding of how individual and population health can be influenced by the health care system and public policy, and settings in which practitioners can work to assist communities to address physical activity needs. You will design a basic population intervention, based on best practice, to increase physical activity and reduce sedentary behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Explore and critique the impact of public policy, individual and population-level interventions on promoting physical activity and reducing sedentary behaviour.
Critique evidence to explain the role of sedentary behaviour and lack of physical activity on lifestyle-related chronic disease.
Critically assess ways in which the health care system influences physical activity and sedentary behaviour at a national level.
Interpret population data and research to evaluate factors that contribute to sedentary behaviour and insufficient physical activity.
Evaluate the influence of individual differences on physical activity guidelines for people across the lifespan.

title: SKILL ACQUISITION
syllabus_overview: Success in exercise and sport depends on your ability to develop a specific set of perceptual, cognitive and motor skills. This subject will expand your theoretical and practical understanding of motor performance and skill learning. In this subject you will explore the principles and apply the concepts of skill acquisition to a variety of real-world settings such as coaching, rehabilitation and everyday motor skill learning. In particular, this subject considers the role that different types of learning, practice, instruction and feedback have on the skill acquisition process. Throughout this subject, the implications of current research that has shaped our understanding of motor skill learning will be reviewed, in particular, evaluating the major characteristics of change that occur in human performance during the skill acquisition process.
learning_outcomes: Explore the role of the brain and nervous system in movement control and perceptual, cognitive and motor skill learning.

Critically assess different methods for facilitating, structuring and supplementing the learning experience, evaluating the impact on learning and to describe the major characteristics of change that occur with skill learning.

Construct, perform and evaluate appropriate feedback and measurement methods to perform and report motor skill learning and demonstrate an ability to design training or practice sessions to maximise skill learning.
Critically evaluate the sensory contribution to skilled performance, motor control and movement accuracy and identify models of motor programming for movement production.

Compare and contrast individual differences with respect to learning motor abilities and demonstrate an ability to identify the perceptual, decision-making and motor responses required for a range of motor activities.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICE FOR EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will advance your knowledge of movement and functional capacity. You will integrate your skills in analysing movement and functional capacity and posture to inform therapeutic exercise aiming to restore and optimise musculoskeletal and neurological function.
learning_outcomes: Apply and critically evaluate assessments to analyse body and movement mechanics, posture and functional capacity appropriate for use by Accredited Exercise Physiologists.
Critically evaluate literature investigating the components of exercise prescriptions to inform therapeutic exercise treatment plans.
Expertly interpret and communicate the outcomes of functional capacity evaluations and explain the potential contributions to treatment from various healthcare practitioners.

title: ASSESSMENT AND EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION FOR CARDIORESPIRATORY AND METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will utilise online platforms along with face-to-face theoretical and practical sessions to analyse the pathophysiology of cardiovascular, pulmonary and metabolic conditions. Pathophysiological knowledge will be applied to perform appropriate clinical assessments and examinations of individuals, critically interpret outcomes, and design, prescribe, deliver, and monitor safe and effective clinical exercise interventions. Exercise interventions will be prescribed with knowledge and appreciation of expected clinical responses, supervised to ensure safety and monitored for adverse responses.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate, critique, and interpret assessments of cardiorespiratory and metabolic dysfunction including physical capacity with consideration of typically prescribed pharmaceutical medications.
Critically analyse expected and adverse cardiorespiratory and metabolic outcomes from, and responses to, different types of exercise.
Analyse and synthesise cardiovascular, pulmonary and metabolic pathophysiology as they relate to the Accredited Exercise Physiologist scope of practice.

Reflect on clinical measures and consider outcomes to design, prescribe, deliver, and monitor safe and effective clinical exercise interventions for individuals with cardiorespiratory and metabolic dysfunction.
Critique and interpret cardiorespiratory and metabolic testing results.

title: MENTAL HEALTH AND BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IN EXERCISE THERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide students with opportunities to explore and understand mental health pathologies and recognise factors that contribute to mental health conditions. Students will consider and implement the guidelines around diagnosing and managing mental health conditions from the context of an exercise physiologist and implement exercise-based therapies. The use of pharmaceutical medications and interactions with exercise will be considered, and the common physiological pathways that exercise and pharmaceuticals activate will be explored. The implementation of behaviour change frameworks will be critiqued and practiced to enhance compliance with prescribed therapies.
learning_outcomes: Appraise presenting health symptoms for determining pathophysiology of mental health and guiding the health assessment
Evaluate guidelines relating to diagnosing and managing mental health conditions in the context of providing exercise therapy
Collaborate with health care providers and consumers to deliver patient-centred evidence-informed care for mental health conditions
Critique behaviour change frameworks to inform clinical practice that facilitates behaviour change and therapy compliance in people with mental health conditions

title: ASSESSMENT AND EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will utilise online platforms along with face-to-face theoretical and practical sessions to analyse the pathophysiology of sub-acute and chronic muscular and skeletal conditions. Pathophysiological knowledge will be applied to perform appropriate assessments and examinations of individuals, before interpreting and utilising this information to design and prescribe effective clinical exercise interventions. Exercise interventions will be prescribed with knowledge and appreciation of expected physiological responses, supervised to ensure safety and monitored for adverse responses.
learning_outcomes: Critique and interpret musculoskeletal testing results.
Evaluate and interpret assessments of musculoskeletal dysfunction with consideration of typically prescribed pharmaceutical medications.
Analyse and synthesise the pathophysiology of various musculoskeletal conditions as they relate to the Accredited Exercise Physiologist scope of practice.
Design clinical exercise interventions for individuals with musculoskeletal conditions.
Critically analyse expected and adverse musculoskeletal outcomes from different types of exercise.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE FOR EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore concepts relating to professional practice as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist (AEP). These concepts will revolve around effective communication with patients, accessing clinical information, conducting appropriate assessments and effective documentation and clinical reporting. You will also analyse different clinical frameworks and compensatory schemes to implement reasoned case management with high professional and ethical standards.
learning_outcomes: Obtain and evaluate clinical data and provide appropriate clinical reasoning for proposed clinical exercise interventions for individuals with pathology consistent with those listed in the Accredited Exercise Physiologists Scope of Practice.
Critically interpret and stratify risk factors, indicators and contra-indicators, and manage emergency situations
Evaluate various clinical frameworks and compensation schemes that are used to guide clinical practice.
Critique strategies (verbal and non-verbal) for communicating with patients, medical and allied health professionals.

title: ASSESSMENT AND EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION FOR NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will utilise online platforms along with face-to-face theoretical and practical sessions to analyse the pathophysiology of neurological, immunological and anxiety conditions. This will include the study of the inflammatory and immunological processes and analysing the role of inflammation on the immune system and its consequential health outcomes. Pathophysiology knowledge will be applied to perform appropriate assessments and examinations of individuals, before interpreting and utilising this information to design and prescribe effective clinical exercise interventions. Exercise interventions will be prescribed with knowledge and appreciation of expected physiological responses, supervised to ensure safety and monitored for adverse responses.
learning_outcomes: Design clinical exercise interventions for individuals with neurological, immunological and anxiety dysfunction.
Critique and interpret neurological, immunological and anxiety testing results.
Analyse and synthesise neurological, immunological and anxiety pathophysiologies as they relate to the Accredited Exercise Physiologist scope of practice.
Evaluate and interpret assessments of neurological, immunological and anxiety dysfunction with consideration of typically prescribed pharmaceutical medications.
Critically analyse expected and adverse neurological, immunological and anxiety outcomes from different types of exercise.

title: EVIDENCE-BASED CLINICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the evidence base for clinical practice to treat and manage people with a range of pathologies across a series of complex case scenarios. Using available clinical frameworks and individual scopes of practice, you will evaluate published literature to design therapeutic treatment plans that include all appropriate medical and allied health disciplines. You are required to interpret clinical outcomes from complex case scenarios (including those with chronic disease and mental illness) and plan treatment that includes behaviour change techniques.
learning_outcomes: Create evidence-based, person-centred health and wellness interventions, using relevant clinical frameworks, which consider psychological outlook and current behaviours.
Critically evaluate barriers to active participation in clinical treatment along with the role of different health professionals in managing people with a range of clinical conditions.
Differentiate clinical pathologies, interpret clinical data and design appropriate therapeutic interventions and clinically reasoned treatment plans.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete professional practicum within an approved health organisation. These hours will contribute to the requirements for registration as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist with Exercise and Sports Science Australia. Your professional skills, including communication skills, assessment and clinical exercise prescription skills will be developed under direct supervision from appropriately qualified and experienced clinicians working in a range of healthcare settings. You will develop your ability to be a reflective practitioner through learning activities completed while undertaking your practicum. Students will complete a pre-clinical program prior to commencing practicum.
learning_outcomes: Implement a range of strategies for communicating with patients, medical and allied health professionals.
Investigate and apply skills in exercise assessment to inform management strategies in clinical populations.
Apply clinical exercise physiology principles that demonstrate adaptability and responsibility.
Apply advanced theoretical knowledge of, and skills in, exercise-based interventions to implement effective healthcare delivery in clinical populations.
Critically reflect upon theory, contemporary research and supervision feedback to improve professional practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete professional placement within an approved health organisation. These hours will contribute to the requirements for registration as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist with Exercise and Sports Science Australia. You will need to prove your professional skills, including communication and patient assessment. You will expand your clinical exercise prescription skills, under direct supervision from appropriately qualified and experienced clinicians working in a range of healthcare settings. You need to demonstrate your ability to be a reflective practitioner through the completion of specific learning activities during your professional placement. You will further develop your critical analysis and communication skills through oral case presentations.
learning_outcomes: Plan and complete appropriate exercise assessments to inform management strategies in clinical populations.
Apply clinical judgement and self-responsibility in a healthcare setting, different to the previous placement.
Critically reflect upon theory and contemporary research to identify areas of professional practice for development.
Justify the implementation of effective exercise-based interventions for clinical populations based on specialised theoretical knowledge.
Select and apply appropriate strategies for communicating with patients, medical and allied health professionals, in clinical settings

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete 140 hours of professional placement within an approved health organisation. These hours will contribute to the requirements for registration as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist with Exercise and Sports Science Australia. You will need to prove your professional skills, including communication and patient assessment. You will demonstrate your independent clinical exercise prescription skills under minimal supervision from appropriately qualified and experienced clinicians working in a range of healthcare settings. In this subject you will refine and finalize your skills and knowledge necessary for competent practice. This subject will prepare you for graduate practice; you will create your professional portfolio and prepare a cover letter for a job application. A practical competency exam (simulated patient exam) is an important part of this subject.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced skills in exercise assessment to inform management strategies in diverse clinical populations..
Use evidence based practice to justify the implementation of effective exercise-based interventions for diverse clinical populations based on specialised theoretical knowledge.
Adapt strategies for communicating with patients, medical and allied health professionals across different healthcare settings.
Critical reflect upon theory, contemporary research, and professional practice to identify areas of professional practice for development
Apply advanced knowledge and skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility across diverse health care settings and clinical populations.

title: RESEARCH STUDY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop professional practice as an allied health professional by using research to inform clinical reasoning. This subject aims to develop your research skills and apply discipline-specific knowledge and techniques to address a clinically relevant question. Both individually and as part of a small group, you will work on a research project that will include: planning, project management, data collection/cleaning, data analysis, critical interpretation/evaluation and dissemination of findings. These are essential skills to support evidence-based clinical practice. You will be expected to work independently in self-directed learning.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine, analyse and interpret data using appropriate quantitative and/or qualitative methods to inform clinical reasoning and implications for practice.
Disseminate and defend findings, actions and recommendations using oral and written formats.
Synthesise and critique relevant literature to inform clinical practice or areas for further research.
Conduct independent and collaborative scholarly work to review and evaluate the efficacy and effectiveness of clinical interventions to health and healthcare.

title: INTRODUCTION TO FINANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an introduction to the principles and practices of corporate finance, focusing on how financial managers create value through investment and financing decisions. Key topics include the scope of corporate finance, financial statement and cash flow analysis, the time value of money, the valuation of bonds, shares, and options, and the trade-off between risk and return. You will examine the application of portfolio theory, the capital asset pricing model (CAPM), and market efficiency theory in explaining the behaviour of capital markets. Capital budgeting techniques are introduced to evaluate long-term investment decisions under conditions of risk and uncertainty. Through applied analysis and problem-solving, you will develop the ability to interpret financial information, value securities, assess risk and return, and apply decision-making frameworks to real-world business finance scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate business and investment risk and return applying portfolio theory and the capital asset pricing model (CAPM), including the application of market efficiency theory to explain the behaviour of capital markets.

Apply capital budgeting techniques and decision criteria to evaluate investment projects, incorporating cash flow estimation, risk assessment, and sensitivity analysis to support sound business finance decisions.

Identify the various sources of financing available to businesses and apply appropriate theoretical and quantitative considerations in determining the most suitable financing source given business circumstances.

Explain the scope and role of corporate finance, and apply fundamental concepts—including financial statement analysis, the time value of money, security valuation, and dividend policy—to understand the financial environment and support informed business decision-making.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF FINANCE
syllabus_overview: Finance defines the process by which individuals and businesses raise and manage funds. Financial skills are a prerequisite for success not only if you are seeking a career in banking and finance, but equally for success in any business career. Indeed, financial literacy is a skill required to successfully manage your personal financial well-being. In this subject, through lessons in our financial trading room and industry-related content, you will examine the nature of the financial environment and the types of financial decision-making required to succeed, both from a business and an individual perspective. You will develop an understanding of the concept of the time value of money, methods of valuing various financial assets such as shares and bonds, and methods of project evaluation. You will consider the trade-off between risk and return in relation to investment assets, and its importance in understanding portfolio theory, and the cost of capital for a business. Finally, you will be able to define a study plan and potential financial career paths.
learning_outcomes: Describe the current financial environment and define a study plan and potential career path.
Apply statistical techniques, the capital asset pricing model and modern portfolio theory to analyse and compare the risk-return characteristics of investment portfolios.
Apply the concept of the time value of money to the valuation of annuities, perpetuities, bonds and equity securities.
Compare the sources of finance available to a business and estimate the cost of capital, cash flows and financial viability of different investment projects.

title: FINANCIAL STATEMENT ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: Financial statements describe the business activities and financial performance of a business. Financial analysts use this information to analyse the financial health and investment value of the business. In this subject, you will gain an understanding of how financial statements are constructed in order to distinguish the economic process that generates the values from the accounting process that at times conceals them. You will develop the skills to analyse each of the major financial statements and to build a spreadsheet financial model of the business. In doing so you will not only learn how to analyse the financial performance of the business, but also how to evaluate the quality of the financial information provided in the financial statements, which describes it. International accounting differences are discussed, and relevant research findings are considered.
learning_outcomes: Explain the theories underlying financial analysis and compare accounting standards, focusing on differences between US and International standards
Demonstrate required skills to source, analyse, and interpret a company’s financial statements using digital tools to guide financial decisions
Engage professionally and effectively to support a diverse team, respecting the needs, values, personalities, and abilities of others
Present a financial analysis of a company and communicate your professional conclusions on its implications for stakeholders

title: FINANCIAL STATEMENT ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: Financial statements describe the business activities and financial performance of a business. Financial analysts use this information to analyse the financial health and investment value of the business. In this subject, you will gain an understanding of how financial statements are constructed in order to distinguish the economic process that generates the values from the accounting process that at times conceals them. You will develop the skills to analyse each of the major financial statements and to build a spreadsheet financial model of the business. In doing so you will not only learn how to analyse the financial performance of the business, but also how to evaluate the quality of the financial information provided in the financial statements, which describes it. International accounting differences are discussed, and relevant research findings are considered.
learning_outcomes: Present a financial analysis of a company and be able to communicate your professional and empirical conclusions as to the implications of such analysis for stakeholders.

Explain the accounting, financial and economic theory on which the practice of financial analysis is founded and analyse the differences which exist between accounting standards and their application in different countries – in particular the difference between US and International accounting standards.

Demonstrate the skills, of a financial analyst, to source, deconstruct, and analyse, utilising appropriate digital tools, a company's financial statements, so as to extract meaningful information to guide relevant financial decisions.
Engage professionally and effectively to contribute to the success of a diverse team, in a manner which is respectful of the needs, values, personalities and capabilities of others.

title: INVESTMENT SECURITIES
syllabus_overview: Investment securities provide the primary means by which businesses are able to raise capital to fund their business activities. In this subject you will learn about two major types of investment securities: equity securities and debt securities. The different risk and return characteristics of equity and debt securities will be examined. You will also compare and contrast the different international markets in which equity and debt securities are traded, through learning activities conducted in our financial trading room. You will learn how to buy and sell equity and debt securities and how to monitor the performance of the equity and debt securities you may acquire. Key to making the decision whether to buy or sell any financial security is an evaluation of the market price of a financial security as compared with your estimation of its intrinsic value. Hence, a major focus of this subject is to assist you further develop the skills of a financial analyst, to be able to calculate the intrinsic value of various types of equity and debt securities.
learning_outcomes: Conduct company valuations and present written and verbal investment advice, individually and as part of a team.
Analyse and evaluate the influences on an industry and individual companies within that industry, individually and as part of a team.
Compare the risk and return characteristics of different types of securities with reference to the functioning of the markets in which they are traded.
Demonstrate the skills of a financial analyst, to research, analyse and evaluate the intrinsic value of a company

title: AGRIFINANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject addresses the application of financial management and risk management principles to the decision making of firms operating in the agribusiness environment. In this subject, you will be introduced to the procedures used in the evaluation and analysis of the financial operations of these firms. Further, you will examine and analyse different business structures, undertake an analysis of the issues related to capital structure, and will understand the effect that funding sources have in terms of a firms cost of capital. You will further develop your understanding of the importance of the time value of money concept, particularly as it relates to the strategic decision making process of agribusiness firms. Finally, you will spend time examining the range of risks agribusinesses confront and will develop an understanding of the risk mitigation techniques and project evaluation methods utilised by these firms in the management of these risks.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of financial management and risk management principles, concepts and theories relevant to firms operating in the agribusiness environment.
Apply knowledge garnered from workshops to a case study scenario.
Critically evaluate and effectively apply core financial management and risk management principles, concepts and theories as they relate to firms operating in the agribusiness environment.

title: CORPORATE FINANCE
syllabus_overview: Corporate Finance focuses on planning, organising, directing and controlling the financial activities of corporations. In this subject, you will examine finance theory and develop the skills of a finance manager to evaluate business investment opportunities, manage the capital structure to fund the investment and operating activities of the business and make dividend policy decisions considering the effect of relevant tax law. You will also advance knowledge on related topics, including risk analysis, real options, leasing, and mergers & acquisitions.
learning_outcomes: Apply finance theory to evaluate a firm's investment, financing, and dividend decisions
Use analytical tools, valuation techniques, and digital resources to solve financial management issues
Assess how corporate and personal taxes affect financial policy and decisions across tax regimes, behaviours, and market imperfections

title: INTERNATIONAL FINANCE
syllabus_overview: The continuous growth of financial globalisation and the integration of financial and product markets globally introduces different types of risks and opportunities for corporations. International finance will equip you with the applied knowledge and skills required to seize global investment and financing opportunities and manage risks for firms worldwide. You will cover international business opportunities, country risk analysis, international financial markets, including the foreign exchange market, parity theories, and the management of exchange rate risk. Overall, you will develop a deep understanding the critical financial management functions including exchange rate risk management, of multinational firms to augment long-term value for global firms.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical thinking to assess and communicate foreign exchange behavior and foreign exchange exposure, individually and in group settings.
Evaluate exchange rates using theoretical and market-based approaches to identify and manage foreign exchange exposure for corporations.
Analyse the structure, operations, and role of global financial markets in supporting operations of multinational corporations (MNCs).
Examine the nature, opportunities, and challenges of managing the goal of MNCs by focusing on global investment and financing decisions.

title: DERIVATIVES AND RISK MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In recent years there has been a dramatic increase in the size and complexity of the types of investment securities, the markets in which they are traded, and the institutions which trade them. In order to reduce the risks associated with trading these investment securities, derivative securities, such as forwards, futures, swaps and options, have rapidly evolved. Unfortunately, in some cases these derivative securities have increased rather than reduced the financial risks faced by individuals, corporations and even governments. In this subject you will be provided with a roadmap which will help you to understand derivative securities and derivative markets. Through this subject you will develop the skills of a financial risk manager to price derivative securities and to use them to define risk management strategies which meet the risk-reward objectives of different investors.
learning_outcomes: Use derivatives to manage various risks such as market, interest rates, currency, and credit risks.
Develop and evaluate arbitrage, hedging and other strategies using a range of derivatives and demonstrate their applications using digital tools.
Price forwards, futures, options, swaps and other derivatives.
Compare and contrast the characteristics of various derivative securities.

title: FINANCING INNOVATION
syllabus_overview: Great ideas and innovations require funding to realise their full potential. In this subject you will consider the funding of innovative projects, startups and medium sized ventures, from seed funding, through start-up and mezzanine rounds, to a possible Initial Public Offering (IPO). You will explore the sourcing, structuring, negotiation, value creation and exit strategies involved from both the viewpoint of the entrepreneur and the investor. Finally, you will consider the effect of new technologies, such as the internet, cloud computing and blockchain, on the venture capital process, so as to be able to take advantage of new ways of raising capital as the capital market itself innovates and evolves.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the sources and drivers of firm value and develop a financial case for business.
Apply valuation techniques appropriate for various types of entrepreneurial firms and financial securities.
Compare and contrast the various forms and sources of finance available for innovative projects, startups and medium sized ventures.
Compare and contrast the different strategies available for a venture capital investor to exit the investment.
Analyse the effects of technical innovation in venture capital markets.

title: SUSTAINABLE AND RESPONSIBLE FINANCE
syllabus_overview: Sustainable and Responsible Finance will equip you with the skills and frameworks required to develop investment products, processes and practices that not only generate financial returns but also deliver sustainable development and social value. You will develop the skills required to evaluate and manage environmental, social and governance (ESG) risks, opportunities and their impact. You will learn how to enhance the value of a business by considering ESG criteria along with traditional financial criteria when making capital allocation decisions such as in project valuation and investment and portfolio management. You will also learn how investors use ESG information to develop a more accurate risk profile of alternative investments and to compare assets classes.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate different frameworks for incorporating environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into decision-making processes as an asset owner or manager
Analyse environmental, social and governance (ESG) data to propose and assess the impact of socially responsible investment products and strategies
Analyse how environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues and risks may affect industry and company performance and security valuation across a range of asset classes

title: CASE STUDIES IN FINANCE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, you will examine real-life and practical case studies presented by professionals working in various financial roles within industry. Through these case studies, you will gain an understanding of how theoretical concepts are applied in practical settings. These case studies will help you to demonstrate the practical skills, of a financial analyst, portfolio manager, financial manager, and risk manager, which you have developed through completing a finance degree or financial management major, and apply them to analyse real-life situations and solve real-world financial problems. You will also have the opportunity to demonstrate the teamwork and communication skills required to apply your knowledge of finance in a business environment.
learning_outcomes: Engage professionally and effectively to contribute to the success of a diverse team, including communication with relevant stakeholders using a variety of modes of communication and appropriate digital tools.
Source and analyse financial information and value a range of financial securities, using appropriate digital tools and information services.
Define and justify an investment for an organization, portfolio or project.

Deliver an intelligent, balanced and compelling job interview, demonstrating your suitability for a career in finance and your ability to critique the ethical basis of financial and employment decisions.

title: INTERNATIONAL FINANCE
syllabus_overview: The continuous growth of financial globalization, coupled with the integration of financial and product markets globally, introduces different types of risks and opportunities for corporations. This subject aims to develop a deep understanding of the global financial system and critical financial management functions of multinational firms to equip students with the knowledge and skills to seize global opportunities and manage risks for firms worldwide. Learning materials will cover topics related to international business opportunities, the structure and operations of the international financial system and financial markets, including the foreign exchange market, parity theories and their applications, management of exchange rate risk, analysis of country risk, undertaking global investment and financing decisions, as well as managing short-term assets and liabilities to augment long-term value for global firms.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical thinking to develop and communicate a summative assessment reflecting the acquisition of a comprehensive understanding of foreign exchange behavior and related exposure in this subject individually and in a group setting.
Analyze the structure and operations of the international financial system and the global financial markets.

Evaluate and forecast exchange rates underpinned by various theories, institutional regimes, and market-based determinants to identify foreign exchange exposure and develop strategies to manage such exposure.
Examine the nature, opportunities, and challenges of managing the goal of multinational companies by focusing on global investment and financing decisions.

title: PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Portfolio management concerns the management of an individual’s or business’s investment securities, such as shares, bonds and real estate, with the aim of maximising the return of the portfolio for a defined level of risk. In this subject, you will examine portfolio theory and the application of risk and return concepts to portfolio construction and performance evaluation. You will develop the skills of a portfolio or fund manager, through learning activities in our financial trading room, creating your own financial portfolio, making decisions about investment strategies, aligning investments to objectives, and balancing risk against performance.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the issues relating to the management of bond and equity portfolio, including market efficiency and ethics, and utilise common measures to evaluate the performance of a portfolio.
Formulate the risk return trade-off encapsulated in modern portfolio theory.
Apply the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and alternative factor models to portfolio construction and critique these models using empirical evidence.
Analyse the components of the investment process and the central role of asset allocation decisions in the construction of an investment portfolio to meet investor goals and risk profiles.

title: BANK STRATEGY, OPERATIONS AND TECHNOLOGY
syllabus_overview: New technology, increased data availability, new forms of communication, and new business models are transforming the ways banks serve customers, interact with third parties, and operate internally. Banks need to continuously review their strategy, operations and technology to adapt to and succeed in the evolving economic, financial, and technical context in which they operate. In this subject you will develop the skills to review the strategy, mission and objectives of a bank in light of the dynamic environment in which they operate. You will learn how to define and justify a strategy to better deliver a bank’s mission and objectives in this context and learn how to implement and manage the change process such a strategy might require.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a bank’s strategic position in the external environment, considering the macro-economic environment and the industry or sector environment, with a focus on digital innovations that are affecting banks and banking.

Critically analyse a bank’s resources and capability to respond to changes in the external environment and its ability to take advantage of any opportunities which may arise relative to its competitors. Assess the physical, financial and people resources a bank requires to manage proposed change processes.

Construct a strategy document outlining a bank’s scope, mission, vision, values and objectives. Evaluate the strategic options for a bank, in relation to environmental and organisational considerations, to propose a strategy that supports its objectives.

title: CASE STUDIES IN FINANCE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, working as an analyst in the financial trading room you will examine and advise on case studies presented by professionals working in various financial roles within industry. Through these case studies, you will gain an understanding of how theoretical concepts are applied in practical settings. These case studies will help you to demonstrate the practical skills, of a financial analyst, portfolio manager, financial manager, and risk manager, which you have developed through completing your Master of Financial Analysis, and apply them to analysing real-life situations and solving actual financial problems. You will also have the opportunity to demonstrate the teamwork and communication skills required to apply your knowledge of finance in a business environment.
learning_outcomes: Manage an investment portfolio to meet investor goals and risk profile. Critique the ethical basis of financial decisions.
Source and analyse financial information and value a range of financial securities, using appropriate digital tools and information services.

Negotiate the terms of a merger of two ASX listed companies. Engage professionally and effectively to contribute to the success of a multicultural team, in a manner which is respectful of the needs, values, personalities and capabilities of others.
Communicate professionally and effectively with a range of stakeholders, using a variety of modes of communications and appropriate digital tools.

title: BANK RISK MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Bank risk managers must understand the nature and sources of risks impacting their institutions. Managing and mitigating risks not only ensures a going concern for an institution but contributes to the financial stability of the industry. This subject aims to provide a broad knowledge of the nature of these risks affecting banks and discuss qualitative approaches and quantitative methods used by the industry to measure and manage banks' exposure to these risks. The content covers topics on bank risk governance, current regulatory requirements, and methods applied in the industry to manage various risks, including emerging technology risks and other risks in a world heading toward digital economies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and analyse the nature and sources of various risks affecting banks and apply qualitative and quantitative prudential standards and other methods to manage, quantify and mitigate risk.
Work effectively as part of a team and apply appropriate solutions to manage various risks.
Demonstrate an understanding of approaches to holistic risk management and apply best practices in embedding appropriate risk culture to govern risk.

title: APPLIED CORPORATE FINANCE
syllabus_overview: The evolving landscape of increasing competition and rapid technological adaptation, along with a focus on ESG, compels corporations to be agile in strategic investment, cost-effective in financing, and innovative in driving sustainable value. Applied Corporate Finance trains you to develop the knowledge and skills critical for meeting such challenges. It covers topics such as strategic investment, financing choices and processes, leasing, payout policies, asset management, working capital management, and other treasury functions. You will also develop an understanding of recent issues in corporate finance, including sustainable finance, ESG strategies, an increased focus on agency problems, digital disruption in financing and efficiency, regulatory compliance, and investor relationship management. This unit advances your potential to be part of a top management team and effectively contribute to corporate financial strategies and decision-making for stakeholders' wealth maximization.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and collaboratively in a team to research, analyse, and evaluate various strategic financial policies to maintain a competitive advantage and support top executives' and Board of Directors' decision-making.
Assess firms' financial needs, design financing options, including sustainable financing, optimise the financing mix and cost, and raise capital to support operations and investments.
Critically evaluate the suitability of strategic investment decisions, investment options within the broader framework of the investment portfolio, and strategic goals of the firm.
Assess and undertake effective liquidity management, a sustainable payout policy, and investor relationship management to ensure transparency, efficiency, and sustainable growth.

title: FINTECH AND BLOCKCHAIN APPLICATIONS
syllabus_overview: The financial services industry is rapidly adopting digital technologies to access and understand big data and automate decision-making. This subject introduces the fundamentals of AI technologies, including machine learning and blockchain, and showcases their applications in the financial services industry. You will learn to apply Python to access, manage, and analyse real-time financial data to develop algorithm-based trading strategies and automate financial decision making. Additionally, you will use machine learning techniques to solve classification problems in the financial industry. The course also covers the fundamentals of blockchain technology, demonstrate how blockchain works and showcase its applications in modern digital transactions like smart contracts and decentralised finance. These skills will prepare you to meet the future demands of the finance sector in the age of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess the current state of AI technologies deployed in the fintech industry and examine different uses of these technologies.
Work as a member of a fintech team to analyse different uses of blockchain and build decentralised applications on the Ethereum platform.
Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning techniques for problem-solving in the financial service industry.
Automate trading strategies, investment management, financial decision-making, and communication to various stakeholders by utilising financial programming languages and various libraries.

title: FINTECH APPLICATIONS
syllabus_overview: The financial service industry is experiencing massive deployment of digital technologies to access and understand big data and automate decision-making through the employment of algorithms. You will be introduced to the fundamentals of AI technologies, including machine learning and natural language processing techniques and their applications in the financial service industry. You will learn to apply the R programming language to access and analyze real-time financial trading data, automate data cleaning and visualizations, construct and optimize investment portfolios according to the investor’s risk profile and develop algorithm-based trading strategies. These skills are critical to meet the future demand for the finance sector in the age of digitalisation.
learning_outcomes: To work as a member of a data analyst team, utilising various financial libraries to collect, clean, visualise and analyse financial data.

Explain the fundamentals of AI technologies and apply them to inform decision-making and solve real-world business problems. Analyze and assess the present state of development in the Fintech industry.
Apply R programming language and other related technologies to automate investment portfolio construction, algorithm-based trading strategies, and performance evaluation.

title: DEBT SECURITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop a working knowledge of the characteristics of fixed-income securities, the operation of debt markets, and the mechanics of trading these securities. You will also develop a thorough knowledge of the measurement of the yield of fixed-interest securities, the various relevant yield spread measures, and the term structure of interest rates. This will then be used in the valuation of fixed-interest securities, including the valuation of bonds with embedded options, structured securities, and international bonds. Specific attention will also be given to credit analysis and risk assessment and the measurement of interest rate risk.
learning_outcomes: Value fixed-income securities, measure interest rate risk, and understand basic portfolio management strategy or fixed-income securities;
Apply economic and financial theory to credit analysis for a pubic listed company.
Compare and contrast the characteristics of various types of fixed income securities and markets;
Explain in detail the measurement of the yield of fixed income securities and the term structure of interest rates;

title: FINANCIAL DERIVATIVES
syllabus_overview: With the growing complexity of financial markets and the use of sophisticated instruments, expertise in derivatives is essential as market participants rely on derivatives to hedge risks, exploit arbitrage, and enhance returns, making it crucial to understand their pricing, application, and strategic use. This subject will introduce you to concepts and methods to price financial derivatives such as forwards, futures, swaps, and options on various underlying assets. You will learn about the uses of derivatives by various market participants such as traders, risk and portfolio managers and the application of strategies and techniques to hedge financial risk or take advantage of arbitrage. You will also learn about market cases, feasible uses, and limitations of derivatives and digital applications.
learning_outcomes: Develop and implement arbitrage and risk management strategies using various derivative instruments on various underlying assets, including stocks, bonds, interest rates, indexes, currencies, and others.
Apply financial theories and analytical skills to price and value financial derivatives.
Compare and contrast features of various derivatives and illustrate relevant market operations.

title: EQUITY SECURITIES
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the necessary skills required to undertake equity asset valuation tasks carried out in an investment management or brokerage environment. After completing this subject, you will be able to undertake equity research projects, conduct financial and industry analysis and provide valuation decisions and recommendations about listed equity securities. As such, you will have acquired the equity valuation knowledge and skills required of CFA Levels 1 and 2. Through lessons in our financial trading room, you will develop the skills necessary to work as an effective member of an investment research team, as well as to enhance your independent and collaborative learning skills. Finally, you will have the opportunity to consider ethical issues associated with undertaking investment research.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the skills of a financial analyst, to work as a member of a team, to research, analyse and evaluate the intrinsic value of a public and private company, using appropriate digital tools and information services

Explain the conceptual basis of methodologies used to value a listed company's equity securities. Analyse the competitive nature of an industry, and the financial statements of companies operating in that industry.
Persuasively present your investment advice in respect of a company’s equity securities, in written and oral form. Analyse and resolve ethical issues raised by the investment research process.

title: CORPORATE FINANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject is focussed on introducing you to the key goals and decision-making responsibilities of businesses and corporations. You will develop a thorough and advanced knowledge of the short and long term investment and financing decisions of a firm, including project evaluation and capital budgeting decisions; leasing, replacement and real option modelling; the relative merits of debt, equity, hybrid and derivative forms of capital and evaluation of the capital raising process; theoretical and practical decision-making relating to corporate capital structure and dividend policy decisions; the effect of leverage, taxes and other imperfections on the cost of capital and the value of the firm; and working capital and asset management. Related, and extension, topics that may also be considered include mergers and acquisitions, corporate restructuring and corporate governance applications.
learning_outcomes: Employ practical and quantitative skills to manage the debt and equity capital of a firm, and to value these capital components and the overall firm in this context.

Critically evaluate and analyse the suitability of specific corporate decisions and transactions for different firms in light of the relative impact on firm valuation and shareholder wealth by comprehending the accounting, financial and economic theories on which decision-making processes and the concept of firm valuation are founded.
Structure and present an argument to a decision-making body (such as a CEO or Board of directors) recommending a specific corporate transaction or a restructuring or strategy action,
Understand the operating and financial structures of business organisations and how these impact on the performance and valuation of these organisations.

title: FINANCIAL STATEMENT ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain an advanced appreciation of financial statement analysis from the point of view of the primary users: equity and credit analysts. The subject provides you with an understanding of how financial statements are constructed in order to separate the economic process that generates the numbers from the accounting process that at times obscures them. Each topic is focussed on a specific area of analysis and the effect of differences in accounting methods and estimates on reported financial conditions. The results of operations and financial ratios is highlighted. International accounting differences are discussed and relevant empirical research findings are considered.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the analytical thinking required to apply accounting theory and forensic skills to determining the actual financial state of a company on the one hand and to analysing empirical and theoretical problems in a scholarly manner on the other.
Analyse the differences which exist between accounting standards and their application in different countries, in particular the difference between US GAAP and IASB GAAP.
Explain the accounting, financial and economic theory on which the practice of financial analysis is founded.
Apply advanced financial analytical skills and appropriate digital tools, to extract meaningful information from financial statements to guide decisions.

title: INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Financial globalisation, a heightened geopolitical environment, economic uncertainties, and increased ESG focus present unique challenges and opportunities for investors and corporations worldwide. International Financial Management develops your conceptual and applied knowledge and skills to manage the critical value drivers of firms operating globally. You will examine the structure and operations of global financial architecture, evaluate the economics, institutions, policies, and uncertainties governing exchange rate behavior, forecast exchange rates, and measure and manage exchange rate risk exposures. You will be trained to critically evaluate the relative merits and risks associated with the strategic financial management decisions of multinational companies, including financing, investment, and asset allocation decisions in a competitive global economic setting.
learning_outcomes: Assess foreign exchange behaviour - exchange rate regimes, exchange rate determination, international parity relations - and their implications for forecasting exchange rates and managing exposures.

Design and manage strategic financial decisions, including country risk analysis, foreign direct investment, financing, asset allocation, and tax management in international settings to deliver sustainable value.
Critically evaluate contemporary global financial systems and current issues in international finance that affect the global flow of funds and financial management functions of global firms.

title: PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject seeks to provide a structured and dynamic approach to portfolio management. This approach includes identifying investment objectives and constraints, researching ideas, forecasting exceptional returns, constructing and implementing portfolios, and observing and refining their performance. The approach draws on asset pricing theories, such as the Capital Asset Pricing Model, and a range of statistical tools for its structure and intuition. Particular attention is given to portfolio performance evaluation and risk management.
learning_outcomes: Construct, manage and critically analyse the performance of a portfolio of financial assets consistent with the investment objectives.
Apply financial theory and analytical skills to solving actual portfolio management problems and examining empirical and theoretical problems in a scholarly manner.
Critically evaluate the relative merits of passive versus active portfolio management

title: FRENCH 2
syllabus_overview: This subject is entirely synchronous; it consolidates and builds upon the knowledge acquired in French 1. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. Upon successful completion of this subject, you will have attained the equivalent of an A1 or "breakthrough" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Participate in the exchange of personal information (e.g. residence, acquaintances, possessions), demonstrating accurate use of basic language structures.
Analyse and apply familiar French expressions to construct contextually appropriate responses in concrete situations, demonstrating critical awareness of cultural norms.
Engage in basic spoken interactions in French by responding appropriately to clear, slow speech, and applying strategies to seek clarification or assistance when needed.

title: FRENCH 4
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates and builds upon the knowledge acquired in French 3. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. Upon successful completion of this subject, you will have attained the equivalent of an A2 or "waystage" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Describe in simple terms aspects of their background, immediate environment and matters in areas of immediate need.
Communicate in simple and routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar and routine matters.

Demonstrate understanding of sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance (e.g. very basic personal and family information, shopping, local geography, employment).

title: FRENCH 1
syllabus_overview: This subject is for students with little or no prior knowledge of French. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. You will work towards attaining an A1 or "breakthrough" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Engage in basic spoken interactions in French by responding appropriately to clear, slow speech, and applying strategies to seek clarification or assistance when needed.
Participate in the exchange of personal information (e.g. residence, acquaintances, possessions), demonstrating accurate use of basic language structures.
Analyse and apply familiar French expressions to construct contextually appropriate responses in concrete situations, demonstrating critical awareness of cultural norms.

title: FRENCH 5
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates and builds upon the knowledge acquired in French 4. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in various situations. You will work towards attaining a B1 or "threshold" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Understand the main points of clear, standard French on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.
Deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling in an area where the language is spoken.
Produce simple, connected text on topics that are familiar or of personal interest.
Describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans.

title: FRENCH 3
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates and builds on the knowledge gained in French 2 or VCE French. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation. Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. You will work towards attaining an A2 or "waystage" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance (e.g. very basic personal and family information, shopping, local geography, employment).
Communicate in simple and routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar and routine matters.
Describe in simple terms aspects of their background, immediate environment and matters in areas of immediate need.

title: FRENCH 6
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates and builds upon the knowledge acquired in French 5. It develops the four primary skills of language acquisition – speaking, listening, reading and writing – through a communicative approach to learning. You will discover various aspects of everyday life in France, introduced through imaginative dialogues and reinforced by extensive exercises on French vocabulary, grammar and civilisation.Culture is embedded throughout language, so learning another language develops your intercultural communication skills, preparing you to be responsive and agile in varied situations. You will continue working towards the equivalent of a B1 or "threshold" level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL).
learning_outcomes: Describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans.
Produce simple, connected text on topics that are familiar or of personal interest.
Deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling in an area where the language is spoken.
Understand the main points of clear, standard written French on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF FAMILY AND SYSTEMIC PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with a sound understanding of foundational family therapy concepts and skills to equip you to work effectively with both individuals and families. It will be delivered via weekly online (live streamed) lectures and small skills group learning across 12 weeks of Semester 1.
