title: APPLIED ANATOMY FOR PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject the anatomical principles and terminology learned in previous anatomy subjects will be applied to the detailed study of the anatomy of the upper limb, lower limb, and vertebral column, as relevant to the practice of physiotherapy. The concept of integrated function of multiple body systems will be developed in each region. Teaching will include both online learning and face-to-face teaching sessions including practical classes involving cadaver materials and surface anatomy. You will be required to work together in small groups, to take responsibility for your own learning and understanding of anatomy so that you are able to identify anatomical structure and function on a living body as you would in a clinical physiotherapy context.
learning_outcomes: Critically apply an understanding of anatomical sciences to physiotherapy.

Expand observational and communication skills, including the use of appropriate anatomical and medical terminology, to accurately identify anatomical structures or events and infer their relationship to function using cadaveric material, the living body or medical imaging in a laboratory environment.
Extend anatomical knowledge and principles to the context of normal structure and function of the upper limb, lower limb, and vertebral column.

title: ERGONOMICS PRINCIPLES OF WORK, WORKSTATION AND PLANT DESIGN
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will study biological and psychological evidence and associated ergonomics principles concerning human capacities and limitations relevant to the design of equipment and 'plant', work tasks, workstations and the physical workplace environment. You will learn to understand the interface between humans and their environments, human capabilities and work demands, and apply principles of ergonomics and human factors to achieve effective work performance and good occupational health and safety outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the efficacy of workplace interventions integrating evidence-based theoretical knowledge and practical ergonomics assessment skills.
Analyse aspects of human physical and psychological capacities, including limitations, and their impact on safely and efficiency.
Evaluate work processes, workstation and plant design using ergonomic principles and communicate recommendations for improvement.
Reflect critically on hazards arising from the design of work processes, workstations, and equipment.

title: MUSCULOSKELETAL INJURIES/DISORDERS AND PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: Work-related musculoskeletal and stress related mental health disorders are among the most common and costly workplace problems. In this subject, work-related determinants of health are reviewed within a broad, macro-ergonomics systems framework to develop an understanding of some of the mechanisms and pathways via which people's jobs and working environments can affect their physical and psychological health, safety and wellbeing, both positively and negatively. This subject enables you to develop your knowledge of the aetiology and potential prevention measures to reduce the incidence of complex health problems such as musculoskeletal and stress related mental health disorders.
learning_outcomes: Appraise, synthesise and effectively communicate evidence on a range of issues relating to work-related MSDs and psychological health.
To critically evaluate evidence on a range of topics relating to the development and risk management of complex health problems in the workplace.
Critically analyse the efficacy of workplace interventions using evidence based theoretical knowledge
Implement evidence-based and effective preventive interventions to reduce the incidence of MSDs and stress-related mental health problems.

title: WORKPLACE MANAGEMENT OF HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES IN OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY
syllabus_overview: Many systems of work within organisations use hazardous substances which require controls to manage risks. In this subject you will examine the effects of hazardous substances on humans and risk management principles related to screening, monitoring and control of chemical, biological, radiation and neurotoxic hazards in the workplace, as relevant to OH&S professionals, using risk management and OH&S systems frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Individually and collaboratively analyse regulations for the investigation, management and control of hazardous substances and apply to varied workplace contexts.
Critically evaluate exposures to, and health impacts of, common chemical, biological and radiation hazards on workplace populations.

Individually and collaboratively analyse theoretical knowledge and evidence-based models of practice and apply to development and implementation of integrated strategies for assessment, monitoring and control measures for common hazardous substances.

Critically analyse and synthesize evidence based approaches to development and communication of screening, monitoring and management strategies for common hazardous substances in varied work contexts.

title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY: PRINCIPLES AND LEGISLATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to principles of Occupational Health and Safety through a study of models, trends and relevant legislation. Topics address how changing work demands, patterns, structures and technology impact worker health. Legal and ethical issues in OH&S and injury management, including workers' compensation and rehabilitation, are introduced. Regulation related to dangerous goods and hazardous substances, privacy, professional practice and ethics are presented within risk management and systems frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Investigate and critically evaluate the impact of current and emerging work patterns, and technologies on the workforce, job design and worker health.
Critically analyse, synthesise and apply complex theoretical concepts and models of health and disease to OHS practice.
Effectively translate work-health related regulation and policy into practice.
Critically reflect on ethical dilemmas and boundaries in professional decision-making and practice across a variety of occupational health and safety contexts.

title: WORKPLACE ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject enables you to develop and apply detailed knowledge of selected methods and methodologies that are commonly used by occupational ergonomists and occupational health and safety professionals to monitor, analyse and evaluate potential risks and hazards. You will undertake fieldwork to learn to identify and apply tools specific to a variety of physical, psychosocial and environmental hazards in varied contexts. Using selected methods and tools, you collect and analyse data, and write formal reports to communicate findings and recommendations for interventions to control hazards. In doing so, you evaluate the applicability and functionality of the tools used.
learning_outcomes: Develop detailed, coherent reports which communicate identified workplace problems, measurement methods, findings and interpretations, and recommendations for corrective actions.
Identify, apply, and critically evaluate methodologies and methods to assess workplace hazards and risks.
Integrate evidence based theoretical knowledge and models to analyse and evaluate complex workplace situations and develop interventions
Independently investigate, analyse, evaluate and interpret data collected from workplaces in relation to complex OHS problems.

title: FOUNDATIONS IN SPEECH PATHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the concepts of communication, eating and drinking and develop an awareness of the individual and social factors that shape human communication, eating and drinking across different populations and contexts. You will learn about the human right to communicate and the integral role that communication, eating and drinking play in the formation of individual identity. You will learn about the role of speech pathology in enabling communication, eating and drinking by exploring speech pathology practice in a range of contexts, including health, disability and education. You will also be introduced to the role of research literature in advocacy, support and the delivery of innovative, evidence-based speech pathology services. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Describe the scope of speech pathology practice and its role in enabling communication, eating and drinking
Explain how communication, eating and drinking inform identity and work as a team to compare and contrast the factors that influence others' communication, eating and drinking abilities.
Describe the foundational concepts of communication, eating and drinking
Explain the individual and social determinants on communication, eating and drinking
Explain the role of communication in the preservation of human rights.

title: WORKPLACE RISK MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Using the framework of the ILO OHS Management System, you will develop an understanding of the underpinning concepts and models of practice used in occupational health and safety (OHS) risk management You will explore OHS policy and governance requirements; leadership and change management strategies; worker and workplace engagement and systems for measuring and reviewing system performance and OHS-management systems in varied industry contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect and analyse the content and approaches underpinning the concepts and procedures used in OHS risk management.
Individually and collaboratively evaluate the practical application and implementation of systematic measurement of effective risk management systems.
Investigate and critically analyse the principles and practices underlying differences in risk management between industry sectors with different risk profiles.
Analyse and critique the application of concepts, standards, and theoretical models to the implementation of effective risk management systems.

title: ANALYSING AND COMBINING WORDS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will investigate the structure and function of words. Focusing on Australian English, you will explore the production and description of speech sounds and how these sounds work together as a system. You will also investigate morphological aspects of words, aspects of meaning and how words combine to create clauses. With a focus on clinical relevance to speech pathology, this subject provides foundational knowledge of speech and language to inform clinical reasoning and clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate preclinical competence in broad transcription of Australian English utterances
Demonstrate preclinical competence in analysis of the syllable and foot structure of English words.
Demonstrate preclinical competence in the analysis of morphological, phrase and clause structures of English.

title: INTRODUCTION TO CLINICAL REASONING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore knowledge and skills from the process of understanding and resolving case-based problems illustrating the structural and functional components of communication and swallowing. Across the semester small teams will be presented with authentic speech pathology cases that will provide the trigger for learning about the principles and practices of clinical reasoning and professional practice in the discipline. The case-based learning approach will be supported by specialist lectures, practical workshops and integrated online learning activities that focus on the process of describing and evaluating communication and swallowing.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and describe the benefits and limitations of commonly used formal assessments for people with communication and swallowing disorders.
Integrate assessment data and apply this to determine potential intervention options for people with communication and swallowing disorders.
Explain the fundamental principles and practices of assessment and intervention for people across the lifespan with communication and swallowing disorders.
Analyse and explain information from a range of sources related to the clinical presentation of a person with a communication or swallowing disorder.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will increase your awareness and basic understanding of the nature of the speech pathology discipline, the culture of the speech pathology workplace and the required competencies, roles and functions of the speech pathologist. You will be introduced to the speech pathology practice placement program that will continue throughout the course. This will include orientation to Speech Pathology Australia's (SPA) Professional Standards, Competency-Based Occupation Standards (CBOS) and companion assessment framework, COMPASS. You will demonstrate an understanding of the skills you are required to develop and demonstrate on completion of the Bachelor of Speech Pathology. There will be an emphasis on your understanding and self-evaluation of practice placement readiness. This includes compliance with University and agency onboarding requirements, demonstrated awareness of inherent requirements and fitness to practice. You will then practice and apply generic communication principles and practices involved in conversation, interviewing, assessment and management of clients and their families. You will participate in a range of integrated pre-clinical online learning activities, workshops, guided observation and demonstration, and active participation in highly structured and scaffolded simulations and clinical scenarios. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Observe client and clinician behaviours in a variety of speech pathology contexts and document these accurately and ethically.
Identify and describe emerging professional identity including clinical aspirations
Assess personal skills and behaviours in relation to professional practice requirements.
Communicate clearly in both verbal and written form with a range of communication partners in different clinical contexts, autonomously and with peers.
Interact effectively with clients with communication disabilities during a team based simulation.

title: COMMUNICATION AND SWALLOWING ACROSS THE LIFESPAN
syllabus_overview: Human communication and swallowing evolve across the lifespan. Through lectures, workshops, and integrated online learning activities you will learn about the underlying neurological, cognitive, perceptual, sensory and motor components that support communication and swallowing. You will be able to describe how communication and swallowing abilities develop from infancy through to old age and understand the factors that influence this development. This knowledge will provide you with a sound foundation to understand the scope of practice of speech pathology.
learning_outcomes: Describe how communication and swallowing evolves over a lifespan and analyse factors that influence that development.
Describe a range of communication skills and considerations for interacting with people across the lifespan who have a diverse range of personal and environmental factors.
Apply the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health to communication and swallowing across the lifespan
Analyse key communication and swallowing behaviours to determine if they are indicative of typical development.

title: SOUND FOR COMMUNICATION
syllabus_overview: Human communication is the process by which people exchange information through a common system of symbols and signs. The reception of auditory information (through audition) and the production of oral information (through speech and voice) are aspects of human communication that will be explored in this subject. These processes that enable communication will draw on key concepts from basic acoustics and the physics of objects in motion. The processes that will be covered in this subject include analysis of sound waves and speech, the hearing process (including techniques for gauging hearing ability and hearing loss), the psychology of sound perception and the mechanism of speech and voice production. The overall aim of HCS2SFC is to enable you to understand the role of sound in the communication process, to explain the basic science of perceptual, acoustic, aerodynamic and physiological aspects of the speech signal, and to explain the relevance of the speech signal to clinical practice across different cultural contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explain the basic science of sound transmission
Discuss the impact of cultural awareness on personal views and how cultural diversity impacts clinical practice
Analyse and explain the basic science related to speech production
Interpret and explain psychoacoustic phenomena in relation to sound perception
Interpret and apply the basic science of sound to explain human audition

title: TECHNIQUES FOR ANALYSING COMMUNICATION
syllabus_overview: This subject expands your foundational knowledge of speech and language by introducing less typical speech data and more detailed speech transcription techniques. Aspects of discourse and narrative analysis are introduced, as relevant to clinical practice and clinical reasoning in speech pathology.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the morphology and syntax of language samples
Identify and analyse clinically relevant features of discourse and pragmatics in language samples
Explain and apply key linguistic constructs including phonemes, allophones and phonological rules
Phonetically transcribe utterances using clinically relevant IPA symbols and diacritics

title: ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION A
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on assessment and interpretation of clinical and instrumental data to explore communication and swallowing difficulties. A core component of clinical practice in speech pathology is performing accurate, valid and reliable assessments. You will gain theoretical and practical experience in conducting and interpreting speech pathology assessments. You will also develop related skills such as explaining assessments results to a variety of audiences. You will learn about the available therapeutic techniques used to address communication and swallowing difficulties, and how to select the most appropriate approach for your clients. This includes using research evidence and integrating the client's values and preferences and the clinical context in which you are working. This learning occurs through the use of authentic clinical cases in a case based learning format.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the biological, psychosocial and environmental factors that impact communication and swallowing across the lifespan.
Analyse and describe speech pathology assessment data, intervention plans, and intervention outcomes.in an audience appropriate format
Apply speech pathology assessment data to intervention planning for people with communication and swallowing disorders.
Using the best available evidence, construct long term, short term and session goals for people with communication or swallowing disorders.
Select and apply appropriate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods for clients based on best available evidence.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will start to transfer and apply theoretical knowledge into a clinical setting. This is one of two subjects in third year providing professional practice in either adults or paediatrics. You will be required to cover both areas in order to gain clinical competencies. You will participate in a 10 day placement in an adult or paediatric setting and will complete these placements in various agencies around Melbourne, Bendigo and other regional or rural settings. If you are enrolled in Melbourne, paediatric placements will take place within the La Trobe Communication Clinic. The first and final week of your placement instance will include an on-campus briefing and debriefing session which comprise part of the placement hours. Pass criteria for this subject is Novice level on the COMPASS® assessment. Professional accreditation requires a minimum standard of competency to be met. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a speech pathologist. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Manage professional workload collaboratively with accountability and maximal support
Investigate communication and/or swallowing by applying cognitive, communicative and observational skills and demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.
Apply theory to develop clinical hypotheses about clients' presenting conditions with maximal support.
Reflect on personal performance and feedback to increase knowledge and skills in speech pathology practice.
Incorporate theory and clinical observations to formulate ethically sound, evidenced based interventions with maximal support
Analyse and interpret aspects of speech and language assessments with maximal support.
Communicate effectively with clients, family members and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document interventions with maximal support.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICE C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will attend 30 days of clinic in an adult or paediatric setting. This placement may include a combination of clinical simulation and typical clinical placement activities. It is the first of two professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice in the final year of the course. You will work to refi ne the clinical skills acquired over the previous placements, applying these more independently as the subject progresses with the aim of being ‘near entry level’ on the COMPASS assessment to pass the subject. This means you will be rated at entry level in most competency units, although some competencies may still be moving from intermediate level towards entry level during this placement. In addition, you will complete two clinical practicum examinations. To support your learning, you will also attend a placement briefing session held at the beginning of the subject, and a debriefing session at the end of the subject (these comprise part of the placement hours). This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply initiative to adapt to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups with low to moderate levels of support.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills, demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.
Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention with low to moderate levels of support.
Reflect on personal performance to develop professional identity and improve service and client outcomes
Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention with low to moderate levels of support.
Analyse and interpret aspects of speech and language assessments with low to moderate support.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will start to transfer theoretical knowledge into a clinical setting. This is one of two subjects in third year providing professional practice in either adults or paediatrics. You will be required to cover both areas in order to gain clinical competencies. You will participate in a 10 day placement in an adult or paediatric setting. You will complete these placements in various agencies around Melbourne, Bendigo and other regional or rural settings. If you are enrolled in Melbourne, paediatric placements will take place within the La Trobe Communication Clinic. The first and final week of your placement instance will include an on-campus briefing and debriefing session which comprise of the placement hours. Pass criteria for this subject is Intermediate level on the COMPASS® assessment. Professional accreditation requires a minimum standard of competency to be met. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a speech pathologist. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on personal performance and feedback to increase knowledge and skills in speech pathology practice.
Incorporate theory and clinical observations formulate ethically sound, evidenced based intervention with maximal support.
Analyse and interpret aspects of speech and language assessments with maximal support.
Apply theory to develop clinical hypotheses about clients' presenting conditions with maximal support.
Communicate effectively with clients, family members and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document interventions with maximal support.
Investigate communication and/or swallowing by applying cognitive, communicative and observational skills and demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.
Manage professional workload collaboratively with accountability and maximal support

title: ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION B
syllabus_overview: Building on learning from HCS3AIA the principles of assessment and intervention for clients with impairments of communication and swallowing are applied to clinical scenarios. You will use assessment information, client observation and principles of evidence-based practice to formulate assessment plans and intervention strategies. You are required to provide rationales for clinical decision-making including consideration of the impact of social and cultural issues on service provision and to demonstrate knowledge of the professional role of a speech pathologist in a team. This learning occurs through the use of authentic clinical cases in a case based learning format.
learning_outcomes: Construct and interpret speech pathology assessment data and apply this information to inform evidence based and person centred management.
Formulate intervention-based long term goals, short term goals and session goals for a range of clients guided by the best available.
Appraise speech pathology assessment data, intervention plans and intervention outcomes to explain these in an audience appropriate manner.
Explain the impact of a range of communication and swallowing disorders for people across the lifespan using a biopsychosocial model of health and illness.
Differentiate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods that are best suited to a client based on available evidence.

title: SERVICE AND CONTEXT
syllabus_overview: Given the ever-changing landscape of Speech Pathology in a contemporary society, you need to explore diverse service contexts and types of service delivery. In this subject you will examine relevant government and professional policies and procedures that guide service delivery. You will also identify the social determinants of health that might influence the adequacy and efficacy of a service and compare and contrast diverse service options to deliver client-centred care. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Appraise service delivery options in different contexts to predict the likely outcomes of speech pathology intervention.
Identify the social determinants of health that impact on clients with communication and/or swallowing needs in different contexts.
Analyse how key government and professional policies that determine speech pathology service delivery impact speech pathology services.
Design client-centred speech pathology interventions that are appropriate to individual circumstances

title: CLINICAL PRACTICE D
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will attend 30 days of clinic in an adult or paediatric setting. This placement may include a combination of clinical simulation and typical clinical placement activities. It is the second of two professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice in the final year of the course. You will work to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous placements, applying these more independently as the subject progresses with the aim of being at ‘entry level’ on the COMPASS assessment to pass the subject. In addition, you will complete two clinical practicum examinations. To support your learning, you will also attend a placement briefing session held at the beginning of the subject, and a debriefing session at the end of the subject (these comprise part of the placement hours). This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on personal performance to develop professional knowledge and improve client outcomes
Employ initiative to adapt knowledge to new situations, with autonomy and accountability.
Collaborate and communicate effectively with a variety of teams including research groups and manage a professional workload with a high level of autonomy.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills recognizing both typical and pathological function.
Communicate professional knowledge effectively to plan and evaluate effective and client appropriate interventions.
Analyse, interpret and communicate clinical data, diagnostic and prognostic conclusions to specialist and non-specialist audiences effectively.
Critically review and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention.

title: STRUCTURE OF SPEECH AND LANGUAGE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will analyse the structure of speech and language. Focusing on spoken Australian English (speech), you will analyse words in terms of their component speech sounds and the interaction of those sounds as a phonological system. At the word level, you will analyse the morphological structure of words and examine aspects of word meaning. At levels above the word, you will examine phrase and clause structure and evaluate how linguistic devices are used to create cohesion and coherence in text. With a focus on applied analysis, this subject equips you with linguistic knowledge to facilitate and inform clinical reasoning and clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse key linguistic constructs including phonemes, allophones and phonological rules
Phonetically transcribe Australian English utterances using broad transcription
Analyse the syllable and foot structure of English words
Analyse the morphological, phrase and clause structures of English.
Analyse linguistic devices used to create cohesion in text

title: LIFESPAN COMMUNICATION AND SWALLOWING 1
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on assessment and interpretation of clinical and instrumental data to explore communication and swallowing difficulties across the lifespan. You will apply knowledge of normal communication and swallowing processes to a clinical setting. You will gain theoretical and practical experience in conducting and interpreting speech pathology assessments. You will also develop related skills such as explaining assessments results, writing clinical reports and planning goals for therapy.
learning_outcomes: Analyse how communication and/or swallowing may be impaired in infants, children, adolescents and adults.

Justify appropriate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods for clients based on best available evidence and articulate appropriate adaptations for clients from culturally and linguistically diverse communities
Accurately communicate the ﬁndings from clinical speech pathology assessments, intervention plans and outcomes effectively to a given audience using an appropriate format and mode.
Analyse data from a range of clinical assessments used in speech pathology with a range of clients using a practice-based evidence model.
Appraise appropriate assessments for clients based on best available evidence and justify appropriate adaptations for clients from culturally and linguistically diverse communities.
Analyse the biological, psychosocial and environmental factors that impact communication and swallowing across the lifespan.

title: ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION C
syllabus_overview: Building on learning from HCS3AIA and HCS3AIB, the principles of assessment and intervention for clients with impairments of communication and swallowing are applied to more complex clinical contexts. You will use assessment information, client observation and principles of evidence-based practice to formulate assessment plans and intervention strategies. You are required to provide rationales for clinical decision making including consideration of the impact of social and cultural issues on service provision and to demonstrate knowledge of the professional role of a speech pathologist in a team. You are encouraged to consider interdisciplinary practice and the complexities of appropriate ethical behaviour in all workplaces.
learning_outcomes: Formulate person-centred management in culturally diverse contexts based on assessment data
Critically reflect on your role as a speech pathologist considering the ethical, social and environmental implications of your intervention and as a member of a multidisciplinary team
Appraise and clearly explain speech pathology assessment data, intervention plans and intervention outcomes in an audience appropriate format
Select and apply appropriate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods based on best available evidence.
Plan and construct intervention long term goals, short term goals and session goals for clients based on best available evidence

title: EVIDENCE IN PRACTICE IN SPEECH PATHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will continue to develop the skills required for evidence-based practice in speech pathology. You will further develop the ability to formulate answerable clinical questions, search for the available evidence, critically appraise the literature and make decisions about practice based on the evidence. The subject incorporates lectures related to evidence-based practice, in all aspects of the speech pathology profession, and tutorials to assist you in developing writing and critical appraisal skills for literature related to a given clinical issue.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise and apply evidence to inform patient/client management plans.
Communicate research evidence clearly to clients to provide appropriate rationale for clinical decisions with regard to individual needs.
Incorporate the principles and processes of evidence based practice in a clinical practice context.
Formulate answerable practice-related questions and acquire relevant evidence to address the questions.

title: INTRODUCTION TO SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE

You will be introduced to the speech pathology practice placement program that will continue throughout the course. This will include orientation to Speech Pathology Australia's (SPA) Professional Standards, Competency-Based Occupation Standards (CBOS) and companion assessment framework, COMPASS ® . You will practice and apply generic communication principles and practices involved in conversation, interviewing, assessment and management of clients and their families. You will participate in a range of integrated pre-clinical online learning activities, workshops, guided observation and demonstration, and active participation in highly structured and scaffolded simulations and clinical scenarios. There will be a strong emphasis on learning through structured reflective practice.
learning_outcomes: Use both written and verbal modes of communication to facilitate self-reflection.
Reflect on your ability to relate to and engage in a meaningful manner with a client with communication impairments in their lived situation.
Implement structured therapy programs under high levels of supervision (via simulation).
Use advanced verbal & written communication skills with a range of communication partners in different environments.
Make meaningful observations of client behaviours in a variety of speech pathology contexts and document these accurately.
Work within the professional and ethical guidelines of speech pathologists in Australia.

title: PREPARATION FOR SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will evaluate your personal and professional development over the Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) course. You will analyse and critically appraise workplace environments and evaluate evidence based strategies for maintaining self-care and wellbeing in the workplace. Identifying new and emerging opportunities for speech pathology practice in contemporary society, and appraising these opportunities to make informed decisions about their career will also be explored.
learning_outcomes: Design a plan to support personal and professional wellbeing using evidence-based strategies and reflective practices.
Examine and contrast workplace governance structures and rights and responsibilities within speech pathology workplace environments.
Assess current and emerging opportunities for innovation in diverse environments within contemporary society.
Critically appraise personal strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats to support future career decisions.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE 1

There will be an emphasis on developing an understanding of generic communication principles and practices involved in conversation, interviewing, assessment and management of clients and their families. The subject encompasses workshops, guided observation sessions, simulation activities, and active participation in highly structured evidence-based clinical workshops.
