learning_outcomes: Critically reflect (in both written and verbal modes) on your ability to relate to and engage in a meaningful manner with clients and colleagues.
Apply advanced verbal & written communication skills with a range of communication partners in different environments.
Critically review key components of the Professional Standards and Code of Ethics for speech pathologists in Australia.
Justify evidence-based practice and explain its role for speech pathology practice
Critically review client behaviours and professional activities in a variety of service contexts and document these accurately.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE 3
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will attend 27 days of clinic in a near-entry adult or paediatric setting. This may be within the La Trobe Clinical Teaching Building or at an external facility. You will work to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous placements, applying these more independently as the subject progresses with the aim of being 'near entry level' on the COMPASS assessment to pass the subject: i.e. capability rated at near-entry level in most competency units, although some competencies may still be moving from intermediate towards entry level during this placement. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply creativity and initiative to most new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams with minimal support and managing workload with a high level of autonomy and accountability.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills and knowledge of both typical and pathological function with minimal support
Reflect critically on own performance with minimal support to develop a professional identity and commitment to lifelong learning and actively pursue recent developments in speech pathology.

Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues with minimal support to implement, evaluate and document intervention that is effective and appropriate to the client and professional setting.

Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention with moderate support in complex situations.

Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying established theories to develop diagnostic and prognostic conclusions about clients, communicating this information effectively to clients and colleagues with support in complex situations

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE 4
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete 27 days of clinic, in an entry-level adult or paediatric setting . This may be within the La Trobe Clinical Teaching Building or at an external facility. You will continue to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous three semesters, applying these more independently as the subject progresses, with the aim of achieving entry level on the COMPASS® assessment by the end of the subject. You will continue to develop your clinical management skills further and develop an understanding of, and participate in, the broader range of roles and activities of a speech pathologist in a working week. You will monitor your progress in obtaining the desired level of professional competency and devise a plan of action to address competency gaps. You will complete your professional competency portfolios (PCPs) with the conclusion of your placement. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying established theories to develop diagnostic and prognostic conclusions about clients, communicating this information effectively to clients and colleagues
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills and knowledge of both typical and pathological function.

Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention with support in situations where complex and/or unfamiliar factors are present.

Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention that is effective and appropriate to the client and professional setting.

Apply creativity and initiative to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams and managing workload with a high level of autonomy and accountability.
Reflect critically on own performance to develop a professional identity and commitment to life long learning and actively pursue recent developments in speech pathology.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE 2
syllabus_overview: You will begin to apply your theoretical knowledge to clients and their close others during placements, building on the skills developed in HCS5001 and supplementing learning in HCS4ACS, HCS5005 and HCS5006. You will undertake both an adult and paediatric placement within the teaching period. Each placement will consist of two days of onsite learning comprising of workshops and simulations followed by nine-days over three-week practice placements based in the clinical teaching building or with external industry partners. The pass criteria for this subject is Intermediate-level across a range of clinical competencies. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention with a moderate level of support
Investigate communication and swallowing by applying cognitive, communicative and observational skills and demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.
Complete elements of speech, language and swallowing assessments, analyse and interpret assessment data with a moderate level of support, applying theory to develop clinical hypotheses.
Incorporate theory and clinical observations into planning and delivery of ethically sound, evidence based intervention with a moderate level of support.
Manage professional workload, including coordinating and collaborating with clients and colleagues, with increasing autonomy and accountability through the placement
Reflect critically on own performance with some support, responding to feedback and actively seeking to increase knowledge base and skillset in speech pathology practice.

title: LIFESPAN COMMUNICATION AND SWALLOWING 3
syllabus_overview: You will complete weekly clinical cases delivered within a case-based learning framework. Building on learning from the subject Lifespan Communication and Swallowing 1, you will use assessment information, adult client observation and principles of evidence- based practice to formulate assessment plans and intervention strategies. You are required to provide rationales for clinical decision- making and to demonstrate knowledge of the professional role of a speech pathologist in a team. The impact of social and cultural issues on service provision is considered.
learning_outcomes: Predict the possible ethical, social and environmental implications of speech pathology assessments and interventions.
Justify the selection and application of appropriate speech pathology assessment tools, techniques and methods using best available evidence.
Justify the selection and application of appropriate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods using best available evidence.
Critically evaluate available evidence to develop adult client- centered assessment and intervention plans
Evaluate and report the outcomes of speech pathology assessments and interventions.

Critically examine the possible causes of communication or swallowing impairment, and how these impairments affect adult clients and significant others in regard to wellbeing, activity and participation.

title: LIFESPAN COMMUNICATION AND SWALLOWING 2
syllabus_overview: You will complete weekly clinical cases delivered within a case-based learning framework. Building on learning from the subject Lifespan Communication and Swallowing 1, you will use assessment information, client observation and principles of evidence- based practice to formulate paediatric assessment plans and intervention strategies. You are required to provide rationales for clinical decision- making and to demonstrate knowledge of the professional role of a speech pathologist in a team. The impact of social and cultural issues on service provision is considered.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the possible causes of communication or swallowing impairment, and how these impairments affect paediatric clients and significant others in regard to wellbeing, activity and participation.
Critically evaluate available evidence to develop paediatric client- centered assessment and intervention plans
Predict the possible ethical, social and environmental implications of speech pathology assessments and interventions.
Evaluate and report the outcomes of speech pathology assessments and interventions.
Justify the selection and application of appropriate speech pathology assessment tools, techniques and methods using best available evidence.
Justify the selection and application of appropriate speech pathology intervention tools, techniques and methods using best available evidence.

title: WORKPLACE PREPARATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will evaluate your personal and professional development over the Master of Speech Pathology course. You will analyse and critically appraise workplace environments and evaluate evidence based strategies for maintaining self-care and wellbeing in the workplace. Identifying new and emerging opportunities for speech pathology practice in contemporary society, and appraising these opportunities to make informed decisions about their career will also be explored. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate workplace governance structures and clients’ and speech pathologists’ rights and responsibilities within speech pathology workplace environments
Apply accurate, accessible communication to effectively relate complex information regarding speech pathology assessments, intervention plans and outcomes to clients
Accurately analyse and integrate data from speech pathology assessments and apply clinical reasoning skills based on theory and all client factors to form a diagnosis and intervention plan
Critique the current status of and emerging opportunities for innovation in diverse environments within contemporary society
Critically appraise personal strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats to support future career growth and design a plan to support personal and professional wellbeing throughout a career

title: ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION IN SPEECH PATHOLOGY CLINIC
syllabus_overview: You will begin to apply your theoretical knowledge to clients and their carers during placements, building on the skills developed in HCS4ISP and supplementing learning in HCS4ACS and HCS5AIA. You will undertake both an adult and paediatric placement. The adult and paediatric placements occur simultaneously through two blocks of Semester 2. For your adult experience you will undertake a 6-week placement consisting of four days of onsite learning comprising workshops and simulations and two days practice placement with an external partner agency (Hybrid Model). The clinical component will be offered in community settings in Melbourne. For your paediatric experience you will undertake a 9-week placement consisting of 1 session of clinic per week. The paediatric clinical experience will be offered at Latrobe Communication Clinic (La Trobe University), Bundoora. The pass criteria for this subject is Novice-level across a range of clinical competencies. In addition to placements, you are required to attend the subject orientation workshop (week 29) and practice placement debrief and reflective practice workshop (week48). You will also complete several hurdle assessments including pre-placement online learning modules and commencement of your Professional Competency Portfolio (PCP) on PebblePad. Students may be required to attend placement on a Saturday
learning_outcomes: Complete elements of speech, language and swallowing assessments, analyse and interpret assessment data with support, applying theory to develop clinical hypotheses.
Investigate communication and swallowing by applying cognitive, communicative and observational skills and demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.
Communicate effectively with clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention with a high level of support.
Manage professional workload with increasing autonomy and accountability through the placement
Reflect critically on own performance, responding to feedback and actively seeking to increase knowledge base and skillset in speech pathology practice.
Incorporate theory and clinical observations into planning and delivery of ethically sound, evidence based intervention with maximal support.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF EVIDENCE IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on students' knowledge of evidence based practice theory and skills in searching for and critiquing research evidence and then applies this knowledge to different kinds of evidence and practice contexts. Students will learn how to collaborate and effectively communicate within teams to prioritise actions and manage risks. They will learn how to search and critically evaluate the best available research evidence presented in clinical practice guidelines. They will also synthesise knowledge resources to determine the best available evidence. They will generate ideas and develop new resources that address complex problems in practice settings. This subject addresses La Trobe's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Essential. Innovation and Entrepreneurship entails developing the ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas, taking calculated risks and creating change to achieve ambitions - now and in the future.
learning_outcomes: Communicate research evidence clearly to clients and colleagues to justify rationale for clinical decisions that meet individual client needs.
Critically appraise evidence from a range of traditional and alternative sources.
Apply the principles and processes of evidence-based practice to contexts.
Formulate answerable practice-related questions and acquire relevant evidence to address the questions.
Generate a range of strategies to facilitate the implementation of the best available research evidence into practice.

title: ADVANCED SEMINARS IN SPEECH PATHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject prepares you for the continual evolution of speech pathology practice. Building on your previous learning you will extend, apply and adapt your knowledge of speech pathology assessment, intervention and management of communication and swallowing disorders by exploring advanced and emerging areas of speech pathology practice. In this subject, you will participate in a series of compulsory seminars and workshops facilitated by academic and professional leaders in the field. You will demonstrate your knowledge of the Speech Pathology Australia Professional Standards, reflection on First Nations Health and cultural sensitivity and undertake a clinical oral VIVA.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate areas of specialised speech pathology practice in a range of service contexts and in line with Speech Pathology Australia Professional Standards.

Integrate contemporary gender, cultural and linguistic frameworks to formulate assessment and management of communication and swallowing disorders experienced by people from diverse populations across the lifespan.
Demonstrate Entry-Level competency in the area of paediatric feeding (entry-level is defined by Speech Pathology Australia's Competency Based Occupation Standards framework).

Integrate current best practice models and knowledges to inform culturally responsive ways for Entry-Level speech pathologists to collaborate with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and communities to provide safe and equitable speech pathology services.

title: CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EVIDENCE
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on students' knowledge of evidence based practice theory and skills in searching for and critiquing research evidence and then applies this knowledge to different kinds of evidence and practice contexts. Students will learn how to collaborate and effectively communicate within teams to prioritise actions and manage risks. They will learn how to search and critically evaluate the best available research evidence presented in clinical practice guidelines. They will also synthesise knowledge resources to determine the best available evidence. They will generate ideas and develop new resources that address complex problems in practice settings. This subject addresses La Trobe's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Essential. Innovation and Entrepreneurship entails developing the ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas, taking calculated risks and creating change to achieve ambitions - now and in the future.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise and qualitative research findings.
Interpret and apply findings of research on best practice
Evaluate clinical practice guidelines recommendations in the context of patient experience studies.
Formulate and implement complex systematic literature searches to locate clinical practice guidelines.
Appraise clinical practice guidelines based on best available evidence.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: You will attend 10 days of placement in an adult or paediatric setting. This may be at the La Trobe Communication Clinic or at an external partner agency facility. The placement will usually take place 2 days per week over 5 weeks. You will begin to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous two semesters (HCS4ISP and HCS5AIB), applying these more independently as the placement progresses. You will develop clinical skills related to particular work settings and further develop your clinical management skills. You are expected to reach ‘intermediate level’ on the COMPASS® assessment by the end of the placement. In addition to clinical placement, you will need to complete all subject related assessment tasks, including developing at least three (3) personal learning goals upon commencing your clinical placement, a 1000-word reflection following your placement and uploading your placement evidence to your Professional Competency Portfolio (PCP), to pass the subject. You are required to attend the subject orientation workshop (week 4) and clinical placement debrief and counselling workshops (week 12). Students may be required to attend placement on a Saturday
learning_outcomes: Incorporate complex information and professional decisions into planning and delivering ethically sound, evidence-based intervention
Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention with a moderate level of support

Begin to apply creativity and initiative to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams and managing workload with increasing autonomy and accountability through the placement
Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying theory to develop some diagnostic and prognostic hypotheses about clients
Demonstrate a commitment to lifelong learning, by reflecting critically on own performance and actively seeking to increase knowledge base and skillset in speech pathology practice
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing by applying cognitive, communicative and observational skills and demonstrating knowledge of both typical and pathological function.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE D
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete 30 days of clinic, in either an adult and/or paediatric setting, usually at an external facility. You will continue to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous three semesters, applying these more independently as the subject progresses, with the aim of achieving entry level on the COMPASS® assessment by the end of the subject. You will develop setting specific clinical skills and develop your clinical management skills further. Through block placements, you will develop an understanding of, and participate in, the broader range of roles and activities of a speech pathologist in a working week. You will monitor your progress in obtaining the desired level of professional competency and devise a plan of action to address competency gaps. You will complete your professional competency portfolios (PCPs) with the conclusion of your final placement. There is a reflection piece of work with a focus on teamwork attached to this subject which is submitted with the portfolio. You will also complete two clinical practicum examinations. All students must attend an orientation/reflection workshop in week 28.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying established theories to develop diagnostic and prognostic conclusions about clients, communicating this information effectively to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention.

Apply creativity and initiative to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams and managing workload with a high level of autonomy and accountability.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills and knowledge of both typical and pathological function.

Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention that is effective and appropriate to the client and professional setting.
Reflect critically on own performance to develop a professional identity and commitment to life long learning and actively pursue recent developments in speech pathology.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will attend 27 days of clinic in an adult or paediatric setting. This may be at the La Trobe Communication Clinic or at a community based facility. You will work to refine the clinical skills acquired over the previous placements, applying these more independently as the subject progresses with the aim of being 'near entry level' on the COMPASS assessment to pass the subject: i.e. capability rated at entry level in most competency units, although some competencies may still be moving from intermediate towards entry level during this placement. Through block placements you will develop an understanding of and participate in the broader range of roles and activities of a speech pathologist across a working week.
learning_outcomes: Apply creativity and initiative to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams and managing workload with a high level of autonomy and accountability.
Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills and knowledge of both typical and pathological function

Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention that is effective and appropriate to the client and professional setting.

Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying established theories to develop diagnostic and prognostic conclusions about clients, communicating this information effectively to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Reflect critically on own performance to develop a professional identity and commitment to lifelong learning and actively pursue recent developments in speech pathology.

title: SPEECH PATHOLOGY PRACTICE E
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will attend 10 days of clinic in an adult or a paediatric setting, at La Trobe's Communication Clinic or an external facility. This placement may offer you an experience of a specific nature e.g. voice clinic, intensive fluency , paediatric feeding clinic, but it is not exclusively a specialist placement. This may take the form of one day per week over 10 weeks, or consist of a more intensive and/or varied period (e.g. intensive fluency program). You will continue to refine clinical skills, with the aim of achieving entry level on the COMPASS® assessment. In addition to placement, , students will complete a clinical practicum exam and an OSCE exam assessed at entry level.
learning_outcomes: Critically investigate and synthesise complex information and justify professional decisions to plan and deliver ethically sound, evidence-based intervention.
Investigate clients' communication and/or swallowing using high level cognitive, communicative and observational skills and knowledge of both typical and pathological function.

Apply creativity and initiative to new situations, including consulting, coordinating and collaborating with professional and research groups, communicating effectively in teams and managing workload with a high level of autonomy and accountability.

Apply theoretical knowledge and communicate effectively with a range of clients and colleagues to implement, evaluate and document intervention that is effective and appropriate to the client and professional setting.

Analyse and interpret assessment data, applying established theories to develop diagnostic and prognostic conclusions about clients, communicating this information effectively to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Reflect critically on own performance to develop a professional identity and commitment to life long learning and actively pursue recent developments in speech pathology.

title: THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION AND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject students complete clinical cases delivered in a problem-based learning framework. Building on knowledge of assessment for intervention and management for clients with impairments of communication and swallowing, students use assessment information, clinical experience, client observation and principles of evidence-based practice to formulate intervention and management strategies. Students are required to provide detailed rationales for clinical decision-making and to demonstrate knowledge of the professional role of speech pathologists from a broad range of contexts, from the point of view of the client, their family and their environment. The impact of management across the lifespan is considered. Students will also apply their knowledge of a variety of service delivery options to ensure the best outcome for their clients.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate client progress during speech pathology interventions for a range of clients with varying needs.
Work effectively and responsibly as a member of a team, adapting your role and performance as required, in a variety of professional and community contexts.
Critically reflect on your role as a speech pathologist considering the ethical, social and environmental implications of your intervention and as a member of a multidisciplinary team.
Justify and implement a range of appropriate speech pathology management strategies, for clients with complex needs, based on best research evidence.

title: RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to essential skills needed to understand health research and evidence-based practice. You will develop a basic understanding of descriptive and inferential statistics, assessment of research outcomes and the strengths and limitations of key research designs and contemporary challenges of research in human nutrition. The focus is on the types of research that answer questions about the effectiveness of interventions, and about human experience and meaning and being able to interpret these.
learning_outcomes: Explain the different study designs including strengths and weaknesses, used in health scientific literature and NHMRC levels of evidence.
Apply an evidence-based approach to evaluate health-related challenges and problem solving in the contemporary world.
Recognise and describe the different research paradigms and methodologies that informs evidence based practice.
Interpret selected research outcomes and basic statistics from peer-reviewed journal articles, and other forms of evidence-based material.
Interpret and summarise key design elements of peer reviewed journal articles and other forms of evidence based material to communicate common research and statistical terminology.

title: INTEGRATING EVIDENCE INTO PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain knowledge and skills that are needed to: develop answerable practice-related questions; develop and implement complex and comprehensive database searches to acquire and apply evidence that is relevant to practice related questions; appraise the strength of evidence acquired and reflect on your own performance in applying the answer to practice. During the course of this learning, you will begin to develop an understanding of research processes and, thereby, develop 'research literacy' as an essential tool for health practice and for the utilisation of research evidence in practice. Relevant aspects of research methods are introduced, and you will acquire knowledge relating to the selection and use of measures and/or tests that are used in research and in practice in your discipline.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret different types of data, commonly generated in nutrition science research, using appropriate methods and following ethical research principals.
Acquire evidence relevant to practice by developing and implementing complex and comprehensive search strategies applicable to databases and other repositories of evidence.
Appraise scientific evidence that underpins nutrition science research and collaborate to reach a group decision on study quality.
Integrate evidence with your discipline knowledge with consideration given to the practice context.
Ask, and develop and refine, relevant and answerable practice-related questions using a structured approach.

title: INTRODUCTION TO HEALTH CLASSIFICATION A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an introductory working knowledge of the fundamental conventions and rules for classification of diseases and health interventions using the current Australian version of the World Health Organization's International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10-AM), the Australian Classification for Health Interventions (ACHI) and the Australian Coding Standards (ACS). You will develop an understanding of the complexities of the classification process. You will develop skills in medical record abstraction and interpretation to support the application of health classification systems. You will develop competency in classificatory practice within the parameters of expected industry timeframes and levels of accuracy. You will gain knowledge in diagnostic, therapeutic and radiological techniques, and drug therapy. Only a Pass or Fail is awarded. A Pass will reflect a grade 75% or greater. This is in line with industry standards and expectations This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for first-year undergraduate students, who are enrolled in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Apply the Australian Coding Standards to accurately code inpatient episodes of care.
Identify and abstract from the medical record the appropriate conditions, diagnoses and interventions required for the classification process.
Examine the medical record to identify and further clarify diagnoses and interventions.
Demonstrate an understanding of the structures and basic principles of the health classification systems, ICD-10-AM, ACHI and ACS, used in Australian hospitals.
Apply the standards and conventions of health classification within a time frame that aligns with industry expectations.

title: INTRODUCTION TO DATA ANALYTICS IN HEALTHCARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to quantitative statistics, qualitative coding and the role of health data analytics in healthcare organisations and public health research. Key emphases include understanding the importance of healthcare data as an asset, identifying and applying the key elements of the data capture and analysis process in key research methodologies, along with effective presentation, communication and dissemination of findings beyond peer review publications. You will also investigate the role of health data analytics in quality and performance indicators. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for first-year undergraduate students.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply appropriate data analytic tools and techniques in quantitative and qualitative research.
Analyse the role of data analytics in healthcare quality and performance indicators.
Explain and demonstrate the importance of health data within healthcare organisations and public health research.
Investigate and apply techniques for the collection, cleaning, analysis, reporting, application and governance of health data.
Demonstrate effective communication and dissemination of health data.

title: MANAGEMENT OF HEALTH INFORMATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to types, uses and applications, of personal and aggregate health data and other information within Australian healthcare agencies. Administrative and clinical systems used for capturing health information on individual patients and clients will be examined. Clinical recording methodologies, health information standards and decision support systems are introduced. The uses of aggregate data are studied in relation to information systems; health information flow; and health data quality and integrity. Electronic and manual systems for health record identification, filing, and tracking are discussed. Case studies, enquiries, and professional placements are used to apply critical theories to health applications. You will integrate theory and practice by undertaking a five-day professional practice placement in the Health Information Service of a healthcare agency to which you are assigned. Australian based hospital on-site placements are a core requirement for all students regardless of the instance (blended or online) in which you are enrolled. To meet professional competency requirements students must pass both the professional placement and academic components of the subject.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role(s) of Health Information Managers in the management of a Health Information Service.
Review the operational processes of records management and patient information systems.

Demonstrate high professional ethical standards, participate in multidisciplinary team environments, and demonstrate awareness of the social and ethical implications of professional and personal activities.
Explain the movement of a patient and their record throughout the health service and analyse the flow of health data from collection (at point-of-care) to post discharge.
Use academic and health industry resources to critically examine and communicate health topics.
Apply appropriate health information standards and understanding of key elements of administrative and clinical information systems to describe individual clinical data.

Use health information as a dynamic and strategic resource competently by summarising the content, format, and uses of clinical information for patient care, with a particular focus on a client’s hospital record.

title: HEALTHCARE IN AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: This subject will allow you to develop an understanding of professional healthcare delivery in Australia. Areas of professional healthcare delivery that will be examined include; population health and prevention, general practice and community health; emergency health services and hospital care; mental health, rehabilitation and palliative care. You will review and analyse the overall health of Australia's population and investigate the diverse roles of a range of health professionals in the delivery of healthcare. You will develop critical reasoning skills through relevant case scenarios which introduce enquiry-based learning and teamwork. This subject will support the development of foundation academic skills and information literacy required for successful university study. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for first-year undergraduate students.
learning_outcomes: Examine the human experience of health, illness and disability by navigating through healthcare in Australia.
Effectively use academic resources to develop plans for enquiry and independent learning.
Identify and explain the key health benefits and challenges facing modern Australians from a population health perspective.
Work collaboratively to analyse and solve case scenarios using enquiry-based learning.
Analyse the roles of a range of health professionals in the delivery of Australian healthcare.

title: MEDICAL TERMINOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the terminology, diseases, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures relating to each body system as well as to terms used in specialist areas of medicine, surgery, pathology, imaging, nursing and allied health. You will learn to interpret simple medical documentation. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for first-year undergraduate students.
learning_outcomes: Define the meaning of medical and anatomical words, acronyms and abbreviations used in describing diagnostic, procedural and disease processes.
Analyse human pathophysiology, procedures and treatment in recorded medical documentation.
Apply knowledge of medical word part definitions and human structure and function to correctly build and use medical terms in clinical settings.
Demonstrate speaking and spelling skills in the language/vocabulary of medicine.
Collaboratively prepare and evaluate medical documentation utilised in clinical settings.

title: UNDERSTANDING DIGITAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the role of information and communication technologies (ICT) in the delivery of healthcare. Beginning with an investigation of what is "digital health", you will become familiar with the most common digital technologies utilised by healthcare professionals. The benefits and challenges surrounding the introduction of digital health for both health professionals and consumers will be explored. The common enablers of, and barriers to, adoption will be identified. You will research the technological, clinical, social, legal, and ethical impacts of the digitisation of health care. Past successes and failures, and future trends in digital health, will be explored along with the international and national drivers for a digital health strategy.
learning_outcomes: Explore the impact of digital health on the experience of health consumers.
Describe the current national and international digital landscape in healthcare.
Identify the implications of digitising health for health professionals working in the Australian Healthcare System, including technologies currently in use.
Identify the technological, clinical, social, legal, and ethical impacts of the digitisation of health care.

title: HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEMS ANALYSIS AND DESIGN
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to the broad concepts of health data and system development lifecycle (SDLC) and the purpose, scope, design and functionalities of health information systems. You will explore the theoretical concepts behind systems planning, analysis, design, implementation, evaluation, support and maintenance of the systems development lifecycle including issues that impact systems, data and information security. Through your assessments, you will demonstrate technical skills in systems planning, analysis and design phases of the SDLC by creating user stories and data flow diagrams as well as evaluating systems design. You will develop an understanding of how health professionals interact with the health information systems development lifecycle.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse the professional attributes, skills and knowledge of the Business/System analyst and Health Professionals.
Analyse the elements of the health systems development lifecycles.
Apply user interface design principles to create and evaluate screen designs for health information systems in teams.
Compare and contrast systems relevant to health information.
Apply system, data and process modelling rules.

title: HEALTH INFORMATION GOVERNANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore governance functions in the health sector, including accountability, risk management, accreditation, and quality and safety management, with a focus on health information and supporting technologies within system and organisational contexts. You will develop an understanding of how health information is managed at multiple levels to support quality of care and service delivery. This includes examining individual patient records as evidence of care, aggregated data to measure and evaluate healthcare processes and outcomes, clinical documentation for diagnostic and therapeutic decisions, and coded data used to monitor and improve patient safety.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the contemporary Australian landscape in relation to health-related accreditation, healthcare quality and safety.
Review how governance principles are applied across corporate, clinical, health information, and health information systems contexts.
Apply (practical) managerial and statistical tools and methods to support effective health information management.
Critically analyse theoretical models and standard practices related to governance, including accountability, risk management, and quality and safety functions (individually and in teams).

title: HEALTH CLASSIFICATION C
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop higher level classification skills to a level of competency that qualifies you professionally, as a workforce entry-level clinical/medical coder. You will further develop your working knowledge of medical science and terminology and be introduced to common clinical documentation deficiencies and practice clinical documentation improvement skills. You will be introduced to the health classification-financial relationship within the context of Activity Based Funding and the National Funding Model and develop a deeper understanding of the classification system by examining Diagnostic-Related Group (DRG) and National Weighted Activity Unit (NWAU) assignment. You will have exposure to State and Territory specific guidelines relevant to admitted care data items, which can impact on coding. This subject is graded only as a Pass (P) or Fail (F). A mark of 75% or greater is required to achieve a Pass grade in line with industry standards and expectations. Recommended for students who have completed all first-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Analyse clinical information to inform clinical documentation improvement.
Apply Australian Coding Standards, Conventions and ratified advice accurately in health classification practice at an intermediate level.
Work collaboratively in internal quality control practices for health classification.
Apply Australian Coding Standards, Conventions and ratified advice at a level of expertise and within timeframes that align with industry expectations.
Demonstrate knowledge of health classification-financial relationship through accurate assignment of Diagnostic-Related Group (DRG) and National Weighted Activity Unit (NWAU).

title: HEALTH CLASSIFICATION B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop your competence and confidence in the use of the current edition of the Australian-Modified version of the World Health Organization's International Classification of Diseases, the Australian Classification of Health Interventions, and the Australian Coding Standards for accurate assignment of codes in a timely manner. You will gain familiarity in searching for and applying ratified coding advice to your code assignment. You will develop your working knowledge of medical science and terminology and be introduced to common clinical documentation deficiencies and methods for improvement. This subject is graded as a Pass (P) or Fail (F). A mark of 75% or greater is required to achieve a Pass grade in line with industry standards and expectations. Recommended for students who have completed all first-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Apply Australian Coding Standards, Conventions and ratified advice accurately in health classification practice at an intermediate level.
Analyse clinical information to inform clinical documentation improvement.
Apply internal quality control practices for health classification.
Apply Australian Coding Standards, Conventions and ratified advice at a level of expertise and within timeframes that align with industry expectations.

title: HOSPITAL PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will undertake theoretical studies at the University, and a three-week (equivalent) supervised, professional practice placement in the Health Information Service of an allocated, regional healthcare facility in Australia. You will achieve practice competencies and reinforce professional discipline knowledge. You will undertake key functions on placement to gain understanding of the management, informatics, data analysis, and clinical classificatory roles of hospital health information managers. Prior to placement, you are introduced to the functional components of a Health Information Service and the responsibilities of Health Information Managers in relation to the management of health records, building on the knowledge gained in HIM1003 and developing skills in a related health business communication genre. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours, this means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for second-year undergraduate students who have completed all first-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management. Hospital on-site placements are a core requirement for all students regardless of the instance (blended or online) in which you are enrolled. To meet professional competency requirements students must pass both the professional placement and academic components of the subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate: i. disease and procedure classification skills, using patient records; and ii. a practical understanding of casemix-based systems with particular regard to DRG assignment.
Review and practice clinical governance and quality management activities (i.e., auditing) of the Health Information Service.

Compare the organisational structure and functions of Health Information Services and demonstrate how these affect the role of the health information manager, information systems, policies and procedures, and day-to-day staff and departmental management.

Explain the capture, use, and reporting of clinical information applied to support patient/client care, and associated privacy issues and the operational processes of health records management and patient/client information systems.

Maintain high professional ethical standards and demonstrate awareness of the social and ethical implications of professional and personal activities, skills in health business communication genre, and ability to work in multidisciplinary team environments, necessary for the management of a Health Information Service.

title: HEALTH DATA, FUNDING AND STATISTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop a specialist working knowledge of health data standards; health data collections; government, insurance and other sectoral health data reporting requirements, and the relationship between these and health service measurement and financing. Models of Activity-Based Funding, including case mix-based systems, and their underpinning reporting and analysis requirements are studied. The pivotal role of the Health Information Manager within all of these arrangements is addressed. You will develop an understanding of the policy and funding frameworks for public and private health services and supporting clinical costing and modelling methods. You will develop competency in health data analytics, and analysis and reporting of hospital and health service utilisation statistics and published health data. Case studies inform your learning of these concepts and your analyses of morbidity, mortality, clinical, productivity and health service data. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for second-year undergraduate students, and for students who have completed all first-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to analyse and evaluate the uses of administrative health data collections by state, territory and national health authorities, health service planners, health service managers and researchers.
Demonstrate well-developed skills in applying the principles and standards related to health data to the processes of collection, reporting and verification for administrative health data.
Analyse and report health data underpinned by broad and coherent knowledge of models of health service and care funding, including Activity Based Funding and casemix-based approaches.
Compute and present hospital and health service utilisation statistics and analyse published health activity and service-related data.

title: HEALTH DATABASE FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn design, management, extraction, integration, and reporting of health data. You will gain practical skills in developing and maintaining fully relational health databases using national health data standards and models. Theoretical and logical principles of health database and system administration will be introduced, including entity-relationship diagrams, normalisation, meta-data and an introduction to SQL for relational database queries and reporting. Specialised tools for visualisation of health data sets will also be taught.
learning_outcomes: Investigate and apply database security principles and processes and data quality improvement activities.
Implement basic database design principles (eg. modelling techniques such as entity-relationship diagrams) to design and construct a relational database.
Apply principles of effective data visualisation and use them to develop reports and dashboards.
Apply national health data standards and models for data storage design.
Apply structure query language (SQL) to manipulate and extract clinical and administrative health data to improve health information analysis and reporting.

title: ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION OF HEALTH DATA
syllabus_overview: In this subject you analyse, interpret and use coded and non-coded health data beyond the treatment and disease/operation classification stages. Key emphases include the identification, critical evaluation and objective uses of health data in epidemiological and clinical research; health data and statistics applications in health care management and clinical decision-making; speciality performance indicators; identification and resolution of regulatory, ethical and management issues surrounding registries, health databases and clinical trials; and evaluating the quality , integrity and comparability of coded data and their statistical outcomes. You will become competent in health data analytics through analysing, critiquing, applying and advising upon health data in clinical, epidemiological, and healthcare management environments, and in the context of state and national population health monitoring. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for third-year undergraduate students, and for students who have completed all first and second-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to complete a research proposal ethics application.

Appraise scientific literature, research designs, and techniques for the collection, analysis, reporting, applications and evaluation of health data and information beyond the patient/client treatment and disease and operation classification stages.
Evaluate and report on health data for clinical and related decision-making through the application of data quality and data integrity frameworks.
Evaluate key data quality issues, and management protocols and functions, in specialised clinical and epidemiological settings

Examine the principles and processes of establishing, managing and analysing data in specialised clinical and epidemiological databases and registries, including the legislative, privacy and ethics-related requirements.

Analyse the quality of coded and other administrative data and their statistical outcomes in a clinical or observational epidemiological study and provide expert advice to clinicians and researchers on this data.

title: APPLIED HEALTH CLASSIFICATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will focus on further developing your competence and confidence in the use of the current edition of the Australian-Modified version of the World Health Organization's International Classification of Diseases, the Australian Classification of Health Interventions, and the Australian Coding Standards for accurate assignment of codes in a timely manner. You will gain experience in coding from a range of medical record formats and specialties in coding practicums hosted by industry experts. You will develop a deeper understanding of the national funding model and the important role that internal and external clinical coding auditing plays in health classification quality assurance. Topic areas include audit quality tools, record selection and delivery of coding education. You will achieve competencies in clinical coding auditing for internal data quality control and coding practice management. Pass grade is 50%. Assessment hurdle that students must pass the final online exam with a grade of 50% or more. Placements are expected to be face-to-face unless a suitable location cannot be found and then they may be online.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical coding auditor and clinical documentation improvement specialist skills in communicating with stakeholders for coding quality assurance.
Effectively apply health classification skills in medical record interpretation and clinical abstraction within a timeframe that aligns with health industry expectations.
Identify and analyse coding errors and select records for audit using knowledge of the classification system and funding model.
Apply internal clinical coding auditing processes to identify factors that impact upon the quality and reliability of coded data.

title: HEALTH INFORMATION MANAGEMENT PROJECT PROFESSIONAL PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will further develop your health information practice knowledge and skills through engagement in supervised professional practice placements in healthcare and related agencies across the whole-of-health. The purpose of the subject is to enable you to apply theoretical knowledge to practice, and to consolidate learning from previous professional practice placements. You will undertake 240 hours of placement and complete a range of academic assessments. Regular contact with University supervisors is maintained during placements via telephone, email and on-site visits. As this is a course capstone placement subject, it must be completed by all students. No advanced standing is available. To meet professional competency requirements students must pass both the professional placement and academic components of the subject. Recommended for students who have completed all first- and second-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on current theory and practice and compare and contrast processes across health care agencies translating knowledge into new contexts and demonstrate a commitment to life-long learning.
Extract and analyse health data (which may include the allocation of ICD-10-AM codes according to state and national protocols).

Demonstrate application of health information management skills through supervised engagement in activities which build upon academic studies and previous placement and experiences, including the ability to work independently, professionally, and ethically.
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of health information at agency level, and its collection and applications for clinical and other purposes.

Demonstrate skills in project and time management, including development and achievement of objectives, effective participation in multidisciplinary team environments and high-level communication using a wide range of mediums.

title: SOCIO-TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you learn theories and techniques, including approaches to problem-solving, for managing a Health Information Service (HIS). Areas of focus include: professional issues; health information strategic planning; staffing practices including recruitment, training, performance appraisal and management; staff motivation and management; departmental financial and budgetary management; workplace legislation specific to the HIS's human and operational resources; sociotechnical issues; and the strategic management of change brought about by health information and communications technologies. This subject draws together many components of the course, giving you the opportunity to synthesise critical and emerging theory in the contexts of health technological and policy developments, and to consolidate your HIS and health information management knowledge. You will also explore some theory behind organisational behaviour to facilitate the development of leadership skills providing both vision and direction for the service and team being managed.
learning_outcomes: Strategically plan and problem solve managerial, budgetary, staffing, safety and equity and negotiation functions specific to Health Information Services and health information management workplaces.

Formulate evidence-based approaches to the strategic management of health information-related workplace change brought about by emerging technological, socio-technical, legislative, policy, and health information science developments.
Communicate effectively and confidently in teams or individually when presenting and negotiating on Health Information Service-related matters.
Apply theoretical approaches to the management of staff in patient and client health information management environments through analysis and evaluation of simulated case scenarios.
Evaluate theories of organisational behaviour and their application in the real world context

title: HEALTH SYSTEMS IMPLEMENTATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of project management frameworks and associated project management skills in health information systems and services. You will develop a health information-related project concept and learn how to plan for implementation and evaluation, using project management knowledge and simple tools such as a Gantt Chart template available in Microsoft Excel. You will also learn about the importance of stakeholder engagement, project probity, the role of procurement (purchasing), the tender process and contracts in public health. This subject also contextualises project management practice in a health environment where emerging technologies, changeable work conditions and business operations are influenced by political, socioeconomic and clinical forces. Recommended for students who have completed all first and second-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in the development of specifications and requirements for health technology and service-related contracts, tendering and procuring practices and health service agreements.

Assess new health information system or service implementations and identify opportunities for improvement and change.

title: ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD TECHNOLOGIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply principles of health systems analysis and design to examine the technical requirements and processes involved in implementing electronic health records (EHRs). Using an enquiry-based learning approach, you will develop an in-depth understanding of design, structural, and operational considerations, (including EHR architectures, implementation and adoption strategies, interoperability, privacy and security, person and provider identification, clinical terminologies, clinical decision support systems, audit trails, and health data linkage.) This subject is recommended for students who have completed all first- and second-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the evolution of current policy related to the electronic health record (EHR) and the importance of various types of health information underpinning the EHR (working effectively in teams).
Analyse the design and functionality of clinical decision support systems within EHR environments.

Apply EHR standards, architectures and structures in health service implementations, including terminologies, structures, communications, privacy, and security to support information system integration in healthcare.
Apply best practice strategies and methodologies to support effective implementation and adoption of electronic medical records.
Analyse and apply data linkage and integration methods to effectively connect healthcare datasets.

title: ETHICS AND LAW OF HEALTH INFORMATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop a working knowledge of health information professional responsibilities concerning ethical, legal, compliance, and governance obligations in the computing field and healthcare information industry. These include the ethical and legal frameworks underpinning the creation, collection, reporting, management and uses of health data, related documents, systems, and technologies. Key topics include: privacy; security; confidentiality; access; e-health; ownership; data linkage; and information and documentation issues surrounding biomedical and health technologies and clinical practice. Students develop ethical and legal understandings of: electronic and paper-based health records; managing the organisation-wide privacy function; information systems and services; and the legal implications and responsibilities inherent in health information management work. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for third-year undergraduate students, and for students who have completed all first- and second-year subjects in the Bachelor of Health Information Management.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a practical working knowledge of legislative requirements surrounding the collection, management, and reporting of health information at all levels of the healthcare system.

Work collaboratively to identify contemporary issues and health information management professional responsibilities for ethical and legal governance of health information and systems in the contexts of existing and emerging technologies.
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the practical requirements of the professional Code of Ethics for practising Health Information Managers and Clinical/Medical Coders.
Apply key bioethical theories and principles to health information and its management, and to health/clinical informatics and related ICT health information practice.

Demonstrate an understanding of Health Information Managers' professional responsibilities for the proper governance and use of health data, information and systems throughout the healthcare system in the contexts of custody, confidentiality and privacy.

title: REVIEW AND ANALYSIS OF HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEMS DESIGN
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will review and analyse broad concepts of health data and the system development lifecycle and the purpose, scope, design and functionalities of health information systems. You will appraise various stages of the systems development and health data lifecyles including issues that impact systems, data and information security. Through your assessments, you will critically analyse healthcare cybersecurity frameworks, create user stories and data flow diagrams, and theoretically evaluate systems design. Having completed this subject, you will be able to differentiate between the various roles and positioning of health professionals within the health information systems development and health data lifecycle.
learning_outcomes: Identify the weaknesses and strengths in health information system features using interface design and user-centred approaches.
Analyse and innovate workflow processes using system modelling approaches.
Review and respond to health information system issues affecting the end user, work process, health information and system infrastructure relating to the health data and system development lifecyles
Critically analyse health information and clinical systems to create system model components using standard modelling tools.
Collaborate and communicate on health information system issues to develop the professional attributes, skills and knowledge of the Business/System analyst and Health Professionals.

title: HEALTH DATA ANALYSIS AND FUNDING CLASSIFICATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop specialist working knowledge of the regulatory frameworks governing both public and private sectors, and explore the various funding classifications, alongside clinical costing, modelling and policy and funding guidelines. Models of Activity Based Funding (ABF), such as casemix-based systems will be explored with linkages made to the fundamental role of the Health Information Manager. You will develop an understanding of health data standards, health data collections, and reporting requirements across various sectors, including government, insurance, and other domains; and explore the interconnections between these data practices and their impact on health service measurement and financing. Case studies deepen your understanding of these concepts and your analyses of morbidity, mortality, clinical, productivity, and health service data. You will develop skills in analysing and reporting hospital and health service utilisation statistics and interpreting published health data.

Compute and present hospital and health service utilisation statistics and analyse published health activity and service-related data.

Analyse clinical documentation and interpret and apply Australian Coding Standards, Conventions and ratified advice to accurately classify diseases and interventions.

You will also critique the impact of emergent health information technologies that influence the creation, storage, use, management and protection of health information. The subject broadly explores relevant information standards, clinical terminology systems, cybersecurity considerations and the important role of user-centred approaches to systems development.
