syllabus_overview: This subject explores and analyses Australia's disability law and policy, and aims to support those looking to pursue a legal or policy career in state or federal government, the disability sector or human rights lawyering. The first part of the subject establishes the theoretical and legal framework based on human rights principles within the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. The framework is then tested by an examination of particular case studies, which may vary from year to year. Generally, important practice contexts such as the National Disability Insurance Scheme, discrimination law, supported decision making: inclusive education or the interactions of disability and the criminal justice system will be taught in depth. Throughout the study period the role of law and policy in promoting and protecting the rights of people with disabilities is evaluated: areas requiring reform are identified; and strategies for the change considered.
learning_outcomes: Further develop skills in legal analysis and reasoning using examples from recent developments in disability law and policy.
Develop a critical understanding of legal and social construction of disability in 21st Century Australia and an understanding of the human rights framework for disability law and policy.
Develop an understanding of some of the key issues in contemporary Australian disability law and policy.
Improve legal problem solving, advocacy and creative advice-giving skills in relation to legal problems affecting people with disabilities.

title: COMPETITION POLICY & LAW
syllabus_overview: Competition policy is currently one of the most controversial areas of public policy impacting business. Competition policy represents the framework for legal change creating and encouraging the developments of markets. Competition law, in the form Part IV of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010, regulates competition by proscribing horizontal and vertical practices which are either per se anti-competitive or substantially affect competition. This subject deals both substantially and critically with the economic theory and public policy objectives which underpin competition policy and law, the legal techniques involved in creating and encouraging markets and the laws regulating competition. Students will undertake a number of case studies in competition policy and learn how the law regulating competition applies to various business practices.
learning_outcomes: Apply the existing competition law in Part IV of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 and industry-specific pro-competitive regulation to fact situations setting out complex market behaviours
Describe and critically assess the reasons for and implementation of policies directed at enhancing markets and competition
Ascertain, describe and critically assess general and industry specific pro-competitive regulation

title: EMPLOYMENT AND LABOR RELATIONS LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject you are provided with an introduction to the law of employment and labour relations. You study the principles and practices relating to the creation, categorisation, conduct and termination of the employment relationship. You also examine the roles of common law, awards, legislation, tribunals, collective bargaining and personnel practices in regulating the relationship. The subject is taught in the context of contemporary issues in labour regulation. As part of the subject you will undertake a negotiation, which will require attendance in class.
learning_outcomes: Undertake legal research into a nominated employment law topic.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of employment law in Australia.
Analyse critically complex information, problems, concepts and theories related to employment law.
Apply legal problem solving, collaboration and negotiation skills and creativity to resolve employment law issues.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES LAW
syllabus_overview: Australia faces complex and urgent environmental challenges. In this subject, you explore how to respond to environmental problems, individually and collectively, using law as a tool. You consider the economic and social factors that continue to shape the law in this area and the distribution of authority for environmental governance between the Commonwealth, State and local governments. You explore regulatory tools and examine principles of international environmental law and how they have influenced the development of Australian environmental law. You consider environmental management and regulatory challenges in relation to waste and pollution, biodiversity protection, and climate change and energy. You explore processes of environmental planning, development approval and impact assessment, enforcement and compliance, and environmental litigation. The purpose of the content is to understand how law can be deployed to mitigate ecological degradation, advocate for its protection and contribute to its repair.
learning_outcomes: Understand and critically evaluate key concepts and frameworks of Australian environmental and natural resources law
Consolidate collaborative working skills through group-based tasks
Write well composed, concise and accurately cited legal advice and documents
Develop independent learning and research skills and techniques, including identifying and locating materials relating to environmental problems

title: ISSUES IN FEDERAL CRIMINAL LAW : FRAUD, SMUGGLING AND TERRORISM
syllabus_overview: While much of the criminal law in Australia is State-based, the federal criminal jurisdiction is ever-expanding. In this subject you will gain a solid grounding in this increasingly important part of the work of Australian criminal lawyers. You will explore a range of important Australian federal criminal offences, including: fraud offences (covering white collar and corporate crime as well as social security offences), smuggling and cross-border offences (including customs and drug importation offences, people smuggling and migration offences), terrorism and war crimes, and human servitude and exploitation offences. The subject will also cover the constitutional basis of federal criminal law, the general principles of criminal responsibility in Chapter 2 of the Commonwealth Criminal Code, and federal sentencing.
learning_outcomes: Assess and critique a range of existing Australian federal criminal laws, and to propose and defend reforms to those laws.
Compose a legal advice by applying existing Australian federal criminal laws to new fact situations in order to predict the likely legal outcome.
Explain and summarise a range of key principles of Australian federal criminal law.

title: GENERAL INSURANCE LAW & PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to cover principles of General Insurance Law through an examination of the general principles relating to the construction and interpretation of various classes of insurance cover in relation to land based risks. Some of the common classes of cover which will be dealt with are Fire and Public Liability Risks, Motor Insurance cover, Home Owners and Home Contents policies. The syllabus will deal with regulatory aspects of insurance as covered by key legislation, common law principles which regulate the relationship between the insurer and the insured such as the duty of good faith, non-disclosure and misrepresentation and fraud in insurance contracts. The legislative frame work will also be taken into account. Of relevance here will be coverage of the principles of subrogation, election, waiver and estoppel. From the practical perspective, duties owed by a lawyer when retained by an insurer, as well as a lawyer's professional responsibilities will be considered
learning_outcomes: By the end of the semester, students will have the skills of inquiry bases in legal research to be able to prepare reasoned written arguments by identifying relevant factual issues and applying the relevant principles in Insurance Law, with the view of advising respective parties to a suit on their prospects of success or otherwise.

By the end of the semester, students will be able to critically analyse the known and discoverable facts and the prevailing law, to develop a practical litigation strategy to resolve the client's problem.

By the end of the semester, students will be able to demonstrate an ability to write an opinion based on the facts and law as to the merits of making a claim as a plaintiff or resisting such clam on behalf of the defendant.
By the end of the semester, students will be able to work in a team environment in an organised manner over sustained periods of time in order to produce favourable litigation outcomes for clients.
By the end of the semester, students will be able to demonstrate an ability to make effective oral presentations on a factual scenario arguing for the claimant or defending insurer.

title: HUMAN RIGHTS LAW
syllabus_overview: Students in this unit study the core elements and fundamental issues in international and Australian human rights law. We consider the philosophical basis that underlies the international human rights framework, and then examine various methods for the enforcement or realisation of human rights at both an international and domestic level. We consider case studies in the areas of civil and political rights, economic, social and cultural rights, and the field of emerging rights. .
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to follow instructions and academic conventions in completing set tasks
Summarise and assess the central principles which led to the creation of specific human rights-focused laws and treaties.
Interpret and evaluate the different legislative and international law instruments which protect a selection of human rights.
Select legal principles and instruments to create and defend solutions to human rights problems.

title: INTERNATIONAL COMMERCIAL MEDIATION
syllabus_overview: International Commercial Mediation examines the foundational principles and practice of mediation in the context of cross border commercial transactions. This subject is designed to train and assess students who have been selected to represent La Trobe Law School at the Commercial Mediation Competitions (ICC). You will explore the nature of commercial mediation through theoretical training combined with workshops where you will practice the skills in mock mediation sessions, as well as the opportunity to participate in the competition.
learning_outcomes: Identify the principles of mediation and how a dispute is translated into a mediation claim in written form, using the process of mediation
Demonstrate a critical awareness of how to pursue a mediation claim for a client as effectively as possible.
Synthesise mediation processes and strategies in order to find solutions to legal disputes.

title: ADVOCACY
syllabus_overview: The ability to make persuasive legal argument is a core skill for all legal practitioners, whether inside or outside a courtroom. This subject will introduce you to advocacy and will build your skills as oral and written advocates. Topics covered will include the role of advocacy in an adversarial system, the trajectory of a case through the national and/or international courts and tribunals and the core skills required of advocates. You will have the opportunity to develop oral and written advocacy skills through in class exercises and assessment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the intersection between facts and law in order to present and test evidence in a given context.
Present oral factual and legal arguments persuasively, using the appropriate courtroom etiquette and procedural skills.
Demonstrate the ability to formulate a case concept and craft effective written legal arguments.
Identify and demonstrate the core elements of persuasive advocacy.
Analyse complex factual scenarios, identify the relevant legal questions and formulate persuasive legal and factual arguments in oral and written form.

title: INTERNATIONAL DISPUTE SETTLEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you, to the methods and institutions used in the management and resolution of international disputes between states as well as between states and other actors including individuals and private entities. You will explore diplomatic and legal means of dispute settlement, ranging from negotiation to adjudication. Using cases, you will critically assess the influencing factors for states, individuals, and private entities selecting a particular method of dispute settlement such as arbitration, and the outcomes of such decisions. Through the analysis of examples, the subject examines the procedural, jurisdictional, and compliance challenges that have emerged that span substantive fields of international law such as investor-state dispute settlement bodies. You will become familiar with various dispute settlement bodies and their governing legal frameworks including relevant international treaties. The subject will also examine the current trends, challenges, and the future of international dispute settlement.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the treaties, conventions and statutes relevant to international dispute settlement.
Identify, analyse and reflect on the various forms of international dispute settlement
Identify and engage with issues relating to international dispute settlement including future trends
Assess key cases issued by various dispute settlement bodies and the dispute settlement mechanisms used by them.
Demonstrate knowledge of the processes and principles by which international dispute settlement bodies are created and the application of their governing rules.

title: INCOME TAXATION LAW
syllabus_overview: Taxation is a factor in all commercial and everyday transactions. As such, lawyers are required to be aware of the taxation implications of the advice they provide to clients. As a true multidisciplinary subject, tax law interacts with every legal discipline. In this subject you will learn the fundamentals of Australian tax law including income, capital gains tax, deductions, residency and source, entities and anti-avoidance. The subject will also touch on the tax policy paradigms and philosophies that drive the enactment of tax legislation. The emphasis will be on the practical application of the tax law, allowing technical concepts to be more approachable, with a focus on teaching the skills necessary for practice.
learning_outcomes: Determine, on behalf of a client, alternative methods of structuring a transaction with the constraints of income tax law.
Evaluate different tax policy alternatives.
Demonstrate the ability to apply basic legal knowledge and skills in analysing and interpreting income tax law.

title: JUSTICE AFTER ATROCITY
syllabus_overview: How do societies deal with atrocity and its aftermath? In this subject, you are introduced to the manifold ways in which societies have faced atrocities and mass violence, such as criminal trials (domestic and international), truth commissions, and through art. By examining a number of case studies from across the globe, you are invited to critically reflect on the difficulties in notions of truth, representation, and justice. The focus is on both the theories and the practices of justice mechanisms with the aim of providing you with a well-grounded understanding of the precarious path to justice.
learning_outcomes: Consolidate collaborative working skills through group-based tasks
Critically evaluate the variety of reactions to atrocity and mass violence
Critically assess theories of justice in the context of societal breakdown
Demonstrate critical understanding of the manifold justice mechanisms that have been used in responses to atrocities
Demonstrate high level of comprehension of case studies of the domestic and international landscapes in which claims of peace, truth and justice are made

title: MENTAL DISORDER AND CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY
syllabus_overview: People with cognitive impairments and/or mental disorders are overrepresented at all stages of the criminal justice system. For this reason, mental health literacy is essential for anyone considering a career in criminal law or criminal justice. This subject, which builds upon first-year studies of criminal law, aims to help students develop that literacy. Topics to be covered will be drawn from among the following: the nature of criminal responsibility; the nature of mental disorders and cognitive impairments; fitness to stand trial; the defence of mental impairment; automatism; infanticide; battered woman syndrome; provocation and loss of control; intoxication; mental disorder, criminality and ‘evil’; sentencing of offenders with cognitive impairments or mental disorders; and mental health and mental disorders in the criminal justice system and in post-sentence supervision and detention schemes. Students will analyse the current law and its operation in Victoria and selected other Australian jurisdictions, as well as examine the policy issues raised by the current law. Assessment tasks will focus on critically interpreting and assessing the law and its operation, as well as critiquing and advancing proposals for law reform.
learning_outcomes: Locate, understand and research laws, procedures and policy issues concerning mental disorder and criminal responsibility.
Present persuasive arguments regarding legal and policy issues concerning mental disorder and criminal responsibility in the appropriate formats.
Critically assess laws, procedures, and policy arguments concerning mental disorder and criminal responsibility.

title: NEGOTIATION
syllabus_overview: Students explore approaches to negotiation before finally focusing on the features of principled negotiation as devised by the Harvard Negotiation Project. By engaging in negotiation exercises, students will develop their interpersonal, analytical, and planning skills and how to negotiate fairly and effectively. The subject will also cover theoretical and critical issues in negotiation including ethics, culture, trust and multiparty negotiations through structured lectures and discussion of assigned readings.
learning_outcomes: Apply key elements of the theories and practice of negotiation.
Develop awareness of self, others and cultural contexts in relation to negotiation and apply judgement to particular negotiation scenarios.
Demonstrate negotiation skills at the appropriate level.
Appraise (or evaluate specific areas of theoretical discussion in negotiations, including ethics, fairness and responsibility

title: PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to concepts and doctrines of Public International Law. Public International Law is about rules that govern relationships within the international community including between States, between States and other subjects of international law, and to a limited extent between States and citizens of States. You will be provided with the opportunity to reflect on substantive values underlying international law and the relationship between international and domestic law is considered with a focus on enforceability of international obligations. Topics covered include sources of international law, the creation and recognition of states, state responsibility, state jurisdiction and immunity, international dispute resolution and the use of force under international law. You will be equipped to reflect on domestic and international political events from an international rule of law perspective.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the operation and application of customary and treaty-based public international law principles in contemporary world events.

Demonstrate understanding of public international law principles that regulate the behaviour of States within the international system and the role of States and the United Nations in their development and enforcement.
Exercise critical thinking and judgement in the application of public international law principles to problems arising within the international system.
Undertake international legal research and analysis for the purposes of composing clear and coherent written advisory opinion on international law issues.

title: PLANNING LAW AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the way that planning law and policy regulates the use and development of land. You will consider the concepts of sustainability and social equity and assess whether the policy and legal framework created by planning laws forward these principles. You will also consider the processes of strategic planning, development and environmental assessments and appeals and review of decision-making in a range of different practical, cultural and geographical contexts. This gives rise to a range of issues such as democratic and community participation, climate change, sustainable development, land use conflict and environmental justice.
learning_outcomes: Compose and communicate a response to a problem relating to planning in an appropriate style and tone
Describe, analyse and critique the policy framework for planning in Victoria, demonstrating a capacity to reflect on the interaction between natural, economic, social, political and cultural systems
Describe and critically analyse the use of planning law as a mechanism for public good
Identify and discuss the common law and legislation relevant to planning in Victoria
Demonstrate understanding of the processes of planning and decision-making in planning, and review of decision-making

title: RESTORATIVE JUSTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the foundational theories and principles of Restorative Justice. To this end, it explores the practice of restorative justice from the state, national and international perspectives . It also takes into account the experiences of various stakeholders in the system, such as state representatives, victims, offenders, indigenous persons, minorities and those from non-English speaking backgrounds, with a view to assessing the extent to which it fits the needs of different participants. In this subject, students will also explore the broad application of restorative justice across the spectrum of the criminal justice system, from pre-sentence conferencing to inmate misconduct.
learning_outcomes: Consolidate collaborative working skills through group-based tasks
Apply a restorative justice approach to a range of real life situations
Critically assess the roles of participants in restorative justice processes at state, national and international levels.
Demonstrate a working knowledge of key terms, concepts and ideas in the area of restorative justice
Analyse, debate and critically evaluate different restorative justice approaches and their value in a range of contexts

title: SPORT AND THE LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the intersection of sport and law. It examines the place of sport in Australian society and how different bodies of law govern community- and elite-level sporting activities at local, national and international levels. The recent emergence of sports law allows us to assess and understand how existing legal fields such as contract, tort and employment law apply in sport, while also considering sport-specific fields such as anti-doping, sport tribunals and competition structure and governance. Recent controversies such as the Essendon supplement saga and concussion in sport will be utilised as case studies.
learning_outcomes: Design appropriate strategies to limit potential contravention of law relating to sport, including liability for injury.
Identify and discuss the common law and legislation impacting on participation in and management of sports .
Apply principles of sports law to the facts of problems.
Analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of various sports law regimes and regulatory practices

title: THE LAW OF SUCCESSION
syllabus_overview: This subject will consider the law of succession which concerns the devolution of rights and obligations upon death: Probate, Wills, the Administration of Estates, and dispute processes. The primary focus is the transmission of property interest through testamentary processes (Wills) and through the rules of intestacy. As part of this subject, students can apply to do a minimum of 12 days placement (subject to availability) in a community legal clinic or organisation to gain practical skills in working with clients and drafting documents. To apply for the placement, students must first be enrolled in the subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate enhanced knowledge of legal practice, through participation, observation, research, and reflection, on their practical experience.
Apply the relevant legislation and provide advice to a client regarding a claim against an estate.
Critically discuss the formalities required to make a valid will, the administration of the estate of a deceased person and the rules of construction.
Demonstrate enhanced communication skills in a legal environment.
Ascertain a testator's instructions to create a Will by receiving, considering and implementing instructions.

title: WATER LAW AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: Water resources are of increasing economic significance, whilst water use and management is undergoing increasing environmental scrutiny. Water Law is therefore of increasing relevance in Australian and global environmental sustainability debates. Our program will commence with an analysis of the international framework within which Australian water law is situated, from both an environmental and an international trade perspective. It will consider the federal and state agreements which shape most state legislation, and the federalisation of water resource management in the Murray Darling Basin. It will then consider, from both a policy and a practitioner perspective, the common law and legislation governing water law in Victoria, both in relation to urban, irrigation and environmental water entitlements.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate capacity to identify and analyse issues relating to Australian water law
Reconceptualise water related problems according to multiple stakeholder perspectives and identify potential remediation mechanisms.
Effectively communicate analyses of water-related issues utilising a range of critical perspectives
Critically assess Australian water law and policy and its capacity to fulfil intergenerational obligations and to forward the public good.

Demonstrate critical understanding of the international legal and policy environment in which Australian water law has been developed and to critically reflect on the interaction between water law and policy and natural, economic, social and cultural systems.

title: PRINCIPLES OF EQUITY AND TRUSTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the doctrines and institutions of equity. Approximately half the subject is about trusts: what they are, what they are used for, how to create them, how to administer them, and how to clean up when things go wrong. Other topics covered are fiduciary relationships, confidentiality, and equitable remedies. Together these topics make up "equity", which is often treated as different from other law. You will explore equity by using equitable principles to solve problems and will learn research skills that empower you to find answers to complex problems yourself.
learning_outcomes: Effectively structure and coherently communicate a legal opinion to a standard which accords with the professional conventions of legal writing
Formulate arguments that give legal meaning to people's interactions and review the persuasiveness of those arguments with reference to equitable principles and legal sources.
Apply advanced legal research skills to identify and analyse the statutory provisions and case law as they relate to a specific factual scenario in equity.

title: COMPANY LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain advanced knowledge of and critically analyse the principal features of modern partnership and corporations law (Company Law). The scope of this area of law is wide and the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), dominates. This subject aims to both situate the law contextually and emphasise the practical operation of the law in its social setting. Topics include the constitutional and administrative context of the Corporations Act, incorporation and its effects, corporate governance, various methods of financing (including equity and debt), and external administration. This subject meets the requirements of VLAB for admission to practice in Victoria in the area of Company Law.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and choose the most appropriate legal form of business and identify the most appropriate type of company.
Critically analyse ethical and policy considerations underpinning the development, evolution and practice of company law.
Work collaboratively to produce an appropriate outcome in response to a fictional scenario.
Apply knowledge of company law to analyse complex legal problems and to provide indications of probable outcomes.

title: LEGAL PRACTICE AND CONDUCT
syllabus_overview: This subject focusses upon the legal practitioner's duty to the administration of law, the courts, clients and fellow practitioners. Students are expected to apply knowledge of such duties to real life practice situations. Legal Practice and Conduct highlights the role of the ethical practitioner in the legal system and the importance of practitioner duties to the sustainability of the justice system, and thus to society as a whole. Students are encouraged to reflect on how a legal practitioner's duties and ethics are relevant to daily legal practice, as well as on the efficacy of law, the legal system, the legal profession and the nature of justice. They are to critically analyse professional and ethical responsibilities in the context of access to justice and reforms in the legal profession. This subject meets the requirements of the Council of Legal Education for admission to practice in Victoria in the area Professional Conduct.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the professional and ethical responsibilities of legal practitioners with reference to a variety of lawyering paradigms and conceptual frameworks.
Demonstrate effective legal research skills with an immediate and practical purpose, to a level approaching that of a new entrant to the legal profession.
Critically reflect upon ethical dilemmas facing a legal practitioner and analyse how to handle them in an appropriate and professional manner.
Apply knowledge of the legal aspects of the lawyer/client relationship to real legal practice situations.
Demonstrate in-depth knowledge of the regulatory, complaint and disciplinary processes applicable to the Victorian legal profession, individually or collaboratively in a group.

title: PRINCIPLES OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject principally examines the limitations on the power of the federal and state executive governments to make decisions, and the legal mechanisms available to aggrieved persons for challenging and reviewing the exercise of such powers. Students are expected to analyse statutory language, critically assess real world factual situations and apply their knowledge to predict likely client outcomes. They are asked to effectively communicate a legal claim or defence in a written form which approaches the standard of new entrant to the legal profession. The mechanisms examined at the federal level include judicial review of administrative action under the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act 1977 (Cth), merits review by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate a legal claim or defence in a written form which approaches the standard of new entrant to the legal profession.
Evaluate the likely effectiveness of any recourse to Administrative Law review mechanisms in meeting a client's goals.
Critical analyse complex factual situations and employ problem solving skills to pursue a legal claim or defence for a client as effectively as possible.
Research and critically analyse the scope and nature of the power given to government decision-makers under legislation

title: LEGAL RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop advanced skills in legal research and writing methods by independently designing, planning and executing an honours research project. Students will learn about different forms of legal writing and apply legal writing, research methods and techniques in the development of a research project on a complex legal issue. Students will be expected to demonstrate skills in locating and analysing primary and secondary research materials, devising an honours research plan for completing independent research, effective written communication for a professional audience and self-managing their workload to the successful completion of the research project.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate innovative skills in devising and executing an independent research project.
Independently locate, review and critically analyse primary and secondary research material appropriate to a specific legal research task.
Demonstrate advanced skills in legal research and writing methods
Produce an independent project showing sound reasoning, effective writing and compliance with established style requirements.

title: INTERNSHIP A
syllabus_overview: This subject allows students to participate in a placement at an approved organisation while concurrently undertaking academic study. Placements can be in Australia or overseas in a legal related role. Students are required to complete a research or other type of writing project of their own choosing in addition to reflective elements of assessment. Students may apply for placement opportunities organised by the Law School or apply on the basis of a self-organised placement. Self-organised placements must be approved by the Coordinator. Placement Coordinator or delegate. In this unit there is a focus on practice skills and industry informed career development learning activities to support professional development in readiness for graduate positions.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate critical thinking in the application of research on an approved topic in a writing project
Demonstrate an ability to critically reflect on their practical experience.
Develop their knowledge of the application of their law degree in a working environment, through participation, observation, research, and reflection, on their practical experience.
Develop their communication skills in a professional work environment.

title: COMPARATIVE LAW
syllabus_overview: Comparative Law introduces you to the different legal traditions of the world. By developing a comparative perspective, you sharpen your understanding of how law is made and operates within a global context. Throughout the subject, the comparative method is considered conceptually and applied practically through hands-on exercises that consider similarities and differences in domestic laws, legal institutions and legal systems. You explore the extent to which legal systems are converging or whether local contexts continue to preserve legal distinctiveness. Comparative Law equips you with the foundation to engage in comparative legal research and analysis, an increasingly important attribute for lawyers working in today's interconnected world.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess and articulate the multifaceted implications of globalisation, international legal frameworks and other external forces on the development, implementation and effectiveness of domestic legal systems.
Demonstrate proficiency in written and oral communication, employing effective argumentation to convey comparative legal analysis and findings with clarity and coherence.
Conduct legal research to identify foreign sources of law, including constitutions, statutes and court judgments and apply the comparative method to analyse and interpret those sources
Analyse and evaluate the fundamental principles that underpin diverse legal traditions and systems and compare and contrast them with Australian law

title: SUCCESSION LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject will consider the law of succession which concerns the devolution of rights and obligations upon death: Probate, Wills, the Administration of Estates, and dispute processes. The primary focus is the transmission of property interest through testamentary processes (Wills) and through the rules of intestacy, adopting a practical legal pedagogy which engages students in legal skills development.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate enhanced communication skills in a legal environment.
Analyse and apply the relevant legislation and provide advice to a client regarding a claim against an estate.
Ascertain a testator's instructions to create a Will by receiving, considering and implementing instructions.
Critically discuss the formalities required to make a valid will, the administration of the estate of a deceased person and the rules of construction.
Demonstrate enhanced knowledge of legal practice, through participation, observation, research, and reflection, on their practical experience.

title: ADVOCACY
syllabus_overview: The ability to make persuasive legal arguments is a core skill for all legal practitioners, whether inside or outside a courtroom. This subject will introduce you to advocacy and will build your skills as oral and written advocates. Topics covered will include the role of advocacy in an adversarial system, the trajectory of a case through the national and/or international courts and tribunals and the core skills required of advocates. You will have the opportunity to develop oral and written advocacy skills through in class exercises and assessment
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to formulate a case concept and craft effective written legal arguments.
Present oral factual and legal arguments persuasively, using the appropriate courtroom etiquette and procedural skills.
Analyse complex factual scenarios, identify the relevant legal questions and formulate persuasive legal and factual arguments in oral and written form.
Analyse the intersection between facts and law in order to present and test evidence in a given context.
Identify and demonstrate the core elements of persuasive advocacy.

title: ANIMALS AND LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject will consider the relationship between people and animals in ethics, law, and society. Topics to be considered will be chosen from current issues in animal law and may include the legal classification of animals, companion animals, animals in the wild, regulation of the use of animals for food and entertainment, anti-cruelty laws, live export, animals used in scientific experimentation, zoos and circuses, international wildlife trafficking and international developments including public interest litigation in animal law. The subject also considers the political and social context in which law and policy are formulated and applied in animal law matters. You will also have the opportunity to enhance your research and writing skills.
learning_outcomes: Gain an advanced understanding of the common law and legislation impacting on the welfare of animals
Critically analyse the political and social context in which law and policy is formulated and applied in animal law matters
Evaluate the capacity of current law to improve the welfare of animals

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ETHICS AND THE LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the ethical, legal and regulatory challenges arising from the development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI). It equips you with the analytical and critical frameworks necessary to analyse and respond to the opportunities, risks and governance issues associated with AI systems. AI is rapidly permeating almost every aspect of society, mediating human relationships, institutional practices and social interactions in new and often opaque ways. While these technologies offer significant benefits, they also raise complex concerns relating to privacy, discrimination, human rights, social trust, environmental impacts and the distribution of risk and responsibility. The subject introduces key approaches from normative ethics and applies them to contemporary AI contexts. It also examines how ethical concerns are translated into legal and regulatory responses, including legislation, case law, policy frameworks and standards. The subject emphasises reasoned argument, critical evaluation and the ability to engage with diverse perspectives relevant to law, policy and technology. By the end of the subject, you will be able to analyse the ethical and regulatory dimensions of AI systems and critically assess and justify approaches to their governance.
learning_outcomes: Analyse ethical and regulatory challenges associated with AI technologies.
Critique and justify approaches to regulating artificial intelligence.
Engage in dialogue across diverse perspectives, to design and build technology with an appreciation of the responsibilities attached to creating powerful tools.
Evaluate risks and impacts arising from the development and deployment of AI technologies.

title: CLIMATE LAW
syllabus_overview: Climate change presents many complex and long-term challenges for society, economy and environment. This subject considers how law and legal regimes can contribute to addressing these challenges and the way legal frameworks might need to be re-conceptualised and changed to respond. This subject examines the international legal framework under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Paris Agreement, including questions of mitigation, adaptation and loss and damage. It also examines transnational forms of climate change regulation, including through carbon markets and other voluntary measures, as well how law can promote transitions to a low-carbon society. The course also covers Australian regulatory measures to address climate change, examining federal, state and local law. The subject concludes by considering the growth in litigation to respond to climate challenges as well as the interaction between climate change and other legal regimes, such as trade and human rights.
learning_outcomes: Through collaborative processes analyse, generate and transmit legal solutions to complex problems related to climate change governance
Locate by means of legal research, materials relating to the problem of climate change and its legal regulation, and write well composed, concise and accurately cited legal analysis.
Analyse and evaluate the effectiveness, efficiency and equity of different legal responses to climate change
Examine and understand the different legal regimes and principles applicable to climate change governance

title: LEGAL INTERNSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject allows students to participate in an Australian legal practice placement at an approved organisation such as a community legal centre, law firm, government or private organisation, shadowing a barrister while concurrently undertaking academic study. Students may apply for placement opportunities organised by the Law School or apply on the basis of a self-organised placement. Self-organised placements must be approved by the Coordinator.Law School Placement Coordinator or delegate. In this unit there is a focus on practice skills and industry informed career development learning activities to support professional development in readiness for graduate positions.
learning_outcomes: Develop their communication skills in a legal environment
Demonstrate an ability to critically reflect on their practical experience.
Demonstrate critical thinking in relation to the professional and ethical practice of law.
Develop their knowledge of legal practice, through participation, observation, research, and reflection, on their practical experience.

title: LAW INTERNSHIP B
syllabus_overview: This subject is created for students who are undertaking a volunteer placement in a law or law related field in Australia or overseas and intend to write the Honours research project in connection with that placement. This subject is designed to accommodate placements of a duration of 12 to 30 days. You are required to complete the placement satisfactorily and to complete an academic task which is normally an essay based on a topic or theme arising from the placement. This essay will require you to critically reflect on your experience and thoroughly research and analyse the issue you have chosen.
learning_outcomes: Develop a research topic linked to their placement experience, identify, and apply appropriate research techniques for answering it.
Apply critical thinking skills in the composition of a piece of legal writing to demonstrate a thorough knowledge and understanding of a real world legal issues.
Apply legal research and oral and written communication skills to legal issues encountered during the placement
Demonstrate a reflective approach to learning by engaging with real world legal issues in a clinical context
Communicate effectively in oral and written form research of the legal issues arising from the practicum participation.

title: LEGAL PRACTICE AND CONDUCT CLINICAL PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: Ethical legal practice and conduct are the primary focus of this unit. This includes examining the legal practitioner's duty to the administration of law, the courts, clients, and fellow practitioners, issues of personal and professional conduct, and basic trust accounting. The context for this study is the issue of access to justice and recent reform to the legal system, in particular the legal profession. Additionally, you will be placed in a legal aid environment where you will have the opportunity to be practically involved in legal practice under supervision. You are encouraged to reflect on how a legal practitioner's duties and ethics are relevant to daily legal practice and the efficacy of law, the legal system, the legal profession and the nature of justice. This unit meets the requirements of the Council of Legal Education for admission to practice in Victoria in the area of Professional Conduct.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to critically reflect on their practical experience.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the legal aspects of the lawyer/client relationship including the contractual, tortious and fiduciary nature of the relationship
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the regulatory, complaint and disciplinary processes for the legal profession
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the fiduciary nature of the lawyer/client relationship including knowledge of the statutory requirements regulating trust accounting.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the statutory and common law rules governing lawyers professional conduct in relation to clients, the courts and third parties
Analyse the professional responsibilities of a legal practitioner and apply these to real legal practice situations
Demonstrate effective legal research skills with an immediate and practical purpose
Analyse, evaluate and perform the professional ethical responsibilities of a lawyer in the context of daily legal practice
Demonstrate an understanding of the various frameworks/approaches for making ethical decisions in a practical context
Demonstrate effective legal interviewing, oral and written communication skills

title: DISPUTE RESOLUTION
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the theories, principles, practices and laws relating to dispute resolution and offers an opportunity for Juris Doctor students to cultivate an understanding of the position of dispute resolution in contemporary legal practice. It addresses a range of dispute resolution methods including negotiation, mediation, conciliation and arbitration, with a particular focus on mediation. You will examine how these processes are used in different contexts within Australian jurisdictions and internationally. By the end of the subject, you will have a foundational understanding of the broad factors which determine the appropriate dispute resolution options and a capacity to align various disputes to appropriate dispute process choices.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and critically evaluate different dispute resolution methods and demonstrate an ability to align various disputes to appropriate dispute process choices
Demonstrate a working knowledge of key principles, practices and laws in dispute resolution and their interface with the legal system.
Demonstrate a range of skills used in various dispute resolution processes.

title: MINOR THESIS A
syllabus_overview: This is the first sequence of two subjects that together constitute Minor Thesis. The subject is available to students enrolled in the Juris Doctor or the Bachelor of Laws (Honours) and is by application only. Enrolment requires approval by subject coordinator and generally a WAM above 70. Working under the supervision of a staff member, students are required to design, research and produce a 12,000-13,000 word thesis on an approved topic. Students must also attend the seminar series which is designed to support and further develop students' research skills. Students are required to present a report on their research during the seminar series.The minor thesis demonstrates students' capacity to make an original contribution to their chosen discipline.
learning_outcomes: Produce an original thesis showing sound reasoning, a coherent exposition of knowledge, effective writing, and compliance with established style requirements.
Exercise critical thinking and judgment in developing a new or sophisticated understanding of a specific area of legal knowledge.
Independently locate, review, analyse and synthesise complex primary and secondary material.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of a specific area of legal knowledge of your own choosing.

Develop a research question dealing with a problem in a specific area of law, identify appropriate research techniques designed to investigate and present plausible response(s) to that question, and formulate and present such response(s).

title: MINOR THESIS B
syllabus_overview: This is the second sequence of two subjects that together constitute Minor Thesis. The subject is available to students enrolled in the Juris Doctor or the Bachelor of Laws (Honours) and is by application only. Enrolment requires approval by subject coordinator and generally a WAM above 70. Working under the supervision of a staff member, students are required to design, research and produce a 12,000-13,000 word thesis on an approved topic. The minor thesis demonstrates students' capacity to make an original contribution to their chosen discipline.
learning_outcomes: Exercise critical thinking and judgment in developing a new or sophisticated understanding of a specific area of legal knowledge.
Independently locate, review, analyse and synthesise complex primary and secondary material.
Produce an original thesis showing sound reasoning, a coherent exposition of knowledge, effective writing, and compliance with established style requirements.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of a specific area of legal knowledge of your own choosing.

Develop a research question dealing with a problem in a specific area of law, identify appropriate research techniques designed to investigate and present plausible response(s) to that question, and formulate and present such response(s).

title: PRINCIPLES OF BANKING AND FINANCE LAW AND REGULATION
syllabus_overview: This subject critically examines the theories and principles underpinning the regulation of financial institutions and financial products and examines selected legal issues you may encounter in a banking and finance law department of a legal firm or financial institution. In particular, the subject discusses how economic theory within the dominant paradigm of neo-liberalism has explicitly influenced choices of ways of regulating. The subject is divided into two themes. The first critically examines problems of financial regulation arising out of the Banking Royal Commission, the Global Financial Crisis, and new forms of finance in the digital age - fintech. Topics include problems of financial regulation, difficulties relating to the protection of consumers, compliance in financial institutions, regulation of “Defi”, cryptocurrency, stablecoins, and peer-to-peer lending. The second theme of the subject is selected issues in banking and finance law. Topics include the legal nature of different forms of financial accommodation, the legal relationship between borrowers, lenders, and agents in multi-lender financing, and complex legal issues concerning guarantees.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply the relevant banking and finance law applicable to complex fact situations relating to corporate banking and finance.

Provide in-depth critical analysis of the key principles underpinning financial regulation and how those principles are translated into regulation and applied to regulated financial institutions and their activities and transactions.
Critically evaluate regulatory responses to fast-developing areas of financial regulation, including financial technology (Fintech), and decentralised finance (Defi).

title: COMMERCIAL LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on knowledge acquired in contract law to introduce you to areas of law that regulate and facilitate commercial transactions. These include agency, commercial sale of goods and services, interest over personal property, and insurance. Throughout this unit, you will adopt a skills-based learning approach through problem-solving and promoting an understanding of the dynamic nature of the law in business. These skills will prepare you for your professional career.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate legal principles, including cases and statutory provisions, relevant to commercial law and apply them appropriately to problem-solving scenarios.
Demonstrate advanced understanding of the common law and statutory provisions relevant to commercial law.
Identify, analyse and critically reflect on the common law and statutory provisions governing commercial law.

title: INTERNATIONAL DISPUTE SETTLEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the methods and institutions used in the management and resolution of international disputes between states as well as between states and other actors including individuals and private entities. You will explore diplomatic and legal means of dispute settlement, ranging from negotiation to adjudication. Using cases, you will critically assess the influencing factors for states, individuals, and private entities selecting a particular method of dispute settlement such as arbitration, and the outcomes of such decisions. Through the analysis of examples, the subject examines the procedural, jurisdictional, and compliance challenges that have emerged that span substantive fields of international law such as investor-state dispute settlement bodies. You will become familiar with various dispute settlement bodies and their governing legal frameworks including relevant international treaties. The subject will also examine the current trends, challenges, and the future of international dispute settlement.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess key cases issued by various dispute settlement bodies and the dispute settlement mechanisms behind them.
Identify, analyse and critically reflect on the various forms of international dispute settlement
Demonstrate knowledge of the processes and principles by which international dispute settlement bodies are created and the application of their governing rules.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the treaties, conventions and statutes relevant to international dispute settlement.
Identify and critically analyse at an advanced level issues including future trends relating to international dispute settlement

title: WATER LAW AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: Water Law is of increasing relevance in Australia and globally. Water resources are of growing economic significance, whilst water use and management are undergoing increasing environmental scrutiny. Our program will commence with an analysis of the international framework within which Australian water law is situated, from both an environmental and an international trade perspective. It will consider the federal and state agreements which shape most state legislation, and the federalisation of water resource management in the Murray Darling Basin. It will then consider, from both a policy and a practitioner perspective, the common law and legislation governing water law in Victoria, both in relation to urban, irrigation and environmental water entitlements.
learning_outcomes: Reconceptualise water related problems according to multiple stakeholder perspectives and identify and critique potential remediation mechanisms.
Demonstrate advanced capacity to identify and analyse issues relating to Australian water law
Critically assess Australian water law and policy and its capacity to fulfil intergenerational obligations and to enhance the public good.

Demonstrate advanced critical understanding of the international legal and policy environment in which Australian water law has been developed and to critically reflect on the interaction between water law and policy and natural, economic, social and cultural systems.
Effectively communicate analyses of water-related issues utilising a range of critical perspectives

title: COMPARATIVE LAW
syllabus_overview: Comparative Law introduces you to the different legal traditions of the world. By developing a comparative perspective, you sharpen your understanding of how law is made and operates within a global context. Throughout the subject, the comparative method is considered conceptually and applied practically through hands-on exercises that consider similarities and differences in domestic laws, legal institutions and legal systems. You explore the extent to which legal systems are converging or whether local contexts continue to preserve legal distinctiveness. Comparative Law equips you with the foundation to engage in comparative legal research and analysis, an increasingly important attribute for lawyers working in today's interconnected world.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast Australian law with the structure, functions, substantive provisions, and legal reasoning employed in foreign legal systems.
Conduct legal research to identify foreign sources of law, including constitutions, statutes and court judgments.

Critically assess and articulate the multifaceted implications of globalisation, international legal frameworks and other external forces on the development, implementation and effectiveness of domestic legal systems.
Demonstrate proficiency in written and oral communication, employing effective argumentation to convey comparative legal analysis and findings with clarity and coherence.

Evaluate the roles and interplay between cultural, historical, socio-political factors, and legal traditions, systems, and substantive legal norms, elucidating their impact on the evolution and application of law.
Apply the comparative method to analyse and interpret the constitutions, statutes and court judgments of foreign jurisdictions.
Analyse and evaluate the fundamental principles that underpin diverse legal traditions and systems.

title: INDIGENOUS PEOPLES AND THE LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the way settler-colonial law impacts upon Indigenous peoples in the territory called Australia and the way struggles for Indigenous justice have engaged the legal system. Providing a historical and socio-legal analysis the subject covers a range of topics, including: Indigenous sovereignty; the history of genocide and the Stolen Generations; Indigenous citizenship; police violence, deaths in custody and over-representation in the criminal justice system; Indigenous law in the context of sentencing; land rights and native title; cultural heritage protection; racism and racial discrimination; human rights and self-determination; family surveillance and continuing child removals; and constitutional recognition and treaty. The assessment regime also allows you to research relevant topics of particular interest.
learning_outcomes: By means of legal research, locate and analyse primary and secondary materials relevant to Indigenous interactions with law.
Critically analyse contemporary legal issues relating to Indigenous peoples in Australia.
Demonstrate an awareness of cultural safety in the context of Indigenous interactions with law.
Critically reflect on the way settler-colonial law impacts upon Indigenous peoples and the way struggles for Indigenous justice have engaged the legal system.

title: LAW OF SUCCESSION
syllabus_overview: This subject will consider the law of succession which concerns the devolution of rights and obligations upon death: Probate, Wills, the Administration of Estates, and dispute processes. The primary focus is the transmission of property interest through testamentary processes (Wills) and through the rules of intestacy. As part of this subject, you can apply to do a minimum of 12 days optional placement (subject to availability) in a community legal clinic or organisation to gain practical skills in working with clients and drafting documents. To apply for the placement, students must first be enrolled in the subject.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced and integrated understanding of the law of succession.
Analyse critically, reflect on and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories related to the law of succession.
Interpret and transmit knowledge, skills and ideas to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Apply knowledge and skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a practitioner

title: CURRENT ISSUES IN FEDERAL CRIMINAL LAW
syllabus_overview: Federal criminal law is an increasingly important part of the work of Australian criminal lawyers. In this subject you will gain a solid and extended critical grounding in this significant jurisdiction of criminal law. You will critically explore, at an advanced level, a range of important Australian federal criminal offences, including from among the following: terrorism, treason and related offences, secrecy of information, bribery, fraud, drug offences, people smuggling, and cybercrimes. You will also critically examine, at an advanced level, the constitutional basis of federal criminal law, and the general principles of criminal responsibility under Chapter 2 of the Commonwealth Criminal Code.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced skills and autonomy in research relevant to Australian federal criminal laws and principles.
Demonstrate advanced and integrated skills in the critical evaluation of contemporary issues and areas for reform relevant to Australian federal criminal laws and principles.
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of a range of key principles and substantive provisions of Australian federal criminal law.

title: EMPLOYMENT AND LABOUR RELATIONS LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are provided with an introduction to the law of employment and labour relations. You study the principles and practices relating to the creation, categorisation, conduct and termination of the employment relationship. You also examine the roles of common law, awards, legislation, tribunals, collective bargaining and industrial action in regulating the relationship. The subject is taught in the context of contemporary issues in labour regulation. As part of the subject you will undertake a negotiation, which will require attendance in class.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge and skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability, collaboration and responsibility as a learner.
Interpret and transmit knowledge, skills and ideas to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Demonstrate advanced and integrated understanding of employment law.
Analyse critically, reflect on and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories related to employment law.

title: INSOLVENCY LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the concept of insolvency that derives from the availability of credit and therefore debt. Insolvency law refers to the legal framework that deals with the consequences of an individual or a company defaulting on their debts. You will examine the general principles of insolvency law. You will then study the principles that apply to corporate insolvency as well as the various formal options designed to deal with rescuing companies and/or their business or otherwise dealing with their financial distress. This will include a discussion of the role and duties of company directors in circumstances of looming or actual insolvency.
learning_outcomes: Conduct independent legal research and critically evaluate issues in insolvency law and policy
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of theories, principles and rules of insolvency law
Develop advanced collaborative skills in a team environment
Analyse legal issues and identify and articulate appropriate solutions to legal problems

title: AUSTRALIAN FAMILY LAW
syllabus_overview: This subject offers an in-depth exploration of Family Law in Australia through emphasizing three core components: the substantive legal framework relating to the family, the practical skills necessary for effective legal practice, and a critical examination of how family law interacts with societal changes. Specific topics explored in this subject include the legal regulation of family formation and breakdown, parental responsibility, and children's rights alongside hands-on activities designed to develop essential legal skills such as drafting legal documents, conducting client interviews, and negotiating settlements. These practical skills are complemented by discussions on emerging trends and potential reforms in family law, including the recognition of diverse family structures and the implications of technological advancements.
learning_outcomes: Develop an awareness and capacity to critically analyse the key issues in contemporary Australian Family Law.
Demonstrate advanced collaborative working skills through group-based tasks
Critically analyse the historical, social, economic and cultural context in which family law decision-making arises.
Apply skills in legal analysis and reasoning and improve legal problem solving and communication skills in relation to family law problems
Develop detailed knowledge of the legal framework which regulates the responsibilities, rights and duties of family members in Australia, and of the socio-legal factors that this legal framework

title: AUSTRALIAN INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY LAW
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine the regulatory and legal framework of intellectual property law in Australia. You will analyse the doctrines, principles and policies of intellectual property regulation, including the discrete areas of copyright, patent, design and trade mark laws. You will also examine the concepts and theories of protecting intellectual property as well as the political, cultural and economic context of the reform of intellectual property laws in Australia.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced skills in identifying, using and appraising research material relevant to the operation and reform of intellectual property law in Australia
Critically examine the legal, regulatory, ethical and economic implications of intellectual property law and its reform in Australia
Demonstrate comprehension of the regulatory and legislative framework of Australian intellectual property law

title: INTRODUCTION TO CYBERFORENSICS AND THE LAW
syllabus_overview: The subject will consider ethical and legal issues related to technologically enabled crime and criminal procedure. It will analyse forensic considerations such as the digital identity, admissibility of computer data searches, warrants, production orders, access to subscriber information and data retention laws and principles will be considered, in addition to entrapment, encryption and the expectation of privacy. We will also look at search and seizure, evidentiary issues, and various legal and regulatory environments in cyberspace, and examine how emerging technologies challenge existing laws, social norms, and criminal procedure.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the legal and law enforcement and regulatory challenges around cyber forensics and the law
Critically evaluate and apply case-based and statutory principles relating to cyberforensics and the law
Explain and differentiate key concepts relating to cyberforensics and the law
Propose a solution to a problem raised in a fact situation relevant to cyber forensics and the law.
Evaluate the evidentiary and other legal challenges around the use of forensic evidence in cyber-related cases (e.g. online child pornography)

title: CURRENT ISSUES IN JURISPRUDENCE
syllabus_overview: This subject explores current topics and debates at the cutting edge of Jurisprudence. Jurisprudence, or the philosophy of law, is the critical examination of the fundamental ideas, values, and principles that underpin and shape legal thinking. This subject approaches these issues through an in-depth examination of specific issues such as whether there is a right to disobey the law, whether animals have rights, whether historical injustices can be remedied, whether criminal justice has a place for mercy, and whether there is a right to offend, among others. You will engage with the issues at an advanced level through reading and critiquing a combination of contemporary academic writings and real-world examples drawn from case law, legislation, current debates, and history.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of and critical engagement with the jurisprudential issues covered in the subject.
Produce advanced academic writing that presents clear and logical arguments informed by well-developed skills in legal research.
Create academic work that shows an ability to follow instructions that maintains academic integrity.

title: CRIMINAL JUSTICE AND POLICY
syllabus_overview: The criminal justice system refers to the collection of state institutions and agencies responsible for the processing of persons accused of committing a crime or convicted of a crime. This subject offers an advanced examination of the criminal justice process. Emphasis is placed on the role, discretions, and responsibilities of participants and decision-makers, as well as on the various checks and balances designed to prevent or correct errors. You will be encouraged, through in-depth studies of miscarriages of justice, to critically evaluate the pressure points in the system and examine potential reforms.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced and integrated skills in the critical evaluation of contemporary issues and areas for reform relevant to the administration of criminal justice
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of the law governing the administration of criminal justice in Victoria.
Develop advanced collaborative working skills through group-based tasks
Demonstrate advanced skills and autonomy in research relevant to the administration of criminal justice

title: CONTRACT LAW A
syllabus_overview: Contract Law A examines the foundational principles of the law of contract in Australia. Students will interrogate the common law presumptions of freedom of contract and equality of bargaining power and analyse the capacity of equity to ameliorate the effects of those presumptions. This subject considers the role of contract law as a transactional mechanism and as a method of allocation of risks and assesses the impact of the development of implied duties to cooperate and to act in good faith in the performance of contractual obligations.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate claims made in a factual scenario with appropriate reference to contract law
Write a legal opinion on a factual scenario in contract law in a professional manner
Demonstrate high level research skills in relation to primary and secondary sources of contract law and its context
Critically analyse common law principles in the law of contract with reference to theories of contract law
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of the conceptual and doctrinal framework of contract law in Australia

title: CONTRACT LAW B
syllabus_overview: In Contract Law B students will resume their examination of contract law, with a focus on excuses for non-performance and the impact of key statutory initiatives on contractual rights and obligations. Topics include unconscionable dealings, misrepresentation, undue influence, and mistake; damages for breach of contract; limitations on the enforcement of contractual rights including privity, exclusion clauses, unjust terms and non-excludable statutory guarantees and statutory remedies available for unconscionable and misleading or deceptive conduct. This subject, in combination with Contract Law A, meets the requirements of the Victorian Legal Admissions Board for admission to practice in Victoria in the area of Law of Contracts.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate intellectual and practical skills to justify and interpret theoretical propositions, legal methods and conclusions.
Select, analyse, interpret and apply legal principles and methods and use professional judgement to generate appropriate jurisprudential and practical responses to complex legal problems.
Demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of common law principles at law and in equity and principles of statutory interpretation in the field of contract law.
Utilise appropriate research tools and methods to evaluate and synthesise relevant legal and factual matters.

title: CORPORATIONS LAW
syllabus_overview: In LAW5CPL Company Law students are introduced to the main concepts, principles and rules of modern partnership, corporations and securities law. The scope of this area of law is wide, and statutes (the Partnership Act 1958 (Vic), Corporations Act 2001 (Cth)) dominate. This subject also situates the law contextually and emphasises the practical operation of the law in its social setting. Topics include choice of business entity, partnership law, the social, constitutional and administrative context of the Corporations Act, the external aspect of companies including registration and its effects and various methods of financing (including equity and debt), corporate governance, and external administration. This subject meets the requirements of the Council of Legal Education for admission to practice in Victoria in the area of Company Law. There is particular focus on the ethical dimension of firm behaviour, logical (even mathematical) reasoning, and modalities of writing.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse ethical and policy considerations and other conceptual factors as they apply to partnership and company law.
Analyse complex legal problems using knowledge of company law and provide indications of probable outcomes and/or processes and procedures to be followed.
Demonstrate advanced collaborative skills
Demonstrate critical reflection of the most appropriate legal form of business in particular business situations.

title: CONSTITUTIONAL LAW
syllabus_overview: Constitutional Law is a compulsory subject in the Juris Doctor program offered by the La Trobe Law School. In addition to making possible the acquisition of a general knowledge of federal and state constitutional law in Australia, this subject introduces students to a number of important topics pertaining to federal and state constitutional law in Australia. This includes an examination of the basic concepts and doctrines relating to Australia's federal structure as well as the sources and limits of Commonwealth and state legislative power. A number of specific Commonwealth heads of power will be examined and relevant interpretative (scope) and characterisation issues explored. Students will subsequently consider how various restrictions on these heads of power, such as Chapter III judicial power and express and implied constitutional rights and freedoms, operate in a situational context. Students will also canvass concepts relating to federal/state relations, including the interpretative approaches that apply when there is an apparent inconsistency of laws. This subject seeks to develop student's constitutional problem-solving skills as well as aiming to develop a theoretical appreciation of the significance of Australian constitutionalism.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of federal and state constitutional law and of the fundamental principles that underpin Australian constitutional law.
Critically analyse constitutional doctrine and judicial reasoning in constitutional cases in the light of fundamental constitutional principles.
Demonstrate problem-solving skills using constitutional and interpretative methods.

title: CIVIL DISPUTE RESOLUTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the procedural laws, rules and policy issues relating to the resolution of civil disputes in an adversarial system. The following topics are covered: the overarching obligations of parties and practitioners; the civil jurisdiction of Australian courts; initiating proceedings; service; joinder; parties to litigation; defining the questions for trial; obtaining evidence; interlocutory orders; disposition without trial; alternative dispute resolution; settlement; extra-judicial determination of issues; trial; appeal; costs; and enforcement of judgements.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of how to pursue a legal claim or defence for a client as effectively as possible.
Critically analyse, evaluate and apply civil procedure laws and rules, in order to find solutions to legal disputes.
Demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of how grievances are translated into a legal claim or defence in written form using the conventions of legal drafting

title: INTERNATIONAL CYBERCRIME
syllabus_overview: This subject explores a range of issues concerning cybercrimes that cross national borders. The cybercrimes to be explored include from among the following: hacking, ransomware, online fraud, online copyright crimes, cyberterrorism, cyberstalking, child abuse material, and hate online. You will also examine issues concerning: organised crime and the dark web; the policing and prosecution of cybercrime; the international Convention on Cybercrime; and efforts to harmonise cybercrime laws and improve law enforcement co-operation across international boundaries. You will analyse and critically assess the laws and policies relating to transnational cybercrimes and explore ways of resolving the issues raised.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess laws, policies and arguments concerning issues relating to international cybercrime.
Research and analyse laws, policies and issues relating to international cybercrime.
Present persuasive arguments concerning issues relating to international cybercrime.

title: DISABILITY AND THE LAW
syllabus_overview: People with disabilities encounter significant inequity and discrimination as they seek to exercise their rights as equal citizens to participate in society and access services and community facilities.
