learning_outcomes: Explain standards, codes and considerations relevant to aspects of machine design.
Identify and analyse complex mechanical engineering problems using standard methodologies.
Select and analyse relevant materials to solve engineering problems considering safety, wear, failure, material properties and cost requirements.
Design solutions to mechanical problems that are safe, sustainable and functional.

title: BURDEN OF DISEASE
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the current and historical health burden posed by major communicable and non-communicable diseases, in Australia and globally. You will interrogate the worldwide causation and prevalence of high-burden diseases and learn about current and emerging prevention and treatment strategies, and expected clinical outcomes. Skills you will develop include sourcing, interrogating and describing health data.
learning_outcomes: Describe the approaches used to prevent, diagnose and treat clinically significant diseases and injuries
Describe the aetiology and symptoms of conditions that cause significant mortality and/or morbidity in Australia
Extract and interpret data regarding the incidence and mortality of major health conditions
Compare the impact on populations of medical conditions that pose major health burdens in Australia versus worldwide, and over time
Outline factors that influence human lifespans and healthspans
Communicate medical and scientific information coherently using audience-appropriate language individually or as part of a team

title: NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE
syllabus_overview: Neurological diseases impose a substantial health burden on Australian society, and the impact of these conditions is likely to grow as the population ages. In this subject you will consider the impact of neurological diseases together with current and emerging approaches to detect, diagnose and treat them. Existing knowledge of the aetiology and underlying pathology of neurological disease will be examined with an emphasis on cellular and molecular mechanisms with reference to congenital neurological conditions, stroke, traumatic brain injury and the major neurodegenerative diseases. Together with an exploration of how neuroscience knowledge continues to evolve, this subject will provide a comprehensive understanding of the science of neurological disease and the innovative strategies being developed to combat them.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the experience of neurological disease from published stories and convey a disease overview to peers in an audio-visual format of choice.
Critically analyse and evaluate the neuroscience literature.
Synthesize complex multi-faceted information to develop an in-depth knowledge of specific neurological conditions.

Drawing on diverse perspectives and evidence-based approaches, students will demonstrate an ability to think critically and reflect on a range of topics in neuroscience through interactive discussion.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: Foundations in Biomedical Science introduces students to fundamental concepts for their future studies in biomedical science. These include the evidence-based and evolving nature of biomedical science and the important role of data in its evolution. You will be encouraged to develop skills in quantitative literacy and apply those skills to solve problems. Topics covered will include the emergence of evidence-based medicine, quantitative units in a biological context, conventions in describing and presenting data and an introduction to using data to solve problems. You will also establish an e-portfolio to encourage development of metacognition and reflection as they develop as biomedical scientists.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate scientific ideas together with supporting evidence in both oral and written forms.
Identify, analyse, interpret and represent quantitative data to solve problems in biomedical science.
Work in teams to evaluate contemporary issues in biomedical science by making accurate observations and developing reasonable inferences.
Describe the evidence-based nature of Biomedical Science and recognise the evolving nature and diversity of the current consensus.

title: CANCER
syllabus_overview: More Australians die from cancers than from any other cause. This subject provides a holistic exploration of this important disease category, encompassing epidemiology, causation and therapy. We consider factors that influence the development and spread of cancers and how they affect bodily functions to provoke illness and death. Traditional and modern strategies for cancer detection, diagnosis and treatment are explored. We discuss current challenges and avenues for research to improve the prevention and treatment of cancer.
learning_outcomes: Describe approaches to develop and test anti-cancer therapies
Explain how cancers are detected and diagnosed
Demonstrate proficiency in cancer research techniques, data analysis and interpretation
Define remaining challenges and outline emerging approaches to prevent cancer or improve patient outcomes
Discuss the molecular factors that stimulate cancer development and spread
Compare the mechanisms and performance of traditional and modern anti-cancer therapies
Describe the burden of illness and premature death imposed by cancers, in Australia and worldwide

title: APPLICATIONS OF BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject you will explore various "real-world" applications of the biomedical science learned throughout your degree. Through the prism of forensic biology, the drug development process and traditional and complementary medicine students will further develop their problem-solving and analytical skills as they work individually and in teams to demonstrate their ability to communicate scientific findings as evidence to support a position or argument.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of key principles involved in: the development and testing of therapeutic goods for human use; the use of biological tests in forensic applications and the use and evaluation of traditional and complementary medicine.
Communicate complex scientific information coherently using audience-appropriate language in written, oral and/or multimedia formats.
Critically evaluate and interpret data to demonstrate an appreciation of the nuanced and often complex and contestable nature of science
Collaborate effectively and productively with peers to explore facets of a "real-world" problem and synthesise a coherent solution supported by evidence or clearly reasoned argument.

title: CARDIO-METABOLIC DISEASE
syllabus_overview: Humans require good heart, vasculature and metabolic function to avoid serious illness and death. Diseases associated with deficiencies or defects in these systems represent a major, and increasing, health burden. This subject will canvass the developmental and lifestyle factors that can contribute to cardiovascular disease, and consider the way in which these risk factors have changed over time and geographically. We will consider the interplay between metabolism and cardiovascular function. A diverse range of preventative, pharmacological and surgical therapies will be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the lifestyle, genetic and molecular factors that pre-dispose to cardio-metabolic diseases
Compare the mechanisms and performance of traditional and emerging treatments for cardiovascular and metabolic diseases
Describe the burden of illness and premature death imposed by cardio-metabolic diseases, in Australia and worldwide
Explain how cardiovascular and metabolic diseases are detected and diagnosed

title: ADVANCED BIOCHEMISTRY AND MEDICAL BIOLOGY LABORATORY COURSE
syllabus_overview: This is a thematic, practical-based subject where students will gain experience in current techniques in molecular biology and biochemistry. It will include integrated practicals where students will clone, recombinantly express and purify a chimeric protein.
learning_outcomes: Explain concepts and principles underlying current techniques in molecular biology and biochemistry using appropriate vocabulary.
Discuss current techniques and concepts in molecular biology and biochemistry with your peers both orally and in writing.
Create a scientific report by analysing and evaluating experimental data against relevant scientific literature.
Apply advanced techniques in molecular biology, biochemistry and protein purification to generate experimental data.
Apply fundamental and technical knowledge learned to solve theoretical problems in molecular biology and biochemistry.

title: ADVANCED LABORATORY RESEARCH PROJECT
syllabus_overview: This is a practical subject where theory meets practice in an authentic research laboratory setting. In this hands-on subject, you will gain experience in current cutting-edge techniques in molecular and biomedical biology through completing a laboratory placement project. Working in pairs or individually, you will dedicate 70 hours to practical work under the guidance and supervision of experienced research staff. Throughout the placement, you will conduct original research, meticulously document your progress in a laboratory notebook, write a project background, aims & methodology statement and complete a research report detailing your findings. Additionally, at the end of teaching period, you will advance your presentation skills by delivering a talk at a mini-symposium, where you will share your research discoveries with peers and academics. To further enrich your experience, you will participate in laboratory meetings where you will receive feedback on your research and instruction on the latest advancements in your chosen area of study including biochemistry, cellular biology, molecular biology, microbiology, anatomy and/or physiology. These meetings will also expand your effective scientific communication.
learning_outcomes: Enhance scientific communication skills by effectively articulating project background, aims, methodologies, and research findings in both written and oral formats.
Collect, analyse and critically evaluate information from scientific literature to prepare a scientific report.
Apply advanced techniques and methodologies in molecular and biomedical biology through hands-on laboratory experience.
Develop the ability to conduct original research, including carrying out experiments, along with generating and analysing experimental data.
Cultivate collaborative skills by working effectively as part of a research team and participating constructively in lab meetings to give and receive feedback on research progress.
Retain accurate records of work in the laboratory and maintain a laboratory book demonstrating adherence to best practices in scientific documentation.

title: HONOURS BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE A
syllabus_overview: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Honours) is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree in the disciplines of Biomedical Science or Science. The aim of this stand alone Honours program in the La Trobe Rural Health School (LRHS) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical and theoretical expertise in biomedical science. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. MED4001 is the first of two 60CP subjects for Biomedical Science Honours in the LRHS. Students must take MED4001 first.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of ethical issues involved in scientific research.
Demonstrate the ability to work effectively as a practicing researcher, both independently and/or as part of a team.

Demonstrate highly developed analytical, problem solving and writing skills through the application of complex theoretical concepts that underpin a field of science to the solution of scientific problems.
Critically evaluate research literature, synthesise the information obtained and demonstrate appropriate ethical approaches to research.
Choose appropriate methodologies to address a science research question, and apply safe laboratory practices when performing experiments.
Apply advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.

title: HONOURS BIOMEDICAL SCIENCE B
syllabus_overview: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Honours) is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree in the disciplines of Biomedical Science or Science. The aim of this stand alone Honours program in the La Trobe Rural Health School (LRHS) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical and theoretical expertise in biomedical science. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. MED4002 is the second of two 60CP subjects for Biomedical Science Honours in the LRHS. Students must complete MED4001 before undertaking MED4002.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Demonstrate awareness of ethical issues involved in scientific research.
Choose appropriate methodologies to address a science research question, and apply safe laboratory practices when performing experiments.

Demonstrate highly developed analytical, problem solving and writing skills through the application of complex theoretical concepts that underpin a field of science to the solution of scientific problems.
Critically evaluate research literature, synthesise the information obtained and demonstrate appropriate ethical approaches to research.
Demonstrate the ability to work effectively as a practicing researcher, both independently and/or as part of a team.

title: SPORT DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the theory and practice of sport development in terms of its role in fostering participation in sport and physical activity, and you will learn how government and organisational policies influence the delivery of sport development programs . You will learn to design effective sport development programs and practices that assists with the planning, designing, managing and evaluation of sport systems and pathways for sports organisations and communities, in a range of cultural contexts.
learning_outcomes: Identify the social and ethical considerations for sport delivery as it applies to development programs
Demonstrate effective communication and problem-solving skills in the interpretation, analysis, implementation and evaluation of sport development programs and services
Identify the systems that significantly influence sport development in the context of mass participation and elite performance
Analyse, communicate and develop a sport development plan for an Australian sport organisation

title: EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the key actors in Australia's employment relations system. You will explore the world of work, and the legal and regulatory frameworks which govern the employment relationship. You will analyse the role of trade unions, the processes of determining the terms and conditions of employment, and the responsibilities of employers to create a safe working environment. You will also explore how vulnerable workers are protected by the employment relations system. You will appreciate how conflicts and disputes between employers and employees can be resolved, and reflect upon your own conflict management and negotiation skills.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between different forms of workplace conflict, and demonstrate how workplace disputes can be resolved

Compare and contrast Fox's taxonomy of values in employment relations, and analyse how these values underpin the conduct of different parties involved in employment relations in contemporary organisations
Discuss how employment relations influences the performance of employees, organisations and the national economic and social outcomes
Identify and explain the key elements of State regulation of employment relations in Australia
Critically evaluate the role of the State, management and unions in the employment relations system
Analyse a collective bargaining situation and develop a proposed collective agreement through negotiations with differing stakeholders.

title: AGRIBUSINESS MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Agribusiness describes the food and fibre production and marketing system, which is made up of thousands of businesses ranging from small farms to large multinational companies. A focus for this subject is the effective and efficient management of agribusinesses, which is strongly linked to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) number 12 - Responsible Production and Consumption . In this subject you will be introduced to managers and the management of food, fibre and agribusiness firms. In doing so you will explore the concepts, processes, ideas, issues and experiences of managers and management that will enhance your effectiveness in performing the functions and tasks of an agribusiness manager.
learning_outcomes: Explain and apply the core concepts/theories underlying the effective management of agribusinesses
Demonstrate an understanding of the key elements of the agribusiness environment.
Critically reflect on the role of agribusiness managers in the context of current and future challenges.

title: HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the strategic and operational issues involved in managing staff in the workplace. You will examine the challenges facing human resource managers in contemporary Australian organisations and seeks to develop an understanding of human resource management practices in our continually changing social, economic, industrial relations and organisational environments. You will explore the reasons underpinning the increasing recognition of human resource management (HRM) within organisations as well as the field's underlying purposes. Throughout this subject an emphasis is placed on a strategic approach to HRM in addition to the functional and operational aspects.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and defend the basic concepts of human resource management from theoretical and applied perspectives, including how these make human resource management a unique source of competitive advantage for contemporary organisations.
Justify the need for organisations to facilitate the strategic partnership between management and employees
Critically analyse in teams and individually academic, business and government approaches to a range of Human Resource Management topics

title: MANAGEMENT AND ORGANISATIONS
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces the theories of management and organisations that underpin contemporary management practices. In order to develop an appreciation of organisations as complex and multifaceted, you will study the management of different kinds of organisations - from government to private, from small to large, from local to multi-national, from start-ups to mature firms, from technical production to political advocacy. You will learn about the roles and skills of managers; organisations and cultural diversity; globalisation; technology and the changing nature of work; organisational design; introduction to human resource management; motivation and ethics and social responsibility.
learning_outcomes: Describe key management functions, roles, and skills, and explain how they support effective decision-making
Identify current trends and explain how change influences management practices in a global context
Explain and evaluate management theories, principles and concepts that support effective organisational management

title: FOUNDATIONS OF MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This foundational subject provides an introduction to the management discipline and an overview of the evolution of management theory, the fundamental management concepts and analyses issues relating to the management of firms operating in both the local and global environments. This subject explores management as a process of planning, organising, leading and controlling within the context of both individual effect and organisational outcomes. This subject also highlights threats and opportunities relating to economic changes, technological changes and the profound changes of how organisations are managed.
learning_outcomes: Identify current trends and critically evaluate the impact of change and how it influences management practices.
Explain, and critically evaluate management theories, principles and concepts that guide the effective management of modern organisations.
Explain the four management functions (planning, leading, organising and controlling) and demonstrate how they relate to organisational success.

title: INTRODUCTION TO INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the foundational components in the study of international business. You will learn about the socioeconomic, political, cultural, technological, and environmental forces that shape the international marketplace. You will identify and analyse the factors that influence the internationalisation of organisations and investigate the key determinants of business success in the international environment. You will examine how individuals, organisations, and countries participate in the process of globalisation. You will develop cultural awareness and explore the factors that contribute to effective work in multicultural teams across borders.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate how socioeconomic, political, cultural, technological, and environmental forces influence international business.
Apply international business concepts and theories to explain the internationalisation process of firms.
Demonstrate interpersonal and cultural awareness skills to effectively engage in academic discussions and work in teams.
Research and analyse current and historical business issues to examine how individuals, organisations, and countries participate in the process of globalisation.

title: ORGANISATIONAL BEHAVIOUR
syllabus_overview: Organisational Behaviour will provide an introduction to individual characteristics, interpersonal relationships and group processes, as they relate to individual behaviour and outcomes in organisations. Organisational behaviour theory and concepts will be applied to current organisational problems relating to motivation, decision-making, teamwork, leadership and diversity. In this subject, you will develop the capabilities to work effectively in teams and lead teams to achieve their goals.
learning_outcomes: Analyse team dynamics and design processes for effective teamwork
Explain the forces that affect behaviour in organisations with reference to the theory of organisational behaviour
Critically analyse and interpret information to support effective problem-solving and decision-making
Review your own interpersonal skills and self-diagnose strategies when improvement is required

title: SPORT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the sport industry and the unique features of sport while developing the skills of critical analysis, appraisal, and reflection. You will examine the relationship between sport and society, reflect upon the implication of the UN’s sustainability goals to the sport industry and sport managers, and be encouraged to challenge norms and ideologies. You will also reflect on the continued significance of sport, in Australian culture specifically, while understanding the role of sport managers in being sensitive to that significance and its impact on day-to-day management.
learning_outcomes: Examine the role of sport in society and identify the unique features of sport management and the Australian sport industry
Apply the theoretical principles of management to sport and sports organisations across the profit, non-profit and public sectors
Critically assess and challenge the role of the sport manager in responding to sport’s significance in Australian culture
Develop sport research appraisal skills and understand their application to the role of sport manager

title: RECRUITMENT AND SELECTION
syllabus_overview: Recruitment and selection practices are fundamental function of Human Resource Management. The ability to attract and secure a pool of high-quality talent within the organisation is crucial to meeting the organisation’s strategic goals and securing a sustainable competitive advantage. In this subject, you will acquire the knowledge and skills needed to design, build, implement and evaluate an effective recruitment and selection process. You will also explore the ethical and legal principles which govern recruitment and selection in Australia. You will also learn how to design and implement and effective job analysis and evaluation, to assist in determining the employee qualities that employers are looking for to perform the job in question.
learning_outcomes: Compose accurate job descriptions based on comprehensive analysis and assessment that support informed and effective decision-making in the recruitment and selection process.
Design targeted recruitment and selection strategies by applying appropriate selection and assessment techniques tailored to specific roles, to enhance the efficiency and fairness of hiring outcomes.

Evaluate the legal and ethical implications of incorporating technologies into recruitment and selection, considering anti-discrimination laws and equitable hiring practices, while demonstrating effective teamwork skills in collaborative analysis and presentation

title: SPORT FACILITY AND VENUE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Sport facilities and venues are central to the delivery of sport and recreation activities. In this subject, you will develop theoretical knowledge and practical experience of the issues that underpin the success of sport facility planning and management. Issues examined may include effective and efficient sport facility and venue planning, programming, safety and risk assessment, and crowd management practices. Industry engagement is a feature of this subject allowing you to apply your theoretical knowledge and reflect on contemporary sport management practices
learning_outcomes: Adapt knowledge and managerial skills to make decisions that provide inclusive, sustainable and culturally relevant sport facility services
Identify the role sport facilities play in the development and delivery of community infrastructure and services
Critically analyse management performance of sports facilities or venues
Adapt and apply theoretical knowledge, management best practice and skills in diverse contexts that underpin the effective management of sport facilities and venues

title: INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: The phenomena of internationalisation and globalisation have substantial implications for the human resource management of organisations. In addition to broad strategic concerns, issues such as understanding and appreciating differences between local environments and international staff placement are complex and have far-reaching implications. Even organisations that choose not to operate across national boundaries are affected directly by internationalisation and globalisation. In this subject, you will build on knowledge acquired in the 'Human Resource Management' subject and apply this in an international context using both theoretical and applied approaches. Thereby, you will gain an understanding of the strategies and policies available to organisations in this increasingly important area.
learning_outcomes: Understand the important role, the objectives and purposes of international human resource management (HRM) in multinational organisations
Define and develop international HRM plans/strategies in a variety of industries both individually and in a team environment
Critically analyse the dynamic nature of national and international context and emerging trends and disruptive forces in the marketplace and their impact on the management of people in organisations
Critically analyse theoretical and applied approaches to international HRM

title: OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with a comprehensive understanding of both operations management and project management, equipping them with the knowledge and skills necessary to thrive operational excellence in projects and drive successful outcomes. Through hands-on and case-based approaches, students will gain practical experience in applying operations and project management principles and good practices across different sectors. You will develop the ability to make informed decisions using both qualitative and quantitative tools, ensuring that business processes and projects are aligned with operational objectives. By integrating key concepts such as time management, cost management, risk management, stakeholder engagement, resource allocation, and performance evaluation, you will be prepared to lead operational improvements and project initiatives with confidence.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate operations and project management practices in achieving financial, social, ethical, and environmental objectives to support continuous improvement and sustainable business practices
Analyse business challenges and develop solutions that improve internal operations, including process design, scheduling, risk management, and supply chain coordination
Demonstrate how operations and project management contribute to business success by enhancing efficiency, resource utilisation, and operational outcomes

title: EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the key actors in Australia's employment relations system. You will explore the world of work, and the legal and regulatory frameworks which govern the employment relationship. You will analyse the role of trade unions, the processes of determining the terms and conditions of employment, and the responsibilities of employers to create a safe working environment. You will also explore how vulnerable workers are protected by the employment relations system. You will appreciate how conflicts and disputes between employers and employees can be resolved, and reflect upon your own conflict management and negotiation skills.
learning_outcomes: Explain how employment relations may influence the performance of employees, organisations, and the national economic and social outcomes
Distinguish between different forms of workplace conflict and demonstrate how workplace disputes can be resolved
Explain the main forms of non-union employee representation in Australia and investigate how workplace disputes can be resolved
Identify and explain the key elements of state regulation of employment relations in Australia, considering the role of the state, management and unions

title: BUSINESS ETHICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to a number of moral frameworks that you will use to analyse ethical issues for management. You will participate in an innovative and challenging learning experience/process via the completion of online activities and invigilated assessment tasks. You will adopt relevant roles to participate in a high-level ethics and rights discussion and debate, considering issues relevant to organisations, global trade, advertising, the environment, politics, corruption and governance and the person as an individual. Working individually and in teams, within a collaborative learning environment, you will explore and analyse relevant literature to develop moral reasoning, in order to present an ethically based case to their peers and/or external parties.
learning_outcomes: Analyse complex issues in a business ethics context.
Critique ethical theories using discipline-specific language and concepts within a business ethics context
Apply ethical theories to support or reject specific moral positions as they apply to business ethics dilemmas.

title: MANAGING ACROSS BORDERS
syllabus_overview: This subject will develop and enhance your understanding and appreciation of how constant and/or evolutionary changes to the international business environment influence the operations and conduct of domestic and cross border For-Profit and Not-for-Profit enterprises. You will examine key strategic and structural drivers and tools that support globalisation and the establishment of multi-national entities. You will be exposed to models, approaches and challenges of successful cross-cultural management, negotiations, communications, and knowledge transfer.
learning_outcomes: Research and analyse key opportunities, challenges, and processes in sustainable international business development, including market selection and entry, both individually and in diverse teams
Critically analyse current business-related issues and factors affecting the impact of international management and/or across-border practices and processes on domestic businesses
Analyse and understand the implications for managers of ethical, social, corporate and environmental responsibilities on the behaviour of multi-national / across-border enterprises, including NFP's
Assess the impact of differences in national cultural values and social institutions on the management of multi-national and across border enterprises, including Not For Profits (NFP's)

title: VOLUNTEER MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theory and practice of managing volunteer labour in the community sector. You will learn about the nature and scope of volunteering, the theory and practice of recruiting and the challenges of managing and developing volunteers in a range of settings. You will examine specific issues related to the management of volunteers in specialised roles (officials, coaches, administrators and event volunteers) and specific legal issues relevant to volunteers.
learning_outcomes: Work in a team to understand and research volunteer management approaches
Demonstrate a systematic approach to volunteer management
Develop and incorporate a comprehensive volunteer program for a non-profit organisation
Develop and assess the impact of non-profit voluntary service on social change and community development

title: HUMAN RESOURCE ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the relationship between human resource management and organisational strategy and analyse the impact of high-performance work systems on employee attitudes and behaviours, and organisational performance. You will explore the impact of HR practices and initiatives on various employee-related metrics as well as organisational performance and will learn how to make data-driven decisions for strategically managing your organization's workforce. You will learn how to analyse and interpret qualitative and quantitative employee-related data to solve complex HR issues with new strategic proficiencies and develop an understanding of how HR analytics contributes to a more successful performance of HR’s strategic role.
learning_outcomes: Apply different levels of workforce analytics, and know how to develop and use workforce analytics for managing Human Resources strategically in an organisation
Develop, identify, and implement different types of data as required for Human Resources related problem-solving and decision-making
Understand reasons for an increasing interest and attention to the application of analytics to the field of HR and key functions of HR analytics that add value to organisations
Learn how to use Tableau for analysing Human Resources data and creating a compelling Human Resources Annual Report that summarises the HR function's performance
Understand why Human Resources (HR) needs to align with business strategy and how HR affects the bottom line of an organisation

title: SPORT POLICY AND GOVERNANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the skills necessary to critically analyse the creation, implementation and review of policy and the principles of good governance in sport. You will examine the organisational structures and governance models typically found in sport at the community, state/provincial and national/professional levels in Australia and internationally. You will also consider the relationship between good governance and strategic planning, decision-making processes, risk management, and policy development/implementation.
learning_outcomes: Apply sport policy concepts in the critical evaluation of a corporate policy of a sport organisation as a student team
Identify key milestones in the development of Australian sport policy and sport governance
Apply sport policy concepts in the analysis and comparison of a diverse range of government sport policies
Compare and contrast Government Sport Policy in Australia

title: MANAGEMENT CONSULTING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the knowledge and skills needed by management consultants to address contemporary business problems/opportunities at the individual, organisational and industry/societal level. This subject includes a work based learning experience and provides you with the equivalent of a capstone experience. You will undertake and be assessed on structured activities that allow you to draw, apply and demonstrate your accumulated knowledge from previous subjects and your studies to date. You will learn the mastery of specific consulting tools and techniques and learn how to work successfully in teams. You will be encouraged to plan, reflect and modify your solutions to improve the outcomes in your consulting projects.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate key professional attributes expected of business and management graduates, including time management, business acumen, project management, teamwork, innovation and the ability to manage complexity
Apply interpersonal skills to work in teams and to communicate effectively with clients
Research and analyse business issues to develop practical and ethical recommendations within the constraints of a client organisation
Integrate the theory and practice of business and management studies to solve real-world business problems

title: SPORT MARKETING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine the relationship between marketing and sport and develop the skills necessary to create effective marketing programs for sport products and services, sport programs, sporting organisations (professional and amateur), sport codes, players/athletes and sports events. You will explore the special nature of the sports market, including developing an understanding of consumer behaviour in sport – both spectating and participating – and the implications of that behaviour for marketing practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to plan and develop effective marketing campaigns to meet the strategic marketing objectives of sport organisations
Demonstrate an ability to engage effectively in diverse teams to apply a range of sport marketing concepts in various contexts
Articulate the implications of consumer behaviour for the marketing of and marketing through sport
Determine the appropriate marketing theory and apply a range of tools and creative strategies to effectively promote and market a professional sport organisation and/or event

title: SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject will focus on the role of social entrepreneurship and social enterprise in relation to sustainable development, social impact and value creation. You will explore definitions and characteristics of social entrepreneurship, and different forms and frameworks of social enterprise organisations in dynamic entrepreneurial ecosystems. This includes social oriented community based initiatives, equality issues, sustainable development goals, and contextualisation of industry typologies and business contexts, such as healthcare and the care economy.
learning_outcomes: Apply a social entrepreneurship mindset to solve entrepreneurial challenges and embrace business/industry opportunities
Apply relevant entrepreneurship tools to develop and evaluate successful social enterprise solutions
Engage effectively in diverse teams to explain the role and characteristics of social entrepreneurship
Analyse different forms and frameworks of social entrepreneurship and social enterprise

title: CONTEMPORARY ISSUES IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will critically analyse and reflect on a series of contemporary issues that influence the management and delivery of sport at local, national and/or international levels. These may be influenced by various political, economic, social, environmental, demographic, and technological factors. Contexts examined range from community sport organizations to elite and professional sport.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the impact of various social, cultural, political and physical environments on the management and sustainable practice of sport
Analyse key current critical issues relevant to participation and competition in local, state, national and global sport
Formulate a response to a real world, contemporary sport scenario to a diverse set of stakeholders

title: HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: The pace and volume of organisational change is drawing increasing attention to the ways that human resource development (HRD) activities can ensure that organisation members have what it takes to successfully meet these challenges. In this subject you will focus on an integrated and strategic approach to HRD which fosters a long-term, work-related learning capacity. You will examine the foundational concepts of HRD (including the theory of learning) and the HRD process from theoretical and practical perspectives. You will also examine HRD applications within modern business organisations including skills, and technical training, coaching, career management and, organisational development.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse human resource development gaps and develop innovative strategies for facilitating career development and professional practice
Analyse and communicate a trend or issue that is relevant to Human Resource Development.
Design, implement and evaluate a human resource development program.

title: LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: Leaders have recently had their assumptions challenged about how organisations succeed. Additionally, leaders are struggling to make sense of the shifting environment and learning how to lead the people in their companies effectively and successfully in the midst of turmoil. In this subject, you will examine key leadership theories and the current trends in responsible leadership across a range of workplace contexts. You will apply these theories to critically address these issues that are directly relevant to the current turbulent environment. In this subject, you will have the opportunity to examine, discuss and solve real-world leadership problems.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse key leadership theories and approaches and evaluate their impact on organisational outcomes.
Research and apply evidence-based leadership theories and findings to address real-world management challenges, fostering sustainable individual and organisational growth.
Develop and apply practical leadership skills to create positive changes in a diverse range of organisational contexts.

title: ORGANISATIONAL CHANGE AND DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the various concepts of Organisational Change and Development (OCD). Organisational change and development is concerned with the application of behavioural science knowledge and practice to help achieve greater organisational effectiveness. The focus of this subject is on enhancing the total organisational system within the content of the wider environment in order to enhance the organisation's capacity to achieve its goals. You will develop an understanding of the relevance of theories and principles that underlie the practice of organisational change and development in contemporary organisations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles that underlie the practice of organisational change and development in contemporary organisations.
Critically evaluate the relevance of theories and practices of organisational change in contemporary organisations.
Define and describe the knowledge and skills needed in order to bring about socially responsible and sustainable change management practices in contemporary organisations.
Apply the analytical skills to implement management processes and actions appropriate for local and global management environments.

title: STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain a comprehensive understanding of techniques and models applied in organisations to ensure sustainable competitive advantage. This involves application of key theories to decisions and actions taken by an organisation's senior management team to devise a long-term plan with the intention of developing the organisation's core competencies and increasing the organisation's competitiveness. Key topics in this subject include; understanding the dynamics of the internal and external environments, Value Chain Analysis, the 5 Forces Model, corporate level strategy, business level strategy, modes of entry into domestic and international markets, propensity to innovate and level of competition and corporate governance. The focus will be on developing your ability to understand, evaluate and effectively apply strategic management knowledge to modern organisations.
learning_outcomes: Integrate theories and techniques in the analysis of the strategic management options available to diverse global organisations.
Design a global innovation strategy that aims to enable firms to achieve positional advantage and superior performance.
Analyse the main theoretical approaches to global strategic management and understand the economic, social, and ethical contexts that give rise to their formulation
Appraise and apply the concepts and tools of business strategy in a global context

title: REMUNERATION AND PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine contemporary remuneration and performance management practices from theoretical and applied perspectives. You will focus on debates about moves away from 'traditional' position-based pay towards performance-related remuneration. You are encouraged to consider the relationships between reward systems and employee participation and their impacts on organisational performance at individual and group levels. This subject is built on research as well as real-life examples to explore issues in pay, performance management, motivation, strategy, fairness and organisational effectiveness. The subject provides you with the critical and analytical tools to evaluate the merits of diverse performance and reward management systems in modern business organisations.
learning_outcomes: Solve practical problems that occur in designing pay and performance systems
Evaluate the strategic, psychological, ethical and social implications of remuneration and performance management theories through writing and discuss the approaches that spring from these
Identify the assumptions underpinning different concepts of remuneration and performance management, and critically analyse the theories on which they are based through written and oral form

title: SPORTS PRACTICUM
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build upon operational and management material covered in previous aspects of the program. You will have the opportunity to use the sport management workplace as a rich learning environment from which you can analyse current practices, appraise personal and professional competencies, and apply your theoretical knowledge to contemporary sport management.
learning_outcomes: Enhance your employability skills through career professional development
Prepare, execute and evaluate a vocational experience through the medium of a placement contract.
Apply understand and reflect on contemporary concepts and approaches to Sport Management.

title: VOLUNTEER MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theory and practice of managing volunteer labour in the community sector. You will learn about the nature and scope of volunteering, the theory and practice of recruiting and the challenges of managing and developing volunteers in a range of settings. You will examine specific issues related to the management of volunteers in specialised roles (officials, coaches, administrators and event volunteers) and specific legal issues relevant to volunteers.
learning_outcomes: Develop and assess the impact of non-profit voluntary service on social change and community development
Work in a team to understand and research volunteer management approaches
Develop and incorporate a comprehensive volunteer program for a non-profit organisation
Demonstrate a systematic approach to volunteer management

title: FOUNDATION OF LOGISTICS AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the fundamentals of logistics and supply chain management, along with their implications for operational and strategic business decisions. You will explore essential theories and concepts related to demand and supply planning, distribution network design, sustainable procurement, service supply chain and operations, international transport and logistics, as well as supply chain sustainability and the circular economy. Throughout the subject, you will have the opportunity to learn these concepts in a range of business contexts, preparing you to advance your knowledge in each of those specialised areas. Through both independent and collaborative work on a variety of authentic activities, you will develop foundational knowledge in logistics and supply chain management by solving real-world problems. Additionally, you will cultivate critical and creative thinking, quantitative, and interpersonal skills essential for success in the logistics and supply chain profession.
learning_outcomes: Propose informed solutions to real-world logistics and supply chain challenges, through both individual and collaborative efforts.
Critically analyse foundational concepts in logistics and supply chain management across various business settings.
Examine and evaluate the principles of logistics and supply chain management.

title: ANALYTICS FOR SUPPLY CHAIN AND LOGISTICS
syllabus_overview: Analytics empower managers to make data-driven decisions, optimise inventory management, forecast demand accurately, and streamline the entire supply chain processes. This subject will provide you with a deep understanding of how using data and analytical tools can help supply chain analysts to create efficient and effective logistics and supply chain operations. You will explore the analytical methods and tools used by practitioners to effectively analyse supply chain data, extract actionable knowledge and make decisions. You will study the key drivers of logistics and supply chain performance, including demand and supply planning, inventory planning, facility location analysis and network design. You will learn how to evaluate and select a suitable tool among a variety of methods used for the conception, design, implementation and operation of logistics and supply chains, and apply it in the design and implementation of innovative solutions. Using authentic case studies, you will develop the critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to identify problems in the supply chain and develop practical solutions to address these problems.
learning_outcomes: Select and apply appropriate analytics methods to solve complex problems in supply chain and logistics operations.
Apply descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to critically analyse and optimise the performance of supply chains and logistics operations.
Utilise data analytics tools to develop decision support systems for supply chain and logistics operations.

title: MANAGEMENT OF SERVICE SUPPLY CHAIN AND OPERATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the theories and practices of supply chain and operations management in the emerging service global economy. You will examine the distinctive characteristics of service supply chains and operations, and their implications for the design of businesses. You will have the opportunity to acquire a set of distinctive skills to effectively design and manage service supply chains and operations in a variety of service industry sectors, via real world case studies. Topics include service-dominant logic versus goods-dominant logic, strategic decisions, capacity management, supply risk and agility, service process design, performance analysis and metrics, service delivery assurance and service innovation.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the issues and challenges facing service providers managing operations and supply chains in a rapidly changing global context
Critically analyse various service supply chain frameworks, and configure an appropriate design to ensure the effectiveness of service supply chain and operations
Explore and propose defensible solutions to operations/supply chain problems in a variety of service industry sectors
Assess the body of knowledge and fundamental themes and issues surrounding service supply chain and operations management

title: ORGANISATIONAL BEHAVIOUR AND MANAGEMENT PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the principles of human behaviour in organisational settings and their application to management practice. You will develop an advanced understanding of the psychological, social, and structural factors that shape behaviour at individual, group, and organisational levels. Key topics include motivation, decision-making, communication, team dynamics, conflict resolution, organisational culture, and cross-cultural management. Through case studies, simulations, and reflective activities, you will apply management theories and develop practical skills to analyse organisational challenges, recommend evidence-based practices, and foster positive, effective workplaces.
learning_outcomes: Apply key theories and models of organisational behaviour and management to critically analyse complex workplace scenarios.
Analyse how individual, group, and organisational factors influence performance, engagement, and well-being.
Critically reflect on personal attributes, behaviours, and management capabilities to identify areas for ongoing professional development and strengthen practical leadership and teamwork skills.
Design and propose evidence-based management practices to improve employee engagement, organisational culture, and overall effectiveness.

title: SUSTAINABLE PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLY PLANNING
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with a comprehensive understanding of strategic sourcing, procurement, and supply planning, empowering them to contribute effectively to sustainable procurement and enhance supply chain performance. Students will develop practical expertise and proficiency in using industry-leading tools and data-driven decision-making methods for real-world procurement challenges. The subject also emphasizes critical analysis of environmental and social sustainability in procurement, focusing on ethical sourcing aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), preparing students to make informed decisions for a sustainable future. Hands-on training covers essential business and employability skills such as negotiation, RFP development, contract management, and supplier auditing, applicable to procurement and supply planning roles.
learning_outcomes: Design a procurement plan that addresses environmental and social sustainability, and ethical sourcing aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Critically analyse the role of strategic procurement and supply planning in enhancing the firm competitive advantage.
Identify and apply a diverse range of digital tools to make informed procurement and supply planning problems decisions.
Exercise professional judgement applicable to procurement and supply planning.

title: MANAGING INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
syllabus_overview: As the fourth industrial revolution connects people and industries throughout the world, managers and organisations must increasingly navigate issues related to globalisation, regionalisation and environmental analysis as well as assess political risk, culture and diversity, and global corporate responsibility. In this subject you will analyse and critique the interconnected issues of strategy, structure, culture, and people management in international business operations.
learning_outcomes: Apply relevant international management theories and research to practical management problems and challenges in multinational and transnational enterprises
Critically analyse how local, national and global trends affect management and strategy in multinational and transnational enterprises.
Apply relevant theories and research to align talent management with the strategic objectives and practical challenges of international management.
Critically analyse the role of ethics and corporate governance in international management.

title: CIRCULAR ECONOMY IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: The circular economy is an economic system designed to minimise waste and continually use resources. The circular economy aims to generate economic and social value while ensuring environmental sustainability by creating closed-loop systems that minimise resource input and waste output. As businesses transition towards this model, job requirements are evolving to prioritise sustainability and circular economy practices. This subject explores the interplay between the circular economy and value chain management. In consultation with industry partners, it is designed to provide an engaging learning journey to understand, strategize, and apply circular economy principles, including sustainable resource utilization, waste minimization, and the integration of repair, reuse, and recycling through the lens of value chain management. Students will have the opportunity to work on selected industry projects to enhance their practical skills in identifying and addressing circular economy challenges, utilizing various tools and data-driven methods. Emphasizing the significance and urgency of circular value chain strategies, this subject aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, preparing students to make informed and responsible decisions in various business settings, both individually and collectively. The applied nature of the subject delivery enables the development of critical business skills essential for roles in the circular economy and sustainability domains.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate teamwork and leadership skills to collectively strategise, communicate, and execute practical circular economy practices in various business settings.
Exercise professional judgment in addressing complex circular economy challenges.
Critically analyse circular economy principles within value chains to enhance competitive advantage of organisations in various settings.

title: INTERNATIONAL TRANSPORT AND LOGISTICS
syllabus_overview: When cargo flows and supply chains extend beyond national borders, the complexity of international transport and logistics activities increases. This subject focuses on the global transport of goods, which heavily relies on ships, aircraft, and trains. As a result, more stakeholders become involved, additional documentation is generated and transferred, financial payment risks intensify, and disruptions and uncertainties can impact supply chains. In this subject, you will acquire essential knowledge and develop job-ready skills necessary for roles such as international transport and logistics coordinators and freight forwarders. This includes gaining familiarity with trade and customs policies, understanding documentation requirements for efficient cargo flows and physical distribution, developing the ability to design international transport and logistics plans for various business scenarios, creating recovery plans to address changes and disruptions in international transport and logistics, and effectively communicating information and potential changes to stakeholders. Additionally, the subject explores sustainability concerns, data analytics, and emerging technologies related to digitalisation.
learning_outcomes: Design international transport and logistics plans for efficient, profitable, sustainable and resilient supply chains.
Exercise professional judgement and evaluate international logistics management practices for a collaborative supply chain.
Critically analyse the impact of international transport and logistics on a company's performance and collaborations within global supply chains.
Critically analyse the implications of trade policies, international conventions, sustainability commitments, and digitalisation on global transport, logistics, and supply chains.

title: TOTAL QUALITY MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a comprehensive introduction to Total Quality Management (TQM) and its practical applications in modern organisations. You will explore the historical evolution of quality management and its pivotal role in business contexts. The focus is on enhancing quality management practices to ensure consistent delivery of high-quality products and services. Throughout this subject, you will develop a thorough understanding of TQM principles and their integration into organisational frameworks. Emphasis is placed on equipping you with essential tools, techniques, and practices crucial for sustained organisational success. Topics covered include quality control methodologies, continuous improvement strategies, lean principles, Six Sigma methodologies, Kaizen practices, and other essential management techniques. Additionally, this subject aims to familiarize you with emerging trends in quality management, particularly in the realms of sustainability and digital transformation. By exploring these new perspectives, you will be prepared to address evolving challenges and leverage innovative approaches to drive quality improvements within contemporary organisations.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective teamwork and leadership in fostering efficiency and quality in operational contexts.
Apply TQM techniques and strategies to drive continuous improvement and enhance processes.
Critically analyse the principles of Total Quality Management (TQM) and operational excellence.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY IN SUPPLY CHAIN
syllabus_overview: Environmental sustainability and decarbonisation are no longer incidental but critical business success factors driving innovation across supply chains. However, achieving net-zero targets of emissions presents a multi-tiered challenge due to limited visibility into upstream supplier practices, fragmented transport and logistics networks, and the high cost of implementing sustainable solutions. This subject equips students with a comprehensive understanding of integrating environmental sustainability into end-to-end supply chain processes and operations. Students learn to use analytical and digital tools to solve real-world problems and make informed decisions on natural resource challenges and climate risks. Aligned with national and international regulations such as the Australian Sustainability Reporting Standards, this subject works towards evaluating and improving supply chain sustainability performance, with a particular focus on tackling Scope 3 supply chain greenhouse gas (GHG) emission challenges. Through active learning and authentic assessments, students acquire essential competencies for roles in environmental sustainability within logistics and supply chains, enabling effective implementation of sustainability initiatives to meet the demands of today's eco-conscious business environment.
learning_outcomes: Apply a variety of analytical tools to inform evidence-based decisions in environmental sustainability within supply chains
Evaluate supply chain sustainability performance and compliance against national and international environmental standards and regulations
Critically assess the impact of environmental sustainability on the whole supply chain
Develop effective environmental sustainability plans for supply chains driven by teamwork and leadership

title: MANAGEMENT OF SERVICE SUPPLY CHAIN AND OPERATIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject critically examines the theories and practices of supply chain and operations management within the emerging global service economy. You will examine the distinctive characteristics of service supply chains and operations, and evaluate their implications for the design and management of contemporary organisations. Through real-world case studies, you will develop advanced skills to design, implement, and improve service supply chains and operations across diverse service industry sectors. Key topics include service- versus goods-dominant logic, service supply chain management frameworks, service delivery performance and innovations.
learning_outcomes: Develop and justify solutions to operations and supply chain problems across diverse service industries.
Critically analyse service supply chain frameworks and design effective approaches for managing service provision.
Critically assess the key theories, themes, and issues in service supply chain and operations management.
Critically examine the challenges facing service providers in managing operations and supply chains in a (rapidly changing) global context.

title: ANALYTICS FOR SUPPLY CHAIN AND LOGISTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject examines how analytics can be used to optimise logistics and supply chain operations in a global context. You will gain advanced knowledge of data-driven approaches to demand forecasting, inventory management, facility location, and network design, and evaluate their impact on supply chain performance. Through the study of analytical methods and tools used in practice, you will learn to extract actionable insights from data, select and apply appropriate techniques, and design innovative solutions for complex supply chain challenges. Through authentic real-world case studies, you will develop the critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to identify and analyse issues, make informed decisions, and improve the efficiency and resilience of supply chain systems.
learning_outcomes: Select and apply appropriate analytics methods to solve complex problems in supply chain and logistics operations.
Utilise data analytics tools to develop decision support systems for supply chain and logistics operations.
Apply descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to critically analyse and optimise the performance of supply chains and logistics operations.

title: MANAGING EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE AND REWARD
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine issues concerning performance management and reward. You will critically analyse HRM literature and empirical research on employee performance and reward management theory, systems, and practices. You will evaluate diverse employee performance and reward systems and practices across various contemporary organisations. You will design and develop employee performance and reward management systems and processes.
learning_outcomes: Discover and solve practical problems related to employee performance and reward management practices and systems
Critically analyse HRM literature and empirical research on employee performance and reward management theory, practices and systems
Identify and evaluate contemporary organisational approaches to employee performance and reward management
Design fundamental components of employee performance and reward management systems and processes

title: HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: Organisations that support their employees to learn and develop across their careers can benefit from high performance. In this subject you will examine factors that contribute to high performing organisations through the lens of the human resource development (HRD) function. You will examine contemporary theory and practical examples of the overall process of HRD in organisations, including learning and development, career planning, team learning, and organisation development. From this understanding, you should be able to analyse and recommend HRD interventions and learning plans for a specific workgroup and organisational context. The HRD function is aligned to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) to promote lifelong learning opportunities for all (SDG4) and promote full and productive employment and decent work for all (SDG8).
learning_outcomes: Propose practical solutions to issues and challenges in workforce development.
Analyse the links between HRD and performance at the individual, team and organization level.
Critique and apply the main theoretical positions describing HRD, high performance and high performance issues.
Analyse the problems and challenges in human resource development (HRD).

title: BUSINESS RESEARCH METHODS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will design a research project relevant to the field of business research. You will interrogate the extant literature to identify a gap in our current understanding of a phenomenon, and articulate clear and appropriate research questions to address this gap. Having explored various research methodologies, you will then propose a research design which will address the research questions you have posed, which adheres to the Australian National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research. This subject will provide you with the skills required to undertake independent research in business contexts, including developing research questions and proposals, undertaking literature reviews, designing a defensible research methodology and design, and recognising the hallmarks of ethical research practices.
learning_outcomes: Assess ethical considerations of research
Justify a research idea through the development and presentation of a research proposal
Critically evaluate existing research literature to identify research gaps and articulate appropriate research aims and questions
Compare and contrast various research methodologies

title: ENTREPRENEURIAL BUSINESS PLANNING
syllabus_overview: Entrepreneurial Business Planning provides a systematic, theoretical and analytical framework to explore the dynamic nature of entrepreneurship. You will engage with contemporary issues of entrepreneurship, and explore entrepreneurs, their ventures, the entrepreneurship process and opportunity evaluation tools. You will explore these aspects to enhance your 'theory-for-practice-sake' perspective of entrepreneurship; applied in a range of professional and scholarly contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop robust entrepreneurship arguments, integrating relevant literature and theoretical perspectives to propose evidence-based entrepreneurial solutions in professional and academic contexts.
Apply advanced teamwork and leadership skills to develop innovative solutions for complex entrepreneurial challenges.
Critically evaluate complex information to assess entrepreneurial opportunities and support strategic decision-making.
Apply theoretical frameworks to analyse entrepreneurship research and generate informed insights.

title: EMERGING TRENDS IN LOGISTICS AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In the rapidly evolving global market, advanced technologies such as automation, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and the Internet of Things are revolutionising logistics and supply chain management by enhancing transparency and efficiency. Understanding these emerging trends is crucial for maintaining a competitive edge and effectively responding to dynamic market demands. In this subject, you will have the opportunity to enhance your knowledge in logistics and supply chain management by employing advanced critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills. You will research and analyse the latest emerging trends within these fields to gain insight into how technological advancements ensure efficient and effective delivery of products and services. Furthermore, you will learn to model and design intelligent and digital supply chains, enabling data-driven decision-making, operational optimisation, and the ability to adapt to varying uncertainties and market conditions. Throughout the subject, you will analyse and evaluate different supply chains digitalisation strategies, emphasising economic and sustainable operations as drivers of competitive advantage.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of strategic leadership for logistics and supply chain management in the era of global business, focusing on advanced emerging trends and service driven business environments to make comprehensive assessments when analysing business situations.
Identify emerging trends in logistics and supply chain management by analysing the environment and implementing alternatives to create a supply chain competitive advantage in a globalised world.
Identify emerging problems in the field of logistics and supply chain management, and devise innovative and sustainable solutions to address these problems.
Apply logistics and supply chain management principles to address emerging challenges in the fields of logistics and supply chain management

title: EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the theoretical and historical underpinnings of employment relations in Australia, with specific reference to the role of institutions, actors and processes in the regulation of work. You will explore the current legal frameworks that govern Australian employment relations, and evaluate the impact of these policies on the economic and social fabric of Australian society. You will also study the dynamics of negotiation and dispute resolution in the context of Australian workplace relations. You will develop the necessary skills to effectively manage employee grievances and negotiations.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a critical understanding of core concepts of negotiation and dispute resolution
Develop effective negotiation skills and critically reflect on your own negotiation practices
Formulate strategies to address employee relations challenges faced by Government, businesses, unions and employees.
Examine the key institutions, actors and processes involved in the regulation and management of work and employment in Australia
Critically evaluate the major issues influencing the regulation and management of employee relations in Australia
Critique the contemporary policy debates over the policies and practices governing the relationship between employers and employees

title: INTERNATIONAL PROJECT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In International Project Management, you will be introduced to the differences between and the techniques involved in managing domestic and international projects and the framework to manage an international project. Working with case studies and real-life examples, you will explore how cultural and social differences, languages, legal and regulatory requirements, technologies, infrastructure and time zone differences affect the different elements of the project management framework, and therefore, the execution of international projects. Working independently and collaborating with other students where possible, you will learn about the application of the Project Management Book of Reference [PMBOK] framework in international project management.
learning_outcomes: Prepare project proposals and implement project plans in a range of settings individually and as part of a diverse multicultural team.
Develop effective solutions for challenges that arise in international projects.
Evaluate the needs of a range of stakeholders in global and large international projects.

title: LEVERAGING ENTREPRENEURIAL VENTURES
syllabus_overview: Entrepreneurial ventures and startups are vital to economic growth and job creation. You will explore and provide synthesis between theoretical underpinnings and practical applications in start-ups and/or entrepreneurial ventures on contemporary issues of design thinking, lean-start-up and business model canvas principles. Upon completion of this subject, you should to be able to critically evaluate entrepreneurship validation tools. A distinct theory-for-practice-sake perspective is provided whereby you will apply these tools in start-ups and ventures of your choice.
learning_outcomes: Gather, critically review and use information to meet entrepreneurship and practice outcomes through design thinking, product design, lean-startup and business model design techniques
Effectively formulate personal opinions and integrate the opinions of others into cogent entrepreneurship and startup arguments
Use complex-problem solving techniques to critically review entrepreneurship opportunities for a range of stakeholder perspectives inclusive of leadership and teamwork dynamics.
Critically reflect upon and analyse complex entrepreneurship opportunities using contemporary entrepreneurship validation tools

Assess the knowledge in entrepreneurial ventures through education and research which is entrepreneurial, innovative, responsible and engaged, and which can be applied in a range of entrepreneurial and practice contexts

title: ETHICAL LEADERSHIP AND CHANGE
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the interrelated roles of leadership, and ethics in shaping effective and sustainable organisations. You will gain advanced knowledge and critical skills to lead with integrity, drive transformational change, and navigate complex ethical challenges in contemporary organisational environments. You will explore leadership theories and styles, the psychology of change, resistance and engagement strategies, as well as ethical frameworks for responsible decision-making. Emphasis is placed on understanding the social, cultural, and global dimensions of ethical leadership and managing change in diverse and dynamic contexts. Through case studies, simulations, and reflective learning, you will develop the capacity to lead ethically under pressure, influence stakeholders, and implement strategic change initiatives that align with organisational values and long-term objectives.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and communicate evaluations of contemporary leadership theories, models and their effectiveness in driving organisational performance and change.
Collaboratively design and apply an ethical leadership approach that considers organisational context, stakeholder engagement, and barriers to change.
Evaluate complex ethical issues in leadership and management and justify responsible and values-driven decision-making in diverse organisational settings.
Reflect critically on personal leadership style and ethical values, and demonstrate the ability to lead change with integrity, accountability, and cultural sensitivity individually and in teams.

title: MANAGING INNOVATION IN ORGANISATIONS
