syllabus_overview: Innovation is the key to gaining and maintaining a competitive advantage in the business world. This subject provides a systematic approach to the strategies and processes that underlie successful innovation in goods and services. Using the latest research on the process and practice of innovation, underpinned by an extensive use of site visits to local organisations and the use of case study material, you will focus on market, organisational and technological issues in innovation management.
learning_outcomes: Appraise radical, continuous and discontinuous innovation in the current global environment.
Create an innovation action plan for an existing organisation relevant to their specific attributes and the broader market.
Analyse and evaluate innovation within organisations from a competitive perspective
Initiate effective teamwork skills for collaboration and problem solving.

title: ORGANISATIONAL CHANGE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore and apply the key frameworks that guide the management of organisational change. You will develop the skills required to formulate and implement an appropriate change management intervention. You will also analyse how organisations initiate, resist and stimulate change, and consider suitable strategies to influence organisational stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Develop a well-supported change management intervention to address the challenges faced by an organisation
Analyse effective and ineffective change interventions
Develop your technical and interpersonal skills as a change agent
Design appropriate strategies to facilitate and manage organisational change
Critically analyse the key theories and concepts that shape our understanding of organisational change

title: MANAGEMENT PRACTICE AND THEORY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine the main characteristics of contemporary management practice and theory, and its importance to the ethical, efficient and effective operation of modern organisations. You will investigate the various organisation design options and draw on theoretical models, academic research and current thinking to determine the factors that influence the selection of an appropriate organisational design and management model for competitive advantage and sustainability. You will be guided by global and local case studies and organisational design principles to illustrate the practical application of people and operational management, and advance your analytical and management skills.
learning_outcomes: Create innovative organisational designs and management models that ensure competitive advantage and sustainability in modern organisations.
Assess the roles of management and change management in determining organisational processes and outcomes in dynamic environments.
Collaborate effectively in diverse teams to complete complex tasks or structure projects in culturally diverse employment settings, fostering equality and well-being.
Evaluate organisational problems and formulate evidence-based organisational design and people-management solutions.

title: MANAGING THE SPORT BRAND
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop leaders in sport through introducing students to strategic issues in examining and discussing the role that marketing, specifically branding, sponsorship and promotion, plays in the generation of revenue for sport organisations and events; identifying and selecting strategic partners to develop, promote and strengthen the sport organisation's brand; assessing the appropriateness and evaluating the success of common promotional strategies for sport products and events; developing strategies for cultivating and managing relationships with key brand partners, and applying branding, sponsorship and promotional theory to the sport industry.
learning_outcomes: Develop strategies for cultivating and managing relationships with key brand partners
Apply branding, sponsorship and promotional theory to the sport industry
Examine and discuss the role that marketing, specifically branding, sponsorship and promotion, plays in the generation of revenue for sport organisations and events
Identify and select strategic partners to develop, promote and strengthen the sport organisation's brand
Assess the appropriateness and evaluate the success of common promotional strategies for sport products and events

title: MANAGING MEDIA RELATIONS IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop you as a leader in sport by introducing you to strategic issues in the management of the relationship between sport organisations or athletes and the media, including the selection of appropriate strategies in promoting the achievements of sport organisations and athletes. You will critically evaluate the best ways to manage the reputation and image of sport organisations or individual athletes during a crisis or scandal, critically interpret how sport and athletes are represented in the media and be aware of the ways in which the media will seek to use those athletes.
learning_outcomes: Critically interpret how sport and athletes are represented in the media and be aware of the ways in which the media will seek to use those athletes
Critically evaluate the best ways to manage the reputation and image of sport organisations or individual athletes during a crisis or scandal
Appraise and select appropriate strategies in promoting the achievements of sport organisations and athletes
Recognise and discuss the current commercial and contextual relationships between the media and sport industries

title: MANAGING INNOVATION FOR SPORT GROWTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop as a leader in sport by introducing you to strategic issues with identifying and applying strategies to build sport capacity and increase recreational and competition player participation. Specific topics include recognising barriers and drivers for volunteer participation, developing effective mechanisms to support and manage volunteers within the sport industry, and developing and evaluating innovative business processes to improve sport organisation performance and revenue streams.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply strategies to build sport capacity and increase recreational and competition player participation
Recognise barriers and drivers for volunteer participation, and develop effective mechanisms to support and manage volunteers within the sport industry
Identify established and emerging revenue streams within the sport industry
Develop and evaluate innovative business processes to improve sport organisation performance

title: ORGANISATIONAL BEHAVIOUR
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to equip you with an advanced understanding of the dynamic interactions within organisations that influence behaviour and performance. By exploring the impact of individual differences, group dynamics and organisational culture, you will gain insights into how these elements shape organisational behaviour. This course integrates cutting-edge theories and real-world applications to prepare you to address contemporary organisational challenges. Through a global focus, you will learn to navigate and influence complex organisational outcomes effectively, ensuring alignment with both business objectives and broader societal values.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and apply theories to identify key organisational behaviour issues and explain organisational and management practices.
Generate evidence-based solutions and recommendations for sustainable organisational effectiveness.
Critically evaluate effective approaches for contemporary management of individuals, teams and organisations.

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Project management in Practice is a capstone subject that is designed to strengthen your existing project management knowledge and skills. With the help of A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK® Guide) as one of the industry best practices, you will have the opportunity to enhance your existing project management skills, while applying a wide range of tools, techniques, and processes on a given authentic business problem. You will use project management software and gain advanced project management and hands-on skills that can be immediately applied and communicated in real-world project environments. Working independently and working with other students, both online and face-to-face, you will work toward understanding and analysing a real-life business problem and, developing a project management plan containing inputs from all project management knowledge areas. This subject will provide you with an in-depth knowledge of advanced topics in project management and relevant soft skills (i.e. teamwork, leadership, and communication).
learning_outcomes: Effectively apply project scheduling, resource allocation, and budgeting techniques in any project environment.
Critically examine project management processes as described by "A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK@ Guide).
Effectively identify and assess project stakeholders and successfully manage communications to ensure project success
Effectively demonstrate your capabilities as a project team member and collaborate to acheive the team's project objectives
Effectively synthesise project documentation/information and practically analyse project quality issues and risks to formulate appropriate quality assurance techniques and risk response strategies.
Use project management software for project planning, risk management, monitoring and control.
Efficiently create and evaluate business cases/project proposals. Select and use a range of tools, techniques and processes to develop project plans, monitor and control projects.

title: PROJECT LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with an introduction to the competencies required to support effective leadership and governance for project management. In this subject you will examine a broad range of project management and leadership concepts to illustrate the significant role that effective project management leadership can have in project and organisational success. You will also examine projects as vehicles of strategic change and transformation. A range of issues associated with delivering project success will be covered, including: leadership styles and how effective leaders facilitate project success and change; project team planning; human resources in the project context; the role of effective governance, stakeholder management and engagement, and understanding people management practices to align team performance with project outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Determine and address the diverse needs of project stakeholders, formulate innovative solutions and demonstrate sound decision making related to project management.
Develop high level ability to recommend differentiated actions for leaders in different phases of the project lifecycle.
As a project leader, demonstrate a high level of effective and appropriate communication and collaboration with project team members and different stakeholders.
Examine and critically analyse major streams of leadership theory and how leadership relates to various aspects of project effectiveness and efficiency.

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In Project Management, you will be introduced to the essentials of managing projects which covers a range of issues including the project management life cycle; the functions essential to successful project management; developing a project management plan; verifying and controlling the project scope; defining, scheduling and allocating resources; and monitoring project quality. Working independently and working together with other students, you will learn about organising, planning and performing projects, and develop the ethical, critical thinking and interpersonal skills required to understand, analyse, and improve various projects.
learning_outcomes: Prepare project plans to meet project objectives and requirements
Communicate project plans and updates with stakeholders
Determine the client's project goals, the stakeholders and the project risks.
Develop documentation to achieve project objectives within time, cost and quality parameters
Recommend appropriate management tools for monitoring and control of projects

title: SPORT LEADERSHIP AND GOVERNANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop your skills as a leader in the sport industry. You will be introduced to the key leadership and governance trends and issues impacting local, regional, national and international sport organisations. You will utilise relevant theories and concepts to critically examine current practices.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the contribution of leadership to effective sport organisations
Critically examine the applications of corporate governance best practices to sport organisations
Critically examine the systemic governance of the sport industry

title: INFECTIONS, PANDEMICS AND EPIDEMICS
syllabus_overview: Infectious diseases, both new and ancient, continue to threaten wellbeing by causing localised, epidemic or pandemic disease outbreaks. In this subject students will learn about the chain of infection, immunity and vaccination, disease prevention, and disease surveillance. Selected microorganisms will then be described and compared: the main focus is the natural habitat of the organisms (reservoirs of infection), the ways in which humans can encounter the organisms (routes of infection) and the strategies available at the individual, community and global levels to prevent disease and, in the diseased patient, to cure disease. In parallel, workshops will focus on laboratory techniques that can be used for disease diagnosis including culture-based methods, molecular methods, and immunological approaches. Workshops will culminate in an infectious disease case study.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and interpret results from various diagnostic microbiology techniques.
Analyse factors that can influence the emergence, re-emergence and/or spread of specific infectious diseases.
Apply knowledge of different laboratory techniques that are used to isolate and identify microorganisms, and diagnose infectious diseases caused by these microorganisms.
Describe and compare infectious agents, their biological features, epidemiology, disease effects and disease management, using appropriate microbiological terms and scientific concepts.
Evaluate the different modes of transmission of infectious agents and the effectiveness of corresponding control and prevention strategies.
Work collaboratively with peers in a small group to complete an infectious disease case study, including disease diagnosis, treatment options, and prognosis for recovery.

title: GLOBAL BUSINESS STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn how strategy is formulated, articulated, and enacted in a global context. We will combine ideas, theories and tools from strategic management, international business and innovation to take an interdisciplinary approach to build a comprehensive understanding of the management of organisations operating and competing domestically and across national borders. The subject will enable you to understand the challenges of businesses competing in the global arena and will help you develop the knowledge and skills needed to design strategies that aim for sustainable competitive advantages and increased firm performance. Through this subject you will become aware of key political, socio-economic, and cultural dynamics and trends that characterise the globalised business environment and the ethical and social responsibility consideration when doing business and strategising in a global scale.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and apply the concepts and tools of business strategy in a global context.
Integrate theories and techniques in the analysis of the strategic management options available to a wide range of different types of organisations as the operate and compete in the global arena.
Critically analyse and critique arguments for and against ideas on how global innovation may enable a firm to achieve positional advantage and superior performance.
Demonstrate knowledge of the main theoretical approaches to global strategic management and understand the economic, social and ethical and contexts that give rise to their formulation.

title: INTRODUCTION TO THE WORLD OF MICROBIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: The subject provides you with knowledge in introductory microbiology, microbial genetics, microbial communities and interactions. The key concepts covered in the subject forms a foundation in understanding the life cycle of bacteria and viruses, process in microbial genetics and microbial communities and their interactions. Important key concepts are taught using animations and videos, while other concepts are modelled in laboratory classes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate independent research skills by locating and evaluating experimental data.
Explain the classification and diversity of microbes and the basic requirements for life
Use raw data to calculate variables for scientific data analysis and interpret findings for presentation in effective scientific format
Describe key microbiological techniques to manipulate microorganism in the laboratory

title: MICROBIOLOGY FOR ALLIED HEALTH
syllabus_overview: This subject will suit anyone that has an interest in basic medical microbiology and the potentially pathogenic microbes around us. You will be introduced to your normal flora, medically important bacteria, viruses, and fungi and the ways that we can control and prevent infection by these organisms in a health care setting. In practical classes you will use culturing techniques and biochemical testing to identify microbes and understand the effectiveness of hand washing in stopping the spread of pathogens throughout a population. This subject will teach you to recognise the general characteristics of pathogenic microorganisms that cause disease in humans and the steps involved in disease transmission.
learning_outcomes: Describe how to isolate and identify non-pathogenic and pathogenic microorganisms as part of diagnostic strategies and interpret the findings
Apply knowledge of infection control and tools for optimising disease prevention to identify appropriate treatments for infectious diseases in clinical scenarios.
Apply fundamental knowledge of cell biology and patient genetics to inform disease treatment and outcomes.
Explain and communicate the key principles regarding microorganisms that cause disease in humans to patients and clinicians, individually or as part of a small team.

title: MEDICAL MICROBIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces you to microbial pathogenesis, control of pathogens, immunity, virology, bacteriology and mycology. Pathogenic microorganisms are discussed from both the human and animal perspective, with veterinary examples and instances also covered throughout the subject. Practicals teach you how to isolate and identify medically important microorganisms.
learning_outcomes: Examine and illustrate the key principles underlying the ability of some microorganisms to cause disease in humans and other animals.
Analyse and evaluate the morphological characteristics and distinctions between microorganisms, and proficiently apply microbiological techniques for the identification of pathogenic microbes.

Evaluate and elucidate the mechanisms by which microbes can be effectively controlled and the processes through which the immune system acts to prevent infections caused by bacteria, fungi and viruses.
Formulate and convey findings from assessment of a case study, as well as independent research, while collaborating effectively within a team.

title: IMMUNOLOGICAL DISEASES
syllabus_overview: Our immune system is a powerful yet potentially dangerous weapon. In this subject, you will explore the cells and processes that protect our bodies from external and internal threats. We will focus on immunological diseases that arise when our immune system responds excessively to external danger signals or inappropriately targets components of our own bodies. You will delve into the mechanisms of innate immune recognition of pathogens and host stress, understanding how these processes lead to inflammation as a response to disruptions in host homeostasis. We will discuss how excessive inflammation, dysregulation of the host response, genetic variants, or immunomodulation can result in significant health burdens and diseases all too common amongst Australians. By understanding these principles, you will be better equipped to explain the role of immunology and our immune system in various immunological diseases, developing an immunological ‘tool kit’ to inform others about common immunological diseases. This knowledge is crucial for addressing the significant health challenges these diseases pose to the Australian population, to enlighten about these diseases, and for exploring current and emerging approaches to diagnose and treat these conditions.
learning_outcomes: Communicate information about immunological diseases to different audiences both individually and as part of a team.

Examine the types and mechanisms of hypersensitivity reactions and their roles in immune-related diseases, while evaluating current and emerging therapies, with a focus on public health impact in Australia
Analyse inflammation mechanisms and cytokine regulation, and evaluate their role in chronic inflammatory diseases
Articulate the immune system structure, pathogen response mechanisms, and how their disruption causes immunological disease
Differentiate between innate and adaptive immunity by key mechanisms and evaluate therapies targeting each system.

title: MEDICAL BACTERIOLOGY AND VIRULENCE
syllabus_overview: You will explore concepts relating to the molecular aspects of bacterial infection, the ability of the host to respond to these pathogens, and the ways in which bacteria are able to evade detection by their host to induce disease. This lecture series will also introduce numerous significant bacterial pathogens and discuss concepts of pathogenesis, virulence and pathogen control. You will also explore key aspects of the immune system, including mechanisms of pathogen detection, activation of innate immunity, development of adaptive immunity and problems that may arise as a result of an ineffective immune response.
learning_outcomes: Examine and apply examples of the mechanisms that enable the immune system to be generated and respond to pathogens, and how an ineffective immune response can result in disease and chronic infections.
Evaluate and critique immunology related articles as part of a team for their suitability in communicating complex topics to a general audience.
Analyse and provide illustrative examples of molecular mechanisms used by pathogenic bacteria to successfully infect their hosts, avoid immune clearance, induce pathology and cause chronic infection.
Demonstrate proficiency in the application of key microbiological and immunological techniques, both in theory and in practical laboratory settings.
Apply the principles of bacterial pathogenesis to analyse and solve real world scenarios.

title: THE MICROBIOME OF LIFE
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the diversity and ecology of microbial life across a broad scale. Topics examine the breadth of ways in which microbial communities impact life on this planet, from their importance in planetary nutrient cycles through to the human microbiome in health and disease. The practical component re-enforces lecture content and provides students an opportunity to have an impact on a local real-world issue though the investigation of bacterial and fungal communities from a local community-led restoration project. Class findings will give insight into the restoration program’s success and help direct future restoration efforts. Students will gain firsthand experience and training to analyse microbiome data and will be supported by data analysis and scientific communication workshops.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the use of culture-dependent and independent techniques in the study of microbial communities, including ethical considerations related to microbiome research.
Examine and illustrate the ecological principles and interactions that influence symbiotic, marine, and terrestrial microbiomes.
Examine and compare the ways in which microbial communities contribute to organismal and ecosystem functioning.
Employ experimental and bioinformatic techniques to investigate microbial communities.
Collaboratively engage in group discussions and research projects to investigate microbial communities and demonstrate effective teamwork and integration of findings in the group assessment.
Develop and demonstrate a high level of written and visual scientific communication skills in individual assessments.

title: MOLECULAR MICROBIOLOGY ADVANCES
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to innovative scientific knowledge and skills in molecular microbiology and microbial genetics. The topics will include bacterial gene regulation, horizontal gene transfer, viral genetics/genomics, and genomic trait mapping in pathogens. Advances in technologies such as CRISPR/cas technology and next generation sequencing technologies will be explored. This subject will provide you with a capstone experience comprising a laboratory-based project and workshops linked to the lecture topics, as well as technical and theoretical skills that will equip you working in a molecular microbiology laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Contextualise knowledge of key concepts in microbial genetics, such as gene regulation, genetic recombination, and horizontal gene transfer, to apply modern molecular biology techniques.
Interpret DNA sequences using bioinformatic tools.
Collaboratively investigate modern molecular biology research technique
Formulate hypotheses and predict outcomes for various experimental setups in molecular microbiology.
Communicate verbally and in writing in formats appropriate for scientific contexts

title: MEDICAL VIROLOGY: PATHOGENESIS AND DISEASE
syllabus_overview: This subject will explore concepts relating to the molecular aspects of viral infection principles, including the ability of the host to respond to these pathogens, and the ways in which viruses are able to evade detection by their host and induce disease. The subject will also cover multiple significant viral pathogens including HIV, Influenza and SARS-CoV; and will include guest lecturers from industry, government and research related fields to discuss current relevant topics pertaining to viral infection in the broader community. Students will also be involved in solving a case study during practical classes, where they will utilise and learn common laboratory techniques to decipher the outcome of a viral outbreak scenario in a community setting.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively communicate verbally and in writing in formats appropriate for scientific contexts.
Analyse and propose solutions to real world viral disease scenarios using knowledge of molecular technologies.
Interpret and integrate results of laboratory experiments in medical virology.
Analyse molecular and genetic mechanisms that allow pathogenic viruses to infect their hosts, avoid immune clearance, induce pathology and cause chronic infection.

title: HONOURS IN MICROBIOLOGY A
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Moreover, the program intends to impart undergraduate students with professional skills that extend their career opportunities. Honours in Microbiology consists of a one year (full-time) or two years (part-time) individual research project, supervised by a SABE scientist whose research is in the discipline of microbiology. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. MIC401A is the first subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take MIC401A first.
learning_outcomes: Understand published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Show intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice
Recall knowledge in microbiology when conducting experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Obtain practical experience and advanced knowledge in the field of microbiology.
Extend oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.

title: HONOURS IN MICROBIOLOGY D
syllabus_overview: Honours is a fourth year of undergraduate study offered to students who demonstrate academic success and fulfilled the requirements of a Bachelors degree, with a major in a relevant discipline. The aim of the Honours program in the School of Agriculture, Biomedicine and Environment (SABE) is to provide undergraduate students the opportunity to gain first-class practical, field, and theoretical expertise in a major area of scientific study. Students can commence either in February or July. Students should consult with potential supervisors during their final undergraduate year and will only be accepted into the subject with the written support from a willing supervisor. The School Honours co-ordinator will provide more information on the application process including a comprehensive list of available research projects. MIC401D is the final subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take MIC401D last.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge in microbiology research when devising experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Apply practical experience and advanced knowledge in the field of microbiology.
Apply advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Formulate an original research question based on the comprehensive review of published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Utilise intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice.

MIC401C is the second or third subject of a 90CP research component for Honours in SABE. Students must take MIC401A first.

Refine practical experience and advanced knowledge in the field of microbiology
Develop advanced oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Compare and contrast published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.
Develop intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice

Develop intellectual independence through responsibility and accountability for own learning and practice.
Build oral communication skills to present knowledge and ideas to audiences including individuals with and without detailed specialist expertise.
Develop knowledge in microbiology when devising experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions.
Analyse published scientific information and acquired data and communicate this to a scientific audience in written form.

title: MIDWIFERY, NURSING AND HEALTH CARE CONTEXTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, will explore the Australian health care system, the collaborative nature of health care, and how consumers and professionals interact with health care at various levels. You will explore global health and wellbeing trends, public health initiative and investigate the health care continuum and the quality and safety framework. You will develop the foundation knowledge for working with individuals in health and human services settings in Australia and how different environments can influence consumer access to health care. You will explore the differentiation between the nursing and midwifery professions and discuss the historical and political perspectives of midwifery practice and the evolution of the profession, including contemporary evidence supporting midwifery continuity models of maternity care. Using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, workshops and online activities you will be introduced to the concepts of reflection, evidenced-based practice, cultural safety and holistic health care
learning_outcomes: Explore how health standards influence care quality and patient outcomes
Investigate the role of reflection in professional practice and individual development
Discuss how social and cultural factors shape and determine people's experience of health and illness in different parts of the world
Appraise contemporary developments in global, national, and regional health and wellbeing including the role of midwives and nurses
Examine the provision of maternity care within the health care system including models of care and collaboration with women and other health care professionals
Illustrate the ways in which consumers interact with the health care system to meet individual needs
Explain the principles of patient and personal safety and their relevance to health professional practice

title: FOUNDATIONS OF PREGNANCY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to maternal physiological adaptations that occur to support pregnancy and fetal development. Using evidence-based information, you will develop the skills and knowledge to provide safe and effective pregnancy care to women experiencing a normal pregnancy. This will include information sharing, offering choices and providing support to empower the woman and her family during pregnancy. The subject builds on concepts of reflective, evidence-based practice and clinical decision-making to enable you to engage in pregnancy care provision under supervision of an appropriately registered practitioner. Using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, simulation and clinical placement, you will develop skills and attributes for providing evidence-based woman-centred care during pregnancy.
learning_outcomes: Examine the components of pregnancy care and education for women experiencing a normal pregnancy
Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred midwifery care with women, their families and the interprofessional team during the pregnancy period
Demonstrate (under supervision) safe and effective midwifery care for women during normal pregnancy according to the scope of practice of the midwife
Describe the normal physiological adaptations that support pregnancy
Analyse the evidence that supports current trends in maternity care in pregnancy
Analyse the key events in human reproduction, human pregnancy and fetal development

title: INTRODUCTION TO LABOUR, BIRTH AND POSTNATAL CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to midwifery knowledge and skills for childbirth within a woman-centred model. You will be provided with the theoretical foundations to assist you in understanding the role of the midwife during labour and birth and the initial care of the mother and infant following birth. You will further develop your knowledge of anatomy, physiology and psychosocial concepts. You will build on the development of therapeutic relationships and work in partnership with women and their families to support them in the normal birth process and the transition of the woman and infant following birth. You will also be introduced to midwifery care related to the immediate postnatal period including lactation and breastfeeding. Using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation and clinical placement, you will develop skills and attributes for providing evidence-based, woman-centred care during labour, birth and the immediate postnatal period.
learning_outcomes: Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred midwifery care with women, their families and the interprofessional team during the labour, birth and early postnatal period
Perform thorough midwifery assessments to enable appropriate consultation and referral to provide safe and effective care to women and infants during labour, birth, and the early postnatal periods
Examine culturally safe care for the woman, her partner and family during labour and the early postnatal period

title: MIDWIFERY CARE OF THE POSTNATAL WOMAN, NEWBORN AND FAMILY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on your knowledge of the immediate postnatal period and focus on maternal and newborn care in the postnatal period including infant feeding, bonding and attachment. You will gain an understanding of both the normal and complex physiological and psychological adaptations occurring for new mothers during the first six weeks following birth. You will learn about the role of the midwife in the provision of information, choices and support to empower the woman and her family during this period. You will be introduced to the foundational principles and care for infants requiring additional care in the postnatal setting and special care nursery. Using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation and clinical placement, you will develop skills and attributes for providing evidence-based woman-centred care during the postnatal period.
learning_outcomes: Promote breastfeeding in accordance with the principles of the Baby Friendly Hospital Initiative
Plan, provide and apply safe and effective neonatal care in the postnatal ward setting and special care nursery, including collaborative care for those infants who are premature, sick, or “at risk”
Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred midwifery care with women, their families and the interprofessional team during the postnatal period.
Discuss information about screening tests and immunisation for the infant
Plan and apply evidence-based information to assist and advise the woman on nutrition needs and feeding of her infant
Devise and demonstrate education opportunities for mothers and families during the postnatal period

title: COMMON COMPLEXITIES ACROSS THE PERINATAL PERIOD
syllabus_overview: This subject will prepare you to plan, provide and reflect on midwifery care for women with complex needs during pregnancy and consider how these needs impact across the continuum of birth and into the postnatal period for women and infant. It will enable you to plan for the care and management of women with diverse needs including those with chronic conditions, psychosocial and cultural/social diversity. You will be provided with a theoretical foundation to enable you to explore how midwives as part of the inter and intra-professional team can support women and infants with complex needs and build on the knowledge, skills and attributes for midwifery practice in complex situations. The subject is delivered using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation and clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the underlying physiology/pathophysiology to complexities in pregnancy and plan, provide and apply safe care for women, infants and their families
Critically reflect on the role of the midwife in supporting women who develop complexities during pregnancy or have pre-existing conditions prior to pregnancy using evidence-based practice
Demonstrate an understanding of the impact that complexities in pregnancy can have across the continuum of labour and birth and the postnatal period for both women and infants
Identify infants who are at risk of complications in the neonatal period and plan care accordingly
Evaluate strategies to recognise and facilitate meeting the needs specific to First Nations women and infants and to those of other cultures
Plan, provide and reflect on care in collaboration with the woman, her family and the inter- and intra-professional team in response to complex scenarios

title: CONTINUITY OF MIDWIFERY CARE
syllabus_overview: Using a woman-centred and primary health care approach, this subject will allow you to build on theoretical foundations to assist the further development of supporting women and families during pregnancy, labour and birth and the postnatal period. This subject is designed to assist you in forming woman-centred approached in your relationships with women in the context of a continuity of care model.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrates an understanding of the importance of respectful and professional relationships with women
Apply midwifery, primary health care and other theory to the provision of safe and effective midwifery care for women and their babies across the continuum

title: COMPLEX AND EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT IN MATERNITY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will focus on the care of the woman and her infant in maternity complications and emergencies. This subject will build on prior knowledge of anatomy and physiology, the normal birth process and care of the newborn to further develop your clinical skills and the ability to think critically. You will incorporate evidence-based practice around complex and emergency situations as well as gain skills in situational management, inter- and intra-professional collaborative relationships and leadership. The subject is delivered using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation and clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the role of the midwife in relation to their scope of practice when managing complex scenarios
Identify women and newborns at risk of complex and emergency clinical situations.
Plan, provide and reflect on care in collaboration with the woman, family and the inter- and intra-professional team in response to complex scenarios
Evaluate and apply current evidence for the management of complex clinical scenarios
Demonstrate effective communication within inter- and intra-professional teams in complex/emergency scenarios

title: TRANSITION TO MIDWIFERY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject will explore the transition from student to a registered midwife and prepare you to enter the midwifery profession by promoting commitment to lifelong learning and professional development. This subject will also explore leadership skills and knowledge and how this can influence improved outcomes for women and infants; and more positive working environments. In preparation for entering the midwifery workforce you will also explore strategies for self-care, mitigating personal risk and building resilience to support you throughout your midwifery career. The subject is delivered using a blended learning approach, comprising face-to-face teaching, workshops and online learning modules via LMS and is supported by clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the importance of midwives as leaders, managers, preceptors, educators and agents of change
Evaluate the concepts of self-care, mitigating personal risk and building resilience in relation to midwifery practice
Analyse the midwife’s professional responsibility, personal accountability for practice of self and collaboration with others
Compare and contrast the differences between the student role and the Registered Midwife role and identify strategies to undertake the transition

title: FOUNDATIONS OF MIDWIFERY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the foundations of midwifery care including professional issues, midwifery philosophies that underpin midwifery practice as well as the different governance frameworks in place to support safe, collaborative midwifery care. You will also be introduced to the fundamentals of pregnancy care through a primary health care lens. Using a blended learning approach including lectures, online activities, skills labs and clinical placement, you will develop skills and attributes for providing evidence-based woman-centred care during pregnancy.
learning_outcomes: Perform thorough assessments to enable appropriate consultation and referral to provide safe and effective midwifery care to women during pregnancy
Critically evaluate and apply available evidence to inform best practice in midwifery during the pregnancy period
Analyse the contribution of the midwife in improving health outcomes for women and babies
Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred midwifery care with women, their families and colleagues during the pregnancy period
Apply relevant legal and ethical frameworks to midwifery care

title: LABOUR, BIRTH AND POSTNATAL CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the fundamentals of midwifery care of a woman during labour and birth, as well as postnatal care up to six weeks postpartum. Care of the neonate including optimal infant feeding will be explored. Your learning will encompass common labour and birth interventions and care of the infant requiring additional care in the postnatal setting. Using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation, and clinical placement, you will develop skills and attributes for providing evidence-based woman-centred care during the intrapartum and postnatal period.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply available evidence to inform best practice in midwifery during labour, birth and the postnatal periods
Plan, provide and reflect on safe and effective neonatal care in the postnatal setting, including collaborative care for infants as required
Promote breastfeeding in accordance with the principles of the Baby Friendly Hospital Initiative
Perform thorough midwifery assessments to enable appropriate consultation and referral to provide safe and effective care to women during labour, birth, and the postnatal period
Plan, provide and apply evidence-based information, assistance and advice to the woman on nutrition needs and feeding of her infant
Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred midwifery care with women, their families and interdisciplinary colleagues during labour, birth and the postnatal period

title: COMPLEX MATERNAL AND NEONATAL CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on the knowledge and skills gained in previous subjects to care for women experiencing maternity complications and emergencies, and infants experiencing complexities. You will incorporate evidence-based practice to develop skills in critical thinking, situational management, inter- and intra-professional collaborative relationships and leadership. The subject is delivered using a blended learning approach comprising of lectures, online activities, skills labs, clinical simulation and clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply current evidence to inform best practice in complex maternity and neonatal scenarios
Identify, interpret and communicate complex clinical data to optimise care of the woman experiencing complexities
Plan, provide and reflect on woman-centred care in collaboration with the inter- and intra-professional team in response to complex scenarios
Critically reflect on the role of the midwife in relation to their scope of practice when managing complex scenarios
Plan, provide and reflect on family-centred care of the deteriorating infant requiring stabilisation in collaboration with the inter- and intra-professional team

title: CONTEXT OF WOMEN'S LIVES AND COMPREHENSIVE MATERNITY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop skills to work in partnership with women in the context of their lives. You will explore the global midwifery landscape and consider political issues that influence the maternity care women receive. You will learn effective communication skills to apply a strengths-based approach to providing individualised care to women. In preparation for entering the midwifery workforce you will also explore strategies for self-care, mitigating personal risk and building resilience to support you throughout your midwifery career. The subject is delivered using a blended learning approach, comprising face-to-face teaching, workshops and online learning modules via LMS and is supported by clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and justify the importance of incorporating a strengths-based approach to support women’s wellbeing
Critically evaluate and apply available evidence to support the role of the midwife in improving health outcomes
Demonstrate effective, sensitive communication and collaboration with colleagues, women, families and the community in a variety of professional and social contexts
Evaluate the concepts of self-care, mitigating personal risk and building resilience in relation to midwifery practice
Explain the importance of high-quality midwifery care in improving public health outcomes in both a local and global context

title: ACUTE AND EMERGENCY MATERNITY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will focus on the care of the women and her fetus/baby with additional needs due to high acuity and maternity emergency situations, for example, breech birth, postpartum haemorrhage, cord prolapse, shoulder dystocia. This subject will build on prior knowledge of anatomy and physiology and the normal birth process to further develop clinical skill and the ability to think critically. You will develop theoretical knowledge, through research and enquiry learning methods, around acute and emergency situations as well as gain skills in situational management, multi-disciplinary collaborative relationships and leadership, whilst incorporating woman centred care and therapeutic communication. You will be provided with clinical experience and/or simulated events which will prepare you to recognise and respond effectively in acute and emergency situations.
learning_outcomes: Critique and appraise evidence for the management of specific clinical scenarios.
Demonstrate safe and effective care provided to women and their babies with complex needs as a part of the multidisciplinary team.

Demonstrate effective communication and collaboration within the multidisciplinary team, the woman and her family. Students must be assessed at a proficient or independent level in the midwifery standards assessment.
Identify and apply knowledge of risk factors related to acute and emergency clinical situations.

title: COMPLEX NEEDS IN MATERNITY CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will consolidate all prior learning and have the opportunity to extend their knowledge and skill through application of further psychosocial complexities impacting on maternity care . In collaboration with the multidisciplinary team and in partnership with the woman, the student will build on previous experiences to develop more autonomous skills and knowledge in the provision of safe and effective care required for women with psychosocial. Students will be encouraged to manage care for women, think critically, respond effectively to situations involving these women and learn when to consult and refer appropriately
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate comprehensive therapeutic communication through collaborations with women, the multidisciplinary team, community agencies and support networks.
Critically appraise evidence and plan and implement maternity care according to evidence based practice.
Evaluate the relationship between psychosocial and physical complexities of pregnancy and their impact on maternity care.
Provide safe and effective midwifery care to the woman and her family with minimal supervision in readiness to practice as a novice midwife on completion of the subject/course.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL MIDWIFERY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this unit you will explore evidence-based practice in maternity care to enable the acquisition of knowledge and skills in an advanced midwifery practice skill of your choosing. Learning in this unit is student driven. You will identify your own learning outcomes and plan to achieve competency in your chosen advanced midwifery practice skill. You will be allocated an academic supervisor who will provide guidance throughout the duration of the subject. You will also be required to engage with a clinical mentor at your health service who has relevant experience and competence in the advanced skills that you are interested in developing. Following this subject, you will have examined and critiqued the current literature and practice and achieved competency in an advanced midwifery practice skill.
learning_outcomes: Utilise analytical, problem solving, planning, negotiation and evaluation skills to achieve competency in an advanced midwifery practice skill
Identify learning outcomes and plan to achieve competence in an advanced midwifery practice skill
Incorporate knowledge, assessment and diagnostic skills related to an advanced midwifery practice skill, in the provision of evidence-based, woman-centred care
Critically appraise own practice to improve practice in relation to an advanced midwifery practice skill

title: CONTINUITY OF MIDWIFERY-LED CARE
syllabus_overview: Midwifery-led continuity has been demonstrated to be the gold standard in maternity care, offering improvements to the quality and safety of maternity care and providing benefits for women and babies. In this subject you will summarise, interpret and critically evaluate the existing evidence on midwifery-led continuity of care models and critique how this evidence is translated into practice. You will develop skills in applying evidence to inform practice change pertinent to your master’s specialisation (clinical practice, management, education or research) that will ultimately improve health outcomes for women and babies.
learning_outcomes: Critically review the facilitators and barriers, industrial and policy influences that impact on practice change in the implementation, sustainability and upscaling of midwifery-led continuity models
Appraise the different roles of midwives as clinical leaders, managers, educators and researchers in supporting midwifery-led continuity of care
Critique the available evidence on continuity of midwifery-led care
Assess the benefits of midwifery led- continuity of care for women, midwives and health care systems
Appraise how the continuity of care evidence is translated into domains of midwifery practice (clinical practice, management and leadership, and the education sector)

title: MEDICATIONS FOR MIDWIFERY PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop your knowledge and skills related to diagnostics and investigations with a collaborative and woman-centred approach in order to complete comprehensive assessments that will inform medication prescribing. This subject will also explore the relevant AHPRA/Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and other legislation and frameworks related to prescribing for midwives.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced practice midwifery knowledge and skills to conduct a comprehensive and systematic clinical assessment to identify appropriate medicines and investigations that can be incorporated into management and care plans with women
Critically analyse the scope of practice of the endorsed midwife and safety, quality and risk management in relation to investigations and diagnostics
Clearly demonstrates safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative and regulatory frameworks
Demonstrate evidence of collaborative care and communication of management plans and recommendations clearly to women, families and other health professionals

title: MEDICATIONS FOR MIDWIFERY PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on the knowledge and learnings from NSM5TMA and MID5003 to advance your knowledge and understanding in pharmacology and prescribing in order to prescribe medicines safely, legally, and effectively across areas of use including pregnancy, birth, postpartum and neonatal care. You will apply comprehensive assessment and evidence based critical thinking skills to provide rationales for the initiation of diagnostics, investigations and medications as part of a collaborative and woman-centred approach to midwifery management and care plans.
learning_outcomes: Clearly demonstrates safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative, safety, quality and regulatory frameworks
Critically analyse available evidence to inform and support clinical decision making in the management and delivery of pharmacological interventions across the childbearing continuum
Apply advanced practice midwifery knowledge and skills to identify appropriate medicines that can be incorporated into management and care plans with women

Demonstrate a detailed and specific understanding of the principles of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and pharmacotherapeutics in relation to the specific pathophysiology of women and neonates across the childbearing continuum
Demonstrate evidence of collaborative care and communication of management plans and recommendations clearly to women, families and other health professionals

title: INTEGRATED MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS
syllabus_overview: Integrated Marketing Communications offers overall knowledge of approaches marketers adopt to communicate the value of their products and services across various communication tools. It explores the various strategies and tactics utilised by companies to create cohesive and effective marketing messages. In this subject, you will develop knowledge of the concepts, frameworks, and models of integrated marketing communications. You will learn to critically analyse the integrated marketing communications practices of a business. Further, you will learn to utilise appropriate tools to develop an integrated marketing communications campaign for a company.
learning_outcomes: Develop and articulate an integrated marketing communications campaign using appropriate communication tools and media
Critically analyse, and evaluate the effectiveness of integrated marketing communications practices
Explain key concepts, frameworks, and models of integrated marketing communications, individually and collaboratively

title: MARKETING FUNDAMENTALS
syllabus_overview: Marketing is both an art and a science, combining creativity with structured analysis to understand consumers and support business success. This subject introduces you to key marketing principles through real-world case studies and hands-on exercises, equipping you with practical skills to analyse and apply marketing concepts across different contexts. By establishing a strong foundation in marketing, you will be well-prepared to explore more specialised areas and applications of marketing practice
learning_outcomes: Analyse business information using digital and traditional marketing tools to identify marketing problems and opportunities
Evaluate fundamental marketing concepts by comparing their application and relevance across varied real-world business scenarios
Individually and in teams, develop and explain marketing solutions by applying core marketing theories to address common challenges in contemporary business environments

title: PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES OF MARKETING
syllabus_overview: Marketing refers to the activity, set of institutions, and processes for creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging offerings that have value for consumers, customers, clients, partners, and society at large. In today’s competitive business environment, it is important to understand the role of marketing in society, the marketing process and the marketing related decisions that businesses must take to satisfy the needs and wants of customers, and create value for stakeholders. This subject covers the principles of marketing. You will learn the role of marketing in business and society, and how marketing is based on an understanding of customer value. You will gain knowledge of core marketing principles including scoping and analysing the marketing environment, marketing research, consumer behaviour, and managing the marketing mix to influence consumers. In addition to marketing-specific knowledge you will also develop transferable employability skills in areas including communication, critical analysis and creative thinking, and working collaboratively.
learning_outcomes: Individually and/or collaboratively develop marketing strategies in different business environments and contexts
Evaluate market information, individually and/or collaboratively, to develop segmentation, targeting, differentiation and positioning strategies within culturally diverse business environments
Explain marketing concepts and interpret their application, individually and/or collaboratively, within real-world business scenarios

title: BRAND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Strong brands allow companies to differentiate themselves from the competition. Brand Management offers overall knowledge of the principles and practices of building and managing strong brands. You will critically analyse theories and frameworks of brand management. Utilising brand management theories, you will analyse the brand management practices of a company and develop practical strategies for them across traditional and digital platforms. This subject develops your knowledge of theories and concepts of branding.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate key theories and frameworks of brand management
Develop and articulate branding strategies for a company that align with its positioning and target market
Apply brand management theories to analyse and critique the branding practices of a company

title: AI-POWERED MARKETING
syllabus_overview: As AI and marketing technology (MarTech) continue to reshape the digital marketing landscape, businesses are leveraging AI-driven tools to automate processes, optimise digital engagement, and enhance consumer interactions. You will learn practical knowledge and skills in AI-powered marketing, focusing on data-driven marketing decision-making. By working on industry-relevant projects, you will gain problem-solving and critical thinking skills, and digital marketing expertise—in preparation for a career in an AI-driven business environment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse AI-generated marketing insights to identify customer needs and inform strategic decision-making
Develop practical marketing solutions using AI-informed approaches that address contemporary industry challenges
Evaluate AI-driven marketing practices in real-world business contexts

title: FOOD AND FIBRE MARKETS
syllabus_overview: Food and Fibre Markets provides you with the ability to develop and communicate effective strategies to capitalise on market opportunities within an agribusiness context by drawing upon relevant concepts, theory, analytical tools and frameworks. This is a capstone subject in the Agribusiness Major and builds on a foundation that is strongly aligned with the objectives of the United Nations Sustainability Goal (SDG) number 12 - Responsible Production and Consumption . The subject is delivered online and draws on industry experts to explore key factors influencing marketing strategies in the agribusiness sector.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical concepts in the development and promotion of a market strategy for a new product or service in agribusiness.
Demonstrate an understanding of the key concepts underpinning the food and fibre markets.
Reflect on the lessons learnt from the development and promotion of a market strategy for a new product or service in agribusiness.

title: CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with individual, consumer and managerial understanding of consumer behaviour principles and theories. This subject will develop your knowledge of the theories and concepts underpinning consumer behaviour. You will learn to critically analyse consumer responses to marketing stimuli in the real world. Further, you will learn to exercise ethical judgments and cultural views in the application of consumer behaviour principles.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse consumer responses to marketing stimuli, individually and collaboratively.
Critically discuss consumer behaviour concepts, theories and models.
Exercise ethical judgments and cultural views in the application of consumer behaviour principles.

title: INTERNATIONAL MARKETING
syllabus_overview: Companies may extend their marketing offerings to international markets. To that end, they need to revise their strategies to meet the demands and requirements of particular markets. This subject will equip you with knowledge about international marketing principles. You will learn to critically analyse theories and principles of international marketing. Utilising subject theories, you will learn to identify problems and opportunities for a global company. Further, you will learn to recommend practical solutions that embrace cultural, social, and ethical perspectives of particular markets.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate international marketing problems and opportunities for global companies, individually and as part of a team.
Critically analyse the core theories and frameworks of international marketing
Recommend practical international marketing solutions that integrate cultural, social, and ethical perspectives

title: MARKETING RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: Business managers require insights when learning about problems and identifying solutions. This subject will equip you with knowledge about marketing research principles and tools. In this subject you will learn to utilise market information to develop a research proposal. You will learn to use a statistical package to generate and further develop recommendations for real-world marketing problems based on relevant insights.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate statistical techniques to recommend actionable solutions to marketing problems
Use statistical software to analyse marketing data and generate relevant insights
Critically develop a practical marketing research proposal using market information and collaborative research practices

title: SOCIAL MARKETING
syllabus_overview: Social marketing is the application of marketing principles to solve social problems. These include but are not limited to issues in responsible consumption, poverty, public health, quality education, reduced inequalities, environment protection, sustainable living and climate change communication. You will examine the key principles of social marketing as a strategy for changing behaviour that benefits individuals and communities for the greater social good. You will critically analyse the real-world changing needs from the lens of the United Nations Sustainable Development goals and develop creative solutions using social marketing frameworks and theories.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the key concepts and theories of social marketing
Evaluate the ethical and social responsibility issues associated with the implementation of social marketing initiatives.
Apply professional judgement to recommend practical solutions for social marketing challenges.

title: STRATEGIC MARKETING
syllabus_overview: In this capstone marketing subject you will draw on, apply and demonstrate your accumulated marketing knowledge and acumen to solving applied marketing problems through a live strategic marketing simulation. You will review, analyse and apply strategic marketing concepts through the use of marketing theory, and analytical and data tools and frameworks. You will be required to demonstrate a broad and coherent understanding of marketing knowledge and skills along with employability skills in authentic industry-based activities.
learning_outcomes: Critique strategic marketing planning and activities in relation to firm performance and sustainability
Develop and apply ethical, data-driven marketing strategies for different market offerings in diverse market segments
Exercise professional judgement and evaluate strategic marketing options to implement strategies in diverse marketing contexts

title: MARKETING MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Marketing Management offers overall knowledge of the core principles and practices of marketing. This subject enables you to communicate the value of a specific product or service to target customers by featuring the alignments among the elements of the marketing mix. This subject develops your knowledge of marketing concepts, theories, and frameworks. You will learn how to critically analyse marketing concepts across environments and contexts. Further, you will learn to recommend actionable solutions for marketing problems.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse marketing concepts in different environments and contexts.
Explain concepts and theories underpinning marketing practices of companies, individually and/or collaboratively.
Recommend actionable solutions for a range of marketing problems.

title: BRAND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Strong brands allow companies to differentiate themselves from the competition. Brand Management offers overall knowledge of the principles and practices of building and managing strong brands. This subject develops your knowledge of theories and concepts of branding. You will learn to analyse the process of design and implementation of the brand strategy of a firm. Further, you will apply branding theories to develop and launch a brand.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the process of brand strategy planning and implementation for a company.
Develop actionable and theory-driven strategies to launch a brand.
Critically analyse the theories underpinning branding, individually and/or collaboratively.

title: DIGITAL MARKETING
syllabus_overview: With the prominence of digital platforms, it is critical for companies to supplement and further advance their traditional activities by managing their marketing activities via digital platforms. Digital platforms allow companies to enhance their productivity in achieving their objectives. Digital Marketing offers overall knowledge of digital marketing strategies and principles to enhance firms' digital performance. This subject develops your knowledge of theories and principles utilised in digital marketing. You will learn to analyse the digital marketing practices of a firm. Further, you will apply digital marketing principles to develop solutions for the digital marketing problems of a company.
learning_outcomes: Design and recommend actionable, theory-driven digital marketing solutions such as search engine marketing and optimisation, inbound marketing strategies and customer engagement strategies for business challenges.
Apply digital marketing concepts and theories to critically evaluate and improve company practices, individually and collaboratively.
Critically analyse digital marketing practices including search, social media, content, and data-driven campaigns used by businesses across diverse industries and contexts.

title: SALES MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Sales Management offers overall knowledge of how firms should communicate the value propositions of the solutions they provide to their B2B and B2C customers. Sales management plays a critical role in driving business growth and success. This subject will develop your knowledge of sales management strategies across offline and online settings. You will learn to critically analyse the principles and theories of strategic sales management and personal selling. Further, you will learn to utilise ethics and culture in devising sales management strategies.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse theories and concepts underpinning strategic sales management and personal selling, individually and/or collaboratively.
Apply ethics and consider diverse cultural background in designing sales management strategies.
Critically discuss the appropriate use of sales management strategies via offline and online settings.

title: CONSUMER DECISION MAKING
syllabus_overview: Consumer Decision Making offers overall knowledge of consumer decision-making. This subject explores the psychological, social, and cultural factors that influence consumers' perceptions, attitudes, and purchase decisions. This subject will develop your knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles of consumer behaviour. You will learn to critically analyse consumer responses to firms' marketing efforts by utilising consumer behaviour theories. Further, you will learn to recommend actionable solutions for marketing problems underpinned by consumer behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse theories, concepts, and principles of consumer behaviour, individually and/or collaboratively.
For marketing problems, recommend actionable and theory-driven solutions that embrace ethical and social responsibility.
Critically and theoretically analyse consumer responses to marketing stimuli embracing cultural and global variability.

title: APPLIED MARKETING RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: In response to the swift changes in marketing environments, managers must utilise evidence from research to identify problems and opportunities. Applied Marketing Research offers overall knowledge of the critical role of marketing research in the identification of marketing problems, solutions, and opportunities. This subject will develop your knowledge of the principles and practices of marketing research. You will learn to analyse and develop marketing research projects. Further, you will generate insights and recommend solutions for marketing problems via utilising proper marketing research methods.
learning_outcomes: Critique a marketing research project and develop an alternative version that is methodologically rigorous.
Utilising appropriate methods to analyse data and generate insights, recommend actionable solutions for marketing problems to the audience.
Critically analyse and explain the principles and practices of marketing research, individually and/or collaboratively.

title: HEURISTICS AND BIASES IN MARKETING DECISIONS
syllabus_overview: Heuristics and Biases in Marketing Decisions offers overall knowledge of heuristics in marketing. Heuristics are mental shortcuts that people use to make decisions quickly and efficiently, but nonetheless, they normally lead to biases and, hence, irrational decisions. Relatedly, managing heuristics and biases can shape the quality of marketing decisions. You will learn to identify and analyse heuristics utilised in marketing decisions along with the biases they promote. You will learn about mechanisms that help suppress biases in marketing decisions. Further, you will learn to utilise your knowledge of heuristics and biases in marketing to critique business performance.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate ethically responsible, theoretically grounded strategies to suppress biases in marketing decision-making.
Critically analyse and synthesise how heuristics and cognitive biases shape marketing decisions, drawing on evidence-based analysis, individually and/or collaboratively.
Integrate advanced knowledge of consumer heuristics and cognitive biases to critically evaluate marketing decisions and outcomes in real-world high-profile cases.

title: INTERNATIONAL MARKETING MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Companies may need to apply marketing practices to meet the varied wants and demands of customers across borders. International Marketing Management offers overall knowledge of the challenges that businesses face when they offer their products and services across cultures and international markets. This subject will develop your knowledge of the theories and principles of international marketing management. Further, you will learn to identify and recommend actionable solutions for major business challenges and opportunities driven by variabilities across international markets.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse theories, concepts, and principles underpinning international marketing management, individually and/or collaboratively.
Recommend actionable and theory-driven solutions for international marketing problems.
Critically analyse international marketing problems of a business.

title: MARKETING ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: Marketing professionals face an abundance of data. They need the skills that enable them to figure out the trends and insights from different sources of data as inputs required in designing g a range of marketing strategies and practices. Marketing Analytics offers an integrated view of a variety of computer-aided decision models used in marketing. You will learn to utilise proper analytical tools in marketing to enhance firm performance. You will learn to analyse analytical tools to evaluate the marketing performance of a firm. Further, you will learn to recommend solutions for marketing problems utilising insights generated from marketing analytics techniques.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critique data sources and analytical tools to assess marketing performance, individually and/or collaboratively.
Generate business insights from quantitative analyses to solve strategic and tactical marketing-management problems and communicate in a professional manner to the audience.
Utilise appropriate metrics and analytical tools in marketing to improve business performance.

title: SERVICES MARKETING
syllabus_overview: Nowadays, services are the major drivers of advanced economies. Relatedly, the successful delivery of services is critical for any business. Services Marketing offers overall knowledge of an integrated view of the dynamics of service delivery. This subject develops your skills to critically analyse processes and interactions that facilitate the effective delivery of services. You will learn to analyse the role of AI agents versus humanised agents in the delivery of services. Further, you will learn to design strategies for the effective delivery of services.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the application of AI/humanised robots, and human agents at the service encounter.
Critically analyse service processes and interactions at varied service touchpoints, individually and/or collaboratively.
Exercise professional judgment and design strategies for promoting the effective delivery of services.

title: CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Exceptional customer experiences (CX) drive long-term business success. Customer Experience Management offers overall knowledge of how to create exceptional CX across various touchpoints. You will learn to analyse the design and operationalisation of successful customer experiences. You will learn to feature social and ethical considerations in the analysis of CX. Further, you will learn to develop solutions for CX problems to enhance firm performance.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse customer experiences from social and ethical considerations.
