Critically analyse the design and implementation of successful customer experiences, individually and/or collaboratively.
Develop actionable and theory-driven customer experience strategies that enhance firm performance.

title: MARKETING STRATEGY AND PLANNING
syllabus_overview: Marketing Strategy and Planning offers overall knowledge of the principles and practices of strategic marketing. Firm success relies heavily on the design and implementation of well-crafted and competitive marketing strategies. You will critically analyse the role that marketing management strategies play in the business model of a company. You will learn to communicate marketing strategies in a professional manner to the audience. Further, you will learn to develop marketing strategy solutions that value ethical and cultural values.
learning_outcomes: Communicate marketing strategies professionally in written and oral methods individually and/or collaboratively.
Design and develop marketing strategies that embrace ethical, social, and cultural views to solve marketing problems.
Exercise professional judgment and reflect on the role of marketing management strategies and theories in the business model of a firm.

title: BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS MARKETING STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: Companies may purchase products and services from other firms to serve their own customers. Marketing products and services to these business customers require processes that differ from those utilised to market products and services to customers who purchase them for their own use (i.e., consumers). B2B Marketing Strategy offers overall knowledge of the strategies involved in marketing products and services to business customers. You will analyse the principles and theories that underpin successful B2B marketing. Further, you will learn to apply B2B marketing theories to develop solutions for B2B marketing problems.
learning_outcomes: Utilise appropriate theories to identify business-to-business marketing problems.
Communicate in a professional manner to the audience actionable and theory-driven solutions for business-to-business marketing problems.
Critically analyse theories, principles, and strategies that underpin business-to-business marketing.

title: CONTENT MARKETING STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: Companies rely on content marketing to elicit favourable consumer responses (e.g., engagement, purchase intent, word-of-mouth). Content Marketing Strategy offers overall knowledge of how companies can effectively manage their valuable yet free content to promote desired consumer responses. You will learn to analyse the content marketing practices of a firm. You will learn to utilise marketing metrics to identify content marketing problems. Further, you will apply appropriate theories to enhance the content marketing practices of a firm.
learning_outcomes: Utilise appropriate metrics and analytical tools to identify the content marketing issues of a business.
Critically analyse the content marketing practices of firms, individually and/or collaboratively.
Recommend actionable and theory-driven solutions for enhancing the content marketing practices of a business.

title: COMPREHENSIVE MENTAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will develop fundamental knowledge and skills required in clinical mental health practice. Students will develop comprehensive assessment and management skills and recognise the interrelationship between a person's medical, social and psychological health. This subject provides a theoretical and practical foundation that prepares students for ethically oriented professional practice. This subject enables students to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and specialised clinical proficiency. Using independent judgment, you will plan, implement and evaluate practice in mental health contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate learning strategies that are responsive to reflective practice.
Perform and evaluate clinical assessments appropriate for mental health care.
Critically analyse information to enable informed clinical decision making based to solve problems.

Develop and evaluate evidence-based nursing plans that support therapeutic relationships with mental health consumers and their families and carers that are characterized by co-constructive care and collaborative engagement.

title: DIGITAL MARKETING STRATEGY
syllabus_overview: With the prominence of digital platforms, it is critical for companies to supplement and further advance their traditional activities by managing their marketing activities via digital platforms. Digital platforms allow companies to enhance their productivity in achieving their objectives. Digital Marketing Strategy offers overall knowledge of digital marketing strategies and principles to enhance firms' digital performance. This subject develops your knowledge of theories and principles utilised in digital marketing. You will learn to analyse the digital marketing practices of a firm. Further, you will apply digital marketing principles to develop solutions for the digital marketing problems of a company.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the digital marketing practices of businesses.
Recommend actionable and theory-driven solutions for digital marketing problems of a business.
Critically analyse theories and principles utilised in digital marketing, individually and/or collaboratively.

title: EXPERIENCES AND PERCEPTIONS OF MENTAL ILLNESS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will explore the complexities that exercising choice and control poses for people with mental illness and develop knowledge and skills such as supported decision making and recovery orientated practice. It will also explore the challenges and strategies for ensuring the collective voices of people with mental illness are heard about systemic issues.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate evidence-based interventions that support therapeutic relationships with mental health consumers and their families and carers that are characterised by co-constructive care and collaborative engagement.
Practice professional person centered care and advocacy independently as a team member in mental health and educational settings in accordance with professional ethical standards.
Develop and evaluate learning strategies that are responsive to reflective practice.
Critically evaluate models of care to achieve personalized care strategies that meet the life and health needs of mental health consumers.

title: MENTAL HEALTH DIAGNOSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will critically examine psychopathology, mental health diagnosis and associated co-morbidities. This subject enables students to develop critical thinking and problem solving skills to be clinically knowledgeable in assessment and diagnosis of mental illness. The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM)and International Classification of Diseases (ICD) classification systems are critically evaluated.
learning_outcomes: Consolidate and synthesise knowledge of mental health diagnosis to understand symptoms and psychopathology.
Critically evaluate and apply available evidence to inform best practice in mental health.
Make accurate assessments and informed judgements to develop reasonable and justifiable clinical formulations and plans.
Recognise ongoing learning needs and use effective learning strategies for professional practice.

title: THERAPEUTIC SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will extend their knowledge and application of therapeutic skills to make high level, independent clinical decisions. Students will analyse and consolidate complex communication skills required in specialist mental health practice. Students will combine interpersonal skills with evidence-based therapies to attain specialist skills required for therapeutic interventions relevant to their professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Generate effective communication skills to effectively and sensitively work with colleagues, people accessing mental health services and the public in accordance with professional ethical standards.
Critically analyse information to enable informed decision making aimed to solve problems.
Practice professional person centered care and advocacy independently and with mental health team members in accordance with professional ethical standards.
Apply and evaluate knowledge and skills to collaborate in complex clinical practice outcomes in mental health care.

title: ADVANCED THERAPEUTIC SKILLS FOR MENTAL HEALTH NURSING
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will critically examine theoretical frameworks for conducting advanced therapeutic skills in mental health nursing practice. Students will extend their understanding of therapeutic approaches including talk based therapy and working with people in crisis, using a problem-solving approach in the context of mental health care. Students will gain enhanced knowledge and skills required to undertake therapy with a specific focus on advanced communication and language.
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate learning strategies that are responsive to reflective practice.

Engage creatively in therapeutic relationships with mental health consumers their families/carers and significant others, which are characterized by co-construction of care and collaborative engagement.
Extend the range of psycho-therapeutic interventions applied to recovery in different situations and contexts of care.
Extend your current knowledge and use advanced therapeutic skills in mental health nursing, for common mental health and illness issues.
Generate effective communication skills to effectively and sensitively work with colleagues, people accessing mental health services and the public in accordance with professional ethical standards.

title: ADVANCED MENTAL HEALTH PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will build on their advanced knowledge and skills in mental health. The subject emphasises advanced and specialist practice in mental health. Students will develop cognitive and technical skills that demonstrate a broad understanding of underlying principles and theoretical concepts in mental health practice, and an advanced understanding of mental health conditions and treatment planning in the context of recovery orientated practice.
learning_outcomes: Perform your advanced practice in a safe and ethical manner using the required specific skills, knowledge and attitudes.
Utilise analytical, problem solving, planning & evaluation skills to inform your advanced practice.
Critically reflect on your current practice and determine how to re-frame this practice to meet mental health practice requirements.
Make accurate assessments & develop reasonable and justifiable inferences in complex scenarios.
Critically evaluate available evidence to inform your advanced practice.

title: MENTAL HEALTH NURSING: CONSIDERATION IN TREATMENT AND RECOVERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will analyse the nature and extent of social, political, economic and organisational influences on mental health nursing care. Students will engage in collaborative critical reflection on mental health nursing practice and address constraints in negotiation of options for mental health care. Students will explore the role of mental health nursing in the context of mental health legislation, advocacy and recovery. Students will demonstrate the role of the mental health nurse in a multidisciplinary and multi-professional approach to treatment and recovery
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the role of the mental health nurse in a multidisciplinary and multi professional approach to treatment and recovery.
Critically appraise the nature and extent of influences on mental health to address constraints in negotiation of options for mental health care.
Engage in collaborative critical reflection on mental health nursing practice.
Critically evaluate models of care relevant to the care continuum, to inform co-constructed personalised care strategies which meet the consumer’s life needs as well as health needs.

title: CONSTRUCTIVE PRACTICE RECOMMENDATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will consolidate your learning by developing evidence-based practice recommendations suitable for the workplace. This subject will teach you professional skills and allow you to showcase your skills to your peers and the broader community.
learning_outcomes: Develop evidence-based practice recommendations.
Critically evaluate outcomes of topic of inquiry project
Communicate project processes and outcomes professionally to peers.

title: CRITIQUING RESEARCH LITERATURE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you learn how to critically review research literature, focusing on research methods, ethics and study findings or results. Through building skills in critical evaluation of research methods and results you will be able to compare papers relevant to a given topic and assess their suitability and relevance to specific problems. You will learn to judge whether research studies are appropriately designed to address the problems that they aim to solve or explore.
learning_outcomes: Conduct comparative analyses of research findings relevant to clinical practice.
Critically appraise and compare research methods reported in the published literature.
Critically analyse methodological approaches justified in research studies.

title: CONSIDERATIONS IN TREATMENT, RECOVERY AND SERVICE DELIVERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will analyse the nature and extent of social, political, economic and organisational influences on mental health care. Students will engage in collaborative critical reflection on mental health practice and address constraints in negotiation of options for mental health care. Students will demonstrate the role of the mental health professional in a multidisciplinary and multi-professional approach to treatment and recovery.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate models of care relevant to the care continuum, to inform co-constructed personalised care strategies which meet the consumer’s life needs as well as health needs.
Demonstrate the role of the mental health professional in a multidisciplinary and multi-professional approach to treatment and recovery.
Critically appraise the nature and extent of influences on mental health to address constraints in negotiation of options for mental health care.
Engage in collaborative critical reflection on mental health practice.

title: ADVANCED MENTAL HEALTH NURSING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will build on their knowledge and skills in mental health nursing practice. The subject emphasises advanced and specialist practice in mental health nursing. Students will develop cognitive and technical skills that demonstrate a broad understanding of a body of knowledge of underlying principles and theoretical concepts in mental health nursing., and an advanced understanding of mental health conditions and treatment planning in the context of recovery orientated practice.
learning_outcomes: Utilise analytical, problem solving, planning & evaluation skills to inform your advanced mental health nursing practice.
Generate effective communication skills to effectively and sensitively work with colleagues, people accessing mental health services and the public in accordance with professional ethical standards.
Critically reflect on your mental health nursing practice and determine how to reframe this practice to meet mental health nursing practice requirements.
Make accurate mental health nursing assessments & develop reasonable and justifiable inferences in complex scenarios.
Critically evaluate available evidence to inform your mental health nursing practice.

title: MENTAL HEALTH NURSING AND THERAPEUTIC PHARMACOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will develop knowledge and skills to identify the effects of medications on physiological, biochemical and pathophysiological body systems. Students will apply systematic clinical assessment and evidence based critical thinking skills to justify rationales for the initiation/instigation of therapeutic medications and treatment plans in mental health nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe principles of pharmacology, including the differences between pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, the manner in which medications are absorbed, distributed, metabolised and excreted in the body.
Demonstrate evidence of collaborative care and communicate treatment plan clearly to patients, families and other health professionals.
Expand your knowledge and use of psycho-pharmacology, including medication management, for common mental health and illness issues.
Critically analyse information to enable informed clinical decision making to solve problems in the management and of delivery pharmacological interventions.

title: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT & LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn processes to develop quality improvement initiatives in the workplace. You will plan a quality improvement initiative based on your review of the literature and reflection on current workplace or community needs. This subject will develop your problem-solving and leadership skills and help you create an appropriate and ethical design to address a real-world need.
learning_outcomes: Apply effective reflective practice to planning quality improvement projects
Critically reflect on learning needs through critical literature reviews
Justify ethical approaches in quality improvement projects
Apply critical skills to problem solving in planning evaluations

title: TALK BASED THERAPIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will critically examine theoretical frameworks for conducting talk based therapy sessions using a problem-solving approach to working with people in the context of mental health care. Students will gain enhanced knowledge and skills required to undertake therapy with a specific focus on advanced communication and language.
learning_outcomes: Extend the range of psycho-therapeutic interventions applied to recovery in different situations and contexts of care.
Describe overall formulations of individuals with mental health related issues, leading to appropriate interventions.
Extend the knowledge and use of talk-based therapies for common mental health and illness issues.

Engage creatively in therapeutic relationships with mental health consumers, their families/carers and significant others, which are characterized by co-construction of care and collaborative engagement.

title: THERAPEUTIC PHARMACOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop knowledge and skills to identify the effects of medications on physiological, biochemical and pathophysiological body systems. Students will apply systematic clinical assessment and evidence based critical thinking skills to justify rationales for the initiation/instigation of therapeutic medications and treatment plans.
learning_outcomes: Expand your knowledge and use of psycho-pharmacology, including medication management, for common mental health and illness issues.
Apply scientific judgement and contemporary evidence from a range of sources to inform and support clinical decision making in the management and delivery pharmacological interventions.
Demonstrate evidence of collaborative care and communicates treatment plan clearly to patients, families and other health professionals.

Describe principles of pharmacology, including the differences between pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, the manner in which medications are absorbed, distributed, metabolised and excreted in the body.

title: SCRIPTWRITING PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will acquire the skills and knowledge to begin the development and writing of a full length theatre performance text, series pilot or feature film script, by presenting a pitch, a treatment or concept, a folio of selected scenes, and workshopped readings. This subject explores script writing as a range of practices that are culturally and historically shaped. It combines critical readings of theoretical texts, plays and screenplays with the opportunity to workshop your writing in a supportive, collaborative environment. We will also survey local and national script development and script production opportunities for emerging writers. This is a level 3 subject.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise narrative elements and apply appropriate conventions of form and layout to create a coherent and compelling segment of a performance text, film or television screenplay.
Assemble appropriate elements of style, genre and narrative to devise and propose a long form concept for a performance text, film script or television series.

Construct a coherent and compelling long form narrative expressed in language consistent with the conventions used in storylines, scene breakdowns, synopses and treatments in theatre, film and television production.
Analyse and evaluate a script, identify its problems and suggest solutions for a redraft.

title: SCREENPLAY/RADIOPLAY: AN INTRODUCTION TO SCRIPTWRITING
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to writing short screen and radio plays. It takes a playful and experimental approach to exploring narrative forms for screen and radio such as place, image, and character. This subject will suit those who are new to script writing, as well as those who have had some script writing experience. Your creative work will be informed by critical readings and case studies of short film and radio scripts and productions, and your writing will be developed in a supportive, collaborative environment. These activities will help strengthen your ability to craft stories across all genres, and to critically reflect on your work. We will also consider the opportunities to produce and distribute short films and radio plays, which have increased dramatically in the last few years. This is a Level 2 subject: please consider the subject prerequisites before enrolling. This subject includes live sessions, either online or face-to-face, with the expectation of student attendance and participation.
learning_outcomes: Critically and reflectively engage with one's creative writing.
Work collaboratively and independently on scripted projects.
Apply knowledge of narrative forms and screen and sound production processes, genres and aesthetics to the writing of short form scripts.
Respond flexibly, effectively and creatively to feedback, production requirements, limitations, deadlines and contingencies.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING ONE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will work in collaborative teams, to develop your understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams including the student nurse’s scope of practice. This subject will enable you to explore your own profession, as well as other health and human service providers. You will come to understand the therapeutic use of nursing in various health care scenarios from a quality and patient safety and legal and ethical perspective. You will be introduced to the concept of evidenced based practice. The subject will explore the evolution of nursing and nursing theory across the ages and its representation in current society. You will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. This will require comprehension and demonstration of obtaining specific physiological, psychological, cultural, and social information about people, planning, and implementing basic patient care and effective therapeutic communication techniques with patients to maintain patient safety. This subject will explore care needs across the lifespan from birth to death, including the care of patients with all abilities. You will be introduced to the application of clinical reasoning, clinical decision making and reflective practice. Contemporary nursing theory that underpins practice will be discussed. You will investigate the requirement for comprehensive care to meet individual needs including falls, pressure injuries and nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Use effective written and verbal communication strategies to build therapeutic relationships to facilitate effective communication with patients and other health professionals
Describe the roles and responsibilities of nurses as members of an intra and interprofessional team
Examine the importance of quality and patient safety strategies in the provision of safe patient care
Employ evidenced practice in clinical psychomotor skills to provide focused foundational nursing care
Explain the concept of reflection on practice to professional and individual development
Apply clinical reasoning and decision making process to patients across the life span
Apply appropriate health assessment frameworks to ensure person-centred care across the lifespan

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING TWO
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of person-centred care for people experiencing simple common acute illness requiring hospitalisation. You will examine communication and other strategies to facilitate safe interactions in the healthcare context. The importance of partnering with consumers and involving patient in their care planning will be explored. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. Included care of patients with all abilities. You will be introduced to the theoretical basis of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and to the role of controlling the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration related to oral and topical. Through application of aseptic and infection control principles discuss ways to control healthcare associated infection. The three-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory. In this placement you will undertake health assessments with assigned patients and use the data obtained to develop person-centred plans of care considering principles of personal and patient safety and interprofessional practice in a variety of settings. This subject will also introduce students to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Use appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Demonstrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings
Employ a range of communication and other strategies to facilitate safe and effective clinical and professional care interactions with people and health professionals
Identify the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice
Apply principles of Aspect Non-Touch Technique to prevent and control healthcare associated infection

title: COMMUNICATION FOR RURAL NURSING LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop communication skills, knowledge and attitudes required to manage challenging interactions in the rural health setting. Engagement in complicated, often stressful and distressing communication encounters with other people requires you to be equipped with a range of skills in order to respond effectively and therapeutically. You will explore a range of communication and resilience strategies and develop resourcefulness for leadership in rural health.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the skills required to work independently and as team leader and influential team member in a variety of situations within the rural health settings in accordance with professional ethical standards.
Critically reflect on your own communication approaches that may ameliorate or exacerbate a challenging interaction.
Apply communication theory and techniques to challenging interactions and situations in rural nursing practice.
Identify the resources available within the rural clinical environment for reporting and addressing a challenging interaction.
Apply appropriate communication approaches to situations of crisis in rural nursing practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING THREE
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning and provision of patient-centred care for persons experiencing an illness requiring hospitalisation in acute or subacute settings or management through primary care. You will explore patients with healthcare concerns across the lifespan and end of life care. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will extend your theoretical understanding of pharmacology and the responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in injectable medication administration. This subject will develop knowledge regarding diagnostic testing (haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, medical imaging). Included care of patients with all abilities. The four-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients with acute and or chronic illness that is underpinned by nursing theory. During the placement you will develop your medication administration and refine your patient health assessment using systematic frameworks and use data obtained to develop person-centred plans of care. You will develop your clinical skills in implementing and evaluating patient care in secondary, primary and /or mental health care settings. This subject will refine patient and team-based communication skills and other approaches to support patient safety.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing to individuals at end-of-life or experiencing acute or chronic diseases
Employ evidence-based practice in implementation of clinical nursing care for patients at end-of-life or experiencing acute or chronic health conditions across various health settings
Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings as a member of the health care team
Employ appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers, anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate safe person-centred care for people across the lifespan that is evidenced based and culturally relevant
Demonstrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE PATHWAY TRANSITION
syllabus_overview: This is a transition pathway to the Bachelor of Nursing, enabling students an accelerated degree, specifically for students who have an undergraduate degree other than Nursing or have entered through a health sciences diploma pathway. In this subject, students will explore health standards that influence healthcare including National Safety and Quality Standards (NSQHS), Aged Care Quality Standards, National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), My Health Record, and Aging in Place. Students will develop a deep understanding of the therapeutic use of nursing in various health care scenarios from a quality and patient safety, legal and ethical perspective. Students will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. Students will explore the evolution of nursing and nursing theory across the ages and its representation in current society. They will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery, including care of all patients and abilities. An introduction to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice will also be examined. This subject will introduce students to the application of clinical reasoning and decision making required by registered nurses in the delivering person-centred, evidence-based care for people experiencing hospitalisation with a focus on a variety of systems and diseases, across the lifespan. They will learn to work in inter- and intra-professional teams to develop their understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams, including the student nurse’s scope of practice. Students will be introduced to pharmacotherapies and safe and quality use in medicines. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the student and registered nurse in medication administration will be examined. Through application of aseptic and infection control principles students will examine different ways to control healthcare associated infection. The three-week clinical placement will allow students to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory.
learning_outcomes: Illustrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings
Apply appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Employ a range of communication and other strategies to facilitate safe and effective clinical and professional care interactions with people and health professionals
Apply principles of aseptic non touch technique to prevent and control healthcare associated infection
Examine the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice
Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings
Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Apply clinical reasoning to deliver person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Explore how health standards influence care quality and patient outcomes including NSQHS and Aged Care Quality Standards
Apply knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology to individuals with a range of health conditions, across the lifespan

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING FOUR
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation person-centred care for people requiring hospitalisation in acute or subacute settings experiencing acute deterioration. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will investigate patients with healthcare concerns across the lifespan experiencing gastrointestinal, reproductive, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and immune disorders. You will extend your theoretical understanding of pharmacology and the responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration in urgent care situations. Included care of patients with all abilities. This subject will develop knowledge regarding diagnostic testing (haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, medical imaging) in gastrointestinal, reproductive, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and immune disorders and in to investigate patient deterioration. The four-week clinical placement will enable you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients and recognise, report, and respond to patient experiencing acute deterioration in acute, subacute, primary care and/or mental health settings. This subject will develop your medication administration, refine your patient health assessment skills and enhance patient and team-based communication skills in critical situations. In this placement you will use data obtained to develop, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred plans of care for patient experiencing acute deterioration as part of a healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Use appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to detect and recognise patient deterioration considering individual, anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors across the lifespan
Using knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing, identify deterioration in individuals experiencing acute or chronic disorders
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred care for people experiencing deterioration that is culturally relevant and age specific
Devise strategies to incorporate reflection into professional nursing practice
Develop an awareness of and contribute to the risk management strategies of a healthcare agency, to implement incident reporting procedures and apply risk management procedures

Apply safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication strategies in various health settings as a member of the healthcare team
Demonstrate and evaluate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration of simple and complex medications in a range of settings and situations

title: TRANSLATING EVIDENCE TO PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will compare and critique the approaches taken in the research literature to gain understanding of how others have approached research problems and insight into how evidence is developed and established into practice. You will also use a local example to consider how a recent initiative related to research has been incorporated into practice, with consideration of the barriers and enablers to implementation. You will reflect on the ways that recommendations from research are framed and consider the elements needed for successful approaches for the translation of evidence into practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical thinking in the conduct of comparative analyses of different aspects of research studies
Critique justifications for research recommendations
Analyse processes that enhance and impede the translation of evidence into practice

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE NURSE TRANSITION
syllabus_overview: This is a transition subject to the Bachelor of Nursing as part of the accelerated degree. This subject is specifically for students who have a nursing qualification, either as an enrolled Nurse or a Registered Nurse outside Australia. In this subject, students will work in collaborative teams to develop their understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams. There will be a strong focus on the transition from the role of the enrolled nurse to registered nurse. An introduction to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice will also be explored. Students will be introduced to the concept of evidenced based practice and the use of research in the degree. Foundational academic skills and information literacy required for successful university study will be prioritised and developed. In addition, students will learn the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the comprehensive assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of person-centred, evidence-based care. A lifelong approach to nursing care will be addressed. Students will also have opportunity to revise the theoretical basis of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and to the role of controlling the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration will be examined and practised. The three-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory.
learning_outcomes: Incorporate principles of evidence-based research and literacy skills in academic writing
Demonstrate safe nursing practice within scope of practice that is professional, accountable, ethical, and legal underpinned by evidence-based knowledge
Demonstrate suitable database searches in relation to nursing practice
Examine the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice
Practice appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors
Apply the principles of reflective practice to further develop your professional nursing practice
Critically examine the roles and responsibilities of a registered nurse as members of an intra and interprofessional team
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Demonstrate and practice safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation, and administration in a range of settings

title: RURAL NURSING DURING DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will Identify the importance of disaster planning and preparedness in building resilient health services and communities. You will identify the role of nurses and other emergency personnel in rural communities during disasters. You will explore localised environmental emergencies, disease outbreaks and pandemics. This subject will use the United Nations build back better framework to support rebuilding and transforming rural communities after disasters. You will develop skills and knowledge to build resilience needed to adapt to the changes and challenges in the regulatory environment during a pandemic or emergency and to protect the safety of the community and healthcare workers.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the role of the nurse in providing psychological assistance and responding to socio-cultural context during rural disasters and emergencies and consider the protection, safety and mental wellbeing of disaster survivors, health care workers and others across the disaster response process.
Analyse the impact of changes on the practice environment related to disaster and emergency planning and management.

Reflect upon the importance of technical skill development (related to infection control practices, basic and advanced first aid, and setting up of treatment tents) in provision of practical assistance during disaster and emergency responses.
Reflect on (one's own use of) critical thinking, teamwork, and adaptability in the planning of disaster nursing response with respect to a range of disasters in the rural practice context.
Critically analyse a range of disaster preparedness approaches and disaster nursing models to improve disaster knowledge, preparedness, and response.
Communicate legal and ethical considerations in particular setting of boundaries, scope of practice, professional ethics, and adherence to the law to a range of expert and non-expert audiences.
Evaluate the assessment and triage process in rural disaster and emergency contexts and establish best practice guidelines.

title: RURAL NURSING IN COMMUNITIES WITH PRIORITY POPULATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be focusing on the health priorities of rural and regional people, particularly from priority populations. You will identify how the Australian health care system impacts rural communities and how health services work collaboratively to meet the unique needs of each rural community. This subject will equip you with the skills to conduct comprehensive assessment, care planning and referral to address the health needs of various population groups including children, adolescents, women and men across the lifespan, people with disability, people experiencing mental health, family violence among other specific population groups. This will all be done whilst, recognising the role of culture, beliefs, lifestyle and family dynamics and how this impacts nursing care for these populations.
learning_outcomes: Critically review current knowledge and understanding of health priorities in regional and rural Australia.

Plan comprehensive assessment and care for individuals, families and communities living in rural Australia including specific population groups such as people with mental health illness, family violence and disability.
Appraise the generalist healthcare role of the registered nurse and unique needs for rural communities and specific population groups.
Articulate rural practice models and workforce issues including collaboration between interdisciplinary professionals, healthcare providers and government agencies.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING FIVE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will advance your abilities to develop, implement, evaluate, and manage evidence-based person-centred care for several patients with comorbidities across the lifespan. Nursing theory and evidence based practice will be further studied. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will compare the influence of lifespan and polypharmacy on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. The subject will explore aging and sustainable access and delivery of health services to people living with acute and/or chronic illness across the lifespan including public health strategies and models of chronic illness management. You will look at ways to promote active engagement with health services among people across the lifespan and recommend ways to improve the sustainability of health services for people. Included will be the promotion of health and care of individuals with all abilities. The four-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical knowledge, skills, and attitudes into your nursing practice in acute, subacute, primary care, mental health, aged care, or paediatrics for a group of patients. The clinical practicum will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of multiple patients and plan, implement and evaluate care across the lifespan. In this placement you will be advance your medication management and consolidate your patient health assessment and skills in using data to develop person-centred plans of care across the lifespan for patient with comorbidities as part of a healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication in various health settings as a member of the healthcare team
Interpret knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing and apply to individuals experiencing acute or chronic comorbid disorders
Justify safe use of medicines in a range of settings and situations including polypharmacy
Critique in self and others, strategies to incorporate reflection into professional nursing practice

Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred care for people with acute, chronic and comorbid disease that is prioritised and culturally relevant across the lifespan

Use appropriate health assessment frameworks and techniques for patients across the lifespan with comorbidities that are systematic and person-centred considering, anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors to recognise and respond to clinical change

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING SIX
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will refine your abilities to: manage care for several complex patients; reflect on your personal practice; plan, implement and evaluate prioritised evidence-based person-centred care for multiple individuals. The subject content builds on previously learnt concepts of person-centred care and assessment, situational management, nursing inquiry, therapeutic and professional communication and client education that are applied across the lifespan. The focus of the subject is to assist you to develop the repertoire of skills required in contemporary nursing practice to care for patients with all abilities across the lifespan. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery and self care. The six-week clinical placement will allow you to consolidate your professional nursing practice in readiness to transition to the workforce. You will manage person-centred health requirements in acute, subacute, primary care, mental health, aged care, or paediatrics. The clinical practicum will allow you to integrate learnt theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients and plan, implement and evaluate care across the lifespan. In this placement you will advance your skills and knowledge in medication management, refined health assessment and working as a member of the healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate your own professional nursing practice against the Standards for Practice and Quality and Safety frameworks
Critically review knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing and apply to individuals experiencing acute or chronic comorbid disorders across the lifespan

Apply appropriate health assessment techniques that are practised, systematic and person-centred across the lifespan considering individual, anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors to recognise and respond to clinical change
Develop safe and efficient nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical, legal and underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication
Apply sound clinical reasoning and evidence-based person-centred care to plan, implement and evaluate care that is prioritised and culturally relevant for patients across the lifespan
Exhibit safe use of medicines for multiple patients in a range of settings and situations

title: APPLIED EVIDENCED BASED CARE IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be given an opportunity to further explore the importance of evidenced based care in health care and you will be encouraged to generate ways of thinking and critique wider health practice to form the foundation for future health practice evolutions. You will look at ways to use health care data in a systematic way and use quality improvement tools and techniques. It will consolidate knowledge on the disease process, public health approaches and understanding of interdisciplinary practice environments in the acute, sub-acute, mental health, paediatric, aged care residential and community settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify the components of a health research project using the principles of quality improvement in healthcare
Analyse and recommend practice improvement opportunities based on contemporary research
Conduct a critical review of the literature relevant to your chosen practice improvement topic
Elicit strategies for individuals and groups to communicate results to a range of audiences for different purposes using a variety of modes

title: FOUNDATIONS OF URGENT CARE NURSING
syllabus_overview: Rural urgent care is a specialist rural nursing competency. This subject will equip you to assess and appropriately manage patients in the rural emergency setting. You will apply your knowledge to specialty population groups such as paediatrics and workers in primary industries and mining. You will learn to adapt your practice to low resource settings as well as being able to use the technology and equipment in contemporary rural health care environments. This subject will equip you to prepare and respond, as part of a multidisciplinary team, to high risk, infrequent situations. Apply Advanced Life Support (ALS) within the rural urgent care setting. Collaboratively stabilise, manage and transfer the acutely unwell patient out of the rural urgent care setting. Emergency maternity care for unplanned birth at term or prematurely. Urgent care emergency preparedness response in relation to natural disasters and pandemics. The subject has both theoretical and clinical components to support advanced skill development.
learning_outcomes: Adapt a comprehensive urgent care plan to the resources available in a variety of rural and remote health care contexts
Critically evaluate rural and remote urgent care nursing practice against research and current literature, applying a practice development framework for quality improvement.
Initiate, plan and evaluate related clinical skills and equipment/technology to address patient care needs within the rural and remote urgent care setting.

Manage care for identified speciality population groups such as bariatric, paediatric, obstetric and critically ill patients, as well as patients with difficult behaviours; or occupational/traumatic injury within rural and remote urgent care settings.

title: COMPREHENSIVE HEALTH ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop advanced health assessment skills to support evidence-based nursing care of people across the lifespan in rural health care contexts. You will integrate knowledge of pathophysiology, assessment and diagnostic findings to make informed clinical decisions and prioritise nursing care. You will build on your capability to respond to the deteriorating patient, and you will develop your non-technical skills to take a leadership role in collaborative care.
learning_outcomes: Integrate assessment and diagnostic findings to make informed clinical decisions, to prioritise care and management, and complete appropriate documentation.
Evaluate risk and appropriately respond to the deteriorating patient in varied rural and remote contexts.
Adapt non-technical skills such as leadership, communication, teamwork, and situational awareness to provide effective collaborative nursing care in a rural and remote context.
Evaluate comprehensive health assessment to diverse rural and remote contexts caring for patients across the life span.

title: COMMUNICATION FOR RURAL NURSING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will analyse, critique, and reflect on different styles and methods of professional communication used in healthcare. This subject will build on your knowledge of effective teamwork, workplace culture and conflict resolution, and will explore the differences in healthcare communication strategies used by registered nurses, rural health services and human resources. You will develop an advanced level of understanding related to challenging interactions, including the impact that highly developed professional communication skills have on patient and healthcare outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast the professional communication styles that are used in healthcare.
Appraise and apply the principles of effective workplace culture within written and verbal communications in healthcare.
Evaluate communication theory and its application in rural healthcare.

Critically reflect on the influence of your own communication and the relationship this has to your learning needs in providing optimal patient care, interprofessional communication and teamwork in the rural health context.
Critically analyse and apply conceptual and technical skills which are used to demonstrate professional communication and apply to challenging interactions.

title: AGEING IN PLACE IN RURAL COMMUNITIES
syllabus_overview: Taking a strengths-based perspective, this subject explores models of care for older people as they transition through home based, acute, sub-acute and residential care in the context of complex financial, regulatory, policy and political frameworks. In this subject you will develop your nursing practice to promote healthy ageing. You will assess, plan, deliver and evaluate person centred nursing care for older adults in rural health care settings. In this subject you will also develop your assessment skills in the management of dementia and delirium, frailty, geriatric syndromes, wound management and palliative care.
learning_outcomes: Coordinate the transition of the older person through acute, sub-acute, community and residential care in the context of regulatory, policy frameworks relevant to rural health.
Identify the signs of cognitive deterioration and impairment in older people and identify services and evidence based interventions for their care and referral.
Demonstrate advanced communication skills to maintain positive therapeutic relationships with patients/residents, their significant others, and the multidisciplinary team.
Apply advanced knowledge, skills and attitudes in the assessment and management of people at the end stages of life.
Apply principles of wound prevention, wound assesssment and wound management, including the evaluation and referral of patients with non-healing wounds.

title: DIGITAL HEALTH FOR RURAL NURSING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply the digital competencies required for nurses to practice in rural health care contexts. The subject will enable you to ensure the privacy, legal and ethical domains of digital health underpin your practice. You will take a person-centred approach to providing technology enabled or enhanced care to support culturally safe care that recognises the needs of vulnerable populations.
learning_outcomes: Review current digital health and telehealth guidelines and select appropriate supports to enhance culturally safe digital health and telehealth care.
Evaluate the key consumer benefits and risks associated with digital health and critically analyse the use of digital health information including electronic health records.
Appraise the people, systems and process challenges impacting implementation of digital health in Australian rural health care settings.
Analyse the procedural, policy, legal, ethical, security and privacy requirements of nurses’ use of digital health.
Evaluate strategies to improve nurses’ confidence and skills in providing care and support using digital health, Artificial Intelligence applications and telehealth.

title: POPULATION HEALTH IN RURAL AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: Using the principles of public health and a health promoting approach this subject focuses on the population health priorities of rural communities. Through an understanding of the wider determinants of health you will be able to identify the associations between environmental, social, structural, economic, cultural, biomedical, commercial and digital environments in which rural communities live, play, work and age and their impacts on health and wellbeing. You will use this knowledge to respond to the needs of individuals and communities to develop culturally safe and appropriate care.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate population health care for children, young people and their family in the rural context.
Evaluate chronic health screening in a rural population. Identify strategies for improvement contextualised to rural Australia.

Analyse health data and identify social determinants of health in a rural population. Select and justify the most important National Health Priority in this population and create a health promotion strategy to address it.
Identify individuals and families at risk of, or undergoing, family violence and apply best practice models for support and referral.
Evaluate health promotion material for cultural safety within minority rural populations.

title: PROFESSIONAL NURSING 1: PROFESSIONAL IDENTITY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus on professional nursing practice in Australian healthcare and the development of a professional nursing identity. Through a combination of theoretical, practical, and reflective activities, you will gain a deep understanding of the knowledge, abilities and attitudes required for professional practice as a registered nurse in Australia. You will be guided in constructing your professional identity by fostering situational awareness, self-reflection, and the development of a professional portfolio. By the conclusion of the subject, you will be equipped to navigate the complexities of practice, while upholding nursing standards, ensuring cultural safety, and contributing to the advancement of healthcare outcomes for diverse populations.
learning_outcomes: Examine and identify strategies for self-care, stress management, and burnout prevention for personal well-being.
Reflect on personal values and beliefs to promote self-awareness and culturally safe nursing care.
Critically evaluate professional standards, codes, and guidelines for evidenced based nursing practice.
Classify the roles of nurses and other health professionals within Australian healthcare.
Establish a professional portfolio as evidence of professional identity development and continuing professional development (CPD).
Integrate and apply knowledge, skills, and values necessary for safe, quality, person-centred nursing care in the Australian healthcare context.

title: ADVANCED PATHOPHYSIOLOGY FOR HEALTH PROFESSIONALS
syllabus_overview: This subject provides essential knowledge to support safe, evidence-based care within advanced scope of practice. The subject explores the transition from health to illness through an in-depth understanding of cellular function, genetic and epigenetic influences, inflammation, ageing, and systemic physiological alterations. You will investigate key organ systems, and the pathophysiological changes associated with common and complex conditions encountered in clinical settings. There is emphasis on the clinical relevance of altered physiological parameters and how these inform assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prescribing decisions. You will develop advanced clinical reasoning skills and the ability to interpret assessment findings using appropriate scientific terminology. This course bridges theoretical knowledge with real-world application, enabling students to make informed, person-centred decisions in their advanced area of practice.
learning_outcomes: Communicate using precise scientific and clinical terminology to describe disease processes, analyse findings, and evaluate intervention outcomes.
Analyse the cellular and systemic mechanisms underlying disease, including disruptions in homeostasis, nerve conduction, and physiological function.
Critically evaluate the roles of genetics, epigenetics, inflammation, and ageing in the progression from health to complex disease states
Interpret pathophysiological changes in clinical assessment data to support evidence-based practice.
Integrate advanced clinical reasoning with pathophysiological knowledge to inform safe and effective decision-making in specialty practice.

title: CONTEMPORARY STUDIES 1: LEGAL AND ETHICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with an overview of the Australian legal system, health-related legislation and ethical principles and frameworks for nursing practice. You will examine nursing regulation and the role of the registered nurse in relation to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) professional standards, healthcare legislation and law, ethics, and patient safety in Australia. How prevailing moral theories intersect with ethical nursing practice in the Australia is explored through the application of ethical principles and decision-making frameworks in case studies identifying ethical dilemmas.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse complex ethical dilemmas that arise in nursing practice.
Apply ethical theories and principles to real-world interprofessional and nursing scenarios.
Reflect upon personal values and how these may influence ethical decision making as a registered nurse.
Examine health-related legislation and ethical frameworks relevant to nursing.
Integrate legal principles and ethical frameworks into nursing practice.

title: CONTEMPORARY STUDIES 2: FIRST NATION PEOPLES HEALTH AND HEALING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus on building your capability for working in culturally safe ways with First Nations peoples across the lifespan and within varied healthcare contexts. The subject content integrates key elements of cultural safety for Indigenous peoples, including critical self-reflection, privileging Indigenous knowledges, supporting the right of individuals and groups to self-determination, and addressing racism within the health system. You will examine First Nations understandings of health and healing, and current health outcomes and priorities. The impact of historical, political, and socio-cultural contexts on health outcomes, access, and equity will be analysed. A commitment to improved health outcomes for First Nations peoples will be fostered through the development of advocacy skills that promote social justice and health equity and clinical practice that is holistic, accessible, and safe, free of bias and racism.
learning_outcomes: Review Australian history and analyse the ongoing impacts of colonisation from the perspective of First Nations peoples.
Critically analyse personal and professional values and beliefs to develop reflexive, culturally safe nursing care for First Nations peoples across the lifespan.
Demonstrate an understanding of how cultural safety improves healthcare experiences and outcomes for First Nations peoples.
Critically analyse systemic barriers to health equity and apply decolonising approaches to develop culturally safe practice that encompasses equity and social justice in health.

Explain First Nations peoples’ concept of health and healing, and critically analyse how cultural, historical, and social determinants interconnect and influence health outcomes of First Nations peoples.
Examine responses to different forms of racism and evaluate anti-racism strategies that cultivate culturally safe healthcare environments.

title: PREPARATION FOR NURSING PRACTICE (PNP) 1
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to provide you with the essential knowledge, skills, and competencies required for foundational nursing practice across the lifespan within varied healthcare contexts. In this subject you will utilise the NMBA professional standards and acquire a solid foundation in the fundamental theoretical concepts of nursing and clinical practice, including the principles of clinical reasoning, evidence-based practice, person-centred care, and cultural safety. Throughout the subject, you will have the opportunity to apply these concepts in a simulated environment to develop the essential skills for foundational nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and apply knowledge of foundational principles of nursing and healthcare.
Identify learning needs in respect of professional practice.
Administer oral medications using the National Safety and Quality Health Service (NSQHS) Medication Safety Standard as a framework for safe medication administration and management.
Employ research and evidenced-based practice skills to demonstrate the provision of foundational nursing care according to the NMBA registered nurse standards for practice.
Utilise appropriate health assessment frameworks in the provision of person-centred culturally safe nursing care across the lifespan.
Communicate effectively verbally, non-verbally and in writing.

title: PROFESSIONAL NURSING 2: LEADING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the relationship between professional nursing practice and effective leadership within healthcare contexts. In this subject you will examine current research on the impact of effective leadership in healthcare environments and patient care, and critically analyse real-world scenarios, and contemporary challenges to develop skills required to lead and inspire within the nursing profession. Emphasis will be placed on fostering essential leadership capabilities including emotional intelligence, innovative and strategic thinking, situational awareness, decision-making, and delegation skills. Through engagement with experienced nurse leaders, you will develop an understanding of the complexities and rewards of leading clinical nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Develop leadership capabilities for clinical contexts.
Critically analyse clinical incidents through a leadership lens.
Generate career goals and strategies for their achievement.
Evaluate leadership principles and theories, and their application to nursing practice.
Utilise continuous professional development (CPD) for leadership development.

title: PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE PLACEMENT (PEP) 1
syllabus_overview: Professional Experience Placement (PEP) 1 focuses on developing your foundational nursing practice. Through immersive and supervised placements within various healthcare contexts, you will have the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge and skills gained from Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 1 to real-world healthcare settings. During PEP 1, you will observe, participate, and provide person-centred, culturally safe nursing care under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals. Through this experience, you will gain insights into the dynamics of healthcare environments and the challenges faced by healthcare practitioners, evaluate patient care routines and engage in intraprofessional and interprofessional collaboration. Through reflective activities, case discussions, and debriefing, you will be able to process your experiences, identify areas for growth, and connect your practical experience with relevant theoretical concepts.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively with patients, families, peers, and colleagues.
Address identified learning needs through reflection and continuing professional development (CPD).
Develop practice readiness within real-world healthcare contexts.
Provide person-centred, culturally safe nursing care to individuals across the lifespan and with differing abilities.
Utilise the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice in the application of foundational theoretical knowledge and evidence-based nursing care, within scope of practice.

title: PREPARATION FOR NURSING PRACTICE (PNP) 2
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to provide you with the knowledge, skills, and competencies to transition from foundational to more complex levels of nursing practice across lifespan within varied contexts of practice. The subject builds upon Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 1 to enhance your situational awareness, critical thinking, clinical reasoning, and your ability to recognise and respond effectively to patient deterioration. During the subject, you will use systematic health assessment and data for diagnostic reasoning and decision-making in planning, implementing, and evaluating nursing care for individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease, illness, and deterioration. As you progress through the subject, you will have the opportunity to apply knowledge to clinical situations to further develop your confidence and capabilities as registered nurses according to the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice.
learning_outcomes: Utilise systematic appropriate health assessment frameworks, clinical reasoning and evidenced based practice to assess, plan and implement person-centred, culturally safe nursing care across the lifespan.
Identify learning needs in respect of professional practice.
Use health technology and informatics to identify, plan, revaluate and communicate nursing interventions and outcomes.
Synthesise and apply knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing to individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease, illness, and deterioration
Demonstrate safe quality use of parenteral medicines using the National Safety and Quality Standards Health Service (NSQHS) Medication Safety Standard.
Recognise and respond to patient deterioration, execute rapid response protocols and employ effective communication to convey changes in patient condition to interprofessional healthcare teams.

title: PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE PLACEMENT (PEP) 2
syllabus_overview: Professional Experience Placement (PEP) 2 focuses on transitioning students from foundational to more complex levels of nursing practice and, planning care for individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease, illness and deterioration. Through immersive and supervised placements you will have the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge and skills gained from Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 2 to real-world healthcare settings. During PEP 2, you will observe, plan, implement and evaluate nursing interventions for patients requiring complex care, under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals. Through this experience, you will gain insights into intraprofessional and interprofessional collaboration and the role of registered nurses in complex patient care. Through reflective exercises, case discussions, and debriefing sessions, you will be supported to process your experiences, identify areas for growth, and connect your practical encounters with relevant theoretical concepts.
learning_outcomes: Provide person-centred, culturally safe nursing care to patients across the lifespan, and with differing abilities.
Employ intraprofessional and interprofessional practice skills to collaborate effectively with patients, families, peers, and colleagues.
Address identified learning needs through reflection and continuing professional development (CPD).
Utilise the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice in the application of theoretical knowledge and evidence-based nursing care, within scope of practice.
Develop practice readiness within real-world healthcare contexts.

title: PREPARATION FOR NURSING PRACTICE (PNP) 3
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop your knowledge, skills, and competencies for comprehensive nursing care across lifespan within varied contexts of practice. The subject builds upon Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 1 and 2 to enhance your confidence and capabilities to provide more complex, comprehensive care that is responsive to the needs of individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease and illness. During the subject, you will use comprehensive and systematic health assessment for diagnostic reasoning and decision-making in the planning, implementation, and evaluation of evidenced based nursing care. As students’ progress through the subject, they will have the opportunity to apply knowledge to clinical situations and further develop their capabilities as registered nurses according to the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify learning needs in respect of professional practice.

Utilise comprehensive and systematic health assessment, clinical reasoning, and evidenced-based practice to assess, plan and implement comprehensive person-centred, culturally safe nursing care across the lifespan.
Synthesise and apply knowledge of systems-based pathophysiology to individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease and illness.
Demonstrate safe, quality use of medicines using the National Safety and Quality Health Service (NSQHS) Medication Safety Standard.
Use health technology and informatics to identify, plan, revaluate and communicate nursing interventions and outcomes.

title: PREPARATION FOR NURSING PRACTICE (MENTAL HEALTH AND RECOVERY) (PNP) 4
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to provide you with a comprehensive foundation in mental health, recovery and wellbeing across lifespan and in various healthcare settings. This subject builds on Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 1-3 to equip you with the knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to provide holistic care for individuals experiencing mental health symptoms. As you progress through the subject you will gain insights into the complexities of mental health, therapeutic interventions, effective communication, and advocacy for people with mental health care needs that can be applied across all contexts of nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate common mental health disorders and the signs, symptoms, and impact these can have on an individuals' daily functioning.
Demonstrate safe quality use of medicines using the National Safety and Quality Service (NSHQS) Medication Safety Standard
Evaluate effective communication techniques to develop therapeutic relationships with people in your nursing practice.

Utilise appropriate health assessment frameworks, clinical reasoning and evidenced based practice to assess, plan and implement person-centred culturally safe nursing interventions for individuals with mental health needs.
Synthesise and apply knowledge of foundational concepts in mental health and psychopharmacology.
Identify learning needs in respect of professional practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE PLACEMENT (PEP) 3
syllabus_overview: Professional Experience Placement (PEP) 3 focuses on providing comprehensive care responsive to the needs of individuals experiencing acute and chronic disease and illness across the lifespan within varied healthcare contexts. Through immersive and supervised placements within various healthcare contexts, you will have the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge and skills gained from Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 3 to real-world healthcare settings. During PEP 3, you will observe, plan, implement and evaluate nursing interventions for patients requiring comprehensive care, under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals. Through this experience, you will gain insights into intraprofessional and interprofessional collaboration and the role of registered nurses in comprehensive patient care. Through reflective exercises, case discussions, and debriefing sessions, you will be supported to process your experiences, identify areas for growth, and connect your practical encounters with relevant theoretical concepts.
learning_outcomes: Address identified learning needs through reflection and continuing professional development (CPD).
Utilise the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice in the application of theoretical knowledge and evidence-based nursing care, within scope of practice.
Employ intraprofessional and interprofessional practice skills to collaborate effectively with patients, families, peers, and colleagues.
Provide person-centred, culturally safe nursing care to patients across the lifespan and with differing abilities.
Develop practice readiness within real-world healthcare contexts.

title: CONTEMPORARY STUDIES 3:PRACTICE IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
syllabus_overview: This subject is aimed at developing your knowledge, skills, and competencies for quality improvement to enhance patient care outcomes.
