During the subject you will actively engage in developing, executing, leading and evaluating a quality improvement project to drive positive, sustainable change in healthcare delivery. At completion of the subject, you will have the opportunity to showcase your project and share your experiences with your peers in an intraprofessional, collaborative learning environment.
learning_outcomes: Utilise leadership capabilities and research to inform and promote contemporary, sustainable practice improvement and patient outcomes.
Execute, lead and evaluate practice improvement projects and outcomes.
Effectively communicate practice improvement projects and outcomes.
Undertake a needs analysis and design evidence-based interventions to address practice improvement for better patient outcomes.
Evaluate the fundamental principles and methodologies of quality improvement in healthcare.

title: PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE PLACEMENT (PEP) 4
syllabus_overview: Professional Experience Placement (PEP) 4 focuses on the application of the principles of mental health, wellbeing, and illness to care of patients across the lifespan within varied healthcare contexts. Through immersive and supervised placements, you will have the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge and skills gained from Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 4 to real-world healthcare settings. During PEP 4 you will observe and implement nursing interventions to patients requiring mental health care, under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals. Through this experience, you will gain insights into intraprofessional and interprofessional collaboration and the role of registered nurses in mental health and recovery across the lifespan. Through reflective exercises, case discussions, and debriefing sessions, you will be supported to process your experiences, identify areas for growth, and connect your practical encounters with relevant theoretical concepts.
learning_outcomes: Utilise the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice in the application of theoretical knowledge and evidence-based nursing care, within scope of practice.
Address identified learning needs through reflection and continuing professional development (CPD).
Develop practice readiness and mental health skills within real-world healthcare contexts.
Employ intraprofessional and interprofessional practice skills to collaborate effectively with patients, families, peers, and colleagues.
Provide person-centred, culturally safe nursing care to patients across the lifespan with mental health needs.

title: PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE PLACEMENT (PEP) 5
syllabus_overview: Professional Experience Placement (PEP) 5 focuses on practice readiness and the transition from student to graduate nurse. Through immersive and supervised placements within various healthcare contexts, you will have the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge gained from Preparation for Nursing Practice (PNP) 5 to real-world healthcare settings. During PEP 5 you will observe and provide person-centred, culturally safe care under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals while gaining insights into the responsibilities and challenges faced by graduate nurses. Through reflective exercises, case discussions, and debriefing sessions, you will be supported to process your experiences, identify areas for growth, connect your practical encounters with relevant theoretical concepts, and reflect on your readiness to transition into graduate practice.
learning_outcomes: Develop practice readiness within real-world healthcare contexts.
Employ intraprofessional and interprofessional practice skills to collaborate effectively with patients, families, peers, and colleagues.
Address identified learning needs through reflection and continuing professional development (CPD).
Provide person centred, culturally safe nursing care to patients across the lifespan and with differing abilities.
Utilise the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice in the application of theoretical knowledge and evidence-based nursing care, within scope of practice.

title: PREPARATION FOR NURSING PRACTICE (PNP) 5
syllabus_overview: This subject is aims to develop your readiness for practice and facilitate a seamless transition from your role of student to registered nurse within your chosen context of practice. The subject is designed as a capstone subject to consolidate and apply your learning from across the course, with an emphasis on the unique needs of graduate registered nurses. As you progress through the subject, you will have the opportunity to develop your capabilities in preparation for your registered nurse role and to excel in practice during your first year as a registered nurse.
learning_outcomes: Identify learning needs in respect of professional practice.
Utilise appropriate health assessment frameworks, clinical reasoning and evidenced based practice to assess, plan and implement person-centred, culturally safe nursing care across the lifespan.
Critically evaluate transition to practice and career pathways for registered nurses
Analyse and apply the NMBA Registered nurse standards for practice within different contexts of practice.
Appraise strategies to develop clinical, professional, personal, and industry readiness and support transition to practice.
Demonstrate safe quality use of medicines using the National Safety and Quality Health Standard (NSQHS) Medication Safety.

title: HEALTHCARE AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: This subject will explore the Australian health care system, the collaborative nature of health care, and how consumers and professionals interact with health care at various levels. In this subject you will develop the foundation knowledge for working with individuals in health and human services settings in Australia and how different environments can influence consumer access to health care. You will explore health standards that influence healthcare including NSQHSS, Aged Care Quality Standards, NDIS, My Health Record, Aging in Place. In this subject you will explore the social model of disability in society and how the characteristics and actions of individuals impact on health outcomes. You will investigate how individuals present and progress through health settings including primary, secondary and tertiary heath. You will explore global health and wellbeing trends and investigate the healthcare continuum and the quality and safety framework.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles of patient and personal safety and their relevance to health professional practice
Appraise contemporary developments in global, national, and regional health and wellbeing including the role of nurses and collaborative practice
Explore how health standards influence care quality and patient outcomes including NSQHS and Aged Care Quality Standards
Illustrate the ways in which consumers interact with the health care system to meet individual needs
Examine how individual and social factors shape and determine people's experience of health, illness and disability in different parts of the world

title: FIRST NATIONS HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will begin to develop the knowledge and skills required to work effectively and safely with Australian First Nations peoples in the healthcare environment. You will explore key features and concepts related to traditional and contemporary First Nations cultures and communities; multi- dimensional models of First Nations health and healing; and the underlying social determinants influencing current health outcomes, including historical and cultural factors. You will also explore concepts related to health inequality, reflect on the responsibility of the whole health system in improving First Nations health outcomes, and consider how culturally safe nursing and midwifery practice can contribute to closing the gap in Indigenous health disadvantage. The concepts of honouring First Nations knowledge, strength-based approaches, and evidenced-based learning are strongly reinforced throughout the subject.
learning_outcomes: Identify the factors that contribute to health inequality, and ways of achieving equity in health outcomes between First Nations and non-First Nations Australians
Examine how cultural safety influences effective nursing practices, and health service delivery
Recognise the diversity of First Nations cultures and history, and identify First Nations perspectives of health and healing
Analyse how First Nations concepts of interconnected physical, social, historical, political and cultural factors impact on health outcomes

Collaboratively demonstrate culturally safe communication that facilitates respectful therapeutic relationships, and supports effective partnerships with First Nations peoples, professionals, organisations and communities

title: COMMUNICATION AND THERAPEUTIC ENGAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable you to develop an understanding of the skills required to be a professional communicator. Therapeutic engagement is achieved through professional communication approaches which is a skill that needs to be developed throughout your professional career. The purpose of being a skilled communicator is to help you understand someone else’s viewpoint and reasons for behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate how communication and therapeutic engagement are foundational to professional practice.
Demonstrate effective oral and written communication techniques required as a professional
Develop an understanding of empathy and its role in therapeutic engagement.
Recognise the importance of self-awareness and the use of self in the communication process.

title: PROFESSIONAL STUDIES IN NURSING
syllabus_overview: This subject is an introduction to the use of research in the degree. This subject will also introduce students to the use of research-based evidence in nursing practice. You will learn how an evidence-based approach in health informs clinical practice. This subject supports the development of foundation academic skills and information literacy required for university study.
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of evidence based practice in nursing and midwifery practice
Apply a scholarly approach to your practice
Identify appropriate sources of information to inform evidence based practice in nursing and midwifery
Review critical components of health research evidence
Explain relevant ethical and legal principles as they apply to nursing and midwifery practice

title: INFANT AND CHILD HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop clinical knowledge of infants and children (0-6 years) to plan and implement safe and effective nursing care. This includes physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development, as well as factors that can impact their health and well-being, such as genetics, nutrition, environmental exposures, and social determinants of health. You will build on nursing skills and knowledge to develop advanced critical thinking and problem-solving skills and personal learning goals. The subject is delivered via an online mode which may include online lectures and online learning modules.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate human growth and development and common developmental issues.
Engage in critical reflection to develop your child health nursing practice.
Apply the principles of child and family centred care to the assessment and care of the child with complex care needs and their family, across a range of care settings.
Examine common acute and chronic childhood conditions, considering the impacts for the child and their family.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING ONE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will work in collaborative teams, to develop your understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams including the student nurse’s scope of practice. This subject will enable you to explore your own profession, as well as other health and human service providers. You will come to understand the therapeutic use of nursing in various health care scenarios from a quality and patient safety and legal and ethical perspective. You will be introduced to the concept of evidenced based practice. The subject will explore the evolution of nursing and nursing theory across the ages and its representation in current society. You will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. This will require comprehension and demonstration of obtaining specific physiological, psychological, cultural, and social information about people, planning, and implementing basic patient care and effective therapeutic communication techniques with patients to maintain patient safety. This subject will explore care needs across the lifespan from birth to death, including the care of patients with all abilities. You will be introduced to the application of clinical reasoning, clinical decision making and reflective practice. Contemporary nursing theory that underpins practice will be discussed. You will investigate the requirement for comprehensive care to meet individual needs including falls, pressure injuries and nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate health assessment frameworks to ensure person-centred care across the lifespan
Describe the roles and responsibilities of nurses as members of an intra and interprofessional team
Explain the concept of reflection on practice to professional and individual development
Employ evidenced practice in clinical psychomotor skills to provide focused foundational nursing care
Apply clinical reasoning and decision making process to patients across the life span
Use effective written and verbal communication strategies to build therapeutic relationships to facilitate effective communication with patients and other health professionals
Examine the importance of quality and patient safety strategies in the provision of safe patient care

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING TWO
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of person-centred care for people experiencing simple common acute illness requiring hospitalisation. You will examine communication and other strategies to facilitate safe interactions in the healthcare context. The importance of partnering with consumers and involving patient in their care planning will be explored. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. Included care of patients with all abilities. You will be introduced to the theoretical basis of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and to the role of controlling the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration related to oral and topical. Through application of aseptic and infection control principles discuss ways to control healthcare associated infection. The three-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory. In this placement you will undertake health assessments with assigned patients and use the data obtained to develop person-centred plans of care considering principles of personal and patient safety and interprofessional practice in a variety of settings. This subject will also introduce students to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Apply principles of Aspect Non-Touch Technique to prevent and control healthcare associated infection
Identify the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice
Use appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Demonstrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings
Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings
Employ a range of communication and other strategies to facilitate safe and effective clinical and professional care interactions with people and health professionals

title: MENTAL HEALTHCARE IN NURSING
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses nursing skills, knowledge and attitudes and person-centred care on mental health and illness. In this subject you will explore the recovery-orientated framework for delivery of mental health services. You will investigate the lived-experience and common challenges experienced by individuals with mental health and substance abuse issues. In this subject you will explore ways to enable people and families to maximise self-determination, personal responsibility and self-management of mental health and wellbeing. The importance of working collaboratively with people and their family will be emphasised.
learning_outcomes: Identify the role of biological, psychological and social factors relevant to mental health, illness and recovery across the lifespan
Illustrate the application of Mental Health and Wellbeing Act 2022 in delivery of mental health services
Examine the use of psychotropic medications in the treatment for individuals experiencing mental health disorders
Analyse the role of recovery-oriented principles to enhance and improve comprehensive mental health nursing practice
Demonstrate systematic, foundational mental health assessment skills to identify consumer needs

title: PRIMARY HEALTHCARE IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you an introduction to primary health care. This subject will explore the role of the nurse in health promotion as a member of the primary healthcare team and look at models that support safe patient care. You will explore the evolution and role of digital health and education in primary health. You will analyse the role of the nurse in coordination of care and patient health education to prevent disease and manage illness. Contemporary developments and future challenges including priority populations health, communicable diseases and climate change will be examined. Using the concept of health priorities to inform health promotion activities.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of primary health care principles on health outcomes locally, nationally, and internationally
Analyse how health literacy and health seeking behaviors influence health outcomes in various health populations and regions.
Critically examine how primary health care philosophies, frameworks and principles are applied in contemporary primary care nursing practice, including health promotion knowledge and skills

Critically examine the contemporary evolution of primary health in Australia and globally with a focus on climate change and health, priority populations, communicable disease and social and environmental determinants.
Demonstrate skills in applying health coaching models and principles of health education to work with individuals, groups, and populations to promote health and prevent disease.

title: PHYSICAL HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the interrelationship between physical health and mental health for health care consumers. The impact of psychotropics and managing side effect profile as well as considerations of previous trauma and it’s impact on a person’s health will be central ideas presented. Strategies to assess and plan interventions for common comorbidities will be identified. Students will be interested in the scope of this subject and it’s application to a variety of clinical situations in health care.
learning_outcomes: Create strategies to integrate mental health and physical health support for a person.
Examine the impact of psychotropic medication in physical health.
Recognise the complex relationship between physical and mental health.
Demonstrate trauma informed care in relation to a person’s physical and mental health.
Assess factors that influence comorbidities that influence healthcare outcomes.

title: FAMILY HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop clinical knowledge of family centred care to plan and implement safe and effective nursing care. You will learn about applying a gender lens to address health inequities in women’s, men’s, and gender diverse health. This will include sexual and reproductive health, preventive care, healthy ageing, chronic disease management, substance abuse, mental health and wellbeing, and family violence. You will build on nursing skills and knowledge to develop advanced critical thinking and problem-solving skills and personal learning goals. The subject is delivered via an online mode which may include online lectures and online learning modules.
learning_outcomes: Apply evidence-based information on reproductive and sexual health topics.
Critically reflect on the impact of the social determinants of health such as poverty, housing and education which can impact the health and wellbeing of families.
Analyse normal and abnormal physiologic changes through the life cycle.
Engage in critical reflection to develop your family health nursing practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING THREE
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning and provision of patient-centred care for persons experiencing an illness requiring hospitalisation in acute or subacute settings or management through primary care. You will explore patients with healthcare concerns across the lifespan and end of life care. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will extend your theoretical understanding of pharmacology and the responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in injectable medication administration. This subject will develop knowledge regarding diagnostic testing (haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, medical imaging). Included care of patients with all abilities. The four-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients with acute and or chronic illness that is underpinned by nursing theory. During the placement you will develop your medication administration and refine your patient health assessment using systematic frameworks and use data obtained to develop person-centred plans of care. You will develop your clinical skills in implementing and evaluating patient care in secondary, primary and /or mental health care settings. This subject will refine patient and team-based communication skills and other approaches to support patient safety.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings as a member of the health care team
Employ appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers, anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Employ evidence-based practice in implementation of clinical nursing care for patients at end-of-life or experiencing acute or chronic health conditions across various health settings
Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Demonstrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate safe person-centred care for people across the lifespan that is evidenced based and culturally relevant
Apply knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing to individuals at end-of-life or experiencing acute or chronic diseases

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING FOUR
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation person-centred care for people requiring hospitalisation in acute or subacute settings experiencing acute deterioration. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will investigate patients with healthcare concerns across the lifespan experiencing gastrointestinal, reproductive, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and immune disorders. You will extend your theoretical understanding of pharmacology and the responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration in urgent care situations. Included care of patients with all abilities. This subject will develop knowledge regarding diagnostic testing (haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, medical imaging) in gastrointestinal, reproductive, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and immune disorders and in to investigate patient deterioration. The four-week clinical placement will enable you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients and recognise, report, and respond to patient experiencing acute deterioration in acute, subacute, primary care and/or mental health settings. This subject will develop your medication administration, refine your patient health assessment skills and enhance patient and team-based communication skills in critical situations. In this placement you will use data obtained to develop, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred plans of care for patient experiencing acute deterioration as part of a healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Apply safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication strategies in various health settings as a member of the healthcare team
Devise strategies to incorporate reflection into professional nursing practice
Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred care for people experiencing deterioration that is culturally relevant and age specific
Using knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing, identify deterioration in individuals experiencing acute or chronic disorders
Develop an awareness of and contribute to the risk management strategies of a healthcare agency, to implement incident reporting procedures and apply risk management procedures
Demonstrate and evaluate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration of simple and complex medications in a range of settings and situations

Use appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to detect and recognise patient deterioration considering individual, anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors across the lifespan

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE PATHWAY TRANSITION
syllabus_overview: This is a transition pathway to the Bachelor of Nursing, enabling students an accelerated degree, specifically for students who have an undergraduate degree other than Nursing or have entered through a health sciences diploma pathway. In this subject, students will explore health standards that influence healthcare including National Safety and Quality Standards (NSQHS), Aged Care Quality Standards, National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), My Health Record, and Aging in Place. Students will develop a deep understanding of the therapeutic use of nursing in various health care scenarios from a quality and patient safety, legal and ethical perspective. Students will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. Students will explore the evolution of nursing and nursing theory across the ages and its representation in current society. They will also be introduced to occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery, including care of all patients and abilities. An introduction to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice will also be examined. This subject will introduce students to the application of clinical reasoning and decision making required by registered nurses in the delivering person-centred, evidence-based care for people experiencing hospitalisation with a focus on a variety of systems and diseases, across the lifespan. They will learn to work in inter- and intra-professional teams to develop their understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams, including the student nurse’s scope of practice. Students will be introduced to pharmacotherapies and safe and quality use in medicines. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the student and registered nurse in medication administration will be examined. Through application of aseptic and infection control principles students will examine different ways to control healthcare associated infection. The three-week clinical placement will allow students to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory.
learning_outcomes: Explore how health standards influence care quality and patient outcomes including NSQHS and Aged Care Quality Standards
Apply knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology to individuals with a range of health conditions, across the lifespan
Apply principles of aseptic non touch technique to prevent and control healthcare associated infection
Apply appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural and psychosocial factors
Demonstrate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base in various health settings
Apply clinical reasoning to deliver person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Apply the principles of reflective practice to develop your professional nursing practice
Illustrate safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation and administration in a range of settings
Employ a range of communication and other strategies to facilitate safe and effective clinical and professional care interactions with people and health professionals
Examine the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice

title: NURSING PATIENTS WITH ACUTE ILLNESS B
syllabus_overview: This subject will build upon your current skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses for the provision of patient-centred care for persons experiencing a complex acute illness requiring hospitalisation. You will examine nursing care that is required for hospitalised patients experiencing renal, musculoskeletal, cancer and haematological disorders. This subject will offer an array of teaching modalities including lectures, online activities, workshops, laboratories and simulations. These have been designed to enable you to continue to develop and consolidate your critical thinking and complex nursing care alongside the development and refinement of your technical nursing skills. To achieve the learning objectives of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written and clinical assessments. A clinical placement is embedded within this subject to develop your learning and consolidation. By the end of this subject you will be prepared for third year of your nursing studies.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine the impact of hospitalisation for individuals and their families experiencing acute or chronic illnesses.
Evaluate person-centred care, using the Clinical Reasoning Cycle to individuals experiencing haematological, renal, gastrointestinal and musculoskeletal disorders.

Apply the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Board [ANMB] Standards of Practice for a Registered Nurse when caring for individuals and their families, with a focus on persons experiencing cancer, haematological, renal, gastrointestinal and musculoskeletal disorders.
Apply psychomotor and non-technical skills to individuals experiencing haematological, renal, gastrointestinal and musculoskeletal disorders.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE NURSE TRANSITION
syllabus_overview: In 2026 only, and as an interim measure stemming from contractual arrangements with PSB Academy, the delivery of this subject will differ slightly between the Victorian and Singapore instances. The differences are specified within the 2026 subject details. Students located at LTU Australia This is a transition subject to the Bachelor of Nursing as part of the accelerated degree. This subject is specifically for students who have a nursing qualification, either as an enrolled Nurse or a Registered Nurse outside Australia. In this subject, students will work in collaborative teams to develop their understanding of the foundation concepts that underpin effective nursing practice in interprofessional teams. There will be a strong focus on the transition from the role of the enrolled nurse to registered nurse. An introduction to ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice will also be explored. Students will be introduced to the concept of evidenced based practice and the use of research in the degree. Foundational academic skills and information literacy required for successful university study will be prioritised and developed. In addition, students will learn the skills, knowledge and attitudes required by Registered Nurses in the comprehensive assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of person-centred, evidence-based care. A lifelong approach to nursing care will be addressed. Students will also have opportunity to revise the theoretical basis of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and to the role of controlling the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Responsibilities, practical skills, and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration will be examined and practised. The three-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients that is underpinned by nursing theory. Students located at PSB Singapore This is a transition subject to the Bachelor of Nursing and designed for students who have a nursing qualification as a Registered Nurse in Singapore. There will be a strong focus on the transition from the diploma qualification to a Bachelor degree. Building on previous knowledge, this subject emphasises the academic skills and information literacy required to find evidence-based information which enables students to use evidence in their assessments and day to day nursing practice. In addition, students will learn the knowledge and skills required by degree qualified Registered Nurses in the comprehensive assessment, recognition of patient deterioration, planning, implementation, and evaluation of person-centred, evidence-based care. This subject also introduces clinical reasoning cycle and reflective practice, which will prepare students to assess clinical situations and facilitate appropriate and timely clinical decision making. Using simulation-based learning, students will be provided an opportunity to practice and demonstrate comprehensive focused health assessments. This subject aims to support students in transitioning from diploma to degree-level nursing practice by developing academic skills, information literacy, and the ability to integrate evidence-based knowledge into clinical decision-making. Also, this subject aims to enhance students’ capability to undertake comprehensive and person-centred care through the development of clinical reasoning, reflective practice, and advanced health assessment skills using simulation-based learning.
learning_outcomes: Singapore students: Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
Singapore students: Demonstrate suitable database searches in relation to nursing practice.

Singapore students: Practice appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit subjective and objective health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors.
Singapore students: Incorporate principles of evidence-based research and literacy skills in academic writing.
Singapore students: Apply the principles of reflective practice to further develop professional nursing practice.
Singapore students: Critically examine the roles and responsibilities of a registered nurse as members of an intra and interprofessional team.
LTU students: Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate person-centred care that is culturally relevant, and evidence based for persons across the lifespan
LTU students: Critically examine the roles and responsibilities of a registered nurse as members of an intra and interprofessional team
LTU students: Demonstrate suitable database searches in relation to nursing practice
LTU students: Examine the relevant ethics and law as it relates to nursing practice
LTU students: Demonstrate and practice safe use of medicines relating to storage, preparation, and administration in a range of settings
Singapore students: Demonstrate safe nursing practice within scope of practice that is professional, accountable, ethical, and legal underpinned by evidence-based knowledge.
LTU students: Apply the principles of reflective practice to further develop your professional nursing practice
LTU students: Incorporate principles of evidence-based research and literacy skills in academic writing
LTU students: Demonstrate safe nursing practice within scope of practice that is professional, accountable, ethical, and legal underpinned by evidence-based knowledge

LTU students: Practice appropriate health assessment techniques that are systematic and person-centred to elicit important health data that considers anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors

title: EDUCATION IN HEALTH PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore principles and practices of education in healthcare settings. You will examine foundations of learning and teaching and use these to meet learning requirements of patients and families across the lifespan, as well as those of peers and colleagues. You will explore the role of education in patient management and health outcomes. The subject examines the influence of education and professional development on patient safety. Skills and knowledge will be developed in planning, facilitating and evaluating an effective education session for patients, families, colleagues or peers.
learning_outcomes: Employ appropriate evaluation approaches in teaching and learning to support continuous program improvement
Apply key theories and approaches to learning and teaching to support education in health care .
Develop effective evidence -based teaching sessions that meet the needs of individuals, peers, families, carers or colleagues.

title: HEALTHCARE ETHICS AND LAW
syllabus_overview: Nursing practice is informed by, and framed within, the principles of law and ethics. This subject begins with an introduction to ethics, including an overview of the ethical theories and principles used in health care. Students are then introduced to the law and to the notion of legal systems while reviewing the sources of law and examining the difference between criminal and civil law. Concepts including 'duty of care' negligence, end of life issues, whistleblowing, resource allocation, and conscientious objection will also be explored as students examine the legal, ethical and professional responsibilities of nursing and accountability in nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply common ethical theories and principles.
Critically examine contemporary legal and ethical issues within nursing practice.
Explain the ethical and legal nature of nursing practice.
Critically reflect upon individual values and how these may influence a nurse's practice.

title: FAMILY VIOLENCE BEST PRACTICE RESPONSE FOR HEALTH CARE PROFESSIONALS
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to the societal, professional and health issues associated with the different forms of family violence. In this subject you will explore the policy and programmatic context surrounding this problem, the current government's MARAM(Multi Agency Risk Assessment and Management) approach, you will be supported to identify and develop skills in best practice responses, and strategies for care of self and colleagues. The subject will identify the roles and responsibilities of the systems that assist health care providers in the diverse context of Australian society.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles and skills required for best practice in family violence responses for the varied roles and responsibilities of health care professionals
Identify definitions, prevalence, drivers, myths and misconceptions and the health effects of family violence
Utilise resources available to support the physical and emotional health and safety of self and colleagues
Explain how the health care system fits in the broader context of family violence responses including legal system, justice system, police and other services

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the knowledge and skills necessary for you to engage in evidence based practice as a nurse and/or midwife. Through lectures, pre-recorded lectures and online activities, and workshops you will start to think about the origins of varied clinical practices. You will learn to formulate research questions regarding practice that could enhance service, clinician and client outcomes. You will develop skills to conduct literature reviews to support evidence based practice and learn how to critique the evidence found, and explore the ethics of nursing and midwifery research.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate suitable database searches in relation to nursing and midwifery practice
Analyse the ethical issues inherent in nursing and midwifery research
Identify research paradigms, designs, and steps in the research process
Describe the role of evidence-based practice within nursing and midwifery practice
Synthesise and discuss research evidence on a chosen topic considering quality of the research

title: NURSING: HEALTH PRIORITIES A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you have the opportunity to extend your knowledge and skills in relation to: the aetiology and pathophysiology of inflammation, acute pain and the cardiovascular, respiratory and endocrine systems across the lifespan and; diagnostic testing (haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, medical imaging) and pharmacology related to inflammation, acute pain and three of the National Health Priority Areas (cardiovascular, respiratory and endocrine) across the lifespan. You will be introduced to the theoretical basis of pharmacology including: pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and to the responsibilities, practical skills and scope of practice of the registered nurse in medication administration.
learning_outcomes: Apply safe and therapeutic practice when administering medications.
Apply principles of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing to individuals experiencing cardiovascular, respiratory and endocrine diseases.
Apply principles of pharmacology to individuals experiencing acute pain, cardiovascular, respiratory and endocrine diseases.
Plan appropriate investigations and pharmacological interventions through the application of clinical reasoning and knowledge of the disease processes.

title: PRIMARY HEALTHCARE NURSING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will consider the diversity of contemporary nursing roles and practice through the exploration of comprehensive primary health care. This approach involves health promotion, community development and person centred care. Through workshops, online modules and a clinical practicum you will have opportunities to integrate and apply biomedical, behavioural and social approaches in the provision of person-centred care for individuals and communities. The primary healthcare principles will be emphasised, you will explore the complexities of health policy and systems and consideration will be given to how personal values impact on health practice and mobilisation of community resources. Students will consider the ways in which nurses can act as global citizens in their contribution to sustainable health care systems through innovative evidence based healthcare. To achieve the learning outcomes of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written assessments within the teaching period.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of social and environmental determinants of health and illness
Apply primary health care principles in contemporary nursing practice, including health promotion knowledge and skills
Appraise the impact primary health care principles have on health outcomes locally, nationally, and internationally
Utilise health coaching techniques to work with individuals, groups, and populations to promote health
Differentiate between the terms primary care and primary health care, selective and comprehensive Primary Health Care.

title: LEADERSHIP AND CLINICAL GOVERNANCE IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will extend your knowledge of the components that provide frameworks for accountable and responsible nursing practice. You will explore competency standards, decision making frameworks, direction and delegation guidelines and the Australian safety and quality framework in relation to professional conduct. You will be introduced to the role of contemporary theories of leadership and management, the concept of professional boundaries, health policy, organisational structures, and culture. You will explore the application of digital health in healthcare. Your capacity to engage in your professional role across all practice settings will be enhanced by completion of this subject.
learning_outcomes: Critique contemporary leadership theories, and their importance to individuals, health teams and the nursing and midwifery profession
Critically review the impact of corporate and clinical governance models in health services in relation to person-centred care
Appraise contemporary health policy issues and current legislation as they relate to safety and quality in nursing and midwifery and application of digital health
Critique how organisational structure, organisational culture and contextual variables influence the nursing and midwifery environment and the coordinated approach to person centred care

title: TRANSITION TO BACHELOR OF NURSING
syllabus_overview: This subject is a transition pathway to the Bachelor of Nursing course. This subject is delivered in a number of modules using lectures, online activities, workshops and clinical laboratories. Students will further develop foundational nursing knowledge and practical skills and be able to apply human anatomy and physiology required for person-centred care. Additionally, the subject develops academic skills and investigates the clinical reasoning process, enquiry-based learning, working in teams and evidence-based practice and it role in professional nursing practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competence in nursing care skills.
Outline principles of law and ethics for professional nursing practice
Demonstrate academic study and writing skills for transition to university studies
Explain the clinical reasoning cycle and its use in planning nursing care across the lifespan and in different contexts
Critically examine topics using evidence-based scholarly practice and academic resources to develop plans for enquiry for team and independent learning
Demonstrate understanding of human anatomy and physiology applied to nursing
Use a health assessment framework and techniques to assess an individuals essential care needs.

title: PREPARING FOR PRACTICE IN MENTAL HEALTH AND ADDICTIONS
syllabus_overview: This subject will assist you with preparing for a nursing graduate year in mental health or addictions nursing. The subject will have a focus on contemporary practice with consumers who present with dual diagnosis care needs. You will explore ways to develop skills to assess and intervene using best evidence for practice. Your role as a novice health practitioner in nursing will be considered along with the types of strategies and supports you will need to be successful in your future career.
learning_outcomes: Identify effective skill development for career advancement in mental health practice.
Create strategies that nurture and extend the novice clinician to plan for mental health specialist practice in nursing.
Analyse contemporary nursing practice in mental health and addiction services.
Identify and apply strategies to engage with clinical supervision and reflective practice for clinical skill development.
Evaluate evidence based interventions for effective consumer out comes in mental health and addictions.

title: COMMUNITY HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop your existing public health knowledge and skills. You will explore the links between economic inequality and health and the promotion of optimal development of young children through social justice strategies. You will develop insight into culturally appropriate practice, applying this knowledge when working with families from diverse cultural backgrounds. The subject is delivered via a flexible online mode which may include on-campus or online workshops and online learning modules.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the additional challenges faced by families, including family violence, poverty, insecure housing, rurality, mental health issues, and Culturally and Linguistically Diverse families, including First Nations people.
Engage in critical reflection to develop your public health and health promotion nursing practice.
Critically analyse the application of Primary Health Care principles in community maternal and child health care practice.
Identify and examine models of primary and community nursing practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING SIX
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will refine your abilities to: manage care for several complex patients; reflect on your personal practice; plan, implement and evaluate prioritised evidence-based person-centred care for multiple individuals. The subject content builds on previously learnt concepts of person-centred care and assessment, situational management, nursing inquiry, therapeutic and professional communication and client education that are applied across the lifespan. The focus of the subject is to assist you to develop the repertoire of skills required in contemporary nursing practice to care for patients with all abilities across the lifespan. Evidenced Based Practice will be further developed. Further nursing theories will be explored. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery and self care. The six-week clinical placement will allow you to consolidate your professional nursing practice in readiness to transition to the workforce. You will manage person-centred health requirements in acute, subacute, primary care, mental health, aged care, or paediatrics. The clinical practicum will allow you to integrate learnt theoretical principles to the nursing practice of patients and plan, implement and evaluate care across the lifespan. In this placement you will advance your skills and knowledge in medication management, refined health assessment and working as a member of the healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Develop safe and efficient nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical, legal and underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication
Apply sound clinical reasoning and evidence-based person-centred care to plan, implement and evaluate care that is prioritised and culturally relevant for patients across the lifespan
Critically review knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing and apply to individuals experiencing acute or chronic comorbid disorders across the lifespan
Exhibit safe use of medicines for multiple patients in a range of settings and situations
Critically evaluate your own professional nursing practice against the Standards for Practice and Quality and Safety frameworks

Apply appropriate health assessment techniques that are practised, systematic and person-centred across the lifespan considering individual, anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors to recognise and respond to clinical change

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN NURSING FIVE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will advance your abilities to develop, implement, evaluate, and manage evidence-based person-centred care for several patients with comorbidities across the lifespan. Nursing theory and evidence based practice will be further studied. You will also be encouraged to further explore occupational health and safety as it relates to healthcare delivery. You will compare the influence of lifespan and polypharmacy on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. The subject will explore aging and sustainable access and delivery of health services to people living with acute and/or chronic illness across the lifespan including public health strategies and models of chronic illness management. You will look at ways to promote active engagement with health services among people across the lifespan and recommend ways to improve the sustainability of health services for people. Included will be the promotion of health and care of individuals with all abilities. The four-week clinical placement will allow you to integrate theoretical knowledge, skills, and attitudes into your nursing practice in acute, subacute, primary care, mental health, aged care, or paediatrics for a group of patients. The clinical practicum will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of multiple patients and plan, implement and evaluate care across the lifespan. In this placement you will be advance your medication management and consolidate your patient health assessment and skills in using data to develop person-centred plans of care across the lifespan for patient with comorbidities as part of a healthcare team.
learning_outcomes: Critique in self and others, strategies to incorporate reflection into professional nursing practice
Justify safe use of medicines in a range of settings and situations including polypharmacy

Use appropriate health assessment frameworks and techniques for patients across the lifespan with comorbidities that are systematic and person-centred considering, anatomical, physiological, cultural, and psychosocial factors to recognise and respond to clinical change
Interpret knowledge of pathophysiology and diagnostic testing and apply to individuals experiencing acute or chronic comorbid disorders

Evaluate safe nursing practice that is professional, accountable, ethical and legal underpinned by a sound knowledge base and effective communication in various health settings as a member of the healthcare team

Employ clinical reasoning to plan, implement and evaluate evidence-based person-centred care for people with acute, chronic and comorbid disease that is prioritised and culturally relevant across the lifespan

title: APPLIED EVIDENCED BASED CARE IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be given an opportunity to further explore the importance of evidenced based care in health care and you will be encouraged to generate ways of thinking and critique wider health practice to form the foundation for future health practice evolutions. You will look at ways to use health care data in a systematic way and use quality improvement tools and techniques. It will consolidate knowledge on the disease process, public health approaches and understanding of interdisciplinary practice environments in the acute, sub-acute, mental health, paediatric, aged care residential and community settings.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and recommend practice improvement opportunities based on contemporary research
Conduct a critical review of the literature relevant to your chosen practice improvement topic
Elicit strategies for individuals and groups to communicate results to a range of audiences for different purposes using a variety of modes
Identify the components of a health research project using the principles of quality improvement in healthcare

title: INTERNATIONAL AND CLINICAL ELECTIVE FOR NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable nursing and midwifery students to undertake nursing and/or midwifery learning experience in Australia or overseas, in their own field of practice, in diverse clinical contexts. Students will participate in a clinical or other international learning experience including virtual mobility programs and internationalisation at home programs that will allow them to gain experience and knowledge of nursing and/or midwifery in a culturally and professionally new environment. Students undertaking the virtual mobility option are required to complete an approved combination of internationalisation at home programs. This subject is also available for International nursing and midwifery students undertaking a clinical or international learning experience in Australia. Students are required to either attend a face-to-face overseas clinical experience or participate in a virtual program.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate organisation, time management skills and a professional attitude/orientation at all times.
Critically reflect on the impact of this context and cultural experience on your developing professional identity.
Demonstrate safe and effective communication skills in a culturally and linguistically new environment with a range of audiences.
Identify the practice of your profession in a range of contexts and apply the policy, procedures and guidelines of that service within the context of the experience.
Evaluate the service delivery model with the Australian service delivery model in your field of practice taking into account cultural differences.

title: ENGAGEMENT IN PROFESSIONAL NURSING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will extend your knowledge of the components that provide frameworks for accountable and responsible nursing practice. Through online activities students will explore competency standards, decision making frameworks, direction and delegation guidelines and the Australian safety and quality framework in relation to professional conduct. In addition, students will be introduced to the role of contemporary theories of leadership and management, the concept of professional boundaries, health policy, organisational structures and culture. Your capacity to engage in your professional role across all practice settings will be enhanced by completion of this subject. To achieve the learning outcomes of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written assessments within a 12-week period.
learning_outcomes: Apply awareness of the transition from student to registered health care practitioner through critical self-reflection.
Explain the impact of corporate and clinical governance models in Australia and international health services in relation to person-centred care.
Appraise contemporary health policy issues and current legislation as they relate to safety and quality in nursing.
Critique contemporary nursing leadership theories, core competencies and personal capabilities and their importance to individuals, teams and the nursing profession.
Develop and apply communication skills that directly relate to health information systems.
Critique how organisational structure, organisational culture and contextual variables influence the nursing environment and the coordinated approach to person centred care.

title: NURSING: MENTAL HEALTH AND ILLNESS
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates nursing skills and person-centred care with a focus on mental health and illness. Through lectures, online activities, workshops, clinical skills laboratories and a clinical placement you will explore common challenges experienced by individuals with mental health and substance abuse issues. The clinical practicum will allow you to integrate theoretical principles to the nursing practice of individuals with mental health issues. To achieve the learning outcomes of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written, verbal and clinical assessments within a 12-week period.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate foundational mental health assessment skills.
Examine the application of Mental Health and Wellbeing Act 2022 in delivery of mental health services.
Employ recovery-oriented principles to nursing practice.
Explain the role of biological, psychological and social factors relevant to mental health, illness and recovery.
Administer medications to individuals experiencing mental health disorders using safe and therapeutic practices.

title: NURSING PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC ILLNESS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be given an opportunity to generate ways of thinking that enable sustainable access and delivery of health services to people living with chronic illness. Through the readings, online learning activities, workshops and assessments, you will be consolidating the fundamental knowledge you have gained from previous semesters to be able to select appropriate public health strategies and models of chronic illness management, promote active engagement with health services among people living with chronic illness and recommend ways to improve the sustainability of health services for people living with chronic illness. As such, it is essential to have knowledge on the disease process of chronic illnesses, familiarity with public health approaches and understanding of interdisciplinary practice environments in the acute, sub-acute, residential and community settings to succeed in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Generate evidence-based recommendations for how to improve the sustainability of chronic illness management approaches in terms of their impact on natural, economic, social, political and cultural systems.
Evaluate chronic illness management methods to determine strategies that promote active engagement of persons, families and carers with health services.
Design appropriate chronic disease management plans or interdisciplinary team care arrangements based on the lived experiences of persons with chronic illness.

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY: CONSOLIDATING REFLECTIVE CLINICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject is one of two consolidation subjects of the combined Bachelor of Nursing/Bachelor of Midwifery degree. Opportunities are provided for you to develop and refine your abilities to manage care for a number of complex clients, reflect on your personal practice and critique the wider practice of nurses. The content builds on previous learnt concepts of person centred care, situational management, nursing inquiry, therapeutic communication and client education. The focus of the subject is to assist you to develop the repertoire of skills required by contemporary nursing practice and form a foundation for future nursing practice evolutions.
learning_outcomes: Design and support changes to nursing practice using contemporary research to justify practice improvement opportunities
Critically evaluate practice
Plan and implement effective and efficient nursing care

title: NURSING: REFLECTION AND CONSOLIDATION
syllabus_overview: This subject is the capstone subject for the Bachelor of Nursing degree. Through online activities and workshops you will refine your abilities to: manage care for a number of complex clients; reflect on your personal practice; and critique the wider practice of nurses. The subject content builds on previously learnt concepts of person-centred care, situational management, nursing inquiry, therapeutic communication and client education. The focus of the subject is to assist you to develop the repertoire of skills required by contemporary nursing practice and that form the foundation for future nursing practice evolutions.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate nursing practice.
Design, plan and execute nursing care that is effective and efficient.
Analyse, assess and recommend nursing practice improvement opportunities based on contemporary research.

title: RECOGNISING AND RESPONDING TO THE DETERIORATING PATIENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will have the opportunity to extend your knowledge and skills to complex and dynamic patient situations. Through lectures, online activities, workshops, clinical skills laboratories/simulations, and clinical placement, you will focus on assessment and interventions aimed at arresting deterioration of a patient's health. The clinical practicum will allow you to experience high acuity care settings and assume the responsibility of caring for individuals who may experience a deterioration in health. To achieve the learning outcomes of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written, verbal and clinical assessments within a 12-week period.
learning_outcomes: Apply the clinical reasoning cycle to provide person-centred care for individuals experiencing a deterioration in health in order to provide safe nursing care.
Explain common pathophysiology, as it relates to assessment data and pharmacology, that can result in deterioration of an individual's condition in order to develop appropriate interventions.
Manage the interactions with the patient, family, and the health care team during a clinical deterioration.
Demonstrate competence in technical skills when providing person-centred care for individuals experiencing a deterioration in health.
Develop an awareness of and contribute to the risk management strategies of a healthcare agency, in order to implement incident reporting procedures and apply risk management procedures.

title: RECOGNISING AND RESPONDING TO THE DETERIORATING PATIENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will have the opportunity to extend your knowledge and skills to complex and dynamic patient situations. Through lectures, online activities, workshops, clinical skills laboratories/simulations, and a clinical placement you will focus on the assessment and interventions aimed at arresting deterioration of a patient's health. The clinical practicum will allow you to experience high acuity care settings and assume the responsibility of caring for individuals who may experience a deterioration in health. To achieve the learning outcomes of this subject you will be expected to complete a range of written, verbal and clinical assessments within a 12-week period.
learning_outcomes: Explain common pathophysiology, as it relates to assessment data and pharmacology that can result in deterioration of an individual's condition in order to develop appropriate interventions.
Develop an awareness of and contribute to the risk management strategies of a healthcare agency, in order to implement incident reporting procedures and apply risk management procedures.
Demonstrate competence in technical skills when providing person-centred care for individuals experiencing a deterioration in health.
Apply the clinical reasoning cycle to provide person-centred care for individuals experiencing a deterioration in health in order to provide safe nursing care.
Manage the interactions with patient, family, and the health care team during a clinical deterioration.

title: RE-ENTRY TO PRACTICE (RN)
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will be prepared to meet the requirements for Division One RN registration, allowing re-entry to nursing practice within the Australian healthcare context. Areas covered include the Australian health care system, clinical reasoning, communication in health care, law and ethics in Australian health care, risk management including infection control, mental health issues, medication management, caring for vulnerable groups, community nursing, perioperative care and investigations and fluid and electrolyte balance. The subject has a clinical hurdle component of 160 hrs. Students enrolled in this subject must obtain provisional registration with ANMAC (which is provided prior to LTU accepting their enrollment). Successful completion of this subject will provide participants with the necessary requirements to apply to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia for re-entry to the workforce as a Division One RN Registered Nurse. This is a non-award program.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on nursing knowledge and skills developed and apply them to nursing in the Australian context
Demonstrate autonomy and responsibility to function as a registered nurse in accordance with the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Board standards and codes of conduct for a Registered Nurse
Justify the relevance of the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Board standards and codes of conduct for registered nurses
Demonstrate the interpersonal and communication skills required to be active participants in interdisciplinary practice
Apply critical thinking frameworks and problem-solving skills to nursing practice
Implement the principles of evidence-based practice in the provision and evaluation of person-centred nursing care

title: ADVANCED HEALTH ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will perform an advanced person-centred health assessment, accurately interpret health assessment and diagnostic assessment findings; source, critique, synthesise and incorporate evidence to rationalise and justify interpretations.
learning_outcomes: Accurately interpret health assessment findings and related diagnostic procedures
Determine and justify appropriate advanced health assessment requirements relative to the patient care situation
Demonstrate an ability to accurately perform advanced and targeted objective and subjective nursing assessment techniques

title: ACUTE CARE FOUNDATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop fundamental knowledge and skills required to conduct a comprehensive assessment in a time critical environment and develop appropriate nursing care plans appropriate for all patients across the care continuum. This subject covers advanced anatomy and physiology, a systems based approach to assessment, recognition and responding to the deteriorating patient, teamwork, communication and legal and ethical issues. The knowledge and skills that you will learn in this subject will be directly transferable into Acute Care nursing clinical practice. At the completion of this subject you will be prepared for ethically oriented professional practice and to undertake further studies at more advanced levels relevant to your specialty practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically apply relevant pathophysiology knowledge to complex patient situations
Critically apply clinical knowledge to demonstrate advanced assessment skills in the acute care setting
Critically appraise ethical and professional standards of nursing in the acute care setting
Accurately interpret assessment data to prioritise clinical care

title: CARDIAC CARE FOUNDATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop fundamental knowledge and skills required to conduct a comprehensive assessment in a time critical environment and develop appropriate nursing care plans appropriate for all patients across the care continuum. This subject covers advanced anatomy and physiology, a systems based approach to assessment, recognition and responding to the deteriorating patient, teamwork, communication and legal and ethical issues. The knowledge and skills that you will learn in this subject will be directly transferable into Cardiac Care nursing clinical practice.
