title: THERAPEUTIC MEDICATION MANAGEMENT FOR RN PRESCRIBERS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop and refine your understanding of medication management and its application to your patient cohorts. You will explore the legislative and regulatory frameworks that underpin RN Prescribing in Australia, as well as develop the skills and knowledge around partnered prescribing principles and relay this to your workplace context. You will revisit concepts learned in NSM5004 and apply these concepts to your patient context and link these to practical prescribing principles. You will identify the barriers and enablers to RN prescribing and explore funding systems such as the PBS and its application to RN prescribing and scope of practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative and regulatory frameworks and compliance with the Quality Use of Medicines framework

Justify safe and effective rationale for medication management to achieve therapeutic goals, based on review and analysis of relevant patient information (including comprehensive patient assessment, diagnostics and thorough patient history).
Appraise credible and appropriate sources of medication information and evidence to implement an evidence-informed approach to RN prescribing.
Demonstrate knowledge of partnered prescribing in relation to RN scope of practice.
Implement partnered clinical decision-making processes to tailor appropriate medication plans to meet therapeutic goals, patient informed choices and holistic patient management
Utilise clinical knowledge to rationalise the indications for prescribing and/or use of non-pharmacological therapies in the treatment of patients.

title: COMMUNITY CHILD HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop public health knowledge and skills within a community-based child, family and community nursing context. You will explore the links between economic inequality and child health, and the promotion of optimal development of young children through social justice strategies. You will develop insight into culturally appropriate practice, applying this knowledge when working with families from diverse cultural backgrounds. This subject is delivered via a flexible online mode which may include online classes and online learning modules.
learning_outcomes: Appraise the nurse’s role in contributing to Primary Health Care strategies in community maternal and child health settings.
Facilitate referral to appropriate community services to connect families to the community.
Critically analyse the application of Primary Health Care principles in community maternal and child health care practice.
Plan culturally inclusive interventions appropriate to diverse populations using the social model of health.

title: MIDWIFERY FUNDAMENTALS: POSTNATAL CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop fundamental knowledge and skills required to care for women and their babies, to six weeks post-birth, in the midwifery care context. The subject includes a variety of normal and complex physiological, psychological and social adaptations occurring for new mothers and their families in the first six weeks postpartum. Students will learn about the role of the midwife in providing postnatal care, infant feeding, promotion and establishment of breastfeeding and the provision of education and support to empower women and their families during this period to make evidence based informed choices. This subject is delivered via a blended learning approach comprising of face to face teaching, workshops and online learning modules and is supported by clinical practicum.
learning_outcomes: Provide contemporary best practice information, assistance and advice to the woman on nutrition needs and feeding of her infant
Perform a comprehensive assessment, and provide safe and effective midwifery care to the woman and newborn during the postnatal period according to the scope of practice of the midwife.

Plan individualised care in consultation with the woman, her family and midwifery colleagues, in consideration of psychosocial diversity to achieve positive outcomes for women and their families during the postnatal period
Critically analyse, evaluate and apply current evidence, guidelines and processes in midwifery in order to inform practice in the postnatal setting

title: MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will use your clinical knowledge of women and children (0-6) to plan and implement safe and effective care for families with young children in the community. You will undertake clinical practice in community-based maternal and child health and education settings. This subject enables you to assess the health and development of children and maternal wellbeing, using screening and assessment tools. You will build on nursing and midwifery skills and knowledge, to develop advanced critical thinking and problem-solving skills and develop personal learning goals. The subject is delivered via a flexible online mode which may include on-campus or online workshops, online learning modules and clinical practice in maternal and child health settings.
learning_outcomes: Undertake comprehensive infant, child, and maternal assessments according to the Key Ages and Stages Framework.
Engage in critical reflection to develop your maternal and child health clinical nursing practice.
Using prescribed tools, accurately assess the health and wellbeing of mothers.
Using prescribed tools, accurately assess the health and development of children 0-6 years.

title: CRITICAL NURSING ESSENTIALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop fundamental knowledge and skills required to successfully transition to and engage in post graduate higher education nursing studies. The student will develop appropriate academic literacy skills applied to case based acute clinical nursing care of patients and their families. This subject introduces the student to nursing in the Australian context addressing professional standards, and healthcare organisational systems. This subject covers: recognition and responding to the deteriorating patient; teamwork and communication; legal and ethical issues, healthcare organisational environments and culture and professional standards . At the completion of this subject, you will be prepared for ethically oriented professional practice, and have the foundations to undertake further advanced study relevant to your professional interest.
learning_outcomes: Accurately interpret scenario-based data to identify clinical and non-clinical priorities for patients.
Determine and justify appropriate professional practice requirements relative to patient care scenarios.
Critically assess ethical requirements related to specific clinical and professional scenarios.
Accurately relate theoretical knowledge to practice in relation to caring for patients who are at risk and/or deteriorating.

title: FIRST NATIONS PERINATAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will reflect on aspects of your own cultural self-awareness to advance your knowledge and skills in providing effective and safe care to First Nations Australian families in the maternity context. You will explore Australian history, concepts related to traditional and contemporary Indigenous cultures, the rights of individuals and groups to self-determination, and consider how culturally safe clinical practices can contribute to closing the gap in health outcomes. The skills gained in this subject will enable you to recognise how socio-cultural diversity may impact maternity outcomes equity and access. This subject is delivered online using online activities, and synchronous lectures and workshops to support your learning.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate health inequity, the factors contributing to this, and analyse ways to close the gap in birth outcomes between First Nations and non-First Nations Australians

Evaluate the interconnections between physical, social, historical, political and cultural factors and their impact on perinatal health outcomes by understanding First Nations concepts of health and healing.

Development of culturally competent communication skills to facilitate therapeutic relationships, and support partnerships with First Nations families, health professionals, organisations and communities.
Critically analyse the role of cultural safety in improving maternal and child health outcomes for First Nations Australians and how cultural safety influences practice.
Critically reflect on personal and professional beliefs and attitudes in relation to working alongside First Nations women, babies and families.

title: MIDWIFERY FUNDAMENTALS, PREGNANCY AND BIRTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will be introduced to the fundamentals of midwifery practice in the antenatal and intrapartum periods. Using a primary health care philosophy, students will develop skills and attributes for providing woman-centred care during pregnancy, labour and birth based on contemporary evidence based guidelines. The focus of this subject will be on women experiencing a normal pregnancy, labour and birth. Students will build on their knowledge of human anatomy, physiology and psychosocial concepts to cultivate the ability to provide safe and effective midwifery care. This subject enables students to further develop reflective practice, critical thinking and clinical decision making skills, via a flexible model, with relevant face-to-face lectures and workshops and supported by clinical practicum.
learning_outcomes: Support and educate women in partnership throughout pregnancy and labour.
Identify deviations from normal pregnancy, labour and birth processes.
Critically evaluate and apply available evidence to inform best practice in midwifery.
Plan and communicate midwifery care with women, their families and colleagues, respecting individual rights and responsibilities.
Provide safe and effective midwifery care to women during pregnancy, birth and labour.

title: CARE OF THE NEONATE WITH SPECIAL NEEDS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on earlier theoretical and clinical experiences of the normal newborn, and be introduced to the common conditions of the more complex neonate, that may require admission to the special care nursery. You will encounter and learn to recognise the conditions, and gain the necessary knowledge and skills, to provide appropriate care for the premature, sick or 'at risk' infant. Issues relating to parenting infants, who have complex needs, will be explored, and you will build on their interpersonal skills when examining concepts of attachment, grief and loss. The relationships between maternal conditions and their effects on the infant, and the impact of the birth of a premature or sick infant on the health industry, the local community and society are also considered.
learning_outcomes: Comply care to families with a sick, premature or at-risk newborn in a neonatal nursery setting.
Consult and refer newborns who are premature, sick or at-risk to other health professionals as needed in a neonatal nursery setting.
Generate and provide safe and effective care in the clinical setting for newborns who are premature, sick or 'at risk'.
Create a supportive environment for families and teach the families the specialised neonatal care their newborn requires in a neonatal nursery setting.
Synthesise the management and care of infants who are at risk of complications in the neonatal period in a neonatal nursery setting.

title: TRANSITION TO CRITICAL CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the fundamental knowledge and skills required to care for patients in critical care nursing practice contexts. This subject provides a theoretical and practical foundation that will prepare you for ethically orientated professional practice and to undertake further studies at more advanced levels in critical care nursing. This subject will enable you to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, specialised clinical proficiency, and effective communication skills. You will be able to make independent judgements; plan; implement and evaluate practice in specialty contexts and function effectively as a member of the multidisciplinary team. This subject is delivered via a flexible online mode comprising learning modules via LMS and three workshops (face to face or equivalent online via zoom) and supported by appropriate clinical practicum.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialist knowledge and skills to inform clinical practice in the critical care setting
Accurately interpret advanced patient assessment and diagnostic data relevant to inform critical care nursing practice
Link theoretical concepts to clinical practice regarding pathophysiology relevant to the critical care setting
Employ and evaluate specialty nursing interventions to optimise clinical outcomes in critical care nursing

title: RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE IN MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the research and evidence in midwifery practice. You will learn the skills needed to be able to interpret and understand research evidence and draw on real life examples of midwifery related research. You will gain a broad understanding of various research designs including the application of quantitative and qualitative approaches. You will develop skills in critiquing evidence for application to maternity care. Using an online teaching mode including, online activities, and synchronous lectures and workshops you will develop skills in reviewing the literature, explore the ethics of research and apply the appropriate design and methods to specific clinical and social issues related to maternity care and practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise levels of evidence and how this impacts the relevance of research to a clinical question
Develop a search strategy and conduct a literature review related to a specific topic
Explain the ethical issues inherent in midwifery research
Formulate a research question based on a clinical issue related to midwifery
Explain key principles that underpin evidence- based practice
Justify the choice of different research designs and data collection methods

title: PAIN MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Pain impacts many patients accessing healthcare or following injury and surgery. An individual's pain, pain perceptions and experience of pain have many contributing physiological and psychological factors. Evidence-based pain management strategies, quality patient assessment and quality care of the patient with pain is required. This subject will explore internationally, evidence-based strategies and approaches to acute, persistent and chronic pain management relevant to the healthcare setting.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate available evidence to inform advanced clinical practice in pain management.
Critically discern how best practice evidence is used to improve clinical practice.
Apply analytical problem solving, planning and evaluation skills to advanced clinical pain management practice.
Identify the elements of a comprehensive patient assessment, relevant to pain management.

Apply specialist knowledge and skills to inform clinical practice in the neonatal care setting
Link theoretical concepts to clinical practice regarding pathophysiology relevant to the neonatal care setting

title: TRANSITION TO MEDICAL IMAGING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the fundamental knowledge and skills required to care for patients in medical imaging practice contexts. This subject provides a theoretical and practical foundation that will prepare you for ethically orientated professional practice and to undertake further studies at more advanced levels in medical imaging. This subject will enable you to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, specialised clinical proficiency, and effective communication skills. You will be able to make independent judgements; plan; implement and evaluate practice in specialty contexts and function effectively as a member of the multidisciplinary team. This subject is delivered via a flexible online mode comprising learning modules via LMS and three workshops (face to face or equivalent online via zoom) and supported by appropriate clinical practicum.
learning_outcomes: Employ and evaluate specialty nursing interventions to optimise clinical outcomes in medical imaging
Link theoretical concepts to clinical practice regarding pathophysiology relevant to the medical imaging setting
Accurately interpret advanced patient assessment and diagnostic data relevant to inform medical imaging practice
Apply specialist knowledge and skills to inform clinical practice in the medical imaging setting

title: TRANSITION TO OPERATIVE CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the fundamental knowledge and skills required to care for patients in operative care contexts. This subject provides a theoretical and practical foundation that will prepare you for ethically orientated professional practice and to undertake further studies at more advanced levels in operative care nursing. This subject will enable you to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, specialised clinical proficiency, and effective communication skills. You will be able to make independent judgements; plan; implement and evaluate practice in specialty contexts and function effectively as a member of the multidisciplinary team. This subject is delivered via a flexible online mode comprising learning modules via LMS and three workshops (face to face or equivalent online via zoom) and supported by appropriate clinical practicum.
learning_outcomes: Accurately interpret advanced patient assessment and diagnostic data relevant to inform perioperative practices
Employ and evaluate specialty nursing interventions to optimise clinical outcomes in perioperative practices
Apply specialist knowledge and skills to inform clinical practice in the perioperative setting
Link theoretical concepts to clinical practice regarding pathophysiology relevant to the perioperative setting

title: PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR RN PRESCRIBERS
syllabus_overview: This subject will develop your knowledge and skills to assess the effects of medication on the human body. It will explore the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of medications and their relation to the treatment of illness and injury in the human body. You will apply these principles to identify and illustrate the rationale and clinical reasoning skills, within an RN prescriber framework and scope of practice, to evidence your clinical decision making around pharmacotherapeutic patient management.
learning_outcomes: Rationalise the alterations in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in patients across the lifespan of and within those of diverse ethnicities.
Rationalise advanced clinical practice knowledge and assessment to the pharmacological management of pain.

Articulate principles of pharmacology, including the differences between pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics (the manner in which medications are absorbed, distributed, metabolised and excreted in the body.
6 Critique available evidence to inform and support advanced RN clinical decision making in the management and delivery of pharmacological interventions.
Evidence understanding of medications effects on each body system and utilise this understanding in the application of pharmacological therapies in RN prescribing models of care.
Demonstrate safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative and regulatory frameworks in accordance with partnered RN prescribing frameworks.

title: PERIOPERATIVE NURSE SURGEONS ASSISTANT 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject the students will look to further deepen knowledge and skills as a surgical assistant and further develop in surgical assisting skill. As an advanced clinical practice nurse in the perioperative surgical assisting specialisation, understanding how this complex area of practice positively impacts and connects the surgical team in the provision of the highest level of care provision in pre-operative, intraoperative and post-operative patient or client care is required. Students will leverage academic and clinical practice knowledge to demonstrate and practice at an advanced level while further working toward honing expertise in these skills in the practice setting.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and integrate valid evidence-based research on current developments and determine its impact/relevance on your advanced practice.
Develop and optimise quality and surgical assisting skill acquisition.
Explore effective participation in a multidisciplinary team to ensure safe, ethical practice.
Appraise and integrate valid evidence-based research to design & implement strategies appropriate to the specialist clinical field.

title: PERIOPERATIVE NURSE SURGEONS ASSISTANT 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will build on the advanced knowledge and skills developed within the field of Perioperative Nursing Practice. In undertaking studies in PNSA 1 the student embarks on an advanced practice role toward practicing as a Perioperative Nurse Surgeons Assistant (PNSA). The student PNSA follows the Advanced Clinical Practice stream in the specialist area of Perioperative Nurse Surgical Assistant (PNSA). Students develop their cognitive and technical skills to demonstrate an advanced understanding of the underlying principles and theoretical concepts in the role of surgical assistance. An in-depth understanding of the history of the PNSA role and integration of advanced nursing principle in delivery of care in the three phases of care; Preoperative, Intraoperative and Postoperative Care.
learning_outcomes: Explore the higher-level knowledge skills, legislative requirements, and behaviours of an advanced practitioner
Critically reflect on and discuss the role of an advanced practitioner within an interdisciplinary team.
Demonstrate and evidence an advanced specialist skill set in the delivery of surgical care under the mentorship and supervision of a surgeon/s.
Critically explore the expectations, professional profile and role of the PNSA.

title: FOUNDATIONS IN AGEING AND COMPLEX CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the advanced knowledge and skills required to conduct comprehensive, person-centred assessments. Underpinning any assessment is a detailed understanding of normal physiology and how comorbidities and social determinants of health alter these processes. This subject covers the impact of ageing on anatomy and physiology, a systems-based approach to assessment, recognition and response to physical, mental and/or social deterioration, planning for transitions in care, person-centred care, interprofessional teamwork, communication, and legal and ethical issues. The knowledge and skills learned in this subject will be directly transferable to your practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise ethical and professional standards of nursing to assess and respond to the needs of adults as they transition through care.
Accurately justify and interpret assessment data to inform evidence-based care decisions, in relation to transitions of care.
Critically apply advanced pathophysiology knowledge to evaluate complex care.
Critically apply clinical reasoning and knowledge to demonstrate advanced assessment skills in the care of adults as they transition through care.

title: APPLIED PRACTICE IN AGEING AND COMPLEX CARE
syllabus_overview: This subject enables you to further develop the knowledge and skills required to care for adults in diverse settings. This subject will empower you to provide evidence-based nursing care that enhances person-centred care and improves health outcomes. Through this subject, you will have the opportunity to continue to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, specialised clinical proficiency, and effective communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialist knowledge and skills to support clinical decision-making in the care of adults.
Employ and evaluate specialty nursing interventions to optimise clinical outcomes for adults in diverse settings.
Critically integrate and apply pathophysiological principles to clinical practice in the care of adults in diverse contexts.
Accurately analyse advanced patient assessment and diagnostic data to inform evidence-based care of adults across the continuum of nursing care.

title: SPECIALIST PRACTICE IN AGEING AND COMPLEX CARE
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable you to build your knowledge further, make high-level, independent judgments, and function more independently as an interprofessional team member. You will learn to assess and support adults with complex, chronic care needs. Strategies to support evidence-based practice and maintain physiological, mental and social function will be examined, and you will critically appraise innovative models of care. You will develop comprehensive clinical skills and the required knowledge to effectively use research and other information as the basis of your advanced interprofessional practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate, synthesise, and apply current evidence to inform best-practice in the care of adults.
Execute effective interprofessional leadership and communication strategies, to optimise care in complex contexts.
Employ critical thinking and clinical decision making based on relevant clinical evidence to design, implement and evaluate a person-centred care plan.
Synthesise and apply advanced disciplinary knowledge to manage complex situations in adult nursing care across transitions of care.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL EVIDENCE FOR NURSING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Advanced Clinical Evidence for Nursing Practice aims to enhance your ability to source, synthesise, and apply evidence to inform clinical practice and improve patient care and outcomes. Throughout the coursework, you will develop foundational skills in searching, synthesising, critiquing, and referencing peer-reviewed literature. You will also explore various research methodologies. Key concepts, such as translating evidence into practice, addressing underrepresented groups in evidence-based literature, and upholding ethical standards in research, will be covered. Additionally, you will examine the influence of discursive Artificial Intelligence (AI) on academic research practices. You will be encouraged to reflect on the role of nurses and midwives as leaders in evidence-based practice and research. Learning and development will be supported through research-based activities tailored to your areas of specialty or generalist practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse treatment evidence and patient preferences in clinical decision-making, considering cultural, geographical, and socio-economic factors, including language, literacy, and health beliefs.
Source, critically appraise, and integrate evidence into nursing practice to enhance patient outcomes, inform ongoing professional development, and promote lifelong learning.
Formulate ethically sound research questions which address evidence gaps within your practice area.
Justify the selection and use of validated research tools to ensure methodological rigor and the integration of high-quality evidence into safe and effective consumer care.
Utilise digital technologies and data analysis tools proficiently, while critically assessing the potential benefits and risks of discursive AI in nursing and midwifery research and practice.
Critique how evidence translation impacts health outcomes, focusing on key barriers and the impact of underrepresented vulnerable populations in research literature.

title: CLINICAL INTERNSHIP FOR NURSE PRACTITIONER A
syllabus_overview: Clinical Internship A offers an opportunity for you to enhance your ability to critically analyse and apply specialised knowledge and skills essential for advanced clinical practice. Through a combination of online coursework, clinical supervision, and direct patient care, you will cultivate practice accountability, exercise expert judgment under a supervised model of care, and deepen your understanding of contemporary issues in advanced nursing. Upon completion of Clinical Internship A, you will emerge as an increasingly independent, adept, and knowledgeable advanced practice nurse, equipped to navigate complex clinical environments, uphold practice accountability, and contribute to advancements in specialised areas of nursing practice through research and scholarship.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse current knowledge and healthcare processes to inform the provision of specialty patient care.
Engage in critical reflection on the role of the nurse practitioner in leadership and professional activities that influence care, development, and research in the broader healthcare setting.
Demonstrate effective communication and collaboration skills with clients, families, and healthcare professionals to optimize health outcomes for patients.
Apply advanced practice nursing knowledge, assessment, and diagnostic skills to provide person-centred care and develop treatment plans tailored to meet the clinical needs of patients.
Implement diagnostic reasoning and evidence-based rationale to plan and deliver patient-centred care.
Interpret and integrate legislative, regulatory, and contemporary professional issues into the nurse practitioner practice environment.

title: NURTURING CHILD AND FAMILY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore concepts that underpin early childhood development, particularly those of parent-child relationship-based therapies and practices, and their application to maternal and child health practice. This subject is delivered via a flexible online mode which may include online classes, online learning modules and a follow-through journey with a family in a community setting.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the characteristics of infants and young children which affect the child’s emotional development and capacity for self-regulation.
Reflect on your personal responses to working with families in diverse communities.
Analyse the theoretical concepts that inform the social, emotional, and cognitive development of young children, to apply to clinical practice with families.
Critically appraise the experience of families attending the MCH service.

title: CLINICAL INTERNSHIP FOR NURSE PRACTITIONER B
syllabus_overview: Clinical Internship B represents the culmination of theoretical and clinical learning, providing you with the opportunity to integrate advanced specialty knowledge and nursing skills into your clinical practice. Through a blend of online coursework, clinical supervision, and direct patient care, you will cultivate expert judgment, assume clinical responsibility, and develop leadership skills essential for influencing healthcare outcomes both at the patient level and within the broader healthcare context. By the conclusion of Clinical Internship B, you will emerge as confident, competent, and autonomous advanced practice nurses, ready to navigate complex clinical environments, drive positive healthcare outcomes, and contribute to advancements in nursing practice through research and leadership.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and adhere to professional guidelines, legislation, and common law pertinent to nurse practitioner practice.
Demonstrate nursing leadership and engage in professional activities to positively impact patient outcomes within the broader healthcare context.
Take ownership of professional development and scope of practice, exhibiting a commitment to ongoing learning and professional responsibility.
Utilise critical analysis of evidence and best practice to deliver individualized advanced nursing care.
Foster collaboration with healthcare professionals and patients to optimize health outcomes and promote patient-cantered care.
Apply advanced practice nursing knowledge, assessment, and diagnostic skills to evaluate treatment outcomes and enhance patient care.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL NURSING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Advanced Clinical Nursing Practice equips you with advanced skills in comprehensive health assessment and diagnostic reasoning to inform clinical decision-making in diverse healthcare settings. Through a combination of online coursework and practical application, you will develop expertise in assessing the pathophysiology of human body systems across the lifespan, with a focus on addressing national health priorities such as diabetes, dementia, mental illness, and obesity. Through interactive learning modules, case studies, clinical practice, you will enhance your diagnostic capabilities and critical thinking skills, preparing you to excel as an advanced practitioner in today's complex healthcare landscape.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning and knowledge of own scope of practice to inform decision making round referrals to other healthcare professionals (for either sole or collaborative treatment).

Demonstrate proficiency in clinical reasoning by integrating the process of history-taking, comprehensive and targeted assessment, selection of diagnostic investigations, and formulation of evidence-based primary and relevant differential diagnoses.
Demonstrate a comprehensive, systematic clinical assessment approach integrating relevant underlying physiology and pathophysiology.
Apply critical analysis to comprehensive health assessment and use of diagnostic investigations that consider the impact to the health care consumer.
Develop, implement, and monitor evidence-based treatment plans, including referral to other specialists, appropriate to the Nurse Practitioner role scope in the Australian healthcare context.

Demonstrate understanding of the Nurse Practitioner’s role in the provision of collaborative, person-centred, evidence-based healthcare, addressing issues of equity, access, and national health priorities.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, we will explore the processes associated with clinical audit. You will develop your skills in evaluating evidence to inform advanced nursing practice. You will explore how clinical governance and best practice evidence are used to inform, guide and improve practice in a specified clinical or professional area.
learning_outcomes: Apply analytical problem solving, planning and evaluation skills to advanced clinical practice
Critically discern how clinical governance and best practice evidence are used to improve clinical practice
Design an audit suitable for a specified clinical or professional area.
Critically evaluate available evidence to inform advanced clinical practice

title: COMPLEX CARE IN MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH NURSING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop knowledge and skills to deliver complex child, family and community nursing care, and work in partnership with families facing additional challenges. This subject explores the experience of families who require additional MCH service support, and the methods to effectively work with families to improve health and wellbeing outcomes. The subject is delivered via a flexible online mode which may include on-campus workshops, online classes, online learning modules and clinical practice in maternal and child health settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective collaboration with clients, colleagues, and other professionals to meet the needs of children and families.
Implement targeted interventions or alternative models of care to improve long term outcomes for children and families.
Undertake enhanced family assessments in accordance with legislation, maternal and child health professional practice standards, and program guidelines.
Observe legislative requirements in maternal and child health practice, including mandatory reporting, and the accurate assessment, documentation, and response to identified risk of child abuse.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will investigate the structure and scope of advanced nursing practice. This investigation will involve analysis of contemporary professional roles in your area of specialty practice. Some comparison of the roles in relation to regulation and standards of practice will be expected. The study in NSM5CLB – Advanced Clinical B will build on knowledge and skills that were developed in NSM5CLA – Advanced Clinical A.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical and analytical problem solving, planning and evaluation skills to your area of advanced specialty practice
Demonstrate and evidence an advanced specialist skills set in the delivery of care
Synthesise professional standards in application to your area of advanced specialty practice
Critically evaluate available evidence to inform advanced specialty practice

title: CLINICAL QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the implementation of clinical best practice in healthcare and the ethical implications of clinical quality improvements for the profession and patients. You will review specific clinical practice from their own clinical specialty and create a plan for a clinical audit in order to provide recommendations for best practice. The ethical implications of changes to practice or quality improvements are considered, with particular reference to informed consent and 'benefits versus harms' for patients. Clinical audit poster presentations are delivered online.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise evidence to generate recommendations for best practice.
Design a suitable clinical audit to determine the influence of a specific nursing or midwifery intervention in practice.
Plan a clinical audit and gather appropriate evidence to evaluate the influence of a specific nursing or midwifery intervention on patient outcomes in practice.
Develop an action plan to disseminate findings and support quality improvement implementation.

title: IMPLEMENTING PRACTICE CHANGE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will conduct a critical literature review based on the project topic to be undertaken in NSM5NPI Clinical Project. The literature review must aim to summarise, interpret and critically evaluate the existing evidence to establish current knowledge of a particular subject. The literature review may address a controversy, establish the need for additional research, and/or define a topic of inquiry. It is intended to provide you with current knowledge on an aspect that relates to legal and ethical issues within clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Develop and implement literature search strategies, including appropriate keywords
Critically examine the relevance of the findings to the clinical setting
Conduct a comprehensive literature review, critically evaluating available evidence
Critically reflect on a project topic relevant to the practice of professional practice

title: EDUCATION IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: Education in Nursing and Midwifery focuses on preparing clinicians for their role as facilitator, teacher, mentor, preceptor and clinical supervisor. You will gain an understanding of factors influential to learning in the clinical environment alongside how to design education encounters to maximise learning and minimise barriers. There are opportunities to observe, discuss, analyse and reflect upon contemporary clinical education practices and models. The subject focus includes utilising education theories and principles of instructional design to develop a learning program in the clinical setting. You will align identified outcomes with relevant teaching and learning activities, assessments and established evaluation approaches within the program.
learning_outcomes: Design suitable rigorous evaluation methods to determine effectiveness of teaching and learning in nursing and midwifery education
Critique relevant teaching approaches or clinical supervision models from literature and implement relevant approaches in practice
Apply educational theory and instructional design principles to create a program of learning
Articulate a philosophy of teaching and learning drawing on educational theory relevant to nursing and midwifery education
Critcally review influences on nursing and midwifery education in the clinical environment

title: MANAGEMENT IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students are provided with an opportunity to explore the theory and practice of leadership and management and to consider how these apply in the context of their professional work. The subject will also provide some opportunities for students to explore developmental strategies that can be used to support advancement of management and leadership capabilities in nursing and midwifery contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explore the potential application of key management and leadership skills in relation to nursing and midwifery workplace scenarios.
Critically review and appraise key leadership and management theories that apply to nursing and midwifery disciplinary contexts.
Critically reflect on your current and the ongoing development of your own leadership and management skills.
Consider the application of developmental frameworks to support advancement of management and leadership capabilities in nursing and midwifery contexts.

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY PRACTICE INNOVATION PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are offered the opportunity to design and implement a project that supports the development of your clinical expertise, scholarly inquiry and skills in reporting. You will design and conduct a project, supported by your work in the subject Implementing Practice Change (NSM5IPC), which could precede this subject, or be done concurrently if you are full-time. You are allocated an academic supervisor who offers guidance throughout the duration of the investigation. The subject involves regular communication with a designated academic and/or clinical supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Plan and implement an innovative, evidence-based project in a safe and ethical manner using the required skills, knowledge and attitudes to achieve the negotiated outcome
Apply different forms of evidence to validate conclusions drawn from the project implementation
Report on the outcomes of a project in written format appropriate for different purposes
Utilise analytical, problem solving, planning, negotiation and evaluation skills to inform the design and implementation of a project

title: RESEARCH IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop advanced knowledge of nursing and midwifery practice. You will examine the elements of the research process including identifying a research problem, formulation of a research question, research design, methods, data collection, analyses and dissemination of results. You will acquire skills required to conduct a literature review for research purposes and address the ethics of research, develop cognitive and technical skills that demonstrate a broad understanding of a body of knowledge relevant to clinical practice. You will also acquire skills required to conduct a literature review for research purposes, develop appropriate research methods and address the ethics of research.
learning_outcomes: Identify the important elements of the research process to critically review and report on an area that needs further exploration
Examine appropriate strategies for dissemination of research
Discriminate between different data collection methods and critically judge the most suitable data collection and analysis methods for different study designs
Critically appraise available evidence to inform your advanced nursing or midwifery practice

title: RESEARCH FOUNDATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop advanced knowledge of nursing and midwifery research practice. You will examine the elements of the research process including: identifying a clinical issue or research problem, formulating a research question or statement, research design and methods, data collection and analyses, and disseminating results. You will also acquire skills required to conduct a literature review for research purposes and address the ethics of research. The subject is delivered via a flexible online mode (LMS) comprised of learning modules. It provides essential research knowledge that can be built upon in the Advanced Practice subjects.
learning_outcomes: Conceptually map the strategies for dissemination of research.
Contextualise and critically review the conduct of ethical research.
Critique a body of research.
Discriminate and analyse the important elements of the research process.

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY THESIS B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will continue development from NSM5THA and work on relevant aspects of your research project. This work will be undertaken under the continued guidance of your research supervisor and in consultation with the subject coordinator. The learning activities in this subject concentrate mainly on data collection, data analysis and writing drafts of chapters or a paper for future publication. The focus of the work is primarily negotiated with your supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Report on key insights and findings from your research endeavours during study of the subject.
Apply practical skills in writing-up the research involved in your project.
Implement appropriate methods of data collection and analysis that progress your research project.

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY THESIS A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will design a small research project. Normally this project will be a structured literature review. This work will be undertaken in conjunction with an academic supervisor, in consultation with the subject coordinator. During the semester you will develop practical research skills, including development of a research plan/proposal, and background review. Additionally, you will explore relevant research methods associated with conducting the research.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate available research evidence to identify areas needing further research
Critically discuss relevant research methods associated with conducting research
Prepare a research plan or proposal for an identified research question
Utilise analytical, problem solving, planning and evaluation skills in the development of research

title: NURSING AND MIDWIFERY THESIS C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will complete the work (commenced in NSM5THA and continued in NSM5THB) associated with your research project. This work will be undertaken in conjunction with an academic supervisor and in consultation with the subject coordinator. The final product of your research study will be a written thesis. While not a requirement, the thesis may include drafted papers prepared for publication in high impact Scopus or Web of Science listed journals.
learning_outcomes: Implement practical skills in writing-up the research involved in your project.
Demonstrate high order skills in professional research through the execution and completion of the agreed research project.
Derive a comprehensive report (as a thesis) of the research project undertaken and knowledge outcomes attained and submit a report.

title: THERAPEUTIC MEDICATION MANAGEMENT B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop knowledge and skills to identify the effects of medications on physiological, biochemical, and pathophysiological body systems. Systematic clinical assessment and evidence-based critical thinking skills will be applied to justify rationales for the initiation and instigation of therapeutic medications and treatment plans. Your learning will be assessed through a systems-based case study, a comprehensive clinical case presentation, online examinations, and work-based learning.
learning_outcomes: Critique available evidence to inform and support clinical decision making in the management and delivery of pharmacological interventions.
Exemplify safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative and regulatory frameworks to meet the clinical needs of healthcare consumers.
Utilise advanced clinical knowledge to rationalise the indications for prescribing, de-prescribing and/or use of non-pharmacological therapies in the treatment of patients.
Rationalise the differences in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in patients of diverse ethnicities and alterations noted to these processes across the lifespan.

Articulate principles of pharmacology, including the differences between pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, the manner in which medications are absorbed, distributed, metabolised and excreted in the body.
Evidence understanding of medications effects on each body system and utilise this understanding in the application of pharmacological therapies in relevant area of practice.

title: THERAPEUTIC MEDICATION MANAGEMENT A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain an understanding of the clinical perspectives of therapeutic medication management. The principles of Quality Use of Medicines will be covered, along with how legislative and professional issues inform judicious, safe, and appropriate prescribing and medication management in the Australian healthcare setting. Your learning will be assessed through a series of case studies, a comprehensive clinical case presentation, online examinations, and work-based learning.
learning_outcomes: Justify safe and effective individualised patient medication profiles to achieve therapeutic goals based on review and analysis of relevant patient information (including comprehensive patient assessment, diagnostics and thorough patient history).
Implement critical decision-making processes to tailor appropriate medication plans to meet therapeutic goals, patient informed choices and holistic patient management.
Exemplify safe prescribing practices within applicable legislative and regulatory frameworks and compliance with the Quality Use of Medicines framework.
Appraise credible and appropriate sources of medication information and evidence to implement an evidence informed approach into care planning.
Rationalise advanced clinical practice knowledge and assessment to the pharmacological management of pain in own specialty area of practice.

title: USE MAPS, PLANS, DRAWINGS AND DETAILS
syllabus_overview: Students will learn the skills and knowledge required to read and interpret maps, plans, drawings and specifications and to prepare a simple map or plan.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and use maps, plans, drawings and specifications.
Use maps, plans and drawings.
Record and advise on changes and errors.

title: DIVERSE PERSPECTIVES OF OCCUPATION, HEALTH AND WELLBEING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theoretical foundations of communication in occupational therapy, apply, and adopt intentional communication skills in a simulated telehealth setting. You will explore diverse understandings of health and wellbeing from Eastern, Western, and Indigenous worldviews, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives to provide a foundation for culturally responsive practice. Finally, you will explore the occupational needs of people, families, communities, and populations both locally and globally with a focus on occupational justice and global citizenship. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate engagement, creativity and peer collaboration through evidence based forum contributions.
Demonstrate critical and action-oriented reflection of the ongoing impact of colonisation on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People
Apply knowledge of core occupational concepts and theories to understand health and wellbeing perspectives of individuals and communities.
Collaborate and communicate effectively with peers using professional and culturally responsive verbal and non-verbal skills.

title: OCCUPATIONAL SCIENCE: INTRODUCTION TO OCCUPATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of occupation, environments as contexts in which occupation occurs, and the relationship between human occupation and health and wellbeing at a personal level. You will develop skills in critical reflection of Self, exploring cultural factors including identity, power, privilege, injustice and oppression. You will understand and apply occupational science concepts and theories to analyse individual and group experiences of occupational engagement. Additionally, you will be introduced to various clinical settings in which Occupational Therapists practice, highlighting career options upon graduation, the importance of professional self-management, evidence-based practice, and understanding the lived experience of receiving Occupational Therapy. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Communicate understanding and application of professional knowledge about occupation and its use in occupational therapy practice
Identify, understand and describe various conceptions of human occupation and the associated experiences of meaningful engagement in these occupations.
Critically reflect upon and describe cultural factors and environments that influence privilege, injustice, occupational choices and identity.
Understand and apply occupational science concepts and evidence-based practice to analyse individual and group experiences of occupation

title: ENABLING CHANGE: OCCUPATIONAL FOUNDATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on previous philosophical and theoretical perspectives guiding occupational therapy practice, with a particular focus on the Model of Human Occupation (Taylor, 2024). You will apply your learning to foundational enabling skills including occupational analysis, facilitating occupational groups, evidence-based practice, and relationship-focused intentional communication. You will analyse an occupational narrative and apply research to demonstrate an advanced understanding of relationships between health, meaning, and participation in occupations.
learning_outcomes: Apply peer-reviewed evidence to analyse and understand occupations and narratives about participating in occupations.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of relationships between culture, occupational participation, environment, and health and well-being.
Design, facilitate and evaluate occupationally focused group experiences using principles and processes of occupational analysis and group work.

Apply and reflect on enabling change processes including intentional communication, occupational analysis and group facilitation to support continued development of occupational therapy practice skills.
Demonstrate an advanced understanding of First Nations ways of knowing and reflect on culturally responsive and safe communication skills.

title: ENABLING PARTICIPATION: PSYCHOSOCIAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will describe, apply and evaluate principles of engagement, assessment and intervention for people experiencing mental health conditions, with the aim to promote their capacity to participate in their usual occupations. Clinical reasoning skills in mental health practice will be established, using evidence-based literature to explore conceptual and practice models. Therapeutic communication, reflection and consumer participation in teaching will promote effective selection of intervention principles, applying principles of culturally safe practice and focusing on the use of meaningful occupation, incorporating environmental supports and exhibiting a deep understanding of barriers and faciliators, including advocacy, racism, organisational change, environmental adaptation.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of cultural safety to ensure interventions are appropriate and relationships are respectful
Justify, using professional reasoning and peer-reviewed evidence, interventions selected to support people with mental illness.
Apply specialist knowledge to support people with mental illness in their occupational participation.
Communicate clearly and effectively occupational therapy interventions for people living with mental illness to both lay and professional audiences, demonstrating culturally safe communication.

Select and justify appropriate occupational therapy conceptual and practice models, using prescribed literature to guide assessment and intervention for people experiencing mental illness, addressing restrictions to occupational participation

title: OCCUPATIONAL PERSPECTIVES OF HEALTH A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theoretical foundations of communication in occupational therapy and be taught to apply intentional communication skills in a preclinical setting. You will explore diverse understandings of health and wellbeing from different cultural perspectives including First Nations to provide a model of practice based on cultural safety. You will also be taught reflective skills to consider your cultural identity and communicating in ways that reduce cultural bias and support power sharing and cultural safety and humility. You will also address the occupational needs of local and global communities and consider community-cented occupation-based occupational therapy practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply skills in reflection to self and contemporary community issues
Demonstrate collaborative skills with peers and in teams and communicate effectively using culturally safe verbal and non-verbal skills
Apply skills in cultural sensitivity and cultural safety around issues of diversity, equity and justice to conceptualise, plan and act within culturally diverse contexts.
Apply knowledge of core occupational concepts and theories to support health and wellbeing among individuals and communities.

title: ENABLING CHANGE: GROUPWORK IN OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the ways occupational therapists enhance occupational participation through the use of groups. You will learn about group theory, process and development. You will be a member of a training group the purpose of which will be to participate in its activities and to observe its behaviours, and apply group theories learnt in lectures to your observations. During each weekly interactive workshop, you will undertake two roles to enhance your learning. Firstly, you will take on the role of observer/theorist who observes a group, applying your learning to your observations of how a group functions. You will also participate in a group that has an activity focus, during which you will experience belonging to a group. In this role you will study group processes and functioning.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of occupational therapy literature and group techniques in practice to discuss and appraise the role of occupational therapy group work within various health and community services
Reflect on and document, understanding of group behaviour, processes and development in the context of their experience of group leadership and group membership.
Plan, develop and lead a group to apply foundational skills in facilitating groups, demonstrating understanding of group dynamics.

Apply knowledge of theories, principles and techniques related to group intervention strategies within a context relevant to occupational therapy and considering cultural safety and individual experiences.

title: PARTICIPATION IN DIVERSE COMMUNITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will further develop foundational concepts related to occupation through academic learning and placement within a community agency. You will participate in genuine community service with a diverse population, while developing pre-professional knowledge of occupation, community diversity, social participation, experiential learning and the impact of socioeconomic and environmental factors on participation. Service in the community will enable you to build skills in engaging with community stakeholders, critical reflection and professional behaviour. These concepts and skills will provide a foundation for future professional practice in a diverse and changing local and global communities. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of clinical exposure. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as an Occupational Therapist. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional skills in judgement, self organisation, communication and teamwork in professional environments
Apply theoretical knowledge to identify and address needs arising in dynamic environments
Develop and apply core occupational concepts and theories in diverse and changing health contexts
Reflect on personal assumptions in relation to equity, diversity, and social justice through a variety of communication modes

title: PREPARATION FOR OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the occupational therapy practice education program that will continue throughout the course. This will include orientation to the Occupational Therapy Competency standards, and the Student Practice Evaluation Form- Revised (Second edition) (SPEF-R2) used to evaluate occupational therapy students undertaking professional practice placements. You will critically reflect on your own professional self-management skills and your readiness for participation in 1000 hours of professional practice to meet requirements for registration as an occupational therapist. You will understand your responsibility to practice in an ethical, safe and accountable manner. This will include compliance with university and agency requirements. You will continue to develop self-knowledge and build capabilities in cultural responsiveness. You will demonstrate practice behaviours across four conceptual areas of occupational therapy practice: professionalism, knowledge and learning, occupational therapy process and practice and communication. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of how cultural, social and professional boundaries, identities and expectations influence communication as relevant to occupational therapy practice.
Demonstrate the personal skills, capabilities, knowledge and behaviours required to meet the standards expected for participation in professional practice.
Apply models of reflective practice to support professional reasoning in occupational therapy practice.

Appraise and apply professional reasoning skills in occupational therapy to analyse complex cases, apply evidence-based interventions and make informed decisions to promote optimal outcomes for service users.

title: OCCUPATIONAL FOUNDATIONS OF HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theoretical foundations of occupational therapy and the relationship between occupation, health and well-being. Human occupation will be examined using a range of scenarios, integrating key concepts from Kielhofner’s Model of Human Occupation (Taylor, 2017) and the field of occupational science. You will analyse an occupational narrative and develop skills in writing and critical reflection, develop and apply pre-professional skills of self-management, communication, teamwork, cultural safety and reflection within a scenario-based learning environment
learning_outcomes: Communicate with peers using verbal, non-verbal and written skills.
Apply and articulate key concepts of the Model of Human Occupation including: volition, habituation, performance capacity, occupational identity and adaptation and environment.
Appraise occupation-focused research to increase knowledge of occupational concepts
Apply core occupational concepts and theories in diverse and changing health contexts and demonstrate collaborative and teamwork skills

title: ENABLING OCCUPATION PARTICIPATION:  BODY STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION
syllabus_overview: This subject extends and applies knowledge and skills learned in your earlier anatomy and physiology subjects to occupational therapy scenarios in adult and paediatric populations. You will apply your clinical reasoning which incorporates consideration of body function and structure related to lower limb, upper limb, trunk, spine, and brain impairment impacting occupational participation through typical occupational scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in effective communication of assessment and intervention plans applying culturally safe strategies/practice

Apply, critique, and justify assessment and intervention decisions using evidence-based principles relating to impairment of body function, activity limitations and occupational participation for children and adults with complex conditions.
Describe the structure and function of the musculoskeletal and neurological systems within the upper limb, lower limb, trunk (vertebral column), and brain.

title: ENABLING PARTICIPATION: MUSCULOSKELETAL AND NEUROLOGICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will describe, apply and critique principles of assessment and intervention for people with musculoskeletal and neurological conditions that impact on their capacity to participate in occupations. Clinical reasoning skills will be established which will be further developed through subsequent subjects. Intervention principles will focus on the use of meaningful occupation and also incorporate environmental supports (advocacy, organisational change, environmental adaptation).

Design, communicate and justify occupational therapy interventions that are culturally safe with respect to individual, cultural and linguistic diversity for people living with musculoskeletal and neurological conditions using professional reasoning peer-reviewed evidence.

syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will expand and deepen foundational knowledge and skills required to manage complex occupational performance and participation issues. You will extend your ability to articulate the relationship between occupation, health and wellbeing as a core threshold concept for occupational therapy within the context of complex, contemporary practice scenarios.

Collaborate and communicate professional knowledge and reasoning using culturally safe practices to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Evaluate and apply research evidence to complex cases in occupational therapy practice.
Analyse and apply occupational therapy conceptual and practice models to guide practice with individuals with complex health factors.

syllabus_overview: In this subject you will shift your view beyond the occupational challenges facing individuals, to consider the ways in which occupational therapists enable change at the level of communities and populations. The subject focusses on developing your knowledge of health promotion and primary prevention strategies and how these relate to occupational participation, engagement, and building community capacities. You will critically evaluate and appraise existing projects from an evidence-based practice framework. You will also prepare a health promotion and wellbeing project proposal that is community-focused and occupation-based, to address a preventable population health issue.

Integrate knowledge of macro approaches to practical/practice situations
Critically review and evaluate projects targeting national health priorities in relation to occupation, prevention and project management factors, as a part of a team.

This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Independently devise personal learning objectives and assume responsibility for own learning to support the development of skills, knowledge and behaviour for entry-level occupational therapy practice.

Actively and effectively use culturally safe and responsive communication with key stakeholders within a professional context including clear articulation of professional reasoning and recommendations.
Implement a range of evaluation and reflection strategies to make changes to service provision in response to new information.
Analyse and interpret service user occupational performance information and implement effective service provision informed by relevant and contemporary theory, practice knowledge and best evidence.
Competently and autonomously apply professional practice skills in an ethical, safe, lawful and accountable manner to support service user health and wellbeing through occupation.

title: MACRO STRATEGIES FOR ADVANCED PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will shift your view beyond the occupational challenges facing individuals, to consider the ways in which occupational therapists enable change at the level of the service/organisation, community or population. This is referred to as macro level practice. You will focus on gaining knowledge and skills required for your impending role as health practitioners in a rapidly changing health and social policy context. The subject is comprised of three key themes: health promotion and prevention, project management and preparation for contemporary practice. You will apply, critique and reflect upon major subject themes through appraising other projects and planning and conducting your own team-based project. This subject will develop skills in innovation and entrepreneurship, including the ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas, taking calculated risks and creating change to achieve ambitions - now and in the future. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively with a range of stakeholders to manage the project process and present outcomes.
Critically reflect on, and apply advanced professional capacities to successfully lead and influence the project management process.
Integrate and apply understanding of macro approaches to practical/practice situations
Critically reflect on capabilities, challenges and ongoing learning arising in the project management context and communicate these clearly
Evaluate projects that target national health priorities regarding occupation, prevention and project management factors, as part of a team.
Implement, evaluate and communicate project processes and expected outcomes using principles of project management to a range of stakeholders, individually and as part of a team.
Propose, design and justify ethical health projects underpinned by project scoping principles, in consultation with external agencies

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this placement you will integrate occupational therapy specialized knowledge, professional reasoning and professional behaviour within practice. The focus of this placement is on the development of occupational therapy core practice skills and may occur across a range of health, education and social care settings. Your placement will be guided by learning objectives and supervised and assessed by a registered occupational therapist. Professional accreditation requires a minimum of 1000 hours of clinical exposure. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as an occupational therapist. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Independently devise personal learning objectives to support the development of skills, knowledge and behaviour, including continued learning of cultural capabilities for entry-level occupational therapy practice.
Formulate, defend and apply occupational therapy management plans informed by relevant and contemporary theory, practice knowledge and using evidence-based principles.
Communicate effectively with key stakeholders within a professional context,including clear articulation of professional reasoning.
Apply, with increasing autonomy, professional practice skills in an ethical, safe, lawful and accountable manner to support client/ service user health and wellbeing through occupation.
Evaluate and critically reflect on professional practice skills and act on feedback received to generate improved client/ service user outcomes.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to the historical, philosophical and theoretical foundations underpinning the profession of occupational therapy to transition you to your postgraduate studies in the discipline. You will explore the relationship between occupational participation, health and well-being and integrate key concepts from the Model of Human Occupation (Taylor et el., 2024) and occupational science to develop an understanding of humans as occupational beings. Foundational skills in occupational analysis, person-centered intentional communication and facilitating occupational groups will be developed and applied, alongside application of evidence-based practice principles. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the relationship between occupational participation, health and well-being as experienced by yourself and others, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Analyse qualitative data and formulate an occupational profile using the theory of Kielhofner’s Model of Human Occupation
Design, facilitate and evaluate occupationally focused group experiences using principles and processes of occupational analysis and group work.
Illustrate and critique occupational practice skills including reflective practice, intentional communication, goal setting, environmental interventions and documentation.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE C
syllabus_overview: In this placement you will consolidate, apply and further develop your core occupational therapy practice skills in readiness to practice as an entry-level occupational therapist. The focus of this placement is the transition toward independent practice and, where relevant, management of a small caseload. Your placement may occur across a range of health, education and social care settings. Your placement will be guided by learning objectives and supervised and assessed by a registered occupational therapist. Professional accreditation requires a minimum of 1000 hours of clinical exposure. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as an occupational therapist. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Select and implement appropriate methods of information gathering and interpret service user occupational performance information to formulate advanced intervention planning.
Apply advanced culturally safe and responsive communication skills with a wide range of key stakeholders to deliver effective service provision to improve client outcomes.
Design, deliver and document service provision with responsibility and judgement that is informed by relevant and contemporary theory, practice knowledge and using evidence-based principles.
Independently and responsibly manage a caseload and address occupational performance and participation of service users.

Critically evaluate own learning needs to independently devise personal learning objectives to consolidate skills, knowledge and behaviour, including continued cultural capabilities for entry-level occupational therapy practice.
Independently evaluate and adapt service provision by implementing a range of evaluation and reflection strategies to improve client outcomes.

title: RIVER ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop knowledge, understanding and experience of river environments in order to undertake safe journeys in groups. You will examine natural and cultural perspectives, hydrology and ecology directly relevant to selected river environments of south-eastern Australia. Through weekly lectures and fieldwork, you will develop technical expertise of paddling and interpretative knowledge of river environments as preparation for peer leadership.
learning_outcomes: Perform self-rescue, basic rescue of others, and equipment recovery on flat water (Grade 1) or white water (Grade 2).
Critically examine personal, group and safety experiences in river environments.
Establish technical paddling competence on flat water (Grade 1) or white water (Grade 2).
Develop an understanding of ecological, social and cultural knowledge related to selected river environments.

title: READING AUSTRALIAN LANDSCAPES
syllabus_overview: Overview: You are introduced to the processes that shape Australian landscapes. Specific Victorian bioregions are explored to understand influences and interrelationships of climate, ecology, land forming processes and management practices of natural systems. Through practical work, field work and assignments, you will learn to use a range of techniques that will enable them to "read" landscapes from an ecological and an outdoor environmental educator’s perspective.
learning_outcomes: Develop a range of skills that will enable you to read landscapes that draws on lecture presentations, field-based activities and published literature.
Understand and describe the landforms, soils, water properties, biota and cultural history of a selected field site visited in this subject.
Describe the fundamental interrelationships of geology, landforms, soils, water, climate, biota and human influences on the natural environment within specific Australian bioregions.
Demonstrate an understanding of the formational processes that shape Australian landscapes, and the influence of past and present land management practices.

title: ECOLOGIES OF COASTAL ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will focus on environmental studies by understanding, recording, and critically reflecting on coastal environments. You are introduced to the skills of field observation, recording, and communicating natural and cultural stories within coastal environments. The south-eastern Australian coast is a naturally dynamic environment that changes with influences of wind, tides, waves and weather systems. Learning experiences, including practical field trips, develop knowledge and understanding of the complex relationships in coastal environments. You will develop expertise in safely undertaking a multi-day outdoor environmental education trip in a coastal environment.
learning_outcomes: Undertake research into natural and cultural history and communicate these stories
Develop practical knowledge and skills relevant to safely undertaking a multi-day coastal outdoor education experience
