Apply ecological concepts to field observations, recording and reflection in a range of coastal ecosystems
Recognise patterns and relationships in coastal ecosystems and the challenges facing these ecosystems

title: WAYS OF KNOWING NATURE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to ideas and cultural beliefs that shape the way Australians perceive and interact with nature. You will examine and explore connections between ways of experiencing nature and knowledge of places, with an emphasis on implications for outdoor environmental education. You will critically examine human-nature relationships through enquiry, academic writing, problem-solving, and dialogue. The learning experiences, including practical field trips, provide opportunities for the development of naturalist skills and reflections on theory.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate naturalist observation skills through the practice of nature journaling.
Develop skills required for academic study, including written communication; critical thinking and enquiry; research; problem-solving; reading; and, referencing.
Analyse how particular worldviews, influence human nature relationships.
Describe and evaluate theoretical and practical understandings of the ways in which knowledge is developed through outdoor environmental education.

title: JOURNEYS IN RIVER ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop knowledge, understanding and experience of river environments in order to safely conduct effective outdoor environmental education experiences. Through lectures and fieldwork, you will apply place-based pedagogies, technical paddling and rescue skills, environmental interpretation, and group management skills to teach in river environments.
learning_outcomes: Understand and interpret ecological, social & cultural knowledge of selected river environments.
Demonstrate the skills required for the delivery of educationally relevant, place responsive learning experiences in river environments.
Apply leadership, group management, self-rescue, basic rescue of others, and equipment recovery on flat water (Grade 1) and moving water (Grade 2-3).
Reflect on and critically analyse personal and group experiences within river environments.

title: JOURNEYS IN BUSH ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the understanding and skills to undertake extended overnight journeys in bush environments. In doing so, you consolidate outdoor experiential journey skills, environmental literacy, sustainable practice and introductory outdoor leadership that include safety and educative/guiding opportunities. You will further cultivate technical expertise of bush journeys through learning experiences, including practical field trips, to enable safe exploration and promote experiential and interpretative knowledge of bush environments. This includes natural/cultural perspectives, land management, and ecology directly relevant to selected bush environments of south-eastern Australia.
learning_outcomes: Consolidate and further develop outdoor journeys through preparation and participation in a continuous extended journey in south-eastern Australian bush environments
Identify and undertake leadership, group management and guiding/interpretation skills in relation to extended bush journeys in a range of educational and environmental settings
Examine and interpret specific social/cultural/natural perspectives, ecology and land management practices relevant to south-eastern Australian bush environments

title: LEADING GROUPS IN OUTDOOR ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students investigate, evaluate, and apply the theory and practice of small group leadership in the outdoors in relation to outdoor environmental education. Students examine and critique a range of relevant place based, adventure, and education leadership frameworks, alongside components of professional experience that include reflective practice, communication, facilitation, judgement and decision making. Students will analyse and apply these concepts in a range of learning experiences, including practical field trips in outdoor environments.
learning_outcomes: Apply judgement to enable ethical decision-making regarding group safety and facilitation that enhances learning in outdoor environmental education contexts.
Critique and apply theories, models and principles of leadership in the context of peer led field experiences.
Evaluate outdoor leadership, teamwork, group facilitation and instructional frameworks in relation to outdoor environmental education.

title: SAFETY IN OUTDOOR ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students develop competence and gain experience in outdoor leadership and safety within an outdoor environmental education context. Learning experiences, including practical field trips, emphasise knowledge of safety/risk management including the strict aversion to fatalities approach, sound judgement, trip planning, navigation, safety devices, wilderness first aid, mental health and legal liability.
learning_outcomes: Describe and plan for strategies that support students' well-being and safety working within schools and/or the outdoor profession and legislative requirements.
Identify, analyse and plan for safety planning, management and leadership including the strict aversion to fatalities approach in a range of outdoor environmental education contexts.
Demonstrate knowledge, understanding and skills in wilderness first aid and navigation for outdoor environmental education contexts.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF OUTDOOR LEARNING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students are introduced to the knowledge and skills required for safe participation in self-reliant outdoor journeys in south-eastern Australian environments. Learning experiences, including practical field trips, emphasise the development of safe practice, sound judgement, care for others and the environment, preparation, and the ability for students to be self-aware and responsible for their own learning. Students undertake outdoor-based experiential learning with theories, models and concepts that provide the foundations for professional and personal practice in outdoor environmental education.
learning_outcomes: Establish and demonstrate the fundamental approaches and frameworks that develop effective personal/professional skills in the context of journeying in outdoor environments

Identify and develop foundational practical and theoretical experiential skills and knowledge to develop an understanding of environments utilised in the context of outdoor journeys in south-eastern Australia

Instigate key components of sound judgement, participation in groups, care for others and the environment, sustainable practice, and safe practice as participants in outdoor experiences including bushwalking and navigation
Critique and interpret a range of outdoor environmental education experiences in the context of personal learning and future practice

title: PROGRAMMING AND SAFETY IN OUTDOOR EDUCATION
syllabus_overview: You will plan and undertake a supervised outdoor environmental teaching practice, and a negotiated programme of field experience to extend your outdoor environmental education preparation. You will learn to prepare programme plans, including safety plans informed by a study of serious incidents. You will undertake an agreed applied learning experience, which may include advanced skill development, work integrated learning and/or peer trip leading.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate development of an experience profile, informed self-appraisal, and critical judgement relevant to student career goals
Develop knowledge of programme implementation for effective outdoor environmental education experiences
Understand, plan, and practice safe and impactful pedagogies in introductory outdoor environmental education experiences
Demonstrate depth of understanding in relation to managing safety and serious incidents in outdoor environments

title: TEACHING IN BUSH ENVIRONMENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply and extend bushwalking and environmental interpretation knowledge to conduct pedagogically sound outdoor environmental education experiences. In doing so, you consolidate outdoor experiential journey skills, environmental literacy, sustainable practices, outdoor leadership, pedagogy, safety, and create educative/guiding opportunities. You will synthesise expertise of bush journeys through learning experiences, including practical field trips, to enable safe exploration and promote experiential and interpretative knowledge of bush environments in south-eastern Australia.
learning_outcomes: Understand, plan, implement and practice safe and pedagogically sound educational experiences incorporating specific approaches to safety, leadership, group management and social/cultural/ecological justice issues in a range of south-eastern Australian bush environments
Interpret and teach specific local social/cultural/natural perspectives, ecology and land management practices relevant to south-eastern Australian bush environments
Critically evaluate programme design and demonstrate an informed self-appraisal of personal teaching experience

title: ECOLOGIES OF OUTDOOR LEARNING
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, students will study ecological approaches to education, curriculum development and learning ecologies, and apply these to outdoor environmental education teaching, programme planning, and evaluation. Students plan, implement and evaluate an innovative outdoor programme with considered application of outdoor environmental education disciplinary skills, knowledge, understanding, and ecologies of practice. In this subject, students will gain experience in how to create innovative ideas for developing and teaching outdoor environmental education programmes, including how to develop initial ideas, apply them in practical settings, take account of opportunities and risks associated with these innovative approaches, and evaluate their outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively with peers, agency and university staff and students in a flexible and creative manner.

Critically reflect on and evaluate theoretical perspectives of ecological learning and teaching practice, programme design, implementation and evaluation and be able to apply these to real world situations.

Design, plan, fully develop and implement a safe, innovative, and educationally coherent outdoor environmental education programme in collaboration with an external agency, taking account of identified opportunities and risks.

title: INTRODUCTION TO CLINICAL PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this clinical placement subject, you'll develop professional and technical skills under close supervision by clinical educators. You'll work with adult and child patients, building on what you learned in Year one. You'll analyse clinical information, create personalized care plans, and learn about minimal intervention strategies and infection control. We'll also cover behavioural change techniques and communication skills to enhance patient outcomes. We emphasise reflective practice for ongoing personal and professional growth. You'll develop self-reflection skills and apply them in your clinical work
learning_outcomes: Identify systemic and other health conditions from patients' medical histories and presentations impacting oral structures

Apply the principles and practices of infection control, diagnostic investigation, and preventive care, in the clinical environment with respect to the provision of clinical care and non-complex management of oral diseases.

Analyse the implications for treatment and oral health care which arise from the effects of therapeutic drugs, their impact on patient management and appropriate application to the clinical environment.
Demonstrate continual improvement and clinical practice through self-reflection and appraisal.

title: INTRODUCTION TO CLINICAL PRACTICE AND HEALTH PROMOTION B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you'll enhance your clinical skills with support from your clinical educators, you'll improve in managing both adult and child patients within your scope of practice. You'll analyse clinical information to create personalised care plans and apply infection control practices. You'll also learn communication techniques to better help patients. As you progress, you'll become more skilled in reflecting on your practice. Additionally, you'll explore health promotion principles and create a hypothetical health promotion plan for a community.
learning_outcomes: Identify systemic and other health conditions from patients' medical histories and presentations impact oral structures.
Demonstrate continual improvement of personal and clinical practice through self-reflection and appraisal.

Explain how health determinants including risk factors and behaviours influencing oral diseases and inform the planning oral health programmes for different communities based on their needs and demands.

Analyse the implications for treatment and oral health care which arise from the effects of therapeutic drugs, their impact on patient management and appropriate application to the clinical environment.

Apply the principles and practices of infection control, diagnostic investigation, preventive and restorative care, in the clinical environment with respect to the provision of person centered care, care planning process and non-complex management of oral diseases.

title: ADVANCED ORAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on advanced oral health for populations with special needs. It emphasises skills in diagnoses, management and planning for clients with special needs. Interdisciplinary practices are honed for competent, holistic patient-centred care.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours.
Implement and critically evaluate advanced diagnostic strategies in populations with special needs, promoting optimal oral health outcomes.
Deliver oral health care with an understanding of behaviour management techniques, adapting to diverse patient needs.
Facilitate oral care services in collaboration with other health professionals, demonstrating an understanding of disability issues.
Accurately diagnose oral health conditions in patients with special needs, formulating comprehensive, patient-centred management plans in collaboration with other healthcare providers.

title: INTERDISCIPLINARY HEALTH PROMOTION
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject deepens understanding of the elements of oral health, integrating advanced periodontal and restorative clinical skills, with a focus on populations with special needs. Students will consolidate their skills in diagnosis, management, and interdisciplinary healthcare, particularly in non-clinical settings, preparing for success in diverse clinical environments.
learning_outcomes: Formulate detailed, evidence-based care plans for adults, paediatric patients or special needs patients in collaboration with other healthcare professionals, considering systemic health impacts and patient preferences.
Critique comprehensive diagnostic, periodontal, and restorative techniques in the management of oral health for adults, including aged and special needs care.
Demonstrate personal and professional behaviours.
Comprehend the theoretical principles of behaviour management in diverse environments

title: PREVENTIVE HEALTH CARE
syllabus_overview: This subject centres on advanced preventive oral health, prioritising proficiency in health promotion, diagnosis, and management planning for paediatric and special needs patients. It encompasses clinical treatment in rural settings and orthodontic care. Emphasis is placed on developing culturally sensitive practices to deliver competent, holistic, person-centred care.
learning_outcomes: Deliver oral health care with a deep understanding of cultural sensitivity, especially in rural settings, adapting to diverse patient needs.
Demonstrate communication, leadership, and critical reflection skills in line with the Australian Dental Council's competencies for newly graduated oral health therapists.
Implement and critically evaluate advanced preventive care strategies in paediatric and populations with special needs, promoting optimal oral health outcomes.
Accurately diagnose oral health conditions in children and patients with special needs, formulating comprehensive, patient-centred management plans.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL SKILLS
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, students will further their understanding of adult oral health, incorporating advanced periodontal and restorative clinical skills with a specific focus on elderly and special needs populations. They will consolidate their proficiency in diagnosis, management, and health promotion, with a particular emphasis on rural settings, in preparation for leadership roles across diverse clinical environments.
learning_outcomes: Exhibit advanced communication, leadership, and evaluative skills, fulfilling the Australian Dental Council's professional competencies for oral health care delivery.
Provide culturally sensitive care, demonstrating autonomy and adaptability in diverse clinical environments.
Formulate and execute detailed, evidence-based care plans for adults, considering systemic health impacts and patient preferences.
Integrate and apply comprehensive diagnostic, periodontal, and restorative techniques in the management of oral health for adults, including aged and special needs care.

title: GLOBAL PERSPECTIVES IN ORAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain insight in dimensions of cultures, and you will explore your role as an oral health therapist in a diverse society. You will analyse and further your own cultural competence through an elective regional, interstate, or overseas placement and through participation in a virtual cross-cultural learning activity. You will explore issues of access to oral health care and inequalities in care based on socio-economic status, culture, and age. This subject addresses La Trobe's Global Citizenship Essential, being able to recognise the global context of equity and oral health concepts.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical reflection, and professional self-management through analysis of own beliefs, values, and perceptions.
Interpret values of fairness, social justice, and inequalities based on gender, socio-economic status, culture, religion, age, access to care and other issues particularly related to oral health.
Evaluate dimensions of culture to improve cross-cultural communication skills, particularly related to oral health.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF ORTHOPTIC PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Students will be introduced to the foundational conceptual framework for safe clinical practice in this subject. Students will be supported to develop basic practical skills required for person-centred care and a preliminary understanding of the clinical reasoning process in the context of evidence-based practice. Students will be assisted to develop an understanding of the interpersonal, safe work principles, infection control and ethical and risk mitigation requirements of the clinical environment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse clinical cases applying introductory clinical reasoning
Identify ethical issues in relation to orthoptic practice
Working individually or in a team, communicate discipline knowledge to diverse lay and professional audiences based on clinical data
Explain the processes of infection control in clinical and surgical assisting environments and identify risk mitigation strategies to reduce potential adverse effects in clinical settings
Apply safe work principles to ensure safe clinical practice and engage in team collaboration to develop interpersonal skills and working strategies.

title: BINOCULAR VISION
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the fundamental physiological principals of ocular movement and binocular single vision. You will develop an understanding of the general characteristics of binocular single vision and of the sensory consequences of the abnormal visual experience. The characteristics of strabismus and the relationship between accommodation and strabismus will also be introduced. You will gain experience in the use of orthoptic instruments in the assessment of the normal ranges of ocular motility and binocular vision as a preliminary to the assessment, diagnosis and management of patients with orthoptic problems.
learning_outcomes: Explain the anatomical, physiological and optical principles underlying coordinated eye movements.
Clearly and effectively communicate instructions and information to patients within a simulated clinical context.
Analyse the relationship between accommodation and vergence and explain its influence on ocular alignment and binocular vision.
Demonstrate an understanding of ocular alignment and binocular single vision and the sensory - motor elements necessary to attain and maintain these.
Identify and categorise the different types of strabismus and synthesise the functional and sensory consequences associated with anomalies of motor function.
Accurately and safely administer, record and interpret observations and test outcomes to diagnose anomalies of ocular alignment and binocular vision.

title: OPTICS AND REFRACTIVE STATE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students are introduced to the optical principles of the refractive system of the eye. The physics of light and the principles of physical optics are integrated with the ocular system, including its refractive errors and physiological defects. Emphasis will be placed on developing students' abilities to propose causes of the various refractive errors and their respective optical management. The theoretical content and the clinical investigatory skills of lens measurement, vision assessment and optical prescription reporting will also be taught.
learning_outcomes: Explain how the normal healthy eye can compensate for optical errors to improve vision.
Describe the different types of refractive errors of the eye, their causes and patients symptoms
Describe the underpinning optical principles in managing a patient's refractive error, relating the patient's visual requirements for normal activity.
Analyse physical data and explain the behaviour of light
Perform vision testing and communicate results to others.
Explain to patients how their glasses will correct their refractive error.

title: EYE ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: Students will study the anatomy and physiology of the internal and external structures of the eye, including the physiology of intraocular pressure, accommodation and pupil responses. The process of visual image formation will be explored in terms of specific aspects of retinal anatomy and physiology introducing students to the concepts of visual acuity, contrast sensitivity and colour vision. The anatomy of the visual pathway from retina to cortex and its relationship to basic visual defects will be introduced as part of this subject.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the relationship of ocular anatomy and physiology to sight
Demonstrate the assessment of contrast sensitivity and colour vision on a patient and interpret the preliminary findings
Describe the normal structure and function of the eye and the anatomical organisation including the clear media and internal and external structures
Describe the processes of normal visual acuity, contrast sensitivity and colour vision
Define and correctly use anatomical and physiological terms as they relate to the eye
Describe the normal visual pathway from the retina to the visual cortex using correct anatomical terminology

title: CONCOMITANT STRABISMUS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on concepts presented in Binocular Vision. You will develop an understanding of the theoretical concepts of aetiology, investigation, diagnosis and management of paediatric eye movement disorders and in particular concomitant strabismus and its sensory anomalies. You will integrate theoretical concepts with practical instrumentation and clinical techniques to apply optical, orthoptic, medical and surgical management for these disorders in an evidence-based medical context. This subject includes clinical placement equivalent to 5 days. Attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting minimum requirements for workplace experience and professional accreditation.
learning_outcomes: Analyse relevant clinical data to differentially diagnose concomitant strabismus
Justify the selection of appropriate clinical investigations of concomitant strabismus
Apply safe clinical assessments for patients with concomitant strabismus
Develop treatment plans using best available evidence appropriate for managing concomitant strabismus

title: OCULAR PATHOLOGY A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will extend your knowledge of concepts related to anatomy and physiology of the eye in order to understand a range of ocular conditions affecting the anterior segment of the eye with particular focus on vision and refractive status impact. Foundation knowledge of optics and refractive errors is expanded in this subject to include the investigation and optical repair of refractive errors in both adult and paediatric populations. You will be introduced to the diagnostic procedures required to investigate an anterior segment eye condition and undertake refraction including interpretation of the findings and develop an understanding of advantages and limitations of optical management for various conditions when applicable. You will be equipped to prescribe corrective lenses
learning_outcomes: Discuss potential management options for ophthalmic conditions involving eyelids, clear media and associated structures.
Combine patients' signs and symptoms together with other clinical data to offer provisional diagnoses in relation to the anterior segment and refractive status.

Using appropriate investigative techniques, review and analyse observed changes in ocular anatomy and physiology leading to eye diseases affecting the anterior segment and explain their impact on vision and refractive status.

Evaluate patients' signs and symptoms and communicate an initial differential diagnoses of various ophthalmic conditions which affect the anterior segment and its possible impact on refractive status.

title: OCULAR PATHOLOGY C
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will extend your knowledge of concepts related to anatomy and physiology of the eye in order to understand a range of ocular conditions, with a focus on, but not limited to, the posterior segment of the eye. Ocular conditions include vascular disease, retinal disease, ocular trauma, optic neuropathies, neoplasms and uveitis. During the course of this subject, you will be required to perform investigative techniques to identify and measure the pathology and integrate patient information to lead to a differential diagnosis. These investigative techniques include ophthalmoscopy in addition to ocular imaging techniques. This subject will equip you to progress to the subject Ocular Management and Rehabilitation.
learning_outcomes: Analyse patient signs and symptoms to formulate and communicate appropriate clinical investigation strategies.
Apply investigative techniques to a given patient presentation to develop an accurate and evidence-based provisional diagnosis of ocular conditions.
Apply appropriate investigative techniques and demonstrate proficient use of ophthalmic equipment to measure and document eye disease processes
Investigate and analyse ocular disease of the uveal tract and posterior segment.

title: OCULAR PATHOLOGY B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will extend your knowledge of concepts related to anatomy and physiology of the eye in order to understand a range of ocular pathology, with a particular focus on cataract and glaucoma. You will be required to perform a range of investigative techniques to identify pathology and integrate patient information to lead to a differential diagnosis. You will undertake clinical placement as part of the requirements for this subject. Professional Accreditation requires all competencies be met as defined by the Australian Orthoptic Board. Successful completion of clinical placement during this subject facilitates meeting these clinical competencies. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate clinical practice and critically reflect on one’s own performance in an orthoptic clinical setting.
Synthesise knowledge to diagnose and differentiate between various types or stages of cataract and glaucoma based on clinical presentation, risk factors, diagnostic tests, and imaging modalities.
Demonstrate proficiency in using diagnostic tools commonly employed in the investigation of cataract and glaucoma.
Analyse changes in the ocular anatomy and physiology of the eye to identify clinical manifestations associated with cataract and glaucoma.

title: EYE MOVEMENT DISORDERS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be supported to build on concepts presented in the subjects Neuro-ophthalmology and Incomitant Strabismus. You will broaden your understanding of disorders of the sensory and motor visual pathways. Within this context, neurological control, pathways and functions of the different types of eye movement systems will be studied in detail. You will be given the opportunity to integrate theoretical concepts and clinical techniques to interpret clinical findings for the diagnosis and management of eye movement disorders.
learning_outcomes: Independently interpret assessments of patients with neurological disorders to determine the integrity of eye movement systems.
Interpret clinical findings to formulate differential diagnoses and inform further management.
Interpret patient data in relation to eye movement disorders and communicate these findings clearly and coherently to patients and other health professionals.
Apply clinical reasoning and critical thinking skills to clinical scenarios.
Justify the selection of investigative assessments for patients with neurological disorders

title: INCOMITANT STRABISMUS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on concepts presented in the subjects Binocular Vision, and Concomitant Strabismus. You will develop an understanding of the aetiology, investigation, diagnosis, and management of incomitant strabismus and associated sensory consequences. You will integrate theoretical concepts with practical instrumentation and clinical techniques to apply optical, orthoptic, medical and surgical management for various types of strabismus in an evidence based medical context with multidisciplinary provisions (incorporating ophthalmology, neurology, radiology and endocrinology).
learning_outcomes: Investigate patients with incomitant strabismus safely
Apply best available evidence to develop management plans appropriate for incomitant strabismus
Analyse clinical data to provide a differential diagnosis for incomitant strabismus
Justify appropriate clinical investigations for incomitant strabismus and related sensory consequences

title: NEURO OPHTHALMOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on your understanding of normal ocular and neurological anatomy and physiology. You will utilise and apply your knowledge about the human visual system in order to identify, examine and diagnose colour vision anomalies, pupillary disorders and visual field defects. With this knowledge you will be able to predict the likely site of a lesion along the visual pathway based on a series of patient symptoms and signs. You will integrate theoretical concepts with practical instrumentation and clinical techniques to interpret clinical findings for the diagnosis and management of retinal or neuro-ophthalmic colour vision or pupillary anomalies and visual field defects
learning_outcomes: Clearly communicate, instruct and monitor patients with retinal or neurological complaints during their assessments, and appropriately utilise colour vision, pupillary and visual field test processes to achieve the most reliable results.
Record, interpret and discuss test findings with colleagues and report findings to patients using contextually sensitive terminology.
Independently plan and perform assessments of patients with headaches and neurological disorders to determine the integrity of their visual pathway including the pupillary pathway.
Determine the likely site of a retinal pathway lesion based on the pupillary outcomes and visual field defect to select appropriate further testing, management and urgency.
Select and accurately perform a pupillary assessment and a variety of visual field tests appropriate to patient requirements dependent on their presenting symptoms, signs and condition.

title: OCULAR MANAGEMENT AND THERAPEUTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will integrate your understanding of ocular disease and investigation with the principles of ophthalmic management. You will build upon your knowledge of general pharmacological principles and apply these to ocular-specific drugs used for investigation, diagnosis and management of ophthalmic disorders. Using the most recent evidence for screening and treatment, you will integrate theoretical concepts with clinical techniques to describe the most appropriate ophthalmic management. This subject will also teach you the skills required for surgical assisting, including aseptic techniques and sterilization in addition to the skill of biometry for cataract surgery. Professional Accreditation requires all competencies as defined by the Australian Orthoptic Board should be met. Clinical placement facilitates meeting these competencies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to practice safely by correctly using appropriate aseptic techniques and personal protective equipment in the sterile environment relevant for in-rooms and in-theatre surgical procedures.
Effectively communicate your understanding of recent research related to ophthalmic treatment to your peers.
Demonstrate clinical and legislative understanding of the use of ophthalmic drugs and accurately record drug information in a patient’s electronic medical record.
Integrate and interpret the investigation of a patient to form a diagnosis and undertake effective clinical ophthalmic management of a patient.

Show competency in effective clinical management of a patient with cataract by competently performing optical biometry, interpreting the results in preparation for cataract surgery and providing post-operative monitoring.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE ORTHOPTICS A
syllabus_overview: This subject is one of three final year professional practicum subjects. Dependent on the allocated placement, students will focus on different specialized areas of practice. Supervised clinical practice occurs across one or multiple placement sites. Clinical practicums in this subject are organised outside of normal teaching weeks and include opportunity to travel to non-metropolitan areas, interstate or internationally. In this subject, students will begin refining their clinical and professional skills with the aim of achieving entry level competencies as required for professional recognition as an orthoptist. Attendance at professional placements will also contribute to meeting minimum requirements for workplace experience and professional accreditation. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse complex clinical problems to develop appropriate management solutions in a specialized area of practice
Evaluate complex cases to determine accurate diagnoses in a specialized area of practice.
Reflect on personal professional practice to improve patient outcomes
Effectively communicate a diagnosis and educational or health promotion information to patients and caregivers in a specialized area of practice.
Clearly communicate management plans based on best available evidence
Interpret clinical information in a specialized area of practice for patients, their family and colleagues
Practice with judgement and responsibility in a specialized area of professional practice

title: SPECIALIST LOW VISION CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of the epidemiology, causes and impact of vision impairment and psychosocial impact of irreversible vision loss. Using patient case scenarios, you will integrate theoretical concepts with clinical techniques to apply optical, non-optical and technological aids in the management and rehabilitation of patients with low vision. You will learn about the relevant government bodies, service providers and support service options for patients with low vision. You will develop the skills and knowledge to provide low vision services in a low vision agency. You will also learn how to work in an independent low vision orthoptic practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply initiative to adapt and evaluate low vision investigations
Develop and clearly communicate interdisciplinary management plans that integrate community resources to support people with vision loss.
Integrate knowledge of ocular functions with clinical findings to explain functional vision and potential psychosocial impacts.
Evaluate the effectiveness of treatments and interventions to provide ethical solutions to vision problems.
Design low vision services intervention with consideration of incorporating relevant legal and and ethical guidelines, duty of care and scope of practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE ORTHOPTICS B
syllabus_overview: In this final-year professional practicum subject, students will further consolidate, integrate and enhance their knowledge in theoretical concepts and clinical principles in order to investigate, diagnose and manage patients with ocular disorders. Students are in supervised clinical settings across one or multiple sites. Students will also undertake observational surgical placement in this subject. Opportunity to travel to non-metropolitan or international locations to undertake placements is possible. In this subject, students undertake independent learning activities and are required to meet entry level competencies necessary for professional recognition as an orthoptist. Attendance at professional placements will also contribute to meeting minimum requirements for workplace experience and professional accreditation. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on personal professional practice to improve patient outcomes.
Justify and clearly communicate surgical and non-surgical management plans based on best available evidence
Evaluate complex cases and determine accurate diagnoses in specialized areas of practice.
Effectively communicate a diagnosis and education or health promotion information in a specialized area of practice
Justify and interpret clinical information in a specialized area of practice for patients, their family and colleagues
Practice with judgement and responsibility in a specialized area of professional practice
Review and analyse complex clinical problems and develop appropriate management solutions (including surgical and non-surgical) in a specialized area of practice

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE ORTHOPTICS C
syllabus_overview: In this final-year professional practicum subject, students will extend their clinical skills and consolidate their professional identity by building on their experience of consulting patients of different ages and cultural backgrounds. Students are in supervised clinical practice across one or multiple sites and during this time will also undertake independent learning activities. Clinical practicums may be organised outside of normal teaching weeks and include the opportunity to travel and undertake non-metropolitan, rural and international placements. In this subject, students will further refine entry level competencies. Attendance at professional placements will also contribute to meeting minimum requirements for workplace experience and professional accreditation.This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on personal professional practice to support continuous improvement in patient outcomes
Evaluate complex cases to formulate accurate diagnoses
Interpret clinical information in a specialized area of practice for patients, their family and colleagues
Analyse complex clinical problems and develop appropriate management solutions
Effectively communicate diagnoses and education or health promotion information suitable for patients and caregivers in specialized practice settings.
Clearly communicate management plans based on best available evidence
Practice with judgement and responsibility in a specialized area of professional practice

title: EVIDENCE BASED ORTHOPTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build knowledge and skills necessary to design, critically evaluate and implement evidence-based practices in the orthoptic clinical settings to promote high-quality, patient-centred care. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of translational research through participation in the process of inquiry and will be involved in problem formulation, research design, data collection and synthesis. Students will also consider the clinical relevance of outcomes and the ethics of clinical research.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate clinical knowledge and identify gaps to adapt for best available evidence.
Apply research methodologies to design a research project.
Generate and evaluate evidence-based hypotheses of relevance to the field of orthoptic practice
Translate research findings into practical recommendations for clinical practice

title: LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT IN ORTHOPTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will be prepared to make an effective contribution in an evolving health care environment. Students will be introduced to the Australian healthcare landscape and examine decision making influences in clinical practice, including ethical considerations.Students will also be introduced to private practice business essentials including marketing, strategic management, funding models for allied health services, and responsible leadership and apply these to the development of a business plan. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the ethical consequences of business decisions within the context of orthoptic practice.
Proficiently communicate business concepts within the framework of establishing an orthoptic private practice.
Examine regulatory compliance and clinical practice operations within the Australian health system, applying this to the development of a comprehensive business plan.
Justify financial decisions related to the establishment of an orthoptic clinic
Evaluate Australian funding initiatives, applying them strategically to optimise orthoptic services and provide effective support to patients in the orthoptic practice
Apply business leadership,practice management and strategic marketing principles to establish a successful private orthoptic clinic.

title: HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject you gain knowledge in systems physiology, including the nervous system, muscle tissue, endocrinology and the gastrointestinal system. We will discuss how the nervous system controls body systems, focusing on the electrical transmission of information and how this is modulated. Our focus then shifts to muscle tissue and the mechanisms involved in skeletal muscle contraction, force generation and fatigue. You will gain a detailed understanding of the endocrine system and how it is responsible for controlling many of our bodies daily functions and metabolism. The semester concludes focusing on the gastrointestinal systems where you will gain an understanding of the mechanisms surrounding food digestion and nutrient absorption. The detailed online resources in this subject will be supported by a comprehensive program of enquiry based workshops. Practical classes will allow you to undertake experiments to enhance your learning experience, whilst building on communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Effectively and professionally communicate experimental observations and the conclusions drawn from them individually or as part of a team.
Analyse and integrate experimentally-obtained physiological data with knowledge of basic physiological principles.
Predict how the nervous, muscle, endocrine and gastrointestinal systems of the human body function both during normal physiological conditions and under pathological stress

title: HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject you gain knowledge in systems physiology, including the heart, blood, immune, renal, respiratory and acid-base systems. We discuss how the heart is mechanical pump, followed by how blood vessels control blood flow and pressure. Our focus then shifts to the blood and mechanisms involved in developing immunity. You will gain a detailed understanding of the renal system and how it clears the body of waste while also being an important regulator of blood pressure. The respiratory system then becomes our focus where you will gain understanding of breathing mechanisms and how gasses are transported around the body. We conclude focusing on how the body regulates pH using both renal and respiratory buffers. The detailed online resources in this subject are supported by a comprehensive program of enquiry based workshops. Practical classes will allow you to undertake experiments to enhance your learning experience, whilst building on communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and integrate experimentally-obtained physiological data with knowledge of basic physiological principles.
Effectively and professionally communicate experimental observations and the conclusions drawn from them individually or as part of a team.
Predict how the immune, cardiovascular, renal and respiratory systems of the human body function both during normal physiological conditions and under pathological stress

title: HUMAN STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the basic concepts and principles of both structure (anatomy) and function (physiology) of the human body. Your learning in this subject will be supported by detailed online resources and a comprehensive program of online workshops with expert facilitators. You will also engage in career exploration activities, and begin building your career ready eportfolio.
learning_outcomes: Describe your desired career path, as well as the skills and attributes that employers are seeking in graduates, and reflect on your career planning
Relate the anatomical organisation of selected systems of the body to their physiological function
Work collaboratively to communicate basic physiological and anatomical principles to your peers
Explain how selected systems of the body are controlled to maintain normal function

title: FIRST NATIONS HEALTH FOR PARAMEDICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the foundation knowledge and skills required to work effectively and safely with Australian First Nations peoples in the healthcare environment. You will explore key features and concepts related to traditional and contemporary First Nations cultures and communities; multi- dimensional models of First Nations health and healing; and the underlying social determinants influencing current health outcomes, including historical and cultural factors. You will also explore concepts related to health inequality, reflect on the responsibility of the whole health system in improving First Nations health outcomes, and consider how culturally safe paramedicine practice can contribute to closing the gap in Indigenous health disadvantage. The concepts of honouring First Nations knowledge, strength-based approaches, and evidenced-based learning are strongly reinforced throughout the subject. This subject has been designed to align with the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Curriculum Framework.
learning_outcomes: Describe First Nations concepts of health and healing, and analyse how interconnected physical, social, historical, political and cultural factors impact on health outcomes.
Describe the key features of Australian First Nations culture and history, and apply an understanding of diversity within the First Nations population to person-centred care.
Explain the meaning of 'cultural safety' in relation to improving health outcomes for First Nations people and analyse how it influences effective paramedic practices, and health service delivery.

Engage in culturally appropriate communication that facilitates respectful therapeutic relationships, and supports effective partnerships with First Nations health professionals, organisations and communities.
Outline the concepts of health inequality, the factors that contribute to it, and ways of redressing it to close the gap in health outcomes between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians.

title: HEAD, NECK ANATOMY & NEUROANATOMY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, anatomical principles will be applied to the detailed study of head, neck and neuroanatomy. Topic materials will be presented face to face and online lectures, videoclips and worksheets, but you will be responsible for your own learning through supported face to face practical activities and online workshops, including examination of appropriate cadaver materials. Emphasis is placed on the application of anatomical principles to correlate structure with function in developing an understanding of the basis of everyday activities and related clinical problems.
learning_outcomes: Use available anatomical resources to competently identify a given anatomical structure and assess it in a clinical context. Anatomical structures will be presented either as an image or in situ, and evaluate its orientation and operation within the body.
Independently source, assimilate and appraise basic anatomical principles relating to head and neck anatomy.
Work collaboratively with peers in a small group to complete an anatomy report

Independently source, assimilate and appraise basic anatomical principles relating to neuroanatomy. Analyse the neural pathways and develop the basic clinical skills to understand the neurological disorders.

title: LEGAL AND ETHICAL PRACTICE IN PARAMEDICINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the ethical and legal dimensions of paramedic practice, focusing on forming a professional identity that integrates ethical obligations and legal responsibilities essential to healthcare. You will explore key ethical frameworks and principles, gain skills to navigate and resolve ethical dilemmas and understand relevant health-related legislation, codes of conduct and standards, such as the National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards governing paramedic practice. Through theoretical knowledge and practical application, you will learn to apply these frameworks, laws, standards and codes in various scenarios to ensure safe and ethical patient care. Real-world case studies will be analysed to develop your ability to identify and address ethical and legal issues effectively, equipping you with the foundational knowledge and skills to uphold professional standards and provide high-quality care as a future paramedic.
learning_outcomes: Analyse simple real-world scenarios to identify ethical and legal issues and propose appropriate responses based on ethical frameworks, relevant legislation and professional standards.
Explore ethical frameworks and principles of decision-making processes in real-world interprofessional healthcare scenarios through a professional paramedic-specific paradigm.
Describe the importance of forming a professional identity as a registered paramedic that integrates ethical obligations and legal responsibilities in healthcare practice.
Identify the relevant health-related legislation, regulations, standards and code of conduct that govern paramedic practice.

title: FOUNDATIONS OF PARAMEDIC PRACTICE 2
syllabus_overview: You will be provided with a theoretical framework that underpins the paramedic systematic approach to an incident and this will prepare you for further paramedic clinical content. Several clinical concepts will be presented, including safety and wellbeing, the paramedic clinical approach, clinical reasoning and pathophysiology and clinical procedures relating to airway and respiratory status, perfusion and alterations in consciousness.
learning_outcomes: Determine the physiological status of a range of simulated patients through demonstrated correct use of standard assessment techniques.
Describe, provide a rationale for, and implement appropriate airway and unconscious patient management techniques for simulated patients in a variety of settings.
Recognise potential hazards at simulated paramedic response scenes and describe techniques to eliminate or minimise these hazards
Describe the principles underpinning the standard paramedic approach to an incident and implement appropriate measures to simulated patients in correct sequence.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PARAMEDIC PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn techniques and processes essential to patient assessment, and you will be introduced to history taking and decision-making techniques. You will learn the principles of basic life support, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, basic airway management and initial care of a patient in actual life threat. Safe workplace practices, including manual handling, will be covered. The subject will facilitate the integration of your individual and team communication skills into practice.
learning_outcomes: Determine the physiological status of simulated patients using standard assessment techniques and evidence-based practice methods.
Communicate and assimilate available information to approach simulated incidents to provide effective, safe management of the scene and patient.
Use problem-solving skills and professional judgement to apply appropriate basic life support management to simulated patients.
Assess common paramedic situations to prepare self and equipment for paramedic response.
Employ effective situational judgement to communicate effectively for safe patient management in simulated environments.
Use problem-solving and critical thinking to perform effective and safe lifting, manoeuvring and infection control techniques in simulated clinical situations.

title: COMMUNICATION SKILLS IN PARAMEDICINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be provided with a strong foundation in the principles, methods, and application of communication skills required in paramedicine. You will be able to identify and differentiate between a range of counselling and communication skills, and will be able to successfully apply the appropriate skills to a number of simulated cases. The subject will introduce communication requirements specific to paramedicine, and it is expected you will integrate these skills in the classroom and during concurrent and future industry placements.
learning_outcomes: Communicate assimilated health information clearly and appropriately to different population groups.
Identify and discuss barriers to successful communication and formulate plans to overcome them in diverse settings.
Competently employ an empathetic approach while conveying life altering information to both individuals and groups.
Negotiate crisis interventions effectively using advanced verbal and non-verbal communication strategies.
Discuss and apply a number of communication and counselling techniques to both critical and non-critical case simulations relevant to paramedic paramedic practice.

title: COMPLEX TRAUMA MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn the underpinning pathophysiology associated with traumatic injuries including to the head, chest and spine, and burn injuries affecting body structure and function. You will build upon your existing knowledge of clinical approach, patient assessment and management and the clinical decision-making process, and apply this knowledge in the workshops and objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) style simulation scenarios. Communication techniques appropriate to specific trauma patient presentations will be refined and further developed. Emphasis will be placed on the development of rationales for patient management techniques in complex situations where the level of physical trauma is significant.
learning_outcomes: Identify and evaluate the underpinning pathophysiology, including relevant clinical signs and symptoms related to trauma
Competently complete trauma specific patient assessments and determine criticality status
Assess current evidence based clinical practice approaches for use in trauma management and apply clinical reasoning for their applications in a range of situations
Effectively implement the management of a patient presenting with specific trauma conditions, both individually and as part of a team

title: GERONTOLOGY FOR PARAMEDICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about a range of medical conditions associated with ageing and will examine current knowledge of the pathophysiology of ageing, the meaning of ageing, and challenges affecting those who reach advanced ages. Out of hospital management of geriatric patients will be considered, and the physical, psychosocial and psychological aspects relating to ageing will be debated and applied to simulated learning experiences. You will also combine theoretical knowledge with practical skills to effectively manage geriatric patients with a range of long-term medical conditions necessitating specialised and extended care measures. Particular emphasis is placed on decision making, communication, and problem-solving skills integral to the management of this population group.
learning_outcomes: Integrate professional knowledge and skills to effectively communicate with, and care for, elderly patients and their caregivers both individually and collaboratively as part of a team
Critically appraise and debate the physiological, psychosocial, and emotional/mental challenges associated with elderly populations.
Evaluate and justify the assessment and management of a patient's condition using a paramedic decision making process.
Analyse and formulate plans to promote and support the health literacy of elderly individuals and their caregivers.
Formulate approaches to appropriately assess, monitor, and manage elderly patients needing care in prehospital settings.

title: INTEGRATED CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY
syllabus_overview: This subject further develops your understanding of the diversity and complexity of cardiac and respiratory patient presentations. You will have the opportunity to integrate these concepts and skills into practice while on clinical placement in a range of healthcare settings. Your placements enable critical thinking, reflection and application of patient clinical assessments and management strategies for the cardiac and respiratory patients.
learning_outcomes: Assess current evidence based clinical practice approaches for use in clinical management and critique their application in a range of clinical situations
Identify and evaluate the underpinning cardiac and respiratory pathophysiology, including relevant clinical signs and symptoms
Determine and perform roles and responsibilities in paramedic services and other areas of the emergency health system under general supervision

Accurately formulate and refine clinical management plans, by applying pathophysiology, clinical assessment and patient condition trend recognition skills, for a range of cardiac and respiratory conditions

title: INTEGRATED MEDICAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will further develop your understanding of underpinning pathophysiology relating to a variety of medical conditions encountered in the unscheduled healthcare environment. This subject continues on from Paramedic Medical Management, with further emphasis placed on specific acute and chronic manifestations of medical illnesses. Both the initial and ongoing assessment and management of a range of medical conditions will be explored and integrated with clinical placements.
learning_outcomes: Assess current evidence based clinical practice approaches for use in clinical management and debate their application in a range of clinical situations.
Perform comprehensive and timely assessment procedures on patients presenting with a range of medical presentations.
Synthesise theoretical knowledge with practical skills to effectively provide management of acute and chronic medical conditions common in unscheduled healthcare practice.

Accurately formulate and refine clinical management plans, including referral, by applying pathophysiology, clinical assessment and patient condition trend recognition skills, for a range of medical conditions.

title: PAEDIATRICS FOR PARAMEDICS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the specific challenges of caring for paediatric patients. You will develop an understanding of the pathophysiology relating to the commonly encountered health conditions of paediatric patients. You will assess, plan and manage paediatric patients with a diverse spectrum of conditions. You will refine your age specific communication techniques in a variety of clinical settings.
learning_outcomes: Construct and perform comprehensive assessments of paediatric patients with a broad range of medical conditions in a variety of simulated settings
Effectively communicate with paediatric patients presenting with diverse medical conditions.
Assess, plan and manage Paediatric patients with a broad range of medical condition using a paramedic decision-making process

title: PARAMEDIC MEDICAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of the underpinning pathophysiology relating to specific medical conditions and the importance of integrating theory into practice. You will extend your knowledge of systematic assessment procedures and history taking technique, and will apply these to the patient presenting with a medical condition. You will use the decision-making process to assess and plan the management of patients presenting with a variety of medical conditions. Communication techniques appropriate to patient presentations will be identified and developed.
learning_outcomes: Effectively manage patients with medical conditions.
Construct and perform comprehensive assessments of patients with specific medical conditions in a variety of simulated settings.
Assess a patient's medical condition using a paramedic decision-making process.
Communicate effectively with patients presenting with a variety of medical conditions.

title: PARAMEDIC MANAGEMENT - TRAUMA
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of the pathophysiology associated with various trauma conditions and the significance of incorporating this theoretical knowledge into clinical practice. Through workshops and simulation scenarios, you will enhance your technical skills and theoretical knowledge. Additionally, you will extend your practice in systematic assessment procedures and history-taking techniques to effectively address patients with traumatic conditions. You will engage in the decision-making process to assess, manage and monitor patients presenting with diverse trauma-related issues. Furthermore, you will identify and refine communication techniques tailored to patient interactions.
learning_outcomes: Assess patients presenting with traumatic injuries within a trauma setting and demonstrate initiative and judgement in planning, problem solving and decision-making in delivering health care.

Plan and implement management strategies for patients presenting with trauma conditions while effectively monitoring and reassessing these patients to determine the effectiveness of treatments utilised.
Adapt fundamental principles, concepts and techniques of trauma management to known and unknown situations to effectively manage the environments in which trauma occurs.
Communicate effectively with other team members to manage patients presenting with traumatic conditions.

title: MENTAL HEALTH IN PARAMEDICINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on knowledge and skills in advanced communication and therapeutic engagement to provide health care to people experiencing mental health related issues. You will develop cognitive and technical skills that demonstrate a broad understanding of knowledge, underlying principles and theoretical concepts in mental health.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and make use of valid evidence to implement strategies appropriate to diverse mental health related presentations in clinical practice
Communicate rigorous and rational arguments in a manner appropriate to the given audience, situation and context in relation to mental health
Reflect on evidence-based knowledge in the context of mental health related presentations

title: PARAMEDIC CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the underpinning pathophysiology relating to commonly encountered clinical problems of a cardiac and/or respiratory nature (chronic, acute, and life threatening). Practical skills and theoretical knowledge will be combined with clinical problem solving and decision-making skills within this unit. You will assess, plan the management of and monitor patients presenting with a variety of cardiac and respiratory conditions. Communication techniques appropriate to patient presentations will also be identified and developed.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of cardiac anatomy and pathophysiology including electrophysiology
Accurately interpret cardiac rhythms including normal, life threatening and 12 lead ECG recognition
Construct and perform comprehensive assessments of patients with cardiac and/or respiratory conditions in a variety of simulated settings
Effectively manage patients with cardiac and/or respiratory conditions

title: PARAMEDIC PRACTICE PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will consider ways in which paramedics work to enable change at a service, community or population level. You will focus on gaining knowledge and skills required for project work, and for you impending role as health practitioners in a rapidly changing environment. You will identify a gap in paramedic practice and then, develop, plan, manage and complete a self-directed project. You will apply, critique and reflect upon the skills required to complete a self-directed project with the ultimate aim of improving paramedic practice. You will present your work at a final year level conference.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate current paramedicine practice and research evidence to identify areas for quality improvement.
Clearly and coherently communication project outcomes to a variety of audiences.
Design and justify a health project related to enhanced professional practice in paramedicine.
Apply project management skills to implement a paramedicine health project.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply the clinical knowledge and the suite of clinical skills learned to a level that aligns with being able to work with and competently support various emergency healthcare professionals in managing complex and critically ill patients in the out of hospital environment. In-hospital advanced clinical management of acute complex conditions will be reviewed. You will use application, analysis, synthesis and evaluation to further refine the skills and knowledge required to provide advanced clinical paramedic management over a wide range of complex and critically ill patient presentations
learning_outcomes: Perform advanced clinical assessments and manage patients with clinically complex and critical clinical conditions in a variety of simulated settings
Provide a high level of skilled assistance for complex clinical assessments and a range of invasive procedures and associated interventions.
Analyse new and emerging paramedic clinical management methods in and out of hospital environment.

Compare and critique different clinical service models of Paramedics operating in Government, private Paramedic and emergency health sectors, including clinical governance and clinical quality improvement processes.

title: EXTENDED COMMUNITY PARAMEDICINE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the similarities and the differences between the traditional Ambulance Paramedic role and the emerging role of the Community Paramedic. You will develop insight to the concepts of out of hospital care beyond traditional jurisdictional emergency ambulance service models. The subject will introduce you to practice resources and equipment available to the community paramedic as well as commercial and industrial sector paramedics to manage patients with lower acuity and chronic health presentations in a multidisciplinary setting. You will expand the knowledge and skills required to practice as an Extended Community Paramedic (ECP) within a health service team and as a sole practitioner paramedic.
learning_outcomes: Implement and justify safe, effective and evidence-based patient-centred interventions in accordance with assessment findings.

Explain the pathophysiological adaptations associated with common conditions encountered in community paramedicine settings and integrate this knowledge into the interpretation of assessment findings.
Implement and justify a safe, effective and comprehensive patient assessment in the context of community health and extended care contexts.

Analyse the influence of individual and social determinants of health on patient outcomes in community paramedicine, incorporating principles of cultural safety, ethical decision-making, and legal responsibilities into professional practice

Evaluate clinical indications for advanced medical imaging, minor procedures, and interventions within the scope of practice of the community paramedic and facilitate effective referrals to appropriate health services.

title: MAJOR INCIDENT MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore, demonstrate and transmit the concepts of command, control, teamwork and leadership and their application to disasters, major incidents and sentinel events. The framework of planning, preparation, response and recovery will be used to investigate various roles and responsibilities essential to effective emergency management. Events with the potential to stretch ambulance and health resources at a community, state and national level will be examined. You will also develop and apply an ability to utilise risk assessment tools and strategies in a variety of routine and challenging circumstances.
learning_outcomes: Utilise effective leadership and command and control abilities in a variety of mass casualty and emergency incident scenarios.
Critique emergency management frameworks and emergency response procedures at organisational, state, and federal government levels.
Apply a wide range of communication skills to simulated major incident and complex emergency situations involving a variety of population groups.
Recognise and develop strategies to mitigate the potential impacts of disasters and major incidents at both a personal and organisational level.
Assess risk and conduct effective risk assessment for a variety of situations.

title: OBSTETRICS FOR PARAMEDICS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the specific challenges of caring for obstetric patients. You will develop an understanding of the pathophysiology relating to the commonly encountered health conditions of obstetric patients. You will be required to search, analyse, develop and apply education and/or management plans for the diversity and complexities of the obstetric patient.
learning_outcomes: Apply well-developed judgement and adaptability to a range of simple through to complex obstetric conditions, and to formulate and transmit plans of action.

Evaluate the roles of the multidisciplinary healthcare team members involved in the management of a patient within the context of a obstetric clinical situation in both the out of hospital and in hospital settings
Construct and perform comprehensive assessment and management of patients with a broad range of obstetric conditions in a variety of simulated settings

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE CONSOLIDATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will commence the transition from undergraduate to graduate paramedicine through reflection on and consolidation of knowledge, skills and attributes essential for safe and professional paramedic practice. This will be achieved through the combination of (up to) 150 hours of clinical placement with an emergency ambulance service, and associated reflective assessments whilst building your own professional portfolio.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and critically reflect on personal attributes, resilience levels and professional goals relating to paramedicine, and formulate strategies to refine and maintain them in the workplace.

Apply an advanced understanding of the theoretical and technical knowledge of graduate paramedic requirements in the areas of accountability, autonomy and advancement of professional clinical practice.
Synthesise clinical knowledge and decision making with personal and professional attributes to successfully negotiate a range of paramedic-specific performance evaluations.
Apply well-developed judgement and adaptability for a range of complex clinical conditions and formulating and transmitting plans of action.

Evaluate and critically appraise the relationship between leadership, communication and critical thinking skills, and formulate and transmit plans to incorporate these into complex conditions within paramedic practice.
Design and develop a range of individualised resources to facilitate recruitment and transition into the paramedic workforce.

title: POPULATIONS WITH SPECIFIC NEEDS FOR PARAMEDICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn how to manage and care for individuals with specific needs, including people living with disabilities and chronic illness. You will be introduced to working with vulnerable populations, populations experiencing abuse, neglect and/or violence, and those living with special physical, intellectual, mental and emotional needs. Learning activities will cover the management of patients/individuals in accordance with accepted paramedic practice standards. By critically analysing and evaluating education and health promotion strategies, through inquiry and investigation, you will learn how to effectively manage individuals with specific needs.
learning_outcomes: Formulate an approach to appropriately assess, monitor, and manage individuals with specific needs in accordance with paramedic practice guidelines.
Justify prioritized management plans of individuals with specific needs.
Evaluate the health literacy status of individuals with specific needs, and devise plans to advocate for and support individuals and caregivers in the area of health knowledge.
Integrate professional knowledge and skills to effectively communicate with and care for individuals with specific needs and their caregivers both individually and as part of a team

Investigate, establish an understanding of, and formulate patient-centred management strategies to address the emotional, psychosocial and physiological challenges common to individuals living with specific needs.

title: PHARMACOLOGY FOR HEALTH PROFESSIONALS
syllabus_overview: Pharmacology is the study of drugs. Drugs play a key role in the treatment of most human diseases and are used to both cure and prevent disease. In this subject you will learn the general principles of pharmacology including drug classification, formulation, administration and basic pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Drugs affecting the nervous system and major organs will be explored, and the concept of selective toxicity to treat infection will be introduced. You will gain knowledge in commonly prescribed drugs, clinical trials and over the counter and complimentary medications, drugs of abuse and dependence and drugs in sport. Emphasis is placed on human pharmacology including clinical topics, such as, adverse drug reactions and drug interactions.
learning_outcomes: Describe the ways drugs are absorbed, distributed, metabolised and excreted in the body and explain the factors influencing these processes.
Distinguish between the fundamental principles of pharmacology (pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics), and explain the ways that drugs can produce therapeutic actions in the body.
Apply understanding of agonist and antagonist activity to drug action.
Explain the causes of drug contraindications, interactions and adverse reactions using understanding of drug properties and human physiology.
Explain how different classes of drugs used to treat various diseases act to effect living tissue.
Communicate pharmacological concepts and information as part of a team

title: GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF PHARMACOLOGY
syllabus_overview: Pharmacology is the study of drugs, drug targets and how they interact with the human body. In this subject, students will learn the general principles of pharmacology including drug classification, formulation and routes of administration. Basic pharmacokinetics, including the processes of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion, will be discussed, in addition to basic pharmacodynamics which includes principles of drug action, drug targets (ion channels, enzymes, transporters, receptors, genes and the immune system) and cell signaling. Other topics that will be explored include over the counter and complementary medications. Emphasis is placed on human pharmacology including clinical topics, such as adverse drug reactions and drug interactions.
learning_outcomes: Describe the mechanism of action, pharmacological effects, therapeutic uses, contraindications, safety considerations, and side effects of major drug classes and commonly used therapeutic agents.
Demonstrate the ability to source, evaluate and effectively communicate scientific information on the principles and application of pharmacology both independently and as part of a team.

Define core concepts of pharmacology including the definition of a drug, pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion) and pharmacodynamics (how drugs interact with drug targets and produce effects).
Analyse and integrate experimentally-obtained pharmacological data with knowledge of core pharmacological concepts to interpret and form relevant conclusions from the data obtained.

title: DRUG DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will undertake a semester long project to discover and develop a new drug.
