You will also need to perform all of the required safety and regulatory requirements that are needed for new drugs before they are prescribed to patients. An employability module in the subject will allow reflection on attainment of graduate capabilities and consideration of future career pathways.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and align your current graduate capabilities and attributes that will lead to success in Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) careers.
Understand the drug development process, including intellectual property, venture capital funding, clinical trials, Government regulations, and the role of pharmaceutical companies.

Interpret data from pharmacological studies and use effective communication skills to communicate pharmacological terminology, information and arguments effectively to various audiences using a variety of modes, both individually and as part of a team.
Understand the role of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in the development of new, safe, and effective therapeutic drugs.

title: APPLIED HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build upon your existing knowledge of systems physiology by examining the integrated physiological responses to acute exercise of varying intensities and duration. You will also learn about the adaptations occurring in response to chronic endurance training. You will also learn about commonly used legal & illegal substances in sport, including the history of The World Anti-Doping Agency and a host of substances used to enhance sports performance. This subject also provides an in-depth exploration of human physiology with a focus on ageing. It covers theories and models of ageing, and the physiological changes in the brain, muscle, and heart. Special topics include normal vs. premature ageing and strategies for healthy ageing, such as dietary restriction and phytochemicals.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyze and synthesize research on ageing and strategies for promoting healthy and productive ageing.
Evaluate the impact of legal supplements and illegal drugs on athletic performance and health.
Work as a team to articulate the ethical, legal, and health implications of using performance-enhancing substances in sports.
Articulate acute physiological responses and long-term adaptations to aerobic exercise and predict the impact on metabolic processes and the maintenance of homeostasis during exercise.
Utilise raw data to accurately assess metabolic responses to exercise across varying intensities, and critically evaluate the precision of the outcomes.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PHARMACY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This cornerstone subject provides basic skills and information so that students can understand the roles of pharmacy and the pharmacist. It introduces students to pharmacy-related databases, information sources and to the concepts of patient-centred care and health literacy. Students will be introduced to a range of pharmacy practice elements, including the profession of pharmacy in the health care system, its history, ethical and legal issues, dispensing and a range of clinical practice and professional service areas for pharmacy.
learning_outcomes: Describe the concept of health literacy
Discuss pharmacy practice related issues and actively contribute to discussions on these topics
Demonstrate understanding of pharmacy related information in an oral format
Demonstrate an understanding of the quality use of medicine (QUM principles and select appropriate resources for drug information enquiry to discuss medications commonly used in practice.)

Describe and discuss both practical issues and the roles that pharmacists play, including their role as part of the healthcare team and in the broader Australian healthcare system, across both community and hospital settings.
Demonstrate the principles of differential diagnosis.
Describe and apply the requirements that define a legal prescription and label
Apply basic ethical related principles in considering health related issues
Demonstrate understanding of eHealth and mHealth issues relating to the pharmacy profession

title: PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATION A
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the pharmaceutical sciences and covers the areas of physical chemistry and laboratory skills necessary to prepare and understand the formulation of pharmaceutical products. This subject focuses on solution formulations. Students will be introduced to products and routes of administration, absorption, distribution and elimination of drugs. They will study pharmaceutically relevant physicochemical phenomena, formulation of solutions, and pharmaceutical calculations.
learning_outcomes: Predict and explain the properties of solutions by the calculation and interpretation of thermodynamic parameters and describe how these relate to pharmaceutical solutions.
Apply pharmacokinetic principles by describing Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and how this can be affected by dosage form and route of administration.
Assess the advantages and disadvantages of a wide variety of dosage forms by describing how dosage form can impact on factors such as bioavailability, stability and product handling.
Accurately perform simple pharmaceutical calculations
Apply methods of compounding by manufacturing and dispensing a simple solution product in accordance with the PSA Professional Practice Standard for Compounding.

title: FOUNDATIONS IN QUALITY USE OF MEDICINES
syllabus_overview: Quality use of Medicines (QUM) is a concept that underpins the healthcare system in Australia. You will be introduced to the key concepts that make up QUM, as well as counseling and communication techniques that allows you to gain information from patients and through clinical reasoning make informed decisions in directing patient therapy. Practice Based cases are used to develop discipline specific skills in managing primary healthcare pharmaceutical issues. Ethical and legal issues that regulate the practice of pharmacy in Australia shall be further explored and reviewed in experiential clinical placement activity.
learning_outcomes: Appraise the health literacy of a patient and adequately adjust communication to suit literacy level of that patient.
Apply appropriate laws, code of ethics and professional practice standards related to the practice of pharmacy, and justify an ethically sound resolution.
Apply differential diagnosis skills to determine the appropriateness of OTC medications for presenting patients in a primary healthcare setting.
Interpret the Quality Use of Medicines (QUM) principles in the context of supply of over-the-counter (OTC) medication
Critique the process of dispensing with consideration to safe supply of medication, prescribers' intentions and the law.
Apply communication and patient history taking techniques in a community pharmacy

title: PHARMACOLOGY A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will be introduced to physiological control and the body systems involved in control and the relevant pharmacology. The subject will cover receptor kinetics, nerve impulse propagation and transmission, the operation of the nervous and endocrine systems (with special emphasis on the autonomic nervous system) and the pharmacology of drugs acting at synaptic and neuromuscular sites. The practical component will introduce the use of physiological equipment, and ethical considerations for animal and human experimentation.
learning_outcomes: Explain how drugs may interact at the pharmaceutical, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and physiological phase
Explain how drugs interact at the cellular level to alter the operations of the nervous and endocrine systems.
Critically review aspects of drug interactions with human physiology; using safe and ethical practices.

title: PHARMACOLOGY B
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to how our immune system responds to different challenges. You will learn which cells are the main players, what their jobs are and how they get these jobs done (molecular signalling).This will be presented in the context of innate immunity (first response),inflammation, chemical cascades, adaptive immunity (acquired) and humoral immunity (antibodies; complement). What happens when things go wrong with the immune system and how it can be manipulated and harnessed for better health outcomes using immunopharmacology and immunotherapy approaches will also be explored.
learning_outcomes: Assess the clinical problems that arise when the immune system is disrupted and explain how immunopharmacotherapies targeting the innate and adaptive immune systems can be used to treat these conditions.
Explain how the immune system recognises, responds and recovers from infection or tissue damage.
Apply effective communication skills to convey concepts in immunology and immunopharmacotherapy.
Describe the biological mechanisms of the immune system in human health and disease with a focus on leveraging these processes for therapeutic interventions.
Describe how the body defends against viral, bacterial and parasitic infections

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND THERAPEUTICS A (CARDIOVASCULAR AND RESPIRATORY)
syllabus_overview: This subject will integrate the teaching of pharmacology, medicinal chemistry and pharmacy practice relating to the use of drugs for cardiovascular and respiratory disorders. Students will initially explore the mechanism of action of these drugs, specifically how they affect biochemical and physiological processes at the cellular and organ level, and then relate this to the overall clinical effect on the individual. The medicinal chemistry of these drugs will then be explored so that structure-function relationships can be determined at the molecular level. Finally, the pharmacy practice issues relating to these conditions and medications will be addressed, in a manner that highlights how these drugs can ameliorate the various disease states, and affect the overall clinical condition of the patient.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain the pharmacology of drugs for cardiovascular and respiratory disorders, specifically the actions at the receptor, cellular and organ levels, and clinical effect on the patient.
Describe and explain the relationship between drug actions and therapeutic outcomes, specifically the amelioration of disease states of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems
To understand the process behind development and following of clinical practice guidelines, and to translate these to patient care and outcomes in a pharmacy setting
Describe the absorption, elimination and metabolism of cardiovascular and respiratory drugs and relate this to clinical practice and how pharmacogenetics affects this.

title: FIRST NATIONS HEALTH IN AUSTRALIA
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will begin to develop the knowledge and skills required to work effectively and safely with Australian First Nations peoples in the healthcare environment. You will explore key features and concepts related to traditional and contemporary First Nations cultures and communities; multi-dimensional models of First Nations health and healing; and the underlying social determinants influencing current health outcomes, including historical and cultural factors. You will also explore concepts related to health inequality, reflect on the responsibility of the whole health system in improving First Nations health outcomes, and consider how culturally safe pharmacy practice can contribute to closing the gap in Indigenous health disadvantage. The concepts of honouring First Nations knowledge, strength-based approaches, and evidenced-based learning are strongly reinforced throughout the subject. This subject is delivered via a blended learning approach comprising on-line modules and face-to face workshops.
learning_outcomes: Describe First Nations concepts of health and healing, and analyse how interconnected physical, social, historical, political and cultural factors impact on health outcomes.

Engage in culturally appropriate communication that facilitates respectful therapeutic relationships, and supports effective partnerships with First Nations health professionals, organisations and communities.
Outline the concepts of health inequality, the factors that contribute to it, and ways of redressing it to close the gap in health outcomes between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians.

Explain the meaning of 'cultural safety' in relation to improving health outcomes for First Nations people and critically analyse how it influences effective pharmacy practice, and health service delivery.
Describe the key features of Australian First Nations culture and history and apply an understanding of diversity within the First Nations population to person-centred care.

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND THERAPEUTICS C (PSYCHIATRY AND NEUROLOGY)
syllabus_overview: This subject investigates the brain. Ultimately, behaviour is the outcome of cellular and molecular processes within the brain, and subtle changes in brain physiology will result in spectacular and often debilitating behavioural pathologies. Therapeutic intervention based on psychotropic drugs aims to restore or tweak brain physiology - while conceptually a sound approach, our understanding of how neurophysiology ultimately is expressed in behaviour, is limited. As a consequence, this subject will not provide you with answers, but aims to enable you to critically appraise therapeutic intervention. In addition, the pharmacy practice issues relating to neuropsychiatry will be addressed in a manner that highlights how psychotropic drugs can ameliorate the various disease states, and how they affect the overall condition of the patient.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of neurotransmitter systems in the operation of the central nervous system
Follow guidelines to critically assess drug use and disease states in a defined case study scenario.
Describe and explain the relationship between drug actions and therapeutic outcomes, specifically in the amelioration of clinical conditions related to the central nervous system.
Describe the absorption, elimination and metabolism of central nervous system (CNS) drugs and relate this to clinical practice and how pharmacogenetics affects this.
Anticipate and rationalize interaction between drugs (including over-the-counter (OTC preparations)
Initiate appropriate procedures for mental health first aid
Relate the relevant class of drugs to activity at the molecular level, specifically effect on relevant receptors and other regulatory molecules and processes.

title: PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATION B
syllabus_overview: Drugs are used in a wide range of dosage forms and pharmacists need to understand the design and rationale behind available dosage forms. It is assumed that students, from previous subjects, will be aware of two phase systems and simple pharmacokinetics. Pharmacists also need to be able to prepare extemporaneous products with confidence and professional pride. In this subject there is a focus on the preparation of two-phase pharmaceutical products and solid dosage forms. Extemporaneous dispensing continues to be an important skill required by many pharmacists. As mentioned in previous pharmaceutics subjects, the PSA Professional Practice Standard for compounding and competencies relating to compounding are the foundation of extemporaneous dispensing. This subject aims to further develop your skills in extemporaneous dispensing, extemporaneous compounding and pharmaceutical calculations and achieve the level of competency required for a pharmacist.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the inclusion of all the ingredients in suspension, emulsion, tablet, capsule, vaginal and rectal dosage forms.
Critically analyse and accurately complete the different types of pharmaceutical calculations that are commonly encountered by a pharmacist in the pharmacy profession.
Critically analyse, develop, apply quality assurance procedures for compounded products that meet the requirements of the PSA Professional Practice Standard for compounding and competencies
Efficiently prepare safe and elegant extemporaneous products with accurate recording of the manufacturing procedure.

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND THERAPEUTICS B (METABOLIC AND ENDOCRINE)
syllabus_overview: This subject will integrate the teaching of pharmacology, medicinal chemistry and pharmacy practice relating to the use of drugs for gastroenterology, hepatic, reproductive and endocrine disorders. You will initially explore the mechanism of action of these drugs, specifically how they affect biochemical and physiological processes at the cellular and organ level, and then relate this to the overall clinical effect on the individual. The medicinal chemistry of these drugs will then be explored so that structure-function relationships can be determined at the molecular level. Finally, the pharmacy practice issues relating to these conditions and medications will be addressed, in a manner that highlights how these drugs can ameliorate the various disease states and affect the overall clinical condition of the patient. You will have the opportunity to explore and apply their knowledge in drug metabolism and drug interactions during a two-week, mid-year rural community pharmacy placement.
learning_outcomes: Relate the relevant class of drugs to activity at the molecular level, specifically, effect on relevant receptors and other regulatory molecules and processes.
Explain the pathophysiology for a selection of disease states associated with the endocrine system, reproductive system and body metabolism.
Describe and explain the relationship between drug actions and therapeutic outcomes, specifically in the amelioration of disease states associated with the endocrine system or body metabolism.
Anticipate and rationalize interaction between drugs including over-the-counter (OTC and other substances)

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND THERAPEUTICS D (ANTI-INFECTIVES)
syllabus_overview: In this subject, important microbial diseases affecting humans will be studied. A major area of focus is the mechanism of action of chemotherapeutic agents (bacterial antibiotics, antifungal agents, antiviral agents, and disinfectants) to treat and control microbial diseases. This will help explain why certain classes of drugs and antibiotics are useful against some microorganisms but not others.
learning_outcomes: Anticipate and rationalise interaction between drugs including over-the-counter (OTC) drugs.
Demonstrate an understanding of the pharmacology of drugs for infective diseases, specifically the actions at the cellular and organ levels, and clinical effect on the patient.
Relate the mechanisms of gene transfer in micro-organisms to consequent resistance to antimicrobial pharmacotherapy.
Relate procedures for the testing of effectiveness of antimicrobial substances to the problem of the spread of microbial resistance.

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF DRUG USE IN SOCIETY
syllabus_overview: Drug use affects almost everybody in society. The role of the pharmacist in managing the harms of drug use is increasingly recognized as a vital part of the profession. This subject will explore rates of drug use and harms, the pathophysiology and pharmacology behind drug use and the ways that pharmacists can mitigate the risks of harm. You will also apply critical thinking, self-reflection and judgement to recognise the health inequities and disparities, including the impact of social determinants of health in a respectful, culturally appropriate, compassionate, responsive and empathetic manner
learning_outcomes: Apply critical thinking, self-reflection and judgement to recognise the health inequities and disparities in vulnerable members of the community, including the impact of social determinants of health in a respectful, culturally appropriate, compassionate, responsive and empathetic manner
Analyse the delivery of harm minimisation approaches and strategies to reduce harm to patients and the community from misuse of legal and illegal drugs
Critically analyse the role of the pharmacist in treatment and mitigation of risk from drug use
Describe the pharmacology behind commonly abused drugs both legal and illicit and describe the pathophysiology of drug dependence

title: GROUP PROJECT
syllabus_overview: Teamwork, research, project management, and evidence-based practice are important aspects of science and professional pharmacy practice. In this subject, you will undertake either a team-based research project or have the option to participate in an industry-based project. In the team-based project you will be able to choose a topic relevant to pharmacy practice, or chemical, biological, or pharmaceutical science. Your project team will meet regularly to discuss strategies, manage progress, distribute roles within the team, and analyse results. Your team will be mentored to achieve completion of your research project, communication of your findings, and development of skills in effective teamwork and project management. In the industry-based project, you will attend the site on multiple occasions, research the industry, including regulatory affairs, good manufacturing processes, research a topic related to the industry, roles, and opportunities, and complete a detailed report on the topic and potentially undertake a mock job interview.
learning_outcomes: Work in a team and employ strategies to make teamwork a productive collaboration. Identify and articulate the skills required to work effectively as part of a team and demonstrate understanding of time management.
Defend the approach taken to solving a research question when queried.
Communicate research findings in written and oral form to a general audience.
Research a topic in science or pharmacy practice at an appropriate depth, and gain experience in literature searching and critically examining that literature for relevance and quality.

title: PHARMACEUTICAL CARE - QUALITY USE OF MEDICINES B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore information sources to determine the true therapeutic place of various treatment regimes, using an evidence-based medicine approach, and how this information can be conveyed to the patient and other health care providers so that therapy is optimised. You will develop skills to problem solve and apply therapeutic knowledge in a pharmacy practice setting to assist with optimising patient care. An integrated approach is utilised that explores the pharmacist's role as part of the health care team. This subject introduces new topics on common illnesses and incorporates prior knowledge into contemporary clinical practice. Placement, role-plays, clinical scenarios, case studies, Meds Checks and Home Medication Reviews ensure that students will be introduced to the current roles of pharmacists in the delivery of pharmaceutical care.
learning_outcomes: Manage the delivery and administration of approved injections and immunisations by pharmacists and advise patients on appropriate immunization requirements.
Apply differential diagnostic techniques to ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes for patients.
Evaluate the pharmacist role in a large metropolitan hospital through participation and engagement with assigned tasks.
Apply the quality use of medicine principles in the pharmacy practice context
Integrate effective counselling and communication skills to improve patients' therapeutic outcomes in a health literate manner.
Undertake medication review and create an appropriate medication management plan

title: PHARMACEUTICAL CARE - QUALITY USE OF MEDICINES A
syllabus_overview: The ability to integrate and assimilate knowledge is an invaluable skill for pharmacists. This capstone subject aims to integrate knowledge gained in therapeutics subjects and apply it in practice. Workshops and clinical placement provide opportunities to gain experience in providing pharmaceutical care, while case scenarios and oral assessments illustrate the expanding role of the pharmacist in optimising patient outcomes. PHA4PCA and PHA4PCB are designed to be a lead-in to intern year, with learning activities laying the foundation for what is to come during internship, and in professional practice thereafter. Both the Top 40 drugs oral assessment and the case-based oral exams are constructed to reflect sections of the Pharmacy Board of Australia registration exams.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of health literacy advice to counsel patients about therapy in the wide range of disease states encountered in pharmacy practice.
Use appropriate questioning and communication techniques to take thorough medication histories and integrate information from clinical records to develop comprehensive patient management plans.
Apply understanding of the quality use of medicine principles in pharmacy contexts
Apply differential diagnostic techniques to ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes for patients.

title: PERSON-CENTRED CARE IN PHARMACY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Communication is central to the role of any healthcare professional. The ability to communicate with both patients and other healthcare professionals is vital to ensuring the highest level of care can be delivered. This subject will explore various aspects of communication including verbal and non-verbal skills, assessing the listeners understanding and the ability to adjust communication to suit the health literacy of the receiver. This subject will examine particular aspects of communication with respect to patients who are from Indigenous or culturally diverse backgrounds, and patients who are elderly. The role of reflection in development of skills and competencies will be explored. The way that pharmacists in non-traditional roles contribute to and communicate with the extended healthcare team will also be explored through a one-week clinical placement.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the role of pharmacists in different healthcare models with respect to the impact on delivery on pharmacy services, medicine supply and medicine use
Reflect on and evaluate current practice to develop continuous improvement strategies to enhance skills for effective communication across diverse backgrounds and cultures
Apply diverse communicative approaches and to allow successful engagement with patients and healthcare professionals across a spectrum of health literacy
Critically evaluate the roles of pharmacists in the interprofessional healthcare team in optimising patient outcomes

title: PHARMACY HONOURS PROJECT A
syllabus_overview: PHA4PHA is one of a suite of subjects which those students undertaking the individual project stream must complete to qualify for the Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours). The aim of these subjects is to provide students with a thorough introduction to the process of conducting research. After review of the relevant literature, students will, in conjunction with an academic staff supervisor, refine a research question and research design. The method used in the project will depend on the research question. It may involve literature evaluation, experimental or empirical study, case study, theoretical or inferential work, survey etc. Students will plan their research project, collect and analyse data, then give an oral presentation and write a research paper that demonstrates their capacity to conceptualise, conduct and report a research project. At the end of the project, the entire body of project work from PHA4PHA, PHA4PHB and PHA4PHC will be evaluated and a project mark and grade will be recorded against these three subjects.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and demonstrate an understanding of research methodology conducting a research project under limited supervision, and critically analysing and reporting the results using academic conventions including referencing, layout and use of appropriate academic terminology.
Communicate research findings in a logical and understandable way in written and oral form to a general audience.
Demonstrate a capacity to search and critically evaluate research literature by conducting a rigorous literature search and written review.
Define a problem or task through construction of a project brief, generate creative ideas and apply decision-making skills to develop a research plan and work schedule.
Defend the approach taken to solving a research question when queried

title: PHARMACY HONOURS PROJECT B
syllabus_overview: PHA4PHB is one of a suite of subjects which those students undertaking the individual project stream must complete to qualify for the Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours). The aim of these subjects is to provide students with a thorough introduction to the process of conducting research. After review of the relevant literature, students will, in conjunction with an academic staff supervisor, refine a research question and research design. The method used in the project will depend on the research question. It may involve literature evaluation, experimental or empirical study, case study, theoretical or inferential work, survey etc. Students will plan their research project, collect and analyse data, then give an oral presentation and write a research paper that demonstrates their capacity to conceptualise, conduct and report a research project. At the end of the project, the entire body of project work from PHA4PHA, PHA4PHB and PHA4PHC will be evaluated and a project mark and grade will be recorded against these three subjects.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and demonstrate an understanding of research methodology conducting a research project under limited supervision, and critically analysing and reporting the results using academic conventions including referencing, layout and use of appropriate academic terminology.
Defend the approach taken to solving a research question when queried
Communicate research findings in a logical and understandable way in written and oral form to a general audience.
Demonstrate a capacity to search and critically evaluate research literature by conducting a rigorous literature search and written review.
Define a problem or task through construction of a project brief, generate creative ideas and apply decision-making skills to develop a research plan and work schedule.

title: PHARMACY HONOURS PROJECT C
syllabus_overview: PHA4PHC is one of a suite of subjects which those students undertaking the individual project stream must complete to qualify for the Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours). The aim of these subjects is to provide students with a thorough introduction to the process of conducting research. After review of the relevant literature, students will, in conjunction with an academic staff supervisor, refine a research question and research design. The method used in the project will depend on the research question. It may involve literature evaluation, experimental or empirical study, case study, theoretical or inferential work, survey etc. Students will plan their research project, collect and analyse data, then give an oral presentation and write a research paper that demonstrates their capacity to conceptualise, conduct and report a research project. At the end of the project, the entire body of project work from PHA4PHA, PHA4PHB and PHA4PHC will be evaluated and a project mark and grade will be recorded against these three subjects.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and demonstrate an understanding of research methodology conducting a research project under limited supervision, and critically analysing and reporting the results using academic conventions including referencing, layout and use of appropriate academic terminology.
Demonstrate a capacity to search and critically evaluate research literature by conducting a rigorous literature search and written review.
Communicate research findings in a logical and understandable way in written and oral form to a general audience.
Define a problem or task through construction of a project brief, generate creative ideas and apply decision-making skills to develop a research plan and work schedule.
Defend the approach taken to solving a research question when queried

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: As a registered pharmacist, you will invariably find yourself in a position of leadership or management early in your career, whether it is as pharmacist-in-charge of a shift, supervising assistants and technicians, or in a more formal management role. This subject aims to give an introduction to a variety of concepts that will be useful in management, including CPD planning, legislation, OH&S, accounting, human resources, management, and marketing. A key aspect of this subject is to introduce you to a range of professionals and the services that they offer to support the various management functions in pharmacy. This will mean that you know what help is available and where to go to find it when you need it. The subject is delivered as a blended subject. Assessments are designed to mirror tasks that you will undertake as a registered pharmacist and the learning activities are designed to increase your critical thinking, reasoning and ability to justify decisions. This subject has a strong emphasis on groupwork, with an aim to prepare you for working as part of a team in your future practice.
learning_outcomes: Summarise associated risks that impact on pharmacy service provisions and devise mitigation strategies to maximise the safety and viability of a professional service
Define a scope of practice and develop a Continuing Professional Development (CPD) plan based on deficiencies and limitations identified through structured reflection.
Interpret the relevant legislation, codes, and guidelines applicable to pharmacy practice and evaluate their application in context.
Employ principles of strategic planning and SMART goals to collaboratively design and present a novel professional pharmacy service.

title: PHARMACY PRACTICE AND THERAPEUTICS E (ONCOLOGY AND PALLIATIVE CARE)
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces the broad range of drugs used in the treatment of neoplastic diseases, as well as medicines and other treatment modalities employed in the area of palliative care to fourth year pharmacy students. These specialist areas will be covered by an overview of the pathophysiology of cancer, followed by systematic review of the major classes of antineoplastic drugs, including mechanisms of action and patient care issues. Specific issues regarding the delivery of palliative care to terminally ill patients will be explored through a series of structured lectures as well as directed learning and presentations by the students.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise a care plan to address clinical outcomes for oncology and palliative care patients.
Explain how cells become cancerous and metastatic, including the genetic and environmental influences and the various stages of these processes.
Evaluate how pharmaceutical science relates to clinical outcomes for oncology and palliative care medications.

title: THERAPEUTICS IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: The ability to bring together available resources and to identify relevant information is a key skill for clinical pharmacists to develop. This final year subject offers you the opportunity to bring together knowledge amassed throughout the undergraduate degree and apply it to a series of real-world problems. Answers may not be explicitly in guidelines, so you will be required to conduct your own research, appraise and apply research findings, justify your decisions, and communicate those decisions in language accessible to both patients and prescribers.
learning_outcomes: Anticipate and resolve potential medication-related issues for an individual patient.
Take thorough medication histories and integrate information from clinical records to develop comprehensive patient-centered management plans.
Appraise current research within clinical pharmacy as it applies to patients with complex medical histories.
Evaluate patient medication summaries in the context of quality use of medicines principles to minimise risk and maximise therapeutic outcomes for patients.
Effectively communicate with patients and healthcare professionals to reduce risks to patients and ensure safe and effective patient outcomes.
Apply differential diagnostic techniques to ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes for patients.

title: PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC HEALTH
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces you to the concepts and principles of public health as they relate to various times in history and diverse contexts, populations and health challenges. You will acquire an understanding of the environmental, sociocultural, political, economic, technological, organisational, behavioural and genetic factors that interact to shape the health of communities and populations. You will identify and evaluate the range, strengths and weaknesses of evidence that informs public health policies, programs and practice, along with major ethical considerations. Public health successes and failures, and contemporary approaches to protecting and improving health, preventing and controlling disease and injury, and reducing health inequalities will be explored. These will reveal core functions of public health systems such as surveillance and monitoring.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively evaluate public health as a discipline supporting vulnerable and/or priority communities
Identify and describe the often conflicting roles and interests held by the various stakeholders engaged in or affected by public health activities.
Introduce and critically analyse the various concepts, values and strategies relating to public health in Australia and internationally.
Critically articulate the applicability of various public health strategies across levels of society.

title: INTRODUCTION TO HEALTH PROMOTION
syllabus_overview: This subject is concerned with the philosophical, ethical, theoretical and disciplinary foundations of the evolving field of health promotion and effective health promotion action. You will learn about psychological, organisational, social and political theories, models and conceptual frameworks, and the role of these in guiding health promotion practice. You will gain skills in using a theoretically-sound, evidence-informed and ethical approach to design action. These skills include: interpreting the problem to solve or goal to achieve; mapping determinants; assessing current strengths, capacities and needs; identifying potential partners; and using theory, evidence and partners to design appropriate health promotion action. The role of systems thinking in planning and action will be introduced, along with settings-based approaches to prevention and health promotion.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on your values and principles in relation to health promotion practice
Explain the relationship between health promotion, social equity, health inequities, social justice, evidence and ethical health promotion practice.
Discuss the strengths and limitations of a range of health promotion strategies including primary prevention, behavioural, and socio-environmental approaches to health promotion
Critically assess in small groups, the range of theories for promoting health and how they are used in promotion programs.
Describe the principles underpinning contemporary health promotion and illustrate the differing perspectives of health promotion

title: PROMOTING WELLBEING IN INDIVIDUALS AND TEAMS
syllabus_overview: The subject focuses on understanding individuals and teams. You will learn about human behaviour and effective strategies to promote life balance and sustained wellbeing. You will acquire the skills that will contribute to facilitating improved individual , team and organisational performance.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and synthesise the role and scope of key support providers to increase wellbeing and enhance performance
Investigate the influence of individuals and teams on wellbeing and performance
Interpret and implement effective strategies that lead to an increased understanding of individual and teamwork by working individually and in collaboration with others
Identify signs and apply strategies to enhance mental health and wellbeing

title: REHABILITATION CASE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to major concepts and theories in rehabilitation and health intervention. This subject will examine procedures that are useful in rehabilitation when working in health settings. The subject will provide students with an understanding of effective case management skills which leads to proper care coordination, seamless service provider integration and cooperation, and the development and delivery of comprehensive rehabilitation services to those living with chronic conditions or permanent impairments with the aim of achieving optimal health.
learning_outcomes: Critique and interpret major models relevant to Rehabilitation Case Management and apply to practical settings.
Apply, demonstrate and report Case Management principles in relation to local, national and international practical case studies.
Analyse theoretical models and determine the most appropriate assessment tools to create and evaluate a rehabilitation intervention plan.
Work collaboratively to demonstrate effective and innovative rehabilitative strategies and return to work planning, injury management and service provision
Identify and discuss the basic principles of the Case Management process, including its application in different cultural groups and in diverse communities.

title: COMMUNICATION PROCESS FOR REHABILITATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are given the opportunity to increase your knowledge, understanding, and skills in communicating in interpersonal and group settings. The principal aim of this subject is to identify the existing interpersonal skills of students. In addition, it provides an opportunity to develop and practice these skills which are essential when working in health settings. Given that the subject adopts a skills-based orientation, students will be required to attend one weekly 2-hour workshop (either online or face-to-face, depending on subject instance enrolment) which will provide the opportunity to practice effective communication styles, appreciate contextual considerations (e.g., culture), and develop an understanding of the application of interpersonal communication skills in a range of settings (e.g., therapeutic, social, and public health).
learning_outcomes: Describe how contextual factors can impact on communication processes, both collaboratively with peers and as individuals.
Critically reflect on your own existing interpersonal skills, identify your interpersonal skills that require further development and formulate a plan for developing these skills.

Critically reflect on what you have learnt about yourself in the process of engaging in the subject's learning material, and consider how this might contribute to working effectively with clients in the future.

title: HUMANS, HEALTH AND THE ENVIRONMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the health status of humans as individuals, groups, and populations in relation to their adaptation to environmental changes. You will gain an understanding of the interrelationship between the physical environment and human health and how to communicate environmental health issues in preparation for environmental health practice. The main topics include humans, their health and disease in relation to ecosystems, toxicology, air and noise pollution, wastewater systems and management, water and soil quality, land use, and chemical, biological, and radiological hazards. This subject includes synchronous sessions held during business hours. This means that you will attend sessions each week simultaneously with your facilitator and classmates. This subject is recommended for first-year undergraduate students, who are enrolled in the Bachelor of Health Sciences.
learning_outcomes: Summarise the basic underpinning science of environmental health issues
Characterise the interrelationship between the physical environment and human health
Identify and describe the main environmental threats to human health
Work individually and in teams to communicate effectively about key environmental health issues to a wide range of stakeholders

title: INDIVIDUAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the foundation knowledge for working with individuals in health and human services settings. You will learn how particular characteristics and actions of an individual impact on health and welfare outcomes. You will be: (i) presented with frameworks, including a developmental perspective, for understanding how the characteristics and actions of individuals impact on health outcomes; (ii) provided with foundation knowledge for understanding how individuals present in, and progress through, health settings; and (iii) reviewing theoretical approaches to producing individual change in health and wellbeing settings.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with peers to examine how person-related factors can influence an individual’s behaviour and ways in which to facilitate optimal health and wellbeing for patients/clients in a health care setting.
Apply psychological theories and concepts of human behaviour across the lifespan to real-world settings
Examine the concept of reflection on practice and apply this to professional and individual development
Explore aspects of human behaviour across the lifespan from a psychosocial perspective through the study of fundamental psychological theories and concepts (health)

title: SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine the ways health, well-being and illness are experienced, understood, and responded to by people as social beings who participate in various groups, organisations, communities, and societies. Critical factors such as education, social class, gender, ethnicity and culture will be explored to examine how social practices, positions, and processes influence access to and use of resources supportive of health and well-being. Theories and frameworks will be examined and assessed so that you can develop an ability to become aware of and interpret various life concerns both personally and professionally and gain a more nuanced awareness of the dynamics operating between the personal and public domains.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with peers to examine the life expectancy gap between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians using the social determinants of health.
Research and use different types of data and information to understand and explain health and illness issues within a diverse social and cultural context.
Compare health and illness outcomes experienced by groups from different social and cultural contexts and explain why differences occur.
Examine how social and cultural factors shape and determine people's experience of health and illness in different parts of the world.
Discuss the interactions between health and illness, social perceptions of disease, culture and other societal structures and institutions.

title: UNDERSTANDING HEALTH AND WELLBEING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop a broad understanding of health and wellbeing, examining key theories that underpin concepts in contemporary health and wellbeing. You will investigate the complex range of interactions that influence the health and wellbeing of individuals, communities and populations. As health is a dynamic concept, you will further examine the social, environmental and biomedical determinants of health and wellbeing within an Australian and global context.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the contemporary issues of health and wellbeing in an Australian and global context.
Describe the key perspectives and theories of health and wellbeing.
Analyse the role of various health practitioners in health care systems and health promotion settings to facilitate optimal health and wellbeing.
Identify and explain the determinants of health and how they influence health and wellbeing of individuals, communities and populations.

title: EPIDEMIOLOGY FOR PUBLIC HEALTH
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this subject is to provide you with an understanding of the role of epidemiology in public health. You will learn about the different epidemiological study designs, their strengths and weaknesses, and how to apply those methods to address public health problems. You will learn how to write a clear and comprehensive research proposal and to critically appraise epidemiological studies from the public health literature. You will be introduced to the basic principles of infectious diseases surveillance and the investigation of disease outbreaks and you will learn about the epidemiological principles of screening.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply the methods of descriptive and analytical epidemiology.
Critically appraise epidemiological papers from the public health literature.
Understand the main strengths and weaknesses of different epidemiological study designs.
Be able to apply epidemiological methods in a variety of situations.
Understand the role of epidemiology in the practice of public health.

title: SOCIO-ECOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVES ON PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS
syllabus_overview: This subject explores social, cultural and ecological determinants shaping health in communities and populations. You will examine critical social factors such as education, occupation, social class, gender, ethnicity and culture as a basis for understanding how social structures, practices and processes influence health, well-being and equity. You will gain an understanding of the interrelationships between people, other species, natural and built environments, human health and public health practice. Responses to public health risks and disruptions, such as climate change, natural disasters and emergencies, will be explored as well as the role of public health professionals in their prevention, management, mitigation and adaptation. You will be introduced to the frameworks that public health practitioners use to contribute to a socially and ecologically sustainable world, and to improve human health
learning_outcomes: Analyse frameworks used by public health practitioners in day-to-day practice and as responses to public health threats, disasters, and emergencies.
Identify and explain social, cultural, and ecological determinants shaping health, well-being and equity in communities and populations.
Discuss the intersection between the environment, public health disasters and emergencies, the health of populations and the factors that influence responses.
Communicate public health threats, disasters, and emergencies in relation to the determinants of health, well-being, and equity, collaboratively and individually

title: ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about elements of environmental health practice, risk management and health impact assessment including the assessment, correction, control and prevention of environmental health hazards in order to promote health, protect individuals, protect communities and prevent disease (for example, health protection strategies such as immunisation, and tobacco, e-cigarettes control and building control). You will examine aspects of environmental health practice and further develop an understanding of the role of environmental health practitioner in Government and industry settings.
learning_outcomes: Conduct health impact assessments to identify and reduce the impact of environmental health issues.
Apply the principles that underpin environmental health practice to the assessment, correction, control, prevention and management of a range of environmental health hazards.
Design programs that manage and communicate risk to respond to public and environmental health issues.
Formulate a risk management plan to reduce risk to human health spanning from an environmental health issue.

title: HEALTH PROMOTION PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will have the opportunity to develop knowledge and skills required to plan and implement health promotion strategies. In this project-based subject, you will develop skills in program planning, implementation, engaging with key stakeholders, leadership skills and project management skills. It will provide you with the links between using heath promotion theories and the implementation needs assessment information to inform, develop and implement health promotion interventions.
learning_outcomes: Identify and examine health promotion interventions and frameworks.
Critically reflect on the implementation of the health promotion project.
Identify and apply project management principles to a group health promotion project.
Plan and implement a health promotion project using appropriate project management approaches and health promotion frameworks.

title: APPLIED HEALTH RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn how to apply research to solve real world problems of the sort that you will encounter in your practice as health professionals. This subject will employ experiential learning principles through nested and authentic assessments. This will give you the opportunity to learn research methods in a sequential manner and receive focused feedback, thereby increasing confidence to use your research skills in future professional roles. From the first week you will be placed in research teams to enable collaboration and support across the subject. In groups, you will begin by developing your skills in identifying a problem, developing a research question and objective, and designing a review protocol to locate, appraise and extract information from relevant high-quality sources. Next, you will conduct a search and synthesise findings in a transparent scientific format whereby you practice the skills of narrative and tabular summaries. Subsequently, you will be exposed to data and gain basic statistical knowledge needed to prepare a data report and contextualise your findings within the broader literature. Finally, student research teams will take part in a group poster presentation whereby the findings from across the semester are summarised and contextualised. You will have the chance to identify future research cycle improvements and reflect on your work across the semester. Additionally, members of the La Trobe research community will present their work to demonstrate practical applications of research skills relevant to health professionals. In conclusion, PHE2AHR is a second year subject, therefore to ensure your best opportunity for success in meeting the subject's intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you have completed at least 120 credit points before enrolling.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and interpret key aspects of research studies
Work effectively individually and in teams to produce reviews, reports and posters
Compare key aspects of research design across different research studies
Prepare and present health research in different formats that can include basic statistical analyses and presentation of data

title: HEALTH EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine theoretical and practical approaches to health education and communication. Based on relevant models and frameworks, you will develop the necessary knowledge and skills to critique, design and deliver health communication and education campaigns using a range of channels and modes. You will build skills to explore and identify the needs of diverse audiences to develop targeted health education and communication strategies and materials, whilst applying culturally sensitive, ethical and equitable perspectives to address population or community health challenges.
learning_outcomes: Understand and evaluate approaches to health education and communication.
Critique and design health education and communication campaigns to address population or community health issues and inequities.

Describe and apply theoretical models/frameworks of communication (e.g. the World Health Organization Strategic Communications Framework, the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Communication Planning Toolkit and risk communication) taking ethical, equity and culturally appropriate lenses.
Use a range of health communication skills to mediate, advocate and enable enhanced health and wellbeing for diverse communities and populations

Demonstrate practical skills, including teamwork, when working with the media (i.e., obtaining media coverage, writing press releases, and writing materials for dissemination via social media platforms) and delivering health education.

title: MENTAL HEALTH AND REHABILITATION
syllabus_overview: Approximately one-third of all individuals reporting somatic complaints also have anxiety disorder and / or depression. Thus, many people presenting to health practitioners will also have mental health conditions. One aim of this subject is for you to be able to identify mental health conditions, and some core principles of working with people with such conditions. People presenting for assistance in rehabilitation settings also frequently present in a state of distress - for instance, persistent pain, anger, anxiety, and shame - which can have a substantial impact on how well such people progress. It's therefore important for you to have a thorough knowledge of these states, how they can impact on a person's behaviour, and core principles of working with people in such states. As well, you will be asked to apply these principles in analysing how to tailor your approach when working with people with these conditions. This subject is designed for second-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second year.
learning_outcomes: Analyse how mental health conditions impact on interactions in clinical settings, collaboratively within a group of peers.
Identify and recognise diagnostic criteria for major psychiatric disorders, including sub-clinical manifestations of these disorders
Identify and recognise how the signs and symptoms of particular mental health conditions can impact on how a person presents in a health setting
Identify and recognise how states of distress can impact on how people present and interact in rehabilitation settings
Select and apply creative thinking and problem-solving strategies to facilitate interactions with people experiencing distressed states

title: MULTICULTURAL PERSPECTIVES ON HEALTH AND WELLBEING
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with a broad understanding of health and wellbeing among Indigenous, culturally and linguistically diverse communities. This understanding is important for people working with diverse populations in healthcare settings who need to develop culturally-appropriate health promotion initiatives. Through guest and expert presentations, workshops and consideration of theoretical frameworks, you will cover topics such as risk factors to diseases, interactions with healthcare institutions and services, Australian settlement and migrations policies, and inequities of gender to good health and wellbeing. Your learning in this subject will be assessed through participation in group work and producing individual written work.
learning_outcomes: Apply a theoretical perspective to argue the need for culturally sensitive health promotion initiatives.

Individually and collaboratively, critically analyse how being of Indigenous, culturally and linguistically diverse, or immigrant background may influence health of these populations in contrast to the host population.
Examine how cultural and social factors contribute to health risk and the experience of health and illness.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH ISSUES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain an understanding of the interrelationship between the physical environment and human health, and environmental health and public health practice. The main themes covered within this subject include global and local environmental issues, environmental justice, ecological sustainability, environmental management and legislation. This subject will also provide you with an introduction to the frameworks that public health and health promotion practitioners can use to contribute to an ecologically sustainable world, and so contribute to improving human health. This subject is taught online. Please note that this subject is designed for students in the final year of their course.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the main ecological and health promotion theories, action frameworks and tools that support public health practice.
Analyse the basic principles of environmental health justice.
Appraise the environmental health literature and communicate environmental health issues to audiences using a range of communication modes and media.
Critically review the global and local human-environment interface as it relates to public health practice.

title: POSITIVE PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the science and application of positive psychology through experiential learning strategies. Key theories and models covering a broad range of positive psychology topics will be discussed. Topics include: character strengths, mindfulness, positive emotions, flow, positive relationships, meaning, goals, accomplishment, hope and optimism, growth mindset, grit and resilience. You will investigate a range of positive psychological interventions by applying them to your own lives. You will also be required to complete measures of wellbeing to gain enhanced self-awareness of your own strengths. You will learn to critically analyse and synthesise evidence-based literature in order to ascertain the contexts in which positive psychological interventions have been shown to be effective. You will complete this subject having set goals that are designed around your strengths and best possible self. This subject is designed for second-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second or third year.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate findings from the academic literature and consider its application to your personal experiences of implementing behaviour change
Apply key positive psychology theories and models to real world situations
Work individually and collaboratively to apply positive psychology principles to promote flourishing in your own life and others.
Analyse positive psychology literature through a critical lens to ascertain the effectiveness of positive psychological interventions

title: PUBLIC HEALTH RESEARCH AND METHODS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the broad array of public health research methods and acquire practical skills to conduct human research in your everyday practice. You will examine the rationales behind how research shapes good public health practice and the diverse paradigms that guide public health research. You will identify ethical principles, challenges and strategies that underpin robust research. Qualitative and quantitative methodologies will be explored with a focus on practical application and critical reflection. Skills addressed include critical appraisal of research, literature review, selection of appropriate search strategies, study design, recruiting research participants, data collection techniques, questionnaire design, and data analysis.
learning_outcomes: Determine the range of practical and ethical considerations in public health research projects.
Select and justify the application of appropriate research methods
Articulate the contribution of research to the broader public health context.
Critically appraise diverse research methods
Synthesise and interpret key aspects of research studies

title: PUBLIC HEALTH POLICY
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the development and implementation of public health policy, including healthy public policy. You will develop skills to participate competently in problem identification and framing, policy development, analysis, advocacy, implementation and evaluation. Key themes are: What is policy? How and when is policy formulated? Who is involved in policy and why? How is policy implemented and monitored? How is policy analysed, reviewed, evaluated and improved? Various theories and frameworks used to explain the policy making process will be introduced. Institutional and broader systems, and structures that influence health policy making will be examined. Particular attention will be given to investigating contemporary environments for policy making, including policy and political, commercial, and broader global environments, and the use of advocacy, evidence and policy instruments such as legislation and regulation. You engage with topical case studies that illustrate key policy issues throughout the subject.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse the major state, national and international institutions, stakeholders and arrangements that shape and deliver health policy.
Evaluate different forces involved in the contemporary policy environment within which health policy making occurs.
Differentiate theories, models and frameworks of the policy process and use them to analyse contemporary health policy issues and arguments.
Analyse existing policies on significant public health or health issues to inform recommendations for improvements.
Work collaboratively to analyse and evaluate policy and policy processes

title: POSITIVE WELLBEING AND COUNSELLING FOR GROUPS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop the core knowledge for enhancing wellbeing and promoting flourishing in group settings. Through exposure to evidence-based literature on topics such as positive emotions, mindfulness, autonomy support, motivation and resilience you will learn how to create positive environments for individuals, teams and organisations. You will also learn the counselling and communication skills required to promote wellbeing and flourishing within these environments. Specifically, you will learn how to work with groups and deliver core counselling skills and strategies within a motivational interviewing and acceptance and commitment therapy framework. This subject is designed for third-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second or third year.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to critique wellbeing technology resources for promoting wellbeing and to develop innovative approaches that improve their effectiveness.
Apply counselling skills and evidence-based counselling strategies for groups within a motivational interviewing framework.
Interpret and apply core principles of positive psychology to design strategies for creating positive environments at individual, group and organisational levels.
Critique personal performance in facilitating positive wellbeing outcomes.
Analyse counselling interactions to identify barriers to wellbeing and flourishing.

title: CHALLENGING CONTEXTS AND HEALTH PROMOTION ACTION
syllabus_overview: The consideration of context is critical to success in health promotion, whether the focus of the activity is on the actions of individuals, communities or governments. Conventional approaches to health promotion often exclude our most marginalised populations. In this subject you will analyse the role of key health promotion principles: ethics, social justice, human rights, community empowerment and participation, and advocacy when developing, implementing, and evaluating health promotion strategies in controversial contexts or with marginalised populations. This subject will assist you to develop critical health promotion skills through exploring potentially contentious health issues such as prisoner health, migrant and refugee health, mental health, alcohol and other drugs, and gender and health.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the links between self determination and empowerment and health promotion activities.
Apply the ‘generic health promotion model’ to challenging contexts and marginalised populations to understand its limits.
Build collaborative teamwork and leadership skills to advocate for health promotion values, approaches and interventions in a board range of settings and sectors.
Identify and explain the strengths and limitations of context and environment in the development of health promotion initiatives.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH CASE STUDIES
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject provides you with an opportunity to examine a series of environmental health issues with the goal of completing a small project on your chosen issue. You will focus on the application of environmental health knowledge and skills to investigate an environmental health issue (such as air, soil, water, food contaminants, noise, infectious diseases, and chemical, biological and radiological incidents) drawing on relevant theories, approaches, principles, and frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Propose evidence-based solutions for environmental health issues
Apply environmental health theories, frameworks, principles, and approaches to local environmental health issues
Investigate environmental health issues using systematic and appropriately documented methods
Integrate the determinants, systems, and structural enablers and constraints including resourcing when addressing environmental health issues

title: FOOD AND WATER SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: This subject draws attention to the impact of food and water systems on human health. You will learn about the nature of the aquatic environment, chemical, biological, and physical processes and how these may be unbalanced by human activity and subsequently affect human health. Adopting a multi-disciplinary approach, you will then examine the basics of food science, the chemistry and biology of food using a HACCP framework, food handling procedures and processes including sample collection for analysis, the scientific basis for modern processing techniques used to extend the shelf life and maintain safety of different foods, chemical and microbial spoilage and contamination of food and factors affecting spoilage (pathogenic organisms and microbial toxins), allergens, basic scientific principles for food preservation, and hygienic strategy and legislation.
learning_outcomes: Review the health implications associated with food and water and assess common approaches used to minimise these impacts
Critically analyse the role of water and food quality management within environmental health practice
Identify and apply regulatory requirements for food and water safety
Apply HACCP and other risk-based frameworks to evaluate food and water safety

title: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR REHABILITATION CLIENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be provided with the skills to facilitate adaptive behaviour change process in clients. The subject will address how to motivate clients to change their behaviour i.e.. motivational interviewing, and adhere to the recommendations of health professionals. As well, students will be introduced to techniques to produce better interactions between yourselves, as future practitioners, and your clients; including skills for dealing with clients who are angry, anxious or highly resistant to change. This subject is designed for third-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second or third-year.
learning_outcomes: Analyse rehabilitation interactions to be able to identify barriers to change, and to critique their own performance in facilitating change .
Identify and describe barriers to adaptive behaviour change in rehabilitation settings individually and collaboratively in a group of peers.
Describe core behaviour change principles and apply motivational interviewing techniques and core communication principles to facilitate behaviour change in rehabilitation settings.

title: CULTURE, SOCIETY, GENDER AND HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, we invite you as future health professionals to consider issues relevant to the health needs of a diverse multicultural population in Australia in terms of gender. You will explore current theoretical perspectives of gender and how these can be applied to better understand the impact gender has in relation to individuals, family and culture. This is examined with a particular focus on the health industry, workplaces, politics, sexuality, media and gender-based violence. Through lectures, directed reading and tutorials, you will explore how gender intersects with health within social, cultural and political contexts.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast how culture, society and gender may influence the delivery and impact of services provided by a range of health providers.
Compare and interpret historical, social and cultural influences that shape current thinking on gender and sex.
Conduct a gender analysis of public health issues, policy or program to develop a gender transformative approach to support future patients/clients/populations.
Identify, describe and compare the current theoretical perspectives of gender.

title: RURAL HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will expand their knowledge of the Australian rural health context, as well as be introduced to concepts in rural health practice. Using a public health framework, students will explore differences between rural and urban health status and the relationship to broader social determinants. In doing so, the implications for health policy, rural health service delivery and professional practice are examined. Students also have the opportunity to review discipline-specific professional practice in a rural setting.
learning_outcomes: Discuss differences in health outcomes between rural and metropolitan Australians in relationship to socio-environmental characteristics of rural and remote areas.
Apply concepts of practice issues for working in rural and remote Australia.
Analyse and discuss models of health care service delivery available to rural communities and how this impacts on access to health care.
Engage with colleagues and participate in an online environment for the exploration and discussion of rural and remote health contexts and concepts in Australia.

title: DRUGS, HEALTH AND SOCIETY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to public health perspectives on alcohol and other drugs. The subject will give you better understanding of harm minimisation and health promotion approaches that are currently practiced and develop your capacity to critique the complexity of health issues in modern society. The subject provides the historical context to drug use problems and encourages you to think creatively about difficult issues. Popular myths about drugs and drug use will also be addressed. This subject addresses La Trobe's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Essential, which entails developing ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas and taking calculated risks to create change. This subject is designed for third-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second or third- year.
learning_outcomes: Identify, describe and explain public health perspectives on alcohol and other drugs including harm minimisation and health promotion.
Examine and critique the social and policy contexts of harm reduction practice employed in Australia.
Review and critique the current theoretical and empirical literature with respect to the harm minimisation of both licit and illicit drugs.
Understand the specific health outcomes associated with the use of licit and illicit drugs, including implications for the development of community-based responses.
Work collaboratively in a student team to formulate and present an argument about a contemporary drug-related issue.

title: HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain familiarity with the health care systems used around the world and will compare and contrast underlying rationales, policies and aims in the context of societal needs and resource demands. The interface between health and politics, economics and social structure will be considered and you will analyse the comparative advantages and disadvantages of approaches to health care provision. Topics to be covered include public and private systems, decentralised health care, national contributory plans such as Medicare, and social insurance, among others. Case studies will be drawn from health care systems around the world.
learning_outcomes: Compare, contrast and evaluate the rationale and aims of different types of health systems.
Critically review the political, social and economic forces that contribute to health care choices at the national level.
Identify, analyse and evaluate challenges faced by health care systems.
Analyse the ways in which the orientation and structure of the health care system relate to health care practice.

title: LIVING WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine chronic conditions with emphasis on issues pertaining to the management of these conditions at a community level. There will be a concentration on theories and constructs relevant to healthy self management and effective social support for those living with chronic conditions. The content of the subject includes a presentation of the World Health Organization's classification systems relevant to disability (ICIDH - The International Classification of Impairments, Disabilities, and Handicaps, ICF - International Classification of Functioning) and an illustration of the application of this framework to chronic illness conditions across the life-span. This subject is designed for third-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your second or third year.
learning_outcomes: Apply chronic disease management knowledge and skills to health promotion/education practice.
Apply the ICF framework to chronic conditions across the lifespan.
Analyse how policy and community services can impact on persons living with a chronic condition.
Analyse how psychosocial factors can impact on persons living with a chronic condition, independently and collaboratively within a group of peers.

title: LAW AND MANAGEMENT IN HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about ethics, law and management in the Australian context, and how they will influence, or be the focus of, your practice as health professionals. An understanding of ethics, law and management pertaining to the fields of health care and public health is important for students studying in diverse professional areas including health promotion, public health, allied health, paramedicine, nursing, dentistry, occupational health and environmental health.
