Using contemporary resource materials, case studies and online peer to peer discussions, you will develop an understanding of fundamental concepts in the fields of ethics, law and management; gain experience in researching and discussing ethical, legal and managerial aspects of their practice as health professionals; and acquire basic skills in fundamental areas of management and in applying ethical principles.
learning_outcomes: Explain and assess the nature, role and effectiveness of management practices and processes operating in the health system, such as quality and change management, and argue the case for improvements
Critically examine the roles of a variety of policy makers, governing bodies, organisations, organisational leaders, managers and teams in the health sector
Identify, apply and discuss ethical principles and theories and form views on ethical issues in professional practice
Critically discuss how law is made in Australia, and how major laws and regulations guide health care and public health practice.

title: HEALTH PROMOTION PLANNING AND EVALUATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will examine various frameworks, models and approaches related to health promotion evaluation planning. You will gain knowledge and build skills to undertake the planning of an evaluation of a health promotion initiative. You will develop an understanding of the levels of evaluation and capability in choosing appropriate methods for each level of evaluation. You will have the opportunity to develop an evaluation plan that incorporates community participatory approaches, data collection, measurement quality and ethical considerations.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and apply community participatory approaches to health promotion evaluation.
Identify and apply ethical considerations when undertaking a health promotion evaluation.
Develop an evaluation plan for a health promotion initiative.
Individually and with peers apply and analyse evaluation approaches, measurement quality and data collection for health promotion practice.

title: SPORT AND EXERCISE PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will focus on the scope, aims and techniques of sport and exercise psychology. The scope of sport psychology is vast and expanding and goes beyond the sporting field. Sport and exercise psychology aims to enhance both performance and wellbeing through the application of psychological principles. This field goes beyond the goal of winning, focusing on improving various aspects of life, including sport, fitness, health and overall enjoyment. This subject combines theory with practical application, employing cognitive-behavioural techniques to boost motivation, reduce competition anxiety, foster teamwork and manage stress in various areas of life such as work, study and family. It also addresses issues such as injury management, promoting physical activity, substance use awareness, working with diverse populations and navigating life transitions. This subject is designed for third-year students. To maximise your chances of success in achieving the intended learning outcomes, it is recommended that you complete this subject in your third- year.
learning_outcomes: Analyse performance scenarios and identify tailored solutions to influence positive behaviours in sport and exercise settings.
Demonstrate an understanding of the psychological influences on injury risk, rehabilitation, and performance to improve outcomes for individuals and multi-disciplinary teams.
Collaborate as part of a team to analyse the impact of psychological factors on athlete performance, and develop an evidence-based intervention to improve performance.
Understand and apply Sport and Exercise Psychology theories and evidence to increase performance in sport and exercise settings.

title: PARTICIPATORY FIELD PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will undertake a work-based placement, either in a relevant external organisation or agency, or internally at La Trobe University. This allows you to engage in approved tasks designed to achieve specific learning objectives relating to continuous and life-long learning in a service-teaching mode. The aim of the subject is to provide you with an opportunity to interpret and apply theoretical concepts, in a supervised setting, to expand relevant skills, knowledge and attitudes. Your placement could include projects and activities in a wide range of programs and services, including mental health, disability, multicultural health, aged care, LGBTIQ health, Indigenous health, homelessness and housing, and refugee health. The seminar series accompanying the placement will orient you to professional and practical considerations of a work environment and allow you to gain a broad perspective about potential employment possibilities. Students must meet all subject requirements, including hurdles: Compliance with pre-placement WIL documentation and immunisation requirements, successful completion of minimum 80 hours (maximum 120 hours) on placement (pass grade required), and attainment of >50 marks for total coursework assessments. Any face-to-face placements need to be undertaken in Australia (and not overseas).
learning_outcomes: Reflect on the experience of work-based learning in the field.
Formulate a placement plan, including objectives, responsibilities and outputs.

Apply knowledge, skills and attitudes from a health science discipline (i.e., Health Promotion, Public Health, Health and Sustainability, Rehabilitation Counselling, Sports Counselling and Athlete Welfare, or Health, Wellbeing, and Performance) to field placement activities under supervision.
Evaluate the placement setting as a site for continuous learning using relevant ethics, practice and discipline-based frameworks.

title: HEALTH RESEARCH METHODS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn the fundamentals of research methodologies to conduct scientifically sound health science research. You will develop skills in literature searching, writing a literature review and applying relevant theories. This subject will equip you with an understanding of the research methods used in health disciplines and help you to carry out your honours research project. You will learn to critically evaluate various research approaches and explore methods for addressing research questions and objectives, as well as techniques for recruiting research participants and collecting or extracting data.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competence in sampling, recruitment, and data collection or extraction methods.
Reflect on and evaluate the strengths and limitations of methodological approaches for addressing specific research questions.
Critically appraise research designs in health sciences and evaluate their applicability to different research contexts
Conduct a literature review to identify knowledge gaps and formulate appropriate research question(s) grounded in current evidence.
Integrate research questions, theoretical positions, methodological choices, and empirical evidence to produce an aligned and coherent research approach.

title: ART THERAPY PLACEMENT AND SUPERVISION A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will participate in group supervision and complete work-based learning as a trainee Art Therapist over 250 hours plus a minimum of 22 hours of small group supervision totaling 272 hours. The 250 placement hours includes 90 hours of direct client contact. Attaining the requisite placement and supervision hours will enable you to meet the professional registration requirements of the Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapies Association (ANZACATA) and the Australian Counselling Association (ACA). In addition to work based learning and supervision classes, you will participate in a range of activities to prepare for placement, including an expression of interest interview to support the placement allocation process, a Placement Preparation Workshop, and 7 individual workshops during the semester. Placement and Supervision is aimed to develop your skill base as a health professional in a clinical or community-based setting. You will be expected to deliver art therapy services that are tailored to the needs of the client group and agency framework, in collaboration with your site supervisor, agency colleagues and clients you will develop initial clinical practice skills including writing progress notes, application of ethical and legal principles and professional self care. To develop clinical competencies as a trainee art therapist, you will reflect upon clinical experience through art making and discussion with peers during small-group supervision class. Here you will explore strategies for managing this initial period of professional development within your placement setting, alongside other trainee art therapy students and facilitated by an art therapist-educator with clinical expertise. You will share and present material from your work with individual clients and groups, to begin to develop an understanding of evidence-based art therapy practice, clinical reasoning, client experience, therapeutic process, and the therapeutic relationship.
learning_outcomes: Identify and implement evidence-based art therapy approaches responsive to client needs and service setting.
Apply interpersonal skills and techniques that build effective, ethical therapeutic alliances with clients.
Articulate clinical reasoning through documentation and synthesis of art therapy observations.
Examine clinical strengths and limitations through reflective art making and supervisory feedback.
Demonstrate professional practice skills as an art therapy trainee within a team, including accountability, integrity, and professional conduct.

title: DATA MANAGEMENT AND ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore concepts and tools for the management and analysis of data. This subject will provide you with training in data management, analysis, interpretation, and result presentation. You will use analytical software and perform quantitative and/or qualitative data analysis, which will help execute your honours research project. This subject will allow you to gain practical experience in interpreting the outcomes of data analysis, providing and addressing feedback, and presenting data to effectively communicate research findings
learning_outcomes: Use relevant software to manage and analyse research data.
Critically evaluate and respond to feedback on your own work, and provide constructive feedback to peers to enhance collective learning.
Develop and justify a data management and analysis plan based on appropriate analytical techniques.

title: THESIS A1
syllabus_overview: This subject provides practical training in conducting an independent research project, culminating in the production of a thesis. You will develop skills in research management tools, time management, research ethics, and reflective practice in relation to your supervisory relationship. The subject also supports you in identifying and organising additional resources needed to complete your research effectively.
learning_outcomes: Develop and maintain constructive and strategic relationships with supervisors and peers.
Develop and implement effective database search strategies to identify literature relevant to the honours research topic.
Identify and reflect on the practical and ethical challenges in the research process and strategies to address them.
Apply project management skills and tools to support the implementation of the research study and development of a thesis.

title: THESIS B2
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on your learning from Thesis 1. To further advance your research, you will apply your chosen research methods to conduct the planned study and progress, finalise and communicate your 12,000-15,000 words equivalent thesis. In this final stage of your research, you will continue to receive support and guidance through consultations with your supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Write a coherent, well-structured thesis that demonstrates Honours-level research and academic writing skills.
Communicate research outcomes clearly and persuasively in a written thesis of examinable standard.
Apply appropriate research methods to collect and analyse data in accordance with the approved research plan.
Demonstrate autonomy and initiative in managing a sustained research project, including responding to feedback and refining research outputs.

title: THESIS B1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply the skills and knowledge to design a research study and demonstrate your knowledge of the ethical guidelines prescribed by the university and the National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research. You will identify a significant research issue, develop an appropriate research methodology, and prepare a project plan and Ethics Committee submission (if necessary). Throughout the research process, you will be supervised by an academic with expertise in your disciplinary field, who will provide ongoing support and guidance through regular consultations.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical principles and institutional guidelines to ensure responsible conduct of research.
Design and develop an original research plan that outlines clear project tasks, realistic timelines, and appropriate resource requirements.
Implement and manage data collection, extraction, and/or analysis to advance the research project to completion.

title: THESIS A2
syllabus_overview: This subject builds upon your learning from PHE4009 and provides practical training in producing a well-presented thesis. You will critically explore any challenges encountered during the research process, including personal biases and potential conflicts of interest, and simultaneously learn strategies how to address these issues. The subject also supports you in identifying and managing practical problems that may arise in the course of your research.
learning_outcomes: Plan, develop, and draft a well-written thesis demonstrating an integrated understanding of the research process (from initiation to finalisation).
Demonstrate the preparation necessary to effectively communicate research findings.
Critically reflect on cultural values, racism, and stereotypes to demonstrate cultural humility and analyse their impact on the research process.

title: ART THERAPY COUNSELLING SKILLS
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with foundational, intermediate and advanced art therapy counselling skills. Theoretical and experiential learning opportunities will build an effective and well-rounded counselling skill set for work as an art therapist. Emphasis is given to developing key therapeutic skills, including building the relationship, responding to client content and emotions, the intentional use of art-making in therapy, navigating challenges and complexities, embracing diversity and difference, among other competencies. A strengths-based and humanistic approach will be front of centre, but other models and theories will be harnessed to offer understandings of the variety of ways to work with clients. Hands on approaches will develop practical skills, including through role plays, peer work and group discussions. You will be offered many opportunities to think critically about stepping into a role as an art therapist.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate foundational art therapy counselling competencies, through the development of empathic observational skills, reflective listening and establishing therapeutic presence in art therapy
Demonstrate reflexive capacities through developing a creative practice to support professional development and growth as a trainee art therapist
Effectively communicate theoretical understandings of the foundations of the art therapy process in writing
Critically examine the unique therapeutic processes and relational dynamics present in the application of art therapy

title: ART THERAPY WITH ADULTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn the stages of adult development, examine and critique the diagnosis of a range of mental health disorders according to the DSM 5-TR, and develop skills in art therapy assessment appropriate to these populations. You will also develop an awareness of considerations of working with clients from cross-cultural and diverse backgrounds and identities. You will gain an understanding of the bio-psycho-social factors involved in well-being, mental health and ill health amongst adult populations. You will also demonstrate knowledge and increased art therapy skills in working with diverse populations of adults.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and integrate cross-cultural perspectives on mental health and the application of art therapy in adult populations, using existing academic evidence.
Identify and articulate key elements in adult mental health assessment, particularly using art therapy tools, in practical demonstrations.
Communicate clinical information effectively in written and oral forms, individually and in groups.
Work independently and in groups to research and present art therapy findings, evidenced in group projects and assignments.

title: DEATH, DYING AND GRIEF
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will explore a range of end-of-life issues that may be encountered in their work settings. Students will be required to demonstrate a well-developed adaptive cognitive assessment of the experiences of dying and grieving people, their caregivers, and the responses of Australian health and community services, including the ambulance service. Participants will apply an advanced level of communication with a deeper understanding of the social and cultural contexts surrounding death in ways that will influence their personal development and practice as health and human services practitioners.
learning_outcomes: Apply reflective practice and death literacy skills that take account of individual values and meanings.
Critically analyse the literature and transmit analysis related to the end of life knowledge, practices and beliefs.
Identify, through critical engagement and reflection, the various contributions informing notions around death and grief.
Analyse personal experiences with death, dying and grief to identify factors contributing to professional and personal responses.
Communicate well-developed insightful and adaptive skills about death, dying and grief across various contexts.

title: ART THERAPY WITH CHILDREN
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of theories and practices of art therapy with children and adolescents. You will learn about theories of typical and atypical child development and how children systematically develop the ability to express themselves using visual art. Art therapy assessments and interventions appropriate for use with children and adolescents will be presented and critiqued, with a focus on child-centered and culturally responsive practice. This will include working with the system of adults in a young person’s life, such as diverse families, welfare systems and school settings. Through the acquisition of art therapy clinical skills, you will gain the ability to practice art therapy with children from diverse cultures in various settings.
learning_outcomes: Analyse child development theories and, in particular, graphic development.
Evaluate subjective and objective information in child observation to generate fundamental self-awareness as a trainee art therapist.

Critically analyse theories and approaches of art therapy assessment and intervention for a range of mental health issues, attachment patterns, ability needs, cultural differences and the impacts of trauma which present in childhood and adolescence.
Critically engage and reflect upon art-making and play typical of childhood to develop self-reflective skills as a trainee art therapist.

title: GROUP ART THERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will explore group art therapy through theoretical and experiential learning. The focus is on learning about experiential group art therapy, gaining an understanding of art making within a group context, an understanding of group development and the group dynamics process and issues of visual and verbal self disclosure. The impact of image making in groups on the individual student, the group process and the learning about group art therapy practice will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and appraise group art therapy literature and practice, including an advanced sense of best practice standards informed by the specific needs of diverse client populations.

Demonstrate a professional capacity to engage in the experience of a training group and subsequently identify and explain relevant proficiencies in relation to self as a member of a learning group and self as a trainee art therapist.
Demonstrate a reflective and relational capacity to understand group dynamics, through the design and implementation of practical group facilitation experiences.
Effectively communicate a nuanced conceptualisation of the historic development of and contemporary practice of group art therapy through academic writing.

title: MATERIALS AND PROCESSES IN ART THERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, the art in the art therapy experience is explored including the impact of materials use, the context and setting. You will explore the creative process both experientially and theoretically. This subject completes the foundation to art therapy training commenced in PHE4FAA Approaches and Theories of Art Therapy.
learning_outcomes: Apply art therapy theory and professional practice principles to formulate an art therapy approach for a client population
Critically analyse the dimensions of the Expressive Therapy Continuum to determine the appropriate use and impact of different art materials
Critically reflect on the personal experience of engaging in a creative process

title: PROFESSIONAL COUNSELLING PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Working effectively and ethically as a counselor requires the development of a core set of professional knowledge, skills and expertise. In this subject you will examine ethical, legal and professional considerations that are relevant to professional counselling practice in Australia. As well, you will develop the core meta-skills that are fundamental to effective and ethical work as a counselor. These include: the ability to conduct an effective intake interview; how to identify and address ongoing learning needs; the development of effective processes and networks for referral; and how to develop clear formulations of clients’ problems within complex systems.
learning_outcomes: Conduct an effective intake interview, and critically evaluate your performance.
Reflect critically about relevant ethical, legal, and professional considerations to counselling issues
Develop formulations of clients’ problems within complex systems with multiple stakeholders.

Critically draw on the evidence base and available scholarship of practice to evaluate your competence in working with clients with particular conditions in varying contexts, and access professional expertise, supervision, and other professional resources (e.g. referral).

title: APPROACHES AND THEORIES OF ART THERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to a diverse range of theoretical approaches, which constitute and differentiate the practice of art therapy. The practice of art therapy draws on theory from the domains of psychology and creativity. In this subject, you will investigate the main psychological theories which have played a role and those in popular contemporary use. The theoretical constructs introduced within the subject are counterbalanced with an experiential understanding of art therapy process through practicing a series of art making techniques during class.
learning_outcomes: Apply a particular theoretical framework to an art therapy activity.
Analyse and critique the application of art therapy theories in relation to certain populations and contexts.
Critically analyse the wider systemic and cultural influences that impact the historical trajectory of art therapy theories.
Critically review the psychological underpinnings of art therapy theories and evaluate their differences.

title: MENTAL HEALTH COUNSELLING B
syllabus_overview: Once a person has been assessed and diagnosed, the focus of mental health counselling turns to the effective treatment of clinical and sub-clinical mental health conditions. Training for this requires the development of knowledge base and skills that enable the counsellor to design and implement evidence-based counselling interventions that will meet complex client needs. In this subject you will examine how to develop case formulations and appropriate treatment plans and will develop the knowledge and skills to be able to design and evaluate intervention plans utilising strategies and principles from some core evidence based counselling therapies including cognitive behavioural therapy, motivational interviewing, and acceptance and commitment therapy delivered within a person-centred therapeutic framework.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate evidence-based counselling interventions to meet complex client needs, including indications and contraindications
Construct and appraise case formulations using evidence-based psychosocial concepts and literature and clinical understanding of relevant cultural and social factors

Design and evaluate intervention plans utilising cognitive behavioural therapy, motivational interviewing, and acceptance and commitment therapy principles and strategies within a person-centred therapeutic framework

title: MENTAL HEALTH COUNSELLING A
syllabus_overview: Effective mental health counselling begins with a highly developed understanding of the types of mental health conditions that people present with and how they are diagnosed. In this subject you will examine how clinical and subclinical mental health conditions are assessed and diagnosed in Australia. You will critically evaluate the reliability and validity of the most common systems for diagnosing mental health conditions in Australia and the assessment tools used in diagnosing mental health conditions in primary health care settings and more broadly in community practice. You will also be able to demonstrate how to apply evidence-based knowledge to identify the presence of potential conditions that people may have not yet been diagnosed with and how to effectively use assessments of mental health, wellbeing, self-efficacy, pain, and broader social functioning.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the reliability and validity of taxonomies of mental health conditions and assessment tools used in diagnosing mental health conditions, and the diagnoses of clients presenting with such conditions

Synthesise knowledge of the mental health conditions people may present with in rehabilitation counselling and counselling settings, and apply this knowledge to facilitate people’s experiences, behaviour and functioning within broader social contexts
Work collaboratively to apply evidence-based knowledge to recognise mental health conditions with which clients may presenting but not have yet been diagnosed
Critically evaluate and employ assessments of mental health, wellbeing, self-efficacy, pain, and broader social functioning

title: FUNDAMENTALS OF EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM COUNSELLING
syllabus_overview: Working effectively as an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counsellor requires a highly developed set of inter- and intrapersonal skills that are common to all counselling settings. However, it also requires the development of a nuanced set of skills that are needed to work effectively and ethically in these settings. In this subject you will examine the ethical and practical challenges of EAP work which include working with multiple stakeholders and their competing demands, and developing the knowledge and skills to be able to design and implement short-term effective counselling interventions that includes a well-resourced referral network capable of addressing the complex needs of clients.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively to assess the ethical challenges of EAP work, and develop plans to manage the inevitable conflicts between stakeholder demands and ethical practice.
Critically reflect on the practical complexities of working with multiple clients from a single workplace, to be able to counsel effectively and ethically.
Design and plan for the use of different counselling modalities (onsite, offsite, telehealth) to meet the needs of multiple stakeholders in complex environments.
Design and plan to implement short-term counselling interventions and the effective referral networks required to meet the needs of working in the EAP environment.

title: COURSEWORK THESIS A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will commence the first stage of the research process. You will develop the necessary skills and knowledge to design a research study in your chosen discipline and demonstrate your knowledge of the ethical guidelines prescribed by the university. You will be supervised by an academic who is an expert in the disciplinary field. Throughout the research process, you will receive support and guidance through consultations with your supervisor and via workshops. The research workshops will engage you in learning activities to develop your knowledge about how to undertake a literature review, which includes effective data search techniques and the use of the recommended reference management tool, EndNote.
learning_outcomes: Select and justify an appropriate research method
Design and develop a research study in line with established ethical guidelines
Formulate a research proposal

title: COURSEWORK THESIS B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on your learning in PHE5005 to progress your research. You will further develop the skills and knowledge required to undertake a literature review. You will apply your chosen research methods to advance your study and enhance and apply your organisational and time management skills to formulate a research plan. Throughout the research process, you will continue to receive support and guidance through consultations with your supervisor and via workshops.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and synthesise key literature and theories relevant to the research study
Formulate a research plan demonstrating research progress against key milestones
Critically apply research methods appropriate to the research

title: COURSEWORK THESIS C
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on your learning from PHE5005 and PHE5006. You will progress, finalise and communicate your 15,000-word thesis. You will be guided in this final stage of your research by an academic supervisor who is an expert in the disciplinary field. Throughout the research process, you will continue to receive support and guidance through consultations with your supervisor and via workshops. The thesis grade will be awarded after the final submission of your thesis in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Produce a thesis of examinable standard
Create and present an oral presentation, which communicates the research approach, findings, and contribution to knowledge.

title: PLACEMENT AND SUPERVISION B
syllabus_overview: This subject will develop your skill base as a health professional in a clinical or community-based setting. In this subject you will consolidate skills gained in PHE4005 and complete work-based learning in the form of a clinical placement over 240 hours (of which 90 hours are direct client contact) plus a minimum of 24 hours of small group supervision totaling 264 hours. You will be expected to consolidate and deliver art therapy services that are tailored to the needs of the specialized client group, organizational context and ethical requirements. The placement component is designed to meet the registration requirements of the Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapies Association (ANZACATA) and the Australian Counselling Association (ACA). Preparatory workshops will support the placement experience. To extend your clinical competencies, you are expected to discuss and critique their progression in an art-based supervision group while attending placement. You will consolidate skills to establish and maintain a therapeutic alliance, improve interpersonal facilitation skills and increase self-awareness of the quality of your professional practice. You will be encouraged to commit to deliberate practice using learning goals to consolidate improvements in therapeutic skills. You will develop your abilities as reflective practitioners based on your experience of working with clients and through being members of clinical and multidisciplinary teams. You will be directly observed in clinical practice and will develop skills to articulate your clinical reasoning with a focus on clinical excellence.
learning_outcomes: Communicate at a professional level, which enables you to articulate clinical reasoning and an approach that demonstrates a commitment to accountability and ethical conduct.
Implement art therapy techniques and interventions that create an effective therapeutic alliance and demonstrate a high level of interpersonal skills.
Evaluate your professional practice by implementing a reflexive approach that focuses on the needs of your clients.
Demonstrate a reflective approach that is culturally responsive, supports diversity and develops a professional identity.
Critically analyse evidence-based approaches and theoretical underpinnings relevant to diverse and complex client group and settings.

title: PLACEMENT AND SUPERVISION C
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will advance skills gained in PHE5008 and complete work-based learning in the form of a clinical placement as a trainee Art Therapist over 242 hours (of which 112 hours are direct client contact) plus a minimum of 22 hours of small group supervision totaling 264 hours. The placement component is designed to meet the registration requirements of the Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapies Association (ANZACATA) and the Australian Counselling Association (ACA). This subject will develop your skill base as a health professional in a clinical or community-based setting. You will be expected to consolidate and deliver art therapy services that are tailored to the needs of the specialized client group, organizational context and ethical requirements. To complete your clinical competencies, you are expected to discuss and critique their progression in an art-based supervision group while attending placement. You will consolidate skills to establish and maintain a therapeutic alliance, improve interpersonal facilitation skills and increase self-awareness of the quality of your professional practice. You will be encouraged to commit to deliberate practice using learning goals to consolidate improvements in therapeutic skills. You will develop advanced skills as reflective practitioners based on your experience of your clients and through being members of clinical and multidisciplinary teams. You will be directly observed in clinical practice and will develop skills to articulate your clinical reasoning with a focus on clinical excellence.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse evidence-based approaches and theoretical underpinnings relevant to diverse and complex client group and settings, at the level of a practicing professional.
Exhibit your advanced self-management and reflexive skills in supervision to reflect on strengths, professional practice and integrity in the service of clients.
Employ advanced therapeutic techniques and interventions that create an effective therapeutic alliance and demonstrate an advanced level of interpersonal skills.

Communicate at an advanced level within a professional team, including sophisticated articulation of clinical reasoning and engagement in professional practice ensuring accountability and ethical conduct.
Assess your advanced skills in reflective approaches from an intersectional and culturally responsive stance that establishes a professional identity.

title: RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES IN HEALTH SCIENCES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn the core principles and processes for conducting research - a systematic and rigorous process for creating new knowledge on a topic or issue. You will develop crucial research skills, including reviewing the literature, formulating research questions, and collecting and analysing data. Guided by values of effective communication and research ethics, you will be introduced to various methodological approaches to research, with a primary focus on quantitative, qualitative, or review methodologies. Once you have finished the first module, you will select and move into one of three streams for focused learning on your selected methodology, each of which will have unique content and assessments. In the quantitative research stream, you will cover methods such as comparing groups using t-tests, ANOVA, and chi-squared tests, analysing relationships between variables using correlation, linear and logistic regression, examining effect modification and interactions, and longitudinal analysis. In the qualitative research stream, you will learn about qualitative research designs, sampling, methods of data collection (particularly, interviews and focus groups), as well as a range of methods for analysing qualitative data. In the review methodologies stream you will be introduced to the major types of approaches to systematically reviewing research evidence. You will gain an understanding of the main steps in conducting systematic reviews including asking structured questions and developing selection criteria, critical appraisal of primary research, data extraction, and different methods of data synthesis.
learning_outcomes: Design ethical research projects using quantitative, qualitative, or review approaches.
Systematically analyse and critically appraise research evidence and methodologies.
Justify the need for quantitative, qualitative, or review methodologies to address research questions.
Develop competence in applying quantitative, qualitative, or review data collection and analysis methods in relevant contexts.

title: POLITICAL, ECONOMIC AND COMMERCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
syllabus_overview: This subject explores how political, economic and commercial determinants such as power structures, economic systems and resources, and commercial interests affect health and health equity. You will examine the relationship between these factors and how they relate to other social determinants, from local to global levels. The subject will provide you with an understanding of established and emerging conceptual frameworks and tools to understand and critique these overarching determinants of health, including political economy approaches and theories for conceptualising power and the influence of commercial actors. Through analysing case studies, you will apply these conceptual frameworks and tools to local and global public health issues and make recommendations for how political, economic and commercial determinants can be managed to achieve equitable health outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Characterise different types of political and economic systems and their relevance to health and health equity
Critique and differentiate frameworks and tools for conceptualising the political economy of the commercial determinants of health
Critically analyse how political economy shapes the commercial determinants of health at national and global levels
Apply political economy and commercial determinants of health frameworks and tools to analyse health outcomes and inequities and inform the development of recommendations to manage them

title: MANAGING WELLBEING AND PERFORMANCE
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to develop leaders in sport through introducing you to strategic issues in the management of athlete and coach welfare programs, to be able to identify appropriate management and communication strategies related to athlete and coach welfare, and to identify the role of a range of support staff in delivering services to athletes and coaches to enhance their well-being.
learning_outcomes: Critique cultural awareness and gender equality and apply key strategies for managing diversity
Work in collaboration to understand mental health strategies that assist athlete and coach welfare needs and issues
Synthesise the role and scope of key support staff (psychologists/player agents/medical) in impacting athlete and coach well-being and performance
Analyse, critique and evaluate duty of care policies and procedures
Investigate and evaluate the athlete and coach relationship and analyse and apply appropriate management techniques

title: FINAL PROJECT IN ART THERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will complete a research project about a self-implemented art therapy program focused on a specific topic. You will have the opportunity to build on the proposal developed in PHE5ATL or can design a new project. You will learn the key ethical and professional issues involved in the development of an art therapy project for a specific clinical setting, population or practice issue. These will include the importance of critical awareness of current issues at the forefront of art therapy practice and an understanding of the social, cultural, contextual and ethical frameworks for art therapy.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the ethical implications of working as an art therapist with a client population.
Critically examine the implications of art therapy program outcomes in relation to discipline theory and peer reviewed research.
Apply disciplinary best practice to implement an art therapy program that aligns with the ethical guidelines of the profession.
Evaluate the impact and client experience of a self-initiated art therapy program.

title: PUBLIC HEALTH PALLIATIVE CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to public health approaches to palliative care, drawing upon key insights of public health and health promotion and applying them to palliative care. The goal of a public health approach is to develop end of life care strategies and policies for the whole population. Evidence that under-girds strategies for integrated palliative care – care incorporating both formal and informal care resources – will be reviewed. Through the seminars you will be encouraged to explore applications to your personal and professional formation and practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect upon your own provision of end of life care in your workplace or community.
Critically assess values, beliefs and ideas that inform current thinking about preferred directions for end of life care.
Apply public health palliative care ideas to end of life policy and practice.
Critically review the contribution of public health principles and practices to developing the social dimensions of palliative care.

title: AGEING, POLICY AND PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an overview of policies and practices that address ageing in contemporary society. Implications of ageing are reviewed in global perspective. Ageing people’s needs for meaningful occupation and activity, and for social inclusion and participation, are explored. Policies that address the implications of these needs for town planning, community engagement and service provision are considered and evaluated, as are services supporting healthy ageing and quality of life for older people.
learning_outcomes: Learn to critically evaluate ageing policies and programs, and identify potential outcomes and consequences based on evidence and theory.
Develop an understanding of problems and possibilities created by the increasing proportion of ageing people in contemporary societies.
Evaluate contemporary policies and programs intended to support health and well-being in ageing adults.
Critically examine social, cultural and environmental determinants of the health and well-being of ageing adults.

title: ACTION LEARNING STUDY A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will gain practical experience, applying analytical and problem-solving strategies to real health care and public health problems using an action learning framework by implementing the project you have designed in PHE5PMH and using the evaluation criteria developed in your research methods subject. You will complete an action learning project directed at improving health by integrating skills and knowledge gained in the postgraduate programs of the School of Psychology and Public Health and deepening skills in reflection, project management, planning and evaluation. The concept of reflective practice is applied and you will have the opportunity to examine their styles and practice, consider their development needs and how they might ensure ongoing learning throughout their careers.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse issues in health policy, provision or management to develop, evaluate and recommend potential solutions using evidence.
Solve complex problems in the delivery of workplace projects using evidence.
Interpret and apply the ethical responsibilities and duties of care health practitioners have to participants and their data
Reflect critically on their own professional practice and provide insight and feedback to colleagues.
Plan, deliver and evaluate projects in an area of interest in public health, health promotion or health services management.

title: ACTION LEARNING STUDY B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will continue to gain practical experience, applying analytical and problem-solving strategies to real health care and public health problems using an action learning framework by implementing the project you have designed in PHE5PMH, using the evaluation criteria developed in their research methods subject and commenced implementing in PHE5ALA. You will complete an action learning project directed at improving health by integrating skills and knowledge gained in the postgraduate programs of the School of Psychology and Public Health and deepening skills in reflection, project management, planning and evaluation. The concept of reflective practice is applied and you will have the opportunity to examine your styles and practice, consider your development needs and how you might ensure ongoing learning throughout your career.
learning_outcomes: Develop and communicate evidence-based recommendations based on the completed project
Analyse and critically reflect on the development of lifelong learning strategies
Identify, analyse and critically reflect on the ethical implications associated with project work
Analyse and critically report on resolution of complex problems in the delivery of workplace projects
Apply theoretical knowledge to evaluate projects in an area of interest in public health, health promotion or health services management

title: ART THERAPY LITERATURE REVIEW
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine, discuss and critique the literature from art therapy and research methods as it relates to art therapy practice. Diverse research methodologies will be presented and you will strengthen your critical appraisal skills as you analyse texts for quality, strengths and weaknesses. You will learn how to identify key themes across the research related to a chosen client population, and to write a literature review that examines this current evidence. Using what you have learned through this process, you will identify a gap or area of interest that will inspire a program proposal for a client population. Both assessment tasks in this subject (a literature review and program proposal ) are designed to support and further develop your capacity to think critically about client needs and how their needs intersect with the art therapy evidence base. The program proposal will form the foundation for the Final Project undertaken in Semester 2 (PHE5AFP).
learning_outcomes: Complete a critical review of the art therapy literature on a specific topic to analyse an evidence base
Develop an art therapy research proposal for a specific clinical setting and population including resourcing, and evaluation methods.
Critically analyse a piece of research for its overall quality and contribution to an evidence base.
Critically review relevant theory and practice models with an awareness of their theoretical frameworks, methodological orientation and argue their respective strengths and shortcomings.
Critically reflect on researcher bias and relevance of a text to art therapy practice.

title: CULTURALLY RESPONSIVE PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will address the issue of culture and diversity in the practices of counselling and art therapeutic work. You will enhance your ability to work with individuals and groups from diverse cultural backgrounds. Issues of diversity and difference will be more broadly explored in relation to groups within society which are seen to diverge from 'dominant' culture. You will be invited to explore your own values in relation to difference and toleration as the basis for developing 'culturally responsive practice'.
learning_outcomes: Display critical reflexivity by probing onto personal strengths and limitations as an art therapist, in working with culturally diverse populations.
Analyse health and well-being issues from a culturally diverse perspective and articulate the need for culturally responsive art therapy.
Critically review, defend and justify the use of therapeutic skills in art therapy from a multicultural social justice perspective.
Reflect and elucidate on one's own socio-cultural positioning and its impact on personal learning and professional interactions with culturally diverse individuals.
Develop and present a model art therapy practice plan that addresses social injustice and caters to a culturally diverse population.

title: ETHICS AT END OF LIFE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an overview of the issues faced by citizens, their family and friends, caregivers, and other providers of end of life services such as health services, funeral services, and financial services, Social and cultural approaches to dying, and concepts of a good death, that inform ethical expectations and decision-making will be outlined. Ethical imperatives of end of life care, particularly recent discussions of compassionate care, will be reviewed. These ideas will then be applied to a critical examination of the ethical governance of formal and informal care, ethical issues in professional practice, and end of life legislation.
learning_outcomes: Assess contemporary end of life legislation and its implications for particular people, professional care providers, and end of life services.
Identify differing ethical stances on end of life issues and relate these to an ethic of compassionate care.
Develop an understanding of social and cultural origins of contemporary ethical issues at end of life.
Analyse the impact of social and cultural determinants on the ethical decision-making of individuals, social networks, and providers of end of life services.

title: EMPLOYMENT AND DISABILITY
syllabus_overview: The aim of this subject is to provide you with knowledge and skills relevant to job analysis, job development, skills needed for effective job seeking and the maintenance of any employment gained. In this subject you will examine topics that include: (i) effective job-seeker skills training; (ii) job interview and related skills preparation; (iii) supported employment; and (iv) functional job analysis.
learning_outcomes: Interpret, critique, and apply the health and well-being benefits of good work.
Critique the key concepts in the Functional Job Analysis including biopsychosocial and cognitive components of work.
Analyse, synthesise and utilise current social supports that facilitate goal achievement and promote client self-advocacy in employment settings.
Analyse, synthesise and apply current legislation and policy on the rights of individuals within these systems in general, and employment settings.
Interpret and critique a content analysis of a client interview to identify a set of desirable job interview behaviours
Identify and analyse the requirements of job seeker skills training and open employment programs
Implement skill analyses to identify job seeking skills of clients, and assess and evaluate independent living support needs.

title: EPIDEMIOLOGY AND BIOSTATISTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with an understanding of the role of epidemiology and biostatistics in public health. You will be introduced to the main concepts and methods of epidemiology and biostatistics, sources of population data, and how these are applied to identify and address public health problems. You will be introduced to statistical software packages and learn how to use these to perform statistical analyses. You will learn how to interpret the results of key epidemiological and biostatistical tests.
learning_outcomes: Explain how the principles of epidemiology and biostatistics can be applied in public health.
Comprehend the fundamental principles of epidemiology and biostatistics.
Explain, differentiate, and apply fundamental concepts of epidemiology and biostatistics.
Recognise, generate, interpret and communicate descriptive and basic inferential statistics.
Calculate, interpret and communicate epidemiological measures.

title: FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT IN HEALTH SERVICES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to financial management in health services, in particular, systems of finance and budgeting as applied in healthcare.In addition, we review how non-monetary resources are recorded and explore the methods in which organisations secure and manage resources needed, and the financial implications associated with procurement. We explore the difference between organisational and management accounting.Topics covered include; accounting principles, basic analysis and management implications related to financial data and quantitative performance data, and basic techniques of quantitative decision making and operations research for dealing with health service resource utilization decisions. You are also introduced to costing and casemix funding in healthcare. In addition, we introduce the impact of procurement of goods and supplies by health services, including common procurement methods and an exploration of ethics in procurement, otherwise known as probity.
learning_outcomes: Apply conventions of basic principles of accounting, such as relevance, reliability, materiality and timeliness and appreciate implications of cash based and accrual based accounting individually and collaboratively
Using evidence-based skills, analyze, evaluate and critique the implications of the applications of different methods of financing health service organizations, such as activity-based funding

Critique and interpret the performance of a health service organisation using preexisting data and predict outcomes within the five major accounting categories of assets, liabilities, owner's equity, revenues and expenses individually and collaboratively

Analyse and interpret between the information provided through a balance sheet, a profit and loss (or income) statement and a statement of cash flows and formulate these financial statements to provide commentary on a health service organisation's performance individually and collaboratively
Explain the management and implications of procurement of goods and services by health services.
Prepare and defend budgets for their organizations or department and apply basic principles of management accounting.

title: GENDER EQUITY AND HEALTH
syllabus_overview: Gender inequality is now acknowledged as core priority for public health in Australia and internationally. As a ‘super’ determinant, the social construction of gender intersects with all other health determinants to positively and/or negatively impact the health and well-being of Australians.In this subject, you will explore current theoretical perspectives to understand and challenge gender inequalities. Using an intersectional gender lens, you will critically analyse the impact of femininities and masculinities on current public health issues (including gender-based violence). Public health approaches will be reviewed in relation to a spectrum of approaches from gender exploitative to gender transformative. In completing this subject, you will have the skills and confidence to conduct a gender analysis on a health issue, policy or programme, apply this to designing a gender transformative approach, and understand the importance of gender equity to achieving safe, healthy communities.
learning_outcomes: Conduct a gender analysis of public health issues, policy or programs to develop a gender transformative approach.
Identify, describe and compare the current theoretical perspectives of gender.
Apply theories of gender equity to current and past public health approaches, policies and programs.
Critique, interpret and communicate how gender is a critical determinant of health.

title: HEALTH ECONOMICS AND FINANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will be given the opportunity to gain a fundamental understanding of economic principles and their application in health and health care. Basic concepts in economic analysis and the allocation of resources in health care are introduced. The application of economic analysis to health policy issues is explored. This subject should enable students to: provide an economic perspective to key issues in health and health care; and critically appraise health economic evaluation studies.
learning_outcomes: Identify how health care, including providers, are financed and disadvantages and advantages approached in different systems.
Analyse and demonstrate understanding of health expenditure and funding in Australia
Identify, analyse and apply core concepts from health economics.
Analyse how alternative health care programs should be evaluated to set priorities.

title: HEALTH CARE QUALITY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will acquire practical knowledge of contemporary approaches to the management of quality and safety in health care, and the available evidence of their effectiveness. You will examine past and present trends in critical incident analysis in health care and the theories, frameworks and methodologies for quality assurance and quality improvement. Clinical governance, measurement of quality, the consumer voice and human factors are explored, building on content covered in other subjects, as well as your own experiences, to address the complexity of health care.
learning_outcomes: Examine the historical perspectives that have shaped quality and safety in health care, including quality frameworks.
Evaluate the challenges facing quality and safety in health care, applying the processes and tools used for managing clinical risk.
Evaluate the components of clinical governance and the leadership qualities required to develop a culture of safety, quality and person-centred care.
Critically analyse how organisational process improvement frameworks and tools are implemented and monitored to achieve continuous quality improvement in healthcare.

title: HEALTH GEOGRAPHY
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the intersection between spatial environments and health, and particularly investigates the relationship between place, space, and health outcomes and determinants of health. The impact that urban and rural settings, and built and natural environments have on access to resources and services important for promoting health are explored. Distinct methodologies advantageous towards the discipline are summarised, and data visualisation techniques and approaches underpinned by geographic information systems are introduced. Additionally, global public health policies addressing place and space are considered and evaluated.
learning_outcomes: Research, analyse and synthesise the evidence to understand the impact that place and space has on health and wellbeing outcomes and determinants of health.
Objectively reflect on the evidence base and design innovative contemporary queries surrounding the intersections between place, space, and health and health determinants.
Explore and apply advanced theoretical and practical contemporary methods to investigating the intersection between place, space and health.
Critically appraise global policies aimed to address spatial aspects of society and theorise how such policies may impact population health.

title: HEALTH SYSTEMS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on understanding the complexity of health care systems around the world through comparing and contrasting their aims and visions, how they are designed, underlying rationales, policies in the context of societal needs and resource demands. The interface between health and politics, economics and social structure will be considered. You will analyse the comparative advantages and disadvantages of approaches to health care provision in different healthcare contexts. Topics to be covered include principles of health care system design, public and private systems, decentralised health care, centralised control, healthcare financing and national health insurance schemes, and how performance of healthcare systems is evaluated. Themes, issues and trends in health sector reform worldwide are explored.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the orientation and structure of the health care system in relation to health care provision needs for diverse populations.
Compare, contrast and evaluate the rationale and aims of different types of health systems.
Synthesize and critically review the political, social and economic forces contributing to health care choices at the national level.
Critically reflect on and analyse the design and evaluation of health systems.

title: HEALTH POLICY ANALYSIS AND RESEARCH
syllabus_overview: In this advanced health policy subject, you will learn how to do policy analysis, methods for policy research and how to evaluate health policy interventions. You are given the opportunity to explore, within the health field, political institutions, operation and function of government and development and implementation of public and other policies. Different theories and frameworks for health policy analysis are explored in depth and applied to a range of health policy problems. Quantitative and qualitative methods used in doing health policy research are discussed (including, for example, case study research, observational studies, and experimental studies focusing on individual problems and their solutions, political and policy processes, or systems and contexts), and issues involved in designing policy research studies will be explored. Case studies from domestic and international areas of health policy are presented to illustrate some of the enduring issues of policy analysis as well as exploring specific policy areas.
learning_outcomes: Conceptualise the policy process using a range of models and theories.
Design, adapt and use analytic methods for undertaking health policy research.
Choose appropriate theories and frameworks to analyse particular health policy problems.
Critically analyse a range of issues in the design and application of policy analysis and research.
Analyse and apply appropriate data sources for health policy research.

title: ISSUES IN AGEING AND DISABILITY
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an overview of the issues that ageing adults and people with disability face. The intersection of ageing and disability is clarified, and you will develop a critical understanding the resource and access to care disparities faced by both groups. Contemporary policies and programs are reviewed, and support your understandings of contemporary issues faced by ageing adults with disability and/or long-term conditions. The impact of the social determinants of health – for example, culture, and socioeconomic status - on the health and well-being of ageing adults and people with disability are explored. The subject provides essential information ensuring that you are able to apply what they’ve learnt towards the development of policies and programs for people with disability and ageing adults within their career of choice.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate ageing and disability policies and programs, and identify potential outcomes and consequences based on evidence and theory.
Evaluate the contemporary policies and programs meant to support ageing adults and people with disability.
Develop an in-depth understanding of contemporary issues in ageing and disability, and the intersection of ageing and disability.
Appraise the distinct impact of social and environmental determinants on the health and well-being of ageing adults and people with disability.

title: HEALTH LAW AND ETHICS
syllabus_overview: This subject presents an overview of the Australian legal system and legal institutions, and how these relate to health and healthcare. You will be introduced to ethics in public health practice, and to fundamental legal (and ethical) concepts, methods and materials. The subject will provide you with an overview of public health law and other laws affecting the health system and health services. A case-study approach will be used to illustrate the influence of the law on public health and health service provision.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse Australia's legal system and legal institutions
Analyse and apply fundamental legal and ethical concepts to complex issues in health systems and services
Analyse and apply legal theory and principles to regulatory issues in healthcare systems and services
Critique and evaluate major aspects of public health law

title: OPEN STUDIO AND POST-TRAUMATIC GROWTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about theoretical components of open studio practices art therapy, its frameworks of practice and also the concept of post traumatic growth.The subject will develop an understanding of how post traumatic growth can be supported in the open studio format of art therapy along with experiential learning through experiencing and hearing from trained art therapists about how they run their open studio workshops. In particular, you will learn about the role of art materials, processes and product in how they integrate with trauma informed theory to facilitate post-traumatic growth. The central vehicle for this clinical application will be the Open Studio method. You will be equipped with skills in facilitating this approach for clients in clinical settings as well as for people affected by traumatic issues in the general community.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced art therapy interventions, including suitable use of materials to reduce trauma impacts for individuals and communities
Differentiate the various forms of trauma relevant to different contexts and how these impact post-traumatic growth
Articulate and critique the structure, form and purpose of the Open Studio method of art therapy
Working collaboratively and independently, reflect and formulate an Open Studio art therapy program for professional practice.
Demonstrate advanced skills in the application of the Open Studio method.

title: PROGRAM EVALUATION
syllabus_overview: This subject is intended for professionals who have responsibility for planning and implementing evaluations of programs and services in public health and health care sectors. You will develop an in depth understanding and gain experience in applying major frameworks, models and approaches for evaluating public health programs and health services in a range of practice contexts. You will develop an in-depth understanding of the approaches and levels of evaluation, and develop skills required to choose appropriate methods for each level of evaluation. Case studies will be used to develop your understanding of the strengths and limitations of different evaluation approaches. You will have the opportunity to develop a comprehensive evaluation plan and data collection instrument.
learning_outcomes: Develop a data collection instrument, aligned with an evaluation plan, that demonstrates an understanding of measurement quality.
Develop a comprehensive evaluation plan and justify the approach adopted.
Appraise how levels of evaluation are applied to health services and public health programs.
Distinguish between research paradigms and methods to select and apply appropriate approaches to different levels and types of evaluation questions
Critique strengths and limitations of different evaluation approaches in a range of practice contexts.

title: MANAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP IN HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to human resources management (HRM) and the key organisational behaviours in the health sector. In particular, we will situate the function of human resource management inside a broader perspective of management theory and practice. The responsibilities of HRM are identified and discussed. You will also focus on how the broader research into organisational behaviour such as effective teamwork can be applied meaningfully to the health sector.
learning_outcomes: Predict how relevant HR principles, will impact your job and that of a team leader or manager
Argue how organisational factors impact on individuals and their performance within organisational settings
Apply and justify the evidence relating to effectively work groups and teams
Appraise and strengthen your skills in planning and implementing staff recruitment and selection, staff motivation and performance management to your workplace.

title: PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSES
syllabus_overview: The public health workforce requires sound knowledge and skills for anticipating and responding to public health risks, disasters and emergencies. This subject introduces you to: the intersection between the environment and health including the physical environment, climate change, environmental sustainability, natural disasters, and pandemics taking account of the politics; the role of public health professionals and managers in anticipating and responding to public health emergencies, surveillance, and risk management; and the four phases of management (mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery). Public health emergencies disproportionately impact some population groups and as such this subject is necessarily underpinned by the concepts of equity and human rights. Furthermore, key to mitigation, response and recovery is effective communication.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast public health responses.
Identify, describe and analyse current and future public health threats and emergencies.
Design public health communication strategies to aid mitigation, response and recovery.
Evaluate public health threats, disasters and emergencies in relation to the determinants of health, equity and human rights.
Critique the intersection between the environment, public health disasters and emergencies, the health of populations and the factors that influence responses.

title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT IN HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the fundamental aspects of managing health related projects, including the project management life cycle; the functions essential to successful project management; ethical delivery of projects, developing a project management plan; verifying and controlling the project scope; defining, scheduling and allocating resources; and monitoring project quality. Working independently and as a part of a team, you will learn to organise, plan and perform projects, and develop the ethical, critical thinking and interpersonal skills required to understand, analyse, and improve projects.
learning_outcomes: Formulate project goals, determine stakeholders, risks, and project logic.
Develop documentation to achieve project objectives within time, cost and quality parameters.
Design a project plan to meet project objectives and deliverables and ethical conduct.
Identify and document appropriate management tools for monitoring and control of projects.
Communicate project plan for stakeholder review and sponsor approval.

title: HEALTH POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the theory and practice of health policy, including health system policy, healthcare policy and public health policy. You will develop skills to participate competently in the design and critical analysis of policy at a level appropriate to a health policy advisor. The process of policy will be conceptualised in terms of development, advocacy, implementation and evaluation. Key themes are: What is policy? How and when is policy formulated? Who is involved in policy and why? How is policy implemented and monitored? How is policy reviewed, evaluated and improved? Various theories and frameworks that seek to explain the policy making process are introduced and critiqued. Institutional systems and structures that influence health policy making will be examined. Particular attention is given to exploring the contemporary policy and political environments for policy making, and the use of advocacy, evidence and policy instruments for implementing policy. The roles of interest groups in policy process are explored. Case studies are used to illustrate key policy issues.
learning_outcomes: Independently evaluate existing policies on significant public health or health issues to inform development of recommendations for improvements
Differentiate theories, models and frameworks of the policy process and use them to analyse contemporary health policy issues and arguments
Identify, analyse and critically appraise the major state, national and international institutions, stakeholders and arrangements that shape and deliver health policy
Critically analyse and synthesise different forces involved in the contemporary policy environment within which health policy making occurs

title: HEALTH PROMOTION STRATEGY AND PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Health promotion is a key field of practice in public health, drawing on a range of scientific disciplines and demanding an understanding of systems thinking. This subject will introduce you to concepts, frameworks and approaches commonly used in health promotion. You will gain skills in how to conceptualise, design and evaluate evidence-informed health promotion programs and strategies.
learning_outcomes: Design evidence-based health promotion programs and strategies to improve the health of a defined community or population group.
Discuss possible scenarios for the future of health promotion and associated issues including the use of digital technologies and ethics.
Critique, differentiate, and apply the major concepts, frameworks and approaches used in health promotion planning and evaluation.
Demonstrate how to communicate health promotion programs, strategies and messages to the population

title: PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will gain insight into major transition points in the health and equity of populations globally, determinants of health, the principles of public health, and current and future challenges for public health. You are introduced to the diverse disciplines contributing to the organised effort in public health and the vital role of citizens in analysis, advocacy, action, and leadership. Public health successes and approaches to contemporary health issues are explored as well as the intervention methods we can bring together to protect and improve health, prevent and control disease and injury, and reduce health inequalities. These include governance, policy, law and regulation; surveillance and screening; public health education; public health advocacy; environmental change; and social mobilisation. Selected public health frameworks will be used to demonstrate how insights and evidence from multiple disciplines and fields can be combined to detect, describe, analyse and prioritise public health problems, and to design, implement, monitor and evaluate, and adapt responses and solutions.
learning_outcomes: Analyse public health successes in terms of enabling conditions, public health approaches and intervention methods used and measures of success.
Select and apply criteria to prioritise public health problems and their possible solutions.
Critique, compare, and contrast approaches in public health and their roles in relation to ongoing and emerging public health issues.
Critique potential evidence-based interventions to address public health problems.
Analyse and explain the defining characteristics of public health.

title: REHABILITATION COUNSELLING PRACTICUM
syllabus_overview: This subject provides practicum experience in which you have the opportunity to develop and practice rehabilitation counselling skills and to demonstrate competency in specified rehabilitation areas. This may include placement in a specialist rehabilitation facility, other rehabilitation-related health facility or human service agency. In addition to the workplace placement, you are required to participate in classroom-based activities relevant to professional issues in rehabilitation counselling practice. You will develop the knowledge and attitudes necessary for ethical and professional approaches in the delivery of rehabilitation services.
learning_outcomes: Communicate and apply core rehabilitation evidence-based counselling knowledge, organisational practices and client and stakeholder feedback to facilitate client outcomes in complex settings .
Effectively design and implement components of team-based rehabilitation services.
Design, implement and revise services to remain compliant with current organisational values, legislation, government policy and funding influencing rehabilitation practice.
Implement core rehabilitation counselling skills through development of clear, logical and concise reports and communications for effective client service delivery.
Identify and analyse client and stakeholder requirements to develop, implement, monitor, and revise client goals, rehabilitation plans and strategies based on the evidence available.

Identify and analyse client psychosocial barriers to change and develop and implement counselling and technical skills to facilitate meaningful community integration for clients (e.g. secure and retain work).

title: REHABILITATION COUNSELLING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will increase your theoretical knowledge and develop your basic skills in the interpersonal helping process, especially as it applies to rehabilitation. This learning will occur in experiential workshops and online content. Topics include: counselling models, theories and assumptions; basic counselling techniques; counselling clients on problems commonly encountered in rehabilitation settings.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialised technical and creative skills to engage a client in a counselling session directed towards behaviour change and demonstrate the capacity to form a durable working alliance, and assist the client to clarify their presenting issues and the associated feelings

Apply specialised core motivational interviewing counselling skills such as active (reflective) listening, summarising, affirmations, and apply specialised evidence- based knowledge and advanced technical skills to deliver other counselling strategies within a motivational interviewing framework.
