syllabus_overview: In this subject you will discover how your brain works in creating your behaviour, how your brain and behaviour change across the lifespan, how, why and in what way you are different from other people. You will learn about how you sense the world and how you process and understand the information that arises from your senses.
learning_outcomes: Apply an understanding of the biological and cognitive basis of psychological science and demonstrate awareness of the basic processes underpinning these perspectives.
Interpret evidence to prepare and present a persuasive oral argument.
Apply ethical guidelines governing appropriate academic conduct.
Identify appropriate information sources and prepare a logical and well supported argument based upon the current research literature.

title: INTRODUCTION TO BEHAVIOURAL NEUROSCIENCE 1A
syllabus_overview: This subject serves as an introduction to the biological bases of behaviour. Nerve cells are the basic building blocks of the brain. Therefore their functioning and methods of communicating form the basic principles of brain and nervous system functioning. Hence this subject includes introductory lectures on the elements of the nervous system that contribute to the conscious and unconscious aspects of behaviour. There is an emphasis on understanding how the cells of the nervous system function and communicate with each other, thus allowing us to explain how sensory information, drugs, and hormonal changes influence behaviour, as well as how behaviour influences the brain.
learning_outcomes: Develop a logical and well supported written argument and conclusion based on empirical evidence.
Demonstrate an understanding of key areas of neuroscience.
Write an argument on a topic in behavioural neuroscience
Identify and use appropriate information sources to support a written argument.

title: INTRODUCTION TO BEHAVIOURAL NEUROSCIENCE 1B
syllabus_overview: The ability to sense and respond to our environment is critical to the survival of all living things, from the simplest of single-celled organisms to complicated animals like us. In this subject, you will explore how we sense our environment, and how our brains use this information to guide behaviour. You will focus on three broad areas; first, you will investigate the senses, smell, taste, vision, hearing, and touch. Then, you will learn how hormones affect multiple body systems to prepare us to act on our environment and the internal processes that keep our bodies working efficiently. Finally, you will uncover the mechanisms of emotions, learning, and memory. This subject consists of self-guided online lessons and timetabled workshop classes. It is typically taken by students in their first year.
learning_outcomes: Identify and use appropriate information sources in behavioural neuroscience to support oral and written arguments.
Develop and apply an understanding of key areas of neuroscience to human and animal behaviour.
Assess common methodologies and experimental outcomes in key areas of behavioural neuroscience.
Develop logical, well supported and appropriately referenced written arguments and conclusions based on empirical evidence.

title: PSYCHOLOGY OF CLOSE ADULT RELATIONSHIPS
syllabus_overview: This subject will introduce you to key elements and psychological processes involved in close adult relationships. These include areas such as attachment, trust and forgiveness, as well as a specific focus on phases during relationships including dating, commitment, and becoming a parent. Research methodologies used to assess relationship dynamics and functioning will be outlined, and outcomes of research studies explored in depth. You will learn about relevant theories proposed to help us understand the complex dynamics inherent in close adult intimate relationships.
learning_outcomes: Identify and interpret research on close adult relationships to develop logical and well supported conclusions about topics of interest
Articulate the role of individual differences and diversity in theories and research relevant to close adult relationships
Apply an understanding of the key psychological concepts, issues, and phases related to close adult relationships

title: HUMAN RELATIONSHIPS WITH ANIMALS AND THE ENVIRONMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with the knowledge and critical thinking skills required to analyse and address questions concerning how humans interact with animals (anthrozoology) and how they interact with the natural environment (ecopsychology). Throughout the subject, you are provided with a broad overview of relevant theories and methods of scientific inquiry. There is an emphasis on developing practical solutions to challenging social issues such as the use of animals, land and water in food production, conservation of endangered species and companion animal breeding and training. Online learning materials are used to provide information about contemporary issues, with tutorials providing many opportunities for you to engage in discussion, debate and further analysis.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the behavioural, cognitive and emotional capabilities of non-human animals.
Articulate the principles of adaptation, evolution and domestication and the psychological, cultural and ethical bases of human relationships with animals and the natural environment.
Work effectively to identify and interpret evidence to critically evaluate a contemporary issue involving human relationships with animals and the natural environment.

title: INTRODUCTORY PSYCHOLOGY: PEOPLE AND CULTURE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to key areas of psychology with a socio-cultural perspective. People share knowledge with others in society. The shared knowledge (i.e., culture) gives meanings to people’s lives as well as influencing their everyday behaviour, the sense of who they are, their personal relationships and psychological wellbeing. We will discuss psychology of individuals in diverse contexts to understand how personal experiences, including emotions, motivation, intimacy with others and health behaviours are shaped by cultural understanding and social expectations in those contexts.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate sensitivity and knowledge of diversity in cultural beliefs, practices, and communication styles.
Identify appropriate information sources to develop logical, well-supported, and appropriately referenced written arguments based on empirical evidence.
Critically reflect on psychological assessment tools within a socio-cultural context
Apply ethical guidelines governing appropriate academic conduct.
Apply an understanding of socio-cultural perspectives of psychology to human behaviour and experiences

title: COGNITION
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with an introduction to the scientific study of human information processing. It will cover (i) the central theories and issues in perception and cognition, (ii) the processes involved in acquiring, storing, retrieving and using knowledge, and (iii) some of the real-world applications of cognitive psychology. This subject will enable students to: - Develop understanding of human cognitive processes, and the means by which they can be studied experimentally; - Develop an in-depth, critical understanding of research in cognitive psychology, including: perception, memory, language, problem solving and creativity, thinking and reasoning, psychology and the law; - Develop understanding of the strengths and limitations of the information-processing approach, and how it applies to human functioning in the real world. This subject consists of timetabled lectures and tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second year.
learning_outcomes: Apply effective library search skills to identify appropriate research resources for assignments and essays.
Develop and apply an understanding of Cognitive Psychology.
Investigate and present well-structured, evidence-based arguments on contentious issues in cognitive psychology.
Independently interpret cognitive psychological research to develop logical and well supported conclusions for written assessments.
Apply knowledge and skills of psychology with awareness of cultural differences and sensitivity to diversity.

title: SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATIONS OF PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the philosophical, historical and methodological foundations of the discipline of psychology. You will critically examine how theories are developed and used in psychological science and examine how they are operationalised in experimental contexts. As part of a team, you will propose your own research question in an applied area of psychology and present this enquiry to your class, and as an individual you will analyse, present and discuss the results in a written report.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively with peers and independently to identify and use appropriate information sources to support an oral and written argument with appropriate formatting and referencing schemes acceptable to international standards, and demonstrate appropriate ethical conduct (e.g. avoiding plagiarism and collusion) in line with professional expectations.

Design a basic research study on a behavioural phenomenon and develop a logical and well supported conclusion based on empirical evidence, including potential solutions to resolve issues such as cultural bias.

Critically evaluate the research design, analysis and interpretation of a basic investigation in psychology, including identification and description of potential cultural biases arising from psychological research and assessment methods.

Apply an understanding of the historical, philosophical and methodological foundations of psychology, including the ethical guidelines governing psychological practice and research to contexts beyond those of psychology itself.

title: DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about developmental psychology from the earliest period of prenatal development through infancy, childhood, adolescence, and into adulthood and older age. Through lectures, required reading, and online activities, you will be introduced to the key theories and research in developmental psychology, and will use these to think about how each aspect of development lays the foundation for the next phase and the importance of context for development. Online activities and quizzes, and tutorials will provide you with the opportunity to apply understanding of developmental psychology to research questions, case studies, and your own development. You will also contribute to and write up a research lab study report related to a key concept in developmental psychology. This subject consists of self-guided online lessons and timetabled tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second year.
learning_outcomes: Use library resources, databases, and peer-reviewed journal articles to investigate developmental research questions relevant to individuals at different stages of the lifespan.
Acquire an understanding of the major milestones and stages of human lifespan development and related key concepts to critically analyse cases and research in developmental psychology.
Develop and apply knowledge of current developmental research findings to interpret data, generate hypotheses, and reach evidence-based conclusions.
Evaluate and apply research methods to investigate a variety of developmental research questions relevant to individuals at different stages of the lifespan and from diverse cultural backgrounds.

title: SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to a range of theories, methods and topics in social psychology. Social psychology is the scientific attempt to understand and explain how the thoughts, feelings, and behaviours of individuals are influenced by the actual, imagined, or implied presence of other human beings. The topics to be covered in this unit include attitudes, self and identity, person perception and social cognition, interpersonal attraction, social influence, prejudice, intergroup relations, and prosocial and antisocial behaviour. This subject consists of self-guided online lessons and timetabled tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second year.
learning_outcomes: Explain and apply key concepts of social psychology to describing and interpreting social psychological phenomena, including significant cultural differences.
Use spreadsheet and data-analysis software to organise, manage, analyse, and communicate information.
Use database, access journal articles and web-links to identify and evaluate information relevant to the topic of inquiry.
Describe, apply, and evaluate the research methods used to address a variety of social psychological questions.

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL RESEARCH METHODS
syllabus_overview: The two parts of this subject deal with statistical inferences that we can make about (1) relationships between measures gathered from a single group of participants and (2) differences in the group means on one variable gathered from two or more groups of participants. In the first part, we start with correlation between variables and move on to more advanced regression topics of using several variables to predict an outcome. In the second part, we start with the basic principles of experimental design to compare data gathered from the same or different groups of participants. We study the Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) in detail, on how we can use it to establish differences between several groups and, following that, how we can compare means between groups.
learning_outcomes: Prepare data to meet the distributional assumptions of statistical tests.
Use software for statistical computing and select the appropriate analytical and output options.
Select and conduct correlational analyses to analyse relationships between variables and Analyses of Variance to analyse differences between means.
Select the statistical techniques that are appropriate to the research hypotheses being tested.
Interpret and report on the outcome of statistical tests in APA format.

title: PSYCHOLOGY OF CULTURE, COMMUNITIES AND GLOBAL CITIZENSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject will explore the influence of culture on both individuals and communities. You will develop the skills to analyse cultural impacts on thoughts, emotions, and behavioural processes though lectures on cultural psychology and tutorial exercises. This subject will also explore how to build culturally diverse yet cohesive communities by creatively applying the knowledge of cultural psychology, social psychology, and community psychology. Tutorial exercises will provide you with opportunities to explore how to put the basic knowledge into practice when considering issues concerning cultural diversity in communities. Global Citizenship entails deep appreciation of how we live in an interconnected world being able to recognise the global context of concepts, act across cultures and boundaries, and work with diverse communities - now and in the future. This subject consists of timetabled lectures and tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second or third year.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of cultural and community psychology to analyse and explore solutions for issues associated with cultural diversity in communities in Australia.
Identify the basic principles of professional ethics and cultural sensitivity when working with different cultural groups and culturally diverse communities.
Analyse everyday psychological processes and experiences using theories and concepts of community and cultural psychology.
Design and communicate a research project using knowledge of community and cultural psychology.

title: UNDERSTANDING AND SUPPORT FOR AUTISM
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore autism, covering a combination of scientific/research, lived experience, and applied perspectives. You will explore the changing views on autism, from the first proposed accounts to contemporary understandings. You will consider the different presentations of autism, Autistic people's lived experiences, and the different support needs of Autistic people and their families across the lifespan – from very early infancy, through childhood and adolescence, and into adulthood. You will develop broad knowledge of autism, including the early signs, diagnostic criteria and tools, and a range of supports for different needs and life stages. You will explore attitudes and perspectives on autism, locally and abroad, including community perspectives, media representation, and government policy. You will develop essential skills for critically evaluating the wealth of information on autism and the ability to communicate evidence-based information on autism to varied audiences.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate ethical awareness with respect to appropriate citation in written work, and the use of personal information provided through case studies and by guest speakers.
Describe, apply, and evaluate individual history and assessment results to address a diagnostic question related to autism.
Critically evaluate the literature and evidence on issues related to autism, and integrate and present this evidence in a manner suitable for varied audiences.
Identify, describe, and evaluate the historical and current conceptualisations, assessment, and support approaches related to autism.

title: CLINICAL NEUROSCIENCE AND NEUROPSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore contemporary theoretical approaches and empirical findings relevant to various neural structures, processes, and functions underlying humans' thinking, feeling, and behaviour. In particular, you develop a sophisticated understanding of brain development, visual perception, motor and cognitive development, as well as different neuroimaging techniques. The subject also provides an overview of a wide range of neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions, and enables you to critically analyse the benefits of different neuropsychological assessments. This subject consists of timetabled lectures and tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second or third year .
learning_outcomes: Analyse how neuropathology alters typical neural function and how this could be observed in a clinical context.
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of different neuroimaging techniques and neuropsychological assessments.
Explain how the interactions between neural systems underpin various patterns of cognition and behaviour.
Develop and deliver an informative group oral presentation by analysing and synthesising knowledge of various neurological conditions.
Discriminate mental health phenomena by identifying relevant neuroscientific and neuropsychological theories and empirical findings.

title: NEURAL BASES OF CONSCIOUSNESS
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the emerging and burgeoning scientific study of consciousness. This introduction will cover ways in which subjective experiences and phenomenology are now being examined empirically across many disciplines, including neurobiology, medicine, cognitive psychology, and functional neuroimaging. The recent boom in research in this field has not only led to better understanding of consciousness and the human mind but has also sparked considerable philosophical and ethical debate, which will be covered in some detail in this subject. This subject consists of timetabled online lectures and timetabled tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their second or third year.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise research findings and communicate neurological aspects of consciousness and how they influence behaviour.
Identify and describe the most appropriate technique for the measurement of different neurological aspects of consciousness.
Identify and describe neural networks and areas of the brain and their role in conscious and unconscious behaviour.
Evaluate ethical principles and philosophical theories on the neuroscientific investigation of consciousness.

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the ability to evaluate and interpret information gathered from measures and approaches used in psychological assessment. The subject will be comprised of three themes covering measurement theory, individual differences, and psychological assessment in applied contexts. Lectures in measurement theory will cover classical and modern psychometric approaches to the construction, implementation, and evaluation of psychological measures. Lectures in individual differences will extend on the coverage of cognitive ability, personality, and emotion offered in introductory psychology subjects, with a focus on assessment. Lectures in applied psychological assessment will cover the issues associated with the appraisal of behaviours, thoughts, interests and emotions across clinical, educational, and forensic contexts. This subject is a capstone subject in a psychology major. This subject consists of self-guided online lessons and timetabled tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their third year.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the key principles, theories, and concepts of psychological assessment and testing. Demonstrate the application of psychological assessment to real world settings and identify issues related to the appropriate use of psychological assessment in diverse contexts, including cultural and individual diversity
Interpret, synthesise, and report on the outcomes of psychological assessment and develop recommendations based on quantitative and qualitative assessment information.
Develop an awareness of the ethical and professional conduct requirements associated with psychological testing and assessment.
Work independently and as part of a group to evaluate empirical evidence for psychometric properties of psychological assessment tools.

title: PSYCHOLOGY FIELD PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: You will engage in a supervised field placement in an organisation or agency with relevance to applying psychology-related knowledge and skills. You will have the opportunity to observe and engage in activities which assist you to learn about how professionals in related fields work and apply skills. You will reflect on the professional, organisational, and ethical issues relevant to the workplace setting as well as the career skills you will obtain while on the placement. The placement, and associated orientation activities, online activities and assessment materials, and assignments focus on your learning. You have the opportunity to reflect on specific intended learning outcomes related to professional practice.To enrol in PSY3PFP, you must apply for and be offered a placement. You can learn about the application process on the Psychological Science Student Portal. This placement will be undertaken in Australia (not overseas) and hosted by an organisation in Victoria.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate responsible behaviour in the workplace related to working in a team, communicating to a supervisor and work colleagues, and completing relevant documentation.
Describe and reflect on skills relevant to a professional in a fieldwork setting.
Demonstrate understanding of professional and ethical issues, such as confidentiality and legal responsibilities, relevant to the workplace
Be able to examine challenging personal and professional workplace experiences and propose solutions to address them professionally.

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH AND ILLNESS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about the biological, social, and psychological factors that influence our psychological health. You will examine definitions and experiences of mental health and illness from a theoretical, clinical, and public health perspective. Concepts such as stigma, diagnostic approaches, and cultural perspectives will be investigated with regards to psychological health and illness. This subject consists of scheduled online lectures and tutorial classes. It is typically taken by students in their third year.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse different theoretical, clinical, and public health perspectives on psychological health and illness.
Evaluate and integrate knowledge about a range of individual, social and cultural factors that influence psychological health and illness
Critically review the literature to produce a sound written argument.
Work cohesively as a group to deliver a professional oral presentation.
Characterize the contributing factors, perspectives, and diagnostic approaches in clinical case studies, including individual differences and culture.

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL RESEARCH IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject is a capstone subject that brings together, reinforces, extends, and illustrates applications of psychological research. You will conduct an in-depth investigation in an area of psychology and generate a report that has implications for the practice and discipline of psychology as a science. You will apply your knowledge in ethics, research methods, and psychological theories to practical and applied issues, and have an opportunity to reflect on the skills you have learned and how these could serve your career next steps.
learning_outcomes: Investigate, synthesise, and critically evaluate key theoretical features of psychological research.
Use information ethically and with culturally sensitively in the design and conduct of psychological research.
Apply advanced psychological and statistical knowledge to develop creative answers to real-world psychological research questions.
Apply independent learning, psychological knowledge, critical thinking and analytical judgement to write research reports on psychological topics.
Work effectively and collaboratively in teams

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an in-depth understanding of a range of different approaches to psychological intervention for psychological and behavioural problems. The main focus will be on psychological interventions for individuals but the subject will also explore group and public health interventions designed to change behaviour. The theoretical and empirical support for different intervention strategies will be explored and students will have opportunities to analyse the merits or otherwise of particular approaches. Students will learn to apply basic listening skills required in helping situations and explore effective strategies to motivate behaviour change.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and discriminate effective psychological intervention techniques and counselling processes and critically reflect on their application with regard to cultural diversity and diversity of individuals.
Synthesise and critically appraise the theoretical and empirical bases of a range of specific psychological intervention techniques for individuals.
Design and implement cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) tasks to facilitate behaviour change and analyse, interpret, and report outcomes from their application.

title: ADVANCED ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will test operating characteristics, including reliability, validity and norm referencing, and how these are affected by social and cultural factors. You will also examine a variety of commonly employed psychometric instruments of cognitive and psycho-pathological function, focusing on administration and interpretation. We will also consider the scientist practitioner model and its implication for a variety of behavioural and cognitive behavioural psychological interventions. You will apply basic interviewing and counselling techniques and evaluate the evidence informing intervention decisions and exercise in-depth knowledge in psychological assessment and intervention which promotes respect and harmony among all cultures and diverse community.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and choose suitable behavioural and cognitive-behavioural treatment approaches to a variety of presentations including depression, anxiety disorders, and personality disorders.

Apply skills and in-depth knowledge in psychological assessment and intervention that is considerate of and responsive to diversity within individuals, with the intention to promote respect and understanding among all cultures and diverse communities.
Apply skills in basic interviewing and counselling techniques.
Critically evaluate the principles underpinning evidence-based assessment of personality and intelligence and its common applications.
Choose suitable approaches to address psychological diagnostic questions and to analyse and interpret the data arising from these.

title: ADVANCED TOPICS IN PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, we will provide you with the knowledge and skills to safeguard your wellbeing and deal effectively with others in the workplace while also building a more nuanced understanding of how to critique literature for a specific research question. This subject will have two lecture streams: STREAM 1: Workplace wellbeing STREAM 2: Synthesising Research In stream 1, you will be provided with a series of interactive 2-hour seminars where you will learn how to apply psychological theories and skills to better navigate your way through the workplace. You will learn about team dynamics and how to measure and reduce the impact of work stress. The stream 1 lectures will be paired with a two-hour tutorial to allow for a deeper dive into the material. In stream 2, you will receive a 2 x 1 hour symposiums on some new, and sometimes controversial, research in psychology. This stream will ask you to dig deep into the research area and develop an advanced understanding of the field, while highlighting the complexities of understanding the implications of seemingly disparate research findings.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate issues in areas of psychology .
Demonstrate in-depth knowledge of the current topical areas in psychology.
Communicate proficiently and professionally when working individually or in a group setting.
Recognise the importance of the relationship between knowledge of the scientific discipline of psychology and the application of this knowledge in the practice of psychology.

title: ETHICS AND PROFESSIONAL ISSUES IN PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject helps you learn about professional and ethical issues that may arise in work as a psychologist or a helping professional. The topics include the contributions of some key professional organisations to the work of psychologists and health practitioners, ethical principles, professional and community standards, current relevant legal frameworks, and approaches to making ethical decisions. You will learn a method for systematically making ethical decisions considering the professional context, by applying an ethical decision-making model to specific cases.
learning_outcomes: Describe a range of legal issues relevant to psychologists.
Access information about and describe the aims and functions of key organisations that have relevance to the psychology discipline and profession.
Apply ethical principles, a professional code of ethics and a broad ethical decision-making model to specific cases.

title: METHODS OF INQUIRIES IN PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject will consolidate and further develop your knowledge, skills and appreciation of a variety of research methods in psychology including qualitative, meta-analysis, multivariate statistics, model testing approaches, quantitative designs and cross-cultural research methods, through weekly online modules and tutorials. Discussion of research designs will strengthen your analytical skills and ability to choose suitable research designs. Tutorial activities and assignments will enhance hands-on competencies in data analysis and report writing.
learning_outcomes: Organise and report analytic procedures and outcomes effectively and appropriately for scientific communication.
Demonstrate an understanding of methodological and ethical issues associated with quantitative and qualitative research and cross-cultural investigation.
Plan and conduct data analysis, including conducting power analysis, data preparation, and testing assumptions.

Critically evaluate the strengths and weakness of a specific research design and a data analytic procedure in collaboration with other students, and choose suitable methods to address psychological questions.

title: HONOURS PSYCHOLOGY THESIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will work closely with your supervisor to conceptualise, plan, execute and report a research project relevant to a field of psychological science. Writing and oral presentation skills will be developed, along with ethical thinking and research literacy. Diverse project choices are available with supervisors drawn from across the Department of Psychology, Counselling and Therapy, research centres and partner organisations.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical principles in psychological research.
Conduct research projects in psychology and critically interpret findings
Communicate research methods and outcomes to peer and lay audiences
Apply suitable methodologies to answer psychological questions and draw appropriate conclusions.
Apply critical skills and in-depth knowledge in a field of study of psychology that promotes respect and harmony among all cultures and diverse communities

title: ETHICS AND SKILLS FOR PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This foundational training subject will assist you in developing the professional competencies and micro-skills needed for counselling and clinical work and will prepare you for initial sessions with clients. You will observe trained psychologists working with clients via recordings. You will engage in role-play with peers and have multiple opportunities to be observed by a qualified psychologist and receive real-time feedback. In addition, you will receive focused training in ethics, professional issues and working in a way that is culturally informed and inclusive of diversity.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in the early stages of culturally-informed assessment and formulation.
Implement fundamental counselling and process skills in simulated clinical settings
Critically reflect on ethical, legal and professional matters relevant to clinical practice

title: ADVANCED PROCESS SKILLS
syllabus_overview: This subject will allow you to extend and expand upon your developing process skills. You will be given the opportunity to learn about, discuss, and practically apply advanced process skills in more depth, such as maintaining boundaries, challenging clients, managing difficult behaviour, dealing with conflict in the therapeutic relationship and managing endings.
learning_outcomes: Integrate advanced process knowledge and skills in diverse contexts, professional settings, and interprofessional teams in a culturally-informed way.
Assess and formulate process issues in clinical practice across the lifespan.
Integrate process considerations in assessment and formulation of complex client presentations and ethical, legal or professional issues.

title: ADVANCED RESEARCH METHODS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, Masters degree candidates continue to work on their approved research project that addresses a research question relevant to their specialised endorsed area of practice in psychology, and develop and submit a research report based on this research project.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and critically analyse the results using appropriate methods and with consideration of cultural context.
Execute research that follows ethical guidelines and practices in an endorsed area of practice in psychology.
Communicate the findings of the research study in a written report format.

title: PROFESSIONAL PSYCHOLOGY PRACTICUM
syllabus_overview: This practicum subject involves practical placement(s) at external placement agencies. Please be aware that this subject includes in-person placement requirements. Students are expected to complete these placements in Australia. You will begin to work as a provisional psychologist under the supervision of a Psychology Board of Australia Approved Supervisor. A total of at least 300 hours practicum experience, including a minimum 80 hours direct client contact and 40 hours of supervision, is required to achieve the required competencies and meet professional placement obligations. If at the final placement review, competencies are not met, you may be offered a set number of additional placement hours and/or supervision hours to work towards competency. Unscheduled online seminars are to prepare you for placement. You will need to watch these recorded seminars prior to commencing placement to be deemed 'compliant' on InPlace (and ready for placement) and to be able to apply for scholarships/bursaries. You will not be able to commence placement until all compliance requirements have been met. Online case analysis tutorials will support you in your casework and facilitate group case discussions designed to mirror case conferencing in the field. You will sit an Objective Structured Clinical Exam (OSCE) on case conceptualisation. The aim of the OSCE is to (1) determine if you have met the required level of competency at this stage of your training and (2) are ready to commence your subsequent internship.
learning_outcomes: Apply assessment, case formulation and intervention skills based on evidence-based professional psychology practice
Exemplify professional integrity by identifying and discussing ethical issues of relevance to professional psychology practice and demonstrating commitment to their application

Demonstrate self-care, self-awareness, and self-reflection skills including appropriate use of supervision and supervisory feedback to reflect on strengths, level of competence and the impact of one’s own values and beliefs on practice

Communicate clearly and coherently with diverse clients and treating professionals in the management of different types of presentations, demonstrating empathetic understanding, professional judgement and reasoning that is culturally informed and inclusive of diversity

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: This practicum subject enables you to achieve the Stage 4 competencies required for practice by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. It takes place in an external agency relevant to the area of practice endorsement in clinical psychology, and/or the Psychology Clinic in the School of Psychology and Public Health.
learning_outcomes: Practice clinical psychology skills in a way that is culturally informed and inclusive of diversity at an advanced level of competence.
Apply clinical psychology knowledge and skills at an advanced level of competence in work with clients.
Communicate respectfully and effectively with clients and other health professionals at an advanced level of competence, both in writing and through other channels.
Apply and adhere to required standards, policies, and procedures, including the APS Code of Ethics, at an advanced level of competence.

title: ADVANCED CLINICAL PRACTICUM A
syllabus_overview: This practicum subject enables you to achieve the Stage 3 competencies required for practice by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. It takes place in an external agency relevant to the area of practice endorsement in clinical psychology, and/or the Psychology Clinic in the School of Psychology and Public Health. You must complete all assessments at 70% or higher.
learning_outcomes: Communicate respectfully and effectively with clients and other health professionals at a high level of competence, both in writing and through other channels.
Practice clinical psychology skills in a way that is culturally informed and inclusive of diversity at a high level of competence.
Apply clinical psychology knowledge and skills at a high level of competence in work with clients.
Apply and adhere to required standards, policies, and procedures, including the APS Code of Ethics, at a high level of competence.

title: ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT OF MAJOR DISORDERS
syllabus_overview: The subject is designed to provide an opportunity to learn in some depth about treatments for major disorders in adult populations, from a standpoint of the critical use of clinical practice guidelines and evidence based practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise evidence based practice
Demonstrate a familiarity with specific treatments for major disorders and their underpinning theoretical models
Demonstrate an ability to participate and lead a peer managed professional development group

title: FOUNDATION SKILLS IN COGNITIVE BEHAVIOURAL THERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject content is based on the Cognitive Behavioural Therapy model (CBT). CBT is a relatively short-term intervention aimed at solving current problems through the evaluation of unhelpful thinking and behaviour. CBT has been shown to have considerable empirical effectiveness for a range of psychological presentations. You will gain an overview of cognitive and behavioural models of psychological disorders, with a particular focus on interventions for high prevalence disorders such as anxiety and depressive disorders. The role of individual case formulation and treatment planning as ways to tailor interventions to account for cultural differences and client diversity, will be emphasised. You will focus on the development of intervention skills relating to CBT, and review process issues in CBT interventions.
learning_outcomes: Construct and appraise case formulations and intervention plans based on cognitive and behavioural models, accounting for cultural differences and client diversity.
Assess the empirical base of CBT interventions including indications and contraindications.
Identify and apply evidence based cognitive and behavioural intervention strategies for common presenting problems such as mild-moderate anxiety and depressive disorders.
Understand cognitive behavioural models of a range of depressive and anxiety disorders.

title: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE IN PROFESSIONAL PSYCHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces key research methodologies and skills relevant for evidence-based practice. You will learn to source, evaluate and apply research findings to developing effective psychological interventions.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to critically appraise and reflect on a research topic relevant to professional psychology.
Develop advanced knowledge in a topic relevant to evidence-based practice in professional psychology.
Apply advanced research skills and incorporate knowledge of culture to professional practice
Interpret and coherently communicate scientific findings in written and oral format

title: ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT OF CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about identifying, assessing, and treating child and adolescent mental health issues and neurodevelopmental conditions. You will learn to analyse child client presentations and identify appropriate therapeutic interventions using the biopsychosocial and developmental models. Other useful models and approaches to understanding the problems of children and adolescents - such as family systems theory, attachment theory, genetics, transdiagnostic psychology, and neurodevelopmental neurobiology - will also be introduced where relevant. During the tutorial each week, you will consolidate your knowledge and learn practical clinical and therapeutic skills in working with children and families.
learning_outcomes: Consider the influence of context (family, peers, school, society) and role of diversity (e.g. cultural, linguistic, gender, and other) in navigating the assessment and treatment of young people.
Discriminate, select, and apply appropriate evidence-based models, assessments, and interventions for child mental health and neurodevelopmental problems.
Design an evidence-based treatment plan for mental health issues of childhood and adolescence; with consideration of the role of the psychologist within multidisciplinary health care.
Identify and consider moral and ethical quandaries specific to the child and adolescent context.
Describe child and adolescent mental health conditions and neurodevelopmental problems with respect to diagnostic criteria, clinical features, prevalence, aetiology, and support needs.

title: HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject deals with a number of aspects of health psychology in health promotion and clinical health psychology in some depth. This subject will build on areas of health psychology that you will most likely have covered in undergraduate health psychology but will be explored at an advanced level.
learning_outcomes: Develop appropriate evidence-based interventions related to a particular chronic disorder and its consequences.
Apply psychological principles to key areas of clinical health psychology.
Demonstrate understanding of the ethical/cultural basis of clinical psychology practice with regard to interconnection between health and mental health.

title: PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides in-depth training in the area of psychological assessment, integrating the scientist-practitioner roles of the professional psychologist. The focus is on concepts and techniques that are foundations for other subjects in the course. The assessment process, emphasising a problem-solving orientation, is examined, taking into account life-span and cultural issues. Psychometric theory, and its relationship to testing, is reviewed. Principles of assessment interviewing are outlined. The contribution of tests and testing to this process is considered in detail. Techniques of test administration and interpretation, with a particular emphasis on the Wechsler Intelligence Scales, are explored. Communication of psychological assessment outcomes, particularly through report writing, is given close attention. Lectures and seminar presentations will be augmented through self-directed experiential activities.
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively to clients, families, referral agencies, and other psychologists about the psychological assessment with understanding of how to incorporate assessment results into treatment planning.
Write assessment reports to a professional standard and suitable for different referral agencies or contexts.
Apply structured history- taking interview as the preliminary component of psychological assessments.

Apply advanced understanding of the principles and theoretical background of psychological assessment with an understanding of issues relating to (i. reliability and validity, (ii. development and aging, and (iii. culture.
Administer psychological tests taking into account issues of validity and reliability, and contextual issues related to development and aging, and cultural diversity.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICUM A
syllabus_overview: In this first-year subject, you begin developing your clinical skills by engaging in supervised practice on a 130 hr internal placement as a provisional psychologist. This supervised practice involves skills training, observation and client sessions within the La Trobe University Psychology Clinic. There will be a weekly Clinic Team meeting involving all trainees. You will also attend a Case Analysis meeting during semester where cases from the La Trobe University Clinic are presented and discussed.
learning_outcomes: Review and analyse the observations made of clients and demonstrate clinical judgement and reasoning.
Demonstrate proficiency in the early stages of assessment, formulation and intervention in the context of the Cognitive Behavioural Therapy framework in working with clients.
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of legal and professional matters in relation to professional work with clients in clinical psychology.
Actively participate and articulate clinical reasoning within a clinical team.
Demonstrate knowledge of counselling skills applied to the engagement of clients.

title: CLINICAL PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: This practicum subject takes place in either the Psychology Clinic in the School of Psychology and Public Health or an external agency. You must complete all assessments at 70% or higher.
learning_outcomes: Apply assessment and treatment skills based on evidence-based clinical psychology practice
Exemplify professional integrity by identifying and discussing the ethical/cultural basis of clinical psychology professional practice
Engage professionally with a range of clients and types of practice
Sensitively communicate outcomes of psychological assessments and treatment decisions
Demonstrate a reflective and flexible approach to clinical psychology practice

title: PROFESSIONAL PSYCHOLOGY PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: This practicum subject involves practical placement(s) at external placement agencies. Please be aware that this subject includes in-person placement requirements. Students are expected to complete these placements in Australia. You will begin to work as a provisional psychologist under the supervision of a Psychology Board of Australia Approved Supervisor. A total of at least 300 hours practicum experience, including a minimum 80 hours direct client contact and 40 hours of supervision, is required to achieve the required competencies and meet professional placement obligations. If at the final placement review, competencies are not met, you may be offered a set number of additional placement hours and/or supervision hours to work towards competency. Unscheduled online seminars are to prepare you for placement. You will need to watch these recorded seminars prior to commencing placement to be deemed 'compliant' on InPlace (and ready for placement) and to be able to apply for scholarships/bursaries. You will not be able to commence placement until all compliance requirements have been met. Online case analysis tutorials will support you in your casework and facilitate group case discussions designed to mirror case conferencing in the field. You will sit an Objective Structured Clinical Exam (OSCE) on case conceptualisation. The aim of the OSCE is to (1) determine if you have met the required level of competency at this stage of your training and (2) are ready to commence your internship.
learning_outcomes: Competently communicate outcomes of psychological assessments and treatment decisions
Exemplify professional integrity by identifying and discussing the ethical basis of psychology professional practice
Apply assessment and treatment skills based on evidence-based professional psychology practice
Communicate clearly and coherently with diverse clients and in the management of different types of practices
Apply advanced clinical and/or professional skills to professional psychology practice

title: PSYCHOPATHOLOGY
syllabus_overview: This subject begins the process of building clinical competence in assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of major disorders. You will also develop a rich appreciation of their psychopathology, including the subjective experience of clients. The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM) and International Classification of Diseases (ICD) classification systems are critically appraised and used, and you will be guided in developing skills in administering a diagnostic interview.
learning_outcomes: Gain insight into, and empathy for, the personal experience of those who are affected by psychological problems

Develop skill independently and collaboratively in conducting and appraising semi-structured diagnostic interviews that routinely consider differential diagnoses, age specific features, and common comorbidities
Demonstrate an understanding of the notion of a taxonomy of mental disorders, with particular reference to the rationale, structure, content, and limitations of the DSM system
Develop and apply a practical understanding of the symptoms and psychopathology of major psychiatric disorders
Integrate cultural considerations in assessment and diagnosis

title: RESEARCH MASTERS A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will discuss a range of approaches to conducting research, with a particular focus on research methods most commonly used in clinical and applied psychological research. This knowledge will support you to work collaboratively with your research supervisor to develop a research proposal for your research project. Presentation and discussion of your research project with your peers within the workshop setting will also facilitate the development of your project and proposal. The research project must address a research question relevant to the field of clinical psychology.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and apply different approaches to research methods to a variety of clinical or applied research topics.
Use knowledge of research methods and importance of cultural context to inform interpretation and critical analysis of previous research studies and results.
Formulate a research question and design and write an appropriate research proposal to address the question.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY SKILLS AND REASONING 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will further develop your knowledge of physiotherapy in Australia, including the history of the profession, scope of practice and funding models. You will learn the importance of managing your own physical and mental wellbeing as a health professional. You will lay foundations for key physiotherapy principles including cultural safety, evidence-based practice and interprofessional collaborative practice. You will undertake work integrated learning that will provide real-world context for your exploration of these professional themes. You will integrate your developing knowledge of anatomy, physiology and biomechanics principles to develop skills relating to physiotherapy for upper limb and spinal conditions, including how to assess clients, develop client-centred problem lists, and perform basic treatment for soft tissue injuries. You will continue to refine your communication and clinical reasoning skills, to support the planning of tailored and culturally responsive physiotherapy care. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning to analyse and interpret physiotherapy assessment findings and develop problem lists for upper limb and spinal presentations.

Demonstrate professional practice and communication skills that are applicable to physiotherapy management of upper limb and spinal conditions and important to culturally safe practice, including verbal, interpersonal, reflective and written skills.
Demonstrate and apply effective subjective and objective physiotherapy assessments that are culturally responsive and relevant to specific clinical contexts, with a focus on the upper limb and spine.
Describe and demonstrate basic treatment approaches for soft tissue injuries, with a focus on the upper limb and spine.

Apply concepts of cultural safety, evidence-based practice, interprofessional collaborative practice, and managing your own physical and mental health, as they relate to your role as a future physiotherapist.
Discuss physiotherapy practice in Australia, including scope of practice and funding models.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY SKILLS AND REASONING 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the profession of physiotherapy. You will learn about the determinants of health, their influence on the wellbeing of individuals, communities and populations, and the role of a physiotherapist in promoting health and wellbeing for people from a variety of backgrounds. You will begin to create your professional identity, critical thinking and curiosity as a healthcare practitioner and reflect on personal and professional behaviour as governed by codes of conduct and relevant legislation. You will integrate your developing knowledge of anatomy, physiology and biomechanics principles to develop skills relating to physiotherapy for lower limb conditions, including how to assess clients, develop client-centred problem lists, and perform basic treatment for soft tissue injuries. You will learn strategies to communicate effectively and respectfully with clients from a variety of backgrounds, and clinical reasoning skills to interpret information to support the planning of tailored and culturally responsive physiotherapy care.
learning_outcomes: Describe and demonstrate basic treatment approaches for soft tissue injuries, with a focus on the lower limb.
Reflect on personal and colleagues' professional behaviour based on relevant legislation, ethical standards and codes of conduct.
Apply clinical reasoning to analyse and interpret physiotherapy assessment findings and develop problem lists for lower limb presentations.
Identify the determinants of health and explain how they influence health and wellbeing of individuals, communities and populations.
Demonstrate and apply effective subjective and objective physiotherapy assessments that are culturally responsive and relevant to specific clinical contexts, with a focus on the lower limb.

Demonstrate professional practice and communication skills that are applicable to physiotherapy management of lower limb conditions and important to culturally safe practice, including verbal, interpersonal, reflective and written skills.

title: EXERCISE AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the importance of physical activity and exercise in promoting health in a range of clinical populations across the lifespan. You will explore the benefits of physical activity, risks of sedentary behaviour and the important role of physiotherapists in promoting physical activity and prescribing exercise. You will develop skills to identify patient risks associated with a range of exercise modes and learn strategies to minimise these. You will integrate your knowledge of anatomy, physiology and biomechanics to assess aspects of the neuromusculoskeletal, cardiovascular and respiratory systems related to physical activity, fitness and balance. You will apply clinical reasoning to interpret assessment findings, prescribe evidence-based exercise interventions and promote physical activity in a range of clinical contexts.
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of physiotherapy in promoting physical activity and prescribing exercise across a range of clinical contexts.
Plan and implement evidence-based individualised exercise interventions that are culturally safe and relevant to assessment findings and goals.
Apply skills in advocacy, health promotion and behaviour change to facilitate physical activity in health-related contexts for individuals, communities and populations.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR OLDER ADULTS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will progress your physiotherapy skills and reasoning to learn about the provision of tailored, effective and client-centred care for older adults, in the context of healthy or disease-related ageing. You will be introduced to the concept of ageism and the resultant need to develop advocacy skills to support the rights of your older clients to health care and self-determination. You will apply your developing knowledge of neuroanatomy and pathophysiology to the exploration of physiotherapy management of common conditions such as dementia, delirium, frailty and falls. You will also develop your skills in manual handling, working in partnership with families and carers, exercise prescription for older adults, and promoting enabling environments.
learning_outcomes: Determine how concepts of autonomy, advocacy and ageism intersect with physiotherapy for older adults.

Adapt physiotherapy practice to manage common risks, complexities and contextual factors such as cognitive impairment, multimorbidity, or working with families and carers, in a manner that is culturally safe and relevant to the client.
Differentiate between healthy and disease-related ageing processes across cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and neurological systems.
Differentiate the role of physiotherapists and the interprofessional team in supporting the health and wellbeing of older people in a variety of healthcare settings.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with and about older clients from a variety of backgrounds, who are experiencing prevalent health conditions.

title: NEUROLOGICAL PHYSIOTHERAPY 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply your knowledge of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and pathophysiology to develop skills and reasoning relevant to client-centred physiotherapy assessment and management of common presentations such as stroke, haemorrhage, vestibular dysfunction, Guillain-Barre syndrome, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, dementia, and cerebral palsy. You will build on your subjective assessment skills to explore the experience of individuals with neurological impairments, and learn how to perform key neurological assessments of motor and sensory pathways, including vestibular. Case studies will be used to introduce clinical reasoning in this area, with a particular focus on WHO-ICF activity areas of standing, dynamic balance, and walking. You will learn about treatment principles for neurological impairments and will start to develop basic treatment and discharge plans.
learning_outcomes: Describe physiotherapy treatment principles that are relevant for people with neurological conditions.
Design and implement a functional based assessment for a person with a neurological condition.
Apply analysis and interpretation of assessment findings for common neurological conditions to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals.
Design and implement a subjective assessment for a person with a neurological condition.
Demonstrate safe and sensitive neurological assessments of motor and sensory pathways.

title: MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply your knowledge of anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise prescription, cultural safety and professional behaviour to appropriately assess and treat patients with peripheral musculoskeletal conditions. Client-centred models of clinical reasoning will be used as a framework to plan your physiotherapy management. You will learn through a series of case studies, including clients across the lifespan and from a variety of backgrounds who present with fractures, joint replacements and peripheral soft tissue conditions.
learning_outcomes: Plan and perform a safe, effective and client-specific assessment relevant to common peripheral musculoskeletal presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
Evaluate the safety and effectiveness of assessment and management plans and reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the interdisciplinary team.
Devise, perform and justify safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred management plans for common peripheral musculoskeletal presentations.

Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals relevant to common peripheral musculoskeletal presentations.

title: INTRODUCTION TO PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will participate in a range of learning activities that will prepare you for clinical placements. You will consolidate your skills in manual handling, communication, and clinical reasoning to effectively assess and treat clients from a range of clinical and community settings. Simulated patient cases will challenge you to consider ethical, medico-legal, cultural responsiveness and regulatory requirements for clinical practice, as well as the need to manage your own physical and mental wellbeing. This subject includes 40 hours of work integrated learning to practice your professional behaviour and communication skills and prepare you for your longer clinical placements later in the program. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in manual handling relevant to the safety of you and your clients in a variety of clinical settings.
Communicate and collaborate with patients, clients, families and other professionals in a person-centred manner that prioritises cultural safety and respect.
Reflect and respond to questions, suggestions and constructive feedback.
Produce a high standard of written documentation and verbal communication including problem lists, patient notes, handovers and discharge plans that are justified via clinical reasoning.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the interdisciplinary team.

title: APPLIED PHYSIOTHERAPY MANAGEMENT A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on professional practice knowledge developed in first year, extend your clinical reasoning skills and develop physiotherapy assessment and management skills. You will explore professional practice issues of informed consent, privacy and confidentiality, risk assessment, goal setting and effective communication in relation to physiotherapy practice. You will apply clinical reasoning frameworks to lower limb and cardiothoracic cases. You will be taught physiotherapy assessment and management skills for lower limb neuro-Musculo-skeletal conditions. Basic assessments for the cardiothoracic region will be introduced, which will be further developed in third year.
learning_outcomes: Conduct effective evidence-based management of lower-limb neuromusculoskeletal dysfunctions
Apply clinical reasoning to client profiles in a range of settings and contexts, individually and collaboratively.
Apply appropriate evidence-based assessments of the cardiothoracic and lower-limb neuromusculoskeletal systems
Demonstrate and apply professional practice in physiotherapy in clinical contexts.

title: APPLIED PHYSIOTHERAPY B
syllabus_overview: This subject continues the knowledge and skills developed in PTY2APA to the upper limb, head and nervous system. You will build on professional practice knowledge developed in first and second years, extend their clinical reasoning skills and physiotherapy assessment and management skills. You will explore professional practice issues of scope of practice, practice thresholds, codes of conduct legislation and regulation in relation to contemporary practice. You will apply clinical reasoning frameworks to the upper limb, head and nervous system and explore physiotherapy assessment and management skills for upper limb neuro-Musculo-skeletal conditions. Basic assessments for the central nervous system will be introduced, which will be further developed in third year. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply codes of conduct legislation and regulations in relation to contemporary physiotherapy practice, individually and collaboratively
Develop discharge plans in a variety of healthcare and interprofessional practice settings, individually and in teams.

Apply clinical reasoning individually and collaboratively to select and apply safe and effective evidence-based patient centred physiotherapy interventions focusing on the head, neck, upper limb and nervous system
Apply clinical reasoning to select, perform and analyse safe evidence-based person-centred assessments of upper limb, head and neck, and the nervous system.

title: PRINCIPLES OF PHYSIOTHERAPY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to human development and participation across the lifespan. Principles of health and wellbeing, behaviour change, communication, and reflective practice in relation to self and others will be explored in the context of the physiotherapist’s role in enhancing participation. Along with typical changes throughout the lifespan, you will also learn about common issues that affect health and well-being at different stages of life, and how using health and wellbeing models such as the World Health Organisation International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (WHO ICF) Model can enhance physiotherapy practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of person-centred communication and interpersonal skills in the context of people from a variety of backgrounds.
Apply psychological theories and concepts of human behaviour to real-world settings in the promotion of health and wellbeing in self and physiotherapy practice
Analyse human development and changes in participation across the lifespan in relation to physiotherapy practice
Implement principles of reflective practice in relation to personal and professional development

title: CARDIORESPIRATORY PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop knowledge, skills and clinical reasoning related to the assessment and management of clients with common cardiorespiratory presentations. You will build upon your prior knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology across the lifespan. You will draw upon this knowledge and previous physiotherapy subjects to broaden your skills in assessment, analysis, and problem identification in the critical care, acute, and community settings. You will develop and implement targeted client-centred management plans which address barriers and facilitators to client participation such as capability, opportunity, and motivation. Throughout the subject you will enhance your skills in professional and reflective practice to consider interprofessional collaboration, the application of evidence-based guidance, and prior knowledge of cultural safety.
learning_outcomes: Critique practice against evidence-based guidance and cultural safety standards to reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Design and demonstrate safe, effective, culturally responsive and client-specific assessment for people with common cardiorespiratory presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of cardiorespiratory assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the interdisciplinary team.

Predict the physiological responses of the cardiac and respiratory systems across the lifespan, under normal conditions, in common pathophysiological presentations and to physiotherapy assessment and intervention.
Devise, justify and implement safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred management plans for people from a variety of backgrounds with cardiorespiratory presentations.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR THE SPINE AND PELVIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply your knowledge of anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise prescription and professional behaviour to appropriately assess and treat common musculoskeletal presentations of the spine and pelvis. Client-centred models of clinical reasoning will be used as a framework to plan your physiotherapy management in a series of case studies, including clients that present with spinal or pelvic conditions, or following spinal, pelvic or oncology surgery.
learning_outcomes: Devise, justify and implement safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred management plans for people from a variety of backgrounds with common musculoskeletal presentations of the spine and pelvis.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the interdisciplinary team.
Evaluate the safety and effectiveness of assessment and management plans and reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Demonstrate high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation techniques to the lumbar and thoracic regions of the spine with appropriate medicolegal documentation.

Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals relevant to common musculoskeletal presentations of the spine and pelvis.

Design and demonstrate safe, effective, culturally responsive and client-specific assessment for people with common musculoskeletal spinal and pelvic presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.

title: NEUROLOGICAL PHYSIOTHERAPY 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will extend your skills and reasoning relevant to physiotherapy assessment and management of complex neurological presentations and will have the opportunity to work with simulated patients to prepare you for clinical practice. You will deepen your capacity for clinical reasoning in this area of practice and consider complexities in motor and sensory dysfunction such as spasticity. More severely impaired clients will be introduced, beginning with the WHO-ICF activity area of bed mobility through to running, and you will learn how to operate advanced equipment such as tilt tables and standing machines. Case studies including stroke, subarachnoid haemorrhage, tumours, traumatic brain injury, functional neurological disorder, vestibular dysfunction, spinal cord injury, and concussion will be explored. You will develop your skills and reasoning to manage physiotherapy intervention from the beginning to the end of an episode of care, including assessment, treatment, interprofessional collaboration and discharge planning.
learning_outcomes: Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the interdisciplinary team.
Devise, justify and implement safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred management plans for people from a variety of backgrounds with neurological presentations.
Design and justify case-based discharge plans for people with neurological conditions.
Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals relevant to complex neurological presentations.
Design and demonstrate safe, effective, culturally responsive and client-specific assessment for people with a range of neurological presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.

title: INTEGRATED CLINICAL REASONING
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will extend your clinical reasoning skills in assessment and treatment of complex cases, including clients who present with more than one physical impairment. Your communication and interpersonal skills will be challenged by needing to adapt your approach to your client's needs relating to responsive behaviours, socioeconomic factors and language. You will also apply your knowledge of evidence-based practice and cultural safety to create client-centred treatment plans and be introduced to caseload organisation and prioritisation.
learning_outcomes: Apply reflective practice and critical self-reflection to identify learning needs.
Adapt physiotherapy assessments for people with complex health care needs.
Apply caseload prioritisation and organisation skills relevant to physiotherapy.
Develop and justify interdisciplinary and evidenced-based management plans for people with complex health care needs from a variety of backgrounds, including First Nations peoples.
Reflect on and appraise professional communication skills used in complex clinical scenarios.

title: PAEDIATRIC PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn the key principles and strategies to adapt your existing physiotherapy skills and reasoning to provide effective care for a range of paediatric populations. You will learn about these key principles, which include family-centred care, age-appropriate communication and child safety, and develop your assessment and intervention skills to tailor your practice to infants, children and adolescents. Common conditions across a variety of clinical areas and settings will be explored alongside these underlying principles. A fieldwork visit in a childhood setting will provide students with experience observing and interacting with children. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Plan and justify case-sensitive and culturally responsive paediatric physiotherapy subjective and objective assessments.
Perform case sensitive analyses of assessment findings relevant to paediatric physiotherapy.
Design appropriate interdisciplinary and evidence-based management plans relevant to paediatric physiotherapy, including in the context of people from a variety of backgrounds.
Apply key principles of paediatric physiotherapy practice in the assessment and management of paediatric conditions.
Analyse development and changes in participation across infancy, childhood and adolescence in relation to physiotherapy practice.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR CARDIO-RESPIRATORY DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be taught knowledge and skills relevant to the physiotherapy management of clients with cardiorespiratory conditions and problems. You will draw on prior knowledge of cardiorespiratory anatomy and physiology while undertaking activities that are aimed at developing skills in: assessment, clinical reasoning, problem identification and prioritisation, planning, implementation and progression of evidence-based interventions, evaluation, discharge planning and the broader role of the healthcare team relevant to adults and children with common cardiorespiratory conditions or problems in various healthcare settings.
learning_outcomes: Explain the anatomical structures and pathophysiological adaptations that occur in common cardiorespiratory clinical presentations.
Implement, and evaluate safe, effective and evidence based client-centred interventions in accordance with problem lists.
Apply ethical and professional behaviours to maintain safe workplaces for both therapists and clients
Implement and justify safe and effective client-centred physiotherapy assessments of the cardiorespiratory system.
Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of cardiorespiratory assessments to produce prioritized, client-centred problem lists.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: You will explore core knowledge, skills and attitudes relevant to physiotherapy management of common neurological problems. The emphasis will be on evidence-based assessment and intervention for people living with neurological dysfunction across the lifespan and in various health care settings. Using an enquiry-based learning approach, case examples will include, but not be limited to stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease and cerebral palsy. The World Health Organisation International Classification of Function Disability and Health will provide a framework that supports a person-centred focus.
