You will be taught in a blended approach, with face to face classes supported by teacher-guided online activities.
learning_outcomes: Apply safe, sensitive and case-specific assessments of common neurological problems in a variety of healthcare settings.
Devise and justify appropriate interventions based on best available evidence for common neurological conditions, individually and collaboratively.

Apply case sensitive analysis and interpretation of assessment findings for common neurological conditions to produce prioritized problem lists and patient-centred goals, individually and collaboratively.
Apply a range of therapeutic interventions commonly used in neurological physiotherapy safely and effectively in multidisciplinary environments.

title: MANAGING COMPLEXITY IN CLINICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Using various healthcare settings and scenarios (including critical care, rehabilitation, the first contact practitioner and the compensable patient), this subject will explore issues of complexity associated with persons with healthcare needs, caseloads, teams, services and/or wider organizations. You will extend your knowledge and skills related to the role of the physiotherapist as an independent practitioner and member of the wider healthcare team. You will have ongoing opportunities to apply the clinical reasoning model that draws on the World Health Organisation (WHO) International Classification of Functioning framework, a biopsychosocial approach to health care and evidence based practice. Self learning guides and online resources will complement workshops, practical classes and tutorials that are scheduled in block mode.
learning_outcomes: Safely and effectively prioritise patient caseloads of people with complex health care needs.
Safely and effectively perform case specific assessments for people with complex health care needs.
Analyse and interpret assessment findings of people with complex health care needs to produce a prioritised problem list.
Responsibly research and apply best-practice physiotherapy knowledge and skills to a range of people and settings.
Develop and justify interdisciplinary and evidenced based management plans that can be safely applied to people with complex health care needs, and translate this evidence into practice
Apply clinical reasoning to safely and effectively perform physiotherapy assessment and treatment techniques for people with complex healthcare needs

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore how to use person-centred models of clinical reasoning to assess and manage common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions. The subject has two modules: 1) Othopaedics (Fractures and Arthroplasties) module and 2) Vertebral (Spinal) module. You will select and perform assessment techniques and interpret the findings to design, implement, and progress management programs for common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions.
learning_outcomes: Apply theory to interpret subjective assessment findings and develop objective assessments for patients with common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions, both individually and collaboratively.
Apply theory and clinical reasoning frameworks to assessment findings to develop treatment plans for patients with common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions, both individually and collaboratively.
Adapt subjective assessments for patients with common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions, both individually and collaboratively.
Apply assessment and treatment techniques for patients with common orthopaedic and vertebral conditions.

title: SKILL DEVELOPMENT FOR PERSON-CENTRED PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will further develop clinical reasoning and communication skills to promote person-centred physiotherapy. You will further develop skills in clinical assessment and integrate these into reasoning processes for complex clinical scenarios. A clear purpose of the subject is to bring together concepts explored in co-requisite subjects and identify the principles that are shared across the breadth of physiotherapy. Clinical reasoning frameworkswill be applied to cases including ethics and medico-legal frameworks that guide clinician behaviour. You will also expand on the role and process of communication in clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning skills both individually and collaboratively to develop person-centred, culturally sensitive, treatment strategies for a range of clients in varied clinical settings.
Generate clear and coherent written information suitable for a variety of audiences in health care settings with cultural sensitivity.
Perform and analyse clinical assessment findings produce person-centred prioritized problem lists, relevant to a range of clinical settings.
Communicate and collaborate with patients, clients, families and other professionals in a person-centred manner that prioritises cultural safety and respect.
Formulate discharge plans that consider the patients perspective and facilitate self-management where appropriate.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: This subject is the second of six (or 5 for Research Honors students) professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice. You will have opportunity to meet competency thresholds in different practice areas for accreditation as a physiotherapist.. In this subject, you are in supervised clinical practice for 20 days over 5 weeks and prescribed independent learning (total subject hours 160). Clinical practicums are supervised by registered physiotherapists and may be organised outside normal teaching weeks. You will develop specific competencies in the assessment of clients' problems and needs, analysis of assessment findings, formulation of short and long term goals and development, implementation and evaluation of intervention plans. You will apply specialised knowledge, cognitive and technical skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a learner. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate assessment findings accurately to identify client problems and set realistic short and long terms goals.

Apply well-developed skills to communicate effectively and appropriately with clients, carers, family and health professional colleagues to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Apply professional behavior in a well-developed, responsible manner appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Evaluate evidence and collaborate with clients to formulate all aspects of client management ensuring safe and appropriate interventions
Conduct well developed, sensitive and case specific client interviews to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Transmit knowledge, skills and ideas to effectively educate clients and caregivers.
Perform broad, safe, and accurate physical assessments.
Apply broad and coherent knowledge and skills to implement discharge planning to address client and carer's needs for ongoing care.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM A
syllabus_overview: This subject is the first of six (or 5 for Research Honours students) professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice. You will have opportunity to meet competency thresholds in different practice areas for accreditation as a physiotherapist.. In this subject, you are in supervised clinical practice for 20 days over 5 weeks and prescribed independent learning (total subject hours 160). Prior to commencing this subject, you must complete a compulsory 5-day pre-clinical program comprising a 1-day seminar at their La Trobe University campus, followed by 4 days of orientation and learning within their clinical school. Clinical practicums are supervised by registered physiotherapists and may be organised outside normal teaching weeks. You will develop specific competencies in the assessment of clients' problems and needs, analysis of assessment findings, formulation of short and long term. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional behaviour in a well-developed, responsible manner appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Analyse and evaluate assessment findings accurately to identify client problems and set realistic short and long terms goals.
Transmit knowledge, skills and ideas to effectively educate clients and caregivers.
Evaluate evidence and collaborate with clients to formulate all aspects of client management ensuring safe and appropriate interventions
Apply broad and coherent knowledge and skills to implement discharge planning to address client and carer's needs for ongoing care.
Conduct well developed, sensitive and case specific client interviews to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Perform broad, safe, and accurate physical assessments.

Apply well-developed skills to communicate effectively and appropriately with clients, carers, family and health professional colleagues both in a team and independently to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR PAEDIATRICS, WOMEN'S AND PELVIC HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will extend your knowledge and skills relating to physiotherapy assessment and management in the practice areas of paediatrics, women's health and continence. The paediatrics module will cover the theoretical background for assessing and managing children with posture and movement disorders. The women's health module will introduce the aetiology, pathology, clinical features and complications, pertaining to conditions specific to women, that are amenable to physiotherapy care. The continence module will introduce the assessment and management of continence problems occurring in women and men, with the emphasis on incontinence resulting from pelvic floor muscle weakness.
learning_outcomes: Safely and effectively perform a selection of physiotherapy interventions commonly used in women's and pelvic health physiotherapy, individually and collaboratively.
Conduct safe, case-sensitive assessments within women's and pelvic health physiotherapy
Critically review, individually and collaboratively, common clinical presentations seen by paediatric, women's and pelvic health physiotherapists.
Analyse common assessment practices in paediatric physiotherapy.
Design appropriate interdisciplinary and evidence based management plans relevant to paediatric, women's and pelvic health physiotherapy.
Perform, individually and collaboratively, case sensitive analyses and interpretation of assessment findings relevant to paediatric, women's and pelvic health physiotherapy

title: SPORT, EXERCISE AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY
syllabus_overview: This subject extends prior learning to apply exercise and physical activity approaches for the prevention and rehabilitation of more complex conditions and populations. You will integrate prior knowledge of anatomy, pathophysiology, and physiotherapy practice with the differential diagnosis and management of common neuromusculoskeletal clinical presentations, including sporting injuries. You will learn to adapt existing exercise and physical activity recommendations or protocols to individual patients or groups from a variety of backgrounds including Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples, or those with complex care needs, including those with cancer, osteoporosis, chronic disease, multi-pathology / co-morbidities, or compensable injuries.
learning_outcomes: Integrate prior knowledge of anatomy, pathophysiology, and physiotherapy practice with the assessment differential diagnosis and management of common neuromusculoskeletal sporting injuries

Tailor exercise therapy and physical activity interventions on the basis of age, pathology, stage of condition, patient goals, compensable status, and cultural factors including the diverse needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Critique advanced prevention and rehabilitation programs and modify them for individual clients and groups, including those with complex care needs

title: CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject will prepare you for a physiotherapy career through career development planning and leadership of a project that enhances physiotherapy practice. You will be facilitated in the preparation of a strategic and goal- orientated career development plan relevant for the initial phase of your physiotherapy career. Relevant career development topics will include reflection on personal and professional attributes, cultural safety, job applications,, mentoring, networking and professional development activities. Workplace management and leadership skills will be explored including interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership styles, emotional intelligence, negotiation, and conflict management. You will then lead an innovative project that enhances aspects of physiotherapy practice, that will be presented at an end of year conference to interprofessional colleagues. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Create strategic and goal-orientated career development plans relevant to future clinical practice.
Critically apply strategies essential for leadership and advocacy for improving health outcomes
Communicate project ideas and findings coherently to engage and educate a variety of audiences, including interprofessional colleagues
Lead innovative professional projects that enhance physiotherapy practice.

title: FOCUS ON SPECIAL CLINICAL AREAS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will have the opportunity to extend your physiotherapy knowledge in special focus areas of clinical practice. You will complete relevant learning activities at the university, in selected areas which may include musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiorespiratory, rural healthcare, women’s and pelvic health, paediatrics.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the assessment, management and clinical reasoning relating to real- world clinical case studies relevant to special focus areas of physiotherapy practice.
Critically analyse and interpret theoretical concepts relevant to a special focus areas of physiotherapy clinical practice
Safely select and medico legally document high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation techniques to the cervical region of the spine.

Critically reflect on your clinical reasoning skills and identify those you will need to refine and further develop, to provide excellent physiotherapy care to clients in special focus areas of physiotherapy practice.

title: ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject involves three modules: (i) advanced spinal physiotherapy, (ii) professional practice, and (iii) a self-directed project. Advanced spinal physiotherapy expands on the clinical reasoning and manual therapy skills developed earlier in the course, with focus on spinal physiotherapy. The professional practice module aims to prepare you to commence practice as a newly graduated health professional, covering legislation, codes of conduct and ethical practice. In the third module, you will identify a gap in physiotherapy practice and develop a creative solution to this issue. As a self-directed project, you will develop solutions with the ultimate aim of improving physiotherapy practice within the chosen context. This subject addresses La Trobe's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Essential. Innovation and Entrepreneurship entails developing the ability to tackle problems creatively, generating new ideas, taking calculated safe risks and creating change to achieve ambitions.
learning_outcomes: Design, justify and conduct a safe, sensitive, advanced and highly case-specific assessment,
Select, safely apply and medico legally document high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation techniques to the lumbar, thoracic and cervical spine regions.
Research, and evaluate evidence to create, and enhance aspects of physiotherapy practice.
Design, justify and conduct an advanced case-specific physiotherapy management plan.
Clearly and coherently communicate research findings to a variety of audiences.
Analyse and critically evaluate assessment findings and prioritise patient needs to at least the minimum standard expected for an entry level physiotherapist.
Critically reflect on personal and colleagues' professional behaviour based on relevant legislation, ethical standards and Codes of Practice, and provide appropriate feedback.
Prioritise and evaluate interventions using reliable and valid outcome measures to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.

title: CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: Chronic conditions are becoming more prevalent in aging societies. In this subject, you will integrate core strands of theory knowledge and practice with contemporary health needs of individuals, groups, communities and populations. You will explore knowledge and skills in health promotion, treatment and self-management of chronic conditions in both a group and individual context. You will critique models of health, theories of health behaviour and apply innovative problem solving skills to health-related scenarios covering a range of chronic conditions. Interprofessional, person-centred, evidence-based and critical reflection approaches will be adopted.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and identify the essential skills to ethically and responsibly manage change and health care projects.
Make evidence-based recommendations for care, considering the patient, family and community and the role of contextual factors that shape healthcare for clients with chronic conditions
Develop, and evaluate culturally sensitive and effective health programs that draw on the principles of inclusion, equity and accessibility for clients with chronic conditions.
Evaluate and respond to intrinsic and extrinsic barriers and enablers of health for clients with chronic conditions
Develop ethical health leadership behaviours that will promote sustainable and contemporary healthcare practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM C
syllabus_overview: This subject is the 3rd of 6 (or 5 for research honours students) professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice. You will have opportunity to meet competency thresholds in different practice areas for accreditation as a physiotherapist. In this subject you are in supervised clinical practice for 20 days over 5 weeks and prescribed independent learning (total subject hours 160). Clinical practicums are supervised by registered physiotherapists and may be organised outside normal teaching weeks. You will develop specific competencies in the assessment of clients' problems and needs, analysis of assessment findings, formulation of short and long term goals and development, implementation and evaluation of intervention plans. You will apply specialised knowledge, cognitive and technical skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a learner. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Conduct advanced, sensitive and case specific client interviews to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Practice responsibly and flexibly, applying well-developed professional behaviour appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.

Apply advanced skills to communicate effectively and appropriately with clients, carers, family and health professional colleagues to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Evaluate evidence to formulate all aspects of client management strategies in collaboration with clients with sometimes complex problems.
Transmit complex knowledge, skills and ideas clearly, to effectively educate clients and caregivers.
Analyse and critically evaluate assessment findings accurately to identify client's problems and set realistic short and long terms goals.
Perform safe, highly skilled and accurate physical assessments.
Clinical Assessment: Assessment of Physiotherapy Practice Tool - items 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION
syllabus_overview: You will learn core knowledge, skills and attitudes relevant to physiotherapy management of common neurological problems. The emphasis will be on evidence-based assessment and intervention of neurological patients across the lifespan and various health care settings. Using an enquiry-based learning approach, case examples will include, but not be limited to, Stroke, Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease and Cerebral Palsy. The World Health Organisation International Classification of Function Disability and Health will provide a framework to demonstrate the need for person centredness. .
learning_outcomes: Complete a safe, sensitive and case-specific assessment relevant to common neurological problems, and in a variety of healthcare settings.
Safely and effectively perform a range of therapeutic interventions commonly used in neurological physiotherapy.
Devise and justify an interprofessional and evidence based treatment that can be safely applied and is relevant to common neurological conditions, individually and collaboratively.

Perform a case sensitive analysis and interpretation of assessment findings relevant to common neurological conditions to produce a prioritised problem list and patient centred goals, individually and collaboratively.

title: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE IN HEALTH
syllabus_overview: Evidence-based practice (EBP) is the use of best available evidence combined with patient preferences, available resources and therapist expertise in making decisions about the care of patients. Evidence-based health care requires the physiotherapist to be able to perform the five steps of evidence-based practice. In this subject you will produce a written Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) for publication in a web-based clinical resource. This resource will be peer reviewed, with you further applying your EBP skills in order to critically appraise the work of other students. In this manner you will further develop the necessary skills to perform evidence-based practice, while gaining a greater understanding of the peer review process and contributing to a valuable evidence-based resource.
learning_outcomes: Critically interpret research findings with colleagues and justify answers to clinical research questions
Reflect on and evaluate team processes in contributing to evidence based practice
Critically appraise with colleagues the methodology of a variety of research designs to determine the relative weight of research evidence.
Review and analyse published work in a process of peer review
Collaboratively assemble current, peer-reviewed evidence, to answer clinically oriented research questions.
Collaborate with colleagues to identify research topics that will enhance clinical knowledge and systematically locate evidence.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM D
syllabus_overview: This subject is the fourth of five full professional clinical placement subjects that you must complete across different practice areas, and in a variety of healthcare settings, to be eligible to apply for registration as a practicing physiotherapist. In this subject, you are in supervised clinical practice for 20 days over 5 weeks and prescribed independent learning (total subject hours 160). Clinical placements are supervised by registered physiotherapists and may be organised outside normal teaching weeks. You will develop specific competencies in the assessment of clients' problems and needs, analysis of assessment findings, formulation of short and long term goals and development, implementation and evaluation of intervention plans. You will apply specialised knowledge, cognitive and technical skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a learner. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Transmit complex knowledge, skills and ideas clearly, to effectively educate clients and caregivers.
Apply highly skilled knowledge and demonstrate adaptability to implement discharge planning to address client and carer's needs for ongoing care.
Perform safe, highly skilled and accurate physical assessments.
Conduct advanced, sensitive and case specific client interviews to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.

Apply advanced skills to communicate effectively and appropriately with clients, carers, family and health professional colleagues to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Practice responsibly and flexibly, applying well-developed professional behaviour appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Evaluate evidence to formulate all aspects of client management strategies in collaboration with clients with sometimes complex problems.
Analyse and critically evaluate assessment findings accurately to identify client's problems and set realistic short and long terms goals for clients from a variety of backgrounds.

syllabus_overview: This subject is the 6th professional practicum subject across different specific areas of practice. title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable you to gain advanced theoretical knowledge and mastery of musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy clinical skills required to optimise the effectiveness of client-centred management.
learning_outcomes: Compile and synthesise information to optimise the effectiveness of client-centred management.
Apply hypothetico-deductive clinical reasoning principles to develop an examination and management plan.
Apply expert knowledge and integrate with specialised clinical skills
Integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical skills to demonstrate advanced professional practice

title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject consists of three topics: Exercise for Musculoskeletal Physio, Advance Spinal Management, and Peripheral Imaging. Topics have equivalent assessments and are designed to develop your knowledge and the skills required for the successful rehabilitation and management of musculoskeletal patients. The topics in this subject will enable you to gain advanced theoretical knowledge and the mastery of clinical skills needed to optimise the effectiveness of person-centred management. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply expert knowledge and to synthesise and integrate this with specialised clinical musculoskeletal physiotherapy skills.
Apply hypothetico-deductive clinical reasoning principles to develop a advanced musculoskeletal specific examination and management plan.
Integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical skills to demonstrate advanced musculoskeletal physiotherapy practice
Compile and synthesise information to optimise the effectiveness of client centred management, including interpreting musculoskeletal imaging.

title: WEBINARS IN MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject takes you through an in-depth analysis of contemporary and controversial topics in Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy. Final Year Master of Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy students will deliver a Webinar to their fellow students, and develop other knowledge translation resources, on a selected topic in Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy. You will critically analyse the literature and develop a clinical topic for an informative webinar, as well as written and visual communication resources, that show cases the interdisciplinary management and clinical leadership required to achieve desired patient specific outcomes. Each topic will be studied in relation to epidemiology, clinical assessment, diagnosis, management, and rehabilitation.
learning_outcomes: Develop engaging written, visual and presentation content to facilitate knowledge translation of evidence in musculoskeletal physiotherapy practice to peers and/or the community.
Provide expert guidance to peers on how to apply current research evidence, related to the causes, treatment and prevention of musculoskeletal pathologies across the lifecycle.
Critically reflect on knowledge and clinical expertise to provide leadership to peers and/or the community related to musculoskeletal physiotherapy.
Critically assess and communicate current knowledge regarding the epidemiology, clinical assessment, diagnosis, management, and rehabilitation of different musculoskeletal injuries.

title: ADVANCED PRACTICE IN SPORTS & EXERCISE PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this placement based subject, you will apply theoretical knowledge in sports and exercise physiotherapy to develop skills in patient examination, diagnosis and management of clients presenting with sports and exercise-related conditions. You will work under the supervision of recognised sports and exercise physiotherapists and complete an extended placement of 120 hours on a part time basis over an eight month period. Supervised clinical practice encourages and facilitated rational decision-making with respect to treatment selection, treatment progression and planning ongoing management programs. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Justify and perform safe, sports specific assessments and the application of appropriate outcome measures to monitor the effectiveness of treatment(s) or management.
Develop short and long-term treatment goals, and treatment progression within a multidiscipline health care team from initial assessment and treatment of athlete or client sport injuries .
Synthesise clinical evidence and communication these to influence athlete, communities, team, sporting administration and other agencies to improve outcomes for athlete clients and other athletes.

Combine and synthesise findings and outcomes from a follow-up assessment of a complex athlete / clients presenting sports injury to refine treatment goals, and progression of treatment within a multidiscipline health care team.
Apply appropriate knowledge, theoretical propositions, methodologies, conclusions to demonstrate reflective evidence based practice in high level sports settings to improve clinical practice.

title: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN SPORTS & EXERCISE PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject consists of three topics: Exercise for Sports Physio, Being a Sports Physio, and Peripheral Imaging. Topics have equivalent assessments and are designed to develop your knowledge and the skills required for the successful rehabilitation and management of athletes. The topics in this subject will enable you to gain advanced theoretical knowledge and the mastery of clinical skills needed to optimise the effectiveness of athlete-centred management. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply hypothetico-deductive clinical reasoning principles to develop a sports specific examination and management plan.
Integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical skills to demonstrate advanced advanced sports physiotherapy practice.
Apply expert knowledge and integrate with specialised sports physiotherapy skills.
Combine clinical findings with the literature to optimise the effectiveness of athlete centred management including interpreting imaging.

title: ADVANCED PRACTICE IN MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you are given the opportunity to develop advanced neuro-musculoskeletal examination and management skills within a clinical reasoning paradigm. Supervised clinical practice encourages and facilitates rational decision making with respect to treatment selection, treatment progression and planning of ongoing management programs. You will also have the opportunity to integrate advanced manipulative physiotherapy manual techniques and exercise prescription into your clinical practice. You will undertake 160 hours of supervised clinical practice within the Australian healthcare environment, which will be accumulated over the year at hospital outpatient departments and/or private physiotherapy clinics. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Combine the outcomes from initial assessment and treatment findings of complex neuro-musculoskeletal clients to reason and develop short and long-term treatment goals relevant to progression of treatment and interventions in multidiscipline health care teams.

Combine and synthesise findings and outcomes from the initial assessment and treatment with the findings from a follow-up assessment of a complex neuro-musculoskeletal client to refine or develop short and long-term treatment goals, and progression of treatment or intervention(s) within a multidiscipline health care team.

Justify and perform safe, systematic, efficient, prioritised advanced physical neuro-musculoskeletal assessments through the application of appropriate outcome measures to monitor the effectiveness of treatment(s) or management to inform treatment decisions and progressions.

Synthesise clinical evidence and demonstrate appropriate communication to influence client, communities, client populations, government and other agencies or organisations to improve health and health outcomes.

Apply appropriate knowledge, theoretical propositions, methodologies, conclusions to demonstrate reflective evidence based practice in the complex neuro-musculoskeletal setting to ensure clinical decisions made during patient interactions improve the effectiveness and efficiency of your clinical practice.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: ESSENTIALS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the profession of physiotherapy in Australia, including the history of the profession, scope of practice, funding models and roles within interdisciplinary healthcare teams. You will reflect on personal and professional behaviour as governed by codes of conduct and relevant legislation. You will begin to create your professional identify, critical thinking and curiosity as a healthcare practitioner. You will develop communication and assessment skills that facilitate the identification of a client’s main problems and individual contextual factors as informed by clinical reasoning. You will undertake work integrated learning that will provide real-world context for your exploration of these professional themes. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with peers to plan and implement an effective subjective assessment that is culturally responsive and relevant to the client and clinical environment context.
Critically review physiotherapy practice in Australia, including history, scope of practice, funding models and roles within an interdisciplinary healthcare team.
Critically reflect on personal and colleagues' professional behaviour based on relevant legislation, ethical standards and codes of conduct.
Apply clinical reasoning processes to analyse and interpret clinical assessment findings in order to develop priority-based client-centred problem lists.
Exemplify culturally appropriate communication across a variety of professional settings, including as a member of an interdisciplinary healthcare team.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: COMMUNITY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn knowledge and skills relevant to physiotherapy practice in community-based settings, including in private practice, rehabilitation and home care settings. You will apply principles of anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and exercise prescription to develop skills in physiotherapy assessment, development of problem lists, planning and management of conditions commonly seen in community-based practice. You will be introduced to patient centred models of clinical reasoning that will provide a framework for your approach to managing common conditions such as fractures, joint and soft tissue injuries of the upper and lower limb.
learning_outcomes: Perform case sensitive critical analysis of assessment findings relevant to common conditions encountered in community-based physiotherapy practice.
Apply principles of exercise prescription and movement analysis to a range of client profiles with upper and lower limb conditions.
Plan and conduct a safe, case sensitive assessment of the upper and lower limbs relevant to common presentations in community-based physiotherapy practice.
Using a clinical reasoning framework, design a patient centred, evidence-based management plan for common presentations in community-based physiotherapy practice.
Evaluate and reflect on the safety and effectiveness of physiotherapy assessment and management skills.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND AGEING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore typical human development and ageing from infancy through to older age and end of life. Common developmental, chronic and geriatric conditions will be introduced, with their impacts considered in reference to the World Health Organisation - International Classification of Function, Disability and Health (WHO-ICF). You will learn to evaluate person-centred barriers and enablers of healthy behaviours and physical activity from infancy to advanced age. You will develop skills for client advocacy, health promotion and behaviour change to facilitate healthy behaviours and physical activity throughout the lifespan, including for people with developmental, chronic or geriatric conditions. A fieldwork visit in a childhood setting will provide students with experience observing and interacting with children. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply advocacy, health promotion and behaviour change skills to facilitate healthy behaviours and physical activity for people from infancy to advanced age, including those with developmental, chronic or geriatric conditions.
Analyse typical human development from infancy to older age, with an emphasis on physical activity and participation.
Critically examine the role of physical activity and exercise for clients with developmental, chronic or geriatric conditions across the lifespan.

Critically evaluate social determinants of health and person-centred barriers and enablers of healthy behaviours for people throughout the lifespan from a variety of cultural backgrounds, including those with developmental, chronic or geriatric conditions.
Critically analyse the impact of common developmental, chronic and geriatric conditions on development and ageing.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: ACUTE CARE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn skills and knowledge in preparation for clinical placement in an acute care setting. You will extend your knowledge of the anatomy and functioning of the central and peripheral nervous systems and the thorax. Using case studies of common clinical presentations to an acute care setting, you will apply your skills in physiotherapy assessment, planning and management to neurological, cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal conditions. A fieldwork visit to an acute care setting will assist in providing context for your learning and understanding of the physiotherapist's role in a multidisciplinary healthcare team in the acute setting. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Plan and conduct a safe , justifiable case sensitive assessment of a patient in the acute care setting.
Using a clinical reasoning framework, design and evaluate a patient centred management plan for common presentations in the acute care setting.
Explain the anatomical structures, pathophysiological adaptations and clinical presentations that commonly occur in cardiorespiratory and neurological clinical presentations in an acute care setting.
Evaluate and reflect on the role of a physiotherapist as a member or leader of a multidisciplinary team in the management of patients in the acute care setting.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: MUSCULOSKELETAL
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply your knowledge of anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise prescription and professional behaviour to appropriately assess and treat common musculoskeletal presentations of the spine and pelvis. Patient-centred models of clinical reasoning will be used as a framework to plan your physiotherapy management in a series of case studies, including patients that present with spinal or pelvic conditions, or patients following spinal, pelvic or oncology surgery.
learning_outcomes: Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals relevant to common musculoskeletal presentations of the spine and pelvis
Demonstrate a high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation technique to the lumbar and thoracic regions of the spine with appropriate medicolegal documentation
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the multidisciplinary team
Evaluate the safety and effectiveness of individual and collaborative assessment and management plans and reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Design, implement and justify a safe, effective and case-specific assessment relevant to common musculoskeletal spinal and pelvic presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
Devise, implement and justify safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred management plans for common spinal and pelvic presentations.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: NEUROLOGICAL
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on your knowledge of physiotherapy in the acute care setting to develop skills and attitudes relevant to the assessment and management of clinical neurological presentations. You will use evidence and clinical reasoning frameworks as the basis for developing skills in assessment, clinical reasoning, problem identification and prioritisation, and for planning, implementing and evaluating intervention for common neurological presentations, including Stroke, Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease and Cerebral Palsy. A person-centred approach will be founded on the World Health Organisation International Classification of Function Disability and Health.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the safety and effectiveness of individual and collaborative assessment and management plans, and reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the multidisciplinary team.
Design, implement and justify a safe, effective and case-specific assessment relevant to common neurological presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
Devise, implement and justify safe, effective and evidence-based client-centred interventions relevant to common neurological presentations.
Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of neurological assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: CARDIORESPIRATORY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on your knowledge of physiotherapy in the acute care setting to develop skills relevant to the assessment and management of clinical cardiorespiratory presentations. You will apply your knowledge of cardiorespiratory anatomy and physiology to evidence-based assessment, clinical reasoning, problem identification and prioritisation and for planning, implementing and evaluating interventions for common cardiorespiratory presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
learning_outcomes: Design, implement and justify a safe, effective and case-specific assessment relevant to common cardiorespiratory presentations in a variety of healthcare settings.
Apply effective clinical reasoning to analyse and explain the findings of cardiorespiratory assessments to produce prioritised problem lists and client-centred goals.
Evaluate the safety and effectiveness of individual and collaborative assessment and management plans and reflect on personal and professional opportunities for improvement.
Devise, implement and justify safe, and effective and evidence-based client-centred interventions relevant to common cardiorespiratorypresentations.
Consistently adopt ethical and professional behaviours to ensure a safe environment for all clients and members of the multidisciplinary team.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: PREPARATION FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will extend knowledge and skills learned in previous subjects in preparation for physiotherapy clinical placements. You will learn the theory and practice of specific physiotherapy assessment and treatment strategies relevant for paediatric clients. Simulated placement learning activities will provide an opportunity to consolidate and extend communication, clinical reasoning, physiotherapy assessment and treatment skills to high fidelity clinical environments across the acute, rehabilitation and community settings. Cases will challenge you to consider ethical, medico-legal, cultural competency and regulatory requirements for clinical practice. Mandatory pre-clinical orientation activities will prepare you to enter clinical placement environments as a physiotherapy student. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.

Design and justify case-specific physiotherapy assessment and interdisciplinary management plans relevant to common paediatric conditions.
Implement timely, safe and effective person-centred, case-based physiotherapy assessments and treatments for clients in acute, rehabilitation and community settings, justified via clinical reasoning.
Produce a high standard of written documentation and verbal communication including problem lists, patient notes, handovers and discharge plans that are justified via clinical reasoning
Critically reflect on physiotherapy practice and competency development

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: Evidence based practice is the use of best available evidence combined with patient preferences, available resources and therapist expertise in making decisions about the care of patients. Evidence based health care requires the physiotherapist to be able to perform the five steps of evidence based practice. In this subject students will build on the skills developed in previous research subjects in the production of a written Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) for publication in a web-based clinical resource. This resource will be peer reviewed, with the students further applying their EBP skills in order to critically appraise the work of other students. In this manner they will further develop the necessary skills to perform evidence based practice, while gaining a greater understanding of the peer review process and contributing to a valuable evidence based resource.

Critically appraise published work in a process of peer review.
Collaborate with colleagues to develop and justify research topics that will enhance clinical knowledge and systematically locate evidence.
Critically appraise with colleagues the methodology of a variety of research designs to determine the relative weight of research evidence.
Critically analyse and interpret research findings with colleagues to justify answers to clinical research questions.
Critically reflect on team strengths and weaknesses in relation to evidence-based-practice

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: SPORT, EXERCISE AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY
syllabus_overview: This subject extends prior learning to apply exercise and physical activity approaches for the prevention and rehabilitation of more complex conditions and populations. You will integrate prior knowledge of anatomy, pathophysiology, and physiotherapy practice with the differential diagnosis and management of common neuromusculoskeletal clinical presentations, including sporting injuries. You will learn to adapt existing exercise and physical activity recommendations or protocols to individual patients or groups with complex care needs, including those with cancer, osteoporosis, chronic disease, multi-pathology / co-morbidities, compensable injuries or Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples.

Integrate prior knowledge of anatomy, pathophysiology, and physiotherapy practice with the assessment differential diagnosis and management of common neuromusculoskeletal sporting injuries

Tailor exercise therapy and physical activity interventions on the basis of age, pathology, stage of condition, patient goals, compensable status, and cultural factors including the diverse needs of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP
syllabus_overview: This subject will prepare you for a physiotherapy career through career development planning and leadership of a project that enhances physiotherapy practice. Workplace management and leadership skills will be explored including interdisciplinary collaboration, leadership styles, emotional intelligence, negotiation, and conflict management. You will then lead an innovative project that enhances aspects of physiotherapy practice, that will be presented at an end of year conference to interprofessional colleagues. title: PHYSIOTHERAPY: FOCUS ON SPECIAL CLINICAL AREAS
syllabus_overview: In this hybrid clinical-theory subject, you will have the opportunity to extend your physiotherapy theory and practice experience to a special focus area of clinical practice. You will complete relevant theory at the university, followed by a two-week clinical placement experience in a selected clinical focus area. Focus areas will vary based on availability, but may include: private practice, neurological rehabilitation, cardiorespiratory physiotherapy, women’s and mens pelvic health, paediatrics. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret theoretical concepts relevant to a special focus area of physiotherapy clinical practice

Practice responsibly, applying professional behaviour and communication skills in one specific area of practice appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Critically evaluate the assessment, management and clinical reasoning relating to real-world clinical case studies relevant to special focus areas of physiotherapy practice.
Safely select and medico-legally document high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation techniques to the cervical region of the spine (musculoskeletal module only)

title: RESEARCH TO INFORM ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this fully online subject, students will develop their knowledge and skills required for evidence-informed practice in musculoskeletal or sports and exercise physiotherapy. The subject includes the completion of a Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) based on a sports or musculoskeletal physiotherapy problem that students have encountered in clinical practice. In completing the CAT, students will develop skills in formulating an answerable clinical question, searching for and critically appraising the available evidence to inform clinical reasoning and practice. Students will also refine their theoretical knowledge on the research process and human ethics to incorporate research into the clinical setting to inform advanced physiotherapy practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise and interpret the evidence base of musculoskeletal/sports and exercise physiotherapy across a variety of qualitative and quantitative research methodologies.
Generate an answerable clinical research question based on reflection and the critical evaluation of your clinical practice
Identify and systematically address ethical considerations associated with research in the musculoskeletal/sports and exercise physiotherapy setting.
Analyse, interpret and synthesise critically appraised research findings from an answerable clinical question to inform the assessment and management of patients in clinical practice

title: PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND PAIN SCIENCE FOR ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this fully online subject, students will develop their knowledge in applying comprehensive concepts of pathophysiology, pain science, and pharmacology to differentiate between normal and abnormal neuromusculoskeletal function within the context of advanced physiotherapy. Students will critically evaluate pathology and pathogenesis related to neuromusculoskeletal dysfunction and interpret the neuromusculoskeletal system’s responses to load, including impacts on function, injury, and tissue healing. This subject provides qualified physiotherapists with comprehensive knowledge of clinical sciences and their influence on assessment and treatments in advanced physiotherapy practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the pathology, and pathogenesis underlying neuromusculoskeletal dysfunctions in advanced physiotherapy practice
Integrate a theoretical understanding of the effects of pharmacology on pain and the neuromusculoskeletal system to inform effective advanced physiotherapy assessment and management.

Interpret how the neuromusculoskeletal system’s responds to load, including its effects on function, injury response, and tissue healing, and evaluate how these factors influence assessment and treatments in advanced physiotherapy practice
Integrate and apply comprehensive knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and pain science to distinguish between normal and abnormal function in the neuromusculoskeletal system

title: ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR THE UPPER BODY
syllabus_overview: In this blended subject, students will gain advanced knowledge and clinical skills in musculoskeletal and sports and exercise physiotherapy, with a focus on the upper limb, cervical and thoracic spine. The subject begins with an online clinical reasoning module designed to enhance decision-making and problem-solving of complex cases. This is followed by an online module to enhance diagnostic imaging interpretation for upper limb and cervical presentations. Practical components include applied clinical anatomy wet labs and advanced physiotherapy assessment and management of upper limb, cervical and thoracic conditions. This subject prepares qualified physiotherapists to integrate advanced assessment and management techniques into clinical practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award .
learning_outcomes: Integrate contemporary, evidence-informed practices into clinical scenarios involving the upper limb, cervical and thoracic spine, demonstrating the ability to adapt and apply advanced physiotherapy techniques in a variety of clinical settings.

Apply advanced clinical reasoning skills to develop and implement comprehensive assessment and management strategies for complex upper limb, cervical and thoracic spine conditions in musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy

Apply advanced theoretical knowledge and practical skills to critically analyse and address complex neuromusculoskeletal presentations of the upper limb, cervical and thoracic spine, with a focus on optimising patient outcomes
Proficiently interpret diagnostic imaging and integrate applied clinical anatomy to inform evidence-based decision-making in patient care for conditions of the upper limb, cervical and thoracic spine

Critically apply self-reflection to identify strengths and areas for improvement in the assessment and management of upper limb, cervical, and thoracic conditions, fostering ongoing professional growth as an effective lifelong learner.

title: ADVANCED SPORT AND EXERCISE PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this blended subject, students will gain advanced knowledge and practical clinical skills in sports and exercise physiotherapy. The subject focuses on sports-specific injury prevention and management, rehabilitation, and performance enhancement. Through a combination of contemporary evidence-informed practices and advanced clinical reasoning, students will learn to effectively assess, treat, and manage complex sports injuries, optimising athlete recovery and performance outcomes. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Critically apply advanced physiotherapy clinical reasoning to facilitate accurate differential diagnosis and management of complex sports injury presentations.
Integrate advanced clinical reasoning and sports-specific physiotherapy knowledge and communication skills to design and implement comprehensive interventions for sports-specific injuries
Critically reflect on and communicate clinical decisions, using evidence-based reasoning to effectively explain and justify management plans for sports-specific injuries.
Apply advanced practical skills in sports and exercise physiotherapy to implement effective injury assessment and management strategies for sports-related injuries

title: ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR THE LOWER BODY
syllabus_overview: In this blended subject, students will gain advanced knowledge and clinical skills in musculoskeletal and sports and exercise physiotherapy, with a focus on the lower limb and lumbar spine. The subject begins with an online module to enhance diagnostic imaging interpretation for lower limb and lumbar presentations. Practical components include applied clinical anatomy wet labs and advanced assessment and management of lower limb and lumbar conditions. This subject prepares qualified physiotherapists to integrate advanced assessment and management techniques into clinical practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award .
learning_outcomes: Proficiently interpret diagnostic imaging and integrate applied clinical anatomy to inform evidence-based decision-making in patient care for conditions of the lower limb and lumbar spine

Apply advanced theoretical knowledge and practical skills to critically analyse and address complex neuromusculoskeletal presentations of the lower limb and lumbar spine, with a focus on optimizing patient outcomes

Apply critical self-reflection by identifying strengths and areas for improvement in the assessment and management of lower limb and lumbar conditions, fostering ongoing professional growth as an effective lifelong learner.

Integrate contemporary, evidence-informed practices into clinical scenarios involving the lower limb and lumbar spine, demonstrating the ability to adapt and apply advanced physiotherapy techniques in a variety of clinical settings.

Apply advanced clinical reasoning skills to develop and implement comprehensive assessment and management strategies for complex lower limb and lumbar spine conditions in musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy

title: ADVANCED MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this blended subject, students will develop advanced skills in musculoskeletal physiotherapy, with a focus on managing complex neuromusculoskeletal dysfunctions. Through a biopsychosocial framework, students will enhance their clinical reasoning, developing proficiency in techniques to differentiate between neuromusculoskeletal and non-mechanical presentations. The subject emphasizes advanced manual therapy, exercise prescription, and integrating theoretical knowledge with examination outcomes to inform effective treatment strategies. Students will apply evidence-based practices to assess and manage complex cases, preparing them for high-level clinical practice in musculoskeletal physiotherapy. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced clinical reasoning by communicating effectively to peers about treatment and outcome evaluation approaches for patients with complex neuromusculoskeletal presentations to peers
Critically apply advanced musculoskeletal physiotherapy skills and clinical reasoning within a biopsychosocial framework to manage musculoskeletal conditions

Apply advanced clinical reasoning skills in musculoskeletal physiotherapy by integrating and applying theoretical knowledge, examination outcomes, and contributing factors to assess and manage complex neuromusculoskeletal dysfunction.
Critically apply comprehensive clinical examination procedures to enable differential diagnoses of neuromusculoskeletal dysfunction.

title: ADVANCED SPORT AND EXERCISE PHYSIOTHERAPY CLINICAL PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will begin with a pre-placement online module designed to equip students for professional practice in a sports environment. This module covers critical topics such as interprofessional collaboration, leadership within a sporting context, injury prevention strategies, designing comprehensive rehabilitation plans, and effective load management. Students will then undertake 120 hours of clinical placement throughout the teaching period under the supervision of experienced sports and exercise physiotherapists. This includes a minimum of 40 placement hours within a sport-specific environment (sporting team, sports tournament, training camp). The remaining hours may be fulfilled across various settings, including sports teams, private practices, or other sports-specific facilities. Supervised clinical practice will foster rational decision-making in treatment selection, progression, and ongoing management planning, ensuring students are well-prepared for roles with professional sports teams. This subject will enable students to apply advanced theoretical and clinical knowledge in sports and exercise physiotherapy to refine their skills in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of sports and exercise-related conditions. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate and justify recommendations to lead and influence athletes, peers, coaches and support staff, while demonstrating competency in optimising strategies for injury prevention, management, and rehabilitation, across sporting populations from a variety of backgrounds.

Critically evaluate physiotherapy management plans for sports and exercise-related conditions, utilising advanced clinical reasoning and reflective practice to adapt interventions, enhance treatment efficacy and promote long-term recovery and performance for athletes

Develop and critically apply advanced physiotherapy management strategies for sports and exercise-related conditions, integrating assessment findings and theoretical knowledge to guide clinical reasoning to support the planning and implementation of effective treatment resulting in optimal patient/athlete outcomes

Integrate advanced physiotherapy skills and clinical reasoning to plan and perform effective assessments that enable the development of person-centred problem lists, and diagnosis of sports and exercise-related conditions.

title: ADVANCED MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY CLINICAL PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop advanced physiotherapy neuromusculoskeletal examination and management skills within a clinical reasoning paradigm. You will undertake 160 hours of supervised clinical practice within the Australian Healthcare System at hospitals/health services and/or private physiotherapy clinics. Supervised clinical practice encourages and facilitates rational decision making with respect to treatment selection, progression and planning of ongoing management programs. You will also have the opportunity to integrate and refine your advanced physiotherapy manual techniques and exercise prescription skills into your clinical practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Deliver ethical, accountable, and culturally responsive client-centered care, while effectively communicating with clients, carers, and health professionals to optimize treatment outcomes

Perform safe, systematic and prioritized advanced musculoskeletal initial assessments and treatments on complex neuromusculoskeletal clients integrating appropriate outcome measures to evaluate, refine, and monitor patient outcomes.

Synthesise initial and follow-up assessment findings of complex neuromusculoskeletal clients to refine or develop treatment goals and guide the progression of interventions within a multidisciplinary healthcare team

Critically apply evidence informed practice and expert judgment to guide clinical reasoning in assessing and managing complex neuromusculoskeletal clients, facilitating safe return to activity and participation.

title: ADVANCED PHYSIOTHERAPY PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: This subject involves three modules: (i) advanced spinal physiotherapy, (ii) professional practice, and (iii) a self-directed project. Advanced spinal physiotherapy expands on the clinical reasoning and manual therapy skills developed earlier in the course, with focus on spinal physiotherapy. The professional practice module aims to prepare you to commence practice as a newly graduated health professional, covering legislation, codes of conduct and ethical practice. In the third module, you will identify a gap in physiotherapy practice and develop a creative solution to this issue. As a self-directed project, you will develop their solution with the ultimate aim of improving physiotherapy practice within the chosen context.
learning_outcomes: Design, justify and conduct safe, sensitive, advanced and highly case-specific assessments.
Analyse and critically evaluate assessment findings and prioritise patient needs to at least the minimum standard expected for an entry level physiotherapist
Communicate competently and clearly and coherently communicate research findings to a variety of audiences, both individually and collaboratively.
Select, safely apply and medico legally document high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) manipulation techniques to the lumbar, thoracic and cervical regions of the spines.
Examine, and critically evaluate evidence to create, and enhance aspects of physiotherapy practice.
Critically reflect in teams on personal and colleagues' professional behaviour based on relevant legislation, ethical standards and Codes of Practice.
Prioritise and critically evaluate interventions using reliable and valid outcome measures to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Design, justify and conduct complex case-specific physiotherapy management plans.

title: ADVANCED PRACTICE OF SPORTS PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students are given the opportunity to develop skills in patient examination and differential diagnosis within a clinical reasoning paradigm. Supervised clinical practice encourages and facilitates rational decision making with respect to treatment selection, treatment progression and planning ongoing management programs.
learning_outcomes: Combine advanced clinical reasoning and an evidence based approach to analyse and interpret assessment findings to minimum standard expected of a postgraduate sports physiotherapist.
Demonstrate professional behaviour appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a postgraduate sports physiotherapist

Manage clients with sports injury disorders by selecting, performing, monitoring and progressing interventions safely and precisely to the minimum standard expected of a postgraduate sports physiotherapist

Assess and manage an athlete/ client's sports injury related problems using appropriate communication and collaboration with clients, coaches and other support staff, carers, family and health professional colleagues to at least the minimum standard expected for a postgraduate sports physiotherapist.
Justify and performs a safe, systematic, efficient, prioritised physical assessment to the minimum standard expected of a postgraduate sports physiotherapist
Plan for improved future performance by reflecting on the processes by which clinical decisions were made during patient interactions
Assess an athlete/ client's sports injury related problem using a sensitive and specific client interview to at least the standard of a postgraduate sports physiotherapist.

title: CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will integrate core strands of knowledge and practice with contemporary health needs of individuals, groups, communities and populations. You will develop knowledge and skills in interventions and management plans for people with chronic conditions in both group and individual contexts as well as health leadership and change management skills. You will critique models of health, theories of health behaviour and apply innovative problem-solving skills to health-related scenarios covering a range of chronic conditions. Principles of ethical leadership, change management, social justice, cultural competence, interprofessional, person-centred, evidence-based practice and critical reflection approaches will be adopted during the exploration of topics.
learning_outcomes: Collaboratively investigate and develop ethical health leadership behaviours to responsibly manage change and promote sustainable and contemporary healthcare practice.

Collaboratively and individually evaluate factors that contribute to health inequality between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians and develop recommendations to improve health outcomes for Indigenous Australians.
Critically evaluate and respond to barriers and enablers of health for clients with chronic conditions
Critically evaluate and design evidence-based recommendations for clients with chronic conditions
Develop and evaluate culturally sensitive, effective and safe health programs that draw on the principles of inclusion, equity and accessibility for clients with chronic conditions.

title: CLINICAL REASONING IN PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: In this subject students are given the opportunity to develop skills in clinical reasoning in a case-based paradigm. Lecturers will present the applied clinical anatomy, tissue pathology, patient presentations, assessment and treatment information, utilising case scenarios to illustrate the clinical reasoning process used by physiotherapists at the masters level.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of clinical examination procedure to enable differential diagnoses.
Demonstrate advanced skills of manual therapy and exercise prescription for safe and effective management.

Manage and rehabilitate patients/athletes/clients with musculoskeletal conditions and sports injuries using advanced neuro-musculoskeletal knowledge and practical skills within a psychosocial framework.
Demonstrate advanced clinical reasoning skills in Musculoskeletal and Sports Physiotherapy through critical evaluation of findings and evidence.

title: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE IN HEALTH
syllabus_overview: Evidence based practice is the use of best available evidence combined with patient preferences, available resources and therapist expertise in making decisions about the care of patients. Evidence based health care requires the physiotherapist to be able to perform the five steps of evidence based practice. In this subject students will build on the skills developed in previous research subjects in the production of a written Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) for publication in a web-based clinical resource. This resource will be peer reviewed, with the students further applying their EBP skills in order to critically appraise the work of other students. In this manner they will further develop the necessary skills to perform evidence based practice, while gaining a greater understanding of the peer review process and contributing to a valuable evidence based resource.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise with colleagues the methodology of a variety of research designs to determine the relative weight of research evidence.
Collaborate with colleagues to develop and justify research topics that will enhance clinical knowledge and systematically locate evidence.
Collaboratively collate current, peer-reviewed evidence, to answer clinically oriented research questions.
Critically reflect on team strengths and weaknesses in relation to evidence-based-practice.
Critically appraise published work in a process of peer review.
Critically analyse and interpret research findings with colleagues to justify answers to clinical research questions.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICUM B
syllabus_overview: This subject is the second of 6 professional practicum subjects across different specific areas of practice. Students are required to meet competency in 6 specific practice areas to meet professional accreditation requirements. In this subject students are in supervised clinical practice for 20 days over 5 weeks and prescribed independent learning (total subject hours 160). Clinical practicums are supervised by registered physiotherapists and may be organised outside normal teaching weeks. Students will develop specific competencies in the assessment of clients' problems and needs, analysis of assessment findings, formulation of short and long term goals and development, implementation and evaluation of intervention plans. Students will apply specialised knowledge, cognitive and technical skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a learner.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate evidence to select, perform, monitor and progress interventions safely in a specific area of practice and appropriately in collaboration with clients.

Communicate effectively and appropriately with clients, carers, family and health professional colleagues in one specific area of practice to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Implement discharge planning to address client and carer's needs for ongoing care in one specific area of practice.
Analyse and interpret assessment findings accurately to identify client's problems and set realistic short and long terms goals for a specific practice area.
Plan and initiate effective education/health promotion in one specific area of practice with clients and caregivers.
Conduct sensitive and case specific client interviews to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist in a specific practice area.
Practice responsibly, applying professional behaviour in one specific area of practice appropriate to at least the minimum standard expected for a beginner/entry level physiotherapist.
Perform safe, systematic, efficient and accurate physical assessments.

title: SEARCH AND EVALUATE EVIDENCE (SPORT AND MUSCULOSKELETAL PHYSIOTHERAPY)
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop the knowledge and skills required for evidence-based practice in musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy. You will develop skills in formulating answerable clinical questions, searching for the available evidence, critical appraisal of the literature and making decisions about clinical practice based on the evidence. The subject is comprised of online learning modules, resources, facilitated discussion board tasks and required readings. You will complete a written Critically Appraised Topic (CAT) based on a sports or musculoskeletal physiotherapy problem that you have encountered in clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and synthesize research findings with individual patient assessments to answer formulated musculoskeletal or sports physiotherapy clinical research questions.
Interpret the diagnostic utility of physiotherapy assessment procedures within the context of the clinical reasoning hypothesis categories

Critically appraise the methodology of qualitative research, diagnosis studies, cohort studies, randomised controlled trials, and systematic reviews that are relevant to musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy.
Construct and execute a comprehensive search strategy to locate evidence from a range of sources relevant to musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy clinical practice.
Integrate research findings into clinical practice, adapting for individual patients.
Reflect on your musculoskeletal or sports physiotherapy clinical practice experience to formulate an answerable clinical research question.

title: WEBINARS IN SPORTS PHYSIOTHERAPY
syllabus_overview: This subject takes you through an in-depth analysis of contemporary and controversial topics in Sports and Exercise Physiotherapy. Final Year Master of Sport and Exercise Physiotherapy students will deliver a Webinar to their fellow students, and develop other knowledge translation resources, on a selected topic in Sports and Exercise Physiotherapy. You will critically analyse the literature and develop a clinical topic for an informative webinar, as well as written and visual communication resources, that showcases the interdisciplinary management and clinical leadership required to achieve desired patient-specific outcomes. Each topic will be studied in relation to epidemiology, clinical assessment, diagnosis, management, and rehabilitation.
