learning_outcomes: Interpret how the neuro-musculoskeletal system responds to forces associated with movement, and how this changes with deconditioning, ageing and injury.
Assess the physical impacts of human interactions with equipment and the environment.
Apply principles of functional anatomy and biomechanics to critically analyse movement patterns and identify strategies to enhance performance, identify deficiencies, and minimise injury risk.
Apply biomechanical principles to the analysis of human movement.
Describe biomechanical principles and their relationship to human movement.

title: SPORT ANALYTICS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theoretical concepts and principles that underpin the field of sports analytics and performance analysis. Using small and pre-existing sports-related data sets, you will be taught basic data handling and analytical skills. You will explore a variety of techniques available to the sports analyst to analyse athlete performance. You will also develop an appreciation of the limitations of performance and sports analytics techniques.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical concepts of data analytics to sport and athlete performance
Design performance analysis plans independently and collaboratively
Apply basic data handling and analytical methods to data captured from sport
Clearly and coherently communicate outcomes of data analysis to peers

title: EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY AND ASSESSMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will investigate the normal range of physiological responses to sport, exercise and performance training. Particular attention will be given to the physiological responses and adaptations of the cardiovascular, respiratory, musculoskeletal, nervous and endocrine systems to sport and exercise to sport and exercise in healthy individuals.
learning_outcomes: Safely monitor and evaluate physiological responses at rest and during exercise.
Evaluate and describe the individual and integrated physiological responses and adaptations to acute and chronic exercise.
Discuss the function, regulation and interaction of physiological systems relating to exercise.
Apply knowledge of the physiological responses to acute exercise and the adaptations to chronic exercise to inform exercise programming.
Analyse and interpret physiological data obtained during acute exercise, and compare such data between time points, individuals and populations.

title: INCLUSIVE SPORT COACHING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with the applied knowledge and skills to modify aspects of your coaching and to be able to plan and deliver a safe and effective coaching environment for every participant, regardless of age, gender, culture, religious affiliation, sexual/gender orientation and ability . Additionally, you will undertake hours of practical learning with specialist schools, which will provide an authentic learning environment to apply theoretical knowledge to professional practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Communicate clearly and effectively to a diverse range of audiences
Collaborate in small groups to modify sessions and programs to individualise to participant skill development needs.
Discuss the Sports Industry standards and benchmarks in terms of inclusive practices
Apply an evidence-based planning process to design, monitor, reflect and evaluate the effectiveness of a coaching intervention.
Apply a social model of philosophy to promote inclusion in physical activity.
Apply knowledge of principles of good coaching to design, implement and evaluate safe and effective coaching sessions for under-represented populations

title: EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION AND DELIVERY
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be provided with the knowledge to design specifically tailored training plans with an emphasis on athlete populations. You will learn how to analyse the demands of a given sport, then prescribe targeted training interventions to enhance relevant strength, endurance and speed qualities. Periodisation strategies will be discussed to enable the short- and long-term development of the athlete with respect to their sport. In the practical component, you will learn how to instruct resistance training exercises and conduct field tests of fitness qualities.
learning_outcomes: Effectively demonstrate verbal and nonverbal communication skills in the context of exercise instruction.
Apply strategies to teach exercise technique and to correct dysfunctional movement
Apply and adapt physiological and biomechanical principles to design safe and effective exercise programs for general and athlete populations.
Analyse outcomes of client assessments to design and modify best-practice exercise programs.
Apply risk measures and discipline-specific knowledge of contraindications for engaging in exercise programs to inform client decisions.

title: SKILL DEVELOPMENT IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you are introduced to the processes and techniques used in the acquisition of motor skills. The common theoretical approaches to understanding how people learn and perform motor skills will be examined. You will learn about key concepts in motor learning and techniques such as the use of feedback, verbal instruction, implicit learning, and constraints-based design as well as how to measure and track the results of learning. You will apply knowledge of practice design to create and test learning programmes to influence the development of sport and exercise skills. The subject will also provide you with an understanding of how to adjust tasks to suit the needs of individual learners and a set of guidelines for selecting appropriate approaches to learning.
learning_outcomes: Explain the common theoretical models in skill acquisition.
Apply principles of learning design to change performance outcomes.
Examine the changes in motor skill performance that occur with learning .
Analyse the major factors that influence the learning and performance of motor skills.
Assess motor learning programs that include performance testing to measure rate of learning, for individual needs

title: EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION FOR DIVERSE POPULATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the assessment, delivery and prescription of exercise for diverse populations. Building upon the skills learnt in SPE1FEP and SPE2EPD, you will learn how to conduct pre-exercise screening and assessments and prescribe and deliver exercise for individuals from diverse life stages, abilities and cultures. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Conduct, interpret, and communicate information and results from exercise and health assessments for diverse populations
Critically review literature and case examples on the effect of exercise for diverse populations across the lifespan
Conduct relevant pre-exercise screenings for diverse populations and identify considerations and contraindications for exercise assessment and prescription.
Design, adapt, and monitor exercise to meet client’s individual needs, abilities, and stage of life.

title: PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND HEALTH
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will evaluate the role of physical activity and sedentary behaviour in population health. From an epidemiological perspective, you will identify population groups at risk of insufficient physical activity and the factors influencing this. You will appraise policy and population-level approaches for physical activity promotion, including planning, implementation, and evaluation practices. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Identify and assess populations at risk of physical inactivity and sedentary behaviour to apply recommendations and inform the development of interventions
Critically analyse the role of physical activity and sedentary behaviour in population health and lifestyle-related chronic disease
Analyse and evaluate the impact of public policy and population-level interventions on promoting physical activity and reducing sedentary behaviour
Interpret population data and research evidence to appraise factors affecting physical activity behaviour

title: SPORT EXPERTISE
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an understanding of the development of elite skills, the characteristics of experts, and the paradigms used in talent identification and development, training, and skill maintenance. It addresses perceptual-cognitive skill, automaticity, decision making and tactics, and the methods used in understanding elite performance in complex domains with physical and cognitive demands, such as sport. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to synthesize and critically review empirical journal articles in the area of expertise research and communicate the findings to peers.
Identify and describe key findings, methods, and paradigms used to measure expert performance in skill acquisition and motor behaviour
Conduct and evaluate assessments of sport expertise using standard and accepted testing protocols
Select and justify methods to measure and develop expertise in human performance

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN SPORT AND EXERCISE SCIENCE 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply theoretical knowledge and integrate a range of professional skills in a professional practice setting. You will access a range of career development tools to acquire the non-technical skills and industry-specific practical skills needed to develop employability and to prepare you professionally for employment in sport and exercise science. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of placement exposure and attendance at industry placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a sport and exercise science practitioner.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional behaviour in accordance with Exercise and Sports Science Australia's Code of Professional Practice and Ethical Conduct as an entry level practitioner.
Communicate knowledge and ideas clearly and coherently with peers and clients in a variety of settings.
Critically review personal performance to identify professional strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement.
Contribute to a team and apply discipline-specific knowledge and skills in order to provide safe and effective exercise related interventions in collaboration with clients and supervisors.
Critically review the skills and attributes required for employment in sport and exercise science

title: TECHNOLOGY IN SPORT, FITNESS AND HEALTH
syllabus_overview: This subject delves into the evolving technologies shaping the sports, fitness, and healthcare sectors, equipping students with both applied skills and a critical lens for evaluation. The subject emphasises hands-on experience with contemporary technologies while concurrently interrogating their validity, reliability, and ethical implications. Through a blend of problem-based learning and case study analysis, students will develop an understanding of technology's role, establish decision-making frameworks, and discern its potential and limits in enhancing human performance. This fusion of technology and critical insight prepares students for responsible innovation in the rapidly changing landscapes of sport, fitness, and healthcare, blending technological proficiency with critical and ethical reasoning. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Examine the ethical, legal, and societal considerations of using technology in sport, fitness, and health.
Gain practical experience through lab sessions, case studies, and collaborative projects, employing real-world technologies within the sport, fitness and health domains.
Explore how technology can be employed in promoting general health and wellbeing.
Evaluate and apply technology to monitor, analyze, and enhance athletic performance and training techniques.
Critically assess various technological tools, including wearable devices, performance analysis software, virtual reality, and their applications in sport, fitness, and health.

title: SPORT AND RECREATION PRACTICUM
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will apply the knowledge and skills developed in the foundation years of the course via an industry placement with a non profit, commercial or government organization. You will have the opportunity to use your industry placement experience as a rich learning environment to assist you refine your personal and professional competencies, and apply your theoretical knowledge to contemporary sport and recreation management issues and challenges. You will also refine your understanding of your graduate capabilities to support your transition to working in the sport and recreation industry. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge and skills in sport and recreation management to interact effectively in professional contexts and facilitate the achievement of project or organisational outcomes.
Identify personal examples of employability skills and create a professional development plan including resources for entry level positions.
Demonstrate your understanding of contemporary concepts and approaches to Sport and Recreation Management and reflect on your own development through the industry placement.

title: VOLUNTEERS IN SPORT AND RECREATION
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the theory and practice of managing volunteers in the sport and recreation industry. You will learn about the nature and scope of volunteering in Australia, the psychology of volunteering, and the theory and practice of recruiting, training, managing and developing volunteers in sport and recreation. You will examine specific issues related to the management of volunteers in specialised sport and recreation roles (officials, coaches, administrators, event volunteers and directors of governing organisations) and specific legal issues relevant to volunteers. Students will be required to self-source 10 hours of volunteering activity early in the semester. This subject will be offered from 2027
learning_outcomes: Design a volunteer management plan for sport and recreation organisation.
Critically analyse the volunteer management practices used in the sport and recreation industry.
Reflect on and critically review the impact volunteers have in supporting the operations of sport and recreation organisations, programs or events.

title: ADVANCED SPORT COACHING B
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject focuses on coaching-specific skill and practice on the level of the individual coach. Specifically, you will further advance your knowledge of sport coaching and development by going beyond program design to consider the coach as leader and manager. You will be required to critically evaluate the context of coaching, and grapple with issues related to the immediate coaching environment (e.g., burnout, wellbeing, mental health, culture, ethics). You will be taught to synthesise previous practical and foundational knowledge to complex coaching environments and scenarios across the sport coaching pathway (i.e., participation to elite). National, state, and community sporting associations, local government, and professional sport will be explored. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement, monitor and evaluate mid-to long-term programmes of practice and competition based on institutional and participant/athlete needs.
Critique prevailing beliefs, values and assumptions within the coaching environment to operate within the organisational culture
Justify appropriate pedagogy, practice and communication methods to facilitate a range of different coaching scenarios to meet the learning needs of the participants
Establish and maintain an effective, inclusive and empathetic relationship with athletes, staff and other stakeholders
Identify own learning needs and take responsibility for the development and application of strategies for further self-development.

title: GOVERNANCE OF SPORT AND RECREATION ORGANISATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the unique governance issues and models prevalent in the sport and recreation industry for organisations such as state and national sport organisations, quasi government agencies, recreation industry peak bodies, community associations and peak governing bodies at an international level. You will examine how governance models, systems and processes influence the growth and sustainability of the sport and recreation industry at local, state and national levels. You will gain a deep understanding of the relationship between governance and organizational outcomes for end users and consumers of sport and recreation.
learning_outcomes: Find and evaluate governance documents, reports and case studies to make informed governance decisions in the recreation and sport sector
Communicate complex ideas and analyses of recreation and sport sector governance issues, models, systems and processes to a variety of audiences
Evaluate the broader social impacts of governance issues and models to support inclusivity, equity, and fairness in access to sport and recreation opportunities for diverse populations.
Apply critical thinking and problem solving to improve the governance of recreation and sport organisations.

title: EXERCISE PRESCRIPTION FOR SPECIAL POPULATIONS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about the delivery of exercise for diverse populations. This subject will explore the pathophysiology of disease, disability, and injury, and the role of exercise in preventing and managing these conditions. Building upon the skills learnt in SPE2EPA and SPE2EPD, you will learn how to conduct pre-exercise screening, deliver assessments and prescribe exercise for people with chronic conditions, including considerations for individuals from different cultures, age groups, and abilities.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and explain the aetiology of common chronic conditions and lifestyle-related diseases
Design and conduct suitable pre-exercise screenings for diverse populations, and identify contraindications for assessment and exercise.
Demonstrate competency across a range of practical and technical skills, including associated data interpretation, in sport and exercise science.
Design, deliver and adapt exercise programmes to meet client's individual need, physical capacity and stage of life.
Critically analyse literature and case studies on the influence of exercise on chronic conditions and across the lifespan.

title: HIGH PERFORMANCE TRAINING FOR SPORT
syllabus_overview: This subject provides you with advanced knowledge in exercise physiology to inform the prescription of training, ergogenic practices and athlete monitoring within high-performance sport. You will use authentic training case studies to highlight the important role of physiological knowledge in applied sport. Practical classes will allow you to apply knowledge and develop a range of skills needed to undertake advanced physiological testing and provide scientific support in high-performance sports. Using an evidence-based approach, you will demonstrate an ability to prescribe and deliver training programs for both individuals and teams, based on best-practice principles.
learning_outcomes: Critically interpret physiological data in response to acute and chronic exercise to communicate variations between time-points, individuals and populations.
Synthesise knowledge of physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise to appraise training and ergogenic practices specific to high-performance sport.
Apply exercise physiology theory to justify the development of testing batteries, training monitoring strategies and exercise programming.
Synthesise knowledge and skills across a range of exercise science disciplines to provide holistic development of training programs.
Critically evaluate best-practice guidelines to design and deliver exercise programs for individuals and groups for a range of performance outcomes.

title: MOTOR BEHAVIOUR IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop an understanding of the theoretical basis of motor behaviour and its application to sport and exercise performance. You will be introduced to the neuromuscular and sensory systems and their influence on movement in exercise, sporting, and clinical environments, techniques for measuring motor behaviour and expertise and how these techniques can be used to design best practice interventions to suit individual motor learning needs. You will also be introduced to the assessment of motor behaviour research and design a research proposal to measure specific motor behaviour outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Appraise motor control function in a range of populations using appropriate testing methods
Analyse and interpret research in the area of motor behaviour in sport and exercise
Critically review the changes in motor behaviour with learning and expertise, ageing, and movement disorders
Critically review prominent theories of motor control and motor behaviour, and how they are applied in exercise and sporting environments
Explain the structure and function of the neuromuscular and sensory systems as they relate to control of movement in motor behaviour and skill acquisition
Select and justify appropriate methods used to measure expert performance in skill acquisition and motor behaviour

title: MUSCULOSKELETAL MECHANICS AND INJURY PREVENTION
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will integrate applied knowledge and practical skills, using an evidence-based approach, in reducing the risk of musculoskeletal injury. You will be introduced to advanced theoretical understanding of the structure, function, response and adaptation of the neuro-musculoskeletal system to loading and injury. Advanced biomechanical concepts will further demonstrate the complex mechanics of human movement. In practical classes, you will apply theoretical knowledge, develop practical skills and use technology to evaluate biomechanical function and mechanical proficiency. You will apply practical skills within the scope of an Exercise Scientist to assist in the assessment of human movement, injury risk, and readiness for return-to-sport.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the effects of exercise, immobilisation, aging and injury on the neuro-musculoskeletal system of the human body.
Evaluate the intrinsic and extrinsic factors associated with injury, disability and disease.
Evaluate the role of exercise scientists in the assessment of human movement, injury risk, and readiness for return-to-sport plans.
Analyse normal gait patterns using appropriate terminology, and recognise the changes associated with injury, disability and disease.
Collaboratively evaluate and engage with advanced biomechanical methods for accurate and safe data collection and analysis.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN SPORT AND EXERCISE SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply theoretical knowledge and integrate a range of professional skills by undertaking an extended professional practice placement. You will access a range of career development tools to acquire the non-technical skills and industry-specific practical skills needed to prepare you professionally for employment in sport and exercise science and ongoing employability. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of placement exposure. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a sport and exercise science practitioner.This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional behaviour in accordance with Exercise and Sports Science Australia's Code of Professional Practice and Ethical Conduct as an entry level practitioner.
Contribute to a team and apply discipline-specific knowledge and skills in order to provide safe and effective exercise-related interventions in collaboration with clients and supervisors.
Critically review personal performance to identify professional strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement
Communicate knowledge and ideas clearly and coherently with peers and clients in a variety of settings.
Critically review the skills and attributes required for employment in sport and exercise science

title: TALENT IDENTIFICATION AND GAME DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: You will appraise and apply criteria of athlete talent identification from theoretical models and practical assessment. You will analyse and compare how athletes are identified in various sports through the key criteria of athlete development. You will be introduced to and discuss the theoretical frameworks and models used to identify and develop talented athletes. Taking a multidisciplinary approach, you will use a variety of assessments for the purpose of identifying talented athletes and measuring their development. You will be introduced to and appraise the potential outcomes of and the justifications for the use of talent identification and development.
learning_outcomes: Critically review factors which can have an impact on the development of talented athletes
Review and assess potential outcomes and use of talent identification and game development with key stakeholders
Justify and implement multidisciplinary approaches to talent identification and development
Review and analyse the frameworks/models used within talent identification and development
Develop talent identification and development protocols based on evidence-based studies

title: ANALYTICAL METHODS IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop expertise concerning research methodology, statistical analysis and data science techniques within a sport and exercise science context. There is an emphasis on the practical interpretation and communication of results to different audiences (e.g. for academic writing versus client consultation). You will learn how to perform various data handling techniques, statistical tests and explore data visualisation techniques to effectively demonstrate outcomes in a professional setting. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply data handling techniques to correctly treat and process data to provide a range of descriptive statistical outcomes.
Critically appraise statistical designs, research methodologies and modern analytical techniques relevant to sports and exercise science
Apply data visualisation techniques that provide practical interpretations and communicate research results to different audiences
Apply high-level understanding of the theories and methodologies underlying modern statistics and data science techniques.
Apply appropriate statistical tests and data science tools to evaluate evidence and to analyse research data

title: SPORT COACHING PRACTICUM
syllabus_overview: This subject will enable you to apply theoretical knowledge and integrate a range of professional skills by undertaking an extended sports coaching placement. In preparation, you will be required to explore the sport coaching industry and undertake activities to enhance your self-development and build a portfolio of evidence of your capability. Alongside the practicum experience you will reflect on your performance, development and learning and apply these in your preparation to become more employable within the sports coaching workforce.This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and reflect on their own performance to identify professional strengths and weaknesses to develop a plan for improvement.
Transmit specialist knowledge, skills and ideas clearly and coherently with peers and participants in a variety of settings.
Critically review the available opportunities and requisite experiences, skills, knowledge and attributes for employment in sports coaching.
Use initiative and judgement to apply the values and ethics expected of professional coaches in accordance with Sport Australia's guidelines.
Synthesise and apply discipline-specific knowledge and skills in order to provide safe and effective coaching for a variety of participants.
Demonstrate autonomy and judgement to develop a range of employment-related skills to prepare for employment in the sports coaching industry.

title: ADVANCED SPORT ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will learn about advanced and contemporary topics in sport analytics and tools for understanding tactics and strategies in team sport by quantifying the value of individual and team actions using spatiotemporal and notation data. You will learn how to quantify skill and randomness in sport performance by understanding the statistical properties of sport performance metrics, and you will learn how to analyse wearable sensor and sport video data with machine learning techniques. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply spatiotemporal and notational data to value sport actions
Analyse and interpret the statistical properties of sport performance metrics
Apply image and video analysis methods to sport video
Critically appraise and implement contemporary methods in sport analytics

title: PRINCIPLES OF SPORT ANALYTICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will explore the principles of analytics within the context of sporting environments. You will learn to apply the mathematical and statistical architecture and rationale that underpins a range of sport analytics methods. Practices in handling, cleaning and processing data generated from sport will be examined. You will learn to apply basic programming and coding skills to analyse sport-related data and answer complex questions. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse mathematical and statistical architecture to synthesize analytical approaches to complex sport-related problems
Apply analytical knowledge, principles and skills with initiative to new situations in sport and sport-related practice environments
Analyse data using basic programming skills to answer complex questions related to sport
Apply theoretical principles to common practices in handling, cleaning and processing data related to sport

title: SPORT ANALYTICS IN PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply theoretical understanding of analytics processes and methodologies to authentic sport-related data sets, such as seasonal AFL data to model and predict ladder positions and match outcomes. You will develop an analysis plan and implement this plan to formulate specific outcomes arising from the data analysis. You will use appropriate visual analytics tools to present your data to communicate formulated outcomes and findings.
learning_outcomes: Analyse existing sport-related data sets that have been generated in response to an identified need or sport-related question, with creativity and initiative.
Coherently communicate the outcomes of the analysis of sport-related data to a range of audiences, using visual analytics tools.

Apply analytical knowledge and skills with a high level of personal autonomy and accountability to the analysis and evaluation of sport-related data in response to an identified need or sport- related question.
Critically analyse sport-related data sets and synthesise a range of relevant outcomes.

title: SPORT DATA CAPTURE
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will learn about contemporary technology applications that generate data from sport. You will systematically appraise data capture technology to identify their limitations using accepted criteria and will explore those factors that influence effective and accurate data capture in sport and its handling and treatment. Using your understanding of these factors and available technology applications, you will identify appropriate applications and processes for a range of analysis scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical knowledge and technical skills to implement and evaluate data capture in sport.
Apply research and technical skills to justify selection and use of an appropriate range of technology applications in order to collect measurable data from sport.
Critically appraise new and existing technology applications that can be employed to generate data from sport.
Critically reflect on the limitations of technology used within sport analytics and their effect on the quality of data generated and collected from sport.

title: SPORT ANALYTICS PROJECT A
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will apply and expand on prior learning in sport analytics, computer and data science by working on an industry-relevant sport analytics project. This subject will prepare you for planning and developing substantial research and workplace projects. A range of interesting and diverse projects will be made available or you may propose your own. This project is part of two subjects (SPE5SPA and SPE5SPB) and is taken under the supervision of an experienced academic member/s of staff. You can choose a research pathway and submit the project as a written thesis or complete an applied project with submitted work aligned with workplace practices and documentation. In SPE5SPA you will write and present a literature review and project plan, along with preliminary data analysis. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Effectively communicate research and project ideas and proposals in written and oral format to academic and professional audiences.
Select and apply relevant statistical, analytical, graphical and programming methods to acquire, manipulate, analyse and visualise sport data.
Critically appraise and synthesise the relevant literature and documentation to justify and design a research or industry project.
Apply technical and project management skills to plan and develop a substantial sport analytics research or industry project.

title: SPORT ANALYTICS PROJECT B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will build on prior learning in sport analytics, computer and data science to continue your work on an industry-relevant sport analytics project. This subject will prepare you for conducting and reporting substantial independent and team-based research and workplace projects. Your completed project will be submitted as a research thesis or as an applied industry project with results and documentation. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Analyse, synthesise and report research and project findings with well supported interpretations using relevant data, literature and correctly referenced prose.
Apply relevant statistical, analytical, graphical and programming methods to acquire, manipulate, analyse and interpret sport data and summarise results using appropriate tables, figures and text.
Effectively communicate research and project findings in written and oral format to academic and professional audiences.
Apply technical and project management skills to execute a substantial sport analytics research or industry project.

title: DEVELOPING STRENGTH AND POWER
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with the tools needed to design and monitor the impact of periodised strength training plans to improve sports performance across a range of contexts. This subject will also give you the opportunity to perform and coach weightlifting and powerlifting actions in addition to their variants. Further, you will explore the acute and chronic response to strength training programs. Advanced methods of resistance training will also be discussed. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Explain and critique the effects of manipulating strength training program variables on the acute and chronic physiological responses to training.
Design and implement methods of testing strength qualities to improve athletic performance
Perform and evaluate the correct technique for weightlifting and powerlifting actions, in addition to their variations.
Design and critique periodised resistance training programs to improve sport performance across a range of sporting contexts for developing strength qualities.
Justify the integration of advanced methods of resistance training into training programs and demonstrate its effects.

title: DEVELOPING SPEED, AGILITY AND ENDURANCE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore, both practically and theoretically, the various speed and endurance qualities along with change of direction and agility. You will learn to design and implement training plans to improve and assess speed, agility and endurance performance across several sporting contexts. You will engage in practical scenarios where you will learn to coach the mechanics of running and apply training tasks to improve speed, agility and endurance performance.
learning_outcomes: Critique the effects of manipulating speed, agility and endurance program variables on the acute and chronic physiological responses to training.
Perform and evaluate the correct technique for sprinting and related actions
Design and implement methods of testing forms of agility, speed and endurance and to improve athletic performance
Explain advanced methods of developing speed, agility and endurance, and justify how they can be integrated into the training program.
Design and critique periodised training programs to improve speed, agility and endurance across a range of sporting contexts.

title: PRINCIPLES OF TRAINING AND MONITORING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be given the opportunity to develop advanced knowledge in relation to how overall training workload is manipulated over time to achieve competition goals. You will also learn to identify and monitor the key determinants of sport-specific performance and the role and scope of practice of the strength and conditioning coach. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Outline the scope of practice and ethical responsibilities for the strength and conditioning coach including the provision nutritional recommendations to athletes
Organise overall training workload across range of sporting contexts and monitor athlete responses
Critique, create and integrate flexibility and mobility programs for athletes
Classify the physical characteristics and determinants of sport-specific performance and understand the role of the strength and conditioning coach in this process
Identify and benchmark aspects of sports performance

title: COACHING PRINCIPLES, PRACTICE AND PROCESSES
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be given the opportunity to develop interpersonal, intrapersonal and professional knowledge in relation to coaching pedagogy. You will also learn key skills related to reflexivity, self-regulation and athlete-centred coaching in relation to your role as a coach. The purpose of this subject is to enable you to be able to develop meaningful relationships with the athletes you work with and understand the broader stakeholder engagement required to improve their performance and participation. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Describe and critique own coaching philosophy and the impact this has on their athletes
Effectively deploy critical incident analysis to inform and improve holistic athlete development practice
Triage theoretical constructs that are fit for purpose and apply into sport specific practice to support a range of athletes
Mediate effectively between key stakeholders responsible for supporting athlete performance
Critically reflect on own and other’s coaching expertise

title: RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE IN STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will become familiar with the multiple types of research undertaken in Strength and Conditioning contexts and prepare to undertake your own research project. This will include searching for and critiquing relevant literature, selecting appropriate study designs and methodologies, determining appropriate analysis techniques and developing your skills in writing-up research studies for dissemination. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Develop and refine writing skills to target appropriate styles for qualitative or quantitative research studies
Report evidence using mixed-methods approaches to cater for different audiences
Compare and distinguish appropriate analytical techniques for both qualitative and quantitative research designs
Critically appraise published research in the field of strength and conditioning
Construct and create research studies by selecting appropriate study designs and methodologies and demonstrate collaboration and teamwork skills.

title: INTEGRATED PROGRAMMING IN SPORT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop advanced skills in the design and delivery of multi-faceted training plans and programs. You will be provided with the opportunity to review, critique, and develop training plans across a range of sports, performance levels and constraints. In doing so, you will combine theoretical and tacit knowledge in strength and conditioning, sport science and medicine with problem solving to develop practical, evidence-based approaches to integrated programming in sport. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Design training plans across a range of sports, performance levels and constraints.
Examine training and design principles and critically appraise training plans.
Devise strategies to implement multi-faceted training plans within the constraints of the high-performance environment.
Develop integrated and tailored programs that balance coaching, strength and conditioning, sport science and medicine requirements.

title: HIGH PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop an understanding of what is required to work in a high-performance environment and the principles that underpin athlete, program and system success in sport. Your role and effectiveness as a practitioner will be considered within the context of an integrated and multidisciplinary program, including concepts related to role clarity, project management and teamwork, leadership, organisational structure and culture. Case studies and problem-based learning approaches will be used to explore contemporary theory and practice of athlete development, performance pathways, monitoring and evaluation, strategic planning, high performance programs and frameworks, and sport system development. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically review the athlete development pathway of a sport.
Identify principles of high performance in sport, and incorporate and evaluate these in a program or sport context.
Reflect and assess current personal status in regard to accreditation criteria of a Strength and Conditioning Coach and High Performance Manager to plan ongoing professional development.
Work independently and collaborate with others to solve complex problems in high performance sport and complete tasks and projects.
Prepare and deliver a short business case for a program initiative or intervention within a high performance program.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE IN STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus on the essential elements that distinguish you as a Strength and Conditioning professional, including identification of a professional brand and strategic career plan. You will access a range of career development tools to acquire the non-technical skills and industry-specific practical skills required to establish yourself as a Strength and Conditioning professional. Your attendance at professional placements will contribute to meeting this requirement. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Design professional profiles for the strength and conditioning industry that consider a range of personal attributes, strengths, motivations, and goals.
Develop strategic career plans for progression in the strength and conditioning industry.
Critically appraise personal performance in a strength and conditioning workplace to identify strengths, weaknesses and motivations and strategies for improvement.
Evaluate the characteristics of strength and conditioning workplaces to determine individual professional fit and alignment to future career goals.

title: DATA-BASED CRITICAL THINKING
syllabus_overview: This subject helps the student evaluate data-based evidence encountered in everyday life. It provides the fundamental numeracy skills required by business people, scientists, lawyers, nurses, journalists, social scientists, teachers and other professionals who need to evaluate data-based arguments, whether found in newspapers, television or on-line websites. This is achieved by a combination of studying newsworthy topics introduced in lectures, laboratory classes which encourage engagement with others and on-line quizzes that assess numeracy skills. The four themes covered in this subject are gathering useful data, turning data into information, probability and from data to decision making.
learning_outcomes: Critique data-based conclusions that are reported in the media and similar outlets
Interpret/derive simple numeric and graphical statistical summary measures of data.
Calculate probabilities in a variety of scenarios that may be used for informed decision making.
Identify and discuss common misconceptions of probability that can lead to poor decisions

title: MAJOR PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will design and undertake a research project in the field of strength and conditioning under supervision. You will work closely with your supervisor to negotiate a research topic. Areas of interest could include validity/reliability of measurement, strength and conditioning interventions and innovations, benchmarking, coaching practice, or related fields. The project will be written up as a final thesis or publishable manuscript for a peer reviewed journal.
learning_outcomes: Design, develop and implement appropriate study methodologies and designs to gather data.
Select and apply relevant statistical and analytical techniques to report data.
Effectively communicate research in written format to academic and professional audiences.
Critically appraise and synthesise the relevant literature relevant to a research question.

title: APPLIED STATISTICAL METHODS
syllabus_overview: Building on the understanding of applied statistical methods developed in first year statistics subjects, STA2ASM provides an understanding of these methods at an intermediate level. The subject places a special emphasis on applications of statistics to biological and medical problems. There are specific questions in the assignments, project, test and examination that reflect such an emphasis. This subject does not require a knowledge of calculus. An introduction to the open source statistical computing package R is included.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate statistical and probabilistic methods for data analysis.
Assess the effectiveness of statistical methods using simulation.
Discuss the importance of "thinking ahead" when planning and designing experiments.
Formulate hypothesis testing related to biological and medical problems; draw and explain the conclusions that follow from a rigorous and systematic analysis.
Explain the codes of conduct that govern professional competence and integrity in the field of statistics.
Execute statistical software functionality for data analysis and interpret the output accurately and meaningfully.

title: BIOSTATISTICS
syllabus_overview: Students will learn to design and analyse experiments in the life sciences and agriculture. The topics covered in this subject include a brief review of non-parametric methods; randomisation, blocking and randomised block designs; one-way and two-way layouts; multiple comparison procedures; fixed and random effects; mixed models; multiple linear regression; analysis of covariance; factorial designs; fractional factorial designs; and an introduction to cluster analysis. This subject makes use of the freely available software package R.
learning_outcomes: Formulate appropriate hypotheses and experimental designs.
Utilise randomization and blocking appropriately in the design of statistical experiments.
Present clear, well structured and rigorous proofs of important fundamental linear model results. This includes appropriate use of statistical and mathematical vocabulary and notation.
Construct statistical experiments using factorial and fractional factorial designs with an emphasis on the construction of simple estimators of effects associated with two-level factors.

title: APPLIED STATISTICS
syllabus_overview: The purpose of STA3AS is to equip graduates with an in depth understanding of modern statistical methods in the following three key topics: 1. Sample surveys with an emphasis on simple random sampling and stratified random sampling. 2. Multivariate analysis with an emphasis on inference for the multivariate mean, checking for underlying multivariate normality, principal component analysis and discriminant analysis. This topic includes an introduction/review of common linear algebra results. 3. Time series analysis with an introduction into the theoretical foundation of Box-Jenkins univariate time series models which form a basis for empirical work with time series data. The software package used in this subject is R.
learning_outcomes: Describe and use key sample survey, multivariate analysis and Box-Jenkins univariate time series analysis tools including a justification of appropriate usage based on known model/data conditions
Appropriately apply methods of model checking in the context of multivariate analysis.

Present clear written communications of statistical results in a manner which can be understood by a scientist who fully understands the variables in the associated data set, but who has only a basic understanding of statistics.

Present clear, well structured proofs of important fundamental results in sample surveys, multivariate analysis and Box-Jenkins univariate time series analysis. This includes clear and concise use of statistical and mathematical vocabulary and notation.

title: ANALYSES OF LINEAR MODELS
syllabus_overview: Modern research often involves the analysis of data for more than one variable and in this regard, linear models are the most widely used class of models. Linear models relate a response variable to one or more explanatory variables enabling researchers to answer important research questions and make predictions about how variables will respond. These methods are used in many areas including biological science, economics, engineering, medical science and psychological science. Topics covered in this subject include simple and multiple linear regression, response and explanatory variable transformations, ANOVA and ANCOVA, as well as more modern methodologies such as generalized linear models and linear mixed effects models. This subject has a strong emphasis on preparing students for future careers in statistics.
learning_outcomes: Present written and oral communications of statistical results clearly in a manner that can be understood by experts and lay audience.
Implement and document various strategies to identify and account for model inadequacies.
Present clear, well-structured proofs of important fundamental linear model results that include appropriate use of statistical and mathematical vocabulary and notation.
Work efficiently and effectively as a member of a team to produce a statistical analysis based on real data.
Describe and use key analytical linear modelling tools including justification of appropriate usage based on known model/data conditions.

title: STATISTICS THESIS A
syllabus_overview: Students commence a project that takes the equivalent of six months of continuous work under the supervision of a staff member. STA4001 will include elements of research training as directed by the supervisor. The project is completed and written up as a thesis when the student completes the subject STA4002. All students are required to present a 10-minute talk outlining the proposed project at a time determined by the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences Honours Coordinator. A list of prospective topics and supervisors is available from the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate autonomy, well-developed judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a researcher.
Analyse, generate and transmit solutions to, or an exposition of, complex problems relevant to the topic.
Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of the research to others.
Demonstrate advanced theoretical and technical knowledge of the topic of the thesis.
Select and apply research methods to critically analyse, evaluate and interpret literature relevant to the topic.

title: STATISTICS THESIS B
syllabus_overview: Students complete the project commenced in STA4001, writing up the results as a thesis. STA4002 will include elements of research training as directed by the supervisor. All students are required to present a 20-minute talk on their project after the thesis has been submitted. A list of prospective topics and supervisors is available from the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences.
learning_outcomes: Select and apply research methods to critically analyse, evaluate and interpret literature relevant to the topic.
Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of the research to others.
Analyse, generate and transmit solutions to, or an exposition of, complex problems relevant to the topic.
Demonstrate advanced theoretical and technical knowledge of the topic of the thesis.
Demonstrate autonomy, well-developed judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a researcher.

title: ADVANCED TOPICS IN STATISTICS B
syllabus_overview: This subject enables 4th year mathematics and statistics students to enroll in externally offered subjects (including AMSI subjects). Enrolment into this subject must be approved by the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences Honours Coordinator.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate autonomy, well-developed judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a statistician.
Use advanced cognitive and technical skills to analyse, generate and transmit solutions to complex problems relevant to the topic.
Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of statistics to others.
Demonstrate advanced theoretical and technical knowledge in a specified statistics topic.
Use advanced cognitive and technical skills to analyse, generate and transmit solutions to complex problems relevant to the topic.

title: ADVANCED TOPICS IN STATISTICS A
syllabus_overview: This subject enables 4th year mathematics and statistics students to enroll in externally offered subjects (including AMSI subjects). Enrolment into this subject must be approved by the Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences Honours Coordinator.
learning_outcomes: Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of statistics to others.
Demonstrate autonomy, well-developed judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a statistician.
Use advanced cognitive and technical skills to select and apply methods to critically analyse, evaluate and interpret tasks relevant to the topic.
Demonstrate advanced theoretical and technical knowledge in a specified statistics topic.
Use advanced cognitive and technical skills to analyse, generate and transmit solutions to complex problems relevant to the topic.

title: MASTER STATISTICS THESIS A
syllabus_overview: The Statistical Science thesis is a minor thesis written during the second master year. In this thesis, you will work on statistical research problems. You will carry out studies in statistics leading to new theoretical results or novel analysis of real-life data. The code for this thesis is split into two parts: STA5002 (which is taken in the first semester of this second year) and STA5THB (which is taken in the second semester of this second year). STA5002 and STA5THB are allocated 30 credit points each, resulting in a total of 60 credit points for the thesis. The same combined grade is given for STA5002 and STA5THB when STA5THB is completed.
learning_outcomes: Use advanced communication skills to present theoretical work and practical data analysis results via an oral presentation and academic writing.
Demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, and adaptability as a researcher.
Apply established theories and research methods to a body of knowledge relevant to the topic of the thesis.
Critically analyse, reflect on and synthesise published scientific work, complex information, and concepts relevant to the topic
Develop and communicate expertise in the theoretical and technical knowledge underlying the thesis topic.

title: SPATIAL ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces you to spatial data analysis. It surveys the theory of spatial random processes, spatial statistics models, and their applications to a wide range of areas, including image analysis and GIS (geographic information system). The subject will cover the methodology and modern developments for spatial-temporal modelling, estimation and prediction, spectral analysis of spatial processes and working with big spatial data. All the methods presented will be introduced and illustrated in the context of specific datasets using statistical software. You will get experience with analysis of real-world data.
learning_outcomes: Present clear, well structured analysis of important statistical model results.
Formulate purposeful questions to explore new statistical ideas and subsequently design valid statistical experiments.
Creatively find solutions to real world problems consistent with those commonly faced by practicing statisticians.
Professionally defend or question the validity of existing statistical analyses and associated evidence-based conclusions that are derived via application of sound spatial statistical methodology.

title: META ANALYSIS
syllabus_overview: The literature abounds with findings that collectively may offer important new insights for the betterment of the medical, psychological and life sciences, to name just a few. This subject is designed to provide students with the ability to combine estimated measures of evidence, known as effects, from comparable studies to increase power. Estimators are introduced which are commonly found in meta-analytic research and pitfalls are discussed. On completion of the subject, the student will have an understanding of the different effects that can be collected from the literature as well as an appreciation of how effect sizes arising from data measured on different scales can be combined. Importantly, this subject also shows students how meta-regression can be used to account for study-specific covariates that cannot be adequately accounted for using random-effects models. The freely available software packages R and RevMan are used throughout the subject.
learning_outcomes: Describe summary output from meta-analyses in a manner which can be understood by scientists with weak statistical backgrounds, but with knowledge from the discipline for which the research question is of interest.
Demonstrate an expert understanding of the use of statistical software packages by carrying out valid analyses of real meta-data and providing clear interpretations of all computer output.

Present clear, well-structured arguments that validate the combination of effect sizes from several studies that may differ in several aspects, including with respect to moderators and data measurement scales.
Critique and summarise published meta-analyses, clearly highlighting weaknesses and flaws that undermine the key findings.

title: ANALYSIS OF REPEATED MEASURES
syllabus_overview: Repeated measures data is used commonly in many disciplines including health, psychology, economics and biology. This subject provides students with the knowledge of how to perform the appropriate statistical analysis in a repeated measures data environment by using models such as the linear mixed model, correlated random effects model and marginal model. Students will learn how to examine research questions by applying these models using the R statistical package.
learning_outcomes: Use advanced written communication skills to disseminate findings from analyses of repeated measures data at a level commensurate with what is appropriate in the scientific literature for a range of disciplines.
Use advanced written communication skills to critique published analyses of repeated measures data and to justify findings that result from applying a variety of methods.
Demonstrate an understanding of complex repeated measures regression models by expressing a research question in the form of a regression model.
Use specialised computer software to critically analyse, reflect on and summarise complex information, problems and concepts for repeated measures data.

title: MODELS FOR BIOINFORMATICS
syllabus_overview: Advances in ‘omics’ technologies have led to an exponential increase in the volume of biological data created over the last decade. Statistical models play important roles in making sense of and drawing conclusions from complex and often noisy ‘omics’ data. This subject will introduce students to statistical issues relating to the analysis of ‘omics’ data, and will cover potential solutions to problems commonly encountered at the various stages of omics data analyses, from data acquisition, alignment, quality control and analysis through to visualization and interpretation. Topics covered include an introduction to microarray and next-generation-sequencing technologies; batch effects and other unwanted variations; multiple hypothesis testing problems; statistical tests and models for high-dimensional data; data visualization; and biological database utilization via pathway-based analyses. Students will also develop an intermediate skill level with the R programming language, and gain experience writing customized scripts and functions. R and Bioconductor packages will be used for all lab sessions, in conjunction with other freely-available bioinformatics software.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialised theoretical and technical skills in solving statistical issues in bioinformatics
Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of the role of statistics in bioinformatics to others
Demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as an applied statistician

Use specialised cognitive and technical skills to critically analyse, reflect on and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories relevant to solving statistical issues in bioinformatics
Apply established theories relevant to statistical issues in bioinformatics

title: MASTERS STATISTICS THESIS B
syllabus_overview: The Master of Statistical Science thesis is a minor thesis written during the second year of the Master of Data Science. In this thesis, the student demonstrates at least one of the following: (a) an understanding of a statistical research problem, (b) the numerical solution of a statistical research problem, (c) carries out research in statistics leading to new results or (d) gains experience in analysing real-life data. The code for this thesis is split into two parts: STA5002 (which is taken in the first semester of this second year) and STA5THB (which is taken in the second semester of this second year). STA5002 is allocated 30 credit points and STA5THB is allocated 30 credit points, resulting in a total of 60 credit points for the thesis. The same combined grade is given for STA5002 and STA5THB when STA5THB is completed.
learning_outcomes: Use advanced communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas of statistics to others.
Demonstrate specialised theoretical and technical knowledge of the topic of the thesis.
Apply established theories and research methods to a body of knowledge relevant to the topic of the thesis.
Use specialised cognitive and technical skills to critically analyse, reflect on and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories relevant to the topic.
Demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a researcher.

title: MAKING SENSE OF DATA
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to modern data analytics, visualisation, and statistics. It equips students with the skills required to take advantage of powerful computing for the analysis and visualisation of complex data. These skills are used to solve problems in areas such as the biological sciences, medical sciences, agricultural sciences, nutrition, health sciences, education, and business. Students will become familiar with data visualisation and computing, descriptive statistics, statistical modelling, and data-based decision making. Using statistical computing packages is an integral part of this subject. This subject allows further study in second-year subjects in statistics and data science.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply appropriate statistical inference methods for decision making.
Calculate probabilities and other quantities from discrete and continuous probability distributions.
Convert data into useful information by using appropriate numerical and graphical summaries.
Apply data visualisation skills and/or statistical knowledge in a chosen applied field of study.
Compute, display, and interpret numerical and graphical summaries, probabilities and various statistical inference procedures using one or more statistical software package(s).

title: ENGINEERING PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS
syllabus_overview: This subject develops an understanding of probability and statistics applied to engineering problems. Probability topics include joint and conditional probability, Bayes' Theorem and distributions such as the uniform, binomial, Poisson and normal distributions as well as properties of random variables and the Central Limit Theorem. Statistical inference and data analysis is also considered covering, among other topics, significance testing and confidence intervals with an introduction to methods such as ANOVA, linear and nonlinear regression and model verification. Applications to engineering such as queuing theory, reliability and efficiency of processes are considered throughout. Students will work to achieve the stage one competencies 1.2 (conceptual understanding of the underpinning mathematics, numerical analysis and statistics), 2.2 (fluent application of engineering techniques, tools and resources) and 3.2 (effective written communication).
learning_outcomes: Defend or question the validity of probability models applied to problems including, but not limited to, system and structural reliability, queuing theory and signal processing.
Present clear, well-structured summaries of findings, both probabilistic and data-based, using appropriate mathematical and statistical vocabulary.
Demonstrate an ability to solve a variety of engineering problems using applications of probability models.
Identify probabilistic traits of engineering problems and choose methods which can be employed to determine valid and informative solutions.
Define a statistical hypothesis with applications to engineering that may be tested using data.

Identify and apply statistical methods for hypothesis testing and estimation with applications in engineering that include, but are not limited to, quality control, reliability and efficiency of processing.

title: STATISTICAL COMPUTING
syllabus_overview: Statistical Computing provides an introduction to methods of computational statistics. It is strongly focused on modern statistical approaches and computational methods and extensively uses R and Python software. All methods are introduced and demonstrated using real world data examples. The topics covered in this subject include optimization, Bayesian methods, MCMC, bootstrap, density estimation and tree-based models. In this subject, you will develop practical skills for data analysis in science, industry and business applications.
learning_outcomes: Execute statistical software functionality for data analysis and appropriately interpret the output.
Apply appropriate computational statistical methods for data analysis.
Analyse properties of statistical models using computational methods.
Explain the underlying principles of computational statistical methods using appropriate vocabulary and notation.

title: PROBABILITY MODELS
syllabus_overview: The analysis of scientific, engineering, and economic data makes extensive use of probability models. In this subject, you will learn the most basic of these models and their properties. More specifically, you will learn a wide range of discrete and continuous univariate distributions; joint distributions; conditional expectation; mean and variance of linear combinations of random variables; Chebyshev's inequality; moment generating functions; the law of large numbers; the Central Limit Theorem. Students with little or no previous knowledge of calculus will also learn relevant mathematical topics to support the other content.
learning_outcomes: Solve problems when randomness is involved
Demonstrate mathematical calculations to investigate numerical properties of probability models
Demonstrate understanding by solving probability problems using both words and precise mathematical symbols.
Derive some basic probability results in selected areas of application
Test the validity of different probability models

title: COMPUTATION AND SIMULATION
syllabus_overview: In mathematics, one uses algebra and calculus to find 'exact' solutions to mathematical problems. In statistics, engineering, physics, and applied mathematics, when dealing with 'the real world', one encounters situations where the best one can do is to find an approximate solution to a problem. This is where computation and simulation plays a vital role. As well as appreciating the numerical methods for obtaining approximate solutions in their own right, understanding concepts such as accuracy and computational efficiency are important. Naturally, computing and simulation are carried out using software programs such as Excel spreadsheets and the technical computing languages MATLAB, Maple or R; in this subject students will gain experience using these. The specific topics studied are: nonlinear equations, interpolation, smoothing and optimization, numerical integration, pseudorandom numbers and simulation.
learning_outcomes: Determine accuracy characteristics of numerical algorithms
Use appropriate mathematical language to write solutions to problems
Interpret and write explanations of the solutions to computational problems in appropriate language and write explanations of associated mathematical and statistical concepts.
Apply appropriate computational methods using calculator and computer to solve mathematical and statistical problems that do not have analytic solutions

title: DATA SCIENCE PROJECTS
syllabus_overview: In this capstone subject, you will work in teams to investigate and solve two problems based on a real-world application of data science. In the first project, you will design an optimisation tool and develop it as a web application in the R Shiny environment. The second project requires the team to develop a neural network model developed in the R programming environment using a training data set. This subject addresses the Innovation and Entrepreneurship La Trobe Essential, and requires you to think creatively, work in a team and present your ideas and results clearly and effectively.
learning_outcomes: Implement appropriate testing strategies to ensure robustness of the developed tools and models.
Construct a model that can be used to predict outcomes with high accuracy for unclassified data.
Explain use of the developed tools and models verbally and in writing, to a general audience.
Work effectively and efficiently as a member of a team to deliver solutions to real-world problems.
Design and develop an online, user-friendly tool that produces solutions for constrained optimisation problems.

title: STATISTICAL INFERENCE
syllabus_overview: Statistical inference is used to describe procedures that draw conclusions from datasets arising from systems affected by random variation. This subject comprises components in estimation and testing hypotheses. Topics in the first component include method of moments and maximum likelihood, reduction by sufficiency and invariance, unbiasedness, consistency, and efficiency. The second component examines size and power of tests, Neyman-Pearson lemma, optimality of tests, the likelihood ratio test and relationship to confidence interval estimation.
learning_outcomes: Compute/derive mathematical calculations to investigate numerical properties of statistical models
Model and solve problems when randomness is involved
Present clear, well structured explanations of numerical results. This includes appropriate use of statistical and mathematical vocabulary
Present clear, well structured proofs of important theoretical statistical model results.

title: LINEAR PROGRAMMING AND PROBABILITY
syllabus_overview: Linear Programming and Probability is a subject with many important real word applications. It is suitable for students taking majors in mathematics, statistics, physics or engineering. Linear Programming involves maximising and minimising a linear function subject to a finite number of linear constraints. This subject also gives an introduction to Game Theory, which deals with decision making in a competitive environment; game theory uses ideas from probability theory combined with the tools of linear programming. The subject also details how linear programming can also used to perform special probability computations, such a regression, and selection of probability distributions.
learning_outcomes: Employ the simplex method moving freely between a problem and its dual.
Solve simultaneous two-player zero sum games using linear programming.
Solve linear programming problems graphically.
Calculate regressions using the norm, geometrically and via linear programming.
Undertake sensitivity analysis on linear programming problems.

title: PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS FOR DATA SCIENCE
syllabus_overview: This subject develops an understanding of probability and statistics applied to Data Science. Probability topics include joint and conditional probability, Bayes' Theorem and distributions such as the uniform, binomial, Poisson and normal distributions as well as properties of random variables and the Central Limit Theorem. Statistical inference and data analysis is also considered covering, among other topics, significance testing and confidence intervals with an introduction to methods such as ANOVA, linear and nonlinear regression and model verification. Applications to data science are considered and students will be exposed to the R statistical package as well as the mathematical type-setting package LaTeX.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an ability to solve a variety of Data Science problems using applications of probability models.
Define a statistical hypothesis with applications to Data Science that may be tested using data.
Identify probabilistic traits of data science problems and choose methods which can be employed to determine valid and informative solutions.
Present clear, well-structured summaries of findings, both probabilistic and data-based, using appropriate mathematical and statistical vocabulary.
Identify and apply statistical methods for hypothesis testing and estimation with applications in Data Science.
Defend or question the validity of probability models applied to data science problems

title: INDUSTRY PLACEMENT
syllabus_overview: This subject has been developed to allow you to enhance your formal learning in a practical setting and develop your understanding of (Australian) workplace culture. You will undertake approximately 240 hours of placement (typically 20 hrs per week over 12 weeks) where you will work with an industry host in an appropriate workplace role. Approximately 96 additional hours will be needed for preparation and report writing.
learning_outcomes: Critically review and implement appropriate solution approaches to industry data analysis problems.
Compare and adapt university subject and course knowledge to industry requirements.
Clearly elucidate by generating context-appropriate reports and documents.

title: BEING A SOCIAL WORKER
syllabus_overview: In this first year subject, you will be provided with an overview of the theoretical framework that guides the La Trobe social work course. You will be introduced to the key aspects of how social work is understood, particularly what it means to be a social worker and how social work is expressed across its many domains of practice (from work with individuals to community work and advocacy) and fields of practice (such as child and family wellbeing, health and disability). You will explore the historical development of social work including contested ideas about how social work is practiced, as well as locating yourself in respect of your own values and beliefs; and how these fit with social work's ethical and values framework.
