You will explore the concept of social justice from a critical, First nations and green social work perspective. You will also be oriented to university study, specifically the development of research, writing and oral communication skills as well as working collaboratively with other students. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Identify LTU social work’s core theoretical framework and begin to engage with critical social work theory and how it applies across multiple social work practice domains.
Describe personal values and how these fit with the social work profession and identity as a social worker, including the concept of social justice.

Demonstrate a beginners understanding of the historical development of social work and the contested debates, such as the influence of colonisation, that have underpinned the discipline's development.
Demonstrate research, oral and written communication and teamwork skills required for first year social work study.
Identify how sociological and psychological perspectives relate to social work

title: SOCIAL WORK IN A POLITICAL CONTEXT
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will examine the notion that " social work is a political activity" through the exploration of political contexts in which social work practice takes place and the role of the profession in contributing to political and social change. You will explore Australia's system of government and consider the influence of legislation and public policy on contemporary Australian society, which provides important foundational knowledge for future subjects. The social welfare system will be examined as a key example of the political context, with implications for human service organisations, social workers, service users and the wider community. You will compare Australia's social welfare system with those operating in other countries and consider the influence of political ideologies on these differences and on broader trends in welfare policies. You will apply learning from the subject to a contemporary political issue and consider this issue from the perspective of social work values including a commitment to progressive social change, human rights and social justice.
learning_outcomes: Identify key features and functions of Australia's system of government.
Discuss information, ideas and concepts relating to the political, structural and environmental context of social work practice
Demonstrate research, oral and written communication and teamwork skills required for first year social work study.
Describe social work values and social justice perspectives to inform discussion of contemporary political issues and how these connect to social change.
Describe and compare Australia's system of social welfare and social policy to those in other countries.
Explain key differences between political ideologies and relational worldviews.

title: REFLECTIVE COMMUNICATION AND SOCIAL WORK
syllabus_overview: Social workers and educators aim to empower others and to help create the conditions for people to thrive. This involves working for a socially just and equitable society and also helping people to better manage the day to day challenges they inevitably confront in their lives. Yet we all experience challenges in life and there will be times we need to deal with problems that seem overwhelming and outside our control. SWP1REF takes as its premise that working to help other people involves first understanding ourselves and building self-awareness and personal skills to deal with our own life situations. In this subject you are introduced to the concept of empowerment and the role this plays in enabling health and wellbeing even in the most challenging and difficult situations. The subject draws from an evidence based Aboriginal Family Wellbeing empowerment program that has been integrated within a wide range of health human services across Australia and internationally. Students will experience the program as both a participant and a facilitator. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in creative collaboration and teamwork
Conceptualise and analyse the concepts of empowerment and wellbeing.
Utilise critical reflection to enhance communication in personal and professional spheres
Critically reflect on personal values, knowledge and skills.
Apply group work intervention informed by First Nation relational ways of knowing

title: INTRODUCTION TO DIVERSITY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore and analyse social work practice in a diverse society. Of particular consideration will be how a sense of 'otherness' or 'difference' is created and maintained. Three broad arenas of 'difference' will be featured from amongst the many forms of social and cultural diversity. These arenas are not exclusive but will in this instance be: sexuality, disability, migration and population movements. As social workers are expected to practice within a framework of social and cultural difference, the aim is to introduce and promote values and skills for 'difference-competent' practice.
learning_outcomes: Explain how social structures, worldviews, international and national development and policy responses impact on the experiences of individuals and groups in terms of marginalization and othering.
Compare and contrast social work theories and practice when working with individuals and families, in organizations and communities in terms of working with difference
Identify how personal experiences influence understanding of what 'difference'; means and how it may contribute to creating a sense of 'difference' or 'otherness'
Describe possible strategies for engaging in culturally competent practice with diverse populations.

title: INTEGRATING PRACTICE AND THEORY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will consolidate your learning of the social work course to date and begin to construct a social work identity. You will reflect on how you understand the challenges people experience within social contexts. You will examine the breadth of social work values, roles and fields of practice to demonstrate how you would address these, given challenges using individual, group, community and policy responses. You will learn how to develop assessments and intervention goals. Further development of skills in reflection, collaboration and research, will be undertaken.
learning_outcomes: Examine different perspectives on social issues through the breakdown of formal knowledge and discourses.
Apply critical social work approaches to address individual, community and policy levels of practice
Articulate both verbally and in writing emerging approaches to social work practice
Explain social work as a values based profession, located in a range of fields, comprising various domains and roles

title: LAW HUMAN RIGHTS AND ETHICS
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be supported to expand your knowledge base of the legal context of Australian social work practice and how human rights and ethical principles guide social work practice. You will have an opportunity to observe and analyse real court/tribunal processes. You will engage with ethical decision-making models and apply these to diverse case studies that illustrate how Australian human rights obligations and social work's commitment to human rights and social justice impact on policy, law and practice in Australia. Case studies and subject resources will be based on contemporary issues relevant to our culturally and linguistically diverse society, including First Nation Australians' worldviews
learning_outcomes: Explain the importance of human rights to Australia's health, welfare and disability service systems.
Explain the impacts of law on social work practice and the role and responsibilities of social work practitioners, using a critical theory lens.
Discuss social work ethics and values and how they relate to ethical decision-making.
Interpret and explain the intersection of law, ethics and human rights for social workers and their practice.

title: SOCIAL WORK IN AN UNEQUAL WORLD
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will explore the issue of inequality in Australia and other parts of the world and its associated impacts. You will explore poverty as a key form of material inequality, and one which significantly impacts on people's wellbeing and opportunities. You will examine various sources of knowledge (including concepts, theories and evidence) relating to inequality and poverty, and consider how the contested nature of such knowledge reflects different sources of information, values, beliefs and ideologies. You will also appraise the role of government policies and global institutions in addressing the issues, particularly those delivered through social welfare systems and international development efforts. How social work values and principles such as human rights, social justice, and respect for persons can be applied to issues of inequality and poverty both in Australia and in international contexts will also be explored
learning_outcomes: Undertake team work demonstrating capacity for effective collaboration
Interpret critical theoretical perspectives and knowledge relating to inequality and poverty at national and global levels
Appraise the role of government policies and global institutions in tackling issues of inequality and poverty
Apply social work values and ethical principles to explain inequality and poverty within national and global contexts
Apply knowledge relating to inequality and poverty to a population group, country or region

title: SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will undertake an exploration of social work research, practice methods - from developing questions to sampling and data analysis. Research design and methodological critique are central, including both quantitative and qualitative methods, as well as understanding the philosophical and sociological bases informing these methods.
learning_outcomes: Identify and appraise quantitative and qualitative research relevant to social work practice
Articulate key research approaches and methods, and their advantages and limitations.
Evaluate the role of research in social work practice.
Demonstrate research, oral and written communication and teamwork skills.
Analyse and assess the application of social work values and ethics in research.

title: TRAUMA, RESILIENCE & DEVELOPMENT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be introduced to the concepts of trauma, attachment, and resilience and will learn how these impact on human development across the life course. Using a critical social work lens, you will discuss and explore the impacts of risk and protective factors, life transitions, adverse events, strengths and self-efficacy on human development. You will consider these issues from a variety of theoretical and cultural perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical frameworks for understanding the lived experience of people to the stages of human development across the lifespan, recognising the cultural and environmental influences on human development.
Apply a critical social work perspective, including the tensions between social care, social control, and social change to trauma-informed practice.

Apply knowledge of the concepts of trauma, loss and grief, attachment, and resilience to describe their impact on the life course of individuals, families and communities with particular reference to age, class and gender.
Apply relational theories relevant to First Nations people and other cultural groups to define family, attachment, healing, self-agency, resilience and relatedness.

title: THEORIES FOR SOCIAL WORK
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will further explore La Trobe University Social Work's core theoretical framework of critical social theory and how it informs social work practice. You will also be introduced to a range of other theories used by social workers to situate their experiences and the experiences of those they work with in a particular social context and physical environment. You will be taught to develop a beginning capacity to understand and engage with different ideas about the world and how it is perceived, how to understand social issues and human behaviour and how to engage with these in practice. More specifically you will explore various discourses (beliefs about the world and related values), explanatory theories (which seek to explain social issues and experience of them) and practice theories and approaches (how explanatory theories are expressed in practice).
learning_outcomes: Illustrate how theories can reinforce each other (e.g. ecofeminism or provide useful contrasts (e.g. psychodynamic compared to strengths).
Explain and discuss key discourses, explanatory theories and practice theories and approaches in social work
Review range of social work practice theories
Distinguish critical theory in social work and the difference between discourses, explanatory theories, practice theories and practice approaches.

title: FIELDS OF PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the theory and knowledge base of two fields of social work practice, child & family welfare and family violence. Your introduction to social work practice in these fields will recognise the importance of respect for and enabling human rights, and taking a person centred approach. You will be introduced to the key debates, policies, programs, service delivery and skills required to undertake beginning level practice in both fields.
learning_outcomes: Critique the success of policy developments in child protection and family violence and the drivers that have led to policy shifts.
Analyse and evaluate the construction of child protection and family violence as social problems to apply practice frameworks and interventions.
Synthesise and apply research outcomes and relevant psychosocial knowledge and skills to case management
Analyse the conceptualisation of child protection and family violence practice over time including the values that underpin these conceptualisations.

title: SOCIAL WORK SKILLS FOR PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: You are expected to play an active role in group-based learning and participate in exercises to develop social work skills: A client here may be an individual, family, group, colleague or community member. Fundamental to this subject is the development of a critical awareness of self, including your style as a worker and the impact of this style on others. The key aspects of this subject are group work, with a focus on individuals roles within the group; and casework practice, with an emphasis on exploring your styles in the application of world views and theories to interviewing skills including assessment, intervention plans and case recording. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at tutorials in this subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker.
learning_outcomes: Formulate clear and effective social work interviews, to develop intervention plans and appropriate documentation.
Apply, with judgment, a critical social work lens to practice and apply other theories to practice when using these skills with individuals, families, groups or communities.
Analyse theoretical concepts and social work practice skills to distinguish effective group work including group facilitation.
Reflect on a First Nations perspective on ways of knowing, being and doing.
Appraise personal ideas and values in relation to theory to improve client outcomes.

title: INCLUSION IN COMMUNITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will focus upon critically reflective social work practice at community and societal levels and explore the conceptual and theoretical underpinnings of community development including principles such as participation, human rights and empowerment. This broad focus will cover social, economic and environmental justice and political and cultural awareness and how these impact on individual and community development. The emphasis for creating social change is grounded in understanding the impact of ideologies and on strategic interventions, incorporating a strengths perspective, community organisation, social action, social policy and planning approaches. You will examine and develop skills in community development as a framework for engaging people, communities, and organisations in promoting community building and social well-being.
learning_outcomes: Appraise community development approaches including contextually appropriate strategies and techniques.
Compare and analyse communities using a critical theory perspective and First Nations worldviews to understand and assess their relevant contexts.
Distinguish and examine the key roles and skills necessary to engage in effective community development processes and initiatives in a variety of contexts
Critically review personal values, knowledge and skills and how these impact on working with communities and related groups

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with experiential learning opportunities to further integrate theory with practice, to demonstrate appropriate professional relationships, and gain working knowledge of organisational contexts. Through this professionally supervised practice experience you will be provided with constructive feedback on your performance and will be challenged to critically self-reflect on your effectiveness. You will have opportunities to further develop skills in basic interviewing, assessment and intervention processes required for practice along with skills in research. Professional competencies will be developed across nine key learning areas and will be assessed against the standard of competency at a beginning level with support. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at workshops and professional placements in this subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Examine the impact of complex organizational contexts on practice.
Critically review professional knowledge, values and skills to employ as a responsible and adaptable practitioner.
Combine social work knowledge, values and skills to solve a range of complex social work problems
Appraise professional knowledge and skills in the context of the Australian Association of Social Workers Practice Standards with accountability as a practitioner.

title: UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXT
syllabus_overview: In this subject students explore the impact of organisational contexts on social work practice. Students analyse the structure, purpose and dynamics of 21st century human service organisations and build an understanding of the role organisations play in implementing social policies and delivering services. Students examine governance and decision making and the role of organisational culture in shaping the experience of service users. Students are introduced to the changing organisational context in which social workers are employed, how they operate effectively in teams and alongside other professionals. Strategies such as the use of professional supervision and critical reflection are considered in light of the common challenges and tensions that occur between professional expectations, social policy imperatives and organisational pragmatics.
learning_outcomes: Develop strategies to address the challenges and tensions between social policy, organisational imperatives and professional social work identity.
Analyse and reflect on the impact of different organisational contexts (e.g. statutory, advocacy, community, clinical on social work practice.
Synthesise knowledge of organisational theories and key features of organisations to collaboratively analyse specific human service organisations and social work roles within them
Reflect on how organisational policies, ideologies, structure and culture impact upon service access and the service user's experience of service delivery.

title: FIELDS OF PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will have the opportunity to develop your knowledge and skills base in a specialty field of social work practice. There will be four streams in this subject, which is offered online. This subject builds on prior knowledge and experiences gained throughout the course and is designed to enable you to enrich and add breadth and depth to your understanding of the chosen field of practice. You will have the opportunity to further develop your appreciation of the importance of respect for, and enabling of, human rights and taking a person-centred approach. You will be introduced to the key debates, policies, programs, service delivery and skills required to undertake beginning level practice in the chosen specialty area/field of practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify and analyse key policy developments in the specialty area and become familiar with the drivers that have led to these policy shifts
Apply social work research evidence to contemporary social work discourse related to the specialty area
Critically review the various ways in which knowledge and practice in this specialty area has evolved.
Critically review personal and professional values and ethics, psychosocial knowledge and skills, and their relation to social work practice in the specialty area
Apply social work theoretical and practice frameworks to contemporary practice in the specialty area

title: SOCIAL WORK WITH INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES & GROUPS: APPLICATIONS A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will develop appropriate levels of skill development to apply theoretical frameworks that inform practice with individuals, families and groups. You will be engaged with enquiries to clarify: the nature of direct social work practice, how social workers go about their practice in different fields, how to identify and organise case data, and the use of formal casework theory to prepare an assessment and, in conjunction with SWP4APB, how to prepare a basic intervention plan.
learning_outcomes: Communicate complexity of knowledge re how organisational, legal, protective, and ethical considerations influence direct social work practice, including how social work practice may be named differently in different contexts.
Consolidate and synthesise knowledge in preparing a plan for a specific social work service occasion

Analyse and compare the basic theoretical concepts underpinning direct social work practice including discourses such as Western and First Nations worldviews and green social work; explanatory theories such as critical theory, psychodynamic and systems; practice theories such using a strengths focus or task focus.
Identify, plan and suggest implementation of case data for a given social work case
Synthesise knowledge of the essential elements of a given presenting situation and comprehensively connect to current practice knowledge and theory

title: SOCIAL WORK WITH INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES & GROUPS: APPLICATIONS B
syllabus_overview: In this subject, the focus is on developing appropriate levels of interpersonal helping skills which relate to theoretical material covered in SWP4APA. You are expected to play an active role in group-based learning and develop an awareness of group dynamics and group process. To facilitate interpersonal helping skill development, you will participate in role play exercises. These exercises help you learn to: (i) establish the context of practice, (ii) develop an effective working alliance, (iii) identify the client's perspective, (iv) develop a sense of the client's strengths and issues, and (v) set a direction for future work. Central to the subject is the development of critical awareness of self, including your style as a worker.
learning_outcomes: Consolidate and synthesise knowledge of how social work practice is contextualised in an agency setting and be able to communicate this knowledge to a variety of audiences.
Critically reflect upon your own practice including how you have applied basic theoretical concepts to your practice.
Analyse, articulate, apply and reflect upon basic theoretical concepts about group processes to a variety of group situations from a social work perspective.
Plan and implement a basic interview or occasion of service with individuals, families and groups.

title: FIELDS OF SOCIAL WORK PRACTICE A
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to the theory and knowledge base of two fields of social work practice, child & family welfare, and family violence. Your introduction to social work practice in these fields will recognise the importance of respect for and enabling human rights and taking a person-centred approach. You will be introduced to the key debates, policies, programs, service delivery and skills required to undertake beginning level practice in both fields.
learning_outcomes: Synthesize and apply research outcomes and relevant psycho-social knowledge and skills to case management
Analyse the conceptualisation of child protection and family violence practice over time including the values that underpin these conceptualisations.
Analyse and evaluate the construction of child protection and family violence as social problems to apply practice frameworks and interventions
Critique the success of policy developments in child protection and family violence and the drivers that have led to policy shifts.

title: SOCIAL WORK SKILLS C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on the knowledge and skills acquired in previous subjects and in your first field placement. In this final year of study, you will focus on extending your ability to integrate a critical theory perspective as well as other key theoretical approaches to social work practice at a deeper level. On completion, you will have been provided with the opportunity to work more confidently with individuals and families experiencing complex problems. You will further analyse practice using critically reflective processes, knowledge and skills. You will actively engage in seminar groups including role plays and will be expected to play an active part in group development and maintenance. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at workshops in this subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply social work knowledge and skills to demonstrate well-developed judgement, knowledge adaptability and responsibility as a social worker
Integrate and apply social work theory and knowledge when undertaking an assessment, intervention, interview or occasion of service in complex social work practice situations.

Critically analyse and describe personal knowledge, skills, beliefs and values as they relate to one's own future social work practice and determine areas for further development in direct social work practice with individuals and families.

title: LAW, HUMAN RIGHTS,  AND ETHICS IN SOCIAL WORK PRACTICE
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will expand your knowledge base in the legal context of Australian social work practice and how human rights and ethical principles guide social work practice. Professional competency will be developed by applying ethical decision-making models to case studies by observing real courts or tribunals. Case studies will address issues of diversity and complexity in our society and guidance will be given on how to make decisions that conform to ethical, legal and professional requirements while respecting clients and their rights.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate case materials by the application of an ethical decision-making framework.
Critically analyse conflicts between competing legal, ethical and human rights principles and their impact on social workers and their practice.
Analyse the impact of the law on social work practice and the role and responsibilities of social work practitioners using a conceptual framework.
Critically analyse how human rights are addressed in social work practice.

title: PROJECT DESIGN AND EVALUATION IN SOCIAL WORK
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with a theoretical and practical understanding of the role and application of program design in social work practice as an organised response to social issues. This knowledge will be contextualised in the contemporary human service environment and will examine program design and outcome evaluation in organisations. You will use these skills to begin to explore your interests in a particular Honours Industry Project with a focus on project and program design.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate capacity to design a logic model that utilises a theory of change to anticipate outcomes
Critically apply an evidence-informed approach to program and project design and outcome evaluation
Critically analyse relevant theoretical and research literature to construct problem analyses and theory of change in relation to identified social issues.
Appraise the impact of social and political context on organisations and influences on program and project designs.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with experiential learning opportunities to further integrate theory with practice, to demonstrate appropriate professional relationships, and gain working knowledge of organisational contexts. Through this professionally supervised practice experience you will be provided with constructive feedback on your performance and will be challenged to critically self-reflect on your effectiveness. You will have opportunities to further develop skills in basic interviewing, assessment and intervention processes required for practice along with skills in research. Professional competencies will be developed across nine key learning areas and will be assessed against the standard of competency at a beginning level of professional practice. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at workshops and professional placements in this subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional knowledge and skills as prescribed by Australian Association of Social Workers Practice Standards with autonomy and judgement.
Critically appraise the impact of complex organisational contexts on practice.
Integrate social work knowledge, values and skills to solve a range of complex social work problems
Practice adaptably and responsibly by critically evaluating professional knowledge, values and skills

title: SOCIAL WORK INDUSTRY PROJECT
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will develop project development skills for direct application in social work practice. You will finalise your project design in an agency allocated by the University, implement this in the agency, write up the project and submit a report to the agency for assessment. You will critically analyse how to act as an agent of social change in generating project activity that contributes to social work knowledge and development. You will also consider relevant leadership theories that contribute to your understanding of being an agent of change. You will be assisted to review the role of social work and social workers in promoting effective social work practice, social policies and social change in national and international communities.
learning_outcomes: Formulate project questions and proposals
Apply project planning skills in project development, design and implementation
Critically reflect on personal approaches to leadership/being an agent of change in social work and the impact on personal social work identity.
Clearly and coherently communicate project outcomes to a variety of audiences.
Reflect on implementation of projects and critically evaluate their effectiveness.

title: SOCIAL POLICY & ADVOCACY
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will further explore the knowledge and skills learnt in previous years, required to make an informed and active contribution to social policy development and advocacy. Active engagement in policy processes and advocacy is a core requirement of all social workers, and you will be taught to develop competence, confidence and commitment to this domain of practice. Your theoretical knowledge of political institutions and processes of policy making, political ideology, social welfare history, policy analysis, and policy advocacy will be explored. You will be taught practical skills relevant to policy analysis, advocacy and report writing. The knowledge and skills developed through the subject will be integrated with broader social work knowledge and values and First Nations principles to inform the critical analysis of contemporary social policy and the formulation of proposals for more appropriate and just policy responses.
learning_outcomes: Analyse contemporary social policy using policy analysis frameworks and social work values
Apply relevant knowledge to inform policy development and change
Critically review the historical, institutional, ideological and environmental contexts that shape Australian social policies
Integrate knowledge of policy and advocacy theory to formulate alternative policy responses and advocacy strategies.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE 1
syllabus_overview: In this subject, you will be provided with experiential learning opportunities to further integrate theory with practice, to demonstrate appropriate professional relationships, and gain working knowledge of organisational contexts. Through this professionally supervised practice experience you will be provided with constructive feedback on your performance and will be challenged to critically self-reflect on your effectiveness. You will have opportunities to further develop skills in basic interviewing, assessment and intervention processes required for practice along with skills in research. Professional competencies will be developed across key learning areas and will be assessed against the standard of competency at a beginning level with support. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at tutorials and professional placements in the subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Integrate social work knowledge, values and skills to solve a range of complex social work problems.
Critically evaluate professional knowledge, values and skills to demonstrate adaptability and responsibility as a developing social work practitioner.
Critically analyse and evaluate the impact of complex organisational contexts on practice.

Apply and appraise professional knowledge and skills in the context of the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS) Graduate Attributes (Australian Association of Social Works [AASW], 2024) with developing autonomy and expert judgement as a beginning social work practitioner.

title: PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE 2
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be provided with experiential learning opportunities to integrate theory with practice at an advanced level. You will be given the opportunity to demonstrate appropriate professional relationships and integrate knowledge of organisational contexts gained from your first field placement. Through this professionally supervised practice experience, you will be provided with constructive feedback on your performance and will be challenged to critically self-reflect on your practice. You will have opportunities to further develop skills in interviewing, assessment and intervention processes required for practice, along with skills in research. Professional competencies will be developed across key learning areas and will be assessed against the standard of competency at a beginning level of professional practice. Professional accreditation requires a minimum level of fieldwork practice. Your attendance at tutorials and professional placements in the subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Silver Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Apply and appraise professional knowledge and skills in the context of the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS) Graduate Attributes (Australian Association of Social Works [AASW], 2024) with developing autonomy and expert judgement as a beginning social work practitioner.
Integrate social work knowledge, values and skills to solve a range of complex social work problems.
Critically evaluate professional knowledge, values and skills to demonstrate adaptability and responsibility as a beginning social work practitioner.
Critically analyse and evaluate the impact of complex organisational contexts on practice.

title: EVIDENCE INFORMED PRACTICE IN CHILD AND FAMILY SERVICE DELIVERY
syllabus_overview: Contemporary Child and Family practice is informed by multiple sources of knowledge derived from lived experience, First Nations perspectives and other theory and research evidence. In this subject, you will explore the unique contributions that each of these makes to effective practice. You will learn to identify the empirical or theoretical underpinnings of practice with individuals and design of programs, and to judge the strength and weaknesses of these. The subject will focus on advances in evidence-based practice in the child and families sector, including child protection. You will also learn how to connect theories and evidence used in child and family practice to other fields of health and social care.
learning_outcomes: Synthesize information, concepts and theories surrounding areas of child and family practice, including lived experience and First Nations perspectives.
Interpret and transmit information about advances in evidence based/informed practice in child and family service delivery.
Critically evaluate the effectiveness and impact of types of interventions or programs in child and family practice.
Communicate research findings effectively and sensitively with service providers, clients, and the public.

title: SOCIAL WORK APPLICATIONS C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will build on knowledge and skills developed in SWP4APA, SWP4APB, and SWP5PPA, SWP5PPB, or SWP5001. Using beginning competency in direct practice, you will focus on extending understanding of key theoretical frameworks and integrating these with practice at a deeper level. On completion, you will have the capacity to work more extensively and confidently with individuals, families and groups at a graduate social worker level. Your attendance at tutorials in this subject will contribute to meeting this requirement for professional recognition as a social worker.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on your own practice in complex social work practice situations, to further develop your skills.
Integrate and apply theory and knowledge when undertaking an intervention in complex social work practice situations with individuals, families and groups.
Apply intervention theory and knowledge to develop an intervention plan, appropriate to direct social work practice with individuals, families and groups.
Critically reflect to evaluate professional knowledge, skills, beliefs and values as they relate to social work practice to improve client outcomes.

title: FIELD OF SOCIAL WORK PRACTICE B
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be introduced to a particular field of social work practice, which is defined in terms of population subgroups (e.g. people with a disability), life course tasks (e.g. parenting), social problems (e.g. child abuse), policy work,(e.g. income security) or types of intervention (e.g. mediation). You will be introduced to the psychosocial and research knowledge base of the social problem area, key debates, policies, program, service delivery and skills required to undertake beginning level practice. This subject builds on and integrates the core social work knowledge, skills and values that you have studied in earlier parts of the course.
learning_outcomes: Critique the success of policy developments in relation to social problems and the drivers that have led policy shifts.
Synthesise research and relevant psycho-social knowledge to interpret the lived experience of individuals, families and groups experiencing social problems.
Research social work practice skills applicable to recognised areas of social problems and the issues that arise in working with individuals, families, groups and communities in these areas.
Analyse the varying ways in which social problems have been conceptualised over time and the values that underpinned these conceptualizations

title: INCLUSION IN COMMUNITIES
syllabus_overview: In this subject the focus is on social work practice at community and societal levels. It covers conceptual and theoretical underpinnings of community development including principles, such as active citizenship, and participatory democracy from Western and First Nations worldviews . It has a broad focus in that it covers social, economic, political, cultural, environmental and personal development. The emphasis for creating socially just change is on strategic interventions, incorporating for example, a strengths perspective and community organising, social action, social policy and planning approaches. It will examine community development as a framework for engaging people, communities, and organisations in the change process and promoting community building and social well-being. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on personal values, knowledge and skills and their impact on community work practice.
Design and evaluate community development approaches and contextually appropriate strategies and techniques and communicate these effectively.
Conceptualise and analyse the nature of communities using relevant theoretical perspectives including Western and First Nations worldviews.

Apply expert judgement to identify the key roles and skills necessary to engage in effective community development processes and initiatives in a variety of contexts to maximise participation from multiple perspectives.

title: FIELDS OF SOCIAL WORK PRACTICE C
syllabus_overview: In this subject you are introduced to a particular field of social work practice, which is defined in terms of population subgroups (e.g. people with disabilities; older persons), life course tasks (e.g. parenting), social problems (e.g. child abuse), policy work, (such as income security) or types of intervention (e.g. mediation). You will be introduced to the psycho-social and research knowledge base of the social problem area, key debates, policies, program, service delivery and skills required to undertake beginning level practice. This subject builds on and integrates the core social work knowledge, skills and values that you have studied in earlier parts of the course.
learning_outcomes: Select and interpret specific practice skills applicable to a field of practice and the issues that arise in working with individuals, families, groups and communities in this field
Synthesise research and relevant psycho-social knowledge to evaluate the lived experience for individuals, families and groups experiencing social problems.
Critically evaluate policy developments and the drivers that lead to policy shifts.
Critically analyse the ways in which social problems are conceptualised and the values that underpin these conceptualisations.

title: LEADERSHIP IN SOCIAL WORK
syllabus_overview: In this subject you will be assisted to draw upon the audit of your individual skills and knowledge which you have studied during the course. You will be assisted to review the role of social work and social workers in promoting effective social work practice, social policies and social change in national and international communities. The focus is upon understanding leadership theories and applying this to the purpose, values, knowledge and practice of social work including reflecting critically on your own practice. You will expand your understanding of diversity and inequality including in relation to Western and First Nations worldviews and will be assisted to explore the above concepts within fields of practice. This subject includes professional learning, practical experiences or portfolio activities which contribute to the completion of the Career Ready AdvantageTM award.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your personal social work practice and identify how you operationalize theoretical knowledge, values and skills in relation to leadership in social work.
Analyse the approach, processes and impact of leaders in social work to create effective social work practice in complex contexts.
Critically analyse, reflect on and communicate your personal leadership style and effectiveness as part of your social work identity as a change agent influencing progressive social change.
Evaluate leadership theories and approaches and their application to social work in a range of contexts including contrasting Western and First Nations worldviews.

title: PROGRAM DESIGN AND EVALUATION
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide you with a theoretical and practical understanding of program design as an organised response to social problems and issues. You will develop skills in identifying research evidence to support an understanding of the causation of specific social issues (creating a theory of change). You will then be introduced to program logic and use this framework to design an evidence informed social work intervention and an outcome evaluation plan to effectively respond to a specific scenario. This knowledge will be contextualised in the contemporary human service environment. You will be also introduced to concepts such as co design, implementation, program resourcing and budgeting, and outcome evaluation.
learning_outcomes: Design program objectives and integrated evaluation strategies.
Analyse data to generate and evaluate a complex program budget
Critically analyse critically the social and political context of designing a social program
Critcally apply an evidence-informed approach to program design and evaluation.
Critically analyse critically relevant theoretical and empirical literature to construct problem analyses and theory of change in relation to identified social issues.

Students will have opportunities to further develop skills in basic interviewing, assessment and intervention processes required for practice along with skills in research. Critically analyse and evaluate the impact of complex organisational contexts on practice.

Apply and appraise professional knowledge and skills in the context of the Australian Association of Social Workers Practice Standards with autonomy and expert judgement as a beginning social work practitioner.

Through this professionally supervised practice experience, students will be provided with constructive feedback on their performance and will be challenged to critically self-reflect on their practise.
